items.statement: Synthetic rutile demand steady with traditional Japanese customers buying again, volumes elevated based on orders in hand
items.quote: The volumes have gone up because of our orders from our regular geography, which is Japan. And the volumes will stay elevated on the basis of the orders in hand.

items.statement: PVC domestic capacity serves only 40% of demand, demand growing at 8% CAGR, India to remain net importer
items.quote: PVC, you see, even today as we talk, the domestic capacity is acting only to serve 40% of the total demand. And even as we talk now, the demand continues to grow at 8% CRG. So, the new capacities coming will only add to that demand growth and India will continue to be a net PVC importer even in the coming years.

items.statement: CPVC prices eroded over 15% QoQ in Q2 FY26 due to import competition and market corrections
items.quote: However, the quarter also saw significant price erosion of over 15% over the last quarter in CPVC, driven by higher import competition and market-led pricing corrections.

items.statement: Synthetic iron oxide pigment volumes and realizations held steady across geographies, insulated from industry volatility
items.quote: Importantly, our synthetic iron oxide pigment business remained insulated from the price volatility seen across the industry, with both volumes and realizations holding steady across geographies.

items.statement: Caustic soda prices expected around $375/tonne (~Rs. 33/kg), tad lower than Rs. 35-36
items.quote: We expect the prices to remain in the current levels of around $ (+/-)375. So, if you put a number, it will be around (+/-)33.

items.statement: Renewable power substitution delivering savings: Q2 savings Rs. 2.75-3 crore, H2 expected ~Rs. 15 crore, annual target Rs. 25-30 crore at full scale
items.quote: So, I think our annual estimate was around Rs. 25 crore to Rs. 30 crores of savings at full scale. The drawdown this time has been around 80% and our savings for the quarter should be somewhere around Rs. 2.75 crores to Rs. 3 crores. Maybe this will go up to Rs. 5 crore, Rs. 5.5 crores.

items.statement: Renewable power currently meets 25% of energy consumption at south facility
items.quote: 25% we communicated when we went into the CAPEX of our south facility will be substituted by solar.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross debt Rs. 365 crore vs Rs. 425 crore in Mar'25, repaid Rs. 70 crore term loans, net debt Rs. 155 crore, cash >Rs. 200 crore
items.quote: H1 gross debt stood at Rs. 365 crores versus Rs. 425 crores in March'25, a half-yearly reduction of gross debt by Rs. 61 crores on account of scheduled term loan repayment to the tune of Rs. 70 crores. The company continues to maintain healthy cash and cash equivalent balance above Rs. 200 crores, thereby having a net debt of only Rs. 155 crores.

items.statement: Scheduled repayments of Rs. 125-130 crore annually till DVC loan closure by mid-FY27, next 10 KT CPVC capex to be funded internally
items.quote: We have a scheduled repayment of around Rs. 125 crores, Rs. 130 crores each year at least till half of next year wherein our DVC loan gets closed, paid off. I think the next NKT, the company is trying to fund itself internally.

items.statement: Expect net debt to reach zero by end of FY27 if no growth capex undertaken
items.quote: The net debt is around Rs. 150 crores. If my repayment is around Rs. 125 crores, Rs. 130 crores, so you can pretty well expect the net debt to become zero.

items.statement: Expect anti-dumping duty (ADD) on PVC to be notified this month, delayed implementation causing Chinese dumping
items.quote: We expect that this month we expect ADD to be notified because beyond this point, industry will find it difficult to sustain.

items.statement: Contingent liabilities reduced from Rs. 280 crore 1.5 years ago, no provisions needed per legal advice, dedicated team resolving cases
items.quote: If you have seen our trend for contingent liabilities, our contingent liabilities a year and a half back was around Rs. 280 crores. It is gradually coming down and there is a dedicated team who is working to close on this one by one.

items.statement: Basic chemicals feed specialty chemicals: PVC resin, chlorine, HCl used for CPVC and SIOP production
items.quote: For example, the PVC resin sits on the basic chemicals that is used to make CPVC. The chlorine is produced in the basic chemicals which is also used to make CPVC and the Hcl what is coming also is used to make SIOP. So, we have an integration of the products.

items.statement: Chinese chemical output growing high single-digits vs flat Indian production, aggressive dumping in PVC/soda ash, freight rate drops enabling competitive landed prices
items.quote: Chinese chemical output grew at a high single-digit rate in this period, while Indian chemical production remained largely flat. This imbalance has directly affected regional pricing and trade flows. Domestically, the Indian chemical industry continues to face aggressive dumping, particularly in PVC and soda ash and several other chlorine-based intermediates.

items.statement: SAP S/4HANA transition successfully completed, reflecting institutional strengthening and governance discipline
items.quote: I am happy to note that our transition to SAP's S4 HANA has been successfully completed. This is more than just a simple technology upgrade, it reflects our commitment to institutional strengthening, governance discipline and long-term stability and scalability.

items.statement: Birla Opus targets number 2 revenue market share and committed profitability within 3 years of full-scale operations
items.quote: we have committed to be number two as well as profitable within three years of full-scale operation. We will stay course on that.

items.statement: Birla Opus guidance of INR10,000 crores turnover by FY28 remains valid
items.quote: And your guidance of INR10,000 crores turnover by FY '28, does that remain valid? Himanshu Kapania: Yes.

items.statement: Birla Pivot on track to achieve INR8,500 crores revenue by FY27, may reach milestone sooner
items.quote: There is a likely chance that we will get there and hit that milestone sooner. But for now, we are not changing any of our direction as of now.

items.statement: Birla Opus expects continued double-digit growth quarter-on-quarter and significantly high growth year-on-year in Q3
items.quote: We are highly optimistic and results of September and October bear us out of a strong quarter 3, both on a year-on-year basis as well as a quarter-on-quarter basis. So our guidance is continued double-digit growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis and a significantly high growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Total capex spend for Paints business INR9,727 crores as on 30th September 2025
items.quote: The total capex spend for Paints business stood at INR9,727 crores as on 30th September 2025.

items.statement: Grasim outlined capex outlay of INR2,263 crores for FY26, INR941 crores deployed in H1 FY26
items.quote: Grasim has outlined a capex outlay of INR2,263 crores for FY '26, of which INR941 crores was deployed in first half of financial year '26.

items.statement: Birla Opus commissioned sixth plant at Kharagpur with 236 million liters per annum capacity on 15th October 2025
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have commenced production at our largest and sixth plant in Kharagpur, West Bengal on 15th October 2025. The plant has 236 million liters per annum capacity and is one of the largest paint plant in West Bengal and Eastern India.

items.statement: Birla Opus decorative paints installed capacity now 1,332 million liters per annum across six plants, second largest in industry with 24% capacity share
items.quote: With this plant's commercialization, the announced project phase of Decorative Paints concludes and the decorative paints installed capacity is now 1,332 million liters per annum across the six plants. This makes Birla Opus the second largest decorative paints company commanding 24% of the industry capacity.

items.statement: Chemicals business chlorine derivative capacity increased by 11 KTPA with aluminum chloride addition; CPVC and ECH projects on track for mechanical completion by Q3 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, chlorine derivative capacity increased by 11 KTPA with addition of aluminum chloride capacities. Two key projects, CPVC in partnership with Lubrizol and ECH remains on track. The mechanical completion is expected by Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: UltraTech Cement targets total gray cement capacity over 240 million metric ton per annum by March 2028 from current 192.3 million metric ton
items.value: over 240 million metric ton per annum
items.quote: The business has recently announced capacity expansion targeting total gray cement capacity of over 240 million metric ton per annum by March 2028. Compared to its current capacity of 192.3 million metric ton per annum for quarter 2 FY '26.

items.statement: Cellulosic fiber lyocell capacity expansion on track for commissioning by mid-2027
items.quote: The lyocell capacity expansion with the cellulosic fiber business is progressing as scheduled and remains on course for commissioning by mid-2027.

items.statement: Organized decorative paint industry grew low single digits YoY in Q2 FY26; excluding Birla Opus, industry degrew slightly
items.quote: As per internal estimates, the organized decorative paint industry has grown in low single digits on Y-on-Y basis in quarter 2 FY'26, largely due to incumbents push for lower-end economy products. However, as per our estimates, excluding Birla Opus revenues, the organized decorative paint industry has degrown slightly on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Birla Opus saw highest ever monthly sales in September and strong October despite extended monsoon
items.quote: Despite the extended monsoon, Birla Opus hits its highest ever monthly sales in the month of September and saw an equally strong October month, indicating increasing brand salience across markets.

items.statement: Cellulosic fiber utilization rates in China improved to 89% in Q2 FY26; inventory days sequentially reduced to 15 days
items.quote: the average quarter 2 FY '26 cellulosic stable fiber utilization rates in China have improved to 89%. And inventory days, though higher year-on-year, have sequentially reduced to 15 days.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibers EBITDA degrew 29% to INR350 crores due to high input prices of key raw materials
items.quote: High input price of key raw materials impacted the EBITDA, which degrew by 29% to INR350 crores.

items.statement: Chemicals EBITDA run rate improved to INR350-400 crores from INR250-300 crores last year; meaningful improvement depends on caustic prices and chlorine demand
items.quote: And Nirav, the honest answer to that is it essentially depends on chloride, given our large exposure still to the chloralkali business. It's a combination of caustic prices and chlorine demand in India. That is the most meaningful factor that drives our results.

items.statement: UltraTech Cement operating EBITDA per metric ton grew 32% YoY to ₹966 led by volume, realization growth and lower power, fuel, logistics cost
items.quote: Operating EBITDA per metric ton grew by 32% year-on-year to ₹966 led by volume and realization growth, coupled with lower power, fuel and logistics cost.

items.statement: Textile business returned to profitability with EBITDA INR24 crores due to normalization of linen input prices; historically 8-10% EBITDA margins
items.quote: The business has demonstrated remarkable turnaround, returning to profitability with EBITDA of INR24 crores due to normalization of input prices in linen segment. Just as a reference, this business historically demonstrated 8% to 10% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Birla Opus achieved 50,000 distributors target; dealer participation grew double-digit in September and October
items.quote: Percy Panthaki: Can you just tell us the number of distributors, your target was 50,000. Have you achieved that target? Himanshu Kapania: Yes, we are there.

items.statement: Birla Pivot revenues grew 15% sequentially in Q2 FY26 despite monsoons; annualizing over INR6,000 crores
items.quote: the revenues are sequentially higher by 15% in spite of monsoons. Secondly, it also gears up for new aspirations, which means newer targets to our businesses beyond its stated revenue guidance of achieving INR8,500 crores or $1 billion mark by FY'27.

items.statement: Birla Opus premium and luxury products revenue contribution at 65% across all categories; launched 13 new products in Q2, portfolio now 190+ products
items.quote: On the product front, the premium and luxury products revenue contribution was upwards at 65% of revenue, covering all categories across emulsion enamel, wood finish and waterproofing, including retail and institutional segment. The company has also launched an array of new products and crossed 190-plus products in this portfolio. Out of this, 13 new products were launched during this quarter.

items.statement: Chemicals specialty chemicals revenue contribution improved to 30% from 26% YoY driven by 34% volume growth from stabilization of newer capacity
items.quote: Specialty Chemicals revenue contribution improved to 30% versus 26% in quarter 2 FY '25 driven by volume growth of 34% year-on-year due to stabilization of newer capacity.

items.statement: Birla Pivot buyers acquired last year purchasing average more than twice the amount this year; strong repeat transaction growth
items.quote: all the buyers who we acquired last year, they've already purchased on an average more than twice the amount this year, giving us the confidence that whatever experience that we're delivering through both a combination of our assortment and our technology backbone is giving results.

items.statement: Standalone net debt declined INR292 crores to INR6,861 crores as on 30th September 2025; net debt to TTM EBITDA improved to 2.19x from 2.41x
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, net debt declined by INR292 crores and stood at INR6,861 crores as on 30th September 2025 as against INR7,153 crores as on 30th June 2025. Stand-alone net debt to TTM EBITDA stood at 2.19x as against 2.41x.

items.statement: Aditya Birla Capital total lending portfolio (NBFC + Housing Finance) highest ever at nearly INR1,78,000 crores, up 29% YoY
items.quote: Total lending portfolio, that is NBFC, and housing finance stood highest ever at nearly INR1,78,000 crores, up 29% year-on-year.

items.statement: Aditya Birla Capital total AUM (AMC, Life and Health insurance) grew 10% YoY to nearly INR550,000 crores
items.quote: Total assets under management of AMC, Life and Health insurance grew by 10% year-on-year at nearly INR550,000 crores.

items.statement: Chemicals profitability depends on caustic prices and chlorine demand; predicting caustic prices long-term is tricky
items.quote: And the business of predicting caustic prices for a long time is very tricky. So far, we can make our best estimates, but it's a tricky business.

items.statement: Green energy savings estimated at ₹30-40 crore annually at full utilization, dependent on DISCOM tariff
items.quote: If the DISCOM tariff remains the same, the savings will be to the tune of ₹30 crores to ₹40 crores at this. If the DISCOM tariff increases further, the savings will increase. If it reduces, the savings will decrease.

items.statement: ₹92 crore investment approved for knit division modernization, capacity expansion from 700 to 900 tons/month, and new printing facility
items.quote: Under the initiative, the company has planned to invest almost ₹92 crores in the modernization and upgradation of the knit division and this will also give us an additional product mix as we are adding a printing facility during this expansion.

items.statement: ₹55 crore modernization capex budget approved for FY26
items.quote: Just to share with you the figure for modernization CAPEX for the year '25-'26, we have approved a budget of ₹55 crores.

items.statement: ₹60 crore equity investment in group captive renewable power with Adani Green Energy Solutions
items.quote: For power, we have invested ₹60 crores as a group captive investment with Adani Energy Solution, which is part of the equity participation, which we have to do if you have to become a group captive member for any power plant.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity increased to 70 MW (10 MW behind-the-meter + 60 MW round-the-clock), covering 70% of total consumption
items.quote: The company have invested significantly in 70 megawatts of renewable energy, 10 megawatts behind the meter, which we shared in the previous call also and 60 megawatts of round-the-clock power, which the Board had cleared a few days back, and today, we approved this further.

items.statement: Knit fabric capacity expanding from 700 to 900 tons/month, with 120 tons/month printed fabric capacity added
items.quote: After this expansion from 700 tons to the current capacity of knitting, we will move to 900 tons of capacity. And out of these 900 tons, 120 metric tons would be printed, and the balance would be nonprinted for the way we are doing right now.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin expanded 195 bps YoY to 38.4%, EBITDA margin expanded 318 bps YoY to 6.8%
items.quote: 445 crores, up 4.1% YoY, with the gross margin expanding to 38.4%, a 195-basis point improvement YoY and 116 basis point QoQ improvement, primarily led by lower raw material costs and a more profitable product mix. EBITDA came in at ₹ 79 crores, rising 85.6% YoY with the EBITDA margin improving sharply to 6.8% compared to 3.6% last year, a 318-bps expansion

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross margin improved 173 bps YoY to 37.8%, EBITDA margin improved 280 bps YoY to 6.8%
items.quote: Gross profit stands at ₹885 crores, an increase of 2.7% YoY with a 173-bps improvement in gross margin to 37.8%. EBITDA stands at ₹160 crores, up 66% YoY, with margin improving 280 bps YoY to 6.8%.

items.statement: Cotton yarn prices fell 5-6% in Q2 due to import duty removal on cotton and cheaper international cotton
items.quote: So, there is an impact of 5% to 6% of cotton yarn prices during this quarter because of the imposition of import duty removal.

items.statement: Cotton yarn price reduction of ₹8-10/kg domestic and 10-15 cents export in Q2 from combined impact of import duty removal, global cotton availability, and US tariffs
items.quote: Overall, the price reduction of cotton yarn has been to the tune of ₹8 to ₹10 for domestic and from 10 to 15 cents in exports.

items.statement: Renewable power expected to reduce energy cost by ~₹1 per unit, with annual savings of ₹30-40 crore at full utilization
items.quote: But overall, this will definitely reduce our energy cost per unit to the extent of almost ₹1.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 average working capital utilization reduced 10%, inventory down 16% (₹121 crore) and receivables down ₹51 crore vs March 2025
items.value: 10% utilization reduction, ₹121 cr inventory, ₹51 cr receivables
items.quote: Our average working capital utilization reduced by 10% in Q2 FY'26, supported by efficient inventory management, faster customer connections and better supply cha in coordination. We have reduced overall inventory by approximately 16%, contributing to ₹121 crores if we compare with the balance sheet, which we reported in the financial year ended March 2025. Similarly, our total receivables reduced

items.statement: Yarn utilization in mid-90s%, mélange down ~5%, knit down 8-10%, denim utilization stable but realization impacted
items.quote: Yarn would be in the mid-90s. So, that is not a challenge. We are maintaining the same level of utilization for the synthetic and cotton business. Some impact is there in mélange, that also to the extent of 5%. Denim and knit are having some impact, denim being very less, but not in utilization, more in realization. So, knit, there will be a utilization gap of around 8% to 10% at this point of tim

items.statement: Focus on optimizing product mix for better margins, especially in synthetic yarn; forward integration into knit printing and denim product mix expansion
items.quote: Second is optimizing the product mix for better profitability margins. This has been done in all the businesses, but the special impact of this is seen in the synthetic yarn business. Third is moving up the value chain, forward integration of knit and denim. We are adding printing and in denim, we are adding the product mix.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 4% QoQ; export volumes declined due to U.S. tariff impact
items.quote: Despite these macroeconomic disruptions, the company navigated the volatility, recording a 4% quarter-on-quarter growth in sales volumes.

items.statement: Domestic demand expected to stay robust; export outlook choppy for next few months but positive medium-term
items.quote: Demand side, I'm quite positive that it should stay quite robust on that front. As far as exports are concerned, I see it to be a bit choppy at least for the next few months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 7% in Q2 FY26 vs 8.1% in H1 FY26; pricing pressure from imports
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for Q2 FY '26 stood at Rs.22 crores as against Rs.31 crores recorded in Q1 FY '26 with EBITDA margin at 7% for Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Management sees pricing bottoming out with cautious optimism; raw material deflation unlikely to continue
items.quote: I feel it's kind of bottoming out because I'm looking at upstream raw material trends and assume that further deflation should not happen.

items.statement: Dahej TDQ capacity expansion 75-80% complete; trial production targeted mid H1 CY2026
items.quote: The work, in my view, 75% to 80% work is already completed. So as we go in this quarter, that is October to December, maybe in January to March, we should be getting into -- I think Anand mentioned briefly that the trial production should commence during H1 CY '26.

items.statement: Operating at ~65% capacity utilization; debottlenecking initiatives underway for specific products
items.quote: We have been operating around 65% capacity utilization. When you have set up a plant for much higher capacity, you're not able to load the volumes.

items.statement: Domestic market share around 38-40% of 80,000-85,000 tons annual demand; imports 20-35% excluding domestic producers using imported intermediates
items.quote: We normally target about 40% as a market share. Maybe we're hovering around 1-odd-percent here and there depending on the quarter-to-quarter and the pricing parameters and competition.

items.statement: Antidumping petitions filed on two antioxidants and two sulphonamides; investigation initiated, outcome expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: The authorities have found merit in our submissions, have initiated detailed investigation and we expect the outcome of these proceedings in the coming months.

items.statement: Antidumping petition on intermediate covering 30% of finished product demand; investigation ongoing
items.quote: The finished product made out of that intermediate was constituting 30% of the Indian demand. So hence, we thought it fit to look at that piece also.

items.statement: Working capital improved 20% via inventory management, production planning, forecasting; price decline also contributed
items.quote: I would say, by 20%. That is definitely there because we have taken some corrective measures in terms of inventory management, better production planning, better forecasting and raw materials, etcetera.

items.statement: High-cost inventory 90-95% exhausted; procurement at competitive rates if prices stay flat
items.quote: I think 90% or more than 95% is over. Maybe some small thing will be there. It's an ongoing thing.

items.statement: Conversion cost efficiency measures (steam, electricity, hydrogen) to kick in by Q4 FY26; sizable impact expected
items.quote: We should start seeing them kick in before quarter 4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Korean imports pricing below Chinese levels in antioxidants, aided by FTA benefits; antidumping duties separate from FTA
items.quote: In a couple of the quarters, there has been pricing by Koreans who have -- actually players have been pricing it below Chinese also. And volumes have gone up on account of that.

items.statement: New products soft launch underway; active commercial sales before end FY26; limited volumes initially until customer approvals and capacity build
items.quote: More an active commercial sales of it should start before the end of this financial year. But coming back to -- but these will be initially limited volumes that we can do until we get more further approvals from customers.

items.statement: Export volumes declined due to U.S. tariffs; domestic ~2/3, exports ~1/3 of Q2 volumes; discussing tariff sharing with U.S. customers
items.quote: I would say, about two-third, one-third, you can say, take a ratio. Two-third domestic, one-third exports.

items.statement: U.S. market structure dominated by EU suppliers; Korea gaining share in one product due to lower duty; India cost competitive vs Europe
items.quote: Europe will continue to dominate because it's a market largely supported by supply by Europe. That has been the core demand, core pattern of structure

items.statement: Long-term trust with customers; not cheapest but competitive on price; volume growth opportunity where share is lower
items.quote: While I think to specifically answer the question on how do we get whether a price or a volume advantage, again, it will depend from customer to customer. But clearly, from a price point of view, some customers don't expect us to be the cheapest always, but at least you have to be in the competitive range.

items.statement: Chinese and Korean dumping intensifying; competitors possibly receiving government support enabling unsustainable pricing
items.quote: Probably -- possibly -- I mean this is something -- it's not an allegation, it's a guess that there is some element of support from their end or from their government and that is enabling them to stay afloat.

items.statement: U.S. tariff impact a 'speed breaker'; exports not at standstill; working on tariff sharing and alternative geographies
items.quote: On the external front, while our exports push in the U.S. has been impacted by the recent tariffs, we view this more as a speed breaker and are positive of a workable way forward.

items.statement: Domestic rubber chemicals demand 80,000-85,000 tons/year growing 5-6%; NOCIL targets 40% share
items.quote: We are looking at 80,000 to 85,000 tons of demand per annum, in which NOCIL share is about -- we normally target about 40% as a market share.

items.statement: Balance sheet maintained in net cash position; working capital cycle reduced
items.quote: Despite these challenges, the company has kept the balance sheet in a net cash position and also reduced the working capital cycle.

items.statement: UK operations expected to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY26 and definitely by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We do expect to turn positive in the 3rd quarter of this year and definitely moving to positive by 4th quarter of this year in UK.

items.statement: Rs 600 crore savings target for FY26 likely to achieve only 75% due to currency and US pricing pressure
items.quote: So, overall, we would be in a broad sense, instead of Rs. 600 crores , we would say that we should be there about 75% of the numbers we get more or less.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 around Rs 1,000 crore; detailed plan with capacity additions to be shared in Q3 results
items.quote: It is going to be around that number, Abhijeet. In 3rd quarter, we will give you much better color.

items.statement: India capacity expansion planned: Soda Ash +500k tonnes (150k quick, 350k in two steps), Bicarb and Silica additions, FOS 5,000 tonnes L55 commissioned
items.quote: We do believe that there is a component of growth which we should be doing in India in terms of the Soda Ash, at least another half a million tonne, 150,000 tonnes of that should come very quickly. The 350,000 tonnes will take a little time, but we will bring it in two steps.

items.statement: Kenya shipment delays resolved; volumes expected to recover in H2 FY26 but at lower pricing than previous year
items.quote: Kenya saw lower sales volume due to shipment delays. However, in the second half of the year, we should see the volumes come back because most of the shipment issues have been resolved. The pricing will be lower than what was previous year.

items.statement: US normalized EBITDA run rate ~Rs 55 crore per quarter after adjusting for $5 mn WIP drawdown and export mix shift
items.quote: So, in all, I would say it is about, if I were to correct this, it will be about Rs. 55 odd crores would be the normalized run rate at the current pricing.

items.statement: India margins sequentially lower due to pricing pressure; prices now stabilized, margins expected to hold at current level
items.quote: The market is the same and stable because there are two issues that have happened. One is the anti-dumping notice itself has given a salutary effect in terms of imports coming down a bit and the pressure on pricing going away.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommendation by DGFT (pending MoF approval); lower end of duty ~$17/tonne, upper end $100/tonne; expected to make operations remunerative
items.quote: The lower end of the band is close to about $17. I think this will make the current producers' operations remunerative.

items.statement: Global soda ash demand flat near-term; robust in India/Asia ex-China, slight downward trend in China, weak in Southeast Asia
items.quote: Overall, the global demand for all key products is estimated to be flat in the near term with stable demand in Europe, Africa and America and also in regions in India and Asia excluding China, the demand is robust.

items.statement: China soda ash oversupplied; inventory 1.65 mt; new Inner Mongolia capacity driving intense competition; 50:50 natural/synthetic target implies 5-6 mt more natural capacity by 2029-30
items.quote: The policy of Chinese government as far as the central planning document is concerned, they want about 50% of Chinese capacity as natural and about 50% as synthetic. That is the stated position, which effectively means another 5 to 6 million tonnes of natural has to come on stream.

items.statement: Kenya litigation resolved in favour at Appeal Court; tax matter settled for ~Rs 16 crore expensed in Q2; counterparty has 14 days to appeal to Supreme Court
items.quote: Also, on the other matter which we have not highlighted but also got resolved during the quarter was all the tax related issues. We have settled the matter after agreeing to pay ~ Rs. 16 crores that is also expensed out in this quarter.

items.statement: Net debt up in H1 FY26 mainly due to Rs 250 crore currency impact and higher inventory; no long-term debt due in H2; next maturity Dec 2026
items.quote: So, the debt has gone up in H1 compared to March ending, mainly on the currency part. Of course, Rs. 250 crores is the impact of the currency impact. And the remaining is because of the higher inventory levels we had in H1.

items.statement: Proposing Rs 1,500 crore NCDs for general purpose; to fund India debottlenecking and capacity growth (Soda Ash, Bicarb, Silica, FOS)
items.quote: This is a general purpose NCDs because we have plans in India and other places which we will highlight, as soon as, we get all the approvals in place.

items.statement: India Q2 FY26 volumes up: Soda Ash +30k tonnes, Salt +50k tonnes, Bicarb +14k tonnes YoY; FOS sales 858 MT vs 675 MT YoY
items.quote: Quarterly volume of all products increased including sales volume of FOS which went to 858 metric tonnes in Q2FY26 compared to 675 metric tonnes in Q2 of the last

items.statement: Rallis Q2 FY26: revenue -7%, volume -10%, price +3%, EBITDA margin 18%
items.quote: Rallis saw overall revenue de-growth of 7%, volume de-growth of 10% and price growth of 3% and overall EBITDA stood at 18% in Q2FY26.

items.statement: US Q2 EBITDA depressed by $5 mn WIP drawdown from plant reconfiguration; export volume pushed from Q1 inflated Q2 export share by ~20k tonnes
items.quote: There was a drawdown of work in progress, which was mainly on account of certain reconfigurations the plant had done. There is nothing to do with sales. It is fundamentally internal work, material work-in-progress stocks, which had to be drawn down that led to under-absorption of fixed costs.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks and tariff uncertainties persist; tariff issues negatively impacted PV glass in Malaysia/Vietnam; resolution expected to ease situation
items.quote: Geopolitical risks and tariff uncertainties persist. The tariff announcements did negatively impact PV glass manufacture in Malaysia and Vietnam. Slow pace of economic recovery is expected to continue into 2026. The tariff issues are getting solved as we move along and as they get resolved, the situation will

items.statement: US domestic contract renegotiation in final leg, range-bound; export side tough in Southeast Asia; domestic pricing to remain in last 2-year range
items.quote: On the export side, while many markets are okay, it is turning out to be tough in terms of the Southeast Asian market. So, we will come back with specific number on the export side only. The domestic should remain pretty much in the range we have been doing last 2 years.

items.statement: UK one-time provision of Rs 65 crore for future contractual obligations after Lostock cessation
items.quote: This is because all the contractual obligations were reviewed this quarter after complete cessation of operation, and we have estimated that it is prudent to provide for Rs. 65 crores which is the future obligations brought forward both from supply and sales side.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit top-line growth in due course, driven by volume-led growth and GST benefits
items.quote: Well, I would certainly think that we should be looking at getting to double digits in due course, because there seems to be a very positive sentiment around consumer goods and especially foods.

items.statement: Underlying demand momentum was strong before GST disruption; rural growing faster than urban
items.quote: Our momentum was very similar. And we were really hoping to see a very-very good September. But unfortunately, it did get stymied a bit.

items.statement: Gross margin headwinds from palm oil and other commodities are behind; EBITDA margin may see slight haircut to drive volume growth
items.quote: if we have to get aggressive top-line growth, then we might have to look at a slight haircut as far as margins are concerned

items.statement: Commodity costs within control: flour up 2% QoQ and 6% YoY; palm oil down sequentially; sugar up 1% QoQ, 3% YoY; cocoa up 5% QoQ, 9% YoY
items.quote: The commodities are looking reasonable, I would say. So, if you were to look at flour versus the previous quarter, we are up 2% in price versus last year, same quarter, we are up 6%.

items.statement: Wafers fifth consecutive quarter of healthy double-digit growth; Croissant and Rusk high double-digit growth
items.quote: Wafers, again, is the fifth consecutive quarter of healthy double -digit growth, augmented by additional capacity that we are putting up in our plant in North.

items.statement: New launches: Pure Magic Choco Tarts, ChocoStars, Choco Frames (Harry Potter), NutriChoice 100% millet cookies, Tiger Doodh Glucose, Chunkies Coconut and Chocochip
items.quote: We have got Choco Tarts, we have got ChocoStars, we have got the Chocolush, which has always been there, and Choco Frames, which has got the Harry Potter theme around it.

items.statement: Hindi belt share gains strong; East distribution 90% normalized; South needs double-digit growth
items.quote: Our focus has been on the Hindi belt. And the Hindi belt has been performing really well on a low base, albeit. So Hindi belt share gains have been very good.

items.statement: Regional players (15-18% market share) fighting on price; GST cut to 5% reduces their tax advantage; national players aggressive in modern trade with discounts
items.quote: These guys are not launching differentiated products. They are basically fi ghting on price. And that's what will become different now

items.statement: GST rate cut to 5% for 85% of business effective 22 Sep 2025; passed benefit via price cuts and grammage increases; state fiscal incentives at risk but engaging governments
items.quote: 85% of our business underwent a change in GST rates with effect from 22nd September 2025, which did cause a little bit of de-stocking, etc., but it was temporary.

items.statement: Africa JV in Kenya shaping up well; cake brownie product doing well after relaunch; cheese seeing sequential market share gains in e-commerce and general trade
items.quote: Our international business, Africa business continues to do well. We have a JV in Kenya, which is shaping up quite well.

items.statement: Trade support during GST transition was minimal and measured to avoid stockpiling; quantified as 2-2.5% top-line impact for quarter
items.quote: We could have probably grown 6 %-6.5%-7% more in the last month of the quarter, which could have overall given us maybe 2 %-2.5% extra growth for the full quarter.

items.statement: Rakshit Hargave joining as CEO in December; Varun Berry to mentor and not handle operations directly
items.quote: Rakshit is a great guy. I have been interacting with him ever since we hired him and I think he is the perfect choice. There is going to be nothing as a portfolio between him and me.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.3%, PBT margin 18.6%, PAT margin 13.8% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Profit from operations is up to 18.3 %, profit before tax is up to 18.6 % and profit after tax is up to 13.8 %.

items.statement: State fiscal incentives may reduce due to lower GST; mitigation via internal optimization and future price increases being evaluated
items.quote: there will be impact prima facie on account of this reduction. However, having said that, we have reached out to the state governm ents already asking them to help

items.statement: Renewable energy up 13% to ~45%; women factory workforce up 1% to 45%; Nutrition Foundation beneficiaries up 22% to ~300,000; S&P Global score 60%
items.quote: Our renewable energy has gone up by 13% to almost 45%. We have had a reduction in the water consumption in most of our plants. The women factory workforce has gone up to 45% by 1%.

items.statement: Volume growth of 6% in personal mobility, 8% in CVO, double-digit in industrial
items.quote: our personal mobility has grown at over 6%. Our CVO has grown at about 8% and industrial is in good double digits

items.statement: Rural B2C volume contribution ~25-30%, growing double-digit
items.quote: close to 25% of our B2C volumes are now beginn ing to come from rural and growing in double digits

items.statement: Lubricant volume of 60 million liters in Q3 FY26
items.quote: 60 million liters in this quarter

items.statement: CVO volume contribution ~38-40% of total
items.quote: CVO does about 38%, 40%

items.statement: Personal mobility volume contribution ~48-50% of total
items.quote: personal mobility is balance, which is 48%, 50%

items.statement: Base oil and forex volatility pressures
items.quote: The market conditions this quarter remained volatile with base oil fluctuations and out-of-range forex movements adding pressure

items.statement: Macroeconomic headwinds and tech shifts
items.quote: we are mindful of the external e nvironment, including the global macroeconomic headwinds and shifts in technology

items.statement: Launch of Castrol All-in-One Helmet Cleaner
items.quote: highlight of the quarter was launch of new products tailored to emerging consumer needs. Let me talk about the Castrol All-in-One Helmet Cl eaner, an innovative foam spray solution addressing helmet hygiene for 2-wheeler riders

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 12-14% from earlier 10-12%
items.quote: And therefore, I think that for this year, we would like to revise the guidance to maybe 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Long-term average growth guidance of 10-12% including new retail business
items.quote: So we indicate a long -term growth average of about 10% to 12% now with this new retail business as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of ~14% for legacy business, with ~150 bps drag from new retail business
items.quote: So we will stick to our original guidance of approximately 14% of EBITDA margin without this retail business, which we have indicated earlier, which will have a hit on EBITDA by about 150 basis points.

items.statement: Capex per new retail store estimated at INR1-1.5 crores including furniture, fixtures and security deposits
items.quote: And the capex that we identified was anywhere between INR1 crores to INR1.5 crores per store, which included capex for furniture fixtures as well as the security deposits.

items.statement: Opened 7 ZECODE and 2 DEVO stores in Q2 FY26; total 23 ZECODE and 12 DEVO stores; targeting ~35 stores cumulative in FY26
items.quote: During Q2 FY '26, we opened 7 new ZECODE stores and 2 new DEVO stores, bringing the total store count to 23 ZECODE and 12 DEVO stores since their launch. As discussed in the last quarter, we are working towards opening approximately 35 stores this fiscal year.

items.statement: Total retail space just under 2 lakh sq ft across ZECODE and DEVO stores
items.quote: In terms of square feet, we are just under 2 lakh square feet for both these stores combined.

items.statement: ZECODE and DEVO combined revenue ~INR30 crores in H1 FY26; initial full-year expectation INR70-75 crores
items.quote: The number I mentioned was INR30 crores, just under INR30 crores for the first half. And our initial expectation of INR70 crores, INR75 crores is still what we are expecting at this moment.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA INR145 crores at 19.5% margin; PAT INR87 crores at 11.7% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR145 crores as against INR110 crores in the quarter 2 of financial year '25, and EBITDA margin stood at 19.5%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA INR177 crores at 15.5% margin; PAT INR92 crores at 8% margin
items.quote: For the first half of financial year '26, our total income stood at INR1,143 crores compared to INR960 crores in first half of financial year '25. EBITDA for the period was INR177 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 saw steady growth supported by improved consumer confidence, early festive season, and gradual recovery in discretionary spending
items.quote: In the second quarter FY '26, the textile and apparel sector witnessed steady growth, supported by improved consumer confidence and strong er market demand. The early arrival of the festive season boosted retail activity, leading to higher footfalls and better sales performance.

items.statement: GST cut on select apparel categories expected to lift consumer sentiment and spending in coming quarters
items.quote: Looking ahead, the recent cut in GST on selected apparel categories is expected to further lift consumer sentiment and encourage more spending.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue mix: Fabric 77%, Garments 15%, Yarn & Other 8%
items.quote: Fabric contributed 77%, garments 15% and yarn and other 8% of the total revenue for the quarter.

items.statement: Traditional fabric & apparel business has similar margin structure; yarn is small B2B segment; apparel is largely outsourced trading model
items.quote: Yarn and knitting is a very small segment, and that is a B2B business. The main business is the branded fabric and apparel business, which has a similar margin structure. Basically, this business is a distribution -driven business, where we are a brand which has manufacturing capabilities, but also relies largely on outsourcing.

items.statement: Legacy business reaches ~50,000-70,000 retailers pan-India via wholesale and direct channels on outright basis
items.quote: So we go through a distribution channel, and the retail count would be approximately 50,000 to 70,000 retailers at minimum. There would be a larger number, but since we have the fabric business goes through a distribution channel where the distributor then buys and then sells ahead.

items.statement: ZECODE focused on Karnataka cluster (Bangalore + Tier 2); DEVO focused on North India cluster (Delhi, UP, Punjab)
items.quote: For ZECODE, for example, we have always mentioned that we want to focus on the Karnataka cluster for the first phase. So we are still focused on that cluster, where Bangalore is a center and most of the stores are in Bangalore city and suburbs and then we move to Tier 2 cities in Karnataka. For DEVO also, we followed a cluster. We started with Delhi and UP, and we've extended to Punjab.

items.statement: Gaining market share in fabric segment as branded players benefit from formalization and tax reforms; market not growing at company's pace
items.quote: So of course, the market, I don't think is growing at this speed. We are gaining some market share. But as a company and as a brand, I think the branded players, there is more aspiration towards the brand. And as the economy gets more formal with tax reforms and other things, then I think branded players will benefit from this.

items.statement: DEVO positioned as mid-premium mens ethnic wear (Kurta Pyjama INR1,700-12,000); sees right to win via Siyaram brand trust and sourcing network
items.quote: For DEVO, we have positioned ourselves as a mid -premium segment brand for menswear. So for example, Kurta Pyjama, which is an important category in the business, we have a starting price of approximately INR1,700 to INR2,000, and it goes all the way up to INR10,000, INR12,000.

items.statement: Marketing spend ~4-5% of turnover; traditional brands use brand ambassadors across media; new brands use localized advertising near stores
items.quote: First question that you asked for marketing, we have indicated an approximate spend of 4% to 5% of our turnover for marketing.

items.statement: ~50% of fabric production outsourced and increasing; garment production outsourced slightly more; ZECODE fully outsourced but leverages fabric expertise for sourcing influence
items.quote: And at the moment, approximately 50% of our production is outsourced. And that is going to increase by the day. This is for a fabric business. In the garment business, it is slightly more than that.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR4 per share (face value INR2)
items.quote: We are delighted to announce that the Board of Directors have approved an interim dividend of INR4 per share for a face value of INR2 each.

items.statement: Legacy distribution brands sell on outright basis with debtor days collection; monitor secondary retail pricing to protect brand equity
items.quote: So there are different brands and cater different markets. And all of these are on the outright basis. So we have a selling system, and we have a debtor days that we collect money in.

items.statement: Retail store economics still early; none of the stores have completed 1 year; larger format stores (5,000-10,000 sq ft) showing better results; some stores may not work and will need monitoring
items.quote: None of the stores have completed 1 year till the second quarter. But initial feedback that we are getting is that the larger sized stores, which were opened only after January in this year, are seeing better results because we are able to give a better consumer experience in that larger format store where all product categories are being displayed and give a better feel for the consumer.

items.statement: Management expects to get closer to 16-18% ROE band in near future
items.quote: Yes, that is the direction with which the management team is certainly working for, and we certainly expect to get closer to those levels.

items.statement: October motor premium grew 5.4% vs industry degrowth of 1.5%, YTD degrowth reducing
items.quote: The private sector in the month of October had a degrowth of 1.5% overall. Chola MS had a growth of 5.4% in the month of October, which means that our YTD, year-to-date degrowth that we had reported at the half year is now getting reduced as at YTD October.

items.statement: Target to reduce motor OD loss ratio by 5 percentage points in H2 FY26
items.quote: See, our point is that in H2, if you were to look at, we would certainly want this number to at least come down by about 5 percentage points for H2.

items.statement: Conservative motor TP reserving adds 3% to combined ratio, 10% higher than peers
items.quote: And in our book, that translates into an effect of at least 3% on the CoR. If without 1/n, if I'm talking of 112, so that means that the correct CoR on a comparative basis, this comes down to about 109.

items.statement: Expense of management at 29.1% excluding 1/n effect, below Board-approved glide path
items.quote: The expense of management for Chola MS for the half year stood at 30.5%, which measured without 1/n works out to 29.1% and is lower than the glide path plan approved by t he Board and presented to the regulator

items.statement: Crop insurance retender loss impacted GDPI by INR323 cr in Q2 and INR383 cr in H1, further INR150 cr impact expected in H2
items.quote: The crop, we have digested a good portion of the deficit that we had written last year. So there will be some more about at best another INR150 crores, which will get impact the growth in H2.

items.statement: Reinsurance accepted premium INR570 cr in H1 across property, crop, motor, group health with better economic combined ratio than core business
items.quote: Yes, the volume is a little higher than what we used to do in the past. And it is actually the volume is spread across lines of businesses. We do have in property; we do have some in crop. We do have some in motor, and we do also have a good portion arising from the group health business.

items.statement: Conscious reduction in 2-wheeler TP business reduced motor TP market share from 5.4% to 4.7%, OD share at 6.3%
items.quote: So if you look at it even in the motor book, while we have a OD market share of 6.3%, we have actually brought down from 5.4% to 4.7% in motor TP. So that is what is impacting the leverage.

items.statement: GST cut on motor parts from 12% to 5% will reduce claim severity, benefit commercial vehicle portfolio (37% of motor)
items.quote: Now the GST change that is coming in, in terms of the GST on parts prices, coming down from 12% to 5% will also give us some advantage as we go along as the severity of the claims will now go down.

items.statement: Motor TP premium unchanged for 4 years, industry expects price hike effective April 1 next fiscal
items.quote: I would tend to think that industry will be very happy even if it comes in from April 1. But then the necessity, the preliminary steps will have to be taken now to make it effective from April.

items.statement: Motor TP provisioning 10% higher than peers, conservative stance on rising third-party claim severity
items.quote: Chola MS continues to be prudent and conservative in its provisioning for motor third-party losses with the level of provisioning a good 10% higher than many of its peers.

items.statement: Combined ratio 115.3% for H1 (112.1% excluding 1/n effect), includes 3% from motor TP provisioning
items.quote: Consequently, the combined ratio for the half year was at 115.3% which without the 1/n effect stands reduced to about 112.1%. This 112.1% includes the 3% arising from the motor period third-party provisioning.

items.statement: Investment corpus INR18,380 cr with INR500 cr mark-to-market gains, PBT INR266 cr, ROE 6.2% not annualized, solvency 2.112x
items.quote: The investment corpus as at the half year was over INR18,380 crores, and the company had mark-to-market gains in both the debt and equity portfolios amounting to about INR500 crores. The PBT for the half year was INR266 crores with the return on equity not annualized at 6.2%. Solvency at 2.112x is comfortable.

items.statement: Investment book shifted to corporate bonds for higher yield, maintaining high rating profile, govt securities at ~40% vs 30% regulatory minimum
items.quote: We moved into a level of more towards the corporate bond in order to increase the yield on the investment book. That's the thing. But what we are doing very clearly is not to reduce our rating profile on those corporate bonds. We are only looking at those profiles which are high in terms of the rating and as well provide higher yield compared to Govt securities. So, we are not diluting anything on

items.statement: Motor OD loss ratios rising due to competitive intensity, corrective measures implemented
items.quote: But one area of concern I should admit, has been the way the motor OD loss ratios have been moving up both for the industry and particularly for Chola MS. We are seized of the problem and have taken several corrective measures.

items.statement: 1/n accounting base effect ends September 2025, growth visible from Q3 onwards
items.quote: With t he base effect of 1/n reporting coming to an end in September '25, the growth in business will be visible from Q3 onwards

items.statement: Management expects O&M revenue of INR 70-100 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: We have an order backlog of roughly about 600 crores in this sector. And most of these projects will go into O&M starting in next year. Next year, some will go into O&M and they will be continuously going into O&M. So, I think by the end of '26-27, we are looking at about 70 to 100 crores of O&M revenue.

items.statement: Consolidated order book reached record high of INR 422 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: Order booking and backlog continued to improve, reaching the highest ever level of INR 422 crores.

items.statement: International project order book stands at INR 930 crores
items.quote: And secondly, on the international project division, we have the order book of 930 crores.

items.statement: Enquiry pipeline remains robust with order book growth expected across all sectors
items.quote: The enquiry pipeline remains robust and order book growth is expected to continue across all sectors.

items.statement: EBITDA margins recovered to 18.87% consolidated in Q2 FY26 and expected to normalize at 16-20% range
items.quote: Our margin profile is between 16 to 20 and that is something we have maintained. The last quarter was a blip because of certain acquisitions which happened and certain one-time expenses which were captured. So, this is a normalized level and we expect to maintain this going forward.

items.statement: CAPEX is negligible as existing plants have sufficient capacity; only brownfield test facility planned at Nagpur
items.quote: So, CAPEX is negligible because we are well kept. I mean, all our plants are having enough sufficient capacity to handle this. As I said, the product business is looking at the big upsurge. So, we are well geared for this. We don't need any substantial CAPEX.

items.statement: Nagpur facility expansion involves adding test facility and manufacturing capacity through brownfield investment
items.quote: We will be putting up a test facility there and we will be adding more manufacturing. But the CAPEX will be quite insignificant, mostly brownfield. That's why it will be less.

items.statement: Product division revenue grew to INR 151 crores in H1 FY26 from INR 138 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: The product division reported strong revenues of INR 151 crores for the first half of FY26 compared to INR 138 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: Naval sector is well established with large orders received and growing traction expected
items.quote: Yes, we are well established in the naval sector and we have received large orders and this is an area we see constantly growing traction going forward.

items.statement: International revenues grew sharply to INR 456 crores in H1 FY26 from INR 288 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: International revenues grew sharply to INR 456 crores in the first half compared to INR 288 crores in the same period.

items.statement: International business now contributes 56-60% of revenue providing good geographic balance
items.quote: The good thing is that the highlight would be that Q2 half year, our international business has brought about stability to the business. We were a bit concerned and we had pointed out that we were getting too much domestic oriented. So, with this 56%, maybe going up to 60% international business, that gives us a good balance.

items.statement: Management is actively looking at larger inorganic acquisition opportunities and has increased authorized capital for flexibility
items.quote: Yes, we are also looking at some larger acquisitions on the inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: US market entry likely through inorganic route as front-end presence needed for application engineering
items.quote: I think in our sector, we find that inorganic approach is more feasible because front-end is needed in each market for a client because there is a lot of application engineering and the front-end is therefore needed. It's not so much an export, it's more, you have to be local.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission outstanding reduced to INR 200-250 crores with payments received from MP
items.quote: The outstandings have come down. We got a good amount of payments from MP but still there is a holdup and it's now in small spurts. About 200-250 crores.

items.statement: JJM project exposure reduced to INR 1,100 crores with projects in final 30% stages; creditor liability negligible
items.quote: Our entire exposure is now down to about 1,100 crores, and which is all in the last 30% stages. So, we have reduced this exposure and financially also, if you see our balance sheet, we received funds and we have reduced our liability. So, I think the good thing from our perspective is that our conceptual liability to client is reduced drastically and our creditor liability is negligible.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission fund resolution between Centre and State anticipated shortly; expected to release blocked cash flows and improve bid pipeline
items.quote: Everybody is very well aware that we are waiting for the resolution of the fund issue between the Centre and State and that is what we are hoping. And the only problem is the timeline is being shifted on a regular basis. We had expected in the budget last year, this year's budget in February. But it's November now and the resolution is still anticipated. However, I think things are moving and we s

items.statement: Domestic project execution dependent on policy resolution; management cautiously moving on new bids
items.quote: Domestically, it is completely dependent on policy, both center state policy, how it moves, and we will be cautious. We are cautiously moving. However, if the fund flow improves, we will accelerate our invoicing and bidding.

items.statement: River linking and irrigation projects expected to pick up in FY26; urban water and rural water catch-up anticipated in FY26-27
items.quote: River linking projects are ongoing and we are well positioned there for product supply. And I think the whole momentum is a bit slower. We expect '26 to pick up the river linking irrigation projects.

items.statement: Employee cost increased sequentially due to fixed site manning costs despite lower project revenue; expected to even out
items.quote: Well, we have a fixed cost there. Sites have to be manned. So, that cost structure is still there. We have had to mobilize to expedite the work and the revenues have gone down. But the type of work which is needed is there. So, I think there is a lag period to revenue and site costs. So, you will see it evening out.

items.statement: Preference shares reclassified to equity shares in authorized capital; never issued, held by promoter group
items.quote: There is a provision in the Companies Act that any type of share which remains unissued, that can be reclassified into any other type of share. So, we are going to reclassify it as equity share.

items.statement: Full-year sales guidance of INR 1,600 crores; H1 achieved INR 828 crores (over 50% of guidance)
items.quote: this has resulted in our highest ever quarterly bookings and showing it at INR 828 crores of advanced sales, thereby showcasing over 50% of our full year guidance coming in just these two quarters.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly bookings of INR 828 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 sales volume 293,000 sq ft carpet area (20% YoY growth)
items.quote: The company has achieved its highest ever quarterl y sales with sales value tripling Y-o-Y basis, which is to INR 720 crores, which is sales adding up to INR 828 crores, which is 48% Y-o-Y growth

items.statement: Strong demand across segments; luxury housing in Mumbai performing well, mid-income and premium segments strengthened; festive season and RBI rate easing boosting affordable/mid segments
items.quote: the luxury housing, primarily in Mumbai per se is performing really well. But the mid-income and the premium segment has also strengthened, that is what we have been seeing.

items.statement: Podium construction cost estimated at INR 2,500-3,000 per sq ft on construction area for Manhattan's 7-acre podium across four buildings
items.quote: if I have to give you a rough thumb number, it will be anywhere between INR 2,500 to INR 3,000 a square feet on the construction area.

items.statement: 15-16 projects with total GDV ~INR 8,000 crores to be delivered, constructed and sold over next 3-4 years; 7 upcoming launches with GDV INR 4,300 crores across 1.6M sq ft carpet
items.quote: Overall, 15 to 16 projects with a total GDV looking in and around INR 8,000-odd crores is what the company is looking to deliver, construct and sell in the next three to four years' time.

items.statement: Realization increased to INR 28,000/sq ft in H1 FY26 from INR 22,800/sq ft in H1 FY25 driven by Manhattan pricing at INR 30,000-32,000/sq ft; expects quarterly variation based on project mix
items.quote: As far as realization is concerned, I think if you see the first half of last year, we were at about INR 22,800 a square feet. This time, we are at INR 28,000 a square feet.

items.statement: Total debt INR 690 crores as of Sep 30, 2025; debt-equity ratio 0.55x; weighted average cost of debt reduced 24 bps to 11.51%
items.quote: The company maintained a strong financial position with total debt of INR 690 crores as on the quarter end September 30, 2025, with a healthy debt equity ratio of 0.55x the net worth.

items.statement: Collections grew 52% YoY to INR 454 crores in H1 FY26; net cash flow pre-tax post-debt from OC received and ongoing projects estimated at INR 1,526 crores
items.quote: collection also with a 52% growth at INR 454 crores.

items.statement: Vikhroli approvals advanced, launch expected in weeks; Versova society redevelopment approvals phased, building breakdown in 20 days; Kanjurmarg approvals delayed by BMC elections, EC application this month
items.quote: Vikhroli, we are in advanced stage of getting approvals. Hopefully, in the next few days, I would say, or next few weeks, we should be able to complete a ll the approvals in place, and we should be able to start launching the project

items.statement: Revenue visibility INR 3,599 crores (INR 1,582 crores committed sales + INR 2,000+ crores available inventory); upcoming pipeline adds INR 4,357 crores GDV; total visibility sub-INR 8,000 crores
items.quote: The total visibility from this stands at about INR 3,599 crores, comprising INR 1,582 crores from the committed sales and about INR 2,000-plus crores from the available inventory to sale and revenue to recognize upon the life cycle.

items.statement: Manhattan 1: 89% sold, 80-90% construction complete, target completion Dec FY26-Mar FY27; Greenfinity: 74% sold, structural work complete; Eden: 98% sold, structure complete; Vihara: 81% sold, 9th floor rehab slab
items.quote: Manhattan 1 as a project, we should be able to complete, our target is by next year, December. But in RERA timelines, obviously, they are higher, but our target is between December FY '26 to March FY '27 is what we are looking at completing it.

items.statement: Manhattan 2 sold 38% inventory in <1 month; Thirty 3.15 Bandra commercial sold 5-6% in last week of September; sustenance sales continuing in October
items.quote: Ajmera Manhattan has witnessed exceptional traction. We have about 38% of our inventory is already sold in less than a month of the launch.

items.statement: Actively evaluating 30-40 society redevelopment projects; three-four new land parcels targeting INR 3,000+ crores revenue; business model spans greenfield, JV/JD, outright purchase, and redevelopment
items.quote: we are at least bidd ing for minimum 30 to 40 societies or probably given our offers or discussions or probably just evaluating. So, that's how we are working on

items.statement: UK investment repatriation ongoing, applied against loan and equity; Bahrain exited in FY22, received INR 35 crores down payment, 10,000+ sq m inventory entitlement to be monetized in couple of quarters
items.quote: Bahrain, we have received about INR 35-odd crores and that too when we exited the project in a few years before in FY '22, and balance of the inventory entitlement of 10,000-plus square meters.

items.statement: BMC elections next month expected to delay approval processes; Kanjurmarg approvals will happen post-elections; pushing to secure launch approvals before election delays
items.quote: Yes, 100%, there will be. That is where we are pushing to get all our approvals, whatever for the project launches, which we need to do in place because once the BMC elections are announced and people will start getting busy, there will be delays coming in over there.

items.statement: H1 FY26 sales driven by Manhattan (luxury, INR 30-32k/sq ft); next quarter Vikhroli to drive volume at lower price; realization varies quarterly based on launch mix
items.quote: Next quarter, we are looking at Vikhroli being the hero where we will see a larger number of volume coming in sales. Obviously, the sales price will be a little lower.

items.statement: Dedicated teams for each of four business buckets: greenfield, JV/JD, outright purchase, and redevelopment; all buckets active simultaneously

items.statement: Summer 2025 was phenomenally bad causing substantial industry degrowth; performance in sync with market

items.statement: Channel inventory slightly higher than normal at end of Q2; expected to normalize as season approaches in January-February
items.quote: We do have very high inventory levels in the channel, which is why the performance in the September quarter hasn't been what it should have been . But that inventory should sort of normalize as we get into the season.

items.statement: Channel inventory at end of September 2025 almost in line with September 2024; sales decline in Q2 automatically adjusted inventory levels
items.quote: as on September '25, overall channel inventory as per the data available with us is almost in line with as on 30th September '24, something here and there.

items.statement: Round-the-year portfolio contributed 21% of Q2 topline and 26% of trailing 12 months; healthy double-digit growth
items.quote: In all, to an extent, it has saved the day as they have contributed about 21% of the top line for the quarter and ~ 26% of the top line in trailing 12 months.

items.statement: Launched 9 new air cooler models in Air Force range (3-7 SKUs) targeting mass, rural, semi-urban markets; 8 new water heater models (6 storage, 2 instant)
items.quote: We have launched 9 new models of air coolers. In Air Force range, it is from 3 to 7 SKUs, and that is targeted towards mass market as well as rural and semi-urban market, while in water heater, total new 8 models viz. 6 storage and 2 instant.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined mainly due to operating deleverage; mass product launches impacted product mix
items.quote: As far as EBITDA ma rgin is concerned, it has declined mainly on account of operating deleverage. And we have also launched the product for the mass consumers and mass products. So that has, to an extent, impacted the product mix

items.statement: Expanded mass portfolio may impact gross margin by 1-2 percentage points but is accretive at absolute value level
items.quote: If this portfolio becomes a significant share of our total numbers, then at the GM level, maybe there is 1% or 2% point kind of impact. But at the absolute value level, this is going to be very clearly accretive.

items.statement: Backend scalability and operational agility built to ramp up production for strong summer seasons
items.quote: So, at the back end, building that kind of scalability and operational agility is something that we are fully geared for.

items.statement: Zero working capital pressure; core business capital employed only Rs 16 crore; treasury surplus Rs 577 crore vs Rs 685 crore prior
items.quote: In fact, you might have joined late in our corporate presentation, we saw we are sitting on treasury i.e. surplus funds at ₹577 crores as on 30th September '25 , which was about ₹685 crores previously.

items.statement: General trade terms remain 100% advance; no modern trade sales in September quarter so no receivables outstanding
items.quote: And with general trade, our trade terms are very clear since many decades, and it is with 100% advance, including this quarter.

items.statement: GSK China advancing towards debt-free; loan from Symphony India reduced from peak Rs 61 crore to Rs 27 crore, expected full payoff in ensuing quarters
items.quote: At the peak, the loan given by Symphony India to GSK China was ~ ₹61 crores, which currently stands at about ₹27 crores, and that should be completely paid off in ensuing quarters.

items.statement: Divestment process for IMPCO Mexico and Climate Holdings Australia ongoing; information memorandum submitted, multiple parties signed NDAs and evaluating
items.quote: Quite a few parties have signed the NDA, and we have shared our information memorandum with them. So, they are in the process of evaluating and hopefully taking the next steps.

items.statement: Interim dividend declared at Rs 1 per share (50%); total payout approx Rs 14 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: And about interim dividend, it is ₹1 per share, that is 50 % and total payout in first 6 months towards that is approx. ₹14 crores.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY26 topline Rs 384 crore (3rd highest in 11 years), EBITDA Rs 50 crore, PAT Rs 65 crore; ROCE high 4-digit % on core capital employed
items.quote: So about first half of financial year '26 on standalone basis, top line is ₹384 crores, EBITDA is ₹50 crores, and PAT stands at about ₹65 crores, down from ₹136 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY26 topline Rs 414 crore, EBITDA Rs 50 crore, PAT Rs 61 crore; core ROCE 64%, return on net worth 17%
items.quote: And all put together, consol PAT stands at ₹61 crores. So at a consolidated level, capital employed stands at ₹288 crores versus ₹286 crores, translating into ROCE in the core business of 64% and return on net worth of 17%.

items.statement: GSK China Q2 topline up from Rs 25 crore to Rs 32 crore, EBITDA Rs 3 crore, PAT Rs 2 crore; strong growth momentum sustained
items.quote: About GSK China for the quarter, top line is up from ₹25 crores to ₹32 crores. EBITDA stands at ₹3 crores and PAT at ₹2 crores. We are happy to share that there is a strong growth momentum, and that has been sustain ed in GSK China

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico Q2 topline up from Rs 10 crore to Rs 17 crore, EBITDA loss narrowed from Rs 5 crore to Rs 4 crore
items.quote: About IMPCO Mexico for the quarter, which is nonseasonal quarter as far as air cooler goes, but on account of other products, the top line is up from ₹10 crores to ₹17 crores and EBITDA is minus ₹4 crores versus minus ₹5 crores.

items.statement: Climate Holdings Australia Q2 topline up from Rs 30 crore to Rs 35 crore, EBITDA loss reduced from Rs 9 crore to Rs 7 crore; transformation executed
items.quote: it continues with somewhat growth momentum in line with past 3 quarters, top line is up from ₹30 crores to ₹35 crores and EBITDA losses have reduced from ₹9 crores to ₹7 crores.

items.statement: US tariff impact minimal as competition is with China which is worse off; no material impact so far
items.quote: Not much so far because our only competition is with China, and China is worse off than us. So, in that sense, it hasn't really impacted us to a great deal at least till now.

items.statement: AC GST cut reduced price gap but overall pricing gap still wide between average air cooler and average AC; channel pricing pressure handled day-to-day
items.quote: And yes, the overall pricing gap is still pretty wide between, let's say, an average air cooler that we sell and an average AC that is there in the market.

items.statement: Omnichannel acceleration leveraging digital platforms and alternate channels; targeted penetration in semi-urban and rural markets with Air Force range

items.statement: Market share stable among organized national brands; unorganized sector data unavailable but always disproportionately large
items.quote: The market share when we talk about the national brands, the organized sector players, our market share has remained the same. Now if people consider a lot of the unorganized smaller brands, then of course, if you increase the denominator, then everybody's market share would decrease

items.statement: Pathway recovery: Rs 50 crore fully provided by Dec 2024; Rs 4.5 crore received earlier, additional Rs 4 crore recovered in October; legal steps pursued aggressively with charge creation on real estate
items.quote: Coming to the update about the pathway recovery, which we had completely provided for by Dec’24, about ₹50 crores. So earlier, we received ₹4.5 crores and in October, post 30th September, we have recovered additional ₹4 crores.

items.statement: Expect good times ahead; next summer not as bad as 2025, even normal summer should yield strong performance; channel inventory to normalize by season

items.statement: R&D spend for FY26 expected at lower end of 6-8% guidance
items.quote: So Neha, I think we should come in the lower end of the guidance overall, that's what is our assessment today.

items.statement: Specialty launch spend increasing sequentially in H2 FY26
items.quote: We did see a slight increase in Q2, and we would expect to see further increases in Q3, Q4 particularly as we launch Unloxcyt.

items.statement: Leqselvi payer access improving, revenue contribution growing throughout FY26

items.statement: ILUMYA psoriasis market growth expected to continue

items.statement: R&D spend at INR7,827 million (5.4% of sales)

items.statement: ROW formulation revenues up 17.7% YoY, driven by generics and innovatives
items.quote: Formulation revenues in Rest of the World were $234 million up 17.7% over Q2 last year. We have seen growth both in the Generics and Innovative Medicines business in Rest of the World.

items.statement: Emerging Markets formulation revenues up 10.9% YoY

items.quote: We are studying and possibly waiting for the clear guidance to come before we take a decision. Because clearly, this would reduce potential investment, but there will also be impact in terms of future competition.

items.statement: Confident of achieving internal EBITDA margin target of 20%-21% for FY26
items.quote: We are confident of achieving our internal margin target of 20%-21% for FY26, as communicated earlier.

items.quote: ARV revenue grew by 69% year-on-year, reaching ₹325 crores or 37 million. This was primarily fuel by higher volumes and new tender wins across multiple geographies and we expect to sustain this momentum over the medium to long term.

items.statement: Average finance cost declined to 4.7% reflecting effective treasury management

items.quote: So, when we take it as a basket, we think we are close to neutral. We have a little bit of erosion with very low single digit , I would say it's closer to 1 for the quarter. And this is based on an overall basket of products.

items.statement: R&D pipeline has couple of products in technological strengths area (not necessarily amines); investment decisions in 3-6 months

items.statement: Global trade volatility from US actions creating demand uncertainty; hope for normalization

items.quote: you have inventories which have gone up broadly by I think so 155 crores-160 crores, right? And as we had alluded to, that we see a better performance, growth performance. So, we have been kind of putting inventory in

items.quote: you may be seeing that there is an addition of one intermediate in Phase-3 that actually may be a result of certain 2-3 intermediates actually being added

items.quote: but definitely, there will be an improvement , maybe double digit, we can Alicon Castalloy Limited’s Q2 & H1 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript expect growth in the next year in the top line. But maybe I think in quarter 4, we will be able to give a
