items.quote: Now we're again refocusing with the newer strategy to be putting, again, taking small B2C customer, which is every door now, which we study in the market where we've seen various small companies directly, you can, rather you can say, D2C, they directly send to customer on the , they're selling on their own platform.

items.statement: Price cuts not a concern in B2B express (freight ~1-1.5% of product value); challenge is volume stagnation from weak manufacturing
items.quote: So basically, Mr. Thomas, so price is really not worrisome in express industry as because what we're charging from customer as from their product value is very, very miniscule kind of like 1% -1.5%. So really, price cut is not main thing in this industry.

items.statement: Receivable days 60, payable 40, net working capital 20 days; debt-free with Rs 150 cr liquid assets; H1 operating cash flow Rs 20 cr
items.quote: Our working capital cycle remains efficient with the receivable days at 60 days, payable at 40 and net working capital requirements 20 days, reflecting strong control over collections and payments. The company continues to operate debt-free, maintaining liquid assets of Rs. 150- crores. Cash flow from operation during this H1 is Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with Rs 150 cr liquid assets
items.quote: The company continues to operate debt-free, maintaining liquid assets of Rs. 150- crores.

items.statement: Rail Express grew 25% YoY with 25 new branches; Air Express grew domestic & international; International Air grew 40% YoY; C2C grew 15%
items.quote: The Rail Express segment delivered another strong quarter from 25% year -on-year growth, supported by 25 new branch openings and growing adoption of appointed -based deliveries that improve pl anning and service reliability.

items.statement: Pharma Cold Chain gaining traction including via rail transport
items.quote: Our Pharma Cold Chain Express service is gaining steady traction driven by demand from temperature-sensitive shipments, including through rail transport, ensuring faster and reliable logistics for pharmaceutical clients.

items.statement: MSME recovery gradual; paper/plastic industry volumes reduced; manufacturing growth weak
items.quote: Second part, MSMEs really hit. So still, they're like trying to recover from that and they're gradually recovering from that because everybody, if you see industry -wide, everybody has impacted due to this MSME is not like improving.

items.statement: Added 30-40 sales/control staff for Surface; hiring for B2C/D2C team
items.quote: So we already put almost 30, 40 more people on controlling level because as you are aware, we have a structure of like 60 controlling offices we have. So, we have already put more team.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences maintains guidance of ~INR500 crore revenue and EBITDA breakeven for FY26.
items.quote: Yes, we are maintaining that. Sunil Kataria: Yes. I think we will be very close to that number on top line, and we are working towards breaking even on EBITDA

items.statement: Crop Protection H2 outlook is moderate to soft due to unseasonal October rains and reduced chilli acreage; diversification into maize and new launches expected from Q4.
items.quote: I woul d say the picture for the second half of CPB may be still moderate to soft is where I would put it. But the diversification and the long -term steps that we're taking, I think, is very clearly we are very positive about on the business

items.statement: Animal Feed delivered strong double-digit volume growth in H1 led by 18% YoY cattle feed growth; market share gains cited across key markets.
items.quote: Overall Animal Feed has grown at strong double-digit volume growth and where cattle feed, which is 50% of our business, right? And we are very, very focused on cattle feed, which is actually going really in the mid-teen's kind of volume growth.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil margins expanded to 22.4% in Q2 driven by higher CPO/PKO realizations and record oil extraction ratio.
items.quote: Vegetable oil posted stellar growth with revenue up 41% year-on-year and margins expanding to 22.4% driven by higher crude palm oil and palm kernel oil realizations and higher oil extraction ratio.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection margins compressed to 23.3% from 43.1% YoY due to excessive rainfall and lower acreages.
items.quote: Stand-alone Crop Protection segment faced a sharp revenue decline of 30% year-on-year and a 62% drop in segment results due to excessive rainfall and lower acreages compressing margins to 23.3% from 43.1%.

items.statement: Astec enterprise margins ~15%, CDMO margins 30-31%; overall gross margin ~44% in Q2 but fixed cost absorption limited by low revenue.
items.quote: So generally, if you see CDMO marginally varies between 30%, 31% and enterprise this year is coming to around 15%.

items.statement: Oil palm planting at very high level this year; benefits visible after 4-5 years.
items.quote: we have been doing a very hig h level of planting this year. The benefits will be seen only after 4 or 5 years, but the benefits will definitely be there

items.statement: Astec R&D centre operating at ~90% capacity utilization with 100 fume hoods and ~100 scientists; 12 molecules in pipeline.
items.quote: So occupancy-wise, we will be in terms of capacity utilization will be somewhere between 90% of the capacity utilizations because today's chemistries are much complex than the normal, say, 15 years, 20 years back chemistry.

items.statement: Astec plant utilization doubled over last 3 quarters; near breakeven utilization across sites.
items.quote: We have doubled the utilization of the plant. We are very near to the breakeven utilization where positivity can be seen in all sites.

items.statement: Creamline Dairy value-added products salience rose to 36% from 32%; Godrej Foods branded salience rose to 86% (85% per CFO).
items.quote: Creamline Dairy remained broadly flat on re venue and EBITDA with value-added products growing 10% and salience rising to 36

items.statement: Debt increased in H1 but expected to be stable for full year; working capital management remains tight focus.
items.quote: Despite the investment, the increase in debt is not in line with that. We have sort of reduced our working capital in the first half as well. And we will continue that in the second half and sort of ensure that the borrowings do not increase significantly.

items.statement: Animal Feed revenue flat despite 18% cattle feed volume growth due to lower realizations from softening commodity prices; vendor discounting continues.
items.quote: Animal Feed delivered strong volume growth, led by 18% year-on-year growth in cattle feed, though revenue remained flat due to lower realizations on account of softening commodity prices.

items.statement: Astec enterprise pricing stabilizing as old inventory clears; CDMO margins formula-based and stable.
items.quote: And in general overall, there is a price revision because of most of the old inventory is moving out, both the demand and the overall prices are slowly increasing in the market.

items.statement: Oil palm FFB volume growth 9% YoY in Q2; full-year FFB growth targeted at mid-teens.
items.quote: By the end of the year, we believe that we will end up in our overall fruit bunches coming in. We believe that we will end up in mid-teens kind of a growth.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY26 revenue INR5,182 crore (+8% YoY); PBT INR313 crore (+14% YoY ex-non-recurring).
items.quote: In half 1 fiscal year '26, Godrej Agrovet Limited reported consolidated revenues of INR5,182 crores, marking an 8% year-on-year growth. Profit before tax stood at INR313 crores, up 14% year-on-year, excluding nonrecurring items.

items.statement: Climate change and erratic monsoon cited as structural risk for agriculture-linked businesses; Crop Protection window narrowed by excessive rain.
items.quote: Now there have been challenges because of climate change, and you saw how the monsoon behaved this year. And there have been similar challenges in agricultural products for Astec as well in other countries because there were problems in Brazil and some other countries.

items.statement: Crop Protection pursuing extended label claims for existing products into new crops; regulatory approvals required.
items.quote: We are looking at some of the current products, can we get label claims registrations done and because they are equally applicable to some of the other crops. So that is an extension that we are also looking at that can we diversify ourselves and extend the usage of our current products to further crops, obviously, getting it approved from the regulatory authorities.

items.statement: Hitweed retains premium pricing and market share; Q2 decline attributed to category-wide spray window compression, not share loss.
items.quote: By all standards, Hitweed continues to command a premium over any other product in the market. And we still come out a premium the brand power is very strong. We don't have our understanding is very clear that we have not lost any market share.

items.statement: Sanjay Sethi stepping down as MD & CEO on 31 Jan 2026; Shwetank Singh taking over as CEO
items.quote: As many of you know, I'll be stepping down as the Managing Director and CEO of Chalet Hotels Limited on 31st of January 2026.

items.statement: Board declared maiden interim dividend of INR1 per share
items.quote: I'm also glad to convey that we were able to raise INR1 billion through our maiden issuance of commercial paper at a fixed coupon of 6.1%, which was rated A1+ by CRISIL ratings.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR25 billion over next 3 years primarily funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Under our current strategy, we have planned capex of INR25 billion over the next 3 years, primarily funded through our internal accruals.

items.statement: Delhi Airport hotel opening expected in H1 FY27; Cignus 2 at Westin Powai completion in Q4 FY27; Varca Goa construction to commence Q4 FY26
items.quote: construction at our upcoming Delhi Airport hotel is progressing on schedule with the opening expected in the first half of next financial year. Our second commercial tower - Cignus 2 at Westin Powai Lake is also on track for completion in Q4 FY27. For our property in Varca, Goa, we still await the final approvals and aim to commence construction in Q4 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Business on books for H2 FY26 remains strong supported by healthy demand across key markets
items.quote: Business on books for the second half of the financial year remains strong, supported by a healthy demand trend across key markets.

items.statement: Strong H2 outlook driven by festive season, domestic travel, MICE, weddings, socials and international inbound travel
items.quote: We expect a robust performance, particularly from our leisure portfolio, driven by festive and holiday season, increased domestic travel and commencement of the MICE season. Additionally, continued traction in weddings, socials and international inbound travel is expected to further support growth.

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin moderated to 40% from 41.4% YoY due to transitory impact of new assets; like-for-like margins stable at 41%
items.quote: EBITDA margins moderated to 40% from 41.4% last year. However, on a like-for-like basis, EBITDA margins were stable at 41%. The margin contraction in quarter 2 was due to transitory impact on account of newly added assets, including resorts in the ramp-up phase.

items.statement: Launched Athiva Hotels & Resorts brand; Dukes Retreat Khandala relaunched as Athiva Resorts & Spa with 147 rooms; 5 more properties (900 keys) to transition to Athiva
items.quote: Athiva made its debut with the transformation of the iconic 'The Dukes Retreat' in Khandala, now relaunched as Athiva Resorts & Spa Khandala, featuring 147 rooms and all modern urban resort facilities. This is just the beginning. We have identified 5 additional properties with 900 keys that will transition into Athiva over the next few years.

items.statement: Net debt INR20.9 billion; avg cost of finance 7.62% (down 38bps QoQ); raised INR1bn commercial paper at 6.1% (A1+); ICRA upgraded rating to AA- stable
items.quote: On net debt, our net debt stood at INR20.9 billion with the average cost of finance contracting by 38 bps quarter -on-quarter to 7.62%. We maintained a healthy liquidity position of INR2.9 billion at the end of the quarter. I'm also glad to convey that we were able to raise INR1 billion through our maiden issuance of commercial paper at a fixed coupon of 6.1%, which was rated A1+ by CRISIL ratings

items.statement: Residential project: sold 7 units at INR21,300/sqft; collected INR1.3bn cash in Q2; 314 of 321 units sold cumulatively
items.quote: For the residential project, during Q2, we sold 7 units at an average rate of INR21,300 per square feet. A total of INR1.3 billion of cash flows were generated by collections during this quarter. As of September '25, cumulatively, 314 units have been sold from a total inventory of 321 units of the entire residential project.

items.statement: Airoli project: Supreme Court order received; approvals expected in 2-3 months; Trivandrum project moving through government corridors
items.quote: The Supreme Court order has come through. And the cases are now being signed off on. We are in the queue, but we expect over the next 2 months to 3 months for Airoli approvals to come through.

items.statement: Payroll and utility costs up 20bps and 70bps as % of revenue due to 166 new rooms in gestation; expected to normalize as occupancy stabilizes
items.quote: We did speak about the opening of 166 rooms, and that's been the real impact on the payroll because while the teams have been hired and they have been trained and then put on the job, we have not started to actualize revenues from these rooms the way that we would in a stable environment.

items.statement: Q2 occupancy impacted by heavy rainfall (57% above avg in Himalayas), fewer long weekends, shifting auspicious dates; transitory margin pressure from new room ramp-up
items.quote: Disruptive weather conditions with long spells of heavy rainfall across the country impacted travel patterns during the quarter. Occupancy was also impacted by the gradual ramp -up of newly added inventory at the Bengaluru Marriott Hotel and the seasonal so ftness at the Westin Resort & Spa Himalayas

items.statement: No immediate asset-light management contracts planned; Athiva creates springboard for potential future asset-light business
items.quote: To answer your final part of the question in terms of an asset-light or managing hotels for others, look, at the moment, we don't have any timeline in mind. I don't think it's imminent. But what we've done is we've created a springboard for an asset-light business at some point of time, sometime in the future.

items.statement: Deepak joined as new Head of Investor Relations replacing Ruchi
items.quote: I also want to share with you that Deepak has joined us to head Investor Relations in place of Ruchi, who's taken on a new role outside.

items.statement: Domestic MDF volume growth in high teens for FY26
items.quote: we now expect domestic MDF volumes to grow in the high teens this year

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin (excluding FX, one-offs) in high single-digit to low-double-digit range for FY26
items.quote: operating EBITDA, excluding FX and one-offs, of high single-digit to early double-digit average for the full year FY26

items.statement: Domestic MDF volumes grew 30.5% YoY and 26.8% sequentially in Q2FY26
items.quote: our domestic MDF volumes grew by 30.5% year-on-year and 26.8% sequentially

items.statement: Plywood volumes down 5% YoY but up 18% sequentially in Q2FY26
items.quote: while the volumes were still lower by 5% year-on-year, we did have 18% growth sequentially

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin (excluding FX, one-offs) at 10.2% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Consolidated operating EBITDA, excluding the impact of currency movement on the Euro borrowing for the new plant and other one-offs impacting the quarter, was stronger sequentially and almost at par with last year at INR39.7 crore or 10.2% of revenues

items.statement: Operational cost reduction improved margins by 5.5% sequentially in Q2FY26
items.quote: we were able to significantly reduce our operating cost of production, the impact of which is 5.5% on our margins in this quarter versus the last Q1

items.statement: Realizations down 4% YoY in Q2FY26, with 2% due to price realignment and 2% due to product mix shift
items.quote: Overall realization was lower by 4% year-on-year. Just to qualify this further, almost half of this was attributable to the change in product-wise salience post-addition of the new plant at AP and also increase in OEM sales, implying a net reduction of only 2% on account of price realignment

items.statement: Domestic MDF demand growth expected to continue; no major capacity additions in sector
items.quote: the expected green shoots remain intact to support domestic demand growth on MDF. No further meaningful capacity additions in the sector

items.statement: MDF imports slowed to <1,000 cubic meters/month in Q2FY26 (vs. 20,000/month in H2 FY25)
items.quote: MDF imports slowed down. Run rate for Q2FY26 was less than 1,000 cubic meters versus 20,000 cubic meters per month averaged during second half of the last fiscal year

items.statement: Timber costs softening sequentially; chemical costs elevated but expected to moderate by Q3FY26
items.quote: improved supplies, timber costs continue to soften sequentially. With every passing quarter albeit, cost of chemicals remain elevated for now. This is expected to moderate from end quarter 3FY26

items.statement: FX loss of INR12.5 crore in Q2FY26 (INR40 crore cumulative H1) due to Euro borrowing
items.quote: the impact of which is INR12.5 crore during the quarter. On a cumulative basis for the first half, this is roughly INR40 crore

items.statement: Value-added products (exterior, HDWR, etc.) contribute ~44% of revenue mix
items.quote: on a pure value added basis, the high value proportion is roughly 44% for us

items.statement: Targets double-digit EBITDA margin for Sunbeam in FY27
items.quote: We are expecting a 10% or double-digit EBITDA for the next financial year.

items.statement: Targets consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA of around 2x for FY27
items.quote: I think we will be closer to the number of two net debt-to-EBITDA for the consolidation for FY27.

items.statement: Indicates FY26 CAPEX around INR 1,000 crores for Craftsman standalone
items.quote: It will be around closer to INR 1,000 crores for Craftsman and DR depends on how much land we buy.

items.statement: Sets minimum pre-tax ROCE threshold of 20% for new CAPEX
items.quote: The new CAPEX, the minimum threshold level will be a pre-tax ROC of 20%.

items.statement: Reaffirms $100 million revenue target for data center business by 2029-2030
items.quote: I stick to the same number from India, $100 million, going into 2029 or 2030, as the case may be.

items.statement: Kothavadi plant has $50 million order book on paper for stationary engines, rest in final discussions
items.quote: The order book is of the $100 million, I think $50 million of the order book is on paper received with us and products are under development, rest of it is in final stage of discussions.

items.statement: Alloy wheel plants have customer orders above 6 million units against 7 million capacity
items.quote: We are having order of the customers above 6 million and we are putting capacity of 7 million because of the seasonality of the business.

items.statement: German subsidiary Fronberg Guss has full order book and growing revenue for data center engine blocks
items.quote: The order book is full. Even the revenue has increased.

items.statement: DR Axion CAPEX of INR 280 crores for cylinder blocks and new land acquisition
items.quote: We have an order on hand for which we need to do a CAPEX, so we just taken a larger piece of land so that we have for the future.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity expanding to 7 million units with phase-II at Hosur coming in next couple of quarters
items.quote: Another 2 million will go to phase-II which is to be installed in the coming couple of quarters at the Hosur plant. With that we are having order of the customers above 6 million and we are putting capacity of 7 million.

items.statement: Kothavadi phase-I operational for industrial engineering; phase-II for large engine blocks work-in-progress with revenue from 2029
items.quote: The Kothavadi plant is operational at phase-I level which is for engineering products. For the Powertrain portion of it which is the stationary engines, as I mentioned, the revenue stream will start in 2029.

items.statement: Powertrain capacity utilization status quo with no new product additions
items.quote: Powertrain more or less it is the same. We have not added any product per se to the Powertrain business.

items.statement: Aluminum Products margins sustainable due to operating leverage and larger base absorbing start-up costs
items.quote: These are sustainable margins, earlier the base was small when we tried to do the new Bhiwadi plant and that start-up operations cost actually really affected the equation of profitability for say a couple of quarters that is behind us now.

items.statement: Automotive sector contributes 80%+ of consolidated revenue
items.quote: The automotive-related business is contributing to 80% of the revenue, it is quite obvious. On a consolidated basis it may be even more I think.

items.statement: Seeing traction from multinational OEMs expanding India capacity by ~50% over next 3 years for domestic and export markets
items.quote: We are going to see the capacity of manufacturing with our existing customers growing around 50% in the next three years totally.

items.statement: India emerging as major manufacturing hub outside China with multinationals investing for export to Middle East, Africa, South America
items.quote: Outside China, I think India is very surely becoming the largest manufacturing hub with eye for the Indian market growth as well as the Middle East, Asia Pacific, the African markets and South Asian markets.

items.statement: Plans to sell Gurgaon land from January 2026 to reduce Sunbeam and group debt; process through mid-FY27
items.quote: From January onwards, the land can be put up for sale. So, we are in contact with the key people and large organizations to look at the land sale. This will be a process which will go more through the middle of the next financial year.

items.statement: Rules out large M&A for next 18 months; only small tuck-ins possible for technology
items.quote: Currently, in the next 18 months, we are not looking at any large inorganic subjects. It may be a few crores here and there for some slump sale for taking over some technological area somewhere, it can be possible, but I would rule out any M&A in a big way in the next 18 months.

items.statement: German subsidiary Fronberg Guss H1 revenue INR 158 crores, EBITDA INR 14.87 crores, PAT ~INR 8 crores
items.quote: The H1 revenue is around INR 158 crores and we had an EBITDA of around INR 14.87 crores, EBIT of around INR 11.4 crores. So, our PAT itself for the first half of the year is almost INR 8 crores totally on this matter.

items.statement: Kothavadi large engine development costs expensed quarterly during 3-4 year validation period before revenue
items.quote: No, see since the phase-I of the plant is operational, we cannot be capitalizing anything. So, we are incurring cost as of today and we are expensing only.

items.statement: Targeting ROA of 1.2% for FY26, translating to ROE of 8-9%
items.quote: At this particular point in time, we are targeting to have an ROE of at least around 1.2% as things stand today from here and then improve with some incremental efforts on our side more in terms of recovery from our recent NPA pool, which is likely to give the uptick.

items.statement: Targeting NIM of around 8% over next two quarters
items.quote: We will be targeting around 8% from where we are today. That's what we have in mind at this particular point in time.

items.statement: Expecting MFI flow forwards of ₹35 crore per month in Q3 and ₹25 crore per month in Q4
items.value: ₹35 crore per month in Q3, ₹25 crore per month in Q4
items.quote: In Q3, we expect flows to be around ₹35 crore per month. And in Q4, we are targeting about ₹25 crore per month.

items.statement: Targeting cost-to-income ratio of 70% in H2 FY26
items.quote: At this particular point in time, from where we are today, being able to touch 70% along with the CGFMU costs that we have. That will be our first objective.

items.statement: Medium-term ROA target of at least 2% with 7-7.5x leverage
items.quote: I think our immediate goal will be to have an ROA target of at least 2% and with about 7x, 7.5x leverage.

items.statement: Gross advances at ₹11,124 crore as of September 30, 2025, up 18.9% YoY
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at ₹11,124 crore as at September 30, 2025, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 18.9% compared to ₹9,360 crore last year.

items.statement: Vikas loan disbursements at ₹905 crore in Q2 FY26, up 111% YoY; inclusive finance mix now 70-30 in favor of Vikas loans
items.quote: Notably, the Vikas loan disbursements stood at ₹905 crore in Q2 FY26, an increase of 111% on a year -on-year basis. This growth is on the back of the strategies that the bank embarked on a couple of years ago to move towards individual loans as against the JLG model. The mix within the inclusive finance model now stands at 70 -30 in favor of the Vikas loan.

items.statement: Inclusive finance run rate at ₹415-425 crore, targeting ₹450-500 crore consistently for next 4-5 months
items.quote: Currently, the run rate in inclusive finance has moved to around approximately ₹415 crore, ₹425 crore. So there is a marginal dip in the month of October. Fairly confident to get it back to close to ₹450 crore to ₹500 crore consistently for the next 4 or 5 months.

items.statement: Yield on advances at 16.5%, expected to rise 100-150 bps to 17.5-18% steady state after write-offs
items.quote: So what you are asking is how much it would be reversed, 16.5% currently, at least technically, it should go up by 100 basis to 150 basis points on upper right. So 17.5% to 18% should be our steady-state yield once we do a complete write-off and the business is as usual.

items.statement: MFI slippages ₹170 crore in Q2 vs ₹237 crore in Q1; bank-level slippages ₹206 crore vs ₹267 crore
items.quote: We had a slippage of around ₹206 crore in this quarter as against ₹267 crore in Q1. That is at the bank level. And if you look at MFI, we had slippages of ₹170 crore in Q2 versus ₹237 crore in Q1.

items.statement: Collection efficiency: 99.5% for last 12 months originated portfolio (60% of book), 98.5% overall in October
items.quote: It's around 98.5% in terms of the overall portfolio, 99.5% in terms of last 12 months originated portfolio, which currently comprises approximately 60% of our portfolio.

items.statement: Reduced SA rates by 1% at lowest bucket; FD rates reduced by 0.50-0.75% in 3-year and 5-year buckets
items.quote: In SA at the lowest bucket, we have been able to reduce our rates by about 1%. In the fixed depo sits in both the 5-year and 3- year bucket, we have been reduced our rates by about anywhere between ₹0.50 to ₹0.75

items.statement: Customer base expanded to 3.6 million as of September'25 from 3.2 million a year ago
items.quote: Our customer base expanded to nearly 3.6 million as of September'25 compared to 3.2 million a year earlier, reflecting our continued focus on financial inclusion.

items.statement: Digital deposits crossed ₹1,300 crore (10% of total deposits); acquired 80,000+ retail FD customers digitally
items.quote: Our bank's digital banking strategy has also played out with digitally sourced deposit, crossing ₹1,300 crore and constituting over 10% of the credit deposits of our bank. This channel has helped the bank acquire over 80,000 retail fixed deposit customers.

items.statement: Paytm UPI credit line: 50,000 customers onboarded, ₹50 crore sanction limits, avg ₹10,000, 15% utilization
items.quote: It comes to 50,000 customers, ₹50 crore of sanction limit. Utilization is up 15% to start with. Apparently kind of there is a pickup, which happens over a period of time and settles down around 25%.

items.statement: ₹1,000 crore equity raise is enabling provision; no immediate plans to raise capital
items.quote: This is an enabling provision. So we kind of already guided that we are comfortable with the capital adequacy of approximately 20%, a little higher than the regulatory requirement of 15%. So to the extent it is an enabling provision and it is not that we h ave any plans immediately to raise

items.statement: Excess liquidity of ~₹1,000 crore; will be deployed as disbursements pick up in Q3
items.quote: Yes. So we have excess liquidity of about ₹1,000-odd crore right now. But over the period of this quarter, it will come down as we basically disburse the new business.

items.statement: Investing in retail secured expansion (branches, infrastructure); targeting ₹125 crore run rate in 6 months
items.quote: Our intent is to really take it closer to around ₹125 crore. So that will be an investment mode in retail assets until we reach around ₹125 crore, which is probably 6 months away max.

items.statement: Karnataka micro mortgage GNPA elevated (₹270-300 crore of ₹490 crore portfolio); 70% of GNPA accounts paying monthly
items.quote: We have a sizable portfolio. We have ₹500 crore or the ₹490 crore portfolio, closer to around ₹270 crore, ₹300 crore is in Karnataka. So there was a pickup in GNPA. Good thing about the whole thing at least in terms of micro mortgages is that around 70% of the GNPA accounts are paying every month.

items.statement: Pre-approved inclusive finance limits at ~₹8,000 crore covering ~1 million customers (including inactive)
items.quote: Our preapproved portfolio in our approval limits for inclusive finance stands close to around ₹8,000 crore, around approximately 1 million customers, which also includes inactive customers.

items.statement: Nykaa expects strong Q3 FY26 growth driven by Nykaa Pink Friday sale and Nykaaland event
items.quote: Definitely for Beauty, we think our third quarter will be strong because of Nykaa, Pink Friday sale and also Nykaaland that’s happening now.

items.statement: Fashion growth momentum to continue in Q3 FY26
items.quote: we think the momentum will continue this quarter, hopefully.

items.statement: Nykaa Fashion Edit stores saw >50% QoQ increase in salience
items.quote: We are almost seeing more than a 50% increase quarter-on-quarter in the salience of merchandise through these stores.

items.statement: Beauty EBITDA margin improved to 9.0% in Q2 FY26 (up 40 bps YoY)
items.quote: the EBITDA margin for the Beauty for this quarter, it comes out at 9.0%, which is about 40 basis points higher compared to a year ago.

items.statement: Fashion EBITDA margin improved to -3.5% in Q2 FY26 (up 550 bps YoY)
items.quote: Fashion vertical EBITDA has improved to only minus 3.5%. This has come down from minus 9.0% a year ago.

items.statement: Nykaa Fashion EBITDA margin improved by 550 bps YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: we saw a massive improvement in EBITDA, 550 basis points improvement in EBITDA from minus 9.0% to minus 3.5%.

items.statement: Nykaa Beauty gross margin highest in 12 quarters at 44.9% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: the gross profit has come out at INR 1,054 crores, which is about 44.9% of net revenue and about 28% increase on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Nykaa EBITDA margin highest since IPO at 6.8% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: the EBITDA has come out at INR 159 crores, which is 6.8% of net revenue, a 53% year-on-year increase and highest EBITDA margin since IPO.

items.statement: Nykaa PAT margin highest since IPO at 1.4% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: PAT, it's come out at INR 33 crores, which is about 1.4% of NR and 154% year-on-year growth.
