items.statement: A&A segment added 4 Sensex listed companies including Airtel, HUL, Reliance and Eternal
items.quote: A&A segment continues to expand its client base, having added 4 Sensex lis ted companies, which include Airtel, HUL, Reliance and Eternal during the quarter

items.statement: Onboarded 13 new vendors for last mile auditing taking total to 60
items.quote: During the quarter, we also onboarded 13 new vendors to strengthen our last mile auditing capabilities, taking the total to 60.

items.statement: Proactive investments in technology and digital capabilities impacting margins short-term but strategic long-term
items.quote: We are making proactive investments in technology and digital capabilities, which, while impacting margins in the short term, are strategic in nature and expected to deliver meaningful benefits over the long horizon.

items.statement: Additional working capital commitment of INR 50-60 crores due to IFM growth; AR cleanup expected from Q3
items.quote: So we right now have an additional commitment to working capital of roughly about between INR50 crores and INR60 crores. So that is something that we are right now cleaning up a lot of the AR pieces. So you will start seeing that show from this Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Paid off INR 44 crores of debt as prudent measure
items.quote: INR44 crores of debt has been taken off the balance sheet as a prudent measure and use of that cash.

items.statement: Avon receivables of INR 280 million under review; conservative provision of INR 30 million taken; independent investigation initiated
items.quote: Now I would like to share an update on Avon, an amount of 280 million, which has come under review primarily due to lapses in thorough due diligence for a few customers. While this has resulted in certain receivables coming under stress, the company has already initiated an independent investigation and taken conservative provisions of 30 million.

items.statement: May see more provisioning on Avon; expect clarity by Q3; INR 5 crore payable may net off against receivables
items.quote: You may see some more provisioning. We are not sure at this point in time what the extent of that will be. But we do not want to guide you to say that we are 100% sure that we will recover th e entire amount. There may be some more provisioning that you will see. There is also a payable of INR5 crores, which you are seeing. So that, depending on the investigation, may well result in a decision tha

items.statement: Shifting towards private sector-driven client mix in IFM; taking government contracts selectively for better margins
items.quote: We continue to shift towards a more private sector -driven client mix and will take government contracts very selectively. This is a conscious and strategic move as private sector contracts generally offer better margins.

items.statement: Athena diversifying client base beyond BFSI into education, retail and real estate
items.quote: More importantly, Athena is broadenin g its client base beyond BFSI into new sectors such as education, retail and real estate to diversify its revenue streams

items.statement: Denave has high exposure to one large global tech customer whose marketing spend dropped
items.quote: Our exposure to that very large customer is very beneficial for the company, but has also resulted in the margin squeeze that we have seen at Denave.

items.statement: EBGC business impacted by IT hiring slowdown across major Indian and global IT firms
items.quote: The environment remains challenging due to significant spending cuts by IT companies amid uncertain demand outlook. Large-scale layoff across major Indian and global IT firms have further impacted hiring activity.

items.statement: IFM revenue grew 10% YoY to INR 9,608 million in H1 FY26
items.quote: In H1 of FY '26, our Integrated Facilities Management, the IFM business recorded a 10% year -on-year revenue growth to INR9,608 million.

items.statement: Denave revenue grew ~10% in H1 but margins under pressure
items.quote: Denave revenues have grown. So in the first half, almost 10% revenue growth is there, but the margin is under pressure.

items.statement: Global flight handling revenue grew ~30% in H1
items.quote: Global has grown by about 30% revenue, so -- but it's a smaller contribution.

items.statement: Athena revenue declined ~20% in H1
items.quote: Athena has declined almost 20% in the first half. So that's been a drag on the growth.

items.statement: Avon revenue dropped ~14% in H1
items.quote: Avon has dropped by about 14% revenue. So that's really the mix that you are seeing.

items.statement: Matrix revenue dropped marginally 2-2.5% in H1
items.quote: Matrix has dropped by a marginal 2%, 2.5% in terms of revenue.

items.statement: In advanced conversations with one acquisition target in value-added services space; margin accretive; may hear update in latter half of Q3 or Q4
items.quote: We are in fairly advanced conversation with one particular target. And if that goes through, then you might hear so mething in the latter half of this quarter or maybe in Q4, so -- depending on how the deal progresses. So -- and that is in a value-added services space, and that is going to be a margin accretive to the overall

items.statement: Denave on-roll employees 7,000-7,500; FMS business 5,500-6,000; non-FMS 1,500-1,800
items.quote: Denave our overall on -roll total count of employees would be between 7,000 to 7,500 at this point of time, out of which a significant chunk is from the FMS business, which would be about 5,500 to 6,000. So about 1,500 to 1,800 would be approximately t he non-FMS

items.statement: Avon issue under investigation; may see more provisioning; legal recovery efforts ongoing
items.quote: We are actively working with our legal team to recover the maximum amount po ssible. Other internal controls and vendor verification processes have been significantly strengthened to prevent any such recurrence

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected to remain under pressure for next 4 quarters; standalone EBITDA expected to improve in coming 2 quarters
items.quote: But yes, over the next three quarters, consolidated EBITDA will continue to be a -- sorry, for the next 4 quarters, consolidated EBITDA will continue to be under pressure.

items.statement: Tritium EBITDA and cash flow breakeven targeted for last quarter of next year
items.quote: Exicom BV, which is the holding company for Tritium Group of Companies, has approved $40 million fund raise to fund product commercialization, working capital investment and fixed cost coverage to enable Tritium to reach EBITDA and cash flow breakeven, which is in -- which will be achieved in the last quarter of next year.

items.statement: Critical Power order backlog exceeds INR1,400 crores at end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: And also, we are ending the quarter with a strong order backlog of more than INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Future tender opportunities in Critical Power total about INR700 crores
items.quote: All of them put together present an opportunity of about INR700 crores.

items.statement: Critical Power revenue grew ~60% QoQ and YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Both consolidated and standalone revenue quarter-on-quarter and serially as well grew by approximately 60%, which was quite a healthy jump.

items.statement: EV charging revenue grew 26% QoQ and 55% YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: When we look at our performance, we grew 26%, almost 27% compared to last quarter and 55% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin increased to INR60.3 crores in Q2 FY26 from INR49.3 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our gross margin with the increase in the revenue has also grown from INR49.3 crores last quarter to INR60.3 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA grew to INR15.1 crores in Q2 FY26 from INR12.6 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA continues to grow with the increase in sales, which is INR15.1 crores in this quarter as compared to INR12.6 crores last quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR32.7 crores in Q2 FY26 from INR38.6 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: But the loss has been lesser, it's INR32.7 crores as compared to INR38.6 crores last quarter.

items.statement: Product mix shift toward lithium-ion batteries constrained margins in Q2 FY26
items.quote: However, the margins have been a little constrained or challenging because there has been a slight shift in the product mix. The sales have also helped come through lithium batteries where the margins are a little lower than the normal other products.

items.statement: IPO funds fully utilized as per plan; INR17.29 crores remaining for Hyderabad plant as of Sep 30
items.quote: We have in Hyderabad as of 30th of September, INR17.29 crores still to be spent.

items.statement: Rights issue raised ~INR260 crores; INR55 crores unsecured debt repaid, INR106.9 crores promoter debt converted to equity, INR85 crores earmarked for Tritium
items.quote: We had also come out with a rights issue. Recently, we had raised almost INR260 crores. The good part is through that, we had repaid the debt of INR55 crores, which is an unsecured debt. We have also converted a debt from promoters of INR106.9 crores into equity, and we had earmarked INR85 crores for investment in Tritium.

items.statement: Critical Power exports to Africa and Southeast Asia accounted for 11% of Q2 revenue
items.quote: In Q2, revenue from Africa and Southeast Asia, these are the two geographies that we export to in critical power segment. They accounted for 11% of quarterly revenue.

items.statement: Added fourth system integrator with multiyear supply and AMC contract in Critical Power
items.quote: We also added a fourth system integrator by getting award for a multiyear supply and AMC contract.

items.statement: Delivered solutions for ~5,000 BharatNet sites in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We delivered solutions for about 5,000 sites for BharatNet in quarter 2.

items.statement: Secured first order from largest tower company in Africa; expect quarterly repeat orders under $1 million
items.quote: We executed first order for one of the -- for the largest tower company in Africa. This was the first order, and we expect quarterly repeat orders of about under $1 million a quarter.

items.statement: Geographically diversified into Ivory Coast and Cameroon in Africa
items.quote: We enhanced our wallet share with some existing large customers in Africa and also geographically diversified into 2 new geography markets, Ivory Coast and Cameroon.

items.statement: Sold ~20 battery systems to data centers in Q2 FY26; growing but small vs telecom
items.quote: Even this quarter, I think we have sold almost 20 battery systems to data center.

items.statement: Partnered with OEM to enter defense segment; supplying 43 chargers next quarter
items.quote: We partnered with an OEM to enter defense segment, and it's not easy to get approval for defense. We received it, and hopefully, it unlocks future opportunities for us. We're going to be supplying in the next quarter about 43 chargers under this project.

items.statement: Won ~50 high-power chargers for bus hubs in Delhi and for a truck OEM
items.quote: We have also won about 50 numbers of high-power chargers for bus hubs in Delhi and for a truck OEM.

items.statement: 100% of DC charger customers migrated to Generation 2 platform
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that 100% of the customers have migrated to this platform, seeing the value it brings to the table for them.

items.statement: Launched portable charger on e-commerce; recorded highest ever e-commerce sales in Sep-Oct
items.quote: We have recently launched portable charger here. And here also in September, October because of the festive seasons, we recorded highest ever sales on e-commerce channels for us.

items.statement: AC charger volume highest ever at >20,000 units in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We achieved the highest ever sales of AC charger by volume. More than 20,000 chargers were supplied in this quarter and also recorded the highest revenue for home chargers.

items.statement: Tritium selected as primary vendor for largest DC fast charging fleet rollout globally; deployment starts H2 CY26
items.quote: Tritium is pioneering another product, which is a DC fed charger. This is the second last point under the commercial traction section and has been selected as the primary vendor for the largest DC fast charging rollout in the fleet sector for deployment in second half of calendar year '26.

items.statement: Tritium Tri-Flex advanced pipeline with global CPOs across US, Canada, UK, EU; orders expected over next 3 months
items.quote: And there are many RFPs which are in very advanced stage with global charge point operators across U.S., Canada, U.K. and EU, and we expect this pipeline to be converted into orders over the next 3 months.

items.statement: PM e-Bus Sewa scheme driving e-bus adoption; majority of buses tendered in Q2, awards expected in 1 month
items.quote: The only difference is majority of the buses were tendered in this quarter. And hopefully, they should be awarded in the next 1 month, which will bring in a lot of -- at least it will bring in a large addressable market for bus depot chargers over the next calendar year.

items.statement: Repaid INR55 crores unsecured debt and converted INR106.9 crores promoter debt to equity via rights issue
items.value: INR55 crores repaid, INR106.9 crores converted
items.quote: The good part is through that, we had repaid the debt of INR55 crores, which is an unsecured debt. We have also converted a debt from promoters of INR106.9 crores into equity.

items.statement: Projects 20-25% revenue growth YoY for FY26 and EBITDA margin of 7-8% for the full year
items.quote: We believe we're currently in a strong phase, with year-over-year growth tracking in the range of 20% to 25%. On the profitability front, we're targeting an EBITDA margin between 7% and 8%.

items.statement: Q2 saw 30% volume decline due to gold price surge; October rebounded with 30-40% YoY growth and strong wedding season demand expected through March
items.quote: And in the second quarter is almost around 30% volume decline in the second quarter. Because the gold price suddenly rose in the second quarter. So, it was a bit slow. But if we talk about the next two quarters, we are confident that the degrowth in the last two quarters will compensate for it.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin improved to 7.83% from 3.79% YoY driven by making charges, studded mix, silver prices and inventory gains; normalized gross margin 8-9%
items.quote: EBITDA came in at ₹75.80 crore, a sharp 99% YoY increase, with margins improving to 7.83% ver sus 3.79% last year, though lower than Q1 due to seasonal marketing spending

items.statement: H1FY26 sales flat at ₹1,507.99 crore; new stores Ajmer and Neemuch added ₹30.33 crore and ₹76.97 crore respectively
items.quote: For H1FY26, total sales stood at ₹1,507.99 crore, broadly flat year-on-year. Ratlam, including both stores, contributed ₹394.08 crore, down 19% due to price-led softness and a strong base effect.

items.statement: QIP process underway to fund store expansion; 1-2 stores expected this fiscal year, 8-10 stores over next 2-3 years; FOCO pilot location closed, launch expected this fiscal year
items.quote: To support this next phase of strategic expansion, our QIP process is underway and expected to conclude soon. Updates will be shared through official channels, and the proceeds will be utilized for store expansion and to enhance products offerings across our stores.

items.statement: Footfall for April-September was 1,06,852 with 79% conversion rate; Ratlam 87%, Neemuch 84%, Ajmer 70%; all new stores follow COCO model
items.quote: Footfall for April –September was 1,06,852 with an overall conversion rate of 79%. Ratlam maintained a strong 87%, while Neemuch and Ajmer achieved 84% and 70%, indicating healthy traction.

items.statement: Average ticket price ₹125-130; consumers shifting to lower carats (18K, 14K) due to high gold prices; 22K remains major category
items.quote: So, the average ticket price is somewhere between INR125 to INR130. And because of the gold price hike, the average ticket size has increased. And definitely, people are starting to take interest in lower carats as well.

items.statement: Gold 91% of revenue; silver grew 103% YoY; diamonds declined 3% YoY; launched Amora brand for 18K segment
items.quote: Segment-wise, gold contributed 91% of revenue, silver grew 103% YoY, and diamonds declined slightly by 3%, indicating continued diversification in product mix.

items.statement: Gold price volatility causing volume declines; consumer budget constraints delaying purchases; potential inventory losses if gold drops >25-30% from peak
items.quote: Gold prices remained elevated, which impacted overall revenue growth on a year -on- year basis. This price surge has led to consumer budget constraints, with m any customers choosing to delay purchases in anticipation of a price correction or

items.statement: E-commerce platform in trial phase, expected to go live before end of FY26 (likely before Q4); omnichannel strategy for pan-India expansion
items.quote: Yes, we are currently in the process of launching our e-commerce platform. It's in the trial phase, and we expect to go live before the end of this financial year likely before the last quarter begins.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 40-45% over FY25 base with operating EBITDA margin of 16-18% for FY26
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving revenue growth of 40% to 45% over the fiscal 25 base, with an operating EBITDA margin in the range of 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 1,308 crore as of September 30, 2025 with Rs 170 crore new order from thermal power player
items.quote: the company continues to maintain a healthy order book of 1,308 crores as of September 30 th, 2025, supported by robust traction across power, oil and gas and process industries. During the quarter, we also secured 170 crore s of new order from leading thermal power player

items.statement: Expected order inflow of Rs 500 crore from power and Rs 100 crore from oil & gas in next 5 months of FY26
items.quote: we are expecting around 500 C r from power sector in this coming 5 months' time till March. And then subsequently we are expecting around 650-700 crores order again in FY26-27 from power sector. And as far as oil and gas is concerned, we are expecting around 100 Cr in next 5 months' time

items.statement: Target order book of Rs 1,100-1,250 crore by April 1, 2026 and Rs 1,600 crore by April 2027
items.quote: 1100-1250 Cr order book will be there on 1 st April, 2026. So, we are purely secured from the execution point. At least 9 months, (three quarters) are fully secured. And again, as I said that we have a good pipeline available for 2026- 2027. Our expectation to book order to the tune of around 1,800 crores further

items.statement: Anjar facility capacity doubled to 30,000 metric tons per annum with 15,000 MT commissioned in September 2025
items.quote: The company successfully commissioned the balanced 15,000 metric tons of process piping solutions capacity at our Anjar facility in September, 2025. This brings the total instal led capacity at Anjar to 30,000 metric tons per annum, effectively doubling our production capabilities in a short period

items.statement: 7,000 MT seamless pipeline expected to commence commercial production by January 2026
items.quote: Additionally, our 7,000 metric ton seamless pipeline is progressing as planned and is expected to commence commercial production by January , 2026.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 operating EBITDA margin expanded 96 bps YoY to 16.3% on better fixed cost absorption
items.quote: Operating EBITDA increases by 47.9% year -on-year to 441 million, with a margin of 16.3%, expanding 96 basis points over Q2 FY25, underscoring efficiency gains and better fixed cost absorption following the ramp-up at Anjar.

items.statement: H1 FY26 operating EBITDA margin improved 179 bps YoY to 16.2%
items.quote: operating EBITDA increased by 46.4% to 799 million, with margins improving by 179 basis points to 16.2%.

items.statement: True business EBITDA margin potential 18-20%, currently guided 16-18% due to biomass power tariff reduction
items.quote: as far as our true potential of the business in terms of earning EBITDA margin, that lies somewhere between 18 % to 20%. Since there is some downwards trend in power tariffs, therefore there is a slight dip in terms of EBITDA margins. So, this year we shall be keeping a range of 16% to 18% EBITDA margin from the overall revenue of the organization.

items.statement: Shift from carbon steel to stainless steel this year, moving to alloy steel dominance next year
items.quote: This year, we had switched mostly from carbon steel to stainless steel. And in the next year, we are going to shift majorly from carbon steel, stainless steel to alloy steel, stainless steel and then I will say that it will be alloy steel, then carbon steel and then stainless steel , and t hat will be the ratio of the perent ages which will happen in the coming year

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 243 days from 247 days QoQ with receivable days 104 and inventory days 223
items.quote: On the working capital front, the cash conversion cycle stood at 243 days, compared to 247 days in the previous quarter, driven by receivable days of 104 and inventory days of 223

items.statement: Proposed equity fund raise suspended due to strengthened cash inflows and new sanctioned credit limits
items.quote: Accordingly, we have decided to suspend the proposed equity fund raise for the time being. Should the need arise in the future to raise funds for growth, we will seek specific approval from the Board of Directors.

items.statement: Expect stronger internal accruals, gradual deleveraging and improved cash generation with Anjar fully operational and seamless pipeline completion
items.quote: With the A njar facility now fully operational and the seamless pipeline made completion, the company expects stronger internal accruals, gradual deleveraging and improved cash generation in the periods ahead

items.statement: Biomass power tariff revision sub judice in High Court of Haryana and Punjab; Plan B includes biomass pellets plant or hydrogen plant at Malwa
items.quote: even if there is no resolution, even if let us say in a worst scenario they do not revise our tariff of Malwa, we told you last time also that we have already started putting up another plant with very minimal investment, which is called Biomass Pellets Plant

items.statement: Return on net worth 7.7% and return on capital employed 9.4% as of September 2025
items.quote: The company's return ratio continued to strengthen, reflecting improved profitability and asset utilization. Return on net worth stood at 7.7% and return on capital employed improved to 9.4% as of September , 2025.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with BHEL and L&T for power sector capacity sharing; clear visibility for next 3 years
items.quote: We had a very large discussion with one of the customers last week. So, where we are talking of sort of a collaboration sort of a thing that ultimately, we have to share the capacities. People do not have the capacities.

items.statement: Market share remains steady with no upgrade or downgrade; fully booked with clear visibility for next 3 years
items.quote: Our market share remains as it is. There is no change in that, but it's very difficult for me to right now say how much percentage is with us and how much percentage is with the other people. But our position remains steady. There is no downgrade or I will say that there is no upgrade also right now.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues affecting material imports from China; confident government will allow imports for infrastructure development
items.quote: there are certain geopolitical situations which had arrived and there is some difficulty in securing the material from outside India, particularly China. But as far as the future is concerned, we are totally hopeful and confident that whatever material which is not available in India, we would be allowed to get it imported from outside India.

items.statement: Power tariff reduction may cause slight deviation from revenue guidance; biomass tariff dispute sub judice with Plan B ready
items.quote: There may be a slight downturn because of the pullback which will happen in terms of power sector orders. But we are not expecting any other major deviation from that. There may be little deviation, I do not say that 100%, but very little deviation may be there. But whatever deviation will come, it will come primarily from the downtrend of the power tariff which we have declared right in the first

items.statement: Strong pipeline in power sector with BHEL 53 units and L&T 23 units of 660-800MW; oil & gas traction from BPCL refineries
items.quote: BHEL has around 53 units of almost 800 or 660 megawatts and L&T has an order of almost 23 units of these bigger units. So, none of these people have that much capacity. We are preparing a paper and we may circulate it shortly on the opportunities available on this particular sector in detail

items.statement: Minimal investment for biomass pellets plant at Malwa as alternative to power generation; hydrogen plant as second option
items.quote: we have already started putting up another plant with very minimal investment, which is called Biomass Pellets Plant and for which the raw material will be the same. We shall be using the power produced by the same fuel and we shall be selling those biomass pellets in the market

items.statement: Hydrogen purification unit proprietary technology via Molsieve Designs; pilot plant commissioning within 3 months at Malwa
items.quote: we have a proprietary through our subsidiary Molsieve Designs Limited, in which we have a proprietary of manufacturing of hydrogen purification unit, which can purify hydrogen to an extent of 99.9999%

items.statement: Oil & gas order execution timeline 6-18 months with 5-6 months for raw material procurement
items.quote: 6 to 18 months are required because initial 5-6 months are required to procure the raw material itself and then the exhibition will start at the shop floor.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 17.5% for FY26, aiming to cross it closer to 20%; 20% growth target for next two years
items.quote: See, we had given a target of 17.5% growth in revenue for FY '25, FY '26. And then 20% per year after that for the next 2 years, that is the guidance we have given earlier. But I think the better performance that we've had in the first half, I have a feeling that we should cross the 17.5% which we had given for this year, maybe closer to 20%.

items.statement: Targeting INR2,000 crore plus revenue in FY27 with new capacity in place
items.quote: Next year, I think definitely, we are planning another 20% increase as we have predicted, so it should cross INR2,000 crores, and for that capacity, we are ready. So, we now have the capacity in place to achieve INR2,000 crores plus in FY'26, FY'27.

items.statement: Capex of INR150 crore over next 12 months for Gujarat PEB and Andhra heavy structure plants; INR60-70 crore in FY26 and INR60-70 crore in FY27
items.quote: About -- both these plants will cost us about INR150 crores in the next 12 months. So I would say another INR60 crores, INR70 crores in this year, and INR60 crores, INR70 crores in the next financial year.

items.statement: Total installed capacity now 200,000 metric tons after commissioning Phase 2 of Andhra Pradesh unit (fourth fully integrated plant)
items.quote: The commissioning of Phase 2 of our Andhra Pradesh unit marks a significant milestone. This is now our fourth fully integrated pre-engineered steel building plant. An d it takes our total installed capacity to 200,000 metric tons

items.statement: Groundbreaking done for Gujarat PEB plant (operational in ~10 months) and Andhra heavy structure plant (25,000 tons/year) for multistorey and heavy steel structures
items.quote: we have started the new plant in Gujarat for pre-engineered building, which should be up in about 10 months from today, that has already started. We have do ne the ground-breaking last week -- last month. So that is the next PEB plant we are adding. The Andhra new plant is a heavy

items.statement: Order book at INR1,634 crore as of 31 Oct 2025; secured INR463 crore orders between 1 Aug and 31 Oct; 80-85% repeat orders
items.quote: As on the order book, as on 31st October '25, our order book stands at INR1,634 crores, reflecting a strong pipeline for the coming quarters. We secured orders worth INR463 crores between 1st of August and 31st of October.

items.statement: Strong pipeline with large inquiries in semiconductors, EVs, renewables, data centers; order intake expected to step up with new capacity
items.quote: Yes, there are a lot of -- always a lot of projects in the pipeline. There's a lot of growth happening in the country. And like I mentioned, more and more people wa nt to go for steel and for pre- engineered steel for faster execution of their projects

items.statement: Heavy structure vertical margins expected similar to PEB (9-10% EBITDA) initially, potential for improvement as scale builds
items.quote: I would say, sir, that the margin profile in this would be pretty similar to the pre-engineered steel buildings to begin with. And as we establish ourselves as one of the major players, there is always a likelihood of doing a bit better on the margin. But generally speaking, it would still be in the range of about 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Per-ton profitability not improving significantly due to high investment in plants, people, exports; operational leverage to improve margins over time
items.quote: I think the margins, I would say, have not improved on a per ton basis, because for us, also, we are investing a lot of money. And when we invest in plants, we also have to invest in people. Also, we are investing in exports.

items.statement: Inventory increased ~INR85 crore in H1 due to special steel requirements for orders and supplier unreliability; expected to come down
items.quote: I think the stocks have gone up a little bit. There has been a litt le bit of unreliability from the customer side, and some of the orders that we obtained required certain special thicknesses and sizes of steel

items.statement: Key wins: repeat orders from Rungta Mines, Havells India; new customers Techno Electric, Jindal Stainless; 80-85% repeat orders
items.quote: Key customer wins during this period included our repeat customers, Rungta Mines, Havells India, and our new customers, Techno Electric, Jindal Stainless, and many others. We take pride in the fact that 80% to 85% of these are repeat orders from our existing customers.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with JSPL for multistorey/heavy steel buildings (joint marketing, Ahmedabad event); Mold-Tek for export capabilities
items.quote: Our strategic partnership with JSPL to jointly explore opportunities in the multistory and heavy steel building segments, along with our collaboration with Mold-Tek Technologies, to enhance export capabilities and global presence, will further help Interarch scale new heights.

items.statement: INR300-350 crore large order ~62% completed (invoiced); rest to complete in Q3 FY26
items.quote: So, sir, this order is above INR300 crores, so close to the range of about 350. Now, out of that, approximately 62% has already been complete d. The rest will get completed during this quarter

items.statement: Execution depends on customer clearances, not just factory capacity; selective order acceptance to avoid overcommitment
items.quote: We also have to be careful that we pick up those that we can execute. We have the capacity; some require very, very fast execution, which we may not be able to do because we are fully booked up for the next few months.

items.statement: Investing in people, technology (SAP HANA, engineering software, AI for engineering/project management) as long-term R&D; all profits historically ploughed back
items.quote: all our investment into people is like an R&D for us. If I don't invest in people, I don't invest in technology. We are doing the new SAP HANA. We have developed a lot of new software and hardware plug-ins for o ur engineering. We are seriously looking at how we can adopt AI for our engineering and

items.statement: Full-year margin guidance unchanged at 15-20 bps YoY decline, factoring in expected December rate cut and portfolio attrition pressure
items.quote: On a full year basis, we are expecting to be in this guidance range only because of the compression we are seeing driven by attrition pressure across the portfolio especially in the home loan side, also in the construction finance side.

items.statement: Medium-term AUM growth guidance expected to resume in FY27 as attrition pressure eases after rate stabilization
items.quote: As the attrition pressure weans off with our rate stabilization in the market, with one more rate cut in December, you can expect stabilization in the market in three four months. As we continue to focus on growing disbursement, we feel that by next year, then we can come back to our normalized or the medium term guidance growth in AUM.

items.statement: Opex to NTI target of 14-16% remains a 3-4 year aspiration trajectory
items.quote: 14 to 16 was always a three to four year aspiration number, three to four year trajectory. I think that we remain on that.

items.statement: Target leverage of 7-8x expected to be achieved in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: I think two years is the time frame where we should be. It will depend upon the growth numbers, of course, but as we give a medium term growth guidance, I think two years, two and a half years is the time frame where we should look at achieving that sustainability vision.

items.statement: NIM held flat sequentially at 4%, down 10 bps YoY due to lower assignment income
items.quote: Net interest margin is holding at 4% on a sequential basis while at a YOY basis it dropped by 10 bps.

items.statement: Gross spread flat YoY at 1.9%, up 10 bps sequentially due to cost of funds benefit
items.quote: Gross spread was flat for the quarter at 1.9% against 1.9% of Q2 FY '25. However, on a sequential basis, gross spread was 10 bps higher due to higher flow-through benefit on cost of funds versus movement across portfolio rate.

items.statement: Portfolio yield moderated 22 bps sequentially and 60 bps YoY to 9.3%
items.quote: Portfolio yield moderated by 22 bps on sequential basis and 60 bps on a YOY basis at 9.3% in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Cost of funds improved to 7.4%, down 50 bps YoY and 34 bps sequentially
items.quote: Cost of funds improved during the quarter and stood at 7.4% having 50 bps reduction on YOY basis against 7.9% in Q2 FY '25. On sequential basis, cost of funds saw a reduction of 34 bps on account of policy rate transmission on existing borrowing as well as incremental borrowing at lower rate.

items.statement: Further 10 bps cost of funds benefit expected in Q4 from December rate cut
items.quote: Now we may have around 10 basis points of further benefit which we may see through the balance part of the year considering the rate cut.

items.statement: Home loans 55%, LAP 10%, LRD 21%+, DF sub-12% of AUM; LRD up 1.1% sequentially
items.quote: Portfolio composition also continued to remain well diversified with home loans at 55 %, LAP at 10% and LRD in excess of 21% and DF at sub 12%.

items.statement: Non-prime (including affordable) yields 1.25-1.5% higher than prime home loans
items.quote: On an aggregate level, the yield, if I collect the entire non-prime business including affordable, yield will be a differential of close to 1.25 to 1.5% from the pure prime business.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 32% YoY to INR 15,914 crore
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter grew by 32% from INR12,000 crores in Q2 FY '25 to close to INR16,000 crores, i.e. INR15,914 crores in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Near-prime/affordable SBU acquiring ~INR 250 crore/month, operating in top 36 markets
items.quote: Currently we are now acquiring close to INR250 odd crores per month business in this line and expecting to rapidly scale further.

items.statement: GNPA improved 4 bps to 0.26%, NNPA improved 1 bp to 0.12%; provision coverage ~56%
items.quote: Asset quality remained healthy with improvement in GNPA at 0.26% and NNPA at 0.12% and annualized credit cost at 18 bps.

items.statement: Annualized credit cost 18 bps vs 2 bps YoY (14 bps normalized excluding prior year overlay release)
items.quote: Annualized credit costs stood at 18 bps in Q2 FY '26 against 2 bps in Q2 FY '25. The normalized credit costs because in Q2 FY '25, in fact in H1 FY '25 we had overlay release which we had created during COVID period. If we would exclude the overlay release in Q2 FY '25 the annualized credit costs would have been 14 bps.

items.statement: Stage 1 assets 99.39%, Stage 2 flat at 0.34%, GNPA 0.26%, NNPA 0.12%
items.quote: On sequential basis stage 1 assets have improved by 3 bps to 99.39% in Q2 FY '26. Stage 2 were flat at 34 bps. GNPA improved by 4 bps to 26 bps and NPA by 1 bps to 12 bps.

items.statement: Minimum public shareholding (25%) deadline extended to September 2029; parent Bajaj Finance to dilute via primary capital raise
items.quote: The guidelines have already come. It's not a consultancy paper in any case. So, we have time till September '29 now to get it. It's not gazetted yet, but the guidelines have come. So, it will get gazetted. The guidelines have come. So, we'll have time till September '29 for the parent to dilute.

items.statement: Network expanded to 220 branches across 176 locations
items.quote: Geographical coverage of BHFL now spans across 176 locations with network of 220 branches.

items.statement: Home loan BT-in rate ~15% of acquisitions, in line with industry 16-17%
items.quote: At an overall home loan acquisition for the company, our BT in is 15% approximately of our overall HL acquisition, which is perfectly in line with the industry. Industry is 16-17% is the BT in, ours is 15%.

items.statement: Home loan BT-out rate estimated at 14-15% (from 21-22% attrition, 20-30% voluntary prepayment)
items.quote: At a 20% annualized attrition I can look at maybe 14%-15% as a BT out rate, from our book. But both BT in and BT out are different metrics. So, percentage wise, it may look at 15%, I request you not to assume both are the same.

items.statement: PSU bank competition in home loans is now a permanent feature, not cyclical; strategy focuses on micro-market deepening and product nuance, not higher payouts
items.quote: in home loan also had been far higher than the industry disbursal growth. We are here to compete. We keep on modifying our strategy. We called out in last quarter saying that deepening the presence and increasing the width of our customer segmentation, deepening our presence in each micro market and the market, is the strategy we follow which is the strategy we will continue to follow to continue

items.statement: Assignment income lower by design: treasury assignment paused due to comfortable ALM; non-HL assignment only for PBC management
items.quote: We took a conscious decision in the current year to not do assignment for treasury strategy because as a treasury as a means of fund, otherwise we had been normally falling 12%-13% of our assets assigned out to our strategy, even as a treasury strategy for our ALM match. But if you look at our ALM, we went long last year. So, our ALM again, even if it is a five year bucket plus, it is quite comfor

items.statement: Annualized ROA 2.3%, ROE 12.2% (down from 13.3% due to capital raise, no overlay release, lower derecognition income)
items.quote: Annualized ROE for the quarter came in at 12.2%. Capital position with CAR at 26.12% remained healthy and PBC criteria which is a regulatory criteria was at 61.21%, against a regulatory threshold of 60

items.statement: Full-year guidance maintained at over 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Based on the strong momentum that we have seen over the last three quarters, we remain committed to delivering a strong full-year performance in line with the guidance, which was over 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth that we had indicated at the beginning of this year.

items.statement: Confident of meeting or slightly exceeding full-year guidance
items.quote: We are confident of meeting it, or probably surpassing it by a few percentage points.

items.statement: Strong volume growth across all segments in Q3 and 9M CY25
items.quote: The Company has delivered a strong volume growth of 26% over the previous year.

items.statement: 9M volume growth of 25% with robust performance across segments
items.quote: We delivered 9.6 million reports, compared to 7.7 million reports for the nine months of 2024, which marking a robust year-on-year growth of 25%.

items.statement: PAT margins expected to stabilize between 40-45%
items.quote: I think we have been delivering consistently between 40-45%. I do not think there’s going to be any significant change there. It has been more or less stable

items.statement: ASP decline driven by smaller carat sizes in natural diamond jewelry, not pricing pressure
items.quote: What we have seen during the quarter is a very high incidence of smaller carat size natural diamond and lab-grown jewelry coming in for certification. So, that is the reason why you see that despite a 29% increase in natural diamond and lab-grown diamond, you are seeing a slight decline in ASP, again, driven purely by a change in the carat size that we are currently receiving.

items.statement: Jewelry pieces now carry smaller average diamond sizes but higher quantities
items.quote: Earlier, the jewelry piece used to carry say one and a half-carat diamonds. Now this average jewelry piece is carrying about a carat plus. You understand? So, the size of the jewelry piece where diamonds are concerned has somewhat been decreased, but the quantities have increased.

items.statement: Pricing stable over last 3-4 quarters, no significant change in Q3
items.quote: We have seen a lot of stability in pricing over the last three, four quarters. So, this is more in terms of segment mix and driven by within the segment, the product size mix.

items.statement: India ASP increased 2% YoY in Q3
items.quote: But as you rightly mentioned, the India ASP for the quarter has seen a 2% increase over the same time last year. So, pretty strong performance of India is what is carrying through the group for us at the moment.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across all channels including independent retailers in tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: We supply, we cater to the entire supply chain in the gem and jewelry industry right from the manufacturer, to the wholesaler, to the trader, to the manufacturing of the jeweler, to the jewelers, to the retail shops, online, offline. So, we are holistically available for all the stakeholders in the gem and jewelry sector.

items.statement: Growth coming from deeper penetration in tier 2/3 cities and LGD jewelry space
items.quote: So, what we see changes, I mean, going into the third and second and the Third-Tier cities, so we are gaining grounds there. We are going inroads into India. And also, I mean, the LGD jewelry space is also rapidly increasing even in India.

items.statement: US contributes ~12% of revenue, Netherlands ~12-12.5%, India ~75%
items.quote: The US business will contribute close to 12% of our revenues and Netherlands another 12-12.5% of our business.

items.statement: Tariff impact on certification business insignificant; domestic market unaffected
items.quote: Tariff has virtually no significant or no impact at all on the domestic sector. So, from that way, the domestic sector has really ramped up and especially during the Diwali season, we have done exceptionally as well.

items.statement: D&A increased to INR 11 cr due to capacity expansion and fixed asset additions
items.quote: I think D&A expense has become some INR 11 crores. I think, obviously, that is because we are expanding our operations as well. There has been some fixed assets that have got added in.

items.statement: Added lab in Dubai this year; continue scouting for expansion in fast-growing markets
items.quote: We have two labs in China. We have a couple of labs in Dubai. We expanded with an additional lab in Dubai this year. So, we continue to scout the market and as and when we see that there are opportunities, nothing will prevent us from expanding in existing geographies as well.

items.statement: Well positioned to ramp up capacity in Dubai, Hong Kong, Turkey if supply chains shift due to tariffs
items.quote: It is possible that in case there is any shift from a supply chain standpoint, I think we are well positioned to leverage that in terms of ramping up capacity in some of the other locations, be it Dubai or Hong Kong or Turkey, etc.

items.statement: Strong cash position (~INR 400 cr); dividends and acquisitions under evaluation
items.quote: At the moment, I think the company is sitting on a very strong cash position. And as we have articulated in the past, some of this will get paid as dividends. But obviously, we are also keeping our eyes open in terms of opportunities for acquisitions, etc.

items.statement: Making significant leadership investments in US to scale up business faster
items.quote: Of course, we also want to have the US business to scale up at a much faster rate, and we are making significant leadership investments and interventions there in the US.

items.statement: Women's World Cup sponsorship split across two quarters; not material to margins
items.quote: It has been split between the two quarters actually. So, it is not significant. I do not think it is going to move the needle as far as

items.statement: Management expects 20-25% revenue growth for FY26 and targets similar year-on-year growth going forward.
items.quote: 20% -- 20% to 25% growth possibility. This year we are going to touch this.

items.statement: Export share for FY26 guided at 12-13% of revenue.
items.quote: This year we are going to maybe, yes, 12% to 13%, yes, possibility is there.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR750-800 crores as of the call date.
items.quote: Today we are not disclosing our order book. But today we have almost INR750 crores toINR800 crores order book

items.statement: Order book split approximately 30% glass lining, 30% metal division, 40% plant and engineering.
items.quote: That is a 30 -- glass is the same. 30% is glass lining and another 30% is the metal division and 40% maybe approximately, I don't know exact figures, 40% maybe plant and engineering.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined in H1 due to export shipment deferrals; expected to sustain and slightly increase in H2 as exports resume.
items.quote: Definitely it will sustain. Growth also very good. Definitely it will sustain. Export also going to happen in H2. So margins going to, slightly going to increase.

items.statement: New 36-acre greenfield facility (6 lakh sq ft) with 100-ton crane and 100mm fabrication capability; capex INR120-150 crores; operational in 14-18 months.
items.quote: New facility in 36 acres. That is, we are building at a time 6,000,000 square feet. Very big facility. And crane capacity also 60 tons to 100 tons capacity. And fabrication capabilities also 60 mm to 100 mm, we are increasing.

items.statement: Dedicated shell & tube heat exchanger unit (Unit 2) capex INR10-15 crores; existing furnaces to be shifted; production starts April next year.
items.quote: In Unit 2, we are doing capex another maybe -- some we are -- some Japanese companies are investing in Japan only. We are not taking that. In India, we are going to invest another INR 10 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: New heat exchanger facility targeting 300 units/month initially; Japan partner also expanding capacity.
items.quote: first initial phase, we are building the -- our facility, per month 300 heat exchangers capacity and based on market acceptance we will increase capacity.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 35% glass lining, rest metal equipment; plant & engineering services growing as company shifts to complete solutions.
items.quote: Sir, segment wise, the glass lining is part is our revenue, 35% glass lining, rest of metal equipment.

items.statement: Company manufactures 91 product varieties; offers design-to-commissioning solutions; unique shell & tube glass-lined heat exchangers with GL Hakko.
items.quote: Today, we are almost 91 variety of products we are manufacturing, and we are supplying and commissioning also. We are not only supplier, we are complete solution provider.

items.statement: Acquiring 51% of C2C Engineering for INR12.25 crores; adds 130 employees and process design, civil, HVAC, electrical & instrumentation capabilities.
items.quote: Total we are acquiring 51% and we are paying INR12.25 crores.

items.statement: Scigenics acquisition (bioprocess/fermentation) completed; strengthens biotechnology presence.
items.quote: we have acquired the biotechnology area, Scigenics. Scigenics is a 40-year-old company. Bioprocess and ferment er they are manufacturing

items.statement: Major export geographies: USA, Europe (Greece), Russia.
items.quote: Geography, exports, majority is in the US. and Greece. Prateek Bhandari: USA. Nageswara Rao Kandula: Europe and US majority. And the third one is Russia

items.statement: Pharma demand intact from large clients; small/medium pharma clients facing cash flow issues and low capex.
items.quote: Pharma, yes, big -- I can say big clients' demand is intact, but still small customers are facing challenges.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand picking up; two large agrochemical clients added recently with big orders.
items.quote: Chemicals, yes, chemicals also improving, sir. Now, recently we added two big clients. Earlier, they were not with Standard Glass, but they now turned up into, we got very big orders from two agrochemicals clients.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~45% of revenue; top 5 are INR2,000+ crore revenue pharma companies doing sustained capex.
items.quote: Top 10 is, I think, 45%.

items.statement: Shell & tube glass-lined heat exchangers priced at 2x graphite exchangers (INR200 vs INR100); life 15 years vs 2-3 years; particle-free.
items.quote: Graphite heat exchanger are suppose INR100, this is INR200 rupees. Vineet: Okay. Nageswara Rao Kandula: graphite heat exchanger life is two years, this heat exchanger life is 15 years. And also graphite heat exchanger –releases particles and this is complete particle

items.statement: Heat exchanger market potential estimated at INR2,000 crores based on 600-700 reactors/month industry-wide, each needing two exchangers.
items.quote: INR2,000 crores means, sir, we are now, glass lining business is almost on INR400 crores Indian market. Every month, including all manufacturers, 600, 700 reactors are producing. And each reactor requires two heat exchangers.

items.statement: Proposed name change to Standard Engineering Technology Limited to reflect multidisciplinary precision engineering identity.
items.quote: we are pleased to announce our intention to seek shareholders' approval to change our name from Standard Glass Lining Technolog y L imited to Standard Engineering Technology Limited, a name that truly captures the full breadth of our engineering strength

items.statement: H1 FY26 results: Total income INR366 crores, EBITDA INR69 crores, PAT INR42 crores despite export deferrals.
items.quote: Even with the deferred export worth INR40 crores to INR45 crores shifting to later quarters, we achieved total income of INR366 crores, EBITDA of INR69 crores and PAT of INR42 crores in the first half of 2026.

items.statement: Expects to maintain current EBITDA margin rate going forward
items.quote: More or less the rate at which we are progressing now. Overall, if you see our first half results it has been, to a fair extent, modulated with regards to the overall performance of the company. So we expect to maintain this rate.

items.statement: Festive season in October saw double-digit sales growth across PV, 2W, 3W and CV segments
items.quote: During the festive season continuing in October, the passenger vehicles, 2- wheelers, 3 -wheelers and commercial vehicle segments all recorded double-digit sales growth, rekindling the hopes for good volumes for the third quarter onwards.

items.statement: Q2 margin moderation due to GST announcement mix impact; expects to maintain current margin rate
items.quote: See, what happened in Q2 is because of the announcement happening on 15th of August almost till the last week of September, we had an impact on our sales with almost everybody saying that let's wait for the GST announcement. And the final GST started only on the 22nd of September. As a result, there was a very big mix impact, which result ed in this small impact that you see.

items.statement: Capex for normal business equal to depreciation; extra cash used for M&A and non-linear growth
items.quote: Equal to the depreciation of the individual companies unless if we have new big businesses where we have to really invest. And in which case, that is something that I will announce at that time.

items.statement: Coimbatore EV motor and controller plant commissioning completed; commercial production expected in ongoing quarter
items.quote: The progress of commissioning of our new facility at Coimbatore for the EV motor and controller plant has been completed, and we expect to start commercial production du ring the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion at SEL Pithampur completed; Phase 3 expansion started due to excess customer demand
items.quote: Further, Phase 2 expansion of our new manufacturing facility at SEL Pithampur, Indore has also been completed, and we have already started with the Phase III expansion due to the continuing excess demand from the customers.

items.statement: Won new businesses across legacy and all subsidiaries; last two quarters saw many new wins in plastics, legacy and EV business
items.quote: I'm very happy to state that the last 2 quarters have been a lot of new wins that we have got in our plastic s business, our legacy business as well as our EV business.

items.statement: Developing components for alternative fuels: CNG, LNG, PNG, Hybrid, Flex, Hydrogen, H-CNG and electric powertrains
items.quote: As a part of our commitment to innovation, we are actively developing components for alternative fuel solutions like CNG, LNG, PNG, Hybrid, Flex, Hydrogen, H-CNG and electric powertrains.

items.statement: EV motor range from 250 watts to 350 kW; making hub motors, mid-drive motors and controllers; PM E-Drive certified
items.quote: We are manufacturing mot ors right from 250 watts right up to 350 kilowatts. And we are making our own controllers. We are probably the only player in the country who manufactures the motors and the controllers together and size it and give it to the customers.

items.statement: Mitigated rare earth magnet non-availability via alternate sourcing; developing ferrite-based solutions for PMSM motors
items.quote: We have also been able to mitigate the nonavailability Shriram Pistons & of rare earth magnets by alternate sourcing methodologies and maintaining our production run and also working on var ious newer technologies, which will give us a substitution to the rare earth magnets

items.statement: Advanced stage on rare earth-free ferrite motors; already introducing in some products; multiple trials and PME-Drive validations ongoing
items.quote: We are in advanced stages. That's all I can say. It's all time tested, and that's what in some of the products, we have already started introducing that also, and that's really helped us during this time.

items.statement: Supplying to Jaguar, Caterpillar and other global OEMs from drawing board stage; added new customers in snowmobile, marine, off-highway
items.quote: Most of the OEMs we supply to Jaguar, we supply to Caterpillar. We supply to so many big names. And I can tell you that we work with those customers on the drawing board.

items.statement: Made good inroads with Japanese and Korean OEMs expanding in India; working on new platforms from drawing board stage
items.quote: And both our Korean customers, our Japanese customers as well as some of our other non-Japanese customers, I think we have actually made very good inroads with our presence as well as working on various newer platforms that we have been working with them right from drawing board stage.

items.statement: Exports resilient across 45+ countries; off-road segment strong in US, UK, Europe; on-road passenger cars slow in those regions
items.quote: Yes. So basically, in the export market, the off-road segment has really done well, both in U.S. as well as in U.K. and Europe. And we are supplying to those segments. We have been able to really get some new businesses also tied up.

items.statement: Export range INR 480-520 cr last 2-3 years; growth challenging due to geopolitical issues, war, forex shortages in many countries
items.quote: But on a very macro basis, last 2 to 3 y ears, our exports has largely been in that INR480 crores to INR520 crores kind of a range.

items.statement: Pursuing bigger M&A opportunities for non-linear growth; focus on ICE-agnostic segments; ongoing and value-accretive
items.quote: And all the e xtra cash that we have is being used for M&A opportunities and for nonlinear growth and I will put it more this way that we are looking at bigger M&A opportunities. And it's already ongoing, and I can only say that various opportunities are there, and we a re working on them.

items.statement: Future M&A to remain in automotive core strength; already supply to railways and defence with existing products
items.quote: Instead, I would prefer to be in the automotive area where our core strength lies, but still make the products which the industrial segment wants if we can make within those segments of business.

items.statement: Expects ICE market CAGR of 6-7% over next 5 years; EV penetration 15-20%; legacy products to grow ~10% annually
items.quote: We expect a CAGR growth of around 6% - 7%. And we expect a penetration of around 15% - 20% as far as EV is concerned. Now if you see the next 5 years, if we are going to grow at around 6%, we are looking at a growth of almost 30% in the end markets and a penetration of 20%, which means even the existing legacy products are going to grow at almost 10% in the next 4 or 5 years.

items.statement: Hybrid pistons require Euro 6/7 features: low friction, hard anodizing, special rings, coatings; realizations improve accordingly
items.quote: So it requires different kind of features. It requires different kind of hard anodizing , requires different kind of rings, it requires different kinds of coating. So it requires a complete different technologies to develop that. And all that are featured products and accordingly, there is an improvement in prices.

items.statement: Global piston supply vacuum as competitors vacate capacity due to EV fears; receiving many global inquiries
items.quote: globally, in the Piston world, there is a huge demand cropping up primarily because of people vacating capacities. Now what happens is when people vacate capacities because of the fear of EV, not really understanding the market well, not really understanding the situation well, then it tends to really create a lot of vacuum with r egards to the supply situation

items.statement: GST reforms effective 22 Sept 2025; auto industry early beneficiary; demand showing improvement post GST 2.0
items.quote: The auto industry has emerged as one of the biggest early beneficiaries under the reforms, reflected by improved demand for all our products from the OEMs. Hence, post GST reduction and what we call it as GST 2.0, the demand is showing signs of improvement.

items.statement: Invested over INR 550 cr in legacy business over last 5 years including SEL for engine valves; huge automation and digitization
items.quote: Frankly, over the last 5 years, including our investments in SEL, which is primarily for our engine valves and other product s that we make, I think we have invested over INR 550 crores here.

items.statement: Subsidiary margins accretive to consolidated EBITDA; all segments maintain EBITDA targets
items.quote: No, all the segment of the subsidiaries that we have been operating on has been a very accretive business for us. We do not want any of our businesses to bring down our overall EBITDA targets. So we have maintained our EBITDA margins across all segments of our business.

items.statement: No practical China dependency risk on rare earth magnets; sales increased even when China stopped magnet supply
items.quote: Practically nothing. Even though we had the magnets being stopped by China, our sales actually increased, not decreased.

items.statement: Won Golden Peacock Award for Corporate Governance 2025; Ecovadis bronze rating (top 35% globally); D&B ESG rating 2 (top 500 value creators)
items.quote: We are happy to state that we have won again the Golden Peacock Award from the Institute of Directors in London for Excellence in Corporate Governance in 2025. We have also received a br onze rating from Ecovadis, putting us into the top 35 percentile globally on sustainability and the ESG rating 2 from Dun & Bradstreet with us being placed in the top 500 value creators globally.

items.statement: India-UK FTA showing green shoots for business
items.quote: Yes, yes, there are green shoots for that.

items.statement: Aspire to continue growing revenue at 30%+ in near-term
items.quote: We aspire to continue growing at 30% -plus in the near-term.

items.statement: Expect GCC revenue to double in next couple of years
items.quote: We expect our GCC revenue to double in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expect ROCE to double in next two years
items.quote: We expect this to double in the next two years, and we continue to see more headroom for ROCE growth beyond that as well.

items.statement: Expect retention to continue upwards of 80-85% in foreseeable future
items.quote: We expect the retention in foreseeable future to continue upwards of 80 -85%, and at the same time, we will continue having some healthy voluntary churn as well in this.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue growth to accelerate with 1M sq.ft new operational supply and 1.4M sq.ft maturing
items.value: 1 million sq.ft new operational supply and 1.4 million sq.ft maturing
items.quote: So, just to give a perspective, we will have 1 million sq.ft. of new operational supply and additionally 1.4 million sq.ft. of our current capacity will mature in H2 '26.

items.statement: Ancillary revenue growth set to double with VAS growing rapidly
items.quote: Our ancillary revenue growth is also set to double, with VAS growing very rapidly and VAS continuing to grow.

items.statement: GCCs contribute >15% of rental revenue, share expected to grow meaningfully
items.quote: GCCs now contribute to more than 15% of our rental revenue, and this share is expected to continue to grow up meaningfully in the future.

items.statement: 1,000-plus-seat cohort tripled to 35% of rental revenue from 12% three years ago
items.quote: In fact, our 1,000 -plus-seat cohort, which three years ago was at 12%, today, has tripled to 35% of our rental revenue.

items.statement: Pre-fill from existing clients drives faster ramp-up; 30%+ rentals from multi-city clients
items.quote: Rentals from multi-city clients continue to be over 30%, which means that if Smartworks adds 3 million square foot of space every year, 1 million is being pre-filled from our existing client base.

items.statement: Industry flex absorption 15-18M sq.ft/year; H1 FY26 saw ~48M sq.ft total office absorption
items.quote: So it continues to be a major driver of overall growth of office market, which has been going very steadily. So, you can expect very easily upwards of between 15 to 18 million square foot of new flex space absorption every year.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin 16.4% in Q2 FY26, up from 13.4% YoY
items.quote: Our normalized EBITDA was approximately about Rs.70 crores, up from 13% from last quarter, and 46% year-on-year, with an overall normalized EBITDA margin of 16.4%.

items.statement: Center-level EBITDA margins 23-24% blended, mature centers higher
items.quote: If you look at our corporate cost, our corporate cost is around 8%. So from a center level EBITDA margin perspective, you can actually add both of them and it will come to approximately 23% to 24%-odd.

items.statement: Corporate costs declined from 13.8% of revenue in 2022 to 7.9% in H1 FY26
items.quote: In fact, our corporate costs as a revenue from operations has declined from 13.8% in 2022 to 7.9% in H1 of 2026.

items.statement: Committed rental revenue exceeds INR 4,400 crores
items.quote: Our committed rental revenue stands in excess of INR4,400 crores as we speak.

items.statement: Signed-up portfolio up to 14M sq.ft; 100% visibility for FY26 and FY27 supply
items.quote: Today, we have a signed -up portfolio of up to 14 million sq.ft. and have visibility of 100% of FY26 and FY27 supply, with FY28 sourcing already underway.

items.statement: Eastbridge property CAPEX ~Rs.110 crores phased with occupancy
items.quote: It will require a CAPEX of close to about Rs.110 crores when the entire building gets occupied , and obviously, the entire CAPEX is not going to be upfront, it is going to be in phases as and when the occupancy increases.

items.statement: H1 FY26 CAPEX deployment ~Rs.186 crores for 9.1M sq.ft footprint
items.quote: If I look at your cash flow, I think it is around Rs.186 crores of CAPEX that we have done in the first half.

items.statement: Total footprint 12.7M sq.ft, 9.1M sq.ft operational across 49 centers
items.quote: Today, our total footprint stands at 12.7 million square feet, with 9.1 million square feet operational across 49(1) centers, the largest managed office portfolio in India.

items.statement: Mature portfolio 7.5M sq.ft at 88% occupancy, committed occupancy >93%
items.quote: Our mature portfolio today stands at 7.5 million square feet, operating at 88% occupancy, with committed occupancy above 93%, providing strong visibility.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR 2,294 crores, normalized EBITDA up 46% to INR 347 crores, PAT up 61% to INR 244 crores in Q2 FY26

items.quote: For the second quarter of FY '26, our consolidated revenue grew by 31% year-on-year, increasing from INR 1,750 crores to INR 2,294 crores. The normalized EBITDA improved by 46%, rising from INR 237 crores to INR 347 crores, and profit after tax increased by 61% from INR 152 crores to INR 244 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 4,013 crores (20% YoY), normalized EBITDA INR 602 crores (24% YoY), PAT INR 419 crores (35% YoY)
items.value: Revenue INR 4,013 cr, EBITDA INR 602 cr, PAT INR 419 cr
items.quote: For the first half of the financial year, revenue from operations stood at INR 4,013 crores, achieving a growth of 20% year-on-year. H1 FY '26 normalized EBITDA stood at INR 602 crores, a robust increase of 24% year-on-year. Profit after tax increased by 35% in H1, INR 419 crores versus INR 310 crores in H1 of FY '25.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth guidance revised to 22-23% from earlier 24-25%
items.quote: So we now would circle up our guidance to 22- 23% growth for full year versus 24-25% that we had pencilled in January'25, when we talked about.

items.statement: FY26 cost of funds expected between 7.5% to 7.55%
items.quote: For FY '26, we expect cost of funds to be in the region of overall full year to be between 7.5% to 7.55%.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost expected at upper end of 1.85% to 1.95% range
items.quote: We expect full year credit cost to be at the upper end of guided range of 1.85% to 1.95% now.

items.statement: FY26 new customer additions expected at 16-17 million
items.quote: We now expect to add 16 to 17 million new customers in FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 fee and other income growth guided at 13-15%
items.quote: All put together, we will see 13% to 15% growth in the current year.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost expected to improve significantly from FY26 levels
items.quote: The number should be much lower as we get into FY'27.

items.statement: AUM grew 24% YoY to INR 462,261 crores in Q2 FY26

items.statement: New business lines contributed 3% of overall AUM growth in Q2
items.quote: New lines of businesses, namely gold loans, new car loans, CV, tractor are growing in a healthy manner and contributed to 3% of overall AUM growth in Q2.

items.statement: MSME growth moderated to 18% YoY; FY26 growth expected at 10-12%
items.quote: We now expect MSME business to grow in the current full fiscal by 10-12% only.

items.statement: Gold loan book at INR 12,000 crores; target INR 16,000 crores by March 2026 and INR 27,000-30,000 crores by March 2027

I -- and we are significantly -- we've just signed up a significant expansion in the business. It should be between INR 27,000 crores to INR 30,000 crores business by March '27.

items.statement: Customer franchise crossed 110 million at 110.64 million; added 4.13 million in Q2

items.statement: Mobility business grew 11.9% YoY in Q2 FY26 driven by power solutions growth of 9.5% from higher diesel component demand

items.quote: Two-wheeler business grew by 81.8%, mainly on account of high sale of exhaust gas sensors, resulting from implementation of OBD-2 norms starting 1st of April 2025.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to INR 47,948 million in Q2 FY26 driven by power solutions and two-wheeler power sports
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, revenue from operations in July to September 2025 stood at 47,948 million INR, which grew by 9.1% over July to September 2024.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 10.1% YoY to INR 6,171 million in Q2 FY26 with margin improvement from favorable product mix and expense optimization
items.quote: EBITDA for July-September 2025 was 6,171 million INR, which grew by 10.1% over the same quarter of previous year. This improvement in EBITDA margin was primarily driven on account of favorable product mix and optimization of expenses.

items.statement: Material cost progress from favorable product mix and localization strategy
items.quote: We have improved in the material cost. So, one reason is we had a favo rable product mix and we could also the share of manufacturing goods was quite good in this quarter. That means our strategy of further localization is now coming

items.statement: Consumer goods growth impacted by adverse exchange rates increasing material cost and initial GST reform slowdown
items.quote: We see a reduction mainly on account of adverse exchange rate moments resulting in slightly higher material cost. We also see again a little bit of initial slowdown on account of GST reforms and then now after that ramp up again.

items.statement: TREM V regulation on horizon; electrification growth expected from clean mobility requirements
items.quote: TREM V is something which is on the horizon for quite a while. So let's hope that, that comes through. I think in terms of other push, it could be electrification. Growth in electrification is anyway on the cards, not necessarily regulation related, but due to clean mobility kind of a requirement.

items.statement: Growth levers shifting from legislation-led to feature, comfort, safety, electrification, clean fuels, hybrid, hydrogen, flex fuels
items.quote: In the auto, we've largely been led so far by growth in, I mean, growth due to legislations. I think we're moving from that phase into growth based on features and comfort and many other factors, safety, for example. So this is something that's an ongoing exercise for us. Content per vehicle will increase. Of course, electrification is an area. Additional clean fuels, hybrid, hydrogen, flex fuels,

items.statement: Non-ferrite motors work in progress; have non-heavy rare earth magnet motors ready for Indian market, exploring non-ferrous magnets
items.quote: On non-ferrite motors or motors without air magnets, there are multiple options here. We are currently exploring all options. And we're working. We have certain non-heavy rare earth magnet motors already prepared for the Indian market. But of course, we will also look at non-ferrous magnets as well as we go forward.

items.statement: Hybrid systems technology available globally, open to Indian market, in discussions with local OEMs
items.quote: On hybrids, our position is quite clear. We have a lot of technology for the hybrid segment. We offer this to several OEMs globally. And we are very open to doing that in the Indian market as well. And we are in discussion with all the OEMs locally.

items.statement: Working with OEMs on flex fuel engines among all technology options
items.quote: Yes, I mean, we work with OEMs on all technology options, including this. So, we certainly are working with OEMs.

items.statement: Sensor-less quick shift technology debuted in Indian market; TVS Ntorq 150 with Bosch Lambda sensor from Bidadi plant; deployed in Bajaj Pulsar NS400Z
items.quote: Our sensor-less quick shift technology made its debut in the Indian market, marking yet another step towards delivering smoother, smarter and more efficient mobility solutions. And here is something we are really proud of, a first for India. The TVS Ntorq 150 with Bosch's Lambda sensor realized in our Bidadi plant. items.statement: Received Hero MotoCorp's Hero Premium Leader Award for excellence and partnership
items.quote: Adding to our a chievements this quarter, Bosch was honored with Hero MotoCorp’s prestigious Hero Premium Leader Award, recognizing our commitment to excellence and partnership

items.statement: Supplying components to a couple of bigger electric two-wheeler makers, mainly scooter segment, engaging with all two-wheeler makers
items.quote: So on the electric two-wheelers, we are working with a couple of the bigger two-wheeler makers. Currently, it's largely the scooter segment that's on and we are supplying our components to them. And we will continue to engage with all two-wheeler makers and support them and provide our components on full range to all of them.

items.statement: Well prepared with capacity for increased ABS demand if two-wheeler ABS mandate implemented as per draft
items.quote: In terms of capacities, we are very well prepared to handle the increased demand that's likely to come out of changes in legislation.
