So right now, I do not want to get into a speculation on which way the ma

items.statement: Cautious on exports due to geopolitical issues, tariffs, landed costs; long-term commitment to increase exports remains valid
items.quote: At this point of time, I would again be a bit cautious on exports. There is a lot happening in the geopolitical space, also connected to tariffs, landed costs and so on. So we are assessing the situation. Our commitment to increase exports in the long run still is very much valid. We want to do that. But at this point of time, we need to watch this space very cautiously on how this overall situati

items.statement: Expect 8-15% hydrogen ICE market penetration in heavy commercial vehicles by around 2030
items.quote: And we expect between 8% to 15% market penetration by around 2030. So that's the sort of expectation we have on hydrogen in heavy commercial vehicle segments.

items.statement: Xperia supply issue resolving but still touch and go; playing cautiously on supplies
items.quote: Yes, I mean, it's still a little tentative. But at this point of time, as you've probably read in the newspapers and many other reports, the issue is resolving well. And we hope to have a good resolution on this. And this applies to be back to normal. But at this point of time, we would like to play it very cautiously because it's still touch and go in terms of supplies. So we need to play it very

items.statement: Mobility aftermarket anticipating strong momentum recovery post GST 2.0 transition next quarter; leveraging portfolio strengths, cost discipline, margin stability
items.quote: We are anticipating strong momentum recovery post GST 2.0 transition next quarter. Our strategy is clear, we are actively leveraging our robust portfolio strengths, maintaining strict cost discipline and focusing on margin stability.

items.statement: Power tools e-channel delivered high double-digit growth from successful festive offers; cordless 2.0 initiatives accelerating adoption
items.quote: Further boosting performance, our e -channel delivered high double-digit growth, thanks to the successful festive offers, affirming our strong digit al strategy and customer reach. Finally, strategic cordless 2.0 initiatives are accelerating and accelerating the adoption of advanced cordless technology through effective tactical interventions, solidifying our position in power tools

items.statement: Consumer goods growth driven by infrastructure activities in construction and mining; power tools growth continuously increasing
items.quote: On the consumer side, I think the large amount of demand has always been due to the excellent growth in infrastructure activities in India. And both construction and mining and many other activities have contributed significantly to demand in our consumer goods division. And power tools growth in this context has continuously increased. And we hope to keep this momentum as we go forward.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 1,099 crores as of September 30, 2025, supported by Indian Railways and OEM inflows
items.quote: Our order book remained strong at Rs. 1,099 crores as of September 30, 2025, reflecting sustained demand momentum across our key product lines.

items.statement: FY26 capex approximately Rs 60 crores, funded by Rs 34 crores term loan and internal accruals
items.quote: FY '26, we can definitely give our numbers, it's maybe approximately Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Backward integration project at Sinnar Plant completed, commercial production of CTC, EPICC, PICC copper conductors started with Rs 56 crores investment
items.quote: A major milestone during the quarter was the completion of our backward integration project at the Sinnar Plant and the commencement of commercial production of critical and highly specialized copper conductors for the transformer industry.

items.statement: Acquired BeLink Solutions (France) for EUR 1.5 million annual funding commitment over 3 years; BeLink has EUR 10 million revenue, not yet profitable
items.value: EUR 1.5 million per year for 3 years
items.quote: We have a commitment that we will fund about EUR1.5 million every year for 3 years. It would be our goal to make it profitable before that, but if not, then this is the maximum amount of commitment that we have given.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 30% year-on-year maintained for next three years; H1 FY26 grew 46.6%
items.quote: As committed previously, I am not changing that number, we have set 30% year-on-year and I will stick to that, and you can see the results and they will speak for themselves.

items.statement: Gross margin contraction in H1 due to copper conductor shortages and air freight costs; expects recovery from Q4 FY26 post backward integration
items.quote: It's basically we have had to because of the shortage of the copper conductors, we have had to import from South Korea, from China. And for certain cases, we have had to lift it by air and not by sea because of a lot of supply chain problems and logistics problems.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 96 in H1 FY25 to 80 in H1 FY26
items.quote: On the working capital front, the company achieved a notable improvement in working capital efficiency with working capital days improved from 96 in H1 FY '25 to 80 days in H1 FY '26 reflecting continued focus on operational efficiency.

items.statement: Propulsion system trials for WAP-5, WAP-7, WAG-9 locomotives to start soon; 50,000 km field trials expected to complete in 2-3 months
items.quote: Secondly, yes, that makes us eligible for P7 and G9 locomotives, P5, P7, and G9. And that's the highest locomotives in quantum today which are running on the field. And the field trials are for 50,000 kilometers, after which there are some other tests that have to be done. And then it gets into commercialization.

items.statement: Exported traction transformer to Germany (commissioned) and IGBT-based inverter to USA (dispatching); exploring further global opportunities
items.quote: We have dispatched and commissioned the transformer that was sent to Germany, and it's working well. And now we are talking to them for more opportunities of other products that they may need, whether it's transformers or some electronic equipment or some converters.

items.statement: Catering to 20-30% market share in hotel load converters and auxiliary converters; qualified for all locomotive types
items.quote: We are catering to, let's say, 20% to 30% of each of these products that you are mentioning.

items.statement: Competitive intensity acknowledged but mitigated by backward integration, IP, and process excellence; no major concern
items.quote: So yes, competitors will keep coming. But how will the competitors be competitive if they do not have good IP or good technology or good process? So it's not really a very big concern at this stage.

items.statement: Manoj Nair appointed CEO with 30+ years experience at Cummins India and CK Birla Group; Suramya Nevatia to focus on global strategy
items.quote: During the quarter, we further strengthened our leadership with the appointment of Mr. Manoj Nair as Chief Executive Officer of Hind Rectifiers.

items.statement: Revenue grew 37% YoY to Rs 227.1 crores in Q2 FY26; EBITDA grew 41.4% to Rs 25.9 crores; PAT grew 44.6% to Rs 14.7 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew 37% on Y -o-Y basis to Rs. 27 ( wrongly s aid, kindly read it as 227.1) crores in Q2 FY '26. Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 25.9 crores which is a growth of 41.4% on a Y-o-Y basis, driven by cost optimization through backward integration and favorable operating leverage.

items.statement: Copper conductor supply chain bottlenecks resolved via in-house CTC, EPICC, PICC production; reduces import dependence and logistics costs
items.quote: This development will enhance our operational efficiency by streamlining the supply chain, addressing shortages of key raw materials, and reducing our dependence on external vendors.

items.statement: Strong order pipeline from Indian Railways with large tenders expected post-budget and scattered throughout the year; no slowdown in inquiries
items.quote: There are huge tenders which are in pipeline that keep coming out from the railways, so wherever we are an approved source, we are bidding for these tenders and we book more of those.

items.statement: BeLink turnaround risk: not profitable for several quarters, requires EUR 1.5M annual funding for 3 years; auto industry downturn caused revenue decline from EUR 300M peak
items.quote: It is not profitable yet, in fact it will not be profitable for at least another several quarters. It will take time for us to bring it to pro fitability, but there are certain products that we have, there is certain IP that we have, that we want to commercialize from there and that can be used for the global market which has big potential

items.statement: Q2 FY26 order intake INR 878 cr; consolidated order backlog INR 2,146 cr including SEMCO
items.quote: Order intake was strong this quarter with INR 878 crores of order intake and the order backlog currently stands at INR 2,146 crores.

items.statement: Target 15-20% improvement in India order backlog at start of next financial year
items.quote: I would hope that at least a 15% to 20% improvement over previous years we would like to start with in terms of order backlog.

items.statement: Aspire for double-digit growth in India; international growth may be slightly lower
items.quote: I think double-digit growth in India should be kind of something that we should aspire for. I think international may be a little bit lower than that.

items.statement: Long-term leverage target below 1.0x
items.quote: We said we would like to keep our leverage below one. And this is also our long-term guidance that we would like to give.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA INR 122 cr, margin 13.5%, up 20% QoQ and 27% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for this quarter is up 20% quarter-on-quarter and 27% year-on-year and stands at INR 122 crores. Our EBITDA margin currently is at 13.5%.

items.statement: India business performing well across glass-lined, non-glass-lined, heavy engineering; agrochemicals returning after 18-24 months
items.quote: India looks strong across the three business lines really. But I think what is also nice is that this quarter we saw agrochemicals coming back in a large way, right? So, two of our big agrochemical clients after really an 18-month, 24-month sabbatical have now started investing again.

items.statement: Europe chemical/pharma slow; US improving; SEMCO Brazil growing in metals, minerals, water treatment; Edlon US semiconductors growing
items.quote: Europe, as I mentioned, has been slow and glass line d particularly has been a bit slow. We are seeing some improvement in the US. But Europe, from a pharmaceutical and chemical perspective, investment is still being delayed

items.statement: No immediate capacity expansion planned for glass-lined India; can add furnaces quickly if needed
items.quote: No, nothing right now. I think there is plenty of capacity that we have. We can very quickly add furnaces if we need.

items.statement: Poland JV investment INR 25 cr; SEMCO acquisition INR 162 cr (USD 18.5m) funded partly by EUR 10m debt
items.quote: We acquired SEMCO for a total purchase price of USD18.5 million, which corresponds to INR 162 crores. And the investment in Poland was 11 million Polish zloty, which is roughly INR 25 crores.

items.statement: Karamsad glass-lined facility running three shifts, 5-6 month backlog, near full utilisation
items.quote: The Karamsad facility is full. We have nearly a five to six month backlog in glass-lined. We are running three shifts. The fu rnaces are obviously now all kind of being used up to capacity

items.statement: Systems and services share rising in India; heavy engineering order book building; nuclear, green hydrogen, fertilizer targeted
items.quote: we also did quite well last quarter was started building a backlog for our heavy engineering business. So, there were some large orders received in heavy engineering. items.statement: SEMCO adds mixing for metals/mining/water in South America; four mixing platforms to be integrated under one umbrella
items.quote: SEMCO, again, a very good, strong company in South America. The focus is really growth. I think today we have a very comforting business in South America where the order backlog is basically a year worth of order backlog that they have.

items.statement: Large peptide contract in South India; discussions with global players like Bachem, Lilly for GLP-1 manufacturing equipment
items.quote: We are currently executing a very large contract for a peptide manufacturer in the south of India. And with that, we have a lot of opportunities, open opportunities, where we are seeing that a lot of these pharma companies are looking at peptides in a very large manner.

items.statement: Glass-lined market share 40-50%; further share gains would come at a cost, so growth focus on new segments
items.quote: In glass-lined, you already know we have a market share of 40%, -50%. In glass-lined, additional market share will come at a cost. So, we are not building our next three-year, five-year plan around the glass-lined business.

items.statement: Acquisition facility EUR 10m drawn for SEMCO; leverage target below 1.0x
items.quote: The acquisition of SEMCO, due to the size, was funded partly by external debt. We draw down an acquisition facility of 10 million euros.

items.statement: Heavy engineering revenue INR 260 cr FY25; ~15% growth in H1 FY26
items.quote: I think last year we were at INR 260 crores in heavy engineering. Yes. And from this half year, we are at what? Yes, I think that there is already like 15% growth or something like that.

items.statement: Services ~10% of consolidated order backlog; fast-moving, executed within 6 weeks
items.quote: I would say at any given time may be 10% of the order backlog would be around services.

items.statement: Glass-lined pricing rationalised and stable; steel and gas cost increases passed over time
items.quote: I think on a pricing front, I think there has been some kind of rationalization of pricing. I think there has been some stability there, and I think that will continue. And as the market improves and as the number of inquiries and opportunities increase, t hen maybe there is a further opportunity to also look at increasing prices

items.statement: Steel prices and gas prices rising; passed through over time
items.quote: We have steel prices going up. We have gas prices going up. So, all those things get passed on over time.

items.statement: US Biosecure Act and Make in US initiatives could drive reshoring demand for US-made glass-lined equipment
items.quote: We have had requests once maybe in the last couple of months, once or twice, for U.S. made equipment to be supplied quickly for a U.S. site, where they clearly mentioned that only U.S. equipment would do.

items.statement: SEMCO acquisition completed (USD 18.5m); Poland JV (INR 25 cr); both consolidated in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The acquisition of SEMCO has also been completed this year and we have consolidated SEMCO for this quarter as well as consolidated the backlog that SEMCO brings along with it.

items.statement: No new senior hires in India; employee cost increase due to internal recharges and integration
items.quote: We have not employed new people, but as part of our tax optimization strategy, we are doing internal kind of recharges and stuff like that. So, that is part of our optimization strategy.

items.statement: Europe chemical/pharma investment delayed due to geopolitical uncertainty; China demand slow, recovery expected next year
items.quote: Europe, from a pharmaceutical and chemical perspective, investment is still being delayed. Decisions are still taking time. I think there is still a lot of uncertainty surrounding global trade and geopolitical issues.

items.statement: Goodwill increased ~INR 200 cr mainly from SEMCO; PPA to be completed within 12 months, goodwill will reduce
items.quote: This is mainly due to the SEMCO acquisition. So, as of now, we have considered everything in goodwill. We will conduct the PPA now in the following, or in up to 12 months, and then the goodwill will be reduced.

items.statement: Q2 FX stable vs Q1 10% USD/EUR move; no material FX loss in Q2; tax rate improved
items.quote: In this quarter, the euro-USD FX rate did not really change significantly and it directly has a positive impact on our results, and therefore you also see a significant improved tax rate on the international business.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance of 35% range
items.quote: We expect operating margins to be in the range of 35%.

items.quote: Jindal Explorer has been recontrac ted at $35,606 per day, and the new contract is from November 2025 onwards. This is the day rate that will be in place for the next 3 years

items.statement: ONGC tender for 4 rigs due December first week; company will bid targeting rates in 60s

items.quote: We have to undertake refurbishment on each of these rigs at the end of every contract, which is an expenditure of INR70 crores to INR120 crores, depending on the condition of the rig.

items.statement: Refurbishment takes 4-6 months; costs amortized over contract duration
items.quote: So once the contract ends, then it takes anywhere between 4 to months for the refurbishment to be completed.

items.statement: ONGC issuing fewer tenders than expected; situation to continue for ~1 year; evaluating international opportunities
items.quote: As long as I see, ONGC, it is still taking out fewer tenders than what is expected, and it will continue for another 1 year is what I read from the

items.quote: Our aim would be to come up to the 65 level. And hopefully, the competition would have also realized that they bid too low in the last tender and would be bidding higher.

items.statement: Income in USD with natural hedge from USD rentals; rupee depreciation positive for company
items.quote: 3 of our rigs are rented. Therefore, the income and rental is also in dollars. So there is a nat ural hedge and generally rupee has

items.quote: The award that we have received was on account of a favorable high court decision. That was a receivable from ONGC denominated in U.S. dollars, which was at INR66 crores in our books. Over the period of past 14, 15 years, that INR66 crores became INR166 crores.

items.statement: Net cash position improved to INR295 crores from INR111 crores in March 2025 despite Jindal Pioneer acquisition
items.quote: The net cash position of the company, which has improved rapidly to INR 295 crores from the net cash position of INR 111 crores in March 2025.

items.statement: Dividend doubled in most recent financial year due to strong cash flows
items.quote: We've already doubled the dividend that we would normally pa y out in the most recent financial year because of the strong cash flow that we are earning

items.statement: No plans for new rig acquisitions in FY27 or FY28
items.quote: Nothing as of now. No.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer redeployment in 1 week to 10 days; Jindal Pioneer refurbishment completion in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Jindal Explorer is currently in its final stages of post refurbishment approval and will be redeployed in another week to 10 days.

items.statement: Order book visibility till FY27; future order book depends on ONGC tender outcomes
items.quote: As of now, the order book is based on the committed cash flows that we will receive.

items.statement: Profitability growth depends on material increase in India oil & gas expenditure; ONGC-BP exercise outcome awaited
items.quote: if oil and gas expenditure does not increase in India, then I don't believe tha t profitability can increase materially with this level of operations

items.statement: Declared 300% interim dividend, highest ever in company history
items.quote: I'm also pleased to note that Nava has declared a 300% interim dividend, which marks the highest ever interim dividend in its history.

items.statement: Nava Global dividend policy is 30% of PAT distributed as dividend
items.quote: So the dividend policy for Nava Global is adopted by the Board is 30% of PAT would be distributed as dividend.

items.statement: Nava Global declared $10 million dividend to Nava after receiving MEL dividend
items.quote: And therefore, Nava Global after receiving the dividend from MEL has declared $10 million to Nava.

items.statement: Maamba Phase 2 total outlay $400 million, $226 million spent so far
items.quote: Total outlay is $400 million for Phase 2. And out of that, currently $226 million has been spent.

items.statement: Total equity commitment of approximately $200 million for agri and energy sector projects
items.quote: we have a total equity commitment of approximately about $200 million, agri and in the energy sector.

items.statement: Odisha 60 MW captive plant transitioned to IPP, secured 5-year PPA for 50 MW at INR 5.95/kWh delivered rate starting Feb 2026
items.quote: This PPA is for 50 megawatt out of the 60 x 2 IPP in Odisha. And we expect the operation to cover at about 50-plus megawatt on an annualized basis.

items.statement: 100 MW solar project under construction with PPA tariff of 7.8 cents/kWh
items.quote: the solar project, the tariff at the power purchase agreement that we've signed with the utility is at 7.8 cents per kilowatt hour.

items.statement: Maamba 300 MW expansion both units expected commissioned by later part of next year
items.quote: We expect to have both the units commissioned by the later part of next year.

items.statement: Energy sales dropped due to planned Maamba semi-annual shutdown and lower India demand from prolonged monsoon
items.quote: One - there was a semi-annual shutdown in Maamba. It was a one-off, and it was planned. And the second one was on account of lower demand in India on account of the prolonged monsoon and weather conditions.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dropped from 48% to 34% YoY due to adverse forex impact and demand conditions, expected to bounce back
items.quote: On the EBITDA part, it is mainly due to -- one is the forex has been impacting us. You are referring to Y -o-Y Q2 of last year, 48% to 34%. So the forex has impacted adversely in this particular quarter, which definitely we feel it will reverse.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to INR 111.6 crore from INR 65.77 crore due to salary revisions effective April 1 and quarterly RSU fair valuation
items.quote: One is the salary increases and the revisions that have happened in second quarter effective 1st of April. That is one. And second is we also do the fair valuation of the RSUs, which is done every quarter.

items.statement: Employee cost not expected to go up beyond current level as Q2 had one-off valuation components
items.quote: We don't expect the employee cost to go up beyond this level.

items.statement: Expect to receive $55 million outstanding from ZESCO before end of FY26 (March 2026)
items.quote: We should expect -- I mean hopefully, I'm not going to commit on anything, but we hope to receive it before the end of this financial year.

items.quote: the borrowings are mainly towards the Maamba Phase 2. We are borrowing in a phased manner in line with the development of the project. A big part of that is still in our cash and cash balance, which will be used subsequently to fund that project.

items.statement: Investments increased to INR 726 crore from INR 597 crore in bonds and other investments with maturity over 1 year
items.quote: it is investment in current investments, which is effectively bonds and other investments, which have maturity of more than 1 year, which are classified as investments.

items.statement: Avocado plantation first crop production this year, scaling up with full production expected by FY28
items.quote: we did have a very small but initial first crop production this year itself. End of next year will be slightly larger, which will slowly scale up. And I think we're looking at probably full production at FY '28.

items.statement: Exploration activities in Zambia and Cote d'Ivoire ongoing, concrete information expected by end of next year but no fixed timeline
items.quote: I can't put a number on it, but we expect to have some news by the end of next year.

items.statement: Nacharam land in Hyderabad still evaluating options as real estate values climbing in the region
items.quote: Nacharam, we're still exploring better -- good options. I mean as you probably know, the Hyderabad real estate values, especially in that region are climbing and they're increasing.

items.statement: Constantly exploring new opportunities in similar verticals for greenfield and M&A activity to add to project pipeline
items.quote: we are constantly exploring new opportunities in similar verticals, both as greenfield and M&A activity, which will definitely add to the pipeline of projects that we want to undertake.

items.statement: No current proposal for bonus shares, focused on dividend distributions
items.quote: Currently, there's no proposal. Right now, we've just declared a dividend.

items.statement: Company has very limited debt and can act immediately on good opportunities evaluating risk versus reward
items.quote: given our assessment of projects that we get into, where we evaluate the risk versus reward, we're in a very good situation where we have very, very limited debt. So whenever a good opportunity arises, we can jump on that immediately.

items.statement: Management commits to a floor of 20% PAT growth sustainably over the next few years.
items.quote: From my side, I think what we can commit to is that a floor of 20% is what you can expect. That is what we have discussed at the Board that we would want to communicate to our investors. On a profit basis, we are quite confident that that we will be able to bring in sustainably over quarter-on-quarter for the next few years.

items.statement: Management targets PBT margin of 7.5% as terminal velocity over the next three years.
items.quote: I think 7.5% is what we have guided to as, call it a terminal velocity of our PBT margin. And the timeframe would be in the next three years.

items.statement: Q2 PAT margin was 3.56%, slightly muted due to one-time acquisition costs and labor issues; expected to improve from Q3.
items.quote: Our Q2 PAT margins stood at 3.56%, slightly muted as the revenue mix continues to shift towards higher-margin businesses. We expect this positive trajectory to get better.

items.quote: With the conclusion of the monsoon and the completion of the plant maintenance activities, there are early signs of demand recovery.

items.statement: CPVC price sensitive to PVC price fluctuations, with major drops impacting CPVC prices
items.quote: For major fluctuations in raw materials, CPVC price will move, but only for minor ones it won’t.

items.statement: Market share by first year premium income was 59.41% for H1 FY26 vs 61.07% in H1 FY25

items.statement: Individual new business premium income declined 3.54% YoY to Rs 28,491 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: The individual new business premium income for 6 months ended September 30, '25, was Rs 28,491 crores. And for the corresponding period last year, it was Rs 29,538 crores, thereby registering a drop of 3.54% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Group total premium income grew 6.73% YoY to Rs 94,965 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: The group business total premium income for 6 months ended 30th September 2025 was Rs 94,965 crores, comprising new business premium of Rs 92,586 crores.

items.statement: Total APE was Rs 29,034 crore in H1 FY26 with individual APE at Rs 17,170 crore and group APE at Rs 11,864 crore
items.quote: The total annualized premium equivalent for 6 months ended September 30 th 2025, is Rs 29,034 crores, which is comprised of individual APE of Rs 17,170 crores and group APE of Rs 11,864 crores.

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE rose to 36.31% in H1 FY26 from 26.31% in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our non-par share of individual APE is 36.31% and par is 63.69% for the 6 months ended 30 th September 2025.

items.statement: Net VNB grew 12.3% YoY to Rs 5,111 crore and VNB margin improved 140 bps to 17.6% in H1 FY26
items.quote: has registered a growth of 12.3% on a year-on-year basis to Rs 5,111 crores for the 6 months ended September 30 th 2025, from Rs 4,551 crores for the 6 months ended Life Insurance Corporation of India November 06, 2025 September 30, 2024. items.statement: Profit After Tax grew 16.36% YoY to Rs 21,040 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: The Profit After Tax for the 6 months ended 30 th September 2025 was Rs 21,040 crores as compared to Rs 18,082 crores for the 6 months ended September 30 th 2024, thereby registering a growth of 16.36% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Overall expense ratio decreased 146 bps YoY to 11.28% in H1 FY26
items.quote: For the 6 months ended September 30, 2025, the overall expense ratio was 11.28% as compared to 12.74% for the first 6 months of last year. You will observe that there is a decrease of 146 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: AUM grew 3.31% YoY to Rs 57,22,896 crore as of September 30, 2025
items.quote: The Assets Under Management as on September 30 th 2025, was Rs 57,22,896 crores as compared to Rs 55,39,516 crores as on September 30th 2024. Therefore, our AUM has registered a growth of 3.31% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Indian Embedded Value was Rs 8,13,230 crore as of September 30, 2025, down 1.03% YoY but up 4.68% from March 31, 2025
items.quote: The Indian Embedded Value as on September 30 th 2025, has been determined at Rs 8,13,230 crores as compared to Rs 8,21,716 crores as on September 30 th 2024. Therefore, the IEV has registered a decrease of 1.03% on a year-on-year basis. However, you will recall that the IEV was Rs 7,76,876 crores as on March 31 st 2025. Therefore, the IEV has improved by 4.68% between 31st March 2025 and September

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 2.13 as of September 30, 2025 from 1.98 a year earlier
items.quote: The solvency ratio as on September 30 th 2025, improved to 2.13 as against 1.98 on September 30th 2024.

items.statement: GST exemption on life insurance products announced in September 2025 expected to boost industry penetration
items.quote: We believe this move is customer-friendly and will provide a major boost to the further penetration due to better affordability and therefore, expand the size of the life insurance industry in India.

items.statement: Bancassurance and alternate channels new business premium grew 67.62% YoY to Rs 2,024.10 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: Bancassurance and Alternate Channels collected a new business premium income of Rs 2,024.10 crores for the 6 months ended September 30 th 2025, as compared to Rs 1,207.54 crores for the 6 months ended September 30 th 2024, thus registering a growth of 67.62% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Bancassurance and alternate channels share of individual new business premium rose to 7.12% in H1 FY26 from 4.1% in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our Bancassurance and Alternate Channels now account for 7.12% of the individual new business premium for the 6 months ended September 30, 2025, up from 4.1% for the 6 months ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Agent count increased to 14,85,325 as of September 30, 2025 from 14,39,658 a year earlier; agent market share 45.86%
items.quote: As on September 30, 2025, the total number of agents was 14,85,325 as compared to 14,39,658 as on September 30, 2024. The market share by number of agents as on 30th September 2025, stands at 45.86% as against 47.56% on September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Bima Sakhi program covered 44% of gram panchayats with 2.57 lakh women agents selling 8.54 lakh policies
items.quote: As of September 30 th 2025, a total of 2.57 lakh women have been designated as Bima Sakhis, successfully selling 8.54 lakh insurance policies and garnering a new business premium income of Rs 1,096 crores in 6-month period ended September 30, 2025. items.statement: Number of policies sold declined to 72.6 lakh in H1 FY26 from 91.7 lakh in H1 FY25 due to Master Circular and GST transition
items.quote: During the 6 months ended September 30, 2025, we sold 72,60,573 new policies as compared to 91,70,420 new policies in 6 months ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Persistency on premium basis: 13th month 75.29%, 25th month 71.37%, 37th month 67.70%, 49th month 63.70%, 61st month 63.81% in H1 FY26
items.quote: On premium basis, the persistency for the 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th and 61st month up to 6 months ended 30th September 2025 stands at 75.29%, 71.37%, 67.70%, 63.70% and 63.81%, respectively, as compared to 77.62%, 72.24%, 67.24%, 66.33% and 61.46%, respectively, up to the 6 months ended 30th September 2024.

items.statement: GST ITC impact on EV estimated below 0.5% disclosure threshold; already factored into H1 FY26 VNB margin of 17.6%
items.quote: We disclosed in the public disclosures that we do not estimate it to be more than 0.5% of that. What we are confirming is as per the current valuation, when we have done for the embedded value, it is much less than that.

items.statement: VNB margin walk: +3.4% from business mix, -1.1% from RFR change, -0.9% from operating assumptions including GST impact
items.quote: The VNB margin walk, which has been provided in the presentation is that because of the business mix, the change is 3.4% positive contribution. Because of RFR change, the impact is negative 1.1% and 0.9% negative is on account of operating assumptions. That includes the impact of GST.

items.statement: RBC solvency ratio under discussion with IRDAI; QIS1 and QIS2 submitted but numbers dynamic and not finalized
items.quote: We have actually submitted QIS1 and QIS2 to IRDAI. While we have submitted the results, we are still in discussion with them on several issues, and we are constantly engaged with them. Now, the ultimate solvency ratio based on the final QIS regime will depend upon the outcome of those things, which we are discussing with the regulator. So at this stage, I think the numbers are quite dynamic and su

items.statement: IDBI Bank remains leader in bancassurance; considerable growth from Axis and IDFC First; new tie-up with AU Small Finance Bank
items.quote: While IDBI continues to be the leader, but the considerable growth has come both from Axis as well as IDFC First. And as also in fact made available earlier, we are, in fact, forging new tie-ups, and that keeps on continue delivering value for us. So one of the things of value creation has been in fact in form of forging a tie-up with AU Small Finance Bank.

items.statement: ULIPs recorded over 100% growth in H1 FY26; non-par growth driven by ULIPs and savings products
items.quote: ULIP is slowly becoming more prominent in the entire insurance -- life insurance industry in India, and LIC has also been catching up in the sale of ULIPs. And it has recorded the highest growth among the various baskets of life insurance in the last quarter and the first half of the year. We are recording more than 100% growth on ULIPs as on date.

items.statement: Focus on top line growth rather than market share target; expect market share to stabilize if growth exceeds industry
items.quote: Again, though our focus will be exclusively on top line growth, not necessarily keeping in mind the market share, we would like the entire pie to grow and LIC to show a good growth, if possible, better than the industry growth. If that happens, naturally, our market share will stabilize and improve. Otherwise, also, we have a target on growth rather than looking at the market share per se directly

items.statement: Noida hospital commenced operations in September 2025 with 226 beds including 81 ICU beds, 5 OTs, 3 cath labs; currently at ~300 beds
items.quote: Currently, 226 beds are operational, including 81 ICU beds, 5 operating theaters and 3 cath labs.

items.statement: Board approved new project cost of INR 15,300 million for Mumbai 750-bed hospital including land, additional FSI, construction, equipment and staff housing
items.quote: The Board has approved a new project cost of INR 15,300 million to cater to the increased bed count of 750 beds.

items.statement: Guwahati land acquisition completed for ~INR 600 million; Bhoomi Pujan done on 31 Oct 2025, construction to commence
items.quote: In Guwahati, we completed the acquisition of a 3.5 -acre parcel of land for ~ INR 600 million.

items.statement: Mumbai FSI approval received to expand from 500 to 750 beds; construction approval pending
items.quote: In Mumbai, Oshiwara we received additional FSI approval, enabling us to expand our b ed capacity from the earlier reported number of 500 to 750

items.statement: Patna added 37 beds in Q2 FY26, total 57 beds added in H1 FY26; Lucknow no bed additions; Noida 226 beds operational
items.quote: During the quarter, 37 new beds were added in Patna, taking the total bed addition to 57 beds in the H1 FY26 in Patna.

items.statement: Consolidated inpatient volumes up 13% YoY, outpatient volumes up 15% YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Inpatient volumes during the quarter increased by 13% and outpatient volumes increased by 15% year -on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated ARPOB INR 65,570 in Q2 FY26, up 6% YoY from INR 62,141
items.quote: Average revenue per occupied bed for the quarter was INR 65,570 compared to INR 62,141 in the same quarter last year, an increase of 6% year -on-year.

items.statement: Mature hospitals ARPOB INR 73,447 in Q2 FY26, up 10% YoY driven by favorable specialty mix
items.quote: ARPOB for mature hospitals stood at INR 73,447 in Q2 FY26 compared to INR 66,989 in the same quarter last year, registering a strong growth of 10%, primarily driven by a favorable change in specialty mix.

items.statement: Developing hospitals ARPOB INR 54,854 (ex-Noida) and INR 54,980 (incl. Noida) in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Occupancy stood at 70% with an ARPOB of INR 54,854 across the developing hospitals. Including Noida, occupancy was 67% with an ARPOB of INR 54,980.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA ex-Noida grew 14% YoY to INR 2,804 million at 25.2% margin; incl. Noida EBITDA INR 2,607 million at 23.3% margin
items.quote: EBITDA ex-Noida grew 14% year-on-year with INR 2,804 million with a margin of 25.2% compared to 25.3% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Mature hospitals EBITDA INR 1,696 million at 23.5% margin; adjusting for OPD pharmacy shift, EBITDA growth 2.2% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA of matured hospitals stood at INR 1,696 million compared to INR 1,689 million in the same quarter last year with a margin of 23.5%.

items.statement: Developing hospitals ex-Noida EBITDA INR 1,112 million at 31.5% margin, up 34% YoY; incl. Noida EBITDA INR 915 million at 25.6% margin
items.quote: Overall, EBITDA from developing hospitals, Global Health Limited – Medanta November 10, 2025 excluding Noida was INR 1,112 million, registering a strong year-on-year growth of 34% with strong EBITDA margins of 31.5

items.statement: Noida hospital generated INR 39 million revenue and EBITDA loss of INR 197 million in first month (September), in line with expectations
items.quote: In the first month of operations, Medanta Noida generated INR 39 million and reported an EBITDA loss of INR 197 million, which is in line with expectations during the initial ramp -up phase.

items.statement: Overall debtor days 80-90 days; CGHS/ECHS collections take 7-9 months; PSU business faster
items.quote: See, overall basis, our debtor days remains about 80 to 90 days of our credit business. But in CGHS and ECHS in the government business, average credit realization happens somewhere between 7 - 8 months.

items.statement: CGHS rates revised after several years; ENT saw high growth, Cardiology/Cancer 5-10% growth; ECHS and PSU may follow
items.quote: We've seen some positive trajectory over there, especially in some of the specialties and departments, which were very, very low and almost unsustainable. So departments lik e ENT have seen high growth. In some of the bigger departments like Cardiology or Cancer, we've seen maybe 5% to 10% growth in different procedures.

items.statement: No senior attrition in Gurugram for 4-6 quarters; one department head moved from Patna to Noida; clinical talent attraction remains industry-wide challenge
items.quote: No, we have not seen any attrition in our Gurugram unit in the last many quarters, I think at least 4 to 6 quarters at any of the senior positions of the heads of department or heads of department minus 1.

items.statement: International patient revenue up 49% YoY to INR 762 million in Q2 FY26 driven by volume growth
items.quote: During the quarter, international patients revenue increased by 49% year -on-year to INR 762 million in Q2 FY 26, driven by increased international patient volume.

items.statement: Balance sheet strong with net cash surplus of INR 7,082 million at end September 2025
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains extremely strong with a net cash surplus of INR 7,082 million at the end of September 2025.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex ~INR 4,252 million primarily for Noida project and equipment upgrades across network
items.quote: Overall, our operating cash flows for H1 FY 26 stood at INR 3,295 million, and capex was approximately INR 4,252 million, primarily towards our Noida project and upgradation of medical equipment across the network.

items.statement: South Delhi digging commenced; Pitampura plans submitted for approval; Guwahati land possessed, drawings underway; Mumbai FSI paid, construction approval pending
items.quote: So in our South Delhi and Pitampura projects, we have commenced the digging activities in our South Delhi project. Pitampura project, we have submitted our plans for approval and as soon as those get approved, we will be commencing all our various construction activities.

items.statement: New hospitals typically take 3-4 years to build; Noida built in 3 years; Guwahati, Mumbai, South Delhi, Pitampura all 3-4 years away
items.quote: All the hospitals are typically about 3 years away, I would say, Noida we built in 3 years from starting construction until now. So, but any hospital typically takes 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: No significant competitive impact in Lucknow; volumes and clinical talent stable; competitive intensity exists but no change seen
items.quote: I haven't seen any change actually in anything that's been happening there in the last several months. So no real impact of this. I'm sure that competitive intensity exists. I'm sure it will remain. But we haven't seen any difference anyway.

items.statement: Clinical talent attraction and retention remains key challenge across all markets including NCR; competition from listed, unlisted, charitable and government hospitals
items.quote: I maintained in past calls that the competition and the ability to attract and retain high-quality and high ethical, more importantly, clinical talent, especially in the kind of full -time model that we have, will remain a challenge, and it is not only in NCR, I think this challenge will remain in most of the major markets.

items.statement: Medanta ALOS ~3-3.06 days, among lowest in industry for complexity; ARPOB growth tapering to mid-high single digits industry-wide
items.quote: If you look at Medanta's length of stay, it's probably amongst the lowest in the industry for institutions of this caliber and complexity of work that we do, around 3 - 3.06 days.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins to reach past historical highs of ~25%
items.quote: What we had said in our earlier analyst calls is that in a sense, '27 as in the next financial year, our hope will be to reach our past historical high levels, which is about 25% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Management plans nominal profit for FY26
items.quote: We are planning to reach to that level, make some nominal profit in the current financial year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 150 bps QoQ to 13.1% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 13.1%, an improvement of 150 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management confident H2 FY26 EBITDA margins will be much better than Q2
items.quote: We are definitely confident that the second half EBITDA margins will be much better than the Q2 margins, much better.

items.statement: Acemoney steady-state EBITDA margin expected at 15-20%
items.quote: At a combined level, I think that business in a steady state can generate about between 15% to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Currency in circulation grew ~8% YoY to INR38 lakh crore as of Aug 2025
items.quote: So the currency in circulation, even if you see the latest data as of August 2025, it is almost INR38 lakh crores growth over same period last year, almost 8% growth over same period last year.

items.statement: October festive season cash volumes strong; trend expected to continue
items.quote: October festive season has been fantastic for -- as you would have seen in many other companies as well. So same is the case for us. October has been go od. We're expecting that the trend will

items.statement: Acemoney installed 14,000+ POS machines in Q2; FY26 target >1 lakh incremental
items.quote: We have installed 14,000-plus POS machines in this quarter and working towards achieving an ambitious target of more than 1 lakh machines for the current financial year.

items.statement: Acemoney transaction volumes ~INR400 crore in Q2; transaction revenue now 25% of mix
items.quote: We clocked transaction volumes of almost INR400 crores in this quarter, and transaction revenues now account for almost 25% of our revenues in this quarter.

items.statement: Direct client revenue share rose to 15.7% of standalone revenue
items.quote: We have strengthened our direct client's business, which has continued to grow at a healthier pace and now constitutes 15.7% of our standalone revenues.

items.statement: E-commerce segment revenue grew 30%+ YoY; Petroleum grew 24%
items.quote: We witnessed healthy growth of 30% plus in E-Commerce segment and 24% in Petroleum segment.

items.statement: Railways and E-commerce Logistics revenue dropped >50% YoY
items.quote: Railways and E-Commerce Logistics reported more than 50% drop in this quarter compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Payment aggregator license investment of INR3 crore; license expected in 2 quarters
items.quote: By next 2 quarters, we hope to have that license and then roll out -- continue to do the same business.

items.statement: Network covers 15,000+ pin codes and 9,000+ locations
items.quote: We continue to expand our geographic footprint with over 15,000 pin codes and close to 9,000 locations.

items.statement: Cost reduction measures targeting INR50 million annualized savings from Q3
items.quote: Through rigorous benchmarking of several productivity measures, which is expected to reduce costs to the tune of INR50 million on an annualized basis at current level of operations from the third quarter onwards.

items.statement: Guard and driver costs rising ~7-8% annually due to market conditions
items.quote: the cost nominally increase typically 7%, 8% to account for cost of living and guards and drivers specifically are at a slightly higher rate because of market

items.statement: Acemoney revenue bounced to INR49 million in Q2 from INR17 million in Q1
items.quote: Radiant Acemoney has bounced back and reached revenues of INR49 million for this quarter, up from INR17 million in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Diamond Bullion Jewellery segment growing but loss-making; breakeven targeted FY26
items.quote: The senior management team has been strengthened and the routes have been consolidated and the management is confident of achieving breakeven in this business vertical in the current financial year.

items.statement: Valuable Logistics (RVL) revenue nearly doubled; breakeven targeted H2 FY26
items.quote: A strong focus on achieving growth and breakeven in valuable Logistics segment has resulted in near doubling of revenues in this division, though on a small base.

items.statement: RVL monthly breakeven revenue target INR1-1.2 crore
items.value: INR1 crore or INR1.2 crores per month
items.quote: INR1 crore or INR1.2 crores per month is where the breakeven level will be at this point in time.

items.statement: Added 10 new clients and 120 new end customers in retail cash management in H1 FY26
items.value: 10 new clients and 120 new end customers
items.quote: During the financial year so far, we added 10 new clients and 120 new end customers in our retail cash management business.

items.statement: AGS Transact bankruptcy not a direct opportunity as business lines differ
items.quote: See, it's not a peer. We don't -- we hardly have any line of business, which is common with AGS. They are more in the ATM segment, and we are not present in that segment at all.

items.statement: RBI mandates payment aggregator license for Acemoney; application in progress
items.quote: RBI has said that they will not allow that business model to continue and payment aggregation players like Acemoney have to obtain a payment aggregator license.

items.statement: Free cash ~INR75 crore of INR242 crore total cash; rest used for operations and bank guarantees
items.quote: about that, not half of it. INR75 crores is free cash. rest of it is cash used in cash management activities. For funding leasing, pickups, for funding holiday pickups, for funding low denomination notes and coins, for funding same day, day 0 funding, etcetera. And also margin money towards bank guarantee that we provide to banks

items.statement: Core cash management revenue flat due to lower bank thrust and extended monsoons
items.quote: In summary, the revenue performance for the year has been muted due to company-specific factors highlighted earlier as well as due to extended monsoons.

items.statement: Cash handled volume flat YoY at INR0.41 trillion in Q2; H1 volume INR0.83 trillion (+1.3% YoY)
items.quote: Volume of cash handled during the quarter at INR0.41 trillion remained flat over the same quarter in the previous year.

items.statement: Spent about Rs 110 crore on new projects in H1 FY26
items.quote: On the CAPEX side, this year so far, we have spent about Rs. 110 odd crores of CAPEX for the new project.

items.statement: Dombivali Hospital on track to start operations in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Dombivali Hospital, as I said, is on track. It is forecasted to start in Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: South Pune Hospital construction commenced in Q3 FY26; Mira Road Hospital in architectural planning stage
items.quote: The South Pune Hospital construction has commenced in this 3rd Quarter of the financial year, and the Mira Road Hospital is now on the architectural drawing board.

items.statement: Mature hospital EBITDA margins expected in mid-20%; new hospitals EBITDA negative in year 1, break-even in year 2
items.quote: On an individual hospital level, mature margins are expected to be in the mid-20%. As the new hospitals come up, they are expected to be EBITDA negative in the first year and break even in the second year.

items.statement: Dombivali Hospital will dilute consolidated EBITDA margin in first year of operations
items.quote: So, as Dombivali comes up, it should lead to a little dilution in consolidated margin in the first year.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at Rs 325 crore; liquid investments and deposits over Rs 500 crore (around Rs 550 crore) as of September
items.quote: So, the current consolidated debt stands at Rs. 325 crores. Against that, we have liquid investments and deposits of over Rs. 500 crores, around Rs. 550 crores if I am not wrong at the end of September.

items.statement: Blended cost of debt between 7% and 8%; carrying cost around 1% due to high liquid investments
items.quote: So, it is between 7% and 8%, I think, currently. But the carrying cost is pretty much around 1% because, as I said, we are holding.

items.statement: IP volumes flat year-on-year in H1 FY26 at ~27,200 vs 27,400; Q2 occupancy impacted by lower infection outbreak in Pune
items.quote: So, the IP volumes are pretty much flat. Last year, I think it was 27,200. This time it is 27,400. So, largely flat.

items.statement: ARPOB increased ~15% to Rs 66,100 in H1 FY26 driven by case mix optimization in Indore, insurance rate revisions, and general inflation-based pricing
items.quote: So, it is a combination of some case mix optimization in Indore. Some of the ongoing rate revisions happen with insurance companies on a periodic basis as and when the contracts expire and general inflation-based pricing.

items.statement: Doctors on minimum guarantees with flexible pay systems; no fixed wage inflation discussions needed
items.quote: So, most of our doctors are on minimum guarantees with flexible paid systems. So, no one is really employed with a fixed cap. So, essentially, there is no wage as such.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansions will be considered once phase 1 occupancy crosses 60%
items.quote: Our general philosophy is that once we cross 60% occupancy of the installed base, we think about expansion.

items.statement: No live inorganic opportunities being pursued; open to sensible opportunities in Western India including Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
items.quote: First inorganic, there is nothing live that we are chasing. But if and when there is something which we are discussing or that materializes, I will be happy to talk about it. On the focus areas, we are open to any sensible opportunity in Western India. We are open to Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh as well, not necessarily Maharashtra.

items.statement: No tracking or targeting of specialty mix; full-service community hospital mirroring local disease burden
items.quote: We do not track specialty mix and we do not even have any target. We are a full service community hospital. So, whichever our specialty mix pretty much mimics the disease burden of the communities that we serve.

items.statement: Consolidated occupancy 64.5% in Q2 FY26 on expanded bed base (added ~150 beds); Thane mid-70s, Pune approaching 70, Indore showing occupancy and revenue growth
items.quote: Consol level, I can tell you for this quarter, we were at 64.5%. This is on the expanded base of occupancy on, I mean, expanded base of beds that we added last year. So, last year, this quarter, we were at 70%. And this year, we are at 64.5%, but we added 150 odd beds this year.

items.statement: Professional fees up 31-32% YoY in Q2 due to Rs 12.5 crore one-time provision from new accounting policy for unbilled revenue and conservative doctor cost provisioning
items.quote: No, sir, this is completely one -off. I have put a short note , and this is pretty much in with the new accounting treatment that we have done. There is a Rs. 12 crore one-time provision in the professional fee component based on this new policy, which we have done. So, if you read the financials without this one -off Rs. 12 crore s, Rs. 12.5 crore impact, then you will see the continual and ongoi

items.statement: Dombivali Hospital expected to reach break-even (40-45% occupancy) by year 2; long-term demand strong due to dense population and lack of supply
items.quote: Yes, so year two, I think we definitely think that a bit of break-even should happen. And that happens upwards of 40%, 45% occupancy, as we have seen. So, yes, I think that could be a decent assumption.

items.statement: Dombivali ARPOB expected slightly lower than mature hospitals in early years due to primary/secondary case mix; pricing similar to MMR region
items.quote: In the early years of a hospital, you generally do more, you know, primary and secondary work and less of tertiary work. And second is pricing, which should be pretty much similar to the MMR pricing that we are getting now. But because of early years, we should definit ely expect a slightly lower ARPOB in Dombivali than we see in matured hospitals

items.statement: Unbilled revenue of Rs 19.2 crore recognized in Q2 FY26; related professional fee cost Rs 3 crore; additional Rs 9.3 crore conservative provision for doctor share on outstanding insurance receivables
items.quote: Yes, so this Rs. 12 crores is two components. One component is a cost pertaining to this Rs. 19 crores that is the professional fee for this Rs. 19 crores, which is Rs. 3 crores. The other component is another Rs. 9.3 crores. That is, while we did this policy of unbilled revenue, we also thought that we should be a little more conservative in our provisions for the professional fee.

items.statement: Doctor variable fees paid only upon insurance collection realization; provisions reversible if bad debts occur
items.quote: Only if we realize the money we pay out. So, if there are any bad debts or anything, then to that extent, the provisions will get reversed.

items.statement: Doctor payment upon collection is industry practice; company adopted more conservative provisioning for outstanding bills
items.quote: This is an industry practice.

items.statement: Three projects (Dombivali, South Pune, Mira Road) expected to be funded from internal resources and accruals; existing debt may be used for potential fourth project
items.quote: The three projects that we have underway, that is Dombivali, South Pune and Mira Road, we expect that we should probably be able to complete with our resources and future internal accrual. This debt might kick in if we need or if we get an opportunity to do one more project.

items.statement: No concrete plans for seventh hospital; in early discussions with land acquisition uncertainties

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.8%; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.5%

items.statement: BESS segment: executing 30 MW Bihar project (land finalization underway); bidding more solar+BESS and standalone BESS projects; planning containerized assembly then cell backward integration
items.quote: So, we have taken this project, which you are talking about is the Bihar project, which is currently, the land is being finalized and will be given by the BSPGCL. Once that is given, then we will start work on it. And we should expect all this to happen in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin range of 8% to 10%
items.quote: Our priorities are clear, drive growth through volume, tighten costs through process engineering and restore margins to our target range of 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Demand visibility encouraging across all operations; RFQ cycles for H1 2026 volumes looking strong
items.quote: Looking ahead, demand visibility across all areas of operations stay encouraging. We are already active in the RFQ cycles for H1 2026 volumes, which are looking strong even though pricing stays tight.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.34% vs 8% in Q1; lower due to Mahad drag and price alignment
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, turnover increased by 20% to Rs. 271 crores, while EBITDA stood at Rs. 17 crores, representing a margin of 6.34% both on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Mahad plant causing 1.5% to 2% point drag on Group EBITDA; expected to normalize over next few quarters
items.quote: Our Mahad Greenfield plant, which is still in the ramp-up phase, is currently causing a 1.5% to 2% point drag on Group EBITDA. This impact is expected to normalize over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Mahad Greenfield plant Phase 1 capacity 250 metric tons annually; currently at 20-21% utilization
items.quote: So, we have stated that our capacity of the Mahad plant in phase one is 250 metric tons annually. Right now and we have also stated that it takes anywhere between five to six months for us to complete one cycle of sampling approvals and commercial shipments.

items.statement: Baroda facility at 90-95% utilization; hydrogenation plant at 65-70%; Bareilly at 85-90%; Ambernath fragrance at 100% in one shift with 3x potential
items.quote: So, if you look at the Baroda facility, the Baroda facility except the hydrogenation plant, runs at anywhere between 90% to 95%. The hydrogenation plant is currently running at around 65% to 70%. In terms of the products that we have taken in, we still have certain capacity which we have to expand, which we have not even started the automation work on those reactors when it comes to Baroda. Bareil

items.statement: Chinese suppliers dumping in non-tariff markets keeping pricing under pressure; Pinene prices firm; rupee depreciation adds cost pressure
items.quote: However, the market stays a buyer's market, with Chinese suppliers dumping into non-tariff markets like India, Southeast Asia, and the EU, keeping pricing under pressure. We are countering this through process re-engineering and yield optimization. Pinene prices remain firmed up, and the rupee depreciation adds to the

items.statement: Conscious choice to focus on penetration and volume leadership in soft price environment; aligning sale prices with market to safeguard volumes
items.quote: Yes, margins are lower, but that is a conscious choice. We have focused on penetration and volume leadership in a soft price environment.

items.statement: Cash flow pressure driven by strategic inventory buildup across camphor, trading, and fragrance raw materials; receivables increased due to last period sales but no collection issues
items.quote: Primarily, I think the cash flow has been because of certain strategic decisions that we have taken which have resulted in inventory at our end. And the cash flow primarily is driven by inventory. But this inventory is definitely useful inventory and will get used up in the due course of time and is going to be used up in a positive way rather than a negative way.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity at 0.6x as of 30 September 2025; healthy and conservative balance sheet
items.quote: Our net debt-to-equity of 0.6x reflects a healthy and conservative balance sheet.

items.statement: Not pursuing anti-dumping duties on camphor imports; evaluating situation; Chinese imports are natural camphor vs domestic synthetic camphor
items.quote: So, the straight answer to your question is we are currently not pursuing any such activities of approaching the government and asking them for any of these tariffs. We are still watching the situation.

items.statement: Camphor market faces oversupply from substantial domestic capacity additions; demand not expanded to same level
items.quote: I think the bigger challenge to profitability is the substantial capacity for camphor that has been built in India by multiple players. And the camphor market per se has not expanded to the same level. So, we are having a classic situation where there is a lot of supply and relatively less demand.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 production grew 26% QoQ and 10% YoY; sales volume rose 30% QoQ and 21% YoY; sales value up 20% QoQ and 15% YoY
items.quote: Production grew 26% sequentially and 10% year-on-year, whereas sales volume rose 30% quarter-on-quarter and 21% year-on-year. That translates into a 20% growth in sales value over Q1 and 15% over the same period last year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 operating revenue Rs. 497 crore, up 10% YoY; EBITDA Rs. 35 crore, margin 7.11% vs 11.20% YoY; net profit Rs. 1.24 crore
items.quote: Moving on to the first half of FY'2026, on a consolidated basis, the operating revenue for H1 FY'2026 was Rs. 497 crore, representing a 10% year-on-year increase. EBITDA for the period stood at Rs. 35 crore compared to Rs. 51 crore in the corresponding half year. The EBITDA margin was 7.11% as against 11.20% in the corresponding period.

items.statement: Buyer's market globally for ingredients; pricing pressure on all existing products including camphor; Mahad ramp-up adds to margin pressure
items.quote: Mahad plus the pressure that we have on the selling price of a lot of the products. Because currently, we are seeing the ingredients side of the business to be a buyer's market globally. And that commentary is consistent with all the companies that are major manufacturers of fragrances and flavors globally, where it is a buyer's market.

items.statement: Trading business launched Q2 FY25 growing well; increased product offerings providing quantity leverage for fragrance division raw material buying
items.quote: But I can very safely say that the business continues to grow pretty well. We have increased the number of product offerings that we are giving to the customers in India. And that gives us an additional benefit of having quantity leverage when we are buying for our fragrance division.

items.statement: Ductile Iron pipe demand slowed due to delays in government spending; production moderated, costs increased, pricing under downward pressure.
items.quote: The Ductile Iron pipe segment continues to face demand slowdown due to delays in government spending. Consequently, production levels have been moderated, costs have increased and there's a downward pressure on pricing.

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA per ton achievable from Q2 FY27; pickup from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Starting next year, I think starting quarter 2 next year, we can start seeing a dramatic improvement in the production levels and also in the margins per ton. So definitely, I think a double-digit margin per ton is very much achievable starting Q2 next year.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR 300 crores (sustenance and debottlenecking); next 4 years ~INR 500 crores sustenance; DI pipe expansion 1 lakh ton on hold, ~INR 60 crores, 6-8 months to install.
items.quote: For this year, predominantly, we are focusing on sustenance CAPEX like at Srikalahasthi, we are rebuilding one of our battery. And apart from that, the major focus is definitely on, I mean, sustenance-based Capex. Figure, it may be difficult for me, but possibly around INR 300 crores or so, everything put together.

items.statement: Installed DI pipe capacity 850,000 tons; target 950,000-1 million tons on hold until inventory cleanup and 850k utilization.
items.quote: At the moment, our installed capacity remains at 850,000 tons, and we are hoping to get to 90%, 95% of that figure next financial year.

items.statement: Order book adequate; ~60% JJM, 50-55% domestic including JJM; irrigation traction good, Amrut slower.
items.quote: A round 60% would be JJM. If you include domestic, it will be around 50% - 55%. And the rest is non-JJM and export.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross margin ~48%, stable as product and raw material prices fell together; EBITDA margin 12.6% consolidated, 13.3% standalone.
items.quote: So gross margins was around 48% for the first half. It has been more in line with what it was last year because the prices of the products have come down, but also at the same time, raw material prices have also come down.

items.statement: DI pipe realization ~INR 6-6.5 per kg in Q2; expect double-digit EBITDA per ton from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: In this quarter, it is around INR 6-6.5 per Kg. Can we expect this is bottom? Or do you see further correction in next 2 quarters? And next year, with expected improvement in the demand, can we expect double-digit EBITDA per kg next year

items.statement: Export volume grew 8% YoY in Q2, partially offsetting domestic weakness; historically export more than industry average.
items.quote: However, export market volume grew by 8% year-on-year partially offsetting the weakness in domestic demand and providing support to overall business performance.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR 1,626 crores, up INR 230 cr from June 2025 due to valve acquisition and business needs; interest cost stable.
items.quote: Net debt at a stand-alone level stood INR 1,626 crores. The utilization increased by around INR 230 crores compared to June 2025 mainly due to cash outflow relating to acquisition of valve company and other business requirements.

items.statement: Centre reviewing JJM delays, quality, financial irregularities; funding paused until scrutiny concludes; extension to 2028 with enhanced budget signals commitment.
items.quote: They want to try and understand why there are certain delays and why there are certain complaints and reports that have gone to them, which are negative in nature. And only it is like a check-back mechanism, sir. So, they are trying to course correct before it gets too late.

items.statement: Demand recovery dependent on government fund release after scrutiny; 2-3 month lag for orders to reflect in dispatches; coal block compensation timing uncertain.
items.quote: Based on the progress they have made so far and the further inquiries that they have shared with the states, that makes me feel that starting calendar year, they would have reached their conclusions and they will start opening up the funds.

items.statement: Employee expenses may rise marginally to ~INR 165 cr/quarter due to valve portfolio expansion.
items.quote: There might be a marginal increase in the employee expenses as we expand our business in the valves product portfolio. In fact, this increment is largely related to that portion. So there will be a marginal increase, but it will not be substantial enough really. It might be that it goes to INR 165 crores or something like that.

items.statement: Coal block compensation: one asset valued ~INR 498 cr, two more large assets pending; hope to realize within FY26.
items.quote: This is the valuation for one particular asset, which had not been valued so far. It is close to our estimate as well. This probably it would be incorrect for me to give any sort of deduction on when we can realize it, but there is active persuasion from the side of the new allotee and also the ministry. So hopefully, within this financial year, sorry, we should see this work out.

items.statement: Casting volume target of 170,000 tons for FY26, with Oliver adding 15,000-16,000 tons
items.quote: And with that, we expect that -- and we are also in the process of merging Oliver with KFIL. I think we will be together would be very close to that number of 170,000 tons.

items.statement: Tube volume target of 200,000 tons for FY26, with 10% growth next year before new facility
items.quote: For the first 6 months, we have already gone to a volume of almost 98,000 metric ton and look forward to seeing 200,000 volume very close to that in this year.

items.statement: Power cost savings of INR 70-80 crores expected in FY26 from renewable energy
items.quote: And this year, we may get it because of th e change of the tariff structures. We may get anywhere between INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores total benefit for the year coming out of the power cost

items.quote: That is another set of improvement to be achieved, which is more than around INR 125 crores of investment to upgrade.

items.quote: We have already started our Oliver foundry, and we have done a production and sale of close to 5,000 tons over there. And we expect that going forward, we will be doing around 15,000 to 16,000 tons at Oliver.

items.quote: We are towards annual run rate of 2 lakh metric ton of seamless tubes. And I expect whatever the debottlenecking measures we have already taken or we are taking. We should be able to achieve another 10% to 12% next year.

items.quote: As on date, we have come very close to we can say 3,000 metric tons per month from Line 1 and about to reach hopefully this month, next month about 2,000 metric ton from Line 2.

items.quote: In last 2 years, 3 years, the INR 10,000 margin has come down to say, INR 3,000. I'm talking on contribution level, gross level. And this has put a lot of pressure in terms of covering the cost.

items.quote: Pig iron prices have come down from INR 41,670 per metric ton to INR 37,098 per metric ton, which is a drop of 11%.

items.quote: We have been able to also win some of the tenders in tube because of which we will continue to have loading up the mills full.

items.statement: Shifting to high value-added castings with more machining, developing new products to retain realization despite commodity downturn
items.quote: Product mix is changing. We are doing more and more high value - added castings. Hence, we have been able to retain the sales reali zation in spite of commodity pricing going

items.quote: We have done so much work on integrating right from pig iron, coke oven, coke oven power generation and efficiency improvement, productivity improvement.

items.quote: With respect to sale, yes, we have over, I think, about 40 days stoppage. And to that extent, I think there is some inventory and sale will happen from inventory, but production loss for 40 days, which is around 21,000, 22,000 tons.

items.quote: One is the government of Maharashtra change in the time slots and a little bit setback on support for solar because now we have come to conclusion only 52% of the power consumption can be from solar.

items.quote: Though there are many issues, including dumping, we are representing to government. But yes, in between, we suffer.

items.quote: We are also in the process of merging Oliver with KFIL. I think we will be together would be very close to that number of 170,000 tons.

items.quote: I will leave this to Mr. Srivatsan, I think who is on an update on the progress on NSE listing.

items.statement: Q2 and Q3 expected to be similar; uptick hoped by Q4
items.quote: I would say Q2 and Q3 should be similar. And hopefully by Q4, we should see an uptick.

items.quote: CV exports to North America are down 48% on a sequential basis and abo ut 67% on a YOY basis

items.quote: Standalone EBITDA in this quarter was at INR 545 crores with 28% margins which was lower by about 7.3% sequentially. This includes INR 24 crores on account of tariff charges.

items.statement: H1 FY26 new business wins INR 1,582 crore across components, defense, casting
items.quote: During H1 of this fiscal, the Company had secured new business worth INR 1,582 crores across all key businesses which includes Bharat Forge Component and Industrial business of INR 823 crores, defense INR 559 crores an d our casting business of INR 200 crores

items.quote: So, aerospace for last year, for the full year was in the ballpark of about INR 250 odd crores. Okay, I think this year should be in excess of INR 350 crores. items.statement: Increasing capacities in India for aerospace and engineering, supplemented by inorganic route
items.quote: In the medium term, we are in the midst of increasing our capacities in India to address opportunities in many new sectors, including aerospace and engineering and this will be s upplemented by the inorganic route in India

items.quote: So, we have taken an enabling approval of up to INR 2000 crores and we will action this depending on when the timing is right.

items.quote: Quarter 2 numbers also include first time consolidation of K Drive Mobility which was the American Axial India Manufacturing business which we acquired. The integration progress is on track.

items.quote: Our Indian manufacturing which is our Indian forging, defense, casting plus axle aggregates now accounts for about two-thirds of our consoli dated revenues across our global business and it's well diversified across segments and geographies. items.statement: Global MNCs increasing sourcing from India; Indian manufacturing geared to tap this demand
items.quote: As global MNCs increase their sourcing from India, our Indian manufacturing business is geared to tap into this demand.

items.statement: Diversified business mix weathering storm better than single-sector peers
items.quote: constant endeavors to diversify our business mix and this has proved to be very relevant and paid off as you can see that we are weathering the storm far better than companies that are directly playing only in one or two sectors

items.statement: Separate Horizon 1 team for existing products/markets and Horizon 2 team for new growth at K Drive Mobility
items.quote: We are going to play Horizon 1 and we have a separate team for Horizon 2. So, Horizon 1 team will focus on existing products, existi ng markets, and improvement in financials for those sectors. And then the new team will also focus on Horizon 2

items.quote: None. There should be monetary allocation, that's all.

items.statement: European steel restructuring roadmap by end of FY26
items.quote: We will have a roadmap in place outlining the sha pe and form of the proposed restructuring of the steel business by the end of this fiscal

items.statement: Gross margin improvement from cost reduction, block shutdowns, in-house value addition, product mix
items.quote: We have done a lot of cost reduction work. When the quarter started and it looked really bleak, we took a lot of block shutdowns, et c. And we are trying to do more value addition in -house, improve our product mix. So, it's a combination of all these

items.statement: JS Auto Q2 sales growth ~26%, EBITDA growth ~44%; margins improving
items.quote: Our Q2 sales growth for JS was about 26% and EBITDA growth of about 44%. So, clearly, even the profitability of the business is improving.

items.statement: MHCV production outlook flat; passenger vehicle strong due to festive season, monitor post-festive
items.quote: MHCV, the broader expectation is it should remain flat. Not a very significant growth or degrowth.

items.statement: Non-auto exports jump sequentially driven by power gen, construction, mining, aerospace
items.quote: It's multiple sectors. It includes power gen, it includes construction, mining and aerospace.

items.statement: Consolidated cash INR 2,300 crore as of H1 FY26
items.quote: we had cash of about INR 2,300 crores on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs.7.20 per share declared for Q2 FY26
items.quote: we have declared another interim dividend of Rs.7.20 paisa.

items.quote: We have also purchased our first Ultramax bulk carrier which will be delivered by Q4 FY26. So, with these, the commitments, we will be at 40 vessels.

items.quote: today, if you build a Suezmax tanker, right, it costs about $80 million to build. So, if you place an order for two, three or four of those, it will absorb a significant amount of money.

items.quote: currently at 41 vessels ; however, we have committed for a crew of our 20-year-old tankers, one is a crew carrier Jag Lok and the other is the product tanker Jag Pooja, both of which will be delivered in this quarter. We have also purchased our first Ultramax bulk carrier which will be delivered by Q4 FY26. So, with these, the commitments, we will be at 40 vessels.

items.quote: the big factor in influencing the crude tanker flows is the OPEC unwinding of the OPEC production cuts and that has resulted in demand for crude tankers, because there is more commodity coming into the market. items.statement: Standalone profit flat QoQ but significantly lower YoY due to prior year ship sale profits and capacity drop from vessel sales; offshore vessels fixed at good levels, four on short-term contracts
items.quote: our profit is more or less the same on a standalone basis as what it was in the previous quarter, that is Q1 FY26; it is significantly lower than in Q2 FY25, which is a corresponding quarter. items.statement: $186 million debt outstanding, all NCDs listed and non-prepayable; loans prepayable have been prepaid to avoid negative carry; net cash position ~$550 million
