So, if we look at it and the standard depreciation over a long period of time is approximately 3% of rupee versus dollar. So, we have got a 5% spread in the interest cost and where you could lose 3% due to depreciation, so you are better off by 2%.

items.statement: Dividend paid in H1 FY26 was Rs.180 crores vs Rs.282 crores in H1 FY25 due to lower profits and timing; dividend based on current quarter profitability and retention needs

items.quote: We have received a couple of high-value orders both from the European and Latin American markets. And I am happy to say that, though it is a new business for us, it is already a profitable business.

items.statement: Net working capital reduced by over INR 108 crore from Dec '24 peak; working capital days increased due to higher Sep '24 base in 12-month average calculation
items.quote: overall net working capital has reduced by over INR 108 crore from the peak of December '24 due to improved net working capital management.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR 338 crore (Mar '25) to INR 181 crore (Sep '25); net cash position of INR 111 crore achieved; finance cost meaningfully reduced
items.quote: Gross debt decreased from INR 338 crore in March '25 to INR 181 crore, as on September '25. This has helped in meaningful reduction of finance cost.

items.statement: INR 157 crore debt repaid in H1 FY26 fully funded through internal accruals; operating cash flow before tax INR 390 crore (123% EBITDA conversion)
items.quote: During the first half of the year, we repaid INR 157 crore of debt, fully funded through internal accruals. Operating cash flows before tax stood at INR 390 crore, translating to a robust 123% conversion of operating EBITDA to cash flow.

items.statement: Will consider improving shareholder payouts if company continues to perform well, after funding growth capex and international expansion from internal accruals
items.quote: if the Company continues to perform well, which we are confident, we would definitely look at further improving our payout to the shareholders.

items.statement: Actively looking at acquisition opportunities to expand international presence for value-added products and services; nothing on table currently
items.quote: we would definitely look at opportunities to further increase our presence in the international markets for value-added offerings. But nothing is on the table at the moment.

items.statement: Wire Rope EBITDA per ton ~INR 55,000; Steel Wire EBITDA per ton ~INR 10,000 (stable); Wire volume target 100,000 tons over 2-3 years
items.quote: whereas for ropes, the value-added is much higher, - upwards of INR 55,000 per ton.

items.statement: US tariffs largely passed through to end customers with minimal margin impact; overall price levels up but margins maintained
items.quote: The tariffs have largely been passed through to the end customers. So, what is happening in the end market is, the overall price levels have gone up, but it has minimally impacted our margins.

items.statement: European competition intense from European and Korean players; One Usha Martin integration with BSUK and direct India shipments improving competitiveness and lead times
items.quote: the competition is equally there with all the European and the Korean players. We all work in the same market. And the intensity is always there.

items.statement: Well positioned with approvals and product offerings for India's shipbuilding, port expansion, and inland waterways initiatives
items.quote: we are fully geared with all the approvals as well as the entire product offerings to be able to serve to these customers.

items.statement: LRPC volumes impacted by extended monsoon slowing infrastructure; project-based plasticated LRPC deliveries dependent on project execution timelines
items.quote: these are highly dependent on how fast the projects are getting executed. It is not a standard LRPC product, which gets fairly, it is project-specific based.

items.statement: Global market demand uncertainty affects volume growth outlook; capability ready but uptake dependent on international market conditions
items.quote: a lot of it also depends on how the global markets pan out in the coming quarters. We are optimistic but let us see as the global situation improves.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% revenue and profit growth for full year FY26
items.quote: Looking at the opportunities from all this explained above, Batliboi is targeting revenue growth of 10% to 12% in both top-line and bottom-line for the entire year.

items.statement: Order backlog reached INR621.44 crore as of September 2025
items.quote: As of September 2025, our order backlog was approximately INR621.44 crore compared to INR490.29 crore at the end of Q1 and on a comparative basis of Q2, INR412 crore of the last year.

items.statement: Targets order inflow of over INR1,000 crore for full year FY26
items.quote: we are pretty confident that when we are sa ying that we will be crossing INR1,000 crores based on today's overall inquiry levels that we have in each and every division, we are pretty confident that we will be crossing INR1,000 crores for the whole year FY 2025 -2026

items.statement: Gross margins expected to remain stable at 38-40% range despite Q2 improvement to 43%
items.quote: our standard guidelines that we had given earlier still hold good, okay? There could be increases in one quarter. There could be slight dips in the next quarter. But overall, our margins will remain stable right through the year.

items.statement: Gross margin regime expected to stay stable, not improve substantially beyond current levels
items.quote: I don't think the gross margin will improve anything substantially more than this. And as I mentioned that our gross margins also depend on product mix. So looking at the way the business is, I would say that we would have a pretty stable gross margin regime.

items.statement: Planning capital expenditure of INR8 crore for expansion in second half of FY26
items.quote: We are now planning for the capital profit of INR8 crore as a part of our expansion for the balanced part of the year.

items.statement: Textile sector faces challenges from US tariffs, EU demand recession, and Bangladesh political uncertainty
items.quote: The textile sector continues to face challenges due to the tariff issues with USA, the demand recession in EU countries partly caused by the Russian -Ukraine conflict and the ongoing political uncertainty in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering division expects big-ticket orders of INR15-20 crore each in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: (So, we have a very strong lead, and those orders are big ticket value orders of something around INR15 crores, INR20 crores each. So, that division is pursuing some very potential prospects, and we expect those order bookings to happen in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Export focus expanding to Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Indonesia, Uzbekistan, Egypt) and Gulf region for Quickmill
items.quote: We are also focusing in, which I think we have put in the presentation somewhere that we are looking at Vietnam, we are looking at Indonesia. We have got a breakthrough order in Indonesia, we are likely to get a breakthrough order in Vietnam in this quarter, the next quarter. We are also pursuing some orders in Uzbekistan. And we have lined up with LMW for all the requirements for the region. And

items.statement: Actively searching for suitable acquisitions in capital goods space to add value to current business lines
items.quote: as we had mentioned earlier when we did the fundraise that we'd be looking at also inorganic growth. So we are co nstantly on the search for suitable acquisitions, which could add value to our current business lines, which is primarily in the field of capital goods

items.statement: No management changes planned but continuously recruiting talented people as additions
items.quote: We don't foresee any management change, but we are always on the lookout for talented people. Okay. So, recruitment will always be there of talented people, but not as a replacement, but as an addition.

items.statement: Bioconserve Renewables (ZLD subsidiary) profitable in Q2, expects reasonable profit for full year, focusing on textile sector first
items.quote: Our new subsidiary, Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited, which is in the field of zero liqui d discharge had again a profitable quarter and expects to end the year with reasonable profits

items.statement: Green hydrogen business pursuing small plant orders (pharma, chemicals) with 2-3 leads expected to close in Q3 or early Q4
items.quote: we are pursuing small time orders and we've got some two -three leads, which we hope that we should be closing in either Q3 or start of Q4, a small step in that direction.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering commenced manufacturing critical fans at Surat factory, will ramp up production in coming quarters
items.quote: This division h as now commenced manufacturing of critical fans in our own factory in Surat and will continue to ramp -up production in the coming quarters and years

items.statement: Air Engineering revenue INR18 crore, order inflow INR14.63 crore; Textile Machinery order inflow INR180.85 crore, order booking INR92 crore
items.quote: The Air Engineering group reported revenue of INR18 crores in this quarter accompanied by an improved order inflow of INR14.63 crores which was again as per the business forecast given in the previous presentation. The Text ile Machinery group had an order inflow of INR180.85 crores compared to INR167.39 crores in Q1 and also our order decision of INR92 crores as compared to INR60 crores in Q1

items.statement: Environmental Engineering inflow INR33.2 crore, revenue INR33.3 crore with healthy order backlog
items.quote: The Environmental Engineering group re ported an inflow of INR33.2 crores and revenue of INR33.3 crores in this quarter which is again as per the forecast given in our earlier presentation. And with a healthy order back for this division, we expect an improved performance for the balanced full year

items.statement: Government policy support (Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, PLI) strengthening domestic manufacturing landscape
items.quote: With policy support from initiatives like Make -in-India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and the production link incentive scheme, the domestic manufacturing landscape is steadily gaining strength.

items.statement: Order backlog conversion timeline varies by division from one month to one year, confident execution within a year
items.quote: it can range from lead time to conversion can vary from one month to one year, depending on the kind of business we are in. So, it would be difficult to forecast exactly when this pending order backlog of INR600 odd crores would get executed, but confidently within a year, it should get executed.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around Rs 1,000 crore as guided earlier
items.quote: CAPEX for the quarter was at Rs. 267 crore and is expected to be around Rs. 1,000 crore for the year FY26, as guided earlier, reflecting continued capital discipline

items.statement: FY27 capex will be substantially lower than Rs 1,000 crore
items.quote: So capex for next year will be substantially lower than INR1,000 crore. We do not have the right number. We are still yet to work out the numbers, but it will be substantially lower.

items.statement: EBITDA surged 36% QoQ to Rs 292 crore driven by improved capacity utilization and cost optimization
items.quote: EBITDA surged to Rs. 292 crore, marking a 36% quarter-on-quarter increase, primarily fuelled by improved capacity utilization and ongoing cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Margin improvement predominantly driven by operating leverage, contribution margins consistent across portfolio
items.quote: The margin's improvement was predominantly driven by operating leverage. At a contribution level, if you see at the overall product portfolio level, we remain quite consistent on the contribution margin level.

items.statement: Cost optimization benefits of Rs 150-200 crore: actions completed but 40-50% yet to flow through, renewable PPAs commissioning April 2026
items.quote: There is a lot of benefit yet to flow through, especially one of the major items there was around sort of renewable power purchase agreements. A large chunk of it is expected to get commissioned only in April 2026.

items.statement: MMA achieved highest-ever quarterly volumes driven by spillover demand and geographic diversification
items.quote: MMA delivered strong performance in Q2 and achieved highest-ever quarterly volumes, driven by spill-over demand from Q1 as well as diversification efforts to various geographies where initial customer response was encouraging.

items.statement: Agrochemicals showing promising volume recovery but margins under pressure; Dyes & Pigments demand muted; Polymer business hit by US tariffs
items.quote: In Agrochemicals, select products are showing promising volume recovery, although overall margins remain under pressure. Demand growth in the Dyes & Pigments segment has been muted. items.statement: Fluoro products margins challenged by aggressive competitive pricing from China
items.quote: Overall, margins for the company's high value fluoro products are experiencing notable challenges due to aggressive competitive pricing from China.

items.statement: MMA faces competitive pricing challenges from China and domestic Indian players

items.statement: US tariffs eroding competitiveness vs European and Chinese suppliers; export mix rebalanced toward Europe, Middle East, Africa
items.quote: The tariff represents a near-term headwind for the Indian chemical sector, temporarily eroding competitiveness against European as well as Chinese suppliers to an extent. In response to the steep tariffs imposed by the United States, we also took steps to diversify and rebalance our export mix, towards Europe, the Middle East, and Africa

items.statement: US share of business significantly lower in Q2 vs Q1; volumes offset by push in other geographies; no revenue loss as volumes actively placed elsewhere
items.quote: Our share of U.S. business in the last quarter was significantly lower compared to Q1. So there was definitely a pain. I t was offset by a push in the other geographies. But potentially to the level where we have already reached, the further downside sort of can be arrested

items.statement: MMA at peak utilization of newly expanded capacities; debottlenecking initiatives to scale volumes further from Q4 FY26
items.quote: On Capacities front, while we have achieved peak utilisation of the newly expanded capacities for MMA, we are in the process of executing various debottlenecking initiatives which will support us to scale up our volumes further from Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Calcium Chloride facility expected to commission in Q3 FY26; new MPP in Zone 4 expected Q4 FY26; 4,000 TPA PEDA project in Zone 4 to commission; 5 incremental blocks in Zone 4 to commission sequentially through FY27

items.statement: Strategic plan targets energy segment 30-40% share in 2-2.5 years; Agro, polymer, pharma shares to inch up
items.quote: We feel energy will remain in kind of 30% to 40% range and the share of Agro, polymer specifically, these two end-applications, along with a little bit of pharma will inch up as we execute on our strategic plans.

items.statement: Long-term strategic partnership with DCM Shriram as exclusive chlorine supplier for Zone 4 downstream chemicals facility
items.quote: During the quarter under review, we also entered into a long-term strategic partnership with DCM Shriram who will serve as the exclusive supplier of chlorine from its Chlor-Alkali plant to our upcoming downstream chemicals facility at Zone 4.

items.statement: Suspected 100+ kt MMA capacity in India and 200-300 kt in China; not reflected in competitor volumes yet
items.quote: We suspect there is sort of another 100-plus kt capacity available in India and maybe 200 to 300 kt capacity available in China. Though that is not reflected in the volumes from competition, but that is the kind of capacity that could be available.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Pretilachlor supports PEDA value chain play; India imports DEA, PEDA, and Pretilachlor at three stages
items.quote: If you look at the entire value chain because India imports 3 different stages of value chain in this particular product, right? We import D EA, we import PEDA, we also import Pretilachlor

items.statement: Working capital cycle stable at 45-50 days; receivables up 65% due to higher export share (60%+) with longer credit terms; inventory days reduced
items.quote: If I combine on an overall working capital basis, the working capital cycle continues to remain at the level what it was. It continues to remain in the range of around 45, 50-odd days. The receivable plus inventory continues to operate at a similar level.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA potentially peaked; focus on medium-scale capex with fast turnaround to manage balance sheet
items.quote: We actually think from a debt-to-EBITDA point of view, we potentially could have already seen the peak. Absolute debt numbers are important. But for us, I think what we track more is debt-to-EBITDA. And I think on that front, we feel that we could have potentially already seen the peak now, and it should improve going forward.

items.statement: FY27 tax rate anticipated below 15%; FY28 between 15-20%
items.quote: On the tax rate, I anticipate FY '27, we should be somewhere at a number below 15%. And FY '28, we should be between 15% to 20%. That is a rough estimate right now.

items.statement: US tariff mitigation levers limited: proactive customer conversations to share burden, and strategic levers for products re-exported from US
items.quote: To be honest, relatively limited things that we can do at an organization level. I think the only couple of levers that have worked for us, and we continue to push that is sort of having the proactive conversations with customers to ensure that the relationship remains intact and the business remains intact where both sides have to compromise to some extent

items.statement: Revenue Rs 2,250 crore, up 21% QoQ driven by improved volumes across key product categories
items.quote: Revenue stood at Rs. 2,250 crore, an increase of 21% Q-o-Q driven by improved volumes across key product categories.

items.statement: PAT Rs 106 crore, up ~150% QoQ reflecting improved operating leverage and exceptional items
items.quote: As a result, Profit After Tax was Rs. 106 crore, an increase of about 150% Q-o-Q, reflecting improved operating leverage and after factoring in the exceptional items that you may have seen in our published financial results.

items.statement: No take-or-pay contracts for upcoming Zone 4 projects; active customer conversations give confidence but no committed offtake agreements
items.quote: We have moved past that industry phase to be very honest. I think there are very rare instances where these are kind of back-to-back customer committed with take-or-pay kind of contract kind of commitments projects.

items.statement: CDMO efforts: 3-4 projects at R&D level with global innovators; 18-24 month journey to convert to large-scale manufacturing
items.quote: As we speak, we are doing sort of 3 or 4 projects, which are at R&D level. So I think the focus remains on building relationships with global innovators and trying to get involved in the very early part of a development cycle.

items.statement: Zone 4 blocks include photochlorination, hydrolysis, nitration chemistry blocks; designed for flexible product optimization based on margin and demand-supply profiles
items.quote: Beyond that, the blocks are sort of chemistry-oriented blocks without getting into too much technicals, but it is kind of a photochlorination block, hydrolysis block, nitration block and so on. These are the kind of chemistry blocks, which allow us to make any product using that particular type of reactions.

items.statement: Targets 15% consolidated EBITDA margin by end of FY27 (H2 FY27 run rate)
items.quote: If we achieved all the volumes in FY27 as promised, then at least towards the end of FY27, we should start hitting that run rate of 15%, that is what we target internally.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue growth in FY27 if salicylic acid ramp-up succeeds
items.quote: If everything goes well, then we can try for 15%-20% growth for next year.

items.statement: Targets high single-digit value growth for H2 FY26
items.quote: For the H2, we will definitely aim towards, high single digit value growth for H2 FY26.

items.statement: Tax rate expected at ~25% for FY27
items.quote: For the next three years, it should be ideally in the range of 25%.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at Rs.150-200 crore; similar amount possible in FY27 for Metformin expansion
items.quote: we estimate around Rs. 150-200 crores of CAPEX investing cash flows in this particular year. A.M. Lodha: Total Rs.200 crores? Adhish Patil: Total Rs.200 crores. And we have some expansion plans for Metformin as well for next year. If everything goes smoothly, then we might require around that much similar kind of investment in

items.statement: Sayakha methylamine plant (60 TPD, scalable to 80 TPD) started commercial production Sep 4, 2025; 40-50% captive needs met, targeting 100% by end FY26
items.quote: the total Methylam ine plant is around 60 TPD. We can scale it up to 80 TPD as well. Yes, that is the Methylamine capacity

items.statement: Salicylic acid Tarapur plant targeting 300 tpm near-term, 500 tpm by Q4 FY26, EBITDA positive at ~800 tpm
items.quote: Production visibility is improving with 300 tons per month achievable in the near-term and a targeted ramp-up to 500 tons per month for Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Pinnacle Life Science to commercialize Bicalutamide in US this quarter and anti-diabetic products in Europe/UK in 6-9 months, adding Rs.60-70 crore revenue
items.quote: We will be commercializing first product in US in this quarter, which is Bicalutamide, and we are also expecting to commercialize a few anti-diabetic products in Europe, UK and other regulated markets, ex-US, between the next six to nine months. items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin just crossed 13% in Q2 FY26 despite Rs.3.5 crore salicylic acid losses and Sayakha start-up costs
items.quote: on a standalone basis, we already just crossed 13%, not too much, just you can say 13%. So, a couple of percent, we still see no doubt, we are still absorbing around Rs.3.5 crores of losses in salicylic acid , p lus, we just commercialized our Sayakha plant for just one month

items.statement: Sayakha project expected to deliver 18-20% EBITDA margin at full capacity
items.quote: At least, we should try to make around 18% to 20% EBITDA margins is what we feel from this Sayakha project.

items.statement: Domestic antibiotic demand weak in Q2 FY26; slight de-growth of couple of percent; recovery expected from Q4 FY26
items.quote: In the antibiotic category, we did face issues in few of the products. Now, Q3 is typically a lean quarter anyways for the acute therapy. So, we hope that from Q4 onwards, there should be some slight pickup in the domestic demand.

items.statement: Export demand robust with >30% volume growth in API exports in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Export did fantastic; we had more than 30% volume growth in exports.

items.statement: Global API pricing showing early signs of stability, supporting volume growth and price recovery in H2 FY26
items.quote: We are also witnessing early signs of stability in global API pricing, which should support both volume growth and price recovery in H2 FY26.

items.statement: Raw material price decline stopped 9-12 months ago; volatility reduced, improving gross margins
items.quote: now that the decline has stopped since last nine to 12 months, the decline is so less, now the volatility has gone down. And because the volatility has g one down, the true margins of the products are now coming down

items.statement: Received voluntary closure direction from MPCB for chlorosulfonation at Tarapur T-150 after HCL gas leak on Sep 8, 2025; no material impact
items.quote: During the quarter, we also received a voluntary closure direction from the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board for the chlorosulfonation process at our Tarapur T-150 unit following an isolated HCL gas leakage incident on September 8, 2025.

items.statement: Pursuing EU certifications for key products to shift production to lower-cost facilities and expand export margins
items.quote: We are in the process to receive EU certifications for several key products from our large-scale plants, allowing us to ship EU-registered products to lower-cost facilities and thereby expand export margins.

items.statement: Targeting US Metformin entry post FY26 after validation completion
items.quote: We are targeting Metformin in the US market post FY26 once ongoing validation processes are completed, an important milestone in our plan to re-enter the regulated market with higher-margin products.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced by Rs.41 crore to Rs.571 crore in H1 FY26; debt-to-equity 0.39; target D/E 0.4-0.7
items.quote: The total debt during H1 FY26 also reduced by Rs.41 crores to Rs.571 crores in total, leading to a reduction in our finance costs and a record low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.39.

items.statement: Company maintains 25-30% PAT payout as dividends; will continue dividend policy
items.quote: What we believe here is that we do give around 25% to 30% of our PAT back to shareholders every year, year-on-year. So, with that kind of shareholder payout in mind and with the higher ROE target, we like to maintain the debt-to-equity ratio at 0.4 to 0.7.

items.statement: API segment mix: antibiotic 36.1%, anti-diabetic 15.3%, anti-protozoal 18.8%, anti-inflammatory 11.8%, anti-fungal 11.7%, others 6.4%
items.quote: Within the A PI business, the antibiotic -therapeutic cat egory contributed 36.1%, anti -diabetic around 15.3%, anti -protozoal 18.8%, anti -inflammatory 11.8%, anti -fungal 11.7% and the rest contributed 6.4% to total API

items.quote: Revenues from formulation stood at Rs.82.4 crores in Q2 FY26 compared to Rs.65.6 crores in Q2 FY25, up 26% year-on-year basis. Exports contributed 68% to this revenue.

items.statement: Salicylic acid product quality now widely accepted; sold to majority of Indian salicylic acid customers

items.statement: Sayakha side-chain products: two secured via captive consumption and group company sale; third seeing good market acceptance
items.quote: Two products are already secured because of captive consumption, second, because of group company sale, and the third one, we are seeing very good acceptance in the market.

items.statement: Salicylic acid ramp-up speed is key risk to FY27 growth and margin targets
items.quote: key challenge will remain would be the r amp up of salicylic acid. If that happens very quickly and very successfully, then it would be that much easier to achieve those numbers

items.statement: Solar JV with Prozeal Green Power underway to reduce power cost and carbon footprint
items.quote: The upcoming solar project being developed through our JV with Prozeal Green Power is an important step towards reducing our pow er cost and carbon footprint while supporting our long - term sustainability commitments

items.statement: H9N2 vaccine sales to begin post-manufacturing license receipt (anticipated December FY26)
items.quote: sales of avian influenza vaccine are expected to begin post -receipt of our ma nufacturing license, which we anticipate by December

items.quote: we are in process of also working towards launching our lumpy skin, but that's going to take some time. It's going to happen in the middle of the next financial year.

items.statement: Africa operations to achieve breakeven by FY28
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve breakeven in our Africa operations by FY '28 as mentioned earlier.

items.quote: we anticipate the pickup in the activity in the large part of the year, particularly in Q4 as execution time lines normalize

items.quote: Our stand alone divisional product sales for Q2 stood at INR 64 crores, making a 12% decline over the sa me quarter last year. For H1 FY26, the sales were at INR128 crores, also down by 13

items.quote: We saw a 50% degrowth in Q2 and a 41% decline in H1, largely due to the delay in the government-led immunization program for PPR and Lumpy Skin Disease.

items.statement: Poultry Healthcare division Q2 FY26 growth 18%; H1 FY26 growth 10% (volume-led)
items.quote: The Poultry Healthcare division remained to be on a positive trajectory, recording an 18% growth in Q2 and 10% growth in H1. This growth was largely a volume-led.

items.statement: Consolidated international division sales INR155 crore (7% degrowth YoY)
items.quote: our consolidated division product sales stood at INR155 crores, marking a 7% degrowth over the previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated margins stable due to operational discipline and cost control
items.quote: a consolidated level, our margins remained stable, driven by operational discipline and cost control

items.statement: EBITDA and NPAT declined 13% and 15% YoY in H1 FY26 due to subdued topline
items.quote: Profitability was impacted cor respondingly with EBITDA NPAT declining by 13% and 15%, respectively, on an H1 basis

items.statement: Dairy sector growing at 5-6% annually; post-Lumpy Skin Disease outbreak, targeted solutions in vaccines and health products being introduced

items.statement: Pet Care segment showing better engagement; measurable growth expected in next few quarters

items.statement: Africa operations face uneven environment due to political and institutional order delays
items.quote: The overall environment in Africa remains uneven due to political and delays in institutional orders.

items.statement: Nepal Q2 FY26 net loss of INR1.1 crore due to timing of institutional orders and logistics disruptions
items.quote: reported a net loss of INR1.1 crores in Q2 though it maintained a profit of INR0.8 crores for H1 on a top line of INR0.5 crores and INR5.6 crores, respectively. The quarter was impacted by the timing of institutional orders and temporary disturbances in Nepal during August

items.statement: Management expects to maintain growth momentum in H2 FY26 supported by festive season and e-commerce demand

items.statement: Demand stable across key segments e-commerce, pharma, manufacturing driving steady cargo movement

items.quote: In Q2 FY '26, we handle a total cargo volume of 15,393 tons, comprising 13,195 tons of domestic cargo and 2,198 tons of international cargo.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 blended realization Rs 59.24 per kg; H1 FY26 Rs 58.22 per kg

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA Rs 5 crore up 2.3% YoY margin 2.61%; PAT Rs 4 crore up 8% YoY margin 2.27%

items.statement: Pune land acquisition not yet concluded; evaluating ROI before proceeding
items.quote: We were in the process of acquiring the land, I agree with you, but we have not still acquired the land till now. We are in the process of discussing and all this one because we want to be an ROI driven company as well.

items.statement: Navi Mumbai airport cargo terminal 0.5M tons initial capacity scalable to 3.25M tons; Jewar airport 0.25M tons initial capacity
items.quote: We include a dedicated cargo terminal with an initial handling capacity of around 0.5 million tons, scalable to about 3.25 million tons in later phases.

And if that increase, the number of airports from 140 airport to 220 airport also increase, definitely that is the roadmap for us.

items.statement: Partnership discussions underway with larger logistics companies; expects to share news soon
items.quote: Yes, it is there, but unfortunately, I cannot divulge, but we are just in the process. Very soon I will share the news with you.

items.statement: Receivables increase due to higher turnover not aging deterioration; debtor quality maintained conservatively
items.quote: Look, this is actually look like closing number because the turnover increase now. As you can see a turnover increase. So, that a closin g number sometimes get skewed and you can see in the quarter end some numbers have increased. But it is not that the aging has increased or something like that

items.statement: Company is net debt-free with cash and equivalents over Rs 20 crore; no working capital issues
items.quote: So, luckily, just to give you first a nswer, we are a net debt -free company now. So, as you can see in our balance sheet also, that more than Rs. 20 crore is reflecting in the balance sheet. So, there is no working capital issue as such

items.statement: GST cut on 22 Sept for 9 days; full impact visibility by Q3 FY26; aviation fuel under GST needed for structural cost reduction
items.quote: Look, yes, there was on the 22nd September, the GST cut for the product and all this one. So, it was basically, as you can see, it is not for the this quarter, last quarter, it will not be fully reflected. It was only for nine days. But we can see, we will be able to more understand now the numbers, we are gathering numbers also for the October month and as well. So, from there, we will get a m or

items.statement: Competition viewed positively as motivation; strong brand since 1959; not unduly concerned about competitive pressure
items.quote: Competition pressure will be there. It is good for us, to be honest with you, we will love to have a competition because that gives us more motivation and driven. At the same time, we are a company which is, as you know, 1959 old company. And in our area of operation, we carry a good brand, visibility and everything. So, we are not undue bother about any competitive pressure as such.

items.statement: Digital platform processes nearly all bookings and deliveries; proprietary receivable control software; direct system integration with British Airways for Canada-regulated cargo
items.quote: Now, nearly all bookings and deliveries are now processed digitally, improving turnaround time and ensu ring transparency across the supply chain. Just to add up in this, we have developed a receivable software also which controls the human receivables to the system apart from the human intervention, women monitoring as well, which in our industry is very well recognized

items.statement: Dividend paid Rs 2.09 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: dividend paid to the shareholders of Rs. 2,08,00,000 crores, in fact, rounding thing up to Rs. 2,09,00,000.

items.statement: Sales down 34% in Agri and 33% in Building Material in Q2 FY26 due to heavy extended rains in core markets
items.quote: Sales are down 34% in Agri and 33% in building material.

items.statement: Expect substantial improvement in top line and bottom line in next year from current initiatives
items.quote: I can only assure you that going forward in the next year, you will see a substantial impact both on the top line and bottom line for whatever initiatives we are taking now.

items.statement: Market showing positive revival signs post-Diwali after extended rains through October
items.quote: But post-Diwali, I think now things are where the monsoon is over. So, everyone was anticipating that from November 6th, 7th, that is last three, four days, the market has started showing positive signs of revival.

items.statement: PVC resin prices stable, no inventory losses from price fluctuation in Q2
items.quote: Resin prices were more or less stable. So, there are no inventory losses here on this account.

items.statement: Per unit realization improved by selling right and appropriate products despite volume decline
items.quote: However, the general realization part, we have definitely improved on per unit basis by selling the right and appropriate products in the market.

items.statement: No market share lost in core geographies MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra; market volumes declined
items.quote: Our first level of study clearly suggests that the areas that is MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, where we are dominant, present, we have not lost market share and market volumes have declined.

items.statement: Estimated market share gain of 5-7% in core markets; MP share estimated at 58-59% from ~50%
items.quote: Particularly last quarter and we are still estimating. You see, I cannot give you exact numbers today but general feeling is that we must have gained say 5% to 7% generally everywhere. That is the estimation as of now.

items.statement: Building material market share insignificant currently, building from scratch in Maharashtra
items.quote: Agri, we will have a reasonable market share, but it will be around 10%, 11%, 12%. DP we have very insignificant market share as of now. We are building from a scratch, so it takes time.

items.statement: Rs 67-68 crores deployed out of Rs 75 crores received from warrant conversion; further capex planned sequentially
items.quote: Out of about Rs. 75 crores, we have already, I would say about Rs. 67 crores, Rs. 68 crores would have been deployed.

items.statement: Professional CEO in place with structured management team including vertical heads and regional in-charges
items.quote: Yes. Professional CEO in place.

items.statement: Agriculture and building material sectors projected to grow for next 6-7 years
items.quote: Even all the projections and studies, they suggest that India on both Agriculture, irrigation, as well as on building material will continue to grow at least for the coming foreseeable six, seven years.

items.statement: Positive demand prospects for agriculture with good rains and full water bodies; building material cycle to improve next year
items.quote: Agriculture, with the kind of rains and good crop we are seeing across, we see quite positive demand prospects going forward.

items.statement: Q2 revenue Rs 86 crores down 27% YoY; EBITDA loss Rs 4 crores vs profit Rs 5 crores; net loss Rs 10 crores
items.quote: The revenue for the quarter stood at approximately INR 86 crores reflecting a 27% decrease on a Y-O-Y basis. At the EBITDA level, the company reported a loss of INR 4 crores compared to a profit of INR 5 crores in the corresponding period last year. The net loss for the quarter was around INR 10 crores.

items.statement: H1 revenue Rs 310 crores down 17% YoY; EBITDA Rs 11 crores at 3.55% margin; net loss Rs 2.4 crores
items.quote: For the first half of the financial year, the revenue stood at INR 310 crores, a decline of 17% on a Y-O-Y basis. While EBITDA stood at around INR 11 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 3.55%. At the PAT level, the company reported a loss of INR 2.4 crores.

items.statement: New geographies being developed but take time to mature; sequential expansion plan with triggers
items.quote: We are already working in new geographies, they take time to mature. And as such, when the good rains are, it means that water bodies are full. So, going forward for this next, I mean, up to summer, if there is an adequate supply of water for the farmland, we hope that the demand would be fairer and better than what it has been because normally there is a shortage of water, it would impact the irr

items.statement: No immediate change in brand positioning seen; all major players present in MP for many years
items.quote: We do not see any immediate change in any positioning of any brand. But you see, market is dynamic. You have to be always alert and keep making efforts in the right way and right direction.

items.statement: MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat constitute 30-35% of India's agri-pipe demand; Maharashtra largest
items.quote: MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Gujarat put together will constitute about 30% to 35% of overall demand of India.

items.statement: Unprecedented widespread rains from May to October impacted both Agri and Building Material sales beyond anticipation
items.quote: We were not prepared for heavy and extended rains in our main Agri sales areas and its impact on both top line and bottom line is beyond our anticipation.

items.statement: Revenue grew 171% YoY in Q2 FY26 driven by execution across both Hi-Tech and Engineering segments
items.quote: For Q2, for this current fiscal, our revenue has grown by 171% year -over-year. The strong growth has been driven by execution across both our segments.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 19.7% in Q2 FY26 from operating leverage and improved mix
items.quote: EBITDA was Rs. 31 crores against Rs. 7 crores, with margins at 19.7%, supported by operating leverage and an improved mix.

items.statement: FY26 CAPEX expected at Rs. 30-35 crores minimum, may increase based on land allotment for MoU projects
items.quote: during the 25-26, CAPEX addition will be another Rs. 30-Rs. 35 crores, the minimum what we are expecting. And it may go up depending on whatever the MoU time.

items.statement: MoU facilities in Karnataka (Rs. 510 cr) and Tamil Nadu (Rs. 250 cr) expected operational in 18-24 months after land acquisition
items.quote: timeline-wise, it will be about the next 18 -24 months is what we are planning once the land is acquired.

items.statement: MoU CAPEX funding to be combination of accruals, debt, potential equity, and government incentives
items.quote: Funding will be a combination of accrual, combination of some debt and if needed some additional equity. And we also have some potential incentives both from the central government and different state governments.

items.statement: Central government offers ~25% CAPEX incentives, state governments additional ~25%, applications being finalized
items.quote: there is about 25% which is publicly announced by the central government. And at the state government level, there is an additional 25%.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 80-85%, new Karnataka facility expected ready by end December or early January
items.quote: the capacity utilization is currently about 80 %-85%. So, similar growth we are expecting in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Employee count slightly over 2,000 with ~40% in Manufacturing/DLM and ~60% in ER&D, ratio expected to remain 60:40 or 50:50
items.quote: we are a little over 2,000 people, right , broadly at a very high level. And in the 2,000 people, about 40% would be what we call Manufacturing, that is DLM and people who are full-time supporting DLM.

items.statement: Total addressable market estimated at $40 billion annually out of $130-140 billion global market in served segments
items.quote: If you take the total addressable market which is available to us across all our sectors, it is somewhere about, say, annually. And this is a global requirement. It is not necessarily India. It would be at least about $40 billion per annum

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute ~60% of overall revenue, some customers use both DLM and ER&D services
items.quote: broadly, 60% is from 10 customers. That is what we can share. Individually, number 1 or number 3 or the top 3 will be difficult. So, 60% would be from top 10 customers.

items.statement: DLM revenue growing rapidly, ER&D being used to support DLM expansion, pivot from pure ER&D to DLM ongoing for 8 years
items.quote: we are very progressively moving into DLM. I think that momentum will continue. We will be having more and more DLM. That is where all our bigger investments are going in.

items.statement: Large MoU CAPEX to be deployed in 3 phases with revenue recognized incrementally as each phase completes
items.quote: in terms of incremental on the larger ones, they will definitely be in phases. We will be probably doing it across 3 phases. And as each phase is implemented, the revenue will be accredited.

items.statement: Solar JV (ASM-HHV) has separate plant expected ready in few months, deliveries expected later this year or early next year
items.quote: we have a separate plant. It should be in place in the next few months as a separate plant for that. And we expect some of the deliveries to happen later this year or definitely early part of next year.

items.statement: Operating in semiconductor equipment for 20 years, pivoting from ER&D to DLM, expect industry to scale with more players entering
items.quote: we have been working in this segment for many years, for about 20 years. It is just that we pivoted from pure ER&D to DLM. So, industry-wise, business-wise, is not new to us

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment life cycle 15-25 years with refresh/upgrade opportunities, consumer electronics 1-1.5 years, industrial 5-8 years
items.quote: If you take semiconductors, it is a very long-life cycle, it would be 15, 20, 25 years. But in that long life cycle , there is a lot of refreshment, there is a lot of upgrade, there is a lot of opportunity during that long life cycle.

items.statement: No differentiation between export and domestic supply to global majors; revenue recognized based on customer entity not shipment geography
items.quote: we don't differentiate whether export or we domestically supply to any of these global majors within India and whether they use it in India or take it wherever in the world, we do not really differentiate too much.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment manufacturing not yet happening in India, but global customer equipment coming to India with local support from ASM
items.quote: some of our customer ’s equipment are in India and will continue to come back into India on the investment which is going on in India right now

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs. 77 crores as of September 2025
items.quote: CAPEX for the half-year stood at about Rs. 11 crores, and the net cash position was Rs. 77 crores as of September 2025.

items.statement: MoU CAPEX execution dependent on government land allotment and incentive finalization
items.quote: We are in discussion with the Government for the allotment of the land. If the land comes through, this CAPEX will go up depending on the allotment of the land.

items.statement: Actively hiring senior management in India and internationally for both segments, design/engineering heavy DLM requires specialized talent
items.quote: Strategically, we are hiring both in India and outside of India. And we continue to do so in both our segments. And again, like I said, we are very design and engineering heavy for the DLM.

items.statement: Growth from existing customers (new geographies, product lines) and new customers across both verticals
items.quote: With the existing customers, w e are always looking to, one, go to new geographies, also going to new product lines, because many of our customers are large customers across both our verticals. So, it is also geography, additional product lines and new customers.

items.statement: ER&D revenue growth expected in Q3-Q4 as fixed-bid projects complete acceptance
items.quote: some of these are fixed projects, so we will hope to finish them in the early part of Q3. So, some of those revenues will reflect in Q3.

items.statement: New Karnataka facility similar to existing one, adding third facility in 12 months while larger MoU facilities progress
items.quote: we are adding one more facility in the next few months in Karnataka, which will be very similar to the one we already have. We should have that up and ready in the next couple of months to add to our capacity.

items.statement: Total order book of Rs 28,758 crore (net of taxes) for about 3.6 crore meters as of 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: As on 30th September 2025, the company had a total order book of INR 28,758 crores (net of taxes) for about 3.6 crore meters for supply to utilities, other AMISPs and to the joint venture Platform.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin improved 456 bps YoY to 21.3%; H1 FY26 margin at 21.2%
items.quote: EBITDA more than tripled year-on-year to Rs. 244 crores with margins improving 456 basis points to 21.3%.

items.statement: RDSS scheme envisages ~25 crore meters; 15 crore awarded, 10 crore pending; additional 5-6 crore from Karnataka/Telangana could take total to 30-31 crore
items.quote: The total meter requirement envisaged under RDSS scheme is approximately Rs. 25 crore meters, out of which Rs. 15 crore smart meters have already been awarded by different state utilities. And remaining Rs. 10 crore smart meters are broadly pending from states like Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Haryana, Delhi, putting a total number of Rs. 10 crores.

items.statement: New injection molding plant in Kotputli, Rajasthan with 40 machines expected operational by end of FY26
items.quote: Further, company is also setting up a new injection molding plant in Kotputli, Rajasthan. In first phase, we are willing to install 40 machines which are expected to be operational by end of FY26.

items.quote: As on 30th September 2025, the company had invested approximately INR 318 crores in the joint venture Platform and SPV of joint venture Platform with GIC. items.quote: Out of 24 AMISP projects which we are implementing, 13 projects totalling 2.10 crore meters have received Operational Go-Live (OGL) certificates from utilities. Remaining 11 projects are expected to achieve Operational Go-Live status in the December 2025-January 2026 timeframe.

items.statement: Maintaining ~25% market share in smart metering; participate in all tenders; aim to maintain or improve share
items.quote: You have to understand it simply that currently we have been maintaining around 25% market share, and we definitely will try to maintain the same market share or even do better. But putting any number for the tendering business is very difficult. As business policy, we participate in each and every tender.

items.statement: Export business currently small but expect meaningful revenue in 2-3 years from strategic markets
items.quote: On the export market, Genus is working strategically in some markets. They take their own time. So, again, we have started working in some strategic markets, and you will see very meaningful numbers coming from the export business in the next two to three ye

items.statement: Latching relays sourced from both China and Indian manufacturers; no plans to manufacture in-house
items.quote: As Genus, we are not manufacturing latching relays. We are buying it from our suppliers. We don't intend to manufacture latching relays in the future also. Eshwar Arumugam: Are we buying it from China? Jitendra Agarwal: It is being imported from China also. It is being made in India also. There are multiple manufacturers based in India who are also supplying us latching relays

items.statement: Cash flow positive now expected in FY27 (delayed from FY26) due to high inventory needs across 24 projects with hundreds of sites
items.quote: Basically, cash flow positive may take some more time, what we were saying in FY26, because the projects have started and a lot of inventory is needed in that. So, put together, as I told in my opening remarks also,

items.statement: Smart meters under Category 1 manufacturing (>60% domestic value addition); Genus comfortably meets Make in India requirements
items.quote: Just to give you an understanding on this, smart meters is already in the Category 1 of manufacturing in India. So, more than 60% of the value addition has to happen in India. Smart meters are already in this category. And Genus, very comfortably, is part of this category being the largest meter manufacturer in the country.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth target of 15%-20% including defence revenue
items.quote: As we have already told that we are for a long-term growth of 15% - 20% and in long-term we are going to maintain it. So, the turnover of this year and the next financial year should be in that line only.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain around current 9.72% level
items.quote: This quarter we have cropped 9.72% and we hope margins to remain in the same space.

items.statement: Artillery shell division has demand visibility for 2-3 years with demand outstripping supply
items.quote: We have a visibility of almost next two years to three years. So, sale is not a question because demand is outstripping the supply.

items.statement: Rs. 400-500 crore capex planned for defence capacity expansion to 4 lakh shells plus missile/aerospace parts
items.quote: Sir, for that we are planning, the project should be almost Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 500 crores and it will be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: Artillery shell capacity to expand from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh shells per annum within next year
items.quote: We plan to expand this capacity to 4 lakhs shells within the next year.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube plant commissioned Jan 2025, targeting 70% utilization by March 2026, then 50,000 MT expansion at 80% utilization
items.quote: Hydraulic Tubes plan we had commissioned in January and it is likely that by this year end, by this financial year end, say March 26, it should ramp up to 70%. And we plan to raise the capacity to the next level of 50,000 once it gets 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Solar tracker tube segment targeting Rs. 500-600 crore revenue by FY27 with 7-8% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Over the coming year, we are targeting a revenue contribution of Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 600 crores from this segment alone.

items.statement: Defence subsidiary Goodluck Defence expects Rs. 100 crore revenue in FY26 and Rs. 300 crore in FY27
items.quote: In FY '26, we are expecting only Rs. 100 crore per revenue and in the next year, we are expecting the full revenue from this capacity, which should be almost Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Artillery shell business EBITDA margin revised upward to 30%-35% from earlier 20%-25% guidance
items.quote: Yes. This market is very dynamic, because everywhere war is going on, demand and supply, it is a perfect match. So, but when we have started, then now we are hoping that the margin should be in the range of 30% - 35% EBITDA.

items.statement: Solar tracker tube segment commands 7-8% EBITDA margin
items.quote: This segment, this solar segment. It is a rising sector and it commands EBITDA of 7% - 8%.

items.statement: Comfortable with long-term debt of Rs. 300-350 crore vs current Rs. 160 crore; Rs. 50-100 crore additional borrowing planned
items.quote: But as Mr. Bansal has said, we are at 160 today, and we are comfortable with Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores long-term debt.

items.statement: Defence subsidiary IPO under planning, timing to be decided; demerger not currently planned
items.quote: Sir, it is under planning. We will let you know nearer the time.

items.statement: Defence expansion includes artillery shells (1.5L to 4L), missile outer parts via ring rolling, and aerospace components for HAL/DRDO/Tata/Godrej
items.quote: First, we are increasing capacity from 1,50,000 to 4,00,000. Number two, we are putting some ring rollings and press, which will enable us to supply the outer parts of the missile and some aerospace parts.

items.statement: Artillery shell customers are mix of domestic and international; international customers have audited facilities
items.quote: Sir, it is a mix of domestic and international customers.

items.statement: Defence shell business working capital cycle of 45-60 days
items.quote: Basically, this is almost 45 days - 60 days is the cycle of capital in this aerospace, in this shell business.

items.statement: Defence shell business peak revenue Rs. 800 crore at 4 lakh shells; aerospace/missile parts peak Rs. 200 crore; total Rs. 1,000 crore by FY28
items.quote: What we are expecting from the shell business, we are expecting almost Rs. 800 crores. And from this aerospace and allied business, we are expecting almost Rs. 200 crores. So the total will be Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube realizations stable year-on-year despite lower volumes; specialized product with good demand
items.quote: No, absolutely not. Price may not have improved, but definitely it was not lower. It is our specialized product. And we had a good demand.

items.statement: H1 demand low due to monsoon; H2 expected better with government capex materialization and project execution pickup
items.quote: Demand, as far as demand is concerned, H1 was definitely low, but H2 as usual also, because it is a busy season, demand is good. Demand, we are having good orders.

items.statement: Met investment obligation under UP Nivesh MoU with Uttar Pradesh government
items.quote: In addition, we are proud to share that we have met our investment obligation under the UP Nivesh initiative, for which we had signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the government of Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Skill development, talent acquisition and retention remain core priorities as company modernizes and expands
items.quote: Skill development, talent acquisition and retention remain core priorities for us. As we modernize our infrastructure and expand into new product lines, we are continuously investing in our workforce to ensure that they are equipped with the right technical and leadership capabilities.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Russia-Ukraine, US tariffs, India-EU trade talks) creating uncertainty for export sentiment
items.quote: On the global front also, environment remains complex, geopolitical tensions continue to influence trade flows from the prolonged Russia-Ukraine conflict and tariff war all over the world.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with BrahMos Aerospace (BATL) and Axiscades on AMCA program; filed EOI for participation
items.quote: Our strategic partnership in Goodluck India Limited with BrahMos Aerospace Thiruvananthapuram Limited, BATL and Axiscades Technology Limited on the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft program is another important milestone. We have filed an expression of interest for participation in AMCA program focusing on enhancing India's aerospace capabilities.

items.statement: Interest costs marginally up due to increased current assets in H1; employee costs up due to increments and new hiring
items.quote: On financial front, our interest costs have marginally gone up due to increase in current assets during first half of half year as compared to previous year and date. Also, employees and salary benefits have increased due to annual increments and new recruitment as compared to previous year.

items.statement: CSR initiatives include medical support, meals for underprivileged, animal fodder, and educational assistance for economically weaker students
items.quote: Our initiatives include supporting medical establishments, providing meals for underprivileged, supplying fodder for animals and offering educational assistance to bright students from economically weaker backgrounds to help them pursue higher education and build their careers.

items.statement: Expects high single-digit growth in Q3 FY26, confident of double-digit if winter sustains; FY27 expected to be much better than FY26
items.quote: I'm definitely expecting close to double digit, but definitely high single digits is 100% on the cards.

items.statement: Strategic investments portfolio expected to grow at strong double-digit in H2 FY26
items.quote: In the second half, we expect the business to grow at even a higher rate than the first half, strong double digit.

items.statement: Rural demand showing good growth across categories, particularly shampoo sachets
items.quote: Recently, we have seen good demand coming up from the rural side for all our categories.

items.statement: Winter season started early and well across North, East, West and Central India
items.quote: Winter has set in exceedingly well across, particularly the North , Eastern and also the Western Central side.

items.statement: Gross margins stable at 71% in Q2 FY26; input costs under control, expects EBITDA and net margin expansion in Q3
items.quote: Gross margins remained stable at 71%, underscoring our cost discipline and input price stability.

items.statement: No input cost pressure, margins to improve in Q3 with high EBITDA and net margin growth
items.quote: Input side, there is absolutely no pressure. It's well under control. And margins are definitely going to improve.

items.statement: Winter loading deferred from September recovered in October, placing company on strong footing for H2
items.quote: October has witnessed a healthy rebound in trade sentiments with the deferred winter loading being recovered, placing us on a strong footing for the second half of the year.

items.statement: Reduced MRP by ~INR 250-260 crores across domestic portfolio after GST cut; 20% of portfolio via grammage increase, balance via price cuts
items.quote: Overall, we have seen almost only in Emami domestic business, the reduction on MRP is roughly INR260 crores.

items.statement: Non-GST impacted portfolio grew: Medico 8%, Zandu cough syrup 43%, Honey 36%, Zandu Care 17%; strategic investments up 16% YoY, 36% QoQ
items.quote: Excluding the GST rate affected categories, some of our non -GST rate impacted portfolio delivered encouraging growth with Medico range up by 8%, Zandu cough syrup by 43%, Honey by 36% and Zandu Care growing by 17%.

items.statement: Relaunched Kesh King as Kesh King Gold with Ayurveda plus science formulation (Gro Biotin, plant Omega 369); clinically tested claims
items.quote: We also recently undertook the strategic relaunch of Kesh King as Kesh King Gold based on deep consumer research, which revealed a shift in expectations.

items.statement: Smart and Handsome extended to 12 new products across categories; initial rollout in modern trade and e-commerce encouraging
items.quote: This quarter, we deepened that journey by launching 12 new products across different categories. Our initial rollout across modern trade and e-commerce platform has been encouraging.

items.statement: Kesh King faced significant challenge from science-backed D2C brands in hair fall category; reformulation addresses this
items.quote: Kesh King faced significantly challenge from the D2C brands, particularly for hair fall categories, okay? And most of the D2C brands are science packed.

items.statement: GST rate cut from 12%/18% to 5% across key FMCG categories; 88% of core domestic portfolio benefited, 93% now at 5% GST
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen a transformational policy development by the Government of India to reduce GST rates across key FMCG categories.

items.statement: International business grew 8% YoY; SAARC up 22% (Bangladesh), GCC/MENA flat (Egypt, Bahrain weak), Nepal >100% growth
items.quote: Our international business delivered a steady 8% growth despite persistent macro and geopolitical headwinds.

items.statement: SAARC markets including Bangladesh delivered over 22% growth; GCC and MENA flattish due to Egypt; issues in Egypt and Bahrain being addressed
items.quote: SAARC has done exceedingly well for us. SAARC markets, including Bangladesh, we had delivered over 22% growth over there.
