items.statement: Copper project trial production targeted between January 2026 and December 2028
items.quote: internal target, as of now it i s an internal target, that from January 2026 to by December 2028, we will be on to trial productions in

items.statement: Copper project financial closure achieved over 95%, awaiting DyStar proceeds
items.quote: It is already there. It has been achieved, let me say, more than 95%. Just waiting for the proceeds to come. That is it.

items.statement: Copper project borrowing mix of dollar and rupee at approximately 8.5-9% in rupee terms
items.quote: It is a mix of dollar and r upee, but in rupee terms, we are trying to be around 8.5% to 9%, somewhere around there

items.statement: Standalone Q2 FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 10 crore and net loss of Rs 21 crore due to elevated legal expenses
items.quote: The company reported an EBITDA loss of Rs. 10 crores and a net loss of Rs. 21 crores, primarily due to elevated legal expenses related to the DyS tar case and higher o perating costs

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 13 crore and net loss of Rs 80 crore before associate profit
items.quote: The company reported an EBITDA loss of Rs. 13 crores and a net loss of Rs. 80 crores before considering the state of profit from associates and other OCI.

items.statement: Dyes and intermediates industry gradual recovery supported by improving downstream textile demand and normalized freight
items.quote: the dyes and intermediates industry continued its gradual recovery during Q2 FY'26, supported by improving downstream textile demand and normalized global freight conditions

items.statement: Continued rationalization of product mix within specialty and dye intermediate segments while enhancing export competitiveness
items.quote: As part of our value-focused strategy, we continue to rationalize the product mix within the specialty and dye intermediate segments while enhancing our export competitiveness.

items.statement: Intermediates affected by raw material volatility in naphthalene-based feedstocks and petrochemical derivatives
items.quote: intermediates such as vinyl sulphone and H. Acid remained affected by intermittent raw material volatility, particularly fluctuations in naphthalene-based feedstocks and other petrochemical derivatives

items.statement: Lonsen Kiri JV sustained healthy operational performance with improved capacity utilization and steady domestic demand
items.quote: Our joint venture, Lonsen Kiri Chemical Industries Limited, sustained healthy operational performance, supported by improved capacity utilization and steady domestic demand.

items.statement: DyStar sale requires NDRC and Ministry of Commerce approvals in China; Longsheng failed to obtain them by extended deadlines
items.quote: the purchaser could not obtain the required approvals, mainly from NDRC and Ministry of Commerce, within the stipulated time

items.statement: Company estimates 50-50 probability of Longsheng obtaining approvals by December 1; >90% chance of deal closure by Dec 31 if second bidder selected
items.quote: based on our own opinion, and again, this opinion could be a biased opinion, because we are very bitter. We say 50-50, I do not give more than 50-50 to them. Sunil Nangalia: And that 31st December? Manish Kiri: 31st December, if the receiver chooses another the second bidder, the chances of 31st December is more than 90

items.statement: DyStar stake sale to Zhejiang Longsheng at $1.9B valuation; base consideration $676.26M plus $20.29M additional; total ~$696M
items.quote: agreed to acquire our entire 37.57% stake in DyStar for a valuation of the company at $1.9 billion. For a base consideration for Kiri of USD 676.26 million, an additional USD 20.29 million was also agreed to be paid by the purchaser to cover any shortfall or s pecific obligations under the SP A, taking the total potential consideration to approximately USD 696 million

items.statement: Management confirms dividend will be paid after DyStar proceeds received
items.quote: Yes. Correct. And that is what we mentioned earlier. I would also confirm to you the same. Yes, there will be.

items.statement: Ranjit Singh Chugh, CEO of Indo Asia Copper Limited, joins earnings calls going forward to lead copper business updates
items.quote: he will now be joining the conference calls with us. And he will be happy to answer your questions. He would be leading, along with our key management team, the copper business.

items.statement: Copper smelter capacity 5 lakh tonnes per annum; integrated fertilizer plant 1 billion setup using sulfuric acid by-product
items.quote: The copper smelter with a capacity of 5 lakh tonnes per annum will produce copper cathodes, rods, tubes, along with other by-products such as gold, silver, and selenium. The integrated fertilizer plant will u tilize sulfuric acid, a by-product of the smelting process, to manufacture phosphoric acid and NPK -DAP fertilizers

items.statement: Legal costs continue at similar levels until DyStar sale proceeds received; expected to drop drastically upon fund receipt
items.quote: the legal cost is still continuing. And legal cost, in fact, is still at a similar level, not reduced. And the reason legal cost is continuing because there is a continuous dealing with the receiver, with the court, with the developments which you have seen in the last two months

items.statement: Standalone revenue Rs 195 crore in Q2 FY26, up 34% YoY and 8% QoQ
items.quote: On a stand -alone basis, revenue from operations for the quarter st ood at Rs. 195 crores, reflecting a growth of about 34% year -on-year and 8% sequentially

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 213 crore in Q2 FY26, up 23% YoY and 6% QoQ
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations during the quarter under review stood at Rs. 213 crores, a growth of 23% year-on-year and 6% sequentially.

items.statement: Share of profit from associates and JVs Rs 161 crore in H1 FY26 vs Rs 203 crore in H1 FY25
items.quote: The share of profit from associates and joint ventures during the first half of FY26 stood at Rs. 161 crores, compared to Rs. 203 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Escrow deposits from Longsheng ($3.48M + $5.11M) would be confiscated if deal fails
items.quote: The extension was granted subject to an additional US$5.11 million being deposited into the es crow account, over and above USD 3.48 million already paid earlier

items.statement: Company has headroom to borrow up to $200M for copper project, drawn $130M so far, no intention to draw more
items.quote: we still had he adroom till $200 million, up to $200 million , we withdrew 130. We still do not want to take further borrowing

items.statement: Exports expected to maintain 15%-20% growth tempo in coming months
items.quote: We expect exports to continue to maintain the growth tempo in the coming months.

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle industry growth expected to improve by 6-8 percentage points in medium term
items.quote: We think that the industry should improve its growth rate by 6 to 8 percentage points in the medium term and offer us very good opportunities to attract customers to our Pulsar portfolio.

items.statement: Three-wheeler sales target of over 100,000 units per quarter
items.quote: We expect E-auto performance to get unlocked due to the removal of supply constraints and we intend to capture a higher share of the improving ICE auto market, maintaining the growth tempo and sales of certainly over 100,000 units per quarter.

items.statement: Chetak EV aims to maintain number 1 position with new model launch by early next year
items.quote: We will aim to maintain the leadership position here on. The launch of an absolutely new model by early next year combined with the growing Chetak network which now stands at 390 exclusive stores and 4,000 points of sale in 800 cities should further strengthen our claims to leadership.

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle industry grew 14% during festive period vs 5-6% normal seasonal uplift
items.quote: This time, the motorcycle industry has grown by about 14%. So, we think that almost 8%-9% swing was due to the GST rate cut, but it will probably not be sustained at that level.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler demand tapered to single-digit growth post-GST but expected to recover to 15-20% in 1-2 months
items.quote: We feel that this will very soon, in 1 or 2 months, get back to the growth rate. The growth rates were at about 20%. We feel that maybe 15% -20% range it will get back.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 20.5%, up 70bps sequentially driven by favorable FX and operating leverage
items.quote: Margins for the quarter came in at 20.5% that is another high that we have seen for years, expanding by 70 basis points sequentially, driven by the obvious benefits from a favorable dollar realization as the rupee had weakened and better operating leverage, given a larger quarter.

items.statement: Net commodity cost inflation impact of 40bps in Q2 after marginal price increase
items.quote: The quarter finally ended with a net cost inflation impact of about 40 basis points after adjusting for the marginal price increase that we had taken.

items.statement: EV portfolio (2W, 3W, Yulu) delivered double-digit EBITDA margin in Q2
items.quote: These collectively delivered almost 20% of domestic revenue but more importantly a double-digit EBITDA percentage in Q2.

items.statement: Exports volume grew 24% to over 550,000 units in Q2, highest ever quarterly export revenue
items.quote: The BU grew volumes by 24% in Q2 with exports of over 550,000 units. This delivered the highest ever quarterly revenue from exports.

items.statement: October exports breached 200,000 units after 40 months with only 25,000 units from Nigeria vs 50,000-60,000 previously
items.quote: In October, the exports business breached the 200,000 mark after almost 40 months. A key point over here is that previously when we were clocking 200,000 units, it used to have a contribution of 50,000 -60,000 units of sales to Nigeria. Right now, it has only 25,000 units.

items.statement: Three-wheeler domestic sales hit all-time record of 145,000 units in Q2
items.quote: Our business continues to perform strongly, delivering an all-time record quarter of 145,000 units and also in revenue terms.

items.statement: Pro-Biking (KTM+Triumph) sold over 30,000 units, up 30% YoY, all-time high
items.quote: Together, the two brands are in an absolutely outstanding quarter selling over 30,000 units, registering a 30% growth. This is again an all-time high and was driven by the new KTM models and steady but growing performance of the Triumph models.

items.statement: BACL AUM crossed Rs 14,000 crores, trending towards Rs 15,000 crores with 40% penetration
items.quote: AUM at the end of the quarter stood at a tad under Rs. 14,000 crores. With the festive season, a very buoyant festive season, that the BACL business has seen as well, the AUM is trending upwards, well upwards of Rs. 14,000 crores, on the verge of getting to Rs. 15,000 crores.

items.statement: Building three-wheeler capacity in next few months, particularly for EV segment
items.quote: We are now therefore taking steps to build three-wheeler capacity in the next few months, particularly in the e-vehicle segment.

items.statement: BACL cumulative investment Rs 2,900 crores, Rs 500 crores infused in FY26, may need Rs 200-300 crores more
items.quote: Maybe the last couple of Rs. 100 crores, between Rs. 200-Rs. 300 crores is what it will need from here onwards to get to a path of being able to sustain its own future growth.

items.statement: Manufacturing operating at peak capacity for three-wheelers, supply chain constraints for EV components being resolved
items.quote: As it is with the surge in exports, manufacturing is operating at peak capacity for three-wheelers and we are now therefore taking steps to build three-wheeler capacity in the next few months, particularly in the e-vehicle segment.

items.statement: Absorbed GST increase on >350cc models (KTM, Triumph, Dominar, NS400) by holding/lowering prices
items.quote: On 350cc plus, where the rate moved from 31% essentially, 28% GST and 3% CESS to 40%, we either held pricing or lowered our pricing across models compared to pre-GST levels, therefore absorbing the impact of the rate change to keep this part of the business competitive and without hurting affordability for customers.

items.statement: Passed on GST reduction benefit (28% to 18%) on motorcycles <350cc, commercial vehicles, spare parts via reduced pricing
items.quote: We passed on the benefit of the rate reduction on motorcycles under 350cc, on commercial vehicles and on spare parts, on all those parts of the portfolio where it moved from 28% to 18% thro ugh reduced pricing to customers

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation seen in steel, noble metals (rhodium, platinum), copper, rubber; hoping currency tailwind offsets
items.quote: On commodity, we are clearly seeing some cost inflation across the metals and noble metals baskets. We have not taken up any pricing yet to mitigate this impact, but I am hoping that the tailwind that we are seeing from currency should be able to make up for this.

items.statement: Premiumization trend: top-end variants in each segment (Pulsar N/NS series, 150cc+ sport) outperformed base models
items.quote: In each segment, we found that the top-end variants performed extremely well, reflecting that the customers with relatively strong wallets had aggressively entered the buying cycle and were happy to upgrade. Hence, our N-series and NS-series of Pulsar motorcycles handsomely beat segment growth rates.

items.statement: New Pulsar variants launching in December, March, May; non-Pulsar ICE brand launch in FY27 earlier than later
items.quote: We have got a few introductions starting from December in the Pulsar range. And there will be some in March and then in May. So, we have got at least 3 good model introductions in December, March, and May.

items.statement: KTM/Triumph portfolio reshaping for lower GST rates underway at feverish pace, new engines in development
items.quote: That work is going on feverish pace. And again, I don't want to just give these timelines. But I hope you understand the complexity of making a new engine. But I think you will all be surprised by how fast we can swing that through.

items.statement: BACL added over 2 lakh customers in Q2, penetration 40% for Bajaj business, PAT Rs 132 crores
items.quote: Over 2 lakh customers were added in Q2 with AUM crossing Rs. 14,000 crores and penetration touching 40% for the Bajaj business. Q2 PAT was above plan, coming in at over Rs. 132 crores.

items.statement: Mexico tariff concession: Bajaj gets 5% tariff vs 35% for others due to investment approvals
items.quote: But there are only two companies which will get a concessionary tariff because of the investments which have been made and approvals which are in place. And this is one Mexican company, and the second one is Bajaj Auto. So instead of 35%, our tariff will be only 5%.

items.statement: ABS mandate discussion with Minister Gadkari on Nov 11; potential cost impact Rs 2,000-3,000 per vehicle
items.quote: There is an importa nt meeting on the 11th with Minister Gadkari, which is when they are meeting the industry for a discussion on the pros and cons of doing the ABS introduction on all two-wheelers. So let us see what happens in that meeting and subsequently

items.statement: KTM acquisition: All regulatory approvals received except EU subsidy control; deemed approval by Nov 10 if no objection
items.quote: The paperwork for this has been filed and the outcome of this will be known by the 10th of November. We have been given to understand that one deems approval to be in place if there is no objection that is filed within 25 days of filing these documents. 25 days expire on 10th of November, so if there are no objections that come through, this is meant to be a deemed approval.

items.statement: Dollar realization improved to 87.1 in Q2 vs 85.6 in Q1 and 83.8 YoY; exports revenue near $600M record
items.quote: Dollar realization stood at 87.1 compared to 85.6 in the previous quarter and 83.8 in the same period last year.

items.statement: Exports revenue reached new record close to $600 million in Q2, surpassing 2022 benchmark in dollar terms
items.quote: Total exports for the quarter were very close to $600 million, a new record surpassing the previous benchmark set in 2022. So, the milestone on exports revenue is not just in rupee terms, but in dollar terms as well.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation ~Rs 4,500 crores in H1 FY26, ~100% PAT conversion; surplus cash >Rs 14,000 crores
items.quote: Consistent with the track record of free cash flow generation, we generated around Rs. 4,500 crores of free cash in the first half of this year, which is a conversion of almost 100% of the profits after tax. The balance sheet continues to remain very healthy. Surplus cash is in excess of Rs. 14,000 crores at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: BACL capital adequacy 19.8%, ROE 17.4% H1, AAA/A1+ ratings; board approved NCD issuance for funding diversification
items.quote: Capital risk adequacy ratio is a little under 20%, at 19.8% at the end of the quarter, and the business continues to operate at a very healthy, almost an industry-leading return on equity at about 17.4% for the half year. BACL continues to enjoy the highest level of creditworthiness with AAA ratings and stable long-term debt ratings and A1+ for its short-term debt programs.

items.statement: KTM acquisition nearing completion: call options exercised, EGM on Nov 19 to rename to Bajaj Mobility AG, line-level consolidation to follow
items.quote: An extraordinary general meeting has been called for and will be convened on 19th of November at which the name of the company will be changed, it is proposed to be changed from Pierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG. It will continue to be listed on the Swiss and the Vienna Stock Exchanges and alongside the boards, both the supervisory board and the management boards of KTM and the newly renamed

items.statement: Paid dividend of nearly Rs 6,000 crores in July/August
items.quote: The cash position has been maintained after two major outflows in these last 6 months. The first is that we paid a dividend of nearly Rs. 6,000 crores in July/ August.

items.statement: EV revenue 18% of domestic revenue (Rs 1,700+ crores) in Q2; EV portfolio EBITDA margin double-digit
items.quote: Well, the EV revenues in Quarter 2 were 18% of domestic revenues. Dinesh Thapar: Yes, so EV revenues are a little over Rs. 1,700 crores, 18%, as Rakesh just called out

items.statement: CNG motorcycle adoption slowed due to under-filling of tanks compromising range and need for better pump density
items.quote: One is the quantum of savings, which sometimes gets impaired by the under filling of gas in the CNG tank because of pressure reasons, even though the CNG network may be available, but sometimes because the gas is not fully filled, it compromises the range.

items.statement: Signed asset transfer agreement with Tata Steel for ferrochrome plant at Kalinganagar (99 MVA furnace capacity, 115 acres) for Rs. 610 crore base consideration, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: We have agreed to a base purchase consideration of Rs. 610 crores. And speaking to the value of the strength of the balance sheet, this is going to be entirely funded from internal accruals.

items.statement: Combined capacity (existing 284,000 tons + greenfield 100,000 tons + acquisition 150,000 tons) will exceed 500,000 tons, making IMFA India's largest and world's sixth largest ferrochrome producer
items.quote: This is a significant acquisition because combined with our existing capacity of 284,000 tons, 100,000 tons greenfield capacity and acquisition being 150,000 tons, it will take us beyond the half a million-ton mark, making us India's largest producer of ferrochrome and the sixth largest producer globally.

items.statement: Expect to close Tata Steel acquisition within three months, targeting calendar year 2025; no tonnage assumed in Q4 FY26, real benefit from FY27
items.quote: Subject to certain conditions and requisite approvals we expect to close it within three months. In fact, both sides are aligned to expedite it and we would try to close it within the calendar year, if possible.

items.statement: Expect 70,000-80,000 tons output from acquired unit in FY27 with upside potential
items.quote: But we are fairly confident about achieving, let's say, between 70,000 to 80,000 tons of output in FY '27 from this unit with an upside potential to that number.

items.statement: Rs. 50 crore capex to commission 33 MVA furnace under construction; total acquisition cost ~Rs. 700-750 crore including GST and working capital
items.quote: And as far as the fifth furnace is concerned, we expect to spend about Rs. 50 crores to commission that

items.statement: Rs. 1,000 crore capex for Sukinda mine transition from open cast to underground (3 to 6 lakh tons) over 4-5 years; Mahagiri mine already underground targeting 6 lakh tons
items.quote: As far as the CAPEX for underground is concerned, broadly, it is about Rs. 1,000 crores, which is what we have briefed earlier as well.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 19.3% (Rs. 138 crore); one-time impacts of Rs. 14 crore RPO certificates and Rs. 14 crore forex MTM; expect Q3 margin improvement
items.quote: our EBITDA also is a healthy 19.3%, more or less in the similar range we were in Q1, and in Q3 we are expecting to be better because the price re alization benefit is about couple of months lag to realize it out

items.statement: India's stainless steel production and consumption growing rapidly; global infrastructure development positive; demand environment remains strong
items.quote: India's own stainless-steel production and consumption are growing rapidly given the country's economic growth and the focus on infrastructure development globally as well we see positive signs.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 ferrochrome production 65,671 tons, sales 69,765 tons; chrome ore production 169,615 tons; captive power generation 309.41 million units
items.quote: So, for Q2, our production of ferrochrome was 65,671 metric ton. And chrome ore production was 1,69,615 metric ton. Ferrochrome sales improved in this quarter, and it was 69,765 metric ton.

items.statement: Target 400,000 tons production in FY27 (260,000 existing + 70,000-80,000 acquisition + rest greenfield); 475,000 tons in FY28
items.quote: As our production goes up from 260,000 tons to 400,000 in FY '27 and further to 475,000 tons in FY '28 and beyond, it is being produced in a more friendly, logistically friendly location.

items.statement: Chrome ore requirement fully met from captive mines; targeting 8.5 lakh tons ore raising in FY26, 12 lakh tons eventually; no ore purchases needed
items.quote: We do not intend to buy any ore going ahead, and we will be meeting our requirement both for the existing capacity plus greenfield plus acquisition from our captive mines.

items.statement: Metallurgical coke prices broadly stable with slight increase due to washery freight; sourced from ultra-low ash sources
items.quote: Broadly the prices are stable. A little bit of washery freight is increasing. So, slight increase is there, but broadly it is stable.

items.statement: 90-91% export oriented, USD invoicing with hedging policy; Q2 forex MTM notional cost Rs. 14 crore (rate 88.79 vs 85.54); Rs. 16 crore forex gain in revenue
items.quote: Almost 90% to 91% of our business is export-oriented, and we invoice in USD, and with the dollar fluctuations, we have a hedging policy to de-risk the future export sales against Forex fluctuation.

items.statement: Q2 sales mix ~90% export, 10% domestic; targeting 60% export, 40% domestic in few years with Kalinganagar capacity; long-term contracts repriced quarterly/monthly
items.quote: going ahead, we are certainly going to align a little bit more towards the domestic market. Given our strategic positioning in Kalinganagar in Odisha, which is really emerging as the stainless-steel hub of India , s o in a couple of years’ time with the entire capacity online, greenfield and acquisition, we are expecting to be about 60 -40

items.statement: Average realization Q2 FY26 Rs. 1,01,000/ton (up from Rs. 95,000 in Q1); PAT Rs. 98.77 crore (up 8% QoQ)
items.quote: In Q1, it improved to Rs. 91.48 crores with the increase in the average realization price to about Rs. 95,000, and this quarter it has further improved by 8% to Rs. 98.77 crores, which is with average realization of Rs. 1,01,000.

items.statement: Greenfield Kalinganagar 1 capex includes Rs. 120 crore for 8.7 MW waste heat recovery plant; land for 3 furnaces (150,000 tons) on 120 acres
items.quote: Second, the greenfield includes about Rs. 120-odd crores towards 8.7 Megawatt waste heat recovery power plant, right.

items.statement: Capex funding mix of equity and debt; Rs. 400 crore sanctioned term loan for greenfield (not fully drawn); ethanol project has small debt sanction; conservative debt approach
items.quote: Currently, we have got Rs. 900 crores in Kalinganagar, of which is about Rs. 400 crores sanction limit. We will not be using to the full extent of this sanctioned limit.

items.statement: One-time Rs. 14 crore impact from Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) certificate purchase due to change in law; ongoing quarterly cost Rs. 2-3 crore
items.quote: There is a change in law with respect to the renewable power obligation. For that we have a one-time impact of Rs. 14 crores. Overall, the outflow was Rs. 16 crores.

items.statement: 110 MW hybrid renewable energy PPA signed, coming online next year to power growth plans and reduce carbon footprint
items.quote: We are doing a pivot towards renewable energy with 110 Megawatts of hybrid renewable energy being signed up to come online next year which will power our growth plans.

items.statement: Chinese ferrochrome cost ~$1,000/ton (higher than IMFA); South African production cuts significant but not all capacity may return; IMFA well-positioned as integrated low-cost producer
items.quote: Based on experience, based on conversations, the sense we get is that they are perhaps somewhere around that $1,000 per ton mark.

items.statement: Receivables spike of Rs. 289 crore in FY25 due to UCL merger; received in subsequent quarter; inventory increase modest at Rs. 60-70 crore
items.quote: That is basically due to merger of UCL with IMFA. There was already an order received by us on that respect. Hence, there was an increase in the receivables in the quarter, which we have received in subsequent quarter.

items.statement: High carbon ferrochrome (HCFC) primary product; specific consumption data (ore, coke, power per ton) commercially sensitive but broadly in line with industry norms
items.quote: So Priya, we will not get into the specifics because these are again commercially sensitive data, but broadly in line with the accepted parameters, so no outliers in that regard.

items.statement: Full management team on call: MD Subhrakant Panda, WTD & COO Bijayananda Mohapatra, CFO Saunak Gupta, Power BU Head Binoy Agarwalla, Mines BU Head Sandeep Narade, Ferro Alloys BU Head Captain Sureshbabu
items.quote: We have with us today, Mr. Subhrakant Panda – Managing Director; Mr. Bijayananda Mohapatra – Whole-Time Director and COO; Mr. Saunak Gupta – Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Binoy Agarwalla – Head (Power Business Unit); Mr. Sandeep Narade – Head (Mines Business Unit); Last but not the least, Captain Sureshbabu – Head (Ferro Alloys Business Unit).

items.statement: Logistics synergy: Kalinganagar close to mines (like Choudwar) vs Therubali disadvantage ~Rs. 4,000/ton; outbound logistics advantage ~Rs. 1,000-1,500/ton for domestic sales from Kalinganagar
items.quote: We have a logistical disadvantage to the extent of about maybe Rs. 4,000 a ton or so as compared to Choudwar. Now, Kalinganagar is more like Choudwar, being close to the mines and therefore every ton that we produce in Kalinganagar is as competitive as Choudwar.

items.statement: Aspires mid- to high single-digit price and mid-single-digit volume growth in Q3 FY26, aiming for double-digit revenue growth in H2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, we aspire for that. I think, yes, that's the way you should look at it. In terms of against last year, we obviously -- our stated aspiration is to get into double-digit growth.

items.statement: Aims for 8-10% annual distribution expansion over next 3-4 years, targeting 1.5x direct distribution growth
items.quote: See, we want to add on a consistent basis, we want to improve our distribution by 8% to 10% every year over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Seeks to grow non-ADHO portfolio ahead of ADHO in long term, shifting mix from current ~80:20
items.quote: If you look at the long term, obviously, we aspire for the non-ADHO portion to grow ahead of ADHO.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved by 500-600 bps YoY to 20.5% (standalone) and 18.6% (consolidated) in Q2 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA on a standalone basis for Q2 grew by 42% to deliver an absolute EBITDA of INR 49.6 crores, which translated into margin of 20.5%, a 500 basis point movement over the same period last year.

items.statement: Margins to stabilize in medium term due to GST price adjustments and pack-level changes
items.quote: So expect a stability in the medium term, and we remain committed in the longer period basically towards that further incremental journey for the margin, but expect near-term stability

items.statement: ADHO revenue growth driven by ~70% pricing, 30% mix change and revenue management
items.quote: So broadly, Percy, yes, around, let's say, the largest portion does come from pricing and the other 2 are combined lesser than the pricing.

items.statement: GST reduction to 5% for ~100% portfolio (excluding Banjara’s), passed on to consumers via price cuts
items.quote: And we believe this GST reduction is a very strong structural positive move to unleash demand growth in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Urban demand strong (double-digit growth in direct retail/wholesale), rural recovery expected in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We expect rural to fully bounce back over the next couple of quarters. Organized trade registered a strong double-digit growth Y-o-Y in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: GST 2.0 expected to accelerate consumption demand structurally
items.quote: We believe this GST reduction is a very strong structural positive move to unleash demand growth in the quarters to come.

items.statement: International business declined 26% YoY due to EMEA distributor transition and US bids
items.quote: In international business, we had a very poor quarter with revenues declining by 26% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Nepal market temporarily impacted by political instability; expects normalization soon
items.quote: We expect Nepal to normalize very soon and this business to be back on track.

items.statement: GST transition caused 3% revenue loss in Q2 FY26 due to channel destocking
items.quote: We believe we've lost close to 10% revenue in the month of September or close to around 3% of the quarter revenue.

items.statement: Inverted GST structure (5% output vs. higher input GST) under review; no material near-term impact expected
items.quote: We are fully studying it and understanding that impact. And it's pretty much like the other companies in the sector who have faced a similar transition.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 18% YoY to INR1,569 crore, with standalone revenue at INR1,330 crore
items.quote: For H1, our consolidated revenue stood at INR1,569 crore, marking a growth of over 18% year- over-year, while stand alone revenue was INR1,330 crore

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin was 13.8%, in line with mid-term guidance of 13%–15%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for H1 stood at INR216 crore with a margin of 13.8%, in line with our target band of 13% to 15% EBITDA, as per the medium-term outlook.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated PAT grew 20% YoY to INR151 crore, with standalone PAT at INR131 crore
items.quote: Consolidated PAT for H1 stood at INR151 crore with a margin of 10%, growing 20% year-on-year. Standalone PAT stood at INR131 crore.

items.statement: Order book expanded 17% YoY to INR16,000 crore as of September 2025, with 38% O&M and 50% international
items.quote: Consequently, our order book position rose by 17% since the start of the year to reach over INR16,000 crore as of September '25, supported by strong payment securities.

items.statement: India's economy showing resilience with policy stability, demand growth, lower GST rates, and benign liquidity supporting H2 FY26 outlook

items.statement: Retail Equities revenue declined 24% YoY due to new F&O regulatory norms
items.quote: Retail Equities income was Rs. 271 crores in Q2 FY‘26 versus Rs. 356 crores in Q2 FY‘25, a decline of 24% and this decline is primarily on account of the new regulatory norms on F&O trading.

items.statement: Institutional income increased 5% YoY to Rs. 186 crores
items.quote: Institutional income, which has increased 5%, Rs. 186 crores versus Rs. 177 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Financial product distribution income increased 22% YoY to Rs. 130 crores
items.quote: FPD income has increased 22%, Rs. 130 crores versus Rs. 106 crores because of increased focus on distribution products and income.

items.statement: Operational PBT flat QoQ at Rs. 164 crores before MTM and other income
items.quote: Operational PBT, which is before other income and MTM income is at about Rs. 164 crores, which is flat on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Operating PBT declined 20% YoY to Rs. 164 crores before MTM
items.quote: Operating PBT is at Rs. 164 crores before MTM and that is a decline of almost 20% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Cross-sell assets at Rs. 44,000 crores with 60% ARR (Rs. 27,000 crores) and 40% non-ARR
items.quote: Currently, cross-sell assets stand at about Rs. 44,000 crores, which is 60% is ARR and 40% is non-ARR. ARR assets is mutual fund, PMS and AI, which is now standing at about Rs. 27,000 crores.

items.statement: Average daily turnover increased QoQ to Rs. 2,63,568 crores driven by F&O growth
items.quote: Our average daily turnover was Rs. 2,63,568 crores, which is a split of F&O at Rs. 2,60,956 crores and cash was Rs. 2,612 crores approximately in the quarter that went by

items.statement: Overall market share unchanged at 0.64%, non-Prop market share increased in both F&O (2.65%) and cash (3.87%)
items.quote: Our market share, if you consider overall market share, that is basically unchanged at about 0.64%, which is about cash market of about 2.52% to 2.55% and F&O was about 0.62% to 0.64%. But the good news is that if you remove non-Prop, because we believe that a large segment of Prop, which is not addressed by us, then non-Prop market share, we have seen an increase in both F&O as well as cash.

items.statement: Wealth management team at 50-55 RMs, flat this quarter; 450 existing broking RMs being upgraded for cross-sell
items.quote: See, actually, to be honest, I think last time also, the same question was asked. So, as of now, we are roughly about 50 RMs - 55 RMs in that range. This quarter, we have not seen a significant increase in the RMs, but it is virtually flat.

items.statement: Wealth business loss of Rs. 20-25 crores in H1 FY26, similar to Rs. 20-24 crores loss in FY25
items.quote: In this financial, if you look at investment, basically, manpower cost is the biggest investment. So, as of now, last year we incurred, we made a loss of about Rs. 20 crores - Rs. 24 crores. And this year for the first half, we would have lost about Rs. 20 crores - Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: Wealth platform tech ~80% ready with wealth spectrum software, reporting and training upgrades implemented
items.quote: Yes, from the back-end perspective, I think we have done quite a lot of work. So, we have implemented wealth spectrum software. We have invested in a lot of reporting software. We have upgraded our training software to omni cell. So, we have done a lot of work. But the most difficult thing is going out and getting access.

items.statement: SEBI consultation paper on brokerage cap (12bps to 2bps) not yet law; impact uncertain but would affect mutual fund segment revenue
items.quote: See, if you look at this, this decision paper is yet to become law. But as you said there has been media reports that 2 basis points might also see some increase. So in the institutional segment, a bulk of our brokerage comes from foreign institutional investors and where the capping is not applicable. Mutual funds, however, are still a significant player on this.

items.statement: Broking revenue split ~60% F&O, 40% cash; Institutional income split ~60% broking, 40% investment banking
items.quote: So, I think Broking business, roughly it is about 60 - 40. It will be broadly in the 60 - 40 range. 60 F&O and 40 cash.

items.statement: Wealth strategy focuses on all cities with existing broking presence, not limited to Tier II/III
items.quote: So, I think it is wrong on my part to say, no, we will be focusing only on Tier II, Tier III, but we are focusing on all the cities where IIFL is present.

items.statement: MTM loss of Rs. 44 crores on BSE and NSE shares held for down selling
items.quote: It is pertaining to both BSE shares and NSE shares. We have bought some NSE shares for down selling. So, on that we have taken some risk.

items.statement: Wealth business expected to become profitable in 2-3 years; focus on growing ARR assets from current Rs. 27,000 crores
items.quote: See, we hope that over the next maybe two years to three years, this business will become profitable. As of now, we have to continue to invest and build this up. So, it will be a big crystal glazing path on my part to give an exact number. But we think we are quite optimistic, because we think that asset gathering and getting ARR revenue is the way to go.

items.statement: Investment banking optimistic on deal pipeline but no specific revenue guidance given
items.quote: Basically, what is happening is that we are quite optimistic about the deal pipeline and there are various deals in the various stages of completion. So, I am quite optimistic. Although, it is very difficult for me to give an exact number that how much deal is done and how much is not done.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to benefit from higher exchange volumes in H2, but wealth investments continue to pressure costs
items.quote: See, actually, my view is that hopefully from second half, as you pointed out earlier also, exchange volume is big. So, we should see some benefits in the cost to income ratio. But on the long term, our view is that this year we continue to invest in the wealth business. So, that is obviously affecting our cost to income ratio.

items.statement: High competitive intensity in RM hiring leading to prudent strategy of upgrading existing 450 RMs instead of external hiring
items.quote: See, as I mentioned earlier, what is happening is that there is a huge competitive intensity in the recruitment of RMs. So, basically, as a part of our prudent strategy, we decided that it is better to upgrade our existing RMs train them and empower them instead of going out and acquiring RMs at any cost.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer growth target of 25% for FY26 maintained, adjusting for US tariff impact
items.quote: We had guided earlier on 25%. So, of course, there was a little bit of ripple, I would say, because of the global situation, particularly the tariff situations in US. However, if adjusting for that tariff part, I think if I look at the rest of our product portfolio, I think we are geared toward achieving the 25%.

items.statement: R32 capacity target of 20,000 tons by end of FY26 remains intact
items.quote: As far as 20,000 ton target is concerned, we had indicated that target by the end of this financial year, which is March. So, we will achieve there.

items.statement: Battery materials EBIT break-even expected in FY27
items.quote: Yes, I think we expect it to happen in FY '27. We should be able to reach that break-even point, yes.

items.statement: Capex for battery materials FY27 estimated at ~Rs 1,500 crore, higher than FY26's Rs 1,200 crore
items.quote: We have not given that guidance yet, but it will be probably be higher than 1200, maybe more like 1500, approximately.

items.statement: Battery materials capex focus on cathode and salt expansion; total 4-5 year plan of ~Rs 6,000 crore
items.quote: The focus, of course, has been primarily on the cathode and the salt side, because those are capital intensive. And that is what our focus area is to expand on those product lines.

items.statement: Fully funded for battery capex up to $125 million over next 6-12 months; no equity dilution currently
items.quote: We are fully funded for another up to $125 million, which would be incurred over next, say, 6-9 months, perhaps a year. So, we will be raising money as and when we need, rather than just keeping the money and putting it into treasury.

items.statement: Expect to capture 50-60% of ~7,000 tons annual PTFE imports in India post anti-dumping duty
items.quote: We are quite positive about capturing a very large fraction of this because, because of the imports are expected to go down. And we expect to capture a very large percentage of that, I would say upward of 50%-60%.

items.statement: Chemical segment EBITDA margin 32% in Q2 FY26, up 608 bps YoY; expected to improve further long-term
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 32%, standing by 608 basis points on year-on-year basis. This improvement was driven by a better product mix and continued cost optimizations. Our EBITDA margins should further improve from the current levels on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by value-added product mix, power cost reduction via renewables, and currency benefit; expected to be sustainable
items.quote: This time, there are multiple reasons, of course, because of the product mix. As we are going up in the value chain, value-added product mix is improving our margin. And we will see more of it as we go along in the next few q

items.quote: A lot of decisions have been kept on hold because a lot of customers were expecting this to be reverted. So, they actually put their buying decisions on hold. A lot of it has to be expected to streamline going forward.

items.statement: R32 demand-supply gap remains healthy; expect high utilization of 20,000 ton capacity in FY27

items.statement: R32 plant restart expected by end of current month after safety upgrades; targeting 20,000 tons by March FY26

items.quote: Most of them are convertible instruments, so that we would not see any dilution happening now. But perhaps, just before the IPO, or at the time of the IPO, there would be some dilution.

items.statement: High single-digit volume growth targeted for FY26 despite flat H1

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin expected from Q4 FY26
items.quote: I think by fourth quarter, you are right. Margins will normalize to our kind of a double-digit EBITDA margin from fourth quarter onwards.

items.statement: 12% EBITDA margin doable in FY27
items.quote: Yes. I agree it is doable, and we are adding -- we have added capacity aggressively. So our focus going forward is on expanding markets hand-in-hand with the capacity additions.

items.statement: Robust double-digit volume growth expected in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: I think over the next couple of years, we should have a robust double-digit volume growth in FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: H2 FY26 capex expected at INR110 crores including Aquel
items.quote: So INR110 crores is something what we are expecting as a cash flow for H2. That includes Aquel as well.

items.statement: Low capacity addition planned for FY27 after major Bihar and Telangana expansions
items.quote: I don't foresee any major capacity addition for existing product line in FY '27. There could be some expansions that we do in new products in piping.

items.statement: Bihar Phase 2 commissioned first week of September adding 65,000 MT capacity
items.quote: And it has completed in first week of September, to be specific. And now it is -- the depreciation is getting fully charged.

items.statement: Quarterly depreciation to be INR30-32 crores post Bihar commissioning
items.quote: It will be in the range of INR30 crores to INR32 crores on a quarter basis.

items.statement: Demand expected to gradually recover in H2 FY26 supported by restocking and consumption improvement
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate the demand to gradually recover in the second half of FY '26, supported by restocking activity and improvement in consumption trends.

items.statement: November demand pickup seen vs October; ADD announcement imminent in November
items.quote: In November, we have seen a pickup compared to what it was in October. And with the duty announcement, which is imminent in N ovember, I think we should see a good second half of the quarter
