items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR55 crores, while margin stood at 9%, registering a 200 basis point growth.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by better product mix and cost optimization
items.quote: It has been a function of 2 things. One is a better product mix. We have grown more in the value-added segments. And PVC, we have not grown as much. So the product mix has been favorable.

items.statement: ADD likely to create INR5-6/kg upside but timing uncertain; sentiment shift more important
items.quote: You are right. I think I do see a INR5 to INR6 kind of an upside, but I will not speculate whether it will happen in one shot or over a couple of weeks.

items.statement: CPVC prices expected to remain stable with no major upside or downside
items.quote: I foresee a stable CPVC pricing. And if you see over past sort of 5, 10 years, CPVC prices are not very volatile.

items.statement: CPVC volume growth strong pan-India; PVC growth muted
items.quote: CPVC, we have seen good volume growth across pan-India. And we have done a few cost optimization drives internally as well.

items.statement: Launching own CPVC brand to diversify sourcing and improve cost efficiency
items.quote: We have also launched our own brand of CPVC going forward. So that is going to be one change going forward as far as our CPVC strategy is concerned.

items.statement: Aquel bathware expanded to Jammu & Kashmir and Uttar Pradesh with new display centers
items.quote: During the quarter, we extended our presence in the northern region by opening new display centers in Jammu & Kashmir and Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Chosen as preferred supplier for Navi Mumbai Airport CPVC piping and cable ducting
items.quote: We are also proud to have been chosen as the preferred supplier of CPVC piping and cable ducting solutions for the newly inaugurated Navi Mumbai Airport project.

items.statement: H1 working capital days improved to 85 from 93; receivables 52 days vs 55; inventory 80 days
items.quote: Our working capital days for H1 FY '26 stood at 85 days as compared to 93 days same period last year. Receivables stands at 52 days compared to 55 days same period last year and inventory days stood at 80 days as on 30th September 2025.

items.statement: Sales team strengthened at feet-on-street and regional head levels; distribution expansion in focus states by March
items.quote: We have strengthened our sales team at the foot-soldier level as in feet-on-street and at the regional head level. So we have strengthened our team, gotten a lot of experienced people.

items.statement: Received Ambition Box Employee Choice Award 2025
items.quote: Additionally, we were honored to receive the Ambition Box Employee Choice Award 2025, which stands as a testament to our strong organizational culture, employee engagement and commitment to creating a positive and empowering workplace.

items.statement: Industry PVC consumption degrew 9% in Q2 FY26; H1 also in degrowth
items.quote: If you see in the September quarter, if you check the overall PVC growth in India is still a degrowth, kind of a 9% degrowth we have seen in the PVC consumption in the September quarter.

items.statement: Bathware revenue INR22 crores in H1; Q2 revenue INR12 crores (40% YoY); H1 loss INR10 crores; Q2 loss INR5 crores
items.quote: So for H1, bathware revenue is at around INR22 crores. And it is -- so last year, quarter 2, we had done INR7 crores. Against that, we have done INR12 crores, which is around 40% growth over the last quarter. And the consolidated loss for the H2 is around INR10 crores -- H1.

items.statement: Bathware breakeven targeted in 4 quarters; need INR25-30 crores quarterly sales
items.quote: So we need to achieve INR25 crores to INR30 crores of sales per quarter.

items.statement: Staying away from government/Jal Jeevan Mission business due to elongated credit cycles
items.quote: We have stayed away from the government business because of extended credit cycles. And for our existing business itself, we are on a drive to reduce our receivables and improve the quality of our sales.

items.statement: Management maintains 15-20% revenue growth guidance for FY26 but notes supply constraints on hydra bottles may prevent achieving it
items.quote: If we had ability to supply, I would definitely stick to that 15%-20% number. We just have to see whether that last few months, we can supply that quantity.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 65 crore capex for three double-wall vacuum insulated steel flask lines at Rajasthan facility via subsidiary Stylenest India Limited
items.quote: During the quarter, our board approved a revised project scope for our upcoming manufacturing facility in Rajasthan through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Stylenest India Limited. The project will now include three double -wall production lines for vacuum -insulated steel flasks, bottles, and containers with an estimated capacity of 3.6 million units per year and with an estimated CAPEX of INR 65 cr

items.statement: Two double-wall lines expected to start commercial production by Q4 FY26, third line by Q1 FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: Estimated commercial production dates from two double -wall lines is by the end of this financial year, that's Q4 FY '26, and from the third double -wall line by the end of Q1 FY'27, subject to receipt of necessary approvals.

items.statement: Non-glassware margins declined from high single digit to mid-single digit due to shift to domestic sourcing and loss of high-margin hydra revenue
items.quote: It's gone from high single digit to mid-single digit, more or less. So, there's been a substantial reduction there. It's, of course, it's definitely beyond break-even. And like I said, it's a short-term phenomenon.

items.statement: Demand picked up from Q1 to Q2 and Q3; management reasonably bullish on demand going forward with GST reduction improving consumer sentiment
items.quote: Overall, I would say demand has picked up from Q1 onwards to Q2 and Q3. And we see, with the GST reduction, I think although not directly impacting our goods at all, but just general consumer sentiments seem to be better than before. So, I am reasonably bullish on demand going forward.

items.statement: Glassware grew 27.4% YoY in H1 FY26 driven by consumer shift from plastic to glass and expanded product choices from new borosilicate plant
items.quote: As far as glassware is concerned, I think the reason for the growth is, and I think this was a thesis playing out, that when you give more choice to the customer, the customer tends to buy products, more items.

items.statement: BIS compliance mandatory for entire non-glassware segment; hydra bottles and appliances affected; steel and gas stoves already made in India
items.quote: Frankly, the entire non-glassware segment is subject to BIS now with what you just mentioned. So, the main drivers were hydra, which is the vacuum flask, then appliances and then steel, the stainless steel.

items.statement: Hydra inventory reduced substantially but will be replaced by BIS-compliant appliance inventory; net working capital reduction expected next year not this year
items.quote: Although, frankly speaking, it will not be that material because last year, our inventory went up because we had a higher inventory of hydra, which has now come down. And that will be replaced by BIS inventory of appliances. So, net-net from last year, I don't think there'll be much impact. But I'd have expected working capital to reduce this year, which may not happen.

items.statement: Past Rs 550-600 crore capex (including Rs 65 crore flask plant) can generate peak revenue of Rs 900-1,000 crore from owned manufacturing only
items.quote: Maybe 900 crores to 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Opalware utilization at 90%+, glassware at around 80%
items.quote: I would say Opalware like (+90%) and glassware is around 80%.

items.statement: Net debt of INR 4.5 crores as on 30th September 2025
items.quote: As on 30th September '25, Borosil Ltd has a net debt of INR 4.5 crores.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs declined from INR 42.3 crores to INR 36.9 crores in H1 FY26 due to solar projects and cost management
items.quote: In addition, power and fuel costs declined from INR 42.3 crores to INR 36.9 crores over the same period, reflecting our continued focus on prudent cost management.

items.statement: Solar plant expected to start supplying energy by Feb-March 2026 (Q4 FY26); first full quarter Q1 FY27
items.quote: Solar plant also, I think in the next couple of months, by maybe also Q4 FY26, we should start seeing some net metering or rather some supply of energy from that plant, maybe Feb -March. The first full quarter for both will be Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, general trade, modern retail, e-commerce, B2B and export networks
items.quote: Our strong omnichannel presence across general trade, modern retail, top e-commerce platforms, and expanding B2B and export networks has driven deeper market penetration. With availability in over 24,000 retail outlets, we built a well -diversified revenue base that reaches both urban consumers and rural users.

items.statement: Hydra bottle supply constraints causing revenue loss; growth would have been 20-25% vs actual 12.4% in non-glassware; some channels rejecting non-BIS goods
items.quote: We have still grown by 12% in non -glassware. But that growth may have been north of 20 % -25%, had we had that inventory. As you rightly mentioned, the inventory is on the lower side now. I think we have enough to last us. You know, frankly speaking, a couple of channels have already stopped accepting non -BIS goods, which is also impacting sales.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin slightly lower at 16.1% vs 16.8% in H1 FY25 despite 9.5% EBITDA growth
items.quote: The operating EBITDA margin was slightly lower at 16.1% compared to 16.8% in the previous year.

items.statement: No significant institutional orders for Opalware in Q2 FY26
items.quote: To the best of my knowledge, we had no significant institutional orders at all this quarter.

items.statement: Glassware revenue 90%+ from own manufacturing (borosilicate press ware plant)
items.quote: I think 90%. I don't have the number off the top. More than 90% will be our own manufacturing.

items.statement: Future capex planned from FY27 onwards in non-glassware segments; nothing finalized or board approved yet
items.quote: From FY'27, not even '28. But like I said, I don't want to get into specifics because these are just under consideration and haven't been approved by the Board yet.

items.statement: Milton Plastics entry in Opalware not expected to cause margin or pricing pressure; distribution overlap limited
items.quote: I don't think so. Milton is a very, I would say, well -established player with very good distribution. And in many cases, our distribution doesn't actually overlap. And they are very mature and seasoned, I would say, company. So, I don't see that margin. They will be doing anything to upset the industry structure from a margin perspective.

items.statement: India brown goods market (kitchen/home appliances) valued at $5B in FY24, projected $9B by FY30 at ~10% CAGR
items.quote: India's brown goods market, which includes kitchen and home appliances, is expanding rapidly. Valued at about $5 billion in FY'24, it is projected to reach $9 billion by FY'30, growing around 10% annually.

items.statement: Health and wellness market $50B in FY24, projected $90B by FY30 at 10% CAGR; supports shift to toxin-free materials
items.quote: The $50 billion health and wellness market is projected to reach $90 billion by FY '30, also growing at 10% CAGR. Consumers are moving towards toxin -free, durable materials and away from plastic due to rising health concerns, regulatory bans, as well as sustainability concerns.

items.statement: Lunchbox market sized at INR 4,000 crore; Borosil gaining share with premium microwave-safe glass lunchboxes
items.quote: We see strong potential in INR 4,000 crore lunchbox market, where consumers are increasingly seeking safer, microwave-friendly, and sustainable options. This is where Borosil stands apart.

items.statement: Recruited good talent for stainless steel flask manufacturing; following process by the book
items.quote: We have followed the process. We have recruited good talent. We have done everything by the book. So, I see no reason why this should take more than any other plant would take.

items.statement: Rs 65 crore flask plant capex to be financed through mix of equity, debt, and internal accruals
items.quote: This INR 65 crore investment will be financed through a mix of equity, debt, and internal accruals.

items.statement: Royalty income of Rs 12.1 crores in H1 FY26 from Borosil Renewables for brand usage (cost plus 10% markup)
items.quote: Other operating income for the first half of 2026 includes INR 12.1 crores from shared service support income compared to INR 8.4 crores in the same period last year with the related expenses reflected under total expenses.

items.statement: Management withdrew previous FY25/FY26 guidance of INR 1,000 crore revenue and 23% EBITDA margin, stating assumptions no longer hold due to tariff and regulatory headwinds.
items.quote: we had very clearly mentioned that these assumptions which we had made at the beginning of that calendar year, they no more hold good because of the reasons already mentioned there.

items.statement: No new guidance provided for FY27 due to unresolved U.S. tariff, Isostearic Acid regulatory approvals, and animal feed project timeline uncertainties.
items.quote: it is difficult to prepare or announce any guidance as far as future is concerned. But as I said, once these things fall in line, we surely will be in double digit margins.

items.statement: Domestic paint sector demand weakened, reducing offtake from a major customer and shifting product mix from Linoleic to Dimer Acid.
items.quote: the domestic paint sector witnessed weaker demand, leading to lower off-take from one of our major customers.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin at 3.77%, H1 at 3.87%; management expects margins to stay at current low levels until U.S. tariff, China competition, and raw material issues resolve.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 4 crores, which declined by 52% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 3.77%.

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margins possible only if U.S. tariff eases, raw material prices soften, Isostearic Acid exports revive, and animal feed product commercializes.
items.quote: If these things fall in line, it will be in double digits, surely.

items.statement: Isostearic Acid export ramp-up to non-U.S. markets delayed due to regulatory compliance with two major European producers; approvals pending.
items.quote: The expected ramp-up in exports to non-U.S. market has been delayed as we work through Regulatory compliance processes mandated by 2 major European producers.

items.statement: Dimer Acid exports to U.S. halted due to 50% tariff; management expects substantial exports to resume if India-U.S. trade deal results in rational tariff of 10-15%.
items.quote: once if India closes the deal with U.S., closes the deal in the sense, closes with a mini mum possible tariff only, closes not with 40% or 50% tariff, closes the deal with, say, rational tariff of, say, 10% or 15% with the U.S. government, then we are again back in game as far as Dimer Acid is concerned

items.statement: Another new product (non-animal feed) progressing well; first commercial production trial by March 2026 or April-June 2026 quarter.
items.quote: the new product that we have bee n talking about since last about 1 year, is progressing well and you will see some light during the quarter of may be by March, 2026 or latest during the quarter of April to June

items.statement: Chinese Dimer Acid prices down >25% over 24 months; Fairchem prices at landed Chinese cost plus duty minus INR 2/kg to retain 65% market share.
items.quote: According to me, it has come down by more than 25%.

items.statement: Raw material (acid oil) prices remain firm despite partial duty rollback due to elevated global vegetable oil market and supplier pricing power.
items.quote: prices remain ed largely firm due to elevated global vegetable oil market.

items.statement: Chinese Dimer Acid dumping continues with 7.5% basic custom duty; Fairchem forced to price below Chinese landed cost to defend market share.
items.quote: we are facing direct competition from China because the basic c ustom duty remains at 7.5% only a nd we do not know how much export rebate, etc., these Chinese suppliers are getting from their government and how they are in a position to sell at this price, even after bearing the ocean freight cost

items.statement: Domestic Linoleic Acid faces competition from 3-4 Soya Fatty Acid manufacturers who also compete for acid oil raw material.
items.quote: there are already 3, 4 other manufacturers of the Soya Fatty Acid. So, they also compete in taking the acid oil from the market along with us.

items.statement: 50% U.S. tariff on certain Indian chemical products imposed, temporarily impacting export business to U.S.
items.quote: Our performance was directly affected by the imposition of a 50% U.S. tariff on certain Indian chemical products, which includes some of our key offerings.

items.statement: Isostearic Acid exports to Europe delayed by regulatory compliance and product approval processes required by two major European producers.
items.quote: we work through Regulatory compliance processes mandated by 2 major European producers. Once these registrations are completed, we expect export volumes of Isostearic Acid to grow steadily in a phased manner.

items.statement: Exports 8.78% of Q2 revenue; mainly Isostearic Acid to Europe, negligible to U.S. this quarter due to tariff.
items.quote: During the quarter, domestic sales accounted for 91.22% of total revenue, while exports contributed 8.78%.

items.statement: Dimer Acid exported mainly to India and U.S.; some to Gulf. U.S. exports stopped this quarter due to tariff.
items.quote: Main customers will be India and USA.

items.statement: Q2 product mix: Linoleic Acid share fell from 40% to 33%, Dimer Acid rose from 27% to 33%; Linoleic+Dimer aggregate stable at ~65%.
items.quote: the share of Linoleic has decreased from 40% to 33% and sha re of Dimer Acid has increased from 27% to 33

items.statement: Major domestic paint customer (Asian Paints) lost share to new entrant (Opus); Fairchem not restricted from supplying Opus but pricing not competitive.
items.quote: If the pricing offered by them is not attractive enough for us, then we will not go for that.

items.statement: Imports of INR 31 crore and INR 59 crore in past two years mainly for catalysts from USA; minor capital goods and one raw material previously imported from Asia now stopped.
items.quote: That is mainly catalysts. We are importing catalysts. Once in a while, we import very minor capital goods also.

items.statement: Further margin decline highly unlikely at current 3.8% level, but recovery dependent on multiple simultaneous external factors.
items.quote: Further fall is highly unlikely, highly unlikely. Further fall than this is highly unlikely. But as I said to the previous speaker, once these 2, 3 things fall in line, we will surely be in double digit margin.

items.statement: Processed 11,492 MT and sold 10,062 MT in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Operationally, we processed 11,492 metric tons and sold 10,062 metric tons of material during the quarter.

items.statement: Backward integration into edible oil refining ruled out; raw material is 1.25% byproduct, selling remaining 98.75% edible oil not in company's expertise.
items.quote: For 1.25% raw material, we cannot take the refinery and where do we sell balance 98% edible oil, which Adani and Patanjali, et c., are selling in a consumer

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 3,050 crores as of November 2025, providing long-term revenue visibility
items.quote: As of now, our order book stands strong at around Rs 3,050 odd crores providing long-term revenue visibility and reaffirming our healthy business pipeline.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 3,050 crores includes Rs 1,300 crores for 15-year production enhancement contract and Rs 1,650 crores executable over 2.5 years
items.quote: So, out of this total order book of more than Rs. 3,050 crores, almost Rs. +1,300 crores is for a production enhancement contract, which is for 15 years. So, if we remove that, more than Rs. 1,650 crores of order book is executable over 2.5 years.

items.statement: Expect FY26 revenue growth of more than 35% YoY, with H2 growth higher than H1
items.quote: This year we are expecting to close with growth of more than 35% YOY. And I think we are right there on that trajectory. So, even if we are not factoring growth in H2, it would be more than 38%-39% kind of growth over previous years.

items.statement: Expect FY27 revenue growth of 35-38% YoY driven by PEC, new rigs, and Dolphin Offshore full-year contribution
items.quote: So, all put together we are expecting growth of another 35% to 38% kind of growth on year-on-year basis in next financial year as well.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to improve beyond 45% in coming quarters
items.quote: So, margin we believe it should improve a bit going forward and we are expecting our EBITDA margins to grow upwards beyond 45% in coming quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin at 46.6%, H1 FY26 average EBITDA margin at 45.7%
items.quote: Good control over operating costs and enhanced utilization of key assets helped us post EBITDA of Rs. 112.9 crores in Q2 FY26, reflecting 74.7% YOY growth with an EBITDA margin of 46.6%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expected to improve to 40% without other income in coming quarters
items.quote: On standalone basis, it should improve to 40% without considering other income. So, in coming quarters, we are expecting to improve from current level.

items.statement: Production enhancement contract gas price realization at $7.5/MMBTU with average volume of 170,000 cubic meters/day
items.quote: Gas price realized was around $7.5 MMBTU and average volume would be somewhere around 1,70,000 cubic meter a day.

items.statement: Production enhancement contract expected to generate Rs 35+ crores in H2 FY26 and Rs 140-150 crores full year from FY27 with ~50% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, we are expecting on full year basis revenue from this particular co ntract to the tune of Rs. 140 to Rs. 150 crores from next financial year onwards. And the margins we are expecting out of this contract in range of around 50% kind of

items.statement: Total CAPEX of Rs 600 crores planned, Rs 100 crores already spent, balance for production enhancement and asset acquisitions
items.quote: So, total CAPEX we are expecting is of 600 crores of which 100 crores has already been done. And balance would be going further, including the CAPEX for production and contract.

items.statement: Two rigs en route from China, expected deployment in December and Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our couple of rigs are on the way from China to our sites and we are expecting them to get it deployed one is December and one in Q4.

items.statement: Added six rigs in last 8 months, contributing to revenue growth
items.quote: In addition to that, we have added quite a few assets in this year. Like, in last 8 months, we have added six more rigs.

items.statement: Planning QIP of around Rs 300 crores for expansion, asset acquisition, and CAPEX for production enhancement contract
items.quote: Yes, so we are working towards raising funds through QIP. And that exercise we have started on. So, we are expecting to raise around (+300) crores by the way of QIP.

items.statement: ONGC contributes ~60% of revenue, down from 75-80% historically due to diversification into private and overseas clients
items.quote: Yes, ONGC is always been our largest client. And since you are into oil and gas support services, I believe ONGC has to be your largest client. And in terms of percentage dependency, yes, they are almost 60% kind of contributor to our revenue.

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore targeting Rs 100 crores revenue in FY26, expecting >40% YoY growth with ~80% EBITDA margins
items.quote: This year, we are expecting to close Dolphin Offshore at around 100 crores of top line in FY26. And from next year onwards, we are expecting good amount of growth with addition of few more assets into the fleet.

items.statement: Shortlisted offshore vessels for Dolphin acquisition, at advanced negotiation stage
items.quote: Yes, we have identified and shortlisted few assets and we are working on it once we will be able to tie up those assets for contracts. We will go for acquisition. So, we are on quite advanced stage of that part.

items.statement: Current bidding pipeline of ~Rs 700 crores with high conversion potential, plus ongoing monthly bidding
items.quote: So, we have a bidding pipeline close to 700 odd crores. How much of that would get converted it is only the matter of time but out of our experience we believe it would be good substantial numbers that can get converted.

items.statement: Competition expected to increase as sector grows, but company's 30+ years technical edge provides sustainable advantage
items.quote: So, as the sector definitely gets more and more of business, potential business competition definitely is bound to come. So, that fact cannot be ignored. But having said that, we have been into this industry for more than three decades. And I believe that the edge that we have over the technical things and providing solutions to the client is something that matters the most.

items.statement: Government push for domestic oil/gas production visible through increased tenders, production enhancement contracts, and sick well revival programs
items.quote: So, energy push is quite visible for the fact the kind of tenders, the kind of generation of enquiries are happening and the ki nd of orders that we are receiving. So, the kind of demand that has been generated clearly demonstrates the push that government has

items.statement: Kandla Energy receivables under evaluation, no provision taken yet, hopeful of recovery in coming quarters
items.quote: So, currently, we are sti ll under an evaluation stage. So, as of now, there is no recovery from last quarter till now. But yes, we are hopeful and we have started following up with them. So, we believe some good news should come in coming quarters

items.statement: Consolidated loan of Rs 23 crores to Prabha Energy at 12% interest, originally given pre-demerger
items.quote: On consolidated you are saying. Correct. So, there one loan is given to company called Prabha Energy and it is a 12% interest bearing loan. And that particular loan was originally given before de-merger.

items.statement: Other income from interest, mutual fund M2M gains, and forex revaluation on overseas receivables expected to continue in H2
items.quote: Other income largely consists of interest and mutual fund M2M gro wth and to certain extent it is revaluation on foreign currency valuation on your overseas receivables. So more or less we believe this kind of other income would continue in next half as

items.statement: No provision taken on Kandla Energy receivables as still under evaluation stage
items.quote: So, we have not taken any provision on that as of now because we are in an evaluation stage of those receivables. So, as of now, we are not taking any provision.

items.statement: Arbitration case with ONGC ongoing, hopeful of resolution soon but cannot comment on timeline
items.quote: So that is going on. And so, we cannot comment on timeline when particularly it is a court matter. But we are quite hopeful it should complete it soon.

items.statement: Majority of contracts are fixed-price long-term (3 years), crude oil price movements do not significantly affect services business
items.quote: I believe our majority of contracts are fixed price contract a nd they are long term contracts of 3 years. So largely movement in crude oil price is not affecting our services business because even if crude oil price is higher or lower, the activity of production is continuously going on in India being energy deficien t country

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore depreciation run rate ~Rs 4 crores/quarter based on 15-year asset life, may increase with further asset additions
items.quote: The estimated life for depreciation we have considered as 15 years. And so based on that, this depreciation would start kicking in. So, in last quarter for some part, it was under capital work in progress. And so last quarter, depreciation would have been lower than the current quarter.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of higher teens for FY27
items.quote: Well, I would wish to, but just to give you a very broad level guidance, we look at expect around higher teens.

items.statement: Retail revenue contribution target 8-10% for FY26 and 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: Given the growth trajectory, we see today and expect retail to account for 8 % to 10% revenue in the FY '26 to accelerate to the tune and contributing 15% to 20% in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Retail revenue contribution target 40-50% over five years
items.quote: Yes. So, over five years, we are looking to having close to 40% to 50% of contribution coming out from the retail straight up.

items.statement: Receivables target of 100 days by year end
items.quote: On the working capital front, our receivable currently stands around 150 days, which we aim to bring down to around 100 days by year end.

items.statement: Retail breakeven expected at Rs 100 crore revenue run rate
items.quote: However, in the coming end of the year or in coming times around one Rs. 100 Cr or so, we are looking to even breakeven and then driving the robust bottom line from thereon.

items.statement: Planned capex of Rs 150-170 crore for FY26 excluding Rajasthan
items.quote: So, this year apart from Rajasthan, we have planned CAPEX of Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 170 crores.

items.statement: Rs 80 crore capex incurred in H1 FY26 with Rs 50 crore capitalized and Rs 30 crore in WIP
items.quote: Out of that, we already incurred Rs. 80 crores of CAPEX, which is Rs. 50 crores already in capitalized and Rs. 30 crores is in WIP.

items.statement: Rajasthan PPP to operationalize 10 labs in November, 25 labs and 500 collection centers by December, balance 152 labs and 1,100 collection centers by end of Q4
items.value: 10 labs in November, 25 labs and 500 collection centers by December
items.quote: We are set to operationalize 10 labs in November, 25 labs, and over 500 collection centers by December, and the balance 152 labs and 1,100 collection centers by the end of Q4.

items.statement: Maharashtra has 15 MRIs under implementation with 10 in completion stage awaiting inauguration
items.quote: Maharashtra, we have the MRIs which are under implementation. Almost 15 MRIs are under implementation, 10 are already in the completion stage. And they are yet to be inaugurated by the respective authorities.

items.statement: Radio centers operationalization expected by December end
items.quote: So, by December end is what we are expecting the radio centers to be operationalized.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin at 29%, up 221 bps year-on-year
items.quote: EBITDA grew by impressive 18% year-on-year to Rs. 60 crores. This performance resulted in 221 basis point expansion in our EBITDA margin, which now stands at 29%.

items.statement: ROCE trending towards 15% and continuing to strengthen
items.quote: I am pleased to say this quarter's number show we are walking the talk, with ROCE now trending towards 15% and continuing to strengthen in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Meaningful revenue accretion expected from Q4 FY25 onwards and full-year contribution in FY27 from PPP projects
items.quote: And this is not just about Rajasthan. Several marquee PPP projects are under implementation, and with these all going live, we expect meaningful revenue accretion from Q4 FY '25 onwards and a full-year contribution in FY '27.

items.statement: Industry-wide seasonal dip in Q3 due to winter, with pickup from Q4 onwards
items.quote: Yes. So, Lokesh, this is something industry-wide trend typically in Q3. Because of whether it is the winter, the cold, there are dips in the revenues. And then Q4 onwards, it starts picking in.

items.statement: Revenue per test improvement driven by high-priced tests and wellness packages across PPP and retail
items.quote: No, Surya, as we said, we had also started focusing on if we could leverage these high priced tests. There are also depending on the patient needs. So, we have been able to generate some benefit out of it.

items.statement: Receivables at 150 days due to new central government payment guideline and SNA-SPARSH system transition
items.quote: The current positions reflect a temporary timing impact largely arising from the implementation of a new central government payment guideline, under which states are aligning their processes and releasing payment through RBI link account.

items.statement: Collected over Rs 50 crore subsequently with SNA-SPARSH teething issues normalizing
items.quote: Even if you see subsequently, we have collected almost more than Rs. 50 crores. So, things are looking better now with the SNA-SPARSH systems getting the teething issues getting normalized.

items.statement: Borrowings mainly for working capital, maintaining tight control and minimum leverage philosophy
items.quote: So, if you see the borrowings largely are mostly on the overall working capital. We have been able to maintain a tight control on the borrowings. As a company philosophy, our approach has always been to leverage these borrowings to the minimum.

items.statement: Maharashtra MRI equipment procured on deferred payment with 20-25% upfront, balance in capital creditors
items.quote: So, this is an outflow. This entirely has not been paid. Balance is still lying in the books, which is payable as in capital creditor.

items.statement: Competition intensity increasing in PPP tenders but Krsnaa maintains leadership due to deep experience
items.quote: The competition intensity continues to increase. People are also looking PPP as a model. But as I said, Krsnaa continues to maintain its leadership position because of our deep experience and expertise.

items.statement: CGHS benefit not applicable currently as rates are per tender contracts, but may impact upcoming tenders as benchmark
items.quote: We are in talks with various authorities. This might impact the upcoming tenders where the new CGH rates could be used as a benchmark. But for the existing because these are contracted rates, I don't see an impact or benefit coming first.

items.statement: Rate escalations embedded in contracts linked to WPI are being received
items.quote: So, there are rate escalations which are embedded in our contracts. Wherever those are, we certainly get them.

items.statement: Over 350 radiologists and 120+ pathologists, largest doctor network in Indian diagnostics
items.quote: Behind all of this, there is a strong team of over 350 radiologists and 120-plus pathologists who trust our systems, technology, and processes.

items.statement: Retail revenue grew 60% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 FY26, contributing ~8% of H1 revenue
items.quote: In the second quarter of this financial year, revenue of our direct-to-consumer businesses surged by impressive 60% quarter-on-quarter growth. Retail has contributed approximately 8% of our revenues in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Expanded to over 2,800 touch points in one year through asset-light partnership strategy
items.quote: In just one year, we have expanded to more than 2,800 touch points across the country, a testament to the strength of our asset -light partnership-driven strategy.

items.statement: Floods in Punjab and Himachal impacted operations and collections due to authorities handling disaster issues
items.quote: Yes, it's certainly. I mean, not only from the funds flow, but also operationally, there have been challenges with authorities handling the disaster issues. And therefore, they were not there to authorize certain payments.

items.statement: FY26 net store addition guidance revised to 80-90 stores from earlier 120
items.quote: In FY '26, we aspire to open 80 to 90 stores net addition basis, which was earlier 120. But looking at the market conditions, we have revised it to 80 to 90 stores for FY '26.

items.statement: H2 FY26 net store additions expected around 40-45 stores
items.quote: We've added about 36 stores in H1. And in H2 also, we'll look at as a 40, 45 number, so we'll be around that 80, 90 store mark.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to remain steady at 62-63% in H2 FY26
items.quote: But I think from a gross margin perspective, things will look very steady at between 62% and 63% of gross margin.

items.statement: ASP expected to grow 2-3% YoY driven by new products not price hikes
items.quote: Well, Devanshu, the ASP will grow at about 2% to 3% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Festive season response positive across key markets with volume improvement
items.quote: The response during the festive season has been positive across key markets, reflecting an improvement in consumer sentiment and strong traction across our core categories.

items.statement: Demand revival seen in certain markets like Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra during festive
items.quote: Like example, Tamil Nadu has done fairly very well for us during festive. So, some key markets during festive have done well. And we have also seen the positive impact on the volumes as well.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 29.7%, H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 30.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 29.7%.

items.statement: Gross margin stable at 62.6% in Q2 and 62.8% in H1 FY26
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR140 crores, a growth of 7% Y-o-Y, with a GP margin of 62.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: H1 FY26 net store additions 36 taking total store count to 812
items.quote: During the first half of FY '26, we added 36 new stores on a net basis, taking our store count total to 812.

items.statement: No major store closures expected; consolidation completed last year
items.quote: I don't think we will see any store closures. I think majority of the consolidation, what we had done was completed last year.

items.statement: Churidars and leggings share stabilized at 35% vs pre-COVID 50-55%
items.quote: And post-COVID, it has slowly settled at being at about 35% because the other categories, the trousers category has done fairly really well and has picked up in volumes.

items.statement: Trousers and pants category growing strongly driving product mix shift
items.quote: So, I think the change in fashion from legging to trousers obviously has played a huge role in this for sure.

items.statement: 70-80% of sales from products below INR1,000 price point
items.quote: From a contribution perspective, 70% to 80% will be less than INR1,000.

items.statement: Products above INR1,000 reduced from 12% to 5% of portfolio after GST rate cut benefit passed to consumers
items.quote: So it's going from 12% to 5%, correct.

items.statement: No price hikes taken; ASP growth driven by new product launches
items.quote: No, we have not done any price hikes. In 1 or 2 products, we have done some price corrections, but those were lower volume products.

items.statement: New customer acquisition above 20% and repeat rates 40-45% in EBO network
items.quote: New customer acquisitions are healthy and above 20% in our overall EBO network, what we are seeing and repeat rates are in the same range of 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Customer age profile stable at 27-33 years with younger audience also growing
items.quote: I think we have seen that consistently stay the same. A majority of the consumers who are shopping with us are in that bucket of 27 and 33.

items.statement: No significant competition from value retailers in Tier 2/3 at INR800-900 ASP
items.quote: We've been present across so many stores of Reliance and many stores of V-Mart as well in Tier 2, Tier 3, and we are seeing very good traction for our ASP, higher ASP products as well.

items.statement: Other current assets increase due to fabric import advances INR15-16 crore
items.quote: Mainly, we have some advances for fabrics, which we'll be closing now when the imports are being done. That is the basic difference.

items.statement: Pledged shares to be reduced by 50% (25-30 lakh shares) over next few months
items.quote: We are on track to reduce more than 50% of the pledge soon. So, I think the reduction on the pledge will happen soon. And whenever it does happen, we will release it to the stock exchange.

items.statement: Income tax search conducted Oct 7-10 at 4 premises; no major findings
items.quote: As of now, from what we have seen and how they have concluded the search, there have been no major findings and nothing to be concerned about.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth muted but uniform across all store vintages and regions
items.quote: Our oldest store also is mid-single digit or low single-digit SSSG. So, I think the SSSG is very uniform across stores of all the financial years.

items.statement: West and North India positive SSSG; South India a drag on like-to-like growth
items.quote: West India has consistently done well, like Maharashtra even now has been positive SSSG. Gujarat has been positive SSSG. North also has done well for us. South obviously has been a little bit of a drag.

items.statement: MBO channel growing at healthy double-digit rate though base is small
items.quote: Qualitatively, we're growing the business, and we are seeing a healthy double-digit growth in that business.

items.statement: New everyday wear pilot stores achieving >INR1,000/sq ft/month sales in Chennai
items.quote: We are achieving more than INR1,000 a square foot of sales per month, SPSF, which is the number what we targeted.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance cut due to weak SSSG and revenue growth to protect P&L margins
items.quote: We didn't want to take a pressure on the P&L as well. I think to be very brutally honest, I also didn't guide well, honestly. And that's why I'm also correcting it now.

items.statement: IOCL contract worth INR 110 crores over 5 years signed in October, largely IoT-led with hardware component of INR 10-15 crores
items.quote: We should all be happy with the INR110 crores contract over a period of 5 years and think about the revenue generation over every year. Now that kind of a business is largely IoT-led. I'm not saying it's only IoT-led, the hardware component might not be more than INR10-15 crores out of total 100 crores.

items.statement: Survey of India contract signed for national geospatial platform, value not disclosed
items.quote: In the space of geospatial, we worked very hard in Q2 and in October, we achieved it in terms of a contract of a good-sized value with Survey of India. Since they have not disclosed the value; we are not at liberty to disclose the exact value also.

items.statement: DMRC signed MoU with MapmyIndia for data sharing and commercial expansion
items.quote: The first step of that has happened where DMRC, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, has already signed an MoU, which is not only just the data sharing between Metro and MapMyIndia, but also gives full scope to the commercial expansion and doing things for DMRC.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of INR 1,000 crores remains unchanged
items.quote: Yes, your thinking is right. FY '28 goal is definitely not changing.
