So, you can safely assume something between 20 to 25% or 22.5% for safer side.

items.statement: Fastener division revenue Rs 44 crores in H1 FY26, up 84% YoY; Chennai plant monthly sales ramp from Rs 1 crore (August) to Rs 82 lakhs (September) to Rs 3+ crores (October)
items.quote: The fastener division delivered the strongest results, with revenue for the first half of 2026 standing at Rs. 44 crores, registering 84% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Chennai plant manufacturing load ramp: July Rs 1 crore, October Rs 4 crores, targeting Rs 5 crores in January 2026
items.quote: So, July we gave the load of 1 crore and that started ramp up to 2 crore, 3 crore and in October we reached to a load of 4 crore, number one. So, this is what we are calling a more manufacturing value load given to the plant.

items.statement: Competitors: Fasteners - Sundaram Partners, Randack (Germany), August Friedberg, Dokka Fasteners (Norway), Cooper & Turner (UK); Disc springs - Mubea, Schnorr, Christian Bauer (Germany), Key Bellevilles (US); Coil springs - NHK Spring (Japa
items.value: Multiple global and domestic competitors per segment
items.quote: In fasteners we mainly compete with Sundaram Partners and Randack which is a German company having plant in Pune and for exports in fasteners we compete with German manufacturers like August Friedberg, Dokka Fasteners in Norway or Cooper and Turner based in UK. As far as the disc springs are concerned, we mainly compete with German producer Mubea, Schnorr and Christian Bauer and some American prod

items.statement: Cash flow generation takes second priority during high growth phase (20%+); inventory and debtor norms (85-90 days) constrain cash conversion
items.quote: But in growth phase, we have to take little bit second priority to the cash flow generation particularly, when we are targeting a growth of above 20% or growth like 25% because these are the industry norm where we have to give debtor 90 days or 85 to 90 days or we have to keep multiple SKU material or FG.

items.statement: Employee cost as % of revenue expected to improve by 0.5-1% but premature to guide due to capability additions for growth
items.quote: As far as the employee cost is concerned, this is the number which should further improve by some half percentage to one percentage, but I do not want to give any as of now indication because in growth phase, we have to then keep on adding some capabilities at different level.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target of 15% and EBITDA margin of 33-34%
items.quote: As guided earlier, we are confident of achieving 15% revenue growth in FY26 and EBITDA margin between 33% to 34%.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 15% annual revenue growth with 1-2% yearly EBITDA and PAT margin expansion
items.value: 15% revenue growth; 1-2% EBITDA margin expansion per year; 1-2% PAT margin expansion per year
items.quote: Yes, top line we would carry on increasing 15% year-on-year. Our EBITDA margin, I believe should increase by 1% to 2% every year and PAT margin should also increase by 1% to 2%.

items.statement: Annual organic capex of INR70 crores for new centres
items.quote: So, we have been talking about investing around INR70 crores every year in making new centers organically

items.statement: Plan to add 12-15 own centres in FY26 (5 large, 13 small); 7 small and 2 large already opened
items.quote: We are on track to adding 12 to 15 centres this financial year, as committed earlier.

items.statement: Network grew to 63 centres at end of September 2025 including 2 Fetomat centres
items.quote: With these additions, our network grew to 63 centres at the end of September 2025, including two centres of Fetomat Wellness, which were added in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: 33% of centres (21 out of 63) not yet mature; 15 centres less than one year old
items.quote: 33% of our centres are not matured yet. In fact, 15 centres are less than one year old.

items.statement: Mature centres (42) at 37-38% EBITDA margin; new centres diluting overall margin to 31.7% in Q2
items.quote: In terms of profitability, our 42 matured centers have an EBITDA margin of 37% to 38%, but our 21 new centers, out of which 15 centers are less than a year-old impact the overall EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 31.7% impacted by floods (INR3.5 cr revenue loss) and Durga Puja timing
items.quote: The margins during the quarter were adversely impacted by heavy rainfall and floods, as well as seasonal festivities.

items.statement: Sustained strong demand and market expansion driving revenue growth
items.quote: For Suraksha, revenue growth has remained strong, reflecting sustained demand and successful market expansion, supported by strong operational execution.

items.statement: Mature centres growing at ~10% same-store sales growth
items.quote: Our matured centers are growing at around 10%.

items.statement: Realisation per test fell from INR389 to INR364 due to new centre discounts and higher B2B share (7%)
items.quote: So, this is because like you rightly mentioned, we do give discounts in the new centers that we set up to -- for traction of patients. That is one. And second is we have increased our B2B business, if you will see by 1%, and that normally consists of packages. Therefore, realization -- discounted packages, therefore, realization per test is a little lower.

items.statement: GST rate cut on medical inputs (12% to 5%) yields minor cost reduction; COGS only 12-13% of revenue
items.quote: Yes, we do see a reduction. But what we have to understand is that our total cost of goods sold is around 12% to 13%. And therefore, a little bit of impact of the GST from 12% to 5% is not very meaningful as far as our business is concerned.

items.statement: Radiology 48%, Pathology 52% of revenue; mix stable year-on-year
items.quote: Radiology is, non-path is 48%, pathology is 52%.

items.statement: B2C 93%, B2B 7% of revenue in H1; B2B includes hospital tie-ups and corporate clients like Reliance
items.quote: Yes. So, our B2C is 93% and B2B is 7%.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate ~30% year-on-year; loyalty scheme software under development (2+ quarters)
items.quote: Yes, our repeat customer rate is around 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: B2B revenue share expected to rise driven by genomics lab serving hospitals/nursing homes
items.quote: Yes. So, our B2B business will definitely increase going forward. Also, on account of the genomic lab setup that we have done, this business generally comes from hospitals and nursing homes.

items.statement: Dominance in Eastern India to persist; market under-penetrated with scope for deeper penetration
items.quote: We believe that given our scale and deep knowledge of the market, our dominance in Eastern India will persist. Even at current levels, the market remains under-penetrated and offers compelling opportunities to enhance our footprint and catalyze the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Rental expenses INR11 crores in H1 FY26; up INR80 lakhs in Q2 due to new centres
items.quote: H1 we have rentalof INR11 crores. H1.

items.statement: Balance sheet underleveraged; can raise debt for acquisitions but currently funding growth via internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, we are and we have a fairly underleveraged balance sheet. So, if required, we can always raise debt, but right now, whatever we are doing is through internal accruals.

items.statement: Fetomat acquisition: INR55 lakhs revenue in H1; remaining stake to be acquired in 3-5 years
items.quote: We have for the H1 noted around INR55 lakhs of revenue and we are very much on track with this Genomics business.

items.statement: Expansion strategy: inorganic in geographies with established players (adjoining states), organic in vacant markets (Northeast)
items.quote: So, we are definitely entering new geographies and our strategy is if there is an established player, then we would like to go for inorganic growth. But if not, then we would set up our own centres.

items.statement: Dividend planned; still working on it
items.quote: Yes, we are still working on it, but we definitely do plan.

items.statement: Corporate overhead includes reference lab and head office; lab capacity at 2.5x current volumes enabling operating leverage
items.quote: Yes. So, our reference lab is under corporate expense and so are all the seniors and the expense that we incur at the HO. And, our lab has a capacity of doing 2.5x the number of tests it does today.

items.statement: Tests performed 4.13M in H1 FY26 (+25% YoY); patients served 0.71M (+16% YoY); revenue per patient INR2,120 (+1% YoY)
items.quote: In H1 FY 2026, the number of tests performed reached INR4.13 million, compared to INR3.29 million in the same period in the previous year. The number of patients served increased to 0.71 million, compared to 0.61 million in H1 of FY25. The revenue per patient increased to INR2,120 compared to INR2,099 in H1 FY 2025.

items.statement: Floods caused ~4 days of 10% normal business; INR3.5 cr revenue shortfall in Q2; patients from districts unable to travel
items.quote: So, there was a -- the whole city was having torrential rainfall and obviously a lot of flood happening in the city, so we don't expect patients to travel then, neither do we expect doctors to be practicing. Therefore, you know, four days we practically were doing 10% of our regular business.

items.statement: New centre losses: INR3 cr EBITDA loss in H1 on INR13 cr revenue; 7 of 15 sub-year centres breakeven
items.quote: Total, in terms of revenue, it was around INR1.37 crores. I mean, what we have incurred was INR13 crores, against which INR3 crores was the EBITDA loss.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 15-20% moving forward
items.quote: On the margin side, I've always said the EBITDA margin will always be in the range of 15% to 20% moving forward. So that's the target of the company, and that's what we should be achieving moving forward as an organization.

items.statement: Profitability range 15-22% for current competencies
items.quote: For the current competencies that we're in, the profitability will always be in the range of 15% to 22%. That's what we're looking at for our current competencies.

items.statement: Confirmed orders over INR720 crores, strategic agreements INR2,500 crores, bids submitted INR920 crores this quarter
items.value: 720 crores confirmed, 2500 crores strategic, 920 crores bids
items.quote: Today we have confirmed orders of over INR720 crores with strategic agreements of INR2,500 crores. This quarter, we've also submitted bids to the tune of INR920 crores to different companies, which are weighted decisions during the course of the year.

items.statement: Confirmed POs INR750 crores with 2-3 year execution, strategic agreement POs placed 6-12 months before delivery
items.quote: So the INR750 crores of confirmed POs we have on hand, I would say, the average execution time then would be two to three years for that. For the balanced strategic agreements, like I mentioned earlier, POs are placed through the strategic agreement six to 12 months before deliveries.

items.statement: Bids submitted close to INR990 crores this quarter
items.quote: Yes, we've submitted bids for close to INR990 crores this quarter, which are weighted decisions through the course of the year.

items.statement: Momentum to continue through next two quarters driving transformative growth in FY26
items.quote: With a robust order pipeline and strong execution capabilities, we are confident that this momentum will continue through the next two quarters, driving transformative growth in financial year 2026.

items.statement: Semiconductor and space revenue ~20-25% this year, targeting ~40% next year
items.value: 20% to 25% this year, closer to 40% next year
items.quote: Ending of this year, it would be approximately 20% to 25% of our revenue would be through semiconductor and space. And next year, it would increase and it would be closer to 40% of our total revenue with these new customers.

items.statement: Major capacity expansion of 150,000 sq ft at INR70 crores, construction starts Q4 FY26, operational in 18 months
items.quote: On the capex side, to support the execution of the substantial new orders we received, Rossell Techsys, is undertaking a major capacity expansion of 150,000 square feet within its existing premises and at an estimated cost of INR70 crores. Construction is scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of this financial year, and the facility is expected to be operational within 18 months.

items.statement: Current 225,000 sq ft facility expanding to 375,000 sq ft
items.quote: Today, we only have one plant. We have a 225,000-square-foot facility in Devanahalli, Bangalore. So, all the manufacturing is done from that one unit and we are planning to expand that facility in the same campus by another 150,000 square feet. So, we should be -- from 225,000, we'll go up to 375,000 square feet.

items.statement: Evaluating QIP up to INR300 crores for capex and working capital, targeting closure by end of December
items.quote: To fuel this growth, we are actively evaluating a fundraise up to INR300 crores through a qualified institution placement, which is a QIP, which will strengthen our balance sheet and enable investments in future-ready capabilities. The major objectives of this fundraise will be for capex and for Working capital.

items.statement: QIP expected to close in 45 days by end of December
items.quote: So another, I would say 45 days, the QIP should be closed. So that's the intent of the company by end of December, that the QIP process is completed.

items.statement: QIP proceeds sufficient for next three years till FY2029
items.quote: I would say, this should meet us for the next three years. So, up to the financial year 2029.

items.statement: Closing inventory INR286.37 crores, up INR32.58 crores QoQ, strategically aligned to FY26 revenue targets
items.quote: Our closing inventory today stands at INR286.37 crores, reflecting an increase of INR32.58 crores over the previous quarter. This is strategically aligned to fuel our ambitions for the year 2026 revenue targets.

items.statement: Target to become 3-month inventory company, significant improvement expected by end of FY26 and FY27
items.quote: The goal of the company is to be a four-term inventory company. That means a three-month inventory moving forward. So, we have a plan to get to those numbers. It will take a bit of time, but the plan is set out.

items.statement: Onboarded Senthil Balasubramanian as CEO with 30 years aerospace/defense experience
items.quote: We have recently onboarded Mr. Senthil Balasubramanian as the Chief Executive Officer of the company. He's a seasoned aerospace and defense professor with 30 years of global experience including a decade at Collins Aerospace and a tenur e as a Country General Manager at ITT Interconnect

items.statement: Workforce 1,092 strong with 856 on-role employees
items.quote: On the people front, we now have 1,092 strong workforce with 856 people on role employees, backed by continuous focus on skill development and capability building.

items.statement: DSIR license renewed through March 2027, cleared Stage 1 AS9110 audit, CMMC 2.0 compliance prep for November 2026
items.quote: On the innovation and compliance front, our DSIR license has been renewed through March 2027. We cleared Stage 1 AS9110 audit and are moving closer to full certification, while preparations for CMMC 2.0 compliance are underway for November 2026.

items.statement: Applied for AS9110 MRO license, expect to secure within 30 days
items.quote: The company has already applied for an AS9110 license, which is the MRO license. We should be able to secure that within the next 30 days.

items.statement: Active dialogues with Airbus, visited recently, hoping to start relationship soon
items.quote: On the Airbus side, we've visited them recently and active dialogues are happeni ng with Airbus. And hopefully, we're hoping that we can start a relationship with them sooner than later

items.statement: Tri-party agreement with Interconnect Systems for Lockheed Martin end-customer
items.quote: No, with Interconnect what we're doing the end customer is Lockheed Martin. And we have a tri-party agreement with -- I mean, you can call it a tri-party agreement between the three companies. So we supply our products to Interconnect and in return, they give that to Lockheed Martin.

items.statement: Localization saves foreign OEMs 20-30% cost, active dialogue to increase India content
items.quote: By localizing a lot of different components in India, we know that the cost savings are over 20% to 30% for our different foreign OEMs that we work with. So, they are saving a lot of money by buying that material from India.

items.statement: Margins lower due to FAI learning curve on new semiconductor/space contracts, automation being introduced to improve efficiency
items.quote: When we get new contracts, especially in the semiconductor and the space segments, it requires a lot of learning. It requires a lot of training that needs to take place, where obviously your efficiency levels are not at its best. Once the product is qualified, like I'm saying, our profit goes up, our efficiency levels get better, we get more lean. We're introducing a lot of automation into the com

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve in Q3/Q4 FY26, target 15-22% range
items.quote: This year itself, in the third and fourth quarter, you should see a change coming in our percentage of EBITDA, and it should get much healthier. And moving forward, very confident it's going to be in the range of 15% to 22%.

items.statement: Win rate slightly over 50% on bids submitted
items.quote: Yes. So, the win rate has been probably slightly over 50%. It's very difficult to tell a percentage because, the number of proposals, what we submit, the value of those proposals vary.

items.statement: Tariff changes not impacting as most customers availed tariff benefits, implemented entitlement tracking for duty-free US entry
items.quote: Most of our customers have availed tariff benefits, so the recent changes have not impacted us at all. Furthermore, we implemented a robust entitlement number tracking system for all defense shipments, ensuring seamless compliance and enabling duty-free entry into the United States.

items.statement: R&D developing in-house wiring analyzer for cable testing
items.quote: We've already developed one. It needs to be qualified, which is a wiring analyzer. So, that's something that's being focused because we use that for our in-house needs. All the cables that we produce need to be tested and we've decided to develop an in-house tester.

items.statement: Expects AGM to remain strong in coming quarters as rare earth supply issue resolved in Q2
items.quote: We expect this to be a one -time hit as the issue was resolved through the course of Q2. So, we don't expect this to repeat in Q3, making us reasonably confiden t about AGM in the coming quarters

items.statement: Believes current portfolio can reach sustainable EBITDA positive without relying on EL platform
items.quote: I think the current portfolio should be strong enough to take us to a sustainable basis standalone. To us internally, EL always has been the product that drives future growth, as opposed to a product that we desperately need to get to break even or

items.statement: Expects EV scooter industry to grow 4x-5x faster than overall two-wheeler industry
items.quote: And within scooters, I believe electric scooters will grow at 2x to 2.5x the growth of the overall scooter market. So that would be a compounding multiplier. So this would be about 4x to 5x faster than the overall two wheeler industry.

items.statement: Festive demand very strong with retail outstripping wholesale and stockouts across experience centres
items.quote: I think recent months have been the first few months where the retail has been ou tstripping wholesale by a considerable margin, and we are working hard to fill that gap up

items.statement: October registrations over 30,000 units at nearly 50% YoY growth with slim channel inventory
items.quote: You saw Vahan numbers in October. You saw more than 30,000 registrations for us, which is at almost a 50% growth over last year, and I can tell you we were – we were stocked out

items.statement: Q2 adjusted gross margin 22% (21% without incentives), up 300 bps YoY and 100 bps QoQ without incentives
items.quote: Adjusted gross margin on an absolute basis was INR210 crores and on a percentage basis was 22%, which is a 300 bps improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA loss under 10% (INR90 cr), 1100 bps YoY and 600 bps QoQ improvement
items.quote: Overall EBITDA came in at lower than negative 10%. The first time we have touched single-digit EBITDA losses in any quarter. 1,100 bps improvement year-on-year and a strong 600 bps improvement quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Rare earth supply crunch caused ~INR20-25 cr EBITDA hit and ~INR20 cr unclaimed subsidy in Q2
items.quote: Even here, the rare earth hit was almost about INR20-25 crores overall. So EBITDA has come in strong.

items.statement: Q2 units sold 66,000, up 67% YoY and 42% QoQ; added 26,000 incremental units vs 23,000 in Q1
items.quote: Units sold were up at 66,000 units, which is a 67% growth year-on-year and a 42% growth quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: New Aurangabad plant delayed 2-3 months due to environment clearances; EL production to start from Hosur to protect timeline
items.quote: On the new plant, there was, I think, a two, three -month delay because of the delay in obtaining environment clearances, but that's be hind us. Work has begun in full swing. To ensure that EL does not struggle because of the delay of the new plant, we have a plan of commencing EL production out of Hosur itself as an early measure to protect EL timelines

items.statement: Fast charging network at nearly 4,300 points across India
items.quote: Our fast chargers are up at almost 4,300 points across the country, making this a very important part of our entire value proposition to our customers.

items.statement: Launched high-range variants (160km) on 450S and Rizta S filling low-tech high-range portfolio gap
items.quote: We finally filled that gap up with the introduction of low-range models on 450S and Rizta S, sorry, the high-range options on 450S and Rizta S with about 160 kilometers of range each.

items.statement: Launched Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) reducing Rizta S upfront price to INR76,000; attach rates low single digits but serves as customer comfort tool
items.quote: In Q2, we also launched Battery as a Service, BaaS, which allowed us to reduce our upfront price of Rizta S to as low as INR76,000. This is an important top-of-the-funnel introduction.

items.statement: Unveiled EL platform with 14-inch wheels, integrated AC/DC charger-motor controller, electronic braking system (AEBS) for launch next year
items.quote: EL is going to bring to the market Ather's first 14-inch wheel in scooters. We are also launching Ather Charge Driv e Controller, AC/DC, which is our integrated charger and motor controller module

items.statement: Launched AtherStack 7.0 with pothole alerts, crash alerts, voice features; 89% attach rate and 12% non-vehicle revenue contribution
items.quote: On the business front, this entire suite continues to pay again strong dividends with an attach rate of 89% for customers for AtherStack and a 12% contribution for non-vehicle revenue.

items.statement: Pan-India market share 17.4-17.5% in Q2; Middle India share jumped from 4% (Q1 FY25) to 14.5% (Q2 FY26)
items.quote: Market share came in at 17.5%, 17.4%. Over the last six, seven quarters, our market share has been broadl y on an upswing

items.statement: Gujarat 20-25% share, Maharashtra ~15%, MP >10% (mid-teens in Oct), Rest of India first time 10% share, J&K >40% share #1 position
items.quote: Gujarat, we have been consistently doing 20%, 25% market share now, cementing us a very strong player there. Maharashtra, we have now started to do almost 15%, market share.

items.statement: South India 25% market share, #1 in all South states in October; density expansion in Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala
items.quote: Q2, we have hit 25% market share, becoming number one in all of South zone once again. I know this is Q3, but still want to call out, in October, we were number one in every single state in all of South.

items.statement: Added 78 stores in Q2, total 524 experience centres; on track for ~700 stores by year-end
items.quote: We added 78 stores, taking our total store count to 524, and keeping us on a strong path for our ambition of nearly 700 stores later this year.

items.statement: New stores mature in 3-4 quarters for dealer profitability; Pro Pack attach rates rise from 40-50% to 70-75% within quarters
items.quote: Typically, we are seeing new stores stabilize in three to four quarters. I would say, again, depends a lot on the exact city, the exact variant mix, but I would say a few quarters, three, four quarters is a reas onable estimate for dealer profitability

items.statement: ASPs extremely steady across geographies including new markets; able to take price hikes in strong markets like 450
items.quote: Fascinatingly, though, our ASPs have been extremely steady. I think the customer landed price, ex-showroom average of vehicle plus pro pack, is probably within a few hundred rupees over the last several quarters now.

items.statement: Cost reduction driven by engineering (LFP share increase, BOM improvements, warranty cost reduction) despite forex headwind
items.quote: I think cost did come down by, I think overall underlying gross margins have improved by 100-150 bps this quarter, accounting for subsidy. I think part of that has been the increasing attach share of business of LFP batteries, but also constant cost reduction by R&D.

items.statement: Not a fan of mandating ABS; portfolio mostly has front disc brakes so ABS cost impact limited to module; developing AEBS as alternative
items.quote: Personally, I'm not a big fan of mandating it. But it's a much larger industry conversation. If ABS is mandated, I think we will obviously prepare for it. Particularly for us, almost our entire portfolio has front disc brake. So, some of the cost that would increase because of ABS is not a challenge.

items.statement: Accessory attach rates in mature markets like Gujarat reached 60-75%; service revenues compounding
items.quote: In the last three, four quarters, we have seen accessory attached rates in G ujarat go up as much as 60% -75%, while newer stores are obviously not that focused on accessories right now

items.statement: Rare earth supply crunch caused one-time Q2 hit; resolved during quarter and not expected to repeat
items.quote: There was a one-time impact because of the rare earth supply crunch in Q2, wherein we had to change our supply chain and because of which the majority of vehicles in Q2 we have not filed for subsidy.

items.statement: Sub-INR1 lakh segment growth was artificially pushed; industry migrating to >INR1 lakh where real organic growth is strong
items.quote: I think the kind of volume that we were seeing out of that segment in those quarters was not strictly fundamental. I think a lot of it was like sort of pushed growth as opposed to real organic growth.

items.statement: Core gases revenue CAGR of 20-25% over next 4-5 years with EBITDA margins around 40%
items.quote: We expect to grow at the CAGR of 20 to 25% over the next four to five years in our core gases segment, considering the last full year financial numbers as a base and all this while maintaining EBITDA margins of around 40%.

items.statement: Total owned and operated capacity to reach 1910 TPD by end FY26 and over 2100 TPD by end FY27
items.quote: These expansions will take our total owned and operated capacity to 1910 tons per day by end of this financial year and over 2100 tons per day by end of next financial year enabling us to serve a more diversified set of industries and geographies.

items.statement: Merchant plant in East India to go live end of October, onsite plant in East India by March 2026, another merchant plant in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our merchant plant in East India is on track to go live end of this month. We also expect to commission our onsite plant in East India by March 2026 followed by another merchant plant in FY27.

items.statement: Strong demand from steel, pharma, chemicals, healthcare, semiconductors, green energy and space research driving sector growth
items.quote: The Indian industrial gases sector is poised for strong growth driven by demand from steel, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, Healthcare and emerging areas such as semiconductors, green energy and space research.

items.statement: Argon now contributes 13% of total revenues with higher margins than other gases, targeting further growth
items.quote: We are strengthening our distribution infrastructure and focusing on high margin value added gases such as Argon which now contributes 13% of our total revenues.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin stable at 38%, long-term target around 40%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at rupees 337 million, maintaining a stable margin of 38%, which we view as a clear validation of our operational discipline and cost management.

items.statement: Argon prices may fluctuate short-term but structural demand-supply imbalance supports long-term bullish outlook
items.quote: However, prices of Argon which while we are bullish on them in the long term due to structural demand supply issues may exhibit short-term fluctuations.

items.statement: New capacity includes contracted onsite plant with fixed monthly fee, not dependent on utilization
items.quote: The second capacity which we are coming with at the end of this financial year, that's a Contracted capacity with a single customer where our revenues will not be dependent on the capacity utilization.

items.statement: Kurnool plant utilization improved from 65% in Q1 to 75-80% in Q2, other plants running at full capacity
items.quote: Kurnool is the ramp up has happened beyond 65% which was in Q1. Now we'd be at the number which is, you know, closer to 75-80%.

items.statement: 220 TPD plant capex frozen, revenue potential of 100+ crore annually still holds, power connection received
items.quote: I think this 220 plant is anyway, you know, about to be commissioned. So, you know Capex is obviously frozen revenue from that plant. I think the revenue potential of 100 plus crores you know still holds.

items.statement: GST on medical oxygen reduced from 12% to 5%, no change for industrial gases
items.quote: For products such as medical oxygen, the GST has actually been reduced from 12% to 5%. Making it of course much more affordable to our end use customers.

items.statement: Developing capabilities for ultra-high purity gases for solar cell manufacturing, margins significantly higher than average for manufactured products, 15-20% for traded products
items.quote: The margins here, at least for the manufactured products that we are making in house, will be significantly higher than the average company margins. But, however, for traded products, of course, because they are traded products, you know, naturally the margins would not be as high as a manufactured product, but it would still, you know, probably be in somewhat of 15 to 20% kind of a margin on the

items.statement: Western India expansion planned as merchant model, site more or less finalized but not yet announced
items.quote: Uh, so uh, we are looking at West as a merchant model. I think there's significant demand there. A lot of new industries coming in as well. Uh site uh for the plant has more or less been finalized, but I think we are not in a position to make an announcement yet.

items.statement: Project execution delays of 1-2 quarters possible, but long-term growth trajectory intact
items.quote: I would say that this is one of the key risks. Uh, that uh, you know any growing business in our sector faces which is you know this small delays in project execution. While it doesn't change the long term trajectory of the business, I think on a shorter term basis you may find that, you know a revenue which was expected to come let's say in Q3 will come in Q4 and things like that.

items.statement: H2 FY26 expected stronger due to new capacity ramp-up and existing capacity utilization
items.quote: So, H2 will be stronger, uh, just from the fact that we have new capacity coming in. So, we would expect H2 to be stronger.

items.statement: Hydrogen electrolyzer pilot ramping up, will be integrated with future air separation plants, not expected to be meaningful revenue contributor
items.quote: Having said that, yes, hydrogen, the hydrogen electrolyzer is also you know, capacity there is being ramped up and of course while it still remains a very small business, but you know this is something that we want to replicate whenever we are setting up our air separation plants in future.

items.statement: Power prices at multi-year lows protecting margins despite product price corrections
items.quote: We've also see also you know we've got to keep in mind that power prices are also corrected, right. So, power pricing is at the multi-year low. And you know given that even if price is correct, our margin remains protected.

items.statement: No short-term quarterly or half-yearly guidance, only long-term 4-5 year CAGR target of 20-25% for core gases
items.quote: Again, yeah, just to be consistent and you know to reiterate, I think we are looking at a long term guidance, you know over four to five years with last year as a base because last year was the last full year number available, based on that full year number, we are looking at a 20 to 25% CAGR just on our core gases business.

items.statement: Targets 20,000-25,000 desk additions annually, slightly above industry growth of ~20%
items.quote: I think on a run rate basis, you should assume that we will basically try to grow slightly above the industry, which is growing at this 20-ish % range, which will translate to about 20,000 to 25,000 desk additions year-over-year for us.

items.statement: Targets upwards of 20% revenue growth for FY26, H1 run rate already near that level
items.quote: I think we are targeting upwards of 20% type of growth numbers, and we have already delivered that across a few of the revenue streams, if you see just from last year to today.

items.statement: Budgeted ~INR 100 crore per quarter, ~INR 1.3 lakh per desk; full year estimate INR 250-270 crore including refurbishment and stamp duty
items.quote: We are roughly spending about INR 100 crores every quarter. Having said that, this was a heavy quarter because we had some big management or managed office deals in the pipeline. So, I wouldn't consider that to be a run rate, but our cost is about a INR 1, 30,000 a desk.

items.statement: Operates 114,000 desks currently; 14,000 under fit-out, 15,000 under LOI; targets 130,000 by March 2026, 145,000 locked-in visibility
items.quote: We currently sit at about 114,000 desks. By the end of March, we already have about another 14,000-15,000 desks in fit-out. So, as of March, we will end at about 130,000 desk capacity. We also spoke about the fact that we have already LOIs and lease commitment signed of another 15,000 desks.

items.statement: Locked-in TCV of order book slightly over INR 2,400 crores as of Q2 FY26
items.quote: Today, we are sitting on nearly about 27 months of average commitment term, which was about 23 months last year, which means we have at least, I think order book is close to a little bit o ver INR 2,400 crores of TCV that we have locked in in the business as of today itself

items.statement: IGAAP-equivalent EBITDA margin 20.3% in Q2 FY26, up 530 bps QoQ; targets steady state over 20% for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We have in the last 2 years delivered around this 20- 21% EBITDA margin with the scalable growth. We will achieve a very similar level, if not slightly higher than what we have done in the past year over a much larger revenue base.

items.statement: Sales velocity 26,000 desks sold in H1 FY26 (~2M sq ft), up 40% QoQ and 62% YoY; on track for ~50,000 desks full year
items.quote: Sales velocity over the first half of this year has grown to close to about, we have delivered or sold about 26,000 desks. 26,000 desks is translating to nearly almost 2 million square foot of leasing that we have done in the first half of this year.

items.statement: Total ARPM ~INR 22,300 per desk in Q2 FY26; revenue-to-rent multiple stable at 3x total, 2.6x license revenue
items.quote: In fact, total ARPM, I would say for the quarter, stood at a nearly about INR 22,300 per desk, which includes every revenue stream, divided by the number of members.

items.statement: Net debt INR 311 crore (INR 119 crore post-IPO settlement), down from INR 529 crore YoY; cost of borrowing down 500 bps to 10.4%; targets net debt near zero by March 2026
items.quote: We currently stand at INR 310 crores as a net debt position. But considering the fact that we had an inflow of settlement of ICD through the OFS or through the IPO, we currently actually are at a net debt position of close to INR 119 crores.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 375 crore in Q2 FY26, up 16% QoQ and 11% YoY; free cash flow post-CAPEX negative INR 14 crore, improved from negative INR 47 crore QoQ
items.quote: Operating cash flow for the quarter was INR 375 crores, up 16% quarter -on-quarter and 11% year -on-year, driven by stronger EBITDA and improved working capital discipline.

items.statement: Enterprise ~75% of revenue, non-enterprise ~25%; VAS 11% of revenue, Digital Products 3%; no target mix but aims to grow both non-linearly
items.quote: Enterprise accounts remain the cornerstone of our portfolio, accounting to approximately about 75% of our business, where the remaining membership revenue of about 25% generated from non-enterprise clients including startups, SMEs and freelancers.

items.statement: Portfolio occupancy 80.2% in Q2 FY26; mature portfolio 84.2%, growth portfolio 51.7% (break-even)
items.quote: As of Quarter 2 FY '26, occupanc ies improved across mature and growth centers, reaching a portfolio level high of 80.2%, driven by the addition of approximately 4,600 occupied desks and an incremental recurring revenue of INR 39.4 crores

items.statement: Average membership tenure increased 17% YoY to 27 months; enterprise (>1000 FTE) tenure ~32 months; >50% desk sales from existing member expansion
items.quote: Our average membership tenure has increased nearly 17% from 23 months in Q2 last year to about 27 months in this quarter itself, reflecting stronger enterprise adoption and longer -term client commitments.

items.statement: Occupancy decline is biggest risk; mitigated by break-even occupancy ~55%, 2.7x revenue-to-lease liability cover, 75% enterprise mix, 27-month avg tenure, INR 2,400+ cr TCV locked in
items.quote: Occupancy always is . A nything that impacts occupancy or can suddenly drastically reduce occupancy continues to or will always be the biggest risk in the business.

items.statement: Targets 100% renewable energy by 2027 and 90% waste diversion by 2028; advancing Scope 3 measurement
items.quote: We have quantified our carbon footprint across S cope 1 and S cope 2, and now advancing into Scope 3 measurement, driving towards a 100% renewable energy target by 2027 and 90% waste diversion by 2028.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work 2025; 45% women representation, engagement score 86, employee NPS ~65
items.quote: WeWork India has been certified as a great place to work across all categories in 2025 with a 45% representation of women, a world-class engagement score of about 86 and an employee NPS of nearly 65.

items.statement: No M&A discussed; growth is organic via fit-outs and LOIs
items.quote: Our expansion will continue to be driven by disciplined and capital-efficient approach, ensuring sustainable and accretive growth. With multiple centres under Fit Out and LOI, we have strong visibility over the next few quarters.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned
items.quote: Our focus remains unchanged. We want to deliver the best workplace experience to our members while continuing to grow profitably, sustainably and responsibly.

items.statement: Low entry barrier for single center but high barrier at scale; differentiated by capital deployment, landlord relationships, brand, technology, full-stack product suite
items.quote: But this business, while it has a low entry point, it has an high barrier to entry at scale. Now to deliver and to reach revenue numbers, EBITDA numbers, and even this operational efficiency that the business has reached today, there is firstly the need to deploy a significant amount of capital over a period of time.

items.statement: Rent per RSF up 1.8% YoY; operating cost per RSF improved 5.3% YoY; center-level EBITDA margin 27.3%, up 420 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our rent per RSF increased just 1.8% year-on-year, while operating costs per RSF improved by 5.3% year -on-year. Center -level EBITDA margins improved to 27.3%, up 420 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: No export/FX exposure discussed
items.quote: We operate 70 centers across 8 cities, covering 7.7 million square foot and 1.15 lakh desks with about 94% of our portfolio in grey day developments.

items.statement: Enterprise (>1000 FTE) contributes ~60% revenue, tenure ~32 months; >50% desk sales from existing member expansion
items.quote: Within these large enterprises, which are companies over 1000 FTEs, contributed about 60% of our revenue and now maintain an average membership tenure of nearly 32 months, which is up from about 28 months a year ago.

items.statement: IPO completed; OFS proceeds used to retire high-cost debt; rights issue by promoter
items.quote: Equity infusion via rights issue, we were able to pay down some high-cost debt. We currently stand at INR 310 crores as a net debt position. But considering the fact that we had an inflow of settlement of ICD through the OFS or through the IPO.

items.statement: Launched WeWork India app as digital backbone for booking, engagement, insights, and new monetization
items.quote: This quarter, we will also launch the WeWork India app, which is the digital backbone of our business, tying our ecosystem together, enabling seamless booking, engagement, and insights, and potentially opening up new monetization streams for us.

items.statement: Global sugar market projected in mild surplus for SY25-26 due to higher production in Brazil, India, Thailand
items.quote: The global sugar market is projected to remain in mild surplus through Sugar Year 25-26, primarily due to increased production in Brazil, India and Thailand.

items.quote: Sugarcane output on account of increased yields and crop is likely to move up by 15% at an all-India level for Sugar Year '26. With the sugar output expected to move up and consumption marginally expected to move up to 28.5 MMT, it's very likely that sugar pricing may soften.

items.statement: Industry representing to policymakers for MSP revision, ethanol blend >20%, higher cane-based ethanol allocation and pricing
items.quote: the industry continues to make very active representation to the policymakers on revision of Minimum Support Price (MSP), increasing the blend percentage beyond 20% in the ethanol blending program, higher allocation towards sugarcane-based feedstock for ethanol and on better pricing for sugarcane-based ethanol.

items.statement: Karnataka government implemented additional INR 50/MT cane price over FRP due to farmer agitations
items.quote: Just last week, the government of Karnataka has declared an additional price of INR 50 per metric ton of cane over and above our FRP to be borne by all sugar mills in the state on account of intense farmer agitations.

items.statement: No imminent capacity addition plans; staying away from capex until sustainable policy framework clarity
items.quote: We're going to stay away from capex for some time. There isn't clarity on a sustainable policy framework as of yet.

items.statement: Distillery capacity 18 crore litres/year; expect to deliver 17 crore litres at 90%+ utilization with combined OMC and private allocations
items.quote: We have a capacity of about 18 crores litres in a year. We will deliver about 17 crores litres, which is the current estimate.

items.quote: I think that's got significantly impacted because of the changes in the government policy that's happened over the last couple of years. We expect the scenario to improve on the back of support from the government.

items.quote: So in the total quarter 2, I think about close to 35% to 40% is the non-sweetener revenue and the balance comes from the sweetener revenue.

items.quote: I think from the pulses and segment, there will be -- I think Q3, we're starting to see a little bit of better pricing. We expect that there's been a, you know, the crop is a little lower in India this year. So we see some better pricing to hold on the pulses side

items.quote: Currently, because of the supply surplus that's been explained by Muthu in the earlier part of the call, we have a big overhang on the supply side, which is resulting in white premiums being depressed because there's enough competition from the low-quality whites coming out of several geographies.

items.quote: we also strengthened the talent pool at Valensa to deliver a stronger business remit.

items.quote: That is generally year over year when our contracts are getting renewed. We aim to get at least a 4% to 5% increase in our rentals.

items.quote: Our direction over next four years, I would say, would be to get into strong double-digit EBITDA in the business, and that's what we are looking to.

items.statement: Expect roughly 20% year-on-year compounded growth

items.quote: On the balance sheet side, despite a moderate increase in inventory to support sales, we have maintained a healthy working capital cycle of 26 days, consistent with March '25 levels and an improvement of 7 days versus September '24.

items.statement: Net debt comfortable at INR 3.6 crores; long-term debt repayment initiated
items.quote: We have also initiated repayment of our long-term debt and our net debt position remains comfortable at INR3.6 crores.

items.statement: Blended gas cost at INR 43.3 per SCM in Q2, slightly lower than previous quarter
items.quote: Ashvath, in this quarter, our average gas cost was around INR43.3 per SCM and it is in line with the previous quarter, which was INR44.5. So slightly, it has reduced.

items.statement: Retail salience at 80%, projects at 20%; retail dependence increasing
items.quote: We have about an 80% of projects and 20% of retail -- sorry, 80% of retail and 20% of projects. We have been -- the dependence on retail has been going up.

items.statement: Selective price increases on 1-2 products; conservative on project discounts
items.quote: We have taken a price increase in 1 or 2 products, not across the board. We have just -- what we have chosen to do is be a bit more conservative on the discounts that we are giving out in projects and all.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization at 68% in Q2; improved vs Q1 and YoY
items.quote: We have planned, done about 68% capacity utilization for manufacturing in this quarter.

items.statement: No forward guidance given; H2 traditionally better than H1 for top line and margins
items.quote: Ashvath, we don't give forward guidance. You know that. As I said earlier, H2 for our industry and for most of Orient Bell is always in terms of both top line and margins, much better than H1.

items.statement: Marketing spend at 3.8% of revenue in Q2, similar to 3.7% last year
items.quote: This quarter also, we have invested 3.8% in marketing. Last year also, it was around 3.7%.

items.statement: Dealer destocking and inventory rationalization trend expected to continue
items.quote: I'm saying, the trend of dealers down stocking and rationalizing the stocks and all is very much there in the market, and I expect it to continue like that.

items.statement: Morbi unit closures and no new capacity positive for domestic market pricing
items.quote: A lot of units, Ashvath, in Morbi, seem to have closed down permanently, which are units, which were smaller units, which I realize that their cost of production is not really going to enable them to compete.

items.statement: Learning and development focus to empower employees for customer delight and sales
items.quote: Learning and development remains a key focus at Orient Bell, aimed at empowering employees to embrace customer delight and sales process.

items.statement: Manufacturing cost reduced 3.7% on like-for-like basis driving gross margin improvement
items.quote: On a like-for-like basis, approximately 3.7% is that we have saved on our manufacturing cost. This is the main contributor for the gross margin increase.

items.statement: Volume-led growth of 3% in Q2; ASP flat; strategy to continue pushing volumes
items.quote: Our volume growth, our 3% growth in quarter 2 has been led by volume growth and not by a growth in ASP. That would give you a direction which the company is moving.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 6% in Q2; operating leverage critical for margin repair
items.quote: With respect to our margins, we had a 6% EBITDA margin this year. In our size of business, we are very -- the operating leverage plays an extremely critical role.

items.statement: Government projects execution, gas costs, geopolitical environment and tariff wars remain decisive factors
items.quote: We maintain as per our previous commentary that government projects execution gas costs, geopolitical environment and tariff wars continue as decisive factors impacting demand across the building and construction industry.

items.statement: Tier 1 at 23%, Tier 2 at 18%, Tier 3 at 59% in H1; growth across all tiers
items.quote: See, the data is not very definitive on this. We are kind of Tier 1 is about 23%-odd in H1 for us and Tier 2 is about 18%, Tier 3 is 59%.

items.statement: Adhesive business leveraging existing manpower and assets; no new capex
items.quote: As I said earlier also, we are not encouraging -- we are not incurring any capex. We are leveraging a lot of our existing manpower and other assets.

items.statement: Adhesive products priced at premium to other manufacturers, slight discount to industry leaders
items.quote: In terms of pricing, this industry again has a very large number of players, but what I can tell you is that we are priced at a premium to the other manufacturers who do adhesives. We are clear. We are at a slight discount to the leaders in this industry.

items.statement: Epoxy and grout products in pipeline for adhesive range
items.quote: Yes, we are now working on epoxy and grout and all, which is something which we would launch in the coming months, so that whole range would slowly get completed.

items.statement: Experience centers additions slower; priority on strengthening existing OBTBs
items.quote: We are adding new experience centers, Orient Bell Tiles Boutique already called it, but a bigger priority this year is to strengthen the customer experience in our existing OBTBs, so the gross tabs will not be as high as what they were last year.

items.statement: Indian auto industry saw steady improvement end of Q2 FY26; H1 2-wheeler domestic sales up 1%, exports up 24%; H2 expected double-digit growth lifting FY26 domestic sales 5-7%
items.quote: The Indian automobile industry witnessed steady improvement towards the end of Q2 FY '26, supported by the rollout of GST 2.0, early festive demand and improving customer sentiment.

items.statement: Standalone fastener business full-year growth target 5-7% for FY26; on track to achieve
items.quote: I think at the beginning of the year, we said we'll probably grow at 5% to 7% for the full year and we are on track to do that in our standalone business on a full year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin and PBT before exceptional items flat YoY in Q2 FY26; confident H2 will be slightly better than H1
items.quote: Our first half numbers bear that out that we have been able to maintain our EBITDA margin and we are quite confident the second half will probably be a shade better than what we have in the first half.

items.statement: New customer traction including Hyundai onboarding; non-scooter MCU customers (LCV, HCV) now >25% of SEM revenue, 2-wheeler ~60%
items.quote: Those customers today contribute more than 25% of our total revenue. And our 2-wheeler business is about 60% of our total revenue now.

items.statement: SEM expanded into integrated motors and MCUs, rare earth magnet-free motors, onboard/off-board chargers, DC/DC converters; STML to start HVDC contactors/relays production Dec 2025
items.quote: Building on our current strong foundation in motor control units, SEM has now expanded into integrated motors and MCUs, rare earth magnet -free motors, onboard and off -board chargers and DC/DC converters.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR50 cr for existing businesses: SEM INR10-15 cr, STML ~INR10 cr, fastener ~INR25 cr; additional greenfield capex for new products to be finalized in 3-6 months
items.quote: So altogether put together, we are looking at about a INR50 crores capex for the existing businesses we have. And for the additional new products we may launch, that will be on top of this.

items.statement: STML Bengaluru fully automated facility to start commercial production of HVDC contactors and relays in December 2025; revenue potential INR200 cr within 5 years
items.quote: Our STML subsidiary will start commercial production of HVDC contactors and relays in December '25 at its state -of-the-art fully automated manufacturing facility in Bengaluru.

items.statement: HVDC contactor market currently INR300-400 cr in India, expected to reach >INR1,000 cr by end of decade; EV subset 60-70%
items.quote: the market currently would be in the tune of INR300 crores to INR400 crores in India, is growing every year and we expect this market to go up to upwards of INR1,000 crores by the end of this decade

items.statement: OBC and power electronics market potential ~INR2,000 cr by 2030; targeting 15-20% market share
items.quote: we are projecting at most 15% to 20% market share. So we are looking at -- so another way to say that we're looking at approximately INR2,000 crores market size by 2030.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue expected to recover to FY25 levels by FY27 with STML kick-in, fastener growth, SEM growth; full visibility
items.quote: I think from a consolidated level, my sense is, hopefully, in FY '27, we'll be very close to our numbers what we had in FY '25 on a consolidated level with the new business of STML kicking in

items.statement: Company maintains net debt-free status with consistent cash flow generation funding group growth internally
items.quote: We continue to maintain a net debt-free status with consistent cash flow generation, enabling us to fund group growth initiatives internally.

items.statement: Four technology partnerships formalized: Jiangsu Gtake, Advanced Electric Machines, Landworld (SEM); Kunshan GLV AC (STML); typical 7-10 year agreements
items.quote: Typically we sign 7 to 10-year agreements.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk mitigation driving own IP development; partnerships used to jump-start then localize; no single overseas product ready for Indian EV ecosystem without redesign
items.quote: we have to also protect against geopolitical risk.

items.statement: REM-free motor in advanced discussions with 1-2 customers; program finalization expected calendar 2026; significant revenue from FY28
items.quote: we are hoping that in the coming calendar year, I won't say fiscal year, but in the coming calendar year, we will finalize programs with 1 or possibly 2 customers, but we won't see revenue from this portfolio till FY '28.

items.statement: Discussions ongoing with all major OEMs (TVS, Bajaj, Honda) for future MCU programs; confident despite some in-house moves by OEMs
items.quote: We are working with -- we are in discussions with all of the major companies for their future programs.

items.statement: Consolidated margins expected to be retained at H1 levels in H2 FY26 despite revenue degrowth from loss of key SEM anchor customer
items.quote: On a consolidated level, I think we'll have a degrowth over last year because we lost our key anchor customer in SEML . But from a overall margin perspective, we hope to retain our consolidated margin numbers as we have for the first half into the second half.

items.statement: GST 2.0 rollout and monetary easing measures supporting auto industry growth momentum in H2 FY26
items.quote: supported by the rollout of GST 2.0, early festive demand and improving customer sentiment.

items.statement: 3-wheelers and commercial vehicles posted strong double-digit export growth indicating broad-based momentum
items.quote: 3-wheelers and commercial vehicles posted strong double digit export growth, indicating broad -based momentum.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; team includes MD Atul Aggarwal, Directors Jaideep Wadhwa and Anish Aggarwal, CFO Pankaj Gupta
items.quote: I'm joined today by Mr. Atul Aggarwal, Managing Director; Mr. Jaideep Wadhwa, Director; Mr. Anish Aggarwal, Director; and SGA, our Investor Relations Advisor.

items.statement: SEM rebranded from Sterling Gtake Mobility to Sterling E-Mobility Solutions Limited reflecting evolution as comprehensive EV powertrain and power electronics provider
items.quote: We are happy to share that Sterling Gtake Mobility Limite d has been rebranded as Sterling E -Mobility Solutions Limited (SEM).

items.statement: OBC/DC/DC assembly uses imported electronic child parts (limited availability in India); HVDC contactors manufacturing-intensive with phased localization from China-sourced child parts
items.quote: In this first phase of localization, we will be sourcing some of the child parts from our partner in China and we will be putting them together here in India.

items.statement: No domestic manufacturer of HVDC contactors/relays for automotive; Schneider not in this business; import substitution opportunity
items.quote: Schneider makes switchgears for industrial applications. They don't really make HVDC contactors and relays. They buy them for industrial applications

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; growth funded internally from cash-generative core business
items.quote: Our mature cash-generative core business provides a strong foundation for strategic diversification into high-growth areas.

items.statement: Not applicable - non-lending business
items.quote: Exceptional item for the quarter and 6 months ended 30th September '25 represents enhanced compensation of INR9.5 crores, including an interest of INR6.22 crores received from Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) against land acquired by DMRC in earlier years.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue growth guided at 7-8% with H2 growth of 10-12%
items.quote: we should end up at something like 7% to 8% growth for the full year

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin guided at 14.5-15%
items.quote: Operating margin should be remaining at that region of 14.5% to 15% that we are seeing right now

items.statement: Faucetware full-year revenue growth guided at 8-10%
items.quote: the numbers which we are saying roughly 8% to 10% growth in Faucetware, seems achievable

items.statement: Project sales contributed 39% of revenue in Q2 FY26, expected to remain at 39-40% for FY26
items.quote: Project sales accounted for 39% of our top line in Q2 FY '26

items.statement: Senator and Polipluz brands targeted to contribute INR 40-45 crore in H2 FY26
items.quote: We anticipate that we should be ending the year with both these brands at something in the region of INR 40 crore to INR 45 crore

items.statement: Senator and Polipluz combined revenue target of INR 150 crore by FY27
items.quote: this should be contributing to something like INR 150 crore of turnover from Senator and Polipluz taken together

items.statement: FY26 capex outlay earmarked at around INR 23 crore for maintenance and brand/retail expansion
items.quote: For financial year '26, we have earmarked a capex outlay of around INR 23 crore

items.statement: Q2 FY26 capacity utilization at 85% for Sanitaryware and 97% for Faucetware
items.quote: capacity utilization stood at 85% for Sanitaryware and 97% for Faucetware during the quarter under review

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin declined to 13.8% from 14.2% YoY due to higher input costs partially offset by efficiencies
items.quote: EBITDA margin slightly declined from 14.2% in Q2 FY '25 to 13.8% in Q2 FY '26, primarily due to increase in input costs

items.statement: Brass prices risen sharply to INR 620-630/kg in Nov from INR 590-600/kg range, impacting margins
items.quote: The metal price, the brass price has again taken a sharp increase. It is beyond INR 600, roughly around INR 620 or INR 630

items.statement: No price hikes planned currently despite brass cost increase; will monitor trend
items.quote: Yes, it is not planned because I think in the month of October, November, the brass prices have grown drastically. But still, we want to see the pattern

items.statement: Gas cost decreased slightly to INR 33.79/cbm in Q2 FY26 from INR 33.95/cbm YoY; 80% sourced from GAIL, 20% from Sabarmati
items.quote: Gas costs witnessed a slight decrease during the quarter with the weighted average cost standing at INR 33.79 per cubic meter in Q2 FY '26 compared to INR 33.95 per cubic meter in Q2 FY '25

items.statement: Premium segment 42%, mid 36%, entry 22% of sales in Q2 FY26; Tier 3 cities 41%, Tier 1 36%, Tier 2 23%
items.quote: In terms of product positioning, 42% of our sales came from premium category, 36% from mid segment and 22% from en try-level products. From a geographical standpoint, Tier 3 cities led with 41% of sales, followed by Tier 1 at 36% and Tier 2 at 23

items.statement: Retail demand subdued for 7-8 quarters; Sanitaryware grew 1.4% YoY in Q2, Faucetware declined 3.5% YoY due to high base
items.quote: In the backdrop of demand environment that remains subdued, particularly on the retail side, we are pleased to report a steady performance this quarter. Our Sanitaryware segment delivered a year-on-year growth of 1.4%

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 77 from 72 YoY; inventory days 83 (from 80), receivables 33 (from 31), payables stable at 39
items.quote: inventory days increased from 80 to 83 days. Receivables raised from 31 to 33 days, while payable days remained stable at 39 days, leading to a Y-o-Y increase in net working capital days from 72 to 77 days

items.statement: Exited two LLPs (Race Polymer Arts and Packcart Packaging) on Sep 29 for INR 18.75 crore consideration, booking INR 5.54 crore profit in other income
items.quote: the total consideration we have received for these two LLPs is what you have rightly told is INR 18.75 crore. And we have recorded the profit on divestment of INR 5.54 crore

items.statement: Annualized employee cost for Senator and Polipluz brands estimated at INR 14-15 crore; H1 spend ~INR 5 crore
items.quote: we would be having an annualized expenditure of something like INR 15 crore, you can say INR 14 crore to INR 15 crore for the full year

items.statement: Full-year employee cost inflation guided at 7-8% (staff 10.5-11%, workers 5%, with H2 wage increase expected)
items.quote: we are anticipating a wage increase to happen in the second half. So that should take it for the whole year to be in the range of, let us say, 7% to 8%

items.statement: New product launches contributed 33% of overall sales in Q2 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, new product launches contributed about 33% of the overall sales

items.statement: Senator brand rollout on track: 28 stores operational, targeting 45-50 by end FY26
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our FY '26 flagship rollout target of 45 to 50 stores with 28 stores already operational as on date

items.statement: Polipluz distribution at 38 distributors and 650 dealers, targeting 100 distributors and 2,000 dealers by Mar 2026
items.quote: At present, Polipluz is being distributed through 38 distributors and 650 dealers with a target to expand the network to 100 distributors and 2,000 dealers by March 2026

items.statement: New entrants in bathware segment noted but confident in brand loyalty, service differentiation and dealer network for long-term
items.quote: Cera being a brand which is established for more than four decades and with product lines, quality and other things well established, brand loyalty and the type of innovation we put in our products, is going to be a sustainable model

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on H2 demand recovery; dependent on consumer discretionary spending pickup and macro factors
items.quote: we remain cautiously optimistic about the demand recovery, we stated would happen in H2 FY '26

items.statement: DMS (Dealer Management System) rolled out to 200+ dealers, improving secondary sales visibility and inventory tracking
items.quote: We have successfully onboarded about over 200 dealers so far with system integration and data connectors now activated at their end

items.statement: Marketing spend for Senator and Polipluz in first year estimated at INR 10-12 crore, increasing from next year
items.quote: We expect it to be in the range of INR 10 crore to INR 12 crore. From next year onwards, you will find that, that amount would increase

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR 736 crore as of Sep 30, 2025
items.quote: As of 30th September '25, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 736 crore

items.statement: FY27 revenue target Rs 2,800 crore at 80-90% capacity utilization
items.quote: So, we do look forward at 80% to 90% of capacity utilization in 2026, 2027 of all our divisions, which will definitely give us revenue of about Rs. 2,800 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 20% YoY from FY25
items.quote: We are looking at a 20% revenue growth from last year, from FY '25.

items.statement: OMCs require 200 crore litres more ethanol; additional tender cycles C2-C4 expected
items.quote: So, for which they will be coming up with additional cycles.

items.statement: Received 17.5 crore litre ethanol allocation for ESY 2025-26 (Nov 2025-Oct 2026)
items.quote: So, the company received allocation of 17.5 crore litres, which is for ESY 2025-2026, which starts in November 2025 and goes up to October 2026.

items.statement: Company has capacity to produce 23 crore litres ethanol annually
items.quote: Company definitely has the capacity to produce 23 crore litres, but it is also subject to the allocations which we receive from the OMCs.

items.statement: Mineral processing margins stable at 23-24%; willing to lose customers to protect margins
items.quote: I think 23% to 24% is a reasonable margin for this division. We are really maintaining this.

items.statement: Grain processing recovery expected in H2 CY2025 after starch shutdown and raw material price correction
items.quote: we are expecting that we will be able to churn over again this division in the second half of the year

items.statement: Current maize prices Rs 21-22/kg, rice Rs 24-25/kg, power & fuel ~Rs 6/litre at MP plant
items.quote: If I talk for MP plant, the current maize prices are at about Rs. 21, Rs. 21-Rs. 22. And rice is at about Rs. 24 to Rs. 25. The power and fuel cost would be about Rs. 6 a litre.

items.statement: Ethanol feedstock mix: 40% FCI rice, 45% maize, 15% DFG (damaged food grains)
items.quote: So 40% will be from FCRIs and when I see the average between MP and Assam plant, 40% is FCI, about 45% is from maize and 15% is from DFG.

items.statement: Working capital borrowings Rs 250 crore currently; may rise to Rs 275-300 crore max this year due to 40% advance FCI procurement
items.quote: So from Rs. 157 crores, we now presently are RS.250 crores. And I think another Rs. 25 crores Rs. 30 crores, maximum Rs. 50 crores, we will not go beyond Rs. 250- Rs. 275 crores or Rs. 300 crores during this year at maximum.

items.statement: Received Rs 5.34 crore PLI from MP govt in Oct (booked as other income in Q3); further Rs 14-15 crore MP sanction and Rs 5 crore Assam NEETs incentive expected H2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, so we have received a PLI of Rs. 5.34 crores in the month of October, which will get factored in in quarter three results. And this will be treated as other income in our P&L account.

items.statement: Term loans availed in 2022-23; recent borrowing jump only for working capital (Rs 157 cr Mar'25 to Rs 250 cr now)
items.quote: So the jump was only to fund our working capital requirement because of the jump into revenue also.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity utilization guidance 80-90% for FY27 subject to OMC allocations
items.quote: I think the guidance for FY 2027 is working on 80%-90% capacity utilization, all subject to allocation from the tender.

items.statement: Grain processing faces overcapacity and China competition; starch (<10% revenue) temporarily shut
items.quote: Hence, the prices have gone down and become very unbuyable for operations. Very fortunately for Gulshan Polyols, because we are a multi-product company, so we have a luxury of closing one division which was loss-making

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 9-10% for FY26
items.quote: Volume guidance we had given 9% to 10% for this year and that we are maintaining.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance unchanged for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Not at this moment, because like we've been saying that with certain challenges that are coming globally and domestically, we don't want to change the guidance until we see better clarity from the market side.

items.statement: Chromeni utilization at 70% in Q2, targeting 80% in H2; NPI at 90% utilization
items.quote: What we have stated, this is true that we have hit the numbers of 70% capacity utilization. And in the second half, we believe that we will be hitting that 80% what we have told you before of capacity utilization.

items.statement: Indonesia melt shop to start early next year; cold rolling capacity expansion on track for end of FY27; HRAP in later half of FY27
items.quote: Our NPI operations have been started at the beginning of the year already and our melt shop in Indonesia should start early next year. And apart from that, like we announced earlier, we are increasing our cold rolling capacities. So, that is also on track to be starting end of FY27.

items.statement: Q2 deliveries at 648,050 MT, up 15% YoY and 3% QoQ; H1 deliveries at 1.274 million MT, up 12% YoY
items.quote: Our Q2 deliveries are at 648,050 metric tons, with an increase of around 15 % on year-on-year and around 3% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Q2 consolidated EBITDA INR 1,388 crore, up 17% YoY and 6% QoQ; PAT INR 808 crore, up 33% YoY and 13% QoQ
items.quote: Our Q2 consolidated EBITDA increased by around 17% year-on-year and around 6 % on quarter-on-quarter to INR 1,388 crores, while our consolidated PAT stood at INR 808 crores, an increase of around 33 % on year-on-year and around 13% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 3,646 crore; net debt/EBITDA 0.73x; net debt/equity 0.2x as of Sep 30, 2025
items.quote: As of September 30th, 2025, our consolidated net debt has further reduced to INR 3,646 crores, with a net-to-debt EBITDA ratio at 0.73x, comfortably below 1, and net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.2x.
For this quarter, it was 34%, 49% and 17%.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across pipe & tube, lift & elevator, passenger coach (Vande Bharat), metro projects, white goods, auto, and infra segments
items.quote: Strong demand from sectors such as pipe and tubes, lift and elevator, along with improved traction in passenger coach driven by roll-out of Van de Bharat sleeper class orders, contributed meaningfully to this performance.

items.statement: Exports to remain on same trajectory short-term due to CBAM uncertainty; clarity expected by mid-December
items.quote: I think currently short-term export would remain in the same trajectory because I think everybody in terms of customers, also producers, everyone is looking what will be the impact of CBAM.

items.statement: QCO suspended till December; company working with government to reinstate it; temporary suspension causing downward price pressure
items.quote: The QCO order has been suspended till December, and we are working with the government to ensure that the suspension removes and QCO comes back.

items.statement: Chrome ore sourced from OMC (Odisha Mining Corp) under long-term linkage; own Sukinda mine operations to start next year targeting substantial quantity
items.quote: For chrome, if you are saying our main source is OMC, which is Odisha Mining Corporation. We have a long-term linkage with them. Apart from that, our own mine operation should start sometime next year actually.

items.statement: Renewable power utilization at Jajpur and Hisar increased to 42% in Q2 FY26 from 26% in FY25; green hydrogen plant (600 NM3/hr) at Jajpur targeted for mid-next year
items.quote: our renewable power utilization at J ajpur and Hisar facilities has increased to 42% Q2 FY26, up from 26 % in FY25, marking a significant step towards cleaner and more sustainable operations

items.statement: Co-branding scheme gaining positive response in utensils, kitchen, and P&T segments
items.quote: We are also actively promoting our co-branding scheme, which is gaining a positive response in the utensils and kitchen segments alongside the P&T sector.

items.statement: Trained 6,700 fabricators in Q2; cumulative 60,400 trained to date via specialized programs
items.quote: These initiatives led to the training of 6,700 fabricators in Q2, bringing the cumulative total to 60,400 till date.

items.statement: Consolidation of subsidiaries (Chromeni, RVPL, RT) planned over next couple of years; Maharashtra land acquisition progressing, investor day planned
items.quote: All in terms of consolidation is in the pipeline and it is in our plans. It is just for certain factors why we are not taking that step right now. But next couple of years, you will see most of the assets being consolidated.

items.statement: NPI EBITDA range $500-1,500 per ton indicated; currently EBITDA positive at 90% utilization
items.quote: NPI, earlier also we had indicated that at EBITDA level, $500 to $1,500 range is what we had indicated. Because in NPI, we all know volatility is there. But with the utilization, what Mr. Jindal has informed with that, the EBITDA is coming into that range, and we are EBITDA positive on that.

items.statement: CBAM clarity delayed; European players also facing challenges; default scores expected first, then factory-level assessment
items.quote: What we know is that they will start with default scores and then it will go company or individual factory-wise. But still timelines, further clarification is still what we are all awaiting.

items.statement: Subsidized, substandard imports rising due to QCO suspension and geopolitical complexities
items.quote: Given the prevailing geopolitical complexities, we anticipate a further rise in low-quality, cheap imports entering the country.

items.statement: Maharashtra expansion land acquisition in progress; FY28 capex plans to be shared at investor day
items.quote: Maharashtra, the land part is going on. Like in India, the land always takes time when you work on it. And for our kind of plant and our kind of scale, what we are talking about, the requirement is also quite fairly large.

items.statement: Debt ratios among lowest globally in metal sector; committed to maintaining ratios during Maharashtra expansion
items.quote: Definitely in terms of if you know and you're tracking the company, we already have one of the lowest debt profiles, our debt to EBITDA, debt to equity is one of the lowest globally in the metal sector.

items.statement: Quality differentiation remains key against substandard imports; ready to supply globally with approvals in place
items.quote: as per our quality and as per our approvals, we are able to supply a nd sell to any industry globally. We are ready with that

items.statement: October volumes met targets; Q3 and H2 volume targets on track despite QCO suspension
items.quote: As a company, in terms of our volumes, we have met our targets in October, and we will meet our targets in Q3 and H2.

items.statement: Potential slight downward pressure on prices due to QCO suspension but sticking to annual guidance
items.quote: There could be a little downward pressure on prices, but we are still sticking to our guidance that we have given at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Rathi Steel utilization at 70-75%; rebar sales picking up (2,000-2,500 tons/month), wire rod moderating
items.quote: Rathi. So, almost 70%-75%. And in that, the good thing is that this stainless rebar is gradually picking up. On an average, now, I can say in the range of 2000-2500, those kind of numbers started...

items.statement: RVPL polishing lines operational; cold rolling facilities plan under development
items.quote: RVPL, so far, whatever we had indicated before, that the polishing lines and all that business is going on. And we are working on a plan now, seriously, which we will come back very quickly on the RVPL, the code ruling facilities and all that.

items.statement: Particle Board revenue guidance of 40% growth for FY26, targeting around INR 200 crores
items.quote: The 40% growth potentially means ending the year at about INR 200-odd crores, if I take the trial sales into account because we already at INR 54 crores, INR55 crores quarter for Q2.

items.statement: MDF industry growth outlook of 15-20%
items.quote: The industry will grow by 15%, 20%, and that's our outlook as well.

items.statement: MDF South plant line extension to increase capacity by 25% in H1 FY27
