items.quote: Our subsidiary, Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory, secured significant orders, including an INR 113 crore contract from Ministry of Railways for 9,000 LHB Axles, and an order for INR 215 crore for 5,376 wheelsets for the Vande Bharat high-speed train project.

items.statement: Private wagon ordering trend remains positive with no slowdown; Indian Railway tenders critical for volume
items.quote: So, on the private side, I don't see a slowdown. I think, as you see from our numbers also , that our private execution is quite strong. And if you see the announcements also, we make, and if you see, we keep on adding private order books to our portfolio. So, we don't see a slowdown, but definitely, Indian Railway tenders are very, very critical because that provides the main volume.

items.statement: Indian Railways requires ~50,000 wagons to meet revenue forecast; big tender expected anytime as outstanding industry order book executes
items.quote: What is very clear is that if you look at the stated position of Indian Railways, is that they require close to about 50,000 wagons to achieve their revenue forecast. So, we expect the tenders to come out anytime. I think one of the reasons for the delay was because of the wheelset position. The outstanding order book was substantial. So, I think Railways is looking for the existing order books to

items.statement: BESS business seeing strong acceptance in C&I and utility segments; export orders also growing
items.quote: Acceptance is very strong, and it is not just diesel generator. There are other significant opportunities which we are there, which I cannot divulge right now, which we are already working on, and it's not that BESS is the only solution which is available. And we don't see any kind of challenge. Adaptability is very strong, and I think this business in the next two to three years is going to scale

items.statement: Container business volume more than doubled YoY driven by specialized segments (battery storage, data centers) with marquee clients like GE, TMEIC, Tata Solar, Reliance, Delta
items.quote: So, see, again, the container business in itself, by itself in India, is growing significantly. And Jupiter as a company is focused on the specialized segments, mainly for the battery storage as well as for the containers which are required for the data center. And we are now working with very marquee clients such as General Electric, with TMEIC – Toshiba, Mitsubishi, with people like Tata Solar,

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 13.2%, PAT margin 5.8%; margins to improve in H2 FY26 as wagon revenues normalize and complex private wagons execute
items.quote: In Q2 FY26, on a consolidated basis, revenue from operations stood at INR 786 crore, a strong 71% sequential growth, primarily driven by normalization of wheelset supplies in our wagon division. EBITDA rose 73% quarter-on-quarter to INR 104 crore, and we reported an EBITDA margin of 13.2%, while profit after tax reached INR 45 crore, reflecting a PAT margin of 5.8%.

items.statement: BESS business is margin accretive with margins comparable to other businesses; specific margins to be disclosed in 3-6 months
items.quote: So, we do expect to enjoy decent margins. However, at this stage, we would not like to comment specifically on the margins, because as I mentioned, this is a business that has only just started . And so maybe in the next three to six months, we will be able to give you a clear view on the margins. But definitely I can say that it is a margin accretive business, and the margins are going to be as c

items.statement: Stone India commissioning expected by Q4 FY26; PAT positive in FY27
items.quote: I think by the last quarter of FY26, Stone India, we expect the commissioning to happen because our final trials are going on, and we are in the process of getting the final certification also done from Indian Railways. So, next year, you will see significant revenues coming from Stone India. Next year, definitely, Stone India is also going to become even PAT positive. I am very confident on that.

items.statement: BESS capacity 40-50 MW/month; not a constraint; shared capacities make investment hard to isolate
items.quote: See, on the BESS side, in terms of capacities, we have built significant capacities. So, we are looking in terms of capacity, we can easily do about close to 40 to 50 Megawatts of BESS systems on a monthly basis. So, capacity is not a constraint right now for us, and we continue to invest in the same.

items.statement: Aurangabad wheelset plant in production for LHB and private orders; capacity limited
items.quote: Yes. There is a plant in Aurangabad which is in production. That capacity is limited but it is used for wheelsets which supplies to LHB and we use it for our private order books.

items.statement: Target: wagon revenue ~50% of total by FY28; non-wagon businesses to drive growth
items.quote: So, the whole idea is that, as is the stated position of the company, that by FY28, wagon revenues would constitute close to about 50% of the overall revenues. And from the other businesses, the revenues would significantly increase. That is our stated position, and definitely that is where we strive to go.

items.statement: Private wagons ~60% of revenue, Railway ~40%; private side larger currently
items.quote: So, I would say that from the overall private would be about 60% of our contribution, and railway would be about 40% of our contribution. Definitely the private side of our business has a larger contribution right now than the railway.

items.statement: Focus on specialized wagons (auto cars) for margin expansion; aluminum wagon market very small
items.quote: No, we are already into aluminum wagons, but the market for aluminum wagons is very small. I think where our focus is that we are now getting into very specialized wagons where there is a significant market opportunity, and which requires a lot of investments and designs and other technologies. And that is where we are focusing on, and that is what is going to lead to margin expansion.

items.statement: EV partnerships with Porter, Pickup and others performing well; eLCV volumes growing 20-30% monthly
items.quote: And our partnerships, not only with Porter, but with other significant players like Pic kkup and others, which I cannot mention names right now, but all our partnerships are doing very well, and we are seeing a lot of strong traction in th is sector. If you look at the segment itself, it is growing month-on-month. The segment itself is showing a growth rate of close to 100

items.statement: Wheelset facility fully integrated (wheels + axles + in-house machining); export capacity earmarked for Europe reduces domestic dependence
items.quote: Regarding competitors, I cannot comment. However, we do have a few differentiators. First and foremost, our facility is fully integrated, enabling us to produce both wheels and axles, with all machining done in-house—something competitors may not offer. Secondly, we are in a strong position because our partners have significant wheelset requirements in Europe, and a sizable part of our capacity is

items.statement: Vinod Kumar Agrawal appointed as CFO and Key Managerial Personnel
items.quote: We are also pleased to welcome Mr. Vinod Kumar Agrawal as our Chief Financial Officer and a key managerial personnel. His financial expertise and strategic insight will further strengthen our leadership team as we enter the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Wheelset supply disruption resolved; no issues expected for next 6-12 months
items.quote: Right now, there is no issue with the wheels, and our expectation is that going forward also at least in the recent, in the next six months to a year there will not be any problem.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at Rs 5,700-5,800 crore for PGEL standalone and Rs 6,550-6,650 crore consolidated including JV; net profit Rs 300-310 crore
items.quote: We are maintaining our guidance shared in 1Q 2026 i.e., FY '26, we expect PGEL to be having revenues in the range of Rs. 5,700-Rs. 5,800 crores and net profit is expected to be between Rs. 300-Rs. 310 crores. At the group level, including our joint venture, Goodworth Electronics, we expect consolidated sales to cross Rs. 6,550-Rs. 6,650 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs 700-750 crore across Greater Noida, Supa, Rajasthan and South India
items.quote: We are continuing with our investment in Greater Noida, Supa, Rajasthan and South India and our FY '26 CAPEX will be in between Rs. 700-Rs. 750 crores, again reiterating that our long-term investment, operational model and growth priorities remain unchanged.

items.statement: FY26 capex breakdown: ~Rs 300-350 crore for refrigerator plant in Sri City, ~Rs 100 crore for washing machines in Greater Noida, ~Rs 200 crore for AC in Supa and Bhiwadi, rest for tooling/coolers in Bhiwadi
items.quote: Out of which, as Vikas ji mentioned, almost half of it, which is Rs. 300-Rs. 350 crores, will be for refrigerator, which will be happening in Sri City. And then there is Rs. 100 odd crores which we are going to be spending, which we have already almost spent in washing machine business in Greater Noida. There is Rs. 200 crores which is getting spent in RAC business in Supa as well as Bhiwadi. So y

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to be much lower than FY26; Andhra Pradesh refrigerator plant phase 1 ~Rs 350 crore, total Rs 1,000 crore over 4-5 years; Maharashtra MoU Rs 1,000 crore over 4-5 years starting FY27
items.quote: Next year, we will be able to update you at the end of the quarter 4. But I can assure you it will be much lower than this year. And it will also depend on the business plan and the opportunities which we foresee. But as of today, we think it will be probably much lower than what we are doing right now.

items.statement: Current AC capacity ~3.5 lakh split/month + 50k window/month; target by Dec ~4.25 lakh split/month; washing machine ~2 lakh/month; coolers ~50k/month; cooler line +25k/month in new plant next year
items.value: 3.5 lakh split, 50k window, 2 lakh WM, 50k coolers
items.quote: Right now, our capacity in AC is almost close to 3.5 lakh ACs per month on the split side and about 50,000 ACs on the window side and once by December, we are hoping to increase it to about 4.25 lakh in the split side and 50,000 in the window side. And in washing machine the capacity is already expanded and we have about close to 2 lakh washing machines per month capacity today. In coolers, it is

items.statement: Industry primary sales down 20-25% in H1; secondary sales declined deeper causing elevated channel inventory estimated at 1.5-2 million units as of Nov 1; H2 expected better due to GST cut, BEE rating change, and client order book
items.quote: So see, primary sales have de-grown by around 20%-25%, but secondary sales have seen a deeper decline. That is why we are seeing an elevated level of inventory in the channel. And as per see, we don't have very accurate data on the channel inventory. But our estimate is still, I think, as of 1st November, it should be anything between at least 1.5-2 million, sir, at least.

items.statement: AC volume growth expected ~15% for full year FY26 vs flattish industry; driven by wallet share gains and market share gains of key brand clients
items.quote: In our case, in the first half, we had a very small growth despite the industry being a decline. And in the second half, we hope to have about 15% or so growth in the overall volume, largely due to two or three factors. One is obviously we are gaining some wallet share. Also, we continue to see some of the brands with whom we work, they are gaining market share in the marketplace and they are goin

items.statement: Competitive intensity high due to inventory overhang; pricing pressure across value chain likely till Jan-Feb; margin guidance built into net profit target of Rs 300-310 crore
items.quote: See, the margin guidance is actually built in the numbers that we have guided for and we are aware of what we need to do and after doing all the consideration only we have given the net profit and sales guidance, but yes right now, as Vishal ji had explained the whole value chain and the AC business is under pressure because of the high inventory and last year or the last season not going well, bu

items.statement: Raw material cost pressure from higher copper, aluminum prices and currency depreciation; brands may need to increase prices of existing and new models
items.quote: And most of it, almost 99.9% can be actually used in the new energy rating as well. So we don't see any impact on the inventory that we are carrying. That is point number one. Point number two is that in general we have seen the prices of some of the raw material have gone up largely because copper and aluminum prices have gone up and also the currency has depreciated. So from that point of view,

items.statement: Washing machine revenue target ~15% of total in medium term (currently 11-12%); growth driven by wallet share gains and insourcing-to-outsourcing shift
items.quote: We will like washing machine to contribute about something like 15% or so in the medium term and we are working towards it. Right now, it is this year probably just about going to be 11%-12% and we are hopeful that in next 2-3 years, it should reach at about 15% on a much higher number for the overall company's revenues.

items.statement: H2 guidance confidence based on firm and committed orders from clients; order book visibility supports revenue and profit targets
items.quote: Now, the visibility that we have is based on the order book that we have from our clients. And we are quite confident of achieving the numbers which we have guided for in the second half based on the firm and committed orders from the clients which we are working with.

items.statement: H1 operating and free cash flow negative due to high inventory; H2 expected improvement from inventory normalization and GST rationalization (28% output vs 18% input credit gap closing); Rs 377 crore capex already spent in H1
items.quote: Cash flow for us in the first half has been okay. We are having higher inventory and that is probably showing a negative cash flow at the operating level as well as at a free cash flow level. Second half should be much better, largely because of two reasons. One is obviously we are hoping to normalize the inventory. And second thing is that because of this GST rationalization, this should help a b

items.statement: Debt increased from Rs 301 crore to Rs 482 crore; finance cost dropped from Rs 34 crore in Q1 to Rs 16 crore in Q2 due to one-time Rs ~20 crore upfronting of buyer's credit and receivables discounting charges in Q1
items.quote: See, last quarter we had some liquidity challenges because on one hand we had a high inventory and on other hand, we were also facing some challenges on our receivables because receivables got delayed because of the lower sales of some of the brands. So we resorted to two aspects to take care of that. One was to basically discount some of the receivables and also on the payable front, we extended

items.statement: BEE rating change effective Jan 2025 expected to drive channel filling in Nov-Dec; GST cut from 28% to 18% on ACs announced Aug 15 expected to aid penetration-led growth in H2 and H1 FY27
items.quote: Having said that, because of the change in the energy rating, so that opens up some opportunity for this channel filling happening. So we have two things, one energy rating change, which will push up the channel filling and there might be something because of the channel is already choked up, there might be some pushback from the channel from taking energy further inventory.

items.statement: AC compressor JV with Chinese partner still pending approval from Chinese government; no resolution yet
items.quote: No, sir. It is still pending. Nothing is getting resolved. As per the latest updates that we have from our partner, they are still waiting for the go-ahead from the Chinese government side on this.

items.statement: EV bike manufacturing with Spiro Mobility delayed; partner unable to get ARAI approval and shifted focus to Africa market
items.quote: So that EV thing is getting delayed and our partner for whom we were supposed to start manufacturing in India, they are not able to get their motorcycle approved from ARAI and at the same time, they have shifted some of their focus to Africa market.

items.statement: Goodworth Electronics JV posted Rs 483 crore sales and Rs 10.33 crore EBITDA in H1 FY26
items.quote: The JV, our Goodworth Electronics has also ramped up well and has posted sales of Rs. 483 crores with Rs. 10.33 crores of EBITDA in first half of FY '26.

items.statement: Plastic moulding component business: Q2 Rs 211 crore, H1 Rs 485 crore; small YoY decline in Q2 due to lower plastic prices; not allocating significant new capex
items.quote: Second quarter, the number is about Rs. 211 crores and for the first half, it is Rs. 485 crores.

items.statement: No large export opportunities currently; only small pursuits unlikely to contribute significantly in short term
items.quote: Right now, we do not have any large opportunities. There are some small opportunities which we are pursuing, but they are nothing to talk about and they are unlikely to contribute anything significant in the short term.

items.statement: AC: same brands continue, added a couple of new names (small contribution initially); washing machine: wallet share gains from existing clients and insourcing-to-outsourcing shift
items.quote: In AC, the same brands continue with whom we were working. We have added a couple of more names, but they will not be contributing so hugely in the very first year. So it is mainly the wallet share gain, which we continue to see at our end. Similarly, in the washing machine also, it is largely the existing client where we are seeing the wallet share gain and also some share gain from insourcing to

items.statement: Competitive intensity very high at manufacturing and brand level due to inventory overhang; pressure likely till end of Jan or Feb
items.quote: The competitive intensity is very high right now, at a manufacturing level also, at a brand level also, because everybody is stuck up with inventories and everybody is trying to clear off their inventory. So competitive intensity will be very high, at least, I believe, maybe till end of January or February.

items.statement: ECMS applications filed in 4-5 component categories via Goodworth JV: camera modules, display modules, mechanical enclosures, PCB; still under review, not approved; capex dependent on approval and technology tie-ups
items.quote: So we have filed the ECMS applications in 4-5 different component categories through our JV Entity Goodworth Electronics. So that is under camera modules, display modules, mechanical enclosures. I think on the PCB side also, we have put up the ECMS application. So that is still under review. It has not been approved as of now. So we are keeping a close watch on it.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; key executives present: Vishal Gupta (MD Finance), Vikas Gupta (MD Operations), Pramod Gupta (CFO)
items.quote: Today, we have with us Senior Management represented by Mr. Vishal Gupta - Managing Director, Finance; Mr. Vikas Gupta - Managing Director, Operations and Mr. Pramod Gupta - Chief Financial Officer.

items.statement: Management not providing specific revenue or EBITDA margin guidance for FY26; aims for high double-digit sales growth and double-digit EBITDA
items.quote: So, unfortunately, at the moment, we are not providing any specific guidance. But generally, we have been growing at high double-digit even on the sales number and we are also working on improving margins as we scale.

items.statement: Capex not sizable; continuous capacity expansion at Solapur plant targeting ~20% capacity growth over next six months
items.quote: So, generally, our business is not very CAPEX driven. It is more OPEX driven. There is continuous CAPEX that we do to increase the capacities available to us, specifically in our Solapur plant. However, it is not very sizable. It is basically to add about so that it grows at about 20% in terms of capacity over the next six months.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 14.94% driven by price increases due to price-insensitive demand, festive pickup and GST rate cut; focus on growth with double-digit EBITDA
items.quote: So, this quarter was a bit peculiar in the sense that what we saw was the GST rate cut being announced after which there was deferred purchases. So, our pricing models that we use, they realized that the customer is not price sensitive. Rather, I would say it is price insensitive.

items.statement: Strong recovery in demand by end of Q2 as asset buying picked up supported by improved consumer sentiment and GST rate cut
items.quote: By the end of the quarter, we witnessed a strong recovery in demand as asset buying picked up, supported by improved consumer sentiment and the GST rate cut coming into effect.

items.statement: Thomas Scott brand revenue Rs 22 crore (+77% YoY); licensed brands Rs 33 crore (+23% YoY); contract manufacturing Rs 3 crore (+40% YoY)
items.quote: Our own brand, Thomas Scott, delivered revenues of Rs. 22 crore, up 77% year-on-year, reflecting the growing strength of our direct-to-consumer franchise and improved assortment planning.

items.statement: Solapur plant capacity expansion targeting ~20% growth over next six months; Gurgaon handbag facility 100% operational after fire incident
items.quote: It is basically to add about so that it grows at about 20% in terms of capacity over the next six months. So, that kind of capacity expansion and capital planning is there for it.

items.statement: Offline stores in Bangalore at pilot phase with six outlets showing double-digit footfall and same-store sales growth; online distribution pan-India
items.quote: So, presently, offline or our stores model is currently in a pilot phase where we are testing out a slightly unique model. So, it is at a base of six stores only where we are trying to identify whether we are able to get the same kind of return on capital employed that we are able to generally generate in our online business.

items.statement: Trade receivables ~Rs 71.5 crore; inventory ~Rs 77.1 crore; inventory building for H2; manufacturing cycle 30-45 days, target sales cycle ~100 days
items.quote: Sure. So, currently, as it stands, we have about Rs. 71.5 crore approximately in trade receivables and we have an inventory of about Rs. 77.1 crores. Now, in terms of inventory, obviously, the inventory increases are there to accommodate greater sales in H2.

items.statement: Marketing spend typically 7-10% of top line, ROI-driven performance marketing; pricing and marketing levers adjusted multiple times daily
items.quote: So, what I was trying to get at is, generally the marketing spends as we are growing are a bit fluid, but we typically target to keep that somewhere between 7% to 10% of our overall top line.

items.statement: Catalog AI improved kids wear conversion by ~80 bps from 1.1-1.2% base to ~1.9-2%
items.quote: Generally, we have applied this in our kids wear segment for the brands that we do kids wear and we have seen a good success on application of this model, resulting in improved conversion by at least 80 basis points in total.

items.statement: Online and offline retail (e.g., Zudio) target different customer profiles; both growing at healthy double-digit rates
items.quote: So, I would look at them as different customer, different target audience, different customer profiles, to be very honest. And both of these areas, the one that you mentioned, such as video or even e-commerce online, are receiving very healthy double-digit growth.

items.statement: GST rate cut announcement caused deferred purchases then demand recovery when implemented
items.quote: We continued to see healthy momentum, despite a temporary slowdown in customer uptake caused by deferred purchases, for when the GST rate cut offered.

items.statement: Quick commerce pilots with Myntra Mnow and Big Basket; profitability focus limits aggressive expansion
items.quote: The thing with quick commerce is that there is a certain amount of overall investment that is required, not only in terms of inventory, but also in terms of other expenses, such as marketing, which may not yield it to be profitable from day one.

items.statement: AI/tech team ~5-6% of workforce; not expected to expand rapidly
items.quote: Generally, our investment in AI is investment in our overall technology team or tech partners who support us in creating these applications. This is not a very sizable investment. Again, it is a 5% or 6% team that does the development.

items.statement: Revenue mix target: Thomas Scott 30-40% of top line, licensed brands remainder, contract manufacturing ~5% (may decline to 4%)
items.quote: Yes. So, generally, Thomas Scott would be between about 30% to 40% of the top line and the remaining would be other brands. About 5% would remain B2B. That 5% could go to 4% as well.

items.statement: FY26 volume guidance maintained at 4.5-5 lakh tons
items.quote: So we think that we'll be able to reach 4.5 lakh to 5 lakh tons of guidance what we have done before as well, and we'll be able to achieve it in full scope.

items.statement: FY27 volume target of 6-6.5 lakh tons
items.quote: On 4.5 -- FY '27, we should be touching 6.5 lakh to 6 lakh tons of sales volume.

items.statement: FY28 volume target of 9 lakh tons and FY29 target of 1 million tons
items.quote: Next year, it should be going to 6.5 lakh tons. And then the year next to that, it should be going to 9 lakh tons. And finally, FY '29, it should be crossing 1 million tons of sales volume.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA per ton target of INR4,000 maintained
items.quote: So we still stick to our target of INR4,000 EBITDA per ton for the full year.

items.statement: Maharashtra plant expansion: narrow GI line by Q4 mid, color-coated by end of H1 FY27, API grade after that
items.quote: But nevertheless, we are hoping to start our facility by this year-end, probably by Q4 mid for narrow. And for wider, we'll be starting again by end of -- before end of H1 next financial year. And the API will be coming in after that.

items.statement: Maharashtra plant capacity to reach 1.4 million tons from current 4 lakh tons
items.quote: The capacity over there at a single location will be 1.4 million tons, which is currently 4 lakh tons right now.

items.statement: Acquired RC Industries as fully owned subsidiary from Q3; historical revenue >INR2,000 crores/year, capacity 16,000 tons, products: phosphorus, bronze, copper, brass
items.quote: So that company will be a fully owned subsidiary of ours starting Q3 onwards itself. And the company -- RC Industries in previous years, which is FY -- FY '16, '17, '18, three consecutive years, it has done a top line north of INR2,000 crores every year.

items.statement: DFT pipes EBITDA per ton improved from negative in Q1 to INR3,500-4,000 in Q2; expect further improvement in Q3-Q4 with project approvals
items.quote: Coming to quarter 2, we have made a healthy EBITDA of INR3,500, INR4,000 range bound in the DFT products. This is not the best margin that we wish to get in the particular product segment, but we are somewhere over there.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA per ton at INR3,200; Q2 at INR4,300; target INR4,000 for full year
items.quote: So our H1 EBITDA per ton is close to INR3,200 right now. So we still stick to our target of INR4,000 EBITDA per ton for the full year.

items.statement: Q2 volumes impacted by Punjab floods (~23,000 tons); expect recovery in Q3 (1.2 lakh tons) and Q4 (1.4-1.5 lakh tons); H2 traditionally stronger
items.quote: The major reason for the drop in volumes was because of the floods that came in Punjab. Because of that, a lot of the dispatches were hampered for quarter 2 particularly, affecting us to the tune of 20,000 tons around closely.

items.statement: Post-Diwali price uptick partially sustained; no major holidays or weather issues expected; demand keen to pick up in H2
items.quote: Post Diwali, there was a short blip in the prices going up and not the entirety of it stuck, but a little part of it did stick on. And now going forward, we don't see any major holidays or the weather being an issue. So the demand is keen to pick up.

items.statement: HRC-Patra spread stable at INR6-7/kg; HRC prices bottomed at INR46.5-47/kg in Q3; expect stabilization or improvement with better demand in H2
items.quote: The difference between the HR coil and Patra still remains about a gap of about INR6 to INR7 per kg. So that is the inherent difference and that we've seen over the last year, the difference remains.

items.statement: Q2/H1 capacity utilization at 43-44%; would have been 50-55% without floods
items.quote: It was close to 43%, 44% utilization levels.

items.statement: VAP share to improve in H2 as DFT moves from commercial to value-added category; expanding SKU range toward higher diameter, pre-galvanized, sheet galvanizing, HRPO
items.quote: Coming to quarter 3, quarter 4, we should be having a healthy margin in DFT and alongside our remaining capex happening at Maharashtra should kick in as well, which altogether should increase our VAP share as well

items.statement: Q2 export sales INR63 crores (+46% QoQ, -18% YoY)
items.quote: The export sales in Q2 FY '26 were INR63 crores. The corresponding figure in Q1 financial year '26 was INR43 crores. This shows an increase of around 46% Q-on-Q.

items.statement: RC Industries subsidiary: 70-71% sales on cash basis (bullet shells, export orders); 15-20% on credit; working capital manageable, no material impact on JTL consolidated debt
items.quote: But the majority of products, which is 70%-71% is sold on cash. So, it depends on what category of product we are entering in the segment. But for us, what we have explored a little bit till now, everything is sold on cash.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY26 volume 182,210 MT (+3.5% YoY); revenue INR973 crores (-2.2% YoY); EBITDA INR37 crores in Q2 (+21.5% QoQ); PAT INR22 crores in Q2 (+37% QoQ)
items.quote: The total volume of sales achieved after eliminating intercompany transactions in HY '26 was 182,210 metric ton, and this compares well with the sales of 176,091 metric tons in the half year of '25. This shows a growth of 3.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY26 volume 160,629 MT (-9% YoY); revenue INR875 crores (-11% YoY)
items.quote: The sales volume in the half year of financial was 160,629 metric tons as opposed to 176,091 in H1 of financial year '25. This is a decline of around 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Revenue split: Airtel 46.5%, Jio 22.7%, VI 26.3%, BSNL 4.5% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our revenue from Airtel is 46.5%, Jio stands steady at 22.7%. VI has increased to 26.3% and BSNL has increased to 4.5%.

items.statement: 5,861 towers and 7,163 tenancies at end of Q2 FY26; 702 sites ready for integration
items.quote: We have ended quarter at 5,861 towers with a total tenancy of 7,163. As per earlier quarter, we have crossed 1,000 tenancies of government sites, and 4,000 tenancies for small cell sites.

items.statement: 1,000+ km aerial fibre tender for MTNL in Mumbai Circle at final approval stage; expect allocation in 30-45 days
items.quote: We are on the final stages of getting 1,000 plus kilometres of fibre, aerial fibre tender in Mumbai Circle from MTNL. It has again completed all the negotiation stage and it is in the final approval with CMD and the top management of BSNL. Again, which we are expecting in a month to 45 days' time. We will also get allocation letter for MTNL 1,000 plus kilometres of aerial fibre.

items.statement: Airtel started 5G rollout on 2,500 ULS sites; gives INR3,000-4,000 per site per month upside with minimal CapEx
items.quote: Now one of the biggest upside for this quarter is Airtel has started deploying 5G rollout on our ULS site. So, we have already started deployment of these 5G sites to Airtel. We are managing around 2,500 sites for Airtel ULS across India on which Airtel has started giving us service order. It is in the process of deployment of 5G which gives us an immediate upside of INR3,000 to INR4,000 per site

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR250 crore, PAT INR80-85 crore maintained
items.quote: So right now, the guidance of top line is around INR250 cr. with PAT of around INR80 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue INR554 million, EBITDA INR417 million (75%), PAT INR166 million (30%)
items.quote: In terms of financials, our revenue – consolidated for quarter was INR554 million. EBITDA stands tall at INR417 million which is almost 75% of EBITDA. So, we have sustained an EBITDA percentage of 75%. Even our net profit is INR166 million and again we have sustained 30% net profit margin, even in current quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin up 201 bps YoY to 75%; PAT margin 30% down from 42% due to higher interest and depreciation
items.quote: My EBITDA margin again has increased by 201 bps. It stood strong at 75% and even if there's -- year-on-year H1 comparison to H1, then it has increased by 297 bps. PAT margin is again strong at 30% which has -- from 42% it has gone upto 30% mainly because of increasing interest cost and depreciation has increased for us.

items.statement: Revenue per tenancy INR25,000 in Q2 FY26 vs INR22,000 in March 2025; driven by Airtel upgrades and Lotus acquisition; BSNL rollout lowers per-tenancy revenue but improves EBITDA/PAT
items.quote: If you see my revenue per tenancy, my March '25 exact tenancy was -- revenue per tenancy was INR22,000 plus figure per tenancy revenue per month which has gone up to INR25,000 in current quarter which is mainly on the basis of the major upgrades which we have done for Bharti Airtel Limited which has given me INR3,000 upside per tenancy on Airtel sites, only on the basis of the upgrade where my Cap

items.statement: Revenue per tenancy expected to stabilize at INR26,000-27,000; Airtel 5G upside offset by BSNL rollout
items.quote: It will not go back to INR29,000, INR30,000 per month because along with Airtel 5G upgrade we are also doing BSNL rollout from Q4 onwards. So, it should be stable between INR25,000 to INR27,000.

items.statement: INR35 crore data centre fibre project in Mumbai; targeting closure by end-November/mid-December; partial execution in Q3, balance in Q4
items.quote: We are also working with some data centre companies where we are planning to lay fibre for them in Mumbai circle majorly, which will be around INR35 crores project which we want to materialize and -- which we want to start in this quarter and want to materialize by December which is also on a good - which is very good progress in terms of negotiation and which should get finalized anytime soon.

items.statement: Target debt INR250 crore; current bank loan INR96 crore; additional INR150 crore sanction pipeline; interest cost 9.5%
items.quote: Shivshankar Lature: Okay. I am saying from the start that I'll keep around INR250 cr. Mahek Talathi: Okay. And what will be the interest cost on this? Shivshankar Lature: Interest cost is 9.5%.

items.statement: In final stages of negotiation with 2-3 companies in Delhi and Rajasthan for inorganic growth
items.quote: We are also on a verge of discussing closing few inorganic growth. We are working with 2-3 companies mainly of Delhi and Rajasthan circle, where we are on the final stages of negotiation. If everything goes as per our plan, we would be soon closing a good number of inorganic growth for Suyog.

items.statement: EPC tender for BSNL: bid for 200+ sites; tender not yet opened; targeting 2,000-2,500 of 6,000-7,000 sites
items.quote: So, they have floating tender for around 6,000 to 7,000 sites across India, out of which we are trying to get 2,000 to 2,500 sites.

items.statement: Tenancy ratio currently 1.2x; expected to remain stable despite tower additions
items.quote: Right now, we have an -- our overall portfolio, we have 1.2 tenancy ratio between macro and small cell. It should continue the same way.

items.statement: Organic tenancy target revised to 8,500-9,000 by March FY26 (from 12,000); spillover to FY27; inorganic growth to bridge gap
items.quote: So, it will get spilled over to FY27 because we were expecting an order of BSNL to go through by October, which it seems now get handed by to December. So, we see yearend something around 8,500 sites by March and balance will get spilled over to next financial year, which more or less should happen by Q1 or Q2 of next financial year.

items.statement: FY27 tenancy target ~15,000+ (including 6,000 BSNL, VI rollout, current base)
items.quote: Sir, let me be more clear. You have seen my projects right now. 6,000 sites will anyways get deployed by FY27. We already have 7,000 tenancies. So, it makes 13,000 plus we will do some Vodafone also. So FY27 will be shortly around 15,000 sites or even more. 15,000 tenancies or even more.

items.statement: Long-term revenue mix target: Airtel 35-40%, Jio 20-25%, VI ~30%, BSNL ~15%
items.quote: It would not be very accurate, but technically what we are targeting is around Airtel should be around 35% to 40% of our revenue. Jio will contribute around 20% to 25% and same would be for -- BSNL should be around 15% and VI should be around 30%. That's what we are targeting right now.

items.statement: Fibre network 6,152 km; fibre revenue expected to contribute 10-15% of total by 2030+
items.quote: In the recent future, it won't be that high, but yes, we are expecting. So, when we say fibre, it includes many materials. It includes ABS fibre, underground fibre, FTTH, and everything put together. If you say we downline 2030 or beyond 2030, it should contribute to 10% to 15% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Advances to suppliers/vendors increased (other loans up to INR35 crore) to prepare sites for BSNL rollout; faster revenue realization upon order receipt
items.quote: What we are doing, since we are very confident of going through the BSNL tender, we are preparing our site well in advance so that whenever we receive the order, we can immediately arrive at the site and we can start booking our revenue. So, we have made advances to suppliers mainly and some vendors to keep our material ready.

items.statement: BSNL order delayed 1-1.5 months; now expected in December; deployment to start Q4 FY26
items.quote: For BSNL, yes, there is a delay in BSNL order but we all know that BSNL --government companies have their own processes which they need to follow but we had a couple of meetings with CMD in last - before Diwali and post Diwali also and we are very confident that it will go through. There is a little bit delay of 1, 1.5 months. We are expecting that order, which we were expecting in month of Octobe

items.statement: BSNL rollout pace dependent on TCS material delivery; TCS committed to deliver by end Q3
items.quote: So recently when we spoke with BSNL about their material, TCS has committed them to deliver all the material by end of Q3. And that's why we are very positive that my new rollout for BSNL will also start from Q4 and this integration also they'll complete in Q4.

items.statement: Strategy: raise debt first (bank sanctions INR150 crore), then equity dilution if needed for further rollout
items.quote: We have raised some funds from -- initially we wanted to do equity last year but now we have taken a strategy, where first we are raising the debt from the banks which is available through which we will do a major rollout. And then as and when required we will go for equity dilution.

items.statement: Vodafone payments now regular; no reversals in Q2 FY26 vs INR40 million reversal in Sep 2024
items.quote: My other income has dropped compared to year-on-year because there was around INR40 million Vodafone reversal in September '24. Right now, we don't have any reversal from Vodafone because payments are coming from Vodafone on regular basis which is one of the very positive and healthy sites for company where one of my private customers who is delaying payment is now started paying on timely basis.

items.statement: Laminates EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 16% on a yearly basis
items.quote: We have given a guidance of around 16% on a longer tenure basis. This quarter, apart from the volume, if you saw, there is an increase and this quarter we had a launch of our flagship brand of Greenlam also.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth target of 18-20% for the year
items.quote: At the overall level, we said we should be able to grow 18% -20% at an organization consolidated level basis. And I think we have maintained that.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 2 million sheets at Naidupeta facility with commercial production expected in Q4 FY27
items.quote: We have also announced a Brownfield expansion of 2 million sheets and boards. This is two lines of Laminates we are expanding at our facility at Andhra Pradesh, Naidupeta. And these two lines of 2 million sheets and boards will generate about, in the range of Rs. 375 crores to Rs. 400 crores of revenue. We are expecting commercial production in Q4 of FY '27.

items.statement: Future laminate line capex estimated at Rs. 45-50 crores per line including civil construction
items.quote: So, Capex, if you do civil, might go up. Because for this line, we do not need civil. We do not need the energy plant. We do not need to construct a resin plant because we already built that in the Phase I. So, while it is looking attractive now, but those investments have already been done earlier. So, it might, let us say, be in the range of, depending on what we do, about Rs. 45 crores - Rs. 50

items.statement: Current laminate capacity at 24 million sheets with 96% utilization in Q2; can add 6-7 more lines across Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat
items.quote: So, space wise, we can add multiple lines in Andhra Pradesh and in our factory in Gujarat. But for these two lines, we do not need to do any civil construction also. Because we have already built a larger space when we set up the factory. So, you can assume, but then the expansion process might involve civil construction in both the factories. But for the land space, we can comfortably add another

items.statement: Chipboard plant utilization at 36% in Q2; EBITDA breakeven expected at 45-50% utilization
items.quote: At about 45% to 50% utilization, we do EBITDA break-even. We are now at about 36% utilization. But you can run the numbers.

items.statement: Laminates production volumes at 5.9 million sheets in Q2 with 96% utilization; sales volume 5.79 million sheets at Rs. 1,104 average realization
items.quote: Products and volumes were the highest in this quarter and stood at 5.9 million sheets and both with a utilization l evel of 96%. Sales volume for the quarter stood at 5.79 million sheets and bo ard, with an average realization of Rs. 1,104 in this quarter

items.statement: US tariff impact: 40% of cost increase passed to market, 60% absorbed; US is 4-6% of export business
items.quote: Of the increase which is impacted to us because we ship to our subsidiary, which then does custom clearance and ships to the customers, of the increase, about 40% is something we are passing on to the market, and we are absorbing about 60% of the cost.

items.statement: Working capital improved to 47 days in Q2 from 59 days YoY; net debt reduced by Rs. 45 crores to Rs. 995 crores
items.quote: In this quarter, working capital improved by 12 days and stood at 47 days as compared to 59 days in Q2 last year. Net debt as on 30th September stood at Rs. 995 crores as against Rs. 1,040 crores in the June quarter with a reduction of Rs. 45 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by Rs. 45 crores sequentially to Rs. 995 crores as of September 30
items.quote: Net debt as on 30th September stood at Rs. 995 crores as against Rs. 1,040 crores in the June quarter with a reduction of Rs. 45 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Chipboard realization mix shifting between melamine and plain boards; plywood realization dipped 1.3% due to volume mix
items.quote: So, I think it will still take some time to settle this mix of melamine Chipboard and plain Chipboard. So, I think for maybe a few more months or quarters, this might be a bit here and there, then we will kind of settle it. So, that is on the Chipboard. Even plywood, the realization has been down by, if I can see, it is a small dip. It is again some mix of orders because volume has gone up Q -on-Q

items.statement: Laminates volume growth 6.7% YoY in H1; average realization Rs. 1,098 per sheet
items.quote: Volume grew by 6.7%. EBITDA margin stood at 16.6%, a growth of 240 basis points on year-on-year basis. Production volumes were at 11.06 million sheets with a utilization level of 90%. Sales volume in this half year stood at 10.73 million sheets with an average realization of 1,098 per sheet and board

items.statement: Chipboard EBITDA breakeven targeted in FY27; Plywood EBITDA breakeven targeted in FY26
items.quote: So, Chipboard, really, I think the way things are moving, we think we should be able to break even EBITDA in FY '27. And ply also, again, we are very close. You see a little bit of more push on the numbers and it should happen. So, yes, maybe be around there.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue growth guidance of 50-60%
items.quote: As our honorable CMD sir has already been talking about 50 % to 60% growth in terms of the revenue, we look forward to the same.

items.statement: Order book stands at 2.2+ GW worth INR 2,900 crore for KP Energy
items.quote: The order book currently stands at 2.2 plus Gigawatt, inching us closer to the ambitious target of 10 Gigawatt on the Group level, giving us a competitive edge in renewables and aligning us for the growth trajectory.

items.statement: Order pipeline of ~3 GW with external clients including PSUs and large corporates
items.quote: So, as I said before, around 3 Gigawatt is already in bid and we are expecting results by the end of next month.

items.statement: Delayed orders expected by December 2025 pending PPA execution
items.quote: So, while we were expecting the orders in this particular quarter, we wish to specify here that everything is lined up and we are just waiting for the PPA execution.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain stable at current levels
items.quote: Yes, more or less they will be on the same line.

items.statement: IPP margins expected to improve as portfolio scales beyond current 48.5 MW
items.quote: So, going forward, we expect the margins to improve. The reason being is if you look at the quantum of IPP in the Group entity of KPI Green, they are much higher and they have the large-scale benefits also in terms of the O&M of the entire plant.

items.statement: IPP expansion targeting additional 50 MW by September 2026 for tax depreciation benefits
items.quote: While we had an original target of 100 Megawatt, of which around 50 Megawatt, 48.5 Megawatt has already been commissioned. And the balanced 50 Megawatt is what we are looking forward to commission it within the next year.

items.statement: Average capex ~INR 3 crore/MW for solar and ~INR 8 crore/MW for wind IPP projects
items.value: INR 3 crore/MW solar, INR 8 crore/MW wind
items.quote: However, on an average, you can take about INR 3 crores on an average per Megawatt in terms of solar and about INR 8 crores per Megawatt in terms of wind is what you can take.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded two notches to A- with stable outlook by CARE Ratings
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that during the quarter, CARE Ratings has upgraded KP Energy's credit rating two notches up from BBB with a negative outlook to A - with a stable outlook.

items.statement: Low debt-equity ratio with no big long-term loans; fund availability not a constraint
items.quote: And if you look at the debt equity and everything of KP Energy is very low. So, there are no big long-term loans on the books. So, we will have that capability to raise the funds whenever it is required for the IPP project also.

items.statement: Operating cash flow jumped from INR 6 crore to INR 85 crore in H1 YoY
items.quote: We have recorded a sharp jump in operating cash flow, which increased from INR 6 crore to INR 85 crore, in comparison to the H1 of previous year, reflecting both higher revenue and improved operational efficiency.

items.statement: IPP portfolio at 48.5 MW (11.5 MW solar, 37 MW wind); targeting 100 MW total
items.quote: Our consolidated IPP portfolio stands at 48.5 Megawatt, which is a combination of both wind and solar projects.

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 600+ MW providing end-to-end support
items.quote: The portfolio is currently 600-plus Megawatts, offering an end-to-end support, including the preventive care and diagnostics towards efficiency enhancements.

items.statement: EPC order book includes both wind and solar; hybrid projects preferred by clients for RTC power
items.quote: So, typically, I would first like to explain, irrespective of whosoever the client is, if you look at the industry, per se, majority of the players are going for hybrid power.

items.statement: 1.3 GW of 2.2+ GW order book from group entity KPI Green; rest from external PSUs and corporates
items.quote: So, in terms of megawatt, if you look at it, then about 1,300, so about 1.3 Gigawatt stands from Group entity.

items.statement: 3 GW bid pipeline entirely from external clients (PSUs and large corporates)
items.quote: These are all that we have already taken up with external clients. A couple of them are PSUs and others are large corporates.

items.statement: Stricter Deviation Settlement Mechanism being addressed via forecasting center, IBM partnership, and energy trading license
items.quote: We have been hit with a regulation that going forward, there will be stringent regulation regarding the Deviation Settlement Mechanism. And there will be more penalties on whether we can deviate or not.

items.statement: IPP tariffs: solar ~INR 7-7.5/unit, wind GUVNL ~INR 2.43/unit gross; net same as transmission borne by client
items.quote: While you talk about the gross rate of the per unit energy in solar, it comes to an average solar and when both together, it comes to an average of about 7 to 7.5. Whereas in wind, the GUVNL specific, it comes to around 2.4, 2.5, 2.43 rather to be precise.

items.statement: Quarterly generation from own IPP projects rose from 0.69 crore to 2.75 crore units YoY in Q2
items.quote: The quarterly unit generation during the Q2 of FY '26 rose from 0.69 crore to 2.75 crore s as compared to the previous year's second quarter, thereby representing a substantial growth in the generation of energy in our own project.

items.statement: UAE MoU for RTC power supply to data centers and life sciences; both KPI and KP Energy to supply wind and solar
items.quote: That is relevant for both KPI and KPE because what we would be doing is we would be supplying again RTC power to data centers and life science projects across the UAE and the India.

items.statement: No merger plans between KP Energy and KPI Green; separate listed entities to continue
items.quote: So, currently, there are no such plans and in case if there is anything, we will definitely announce it on the public portal.

items.statement: Technology agnostic approach; collaborating with all major wind OEMs including Goldwind for 5X-6X MW turbines
items.quote: We are technology agnostic and we work with multiple vendors in this space.

items.statement: Group-level target of 10+ GW by 2030; KP Energy share estimated ~40-60% of group capacity
items.quote: KP Energy has already commissioned 1 plus Gigawatt until today and with 2.2 Gigawatt already in hand. We are already at 3.3 to be commissioned within the next year and a half.

items.statement: Revenue seasonality: 35-40% in H1, 60-65% in H2 due to monsoon and billing milestones
items.quote: One is the seasonality of the particular nature, as you have seen, observed everywhere, every year and every quarter, that while about 35% to 40% of the total revenue flows in the first half of the financial year, whereas the 65 % to 60% of the revenue falls in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Among very few wind EPC operators in India; limited competition gives pricing power
items.quote: KP Energy is one of the very few operators in the wind segment, there are not many players operating here, and the orders which KP Energy has got from KPI are the IPP orders of KPI, which are being executed as CPP orders or EPC orders for KP Energy.

items.statement: Nearshore wind identified as promising avenue; Gujarat and Tamil Nadu selected for nearshore/offshore development
items.quote: Additionally, near-shore wind development are emerging as a promising avenue, offering high wind potential and easier grid integration compared to offshore projects.

items.statement: Expect to close FY26 at the higher end of guidance range
items.quote: Based on this current trajectory, we expect to close FY ' 26 at the higher end of our guidance range.

items.statement: Expect to close FY26 at the higher end of guidance range supported by fintech and AI momentum
items.quote: We expect to close FY '26 at the higher end of our guidance range, supported by momentum across both our fintech and AI-led businesses.

items.statement: Robust merchant onboarding and TPV growth driven by favorable card mix and vertical expansion
items.quote: Domestically, we continue to see robust merchant onboarding and TPV growth supported by favorable card mix and a vertical expansion across travel, entertainment, utilities, recharges and services.

items.statement: International payments in UAE and Saudi Arabia processing billions of dirhams annually with Oman launching next
items.quote: Internationally, our operations in UAE and Saudi Arabia are scaling rapidly, processing billions of dirhams annually with Oman set to launch next.

items.statement: Expect international payments to contribute double-digit net revenue within 12-18 months
items.quote: We expect international payments to contribute double -digit net revenue within the next 12 months to 18 months.

items.statement: Received RBI in-principle authorization for PPI license under CCAvenue Go brand for prepaid instruments
items.quote: We have received in -principle authorizations from the Reserve Bank of India to issue prepaid payment instruments, PPIs, under our new brand CCAvenue Go.

items.statement: Received IFSCA in-principle approval for subsidiary to operate as payment service provider at GIFT-IFSC with cross-border and escrow licenses
items.quote: We have also received IFSCA in-principle approval for our subsidiary IA Fintech IFSC Private Limited to operate as a payment service provider at the GIFT-IFSC.

items.statement: Launched PayCentral.AI as India's first agentic payment platform on Google's agent payment protocol
items.quote: Launch of PayCentral.AI. It is India's first agentic payment platform built on Google's agent payment protocol, enabling AI agents to transact autonomously on any site.

items.statement: Launched Agent Operating System and Agentic.ai marketplace for autonomous digital coworkers
items.quote: The second one is the Agent Operating System, which is a next -generation orchestration layer connecting reasoning, vision, language models, and enterprise workflows.

items.statement: Signed MoU with Nawgati to deploy video LLMs and agentic AI for industrial automation
items.quote: And the last one is the M oU with a company called Nawgati, which is where we deploy our video large language models and agentic AI for real-time reasoning and automation in industrial environments.

items.statement: Partnered with Sree Narayana Guru Co-operative Bank and integrated with TJSB Sahakari Bank for merchant acquisition
items.quote: We have partnered with Sree Narayana Guru Co-operative Bank to power its merchants with advanced digital payment solutions, expanding CCAvenue's reach into the co-operative banking segment.

items.statement: Went live with NPCI Bharat Connect onboarding Bajaj Finance for next-gen net banking experience
items.quote: At CCAvenue platform, we have also gone live with the NPCI 's Bharat Bill Payment Bharat Connect, onboarding Bajaj Finance Limited to deliver next-gen net banking experience at scale.

items.statement: Plan to invest Rs 500-700 crore ($75-100 million) in Rediff over next three years
items.quote: I think, I can see that Rediff will perhaps invest upwards of, $75 million to $100 million in the next three years. So, I am talking about Rs. 500 crore to Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Budgeted Rs 40 crore for RediffPay marketing launch
items.quote: And as far as the budget is concerned, we have budgeted about Rs. 40 crores.

items.statement: Consciously optimized for absolute profit over net take rate; take rate fell from 11.2 to 8.2 basis points but absolute profit grew
items.quote: And rather than optimizing just on the net take rate, if you look at the net take rate it is gone down from 11.2 basis points to 8.2 basis points. But what we realized was that we will monitor the take rate, but we want to make sure that we optimize on absolute profits

items.statement: Deployed 50,000 SoundBox Max devices with credit/debit acceptance; AI integration feasible via existing SIM connectivity
items.quote: We already have a SoundBox Max product, almost 50,000-odd deployed, where you can do credit, debit, apart from a normal speaker, sound, speaker, a UPI, where it announces the transaction result.

items.statement: Gross revenue Rs 1,965 crore up 53% QoQ and 93% YoY; net revenue Rs 153 crore up 14% YoY; PAT Rs 65 crore up 18% YoY
items.quote: Our gross revenue on a consolidated basis went to Rs. 1,965 crores, which is highest ever in the history of the company, which is up by 53%, sequentially and 93% year-on-year.

items.statement: Rediff has 100 million registered email users with 5-10 million daily active users
items.quote: Rediff has more than 100 million registered email users. I am not talking about the RediffOne platform going to 20,000-plus merchants, but there are 100 million registered email users.

items.statement: Rediffmail sends over 1 billion emails monthly across 20,000+ enterprises
items.quote: And it is already live across more than 20,000 enterprises. And we send out about more than 1 billion emails every month.

items.statement: No plans to enter banking or NBFC; will stop at PPI license and connect banks/NBFCs to consumers and merchants
items.quote: We do not have any plans to go into banking or NBFC at all. What we may end up doing as we speak is we are evaluating opportunities, because we will connect the NBFCs and banks to consumers and merchants.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds of Rs 87 crore invested in Rediff; future Rediff capital needs to be raised by Rediff Board
items.quote: As far as the rights issue, we had put in about Rs. 87 odd crores in Rediff. And we think that, there is a lot of opportunity to actually build up this brand.

items.statement: Rediff Board will evaluate all options including listing if additional capital needed
items.quote: That is for the Rediff Board to answer but Yes, I think they would want to look at all options that are available.

items.statement: Rediff app re-engineered with new UI launched 3-4 months ago; 5-10 million daily users on app
items.quote: In fact, we upgraded the app just three or four months ago. And it comes with a completely new, clean UI and many others. So, hopefully, you will see quite see that ratings and so on and so forth are from years ago.

items.statement: RediffPay will combine UPI TPAP and PPI wallet; wallet enables single bank entry for multiple transactions
items.quote: RediffPay entails both. It entails both the UPI, TPAP as well as the wallet. I hope, I am able to...

items.statement: Rediff TV launched in beta as fully AI-driven multilingual content streaming platform
items.quote: The third pillar is Rediff TV, or content. It is currently in beta. This is India's first fully AI-driven content streaming platform, which is multilingual, automated, scalable, and practically with minimal manual production.

items.statement: Management reiterates INR 10,000 crore revenue vision and aspirational EBITDA margin progression to double-digits then teens, but gives no specific yearly forecast.
items.quote: we have already stated a vision of INR 10,000 crores a couple of months back where our Chairman stated the vision, and we are all working towards achieving that milestone. The short-term item like update on what is the outlook for the year, we do not per se give a specific number for the outlook for the year. However, we continue to stay to our vision of INR 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Milk prices rose 16% YoY and 2% sequentially to INR 38/litre; company passed on cost via pricing power, improved mix, and cost efficiencies.
items.value: INR 38 per litre average milk price
items.quote: The milk prices witnessed an inflation of around 16% year-on-year and were sequentially higher by around 2% during the quarter. The average milk price during the quarter inched up to INR 38 per litre.

items.statement: Operating cash flow funded internal capex; depreciation on past capex largely offsets Maharashtra incentive income.
items.quote: The deployment, if you look at is largely gone into capital expenditure, which we have been able to fund ourselves. That is one. And secondly, the interest payout, which is there on the existing debt.

items.statement: Procurement at 15 lakh litres/day; target to scale to 40 lakh litres/day and increase BMC share vs aggregator model.
items.value: 15 lakh litres/day current; 40 lakh litres/day target
items.quote: How do we have a stable procurement? How do we increase our procurement scale from today's 15 lakh litres to, say, 40 lakh litres over a period of time ? How do we go into increasing our share of having BMCs versus the overall aggregator-based milk procurement.

items.statement: Net debt reduced INR 125 crore to INR 436 crore (Sept 2025); net debt/EBITDA 1.4x, net debt/equity 0.4x; FCCB conversion and equity infusion drove deleveraging.
items.value: INR 436 crore net debt; 1.4x net debt/EBITDA; 0.4x net debt/equity

As a result, our consolidated net debt reduced by INR125 crores from a consolidated net debt levels of INR 561 crores as on March 2025 to INR 436 crores as on September 2025. This deleveraging has strengthened our gearing ratios, bringing ou

items.quote: In GST, of course, we had to pass on while there was a benefit on account of the rate reduction and specifically in most of our categories which we operate in. So we have passed on the benefit to consumers and reduce the prices. Having said that, there are categories where even the GST has been made zero. So for example, a category like paneer, this gives an opportunity to again further deepen bet

items.statement: Key risks: scaling procurement from 15 to 40 lakh litres/day, increasing BMC share, deepening distribution in South/North, and execution of strategy.
items.quote: The risk is procurement. How do we have a stable procurement? How do we increase our procurement scale from today's 15 lakh litres to, say, 40 lakh litres over a period of time ? How do we go into increasing our share of having BMCs versus the overall aggregator-based milk procurement. So these are things on the procurement side. Same way, the opportunity exists in expanding our distribution netwo

items.statement: Management maintains mid-double digit revenue growth guidance for FY26 despite uncertainties
items.quote: we will still stick with the numbers and the initial guidance what we have given that we will have this year, like, a mid-double digit growth

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 30-32% and PAT margin 21-22% for FY26 excluding tariff impact
items.quote: we will continue to have the margin of PAT about 21% to 22%, EBITDA of 30% to 32%

items.statement: US inquiries dropped from ~100/month to 4-6/month in last 2-3 months indicating significant demand slowdown
items.quote: the number of inquiries which used to be, let's say, about hundred in a month dropped down to four, five, six new inquiries

items.statement: Standalone total income grew 12% YoY in Q2 to INR 288 crores; H1 grew 12% to INR 567 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew 5% YoY to INR 12.7 crores in Q2; H1 PAT INR 23.5 crores.

items.statement: Standalone FY26 revenue growth guidance 12-14% YoY with EBITDA margins 15-17%
items.quote: For the standalone business, we maintain our FY '26 guidance of 12% to 14% revenue growth with EBITDA margins of 15% to 17%, supported by a robust order book and improved utilization.

items.statement: Innoxel FY26 revenue Rs 65-70 crore driven by milestones; EBITDA breakeven expected

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 clear path to positive PAT by FY27

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 gross margin expanded to 58.3% from 41.8% YoY

items.statement: Varenyam operational margins improved from 39% to 45% in H1 FY26

items.statement: Standalone Q2 orders deferred to Q3-Q4; order book supports H2 rebound
items.quote: Based on that and the operational effectiveness that we were able to achieve in Quarter 2, we remain hopeful of achieving our EBITDA margin improvement anywhere between 15% and 17% for this fiscal year.

items.statement: Rs 210 crore domestic institutional order: Q1 tranche done, Q2-Q3 in H2, final tranche Q1 FY27

items.statement: Innoxel finalized 7 new strategic partnerships (6 CMO, 1 out-licensing) worth $1.85M in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, Innoxel finalized 7 new strategic partnerships including 6 EMO contracts and one out-licensing deal, together valued at $1.85 million in licensing and milestone income.

items.statement: Innoxel pipeline: ~20 active products (60% complex ANDAs, 40% 505(b)(2)), 3 long-acting programs, 40+ molecules lifetime

items.quote: currently, there are about 6,500 members, out of which 55% come back month -on-month. But these memb ers are really your high spending members, and they account for 15% of the overall business

items.statement: No aggressive store expansion; focusing on maximizing existing store throughput and online investment
items.quote: We will not add on a lot more stores. So, we are not doing that. We are trying to get the maximum juice out of existing stores

items.quote: The moment you start getting to INR25 crores, you can probably bring INR25 crores per month, you can bring down that loss to about INR1.5 crores

items.statement: Consolidated sales per square foot improved to INR1,600+ in Q2 from INR1,500 in Q1 and INR1,200 in Q2 last year
items.quote: quarter 2 it's at a INR1,600-plus level versus INR1,500 in quarter 1 of last year. The comparative for last year, quarter 2 is much better

items.statement: Jiffy achieved positive unit economics in August-September with fulfilment costs under INR100 against AOV of INR750+
items.quote: we were able to achieve positive unit economics in August and September. Basically, it means our fu lfilment costs, which is your picking, delivery, things like bank charges and shrink, they came under INR100

items.statement: Jiffy metrics: 100,000+ monthly transacting users, 8,000 orders/day, 90% infill rate, ~30-minute on-time delivery
items.quote: We have more than 100,000 -plus monthly transacting users. The total number of orders are in the range of 8,000 orders per day. The AOV, the average order value continues to be strong, 750 plus

items.statement: Jiffy customer acquisition cost at INR330, benchmarked favorably against industry
items.quote: Our customer acquisition costs are INR330, which, again, if you look at industry benchmarks, is pretty kind, I will say, benchmarked over there

items.statement: Nature's Basket out-of-store (online + phone) mix at 16-17% of business
items.quote: Overall, the out -of-store mix for Nature's Basket is close to 16 -17%

items.statement: Continuing to access promoter group capital largely via debt; evaluating alternate fund raise options
items.quote: the fact that we will continue using similar arrangements to access to capital, I think, which is largely debt. And of course, now that's at a certain level. But we are also looking at what could be alternate ways

items.statement: Online growth limited by capital access vs deep-pocketed peers; will not pursue triple-digit losses
items.quote: we might not be in a similar situation as some of the industry -leading players, which have th e ability to take triple -digit losses because they have access to deeper pockets and deeper pool of capital and private equity

items.statement: Nature's Basket facing online competition from premium gourmet players like FirstClub and Food Square on marketplaces
items.quote: There's FirstClub in Bangalore, which is premium gourmet grocery online retailer. And there are other players who are Food Square i n Bombay, which is using third -party marketplaces to sell their offerings

items.statement: Total order book stands at around INR90,000 crores as of September 30, comprising INR43,000 crores legacy railway orders and INR46,000 crores from competitive bidding
items.quote: So total order book is in excess of around INR90,000 crores at present with RVNL.

items.statement: Order inflow for Q2 FY26 was INR852 crores; H1 FY26 inflow was INR2,000 crores
items.quote: The total orders in the last quarter, we have received the order of INR852 crores in the last quarter. And in the last 6 months, we have got the order of INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 maintained at INR21,000 crores to INR22,000 crores
items.quote: So we maintain the revenue guidance of around INR21,000 crores to INR22,000 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY26 is INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores based on bidding pipeline of INR75,000-80,000 crores and 10-12% success rate
items.quote: And considering our success rate of 10% to 12%, we hope that the order inflow for this year is likely to touch around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be in the range of 4% to 5% for FY26 and FY27, aligned with industry standards
items.quote: Right now, we cannot predict exactly, but we hope to maintain the momentum and our EBITDA margin will be in the range of whatever the industry standard for the infrastructure industry, that is roughly in the range of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Margins lower in H1 due to 30% revenue from competitive bidding projects vs higher-margin legacy projects; focusing on HAM and international projects to improve margins to 5-6%
items.quote: Basically, in this year's turnover, there is almost 30% turnover has come from the bidding projects. Yes. In legacy projects, we have very good margins. But in projects we have owned through competitive bidding, the margins are slightly lower.

items.statement: Order book mix: 33% railway (civil, electrical, signalling), 22% metro, 12% BharatNet, 10% roads, 10% Vande Bharat manufacturing share
items.quote: Then the second largest component is from the metro sector. Metro sector comprises of around our 22% order books and road sector order book is around 10%. Our 12% order book is from basically BharatNet project.

items.statement: Vande Bharat production: first prototype June 2026, second August 2026; 12 trainsets in FY27, then 25 per year for 5 years; O&M for 35 years starts with first trainsets
items.quote: And the first prototype as per the scheme is -- will be coming in June '26. And the second prototype will be coming in August '26. And when these prototypes are tested and certified for further production in the balance period of 26-27, 12 regular rates will be produced, followed by 25 rates every year in the next 5 years.

items.statement: International order book currently INR3,200 crores; bidding for projects in Central Asia, Middle East, East Asia, East Europe; aim to substantially grow global operations
items.quote: Yes. International order book is a total of order of around INR3,200 crores total, out of which some of projects are under execution. And we are also in process of bidding or already bided for many projects in Central Asia, Middle East or East Asia, even East Europe.

items.statement: Order book adequate for next 4 years execution; projects vary from 1-4 year gestation; targeting 10% revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: So average, you can consider this order book considering our growth trajectory is adequate for the next 4 years' time.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in H1 due to reduction in unbilled revenue; cash flow expected to improve from mid-December as construction season picks up
items.quote: Yes. At each reporting date, we calculate the contracts for which the project has been made, but the invoice has not been raised to client. So that varies from quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Entered multimodal logistics parks sector with NHLM; 4 parks in process of operationalization; bidding for HAM projects with 20-25 year concession periods
items.quote: We have entered into multimodal logistics park sectors in collaboration with National Highway Logistics Management Limited and the 4 multimodal logistics parks already in the process of operationalization.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline for FY26 estimated at INR75,000-80,000 crores with 10-12% expected success rate
items.quote: In the current financial year, our bidding will be in the range of around INR75,000 crores to INR80,000 crores. And considering our success rate of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Road sector tendering deferred due to land availability and statutory clearances; NHAI strategy evolving from EPC to HAM/BOT mix
items.quote: Some of the projects, high-value projects, especially in the road sector. They were -- the tendering was repeatedly deferred due to various reasons, be it availability of land or other statutory clearances.

items.statement: Government policy prohibits direct construction work for infrastructure PSUs; RVNL aligning business strategy beyond railway projects
items.quote: Wherein direct combination work for infrastructure has been prohibited from indirectly in order to PSU. So we are aligning our business strategies and developing our product profile in a manner that it goes beyond railway projects.

Singh, who is Director Operations; Mr. Abhishek Kumar, Director Finance and accompanied with him is Mr. Chandan Kumar Verma, who is Chief Financial Officer at RVNL.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 organic constant currency growth expected flattish to marginally positive; Q4 FY26 meaningful growth expected

In terms of Quarter 4, we do believe that there will be a meaningful growth, which will be coming in.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin target maintained at 21% after salary increments
items.quote: we are very confident that what we have talked about, that we will be in a position to maintain 21% EBITDA for the full year.. That would be considering the fact that we will be giving increments, some in next quarter and some in the quarter after.

These are the areas in which the wins have been more and also the products we have in validation, etc., mainly Technica products. So, they have largely compensated for this drop.

items.statement: Solutions revenue more than doubled to 18% of total revenue, improving profitability
items.quote: When we talk about solutions, it means that we take a holistic view and give an end-to-end solution to the client and take full ownership. This kind of revenue we have more than doubled in the last year to 18% of our overall revenues. And that has also helped us improve profitability.

items.statement: Investments in Helm.ai, Caresoft acquisition, and Qorix JV to expand technology portfolio and reduce vehicle manufacturing cost

These are all very related technologies which will really help us improve our wallet share.

items.quote: I would be cautious right now, but I will give you more color on this by end of Q4 only, By that time, I think some of the uncertainties would be less. I would see that it will be a meaningful growth, but it would not be like a hockey stick recovery in the year.

items.quote: Yes, that remains on track. And for the next year also, we will target a full utilization level, which is somewhere between INR 950 crore to INR 1,000 crore.
