items.quote: We have so far completed capex of around INR 620 crore. And by end of this year, we expect another INR 500 crore. And as we complete next year, our existing capacity will increase, we will complete the INR 1,500 crore capex across our Dahej and Pakhajan sites.

items.statement: Greenfield electrolyte plant mechanical completion by end of CY2025; trial production in H1 FY27; commercial electrolyte in H1 FY27 and salt in H2 FY27
items.quote: We anticipate mechanical completion before the end of this year and then commence trial production followed by commercial production in first half of FY27, which is April to September 2026 and electrolyte salt in H2 of FY27

items.statement: PPAP approval received from leading Indian gigascale customer for electrolyte; provisional approval for lithium electrolyte salt from key international customer with final approval expected Q4 FY26
items.quote: A leading Indian gigascale customer has successfully completed the stringent Production Part Approval Process also called as PPAP and approved our Dahej plant for long-term commercial electrolyte supply.

items.statement: Full volume commitment agreements for 5.5 KTA salt capacity; long-term supply agreements for electrolyte under discussion
items.quote: For the salt, we already have agreements in place, which will completely take care of the 5,500 metric tonne or 5.5 KTA capacity, which we are putting up.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 18% +/- 1-1.5% at full utilization (INR 950-1,000 crore); Neogen Ionics targets 20% ROCE with EBITDA margin 16-20% depending on lithium prices
items.quote: But next year, when we hit full utilization, INR 950 crore to INR 1,000 crore on standalone basis, we expect the same (margin) - 18% plus or minus one, 1%, 1.5% margin.

items.statement: Standalone debt INR 722 crore, net debt INR 595 crore; consolidated debt INR 1,078 crore, net debt INR 900 crore; peak debt expected INR 1,800 crore around FY28
items.quote: Our peak debt is expected to be INR 1,800 crore. And we would basically reach this one year closer to our full utilization level. So around FY28 or so, we would reach, whenever peak demand would be there for the peak debt.

items.statement: Private placement of INR 200 crore NCDs executed for Dahej plant rebuild and growth projects
items.quote: To ensure that we maintain our growth trajectory and operational stability, we have successfully executed a private placement of INR 200 crore NCDs.

items.statement: Inventory increased to rebuild INR 170-180 crore lost in Dahej fire; insurance claim of ~INR 300 crore (stock + loss of profit) expected over next year
items.quote: As you are aware, we had indicated we lost around INR 180 crore of inventory in Dahej during fire, INR 170 crore to INR 180 crore of inventory during fire. The increase that you are seeing in last six months is basically making up for the inventory which we have lost.

items.statement: Chinese electrolyte salt prices firming up due to capacity closures and strong energy storage demand; Neogen contracts priced competitively vs non-China benchmarks
items.quote: We have also heard that there was a very strong move in the electrolyte salt, as well as, to some extent, electrolyte cost also in China. And most of the Chinese were selling only at raw material costs and what I call manpower.

items.statement: US 45X tax credits require non-FEOC electrolyte salt supply chain by 2027; customers transitioning throughout 2026; Neogen JV with Morita provides non-FEOC compliant LiPF6 technology
items.quote: US lithium-ion battery cell producers must comply with foreign entities of concern (FOEC) guidelines to secure the lucrative US Government tax credits also known as 45X credits. This requires a complete transition to non-FEOC suppliers by 2027 for electrolyte salt.

items.statement: Indo-Japan JV formed: Neogen Morita New Materials Limited (NML) for LiPF6 salt production; Neogen Ionics holds minimum 80%, Morita Investments maximum 20%
items.quote: We are thrilled to announce this major strategic milestone - the formation of the first Indo-Japan joint venture in the crucial battery material space.

items.statement: Board approved separation of Chairman and MD roles effective Oct 1, 2025; Anurag Surana as Non-Executive Chairman; TCN Sai Krishnan appointed Executive Director
items.quote: The board has approved the separation of the roles of Chairman and Managing Director, effective October 1, 2025. We are pleased to announce the designating Mr. Anurag Surana as Non-Executive Chairman of Neogen Chemicals Ltd.

items.statement: Dahej plant rebuild on track for Q1 FY27; insurance claim delays for stock (Q3 FY26) and loss of profit (Q2-Q3 FY27); bankers extended greenfield moratorium by one year
items.quote: Also, in line with our revised commissioning dates, our bankers have also extended, for our greenfield site, the start date by around one year. So that also will push our repayment schedule by one year.

items.statement: US electrolyte salt demand estimated at 40-60 KTA for 300-500 GWh cell production by 2027; current US production ~140-150 GWh
items.quote: If we take 300 to 500 kind of gigawatt hour, there should be a total demand of around 40 KTA to 60 KTA, if everything has to switch for a 300 gigawatt production.

items.statement: Indian electrolyte demand delayed vs earlier estimates; Ola and Exide gigafactory ramp-up expected H2 CY2026; LFP chemistry requires 2-3x more electrolyte per GWh vs NMC
items.quote: As compared to what we had earlier estimated, demand to start from almost Q2, Q3 itself, electrolyte demand in India has been delayed.

items.statement: FY27 battery chemicals revenue split roughly 50% electrolyte, 50% salt; customers choosing between local salt vs Chinese imports based on PLI localization and cost
items.quote: We feel it will be roughly half-and-half. Almost 50% coming from electrolyte and 50% coming from salt.

items.statement: Neogen positioned as 3rd/4th global non-FEOC LiPF6 supplier; only Indian plant with PPAP for electrolyte; Japanese capacity 3-5 KTA, Korean 2 KTA, Neogen adding 7 KTA total
items.quote: There is still no supply available in Europe. There is still no supply available in the US. There is one Korean company which is talking about starting, but again, we do not know exactly how, but we are way ahead in terms of contracted volume, interest and approval processes.

items.statement: International customers accelerating non-FEOC transition in 2026; some switching Q1-Q2 CY2026, others Q3-Q4 CY2026; Neogen JV enhances credibility for global supply
items.quote: Most of the customers depending on their stringencies have indicated that some of them who are more cautious, they will start switching from Q1, Q2 calendar year 2026 and some who are little bit more price conscious, they would like to switch from Q3, Q4 of calendar year 2026.

items.statement: MUIS technology provides efficient electrolyte manufacturing process with 30-year track record; Morita JV brings proven Japanese LiPF6 technology for non-FEOC salt production
items.quote: Their process is very efficient with 30 years. So, actually the operating costs also can be lower as compared to somebody else.

items.statement: DSCR trailing 12-month at 2.1x; term loan repayment ~INR 40-50 crore next 12 months; project loan interest capitalized until commercial production
items.quote: Debt coverage remains healthy and demonstrated by the trailing 12-month DSCR of 2.1 times.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% YoY revenue growth and 20-25% EBITDA margin for core gaming business

items.statement: Over 90% of gaming revenue from international markets with strong US and UK focus
items.quote: At this point of time, over 90% of our gaming revenue comes from international markets, with a strong focus on the US a nd the UK markets

items.statement: Core gaming EBITDA margin at 23.2% in H1 FY26 and 22.1% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for this business was 23.2%. In Q2 FY26, on a year-on-year basis, the segment grew by 159% in revenues and 213% in EBITDA, with an EBITDA margin of 22.1%.

items.statement: Nodwin targets $1 billion revenue in 5-7 years across Live, Content, eSports, Influencers

items.statement: Funky Monkeys expanding 1-2 stores monthly, targets 100 centers from current 14 in couple years
items.quote: We are launching one to two stores every month, which is going to compound. So I think we are quite excited about that and there's huge scalability. We believe the current 14 centers can get to 100 centers in the next couple of years.

items.statement: AI coding WCC 4 with Claude to optimize costs and increase productivity

items.quote: Human Fall Flat delivering 1.25 million units in September 2025, up 25% year -on-year, while Wobbly Life surpassed 2 million lifetime units.

items.statement: AdTech revenue up 501% and EBITDA up 289% YoY in Q2 FY26; H1 EBITDA INR 10 crores

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin expected to stabilize at 67%-68%

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR 125 crores for 35 new restaurants plus maintenance and corporate capex
items.quote: We plan for close to INR 125 crores in this financial year to meet our plan of around 35 new restaurants.

items.statement: H2 FY26 corporate EBITDA margin expected around 8% pre-Ind AS

items.statement: Premium CDR segment targets 30% network growth in FY26
items.quote: We target for 30% network growth in FY26 in the premium CDR segment.

items.statement: International business plans 4-5 new restaurants in FY26
items.quote: We plan to open 4 -5 new restaurants in FY26, while maintaining focus on Same-Store Sales Growth and operational excellence.

items.statement: October consolidated SSSG up 6-7%; India business up 5%+
items.quote: October was up by approximately 6%-7% on same-store sales growth, on a consolidated basis. And our India business was also up by upwards of 5% in the month of October.

items.statement: Dine-in grew 1.6% QoQ with 2% transaction growth over 4 months; delivery grew 7% QoQ with 12% transaction growth
items.quote: Our Dine-in business grew by 1.6 % quarter-on-quarter, with approximately 2% transaction growth over the 4-month period, while our delivery business grew 7 % sequentially, supported by 12% transaction growth during the same period.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 66.2%, down 150 bps QoQ due to culinary initiatives and value group offers
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 66.2%, down by about 150 basis points sequentially, primarily due to culinary initiatives and value-driven group offers.

items.statement: Mature restaurants delivered ~9.6% pre-Ind AS ROM; consolidated reported EBITDA INR 37.7 cr at 12.4% margin
items.quote: Matured restaurants delivered around 9.6% pre Ind AS restaurant operating margins. Cons olidated reported EBITDA stood at INR 37.7 crores, with 12.4% margin, while adjusted operating EBITDA was INR 3.3 crores, at 1.1% margin.

items.statement: International mature portfolio sustains 20%+ pre-Ind AS ROM; segment gross margin 72%

items.statement: 15 new restaurants under construction; on track for 35 openings in FY26

items.statement: FY26 capex INR 125 cr for 35 new restaurants plus maintenance, renovation, corporate capex

items.statement: Management sees short-term debt ceiling around INR 100 cr; long-term view depends on margin recovery to double-digit EBITDA

items.statement: Marketing spend increased ~1.2% of sales YoY in Q2; largely digital (Meta, Google) plus 20% local trade area

items.statement: International SSSG +8.4% YoY; revenue INR 28 cr, +27% YoY
items.quote: Our international business recorded a revenue of around INR 28 crores, representing 27% year-on-year growth, sup ported by a strong Same-Store Sales Growth of 8.4 %.

items.statement: Premium CDR revenue INR 47.3 cr, +17% YoY; SSSG ~5% for quarter

items.statement: Aspiring for double-digit revenue growth for full year FY26

items.statement: Aspiration to achieve 17-18% EBITDA margins driven by premium portfolio growth

items.quote: I would like to highlight the outstanding performance of our premium segment, that is INR 1,500-plus price point, the saliency of which has improved from 45.2% to 57.2% Y-o-Y leading to an improvement in ASP by INR 50 during Quarter 2 FY '26.

items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at INR490 crores, providing strong visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Executed ~15% of INR190 crore power sector order, targeting completion before June 2026
items.quote: we have executed around more than 15% of the same and balance is under process of execution and we target -- internally, the target is to finish it before June 2026

items.statement: Commissioned 1,800 MTPA seamless capacity in November, total seamless capacity now 16,200 MTPA
items.quote: in November, we successfully commissioned 1,800 (mistakenly said as 18,000) MTPA of stainless steel seamless pipes and tube, taking our total seamless capacity to 16,200 metric tons per annum

items.statement: Fitting and seamless capacity additions on track for H2 FY26, fitting capex ~INR60 crores
items.quote: Fitting would be around INR60-odd crores.

items.statement: Expects steady ramp-up in seamless utilization; fitting plant to start in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect a steady ramp -up in utilization level in the coming months. Additionally, the new capacities for fitting and seamless pipe/tubes remain on track and are expected to come on stream in the second half of this fiscal

items.statement: India's capex cycle driving structural demand across power, railway, engineering, semiconductor, defense
items.quote: India's capex cycle continues to remain on an upward trajectory, supported by a strong policy push and sustained investment momentum.

items.statement: Export demand strong from Europe and Middle East; US demand declining due to uncertainty
items.quote: The orders are there from export -- a good number of orders are coming from Europe currently. You're rightly on the site of US, there's a lot of uncertainty, so that is slightly declining at our side.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin at 16.3%; expects margin improvement in FY27 with new capacities
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 16.3% . On H1 FY '26 EBITDA showed a growth of 4%, standing at INR 92.3 crores, margin at 16.3%.

items.statement: Hedges substantial portion of orders to mitigate raw material price impact on margins
items.quote: Probably, as a company, we generally try to hedge it while taking the order to a substantial portion of it. So, on the margin front, we are not much affected with the changes in prices.

items.statement: Exports reached all-time high INR115.6 crores (53% YoY), 40% of revenue; expects 25-30% export share going forward
items.quote: Export continued to be a significant growth engine for us, reaching an all-time high of INR115.6 crores, marking a 53% year -on-year increase.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duties on stainless steel pipes valid until December 2027
items.quote: It has come in December 2022. On stainless steel stainless pipe, and it is there for 5 years, so primarily, it should be ended by December 2027.

items.statement: No significant CBAM impact expected for Europe exports; India not heavily affected vs China
items.quote: In case of Europe, generally on India, there is no such specific tariff currently. On China, the tariff is substantially high -- there is an additional tariff is there on China.

items.statement: Net debt to peak in FY27 as remaining capex draws loans; EBITDA from new projects to follow
items.quote: It will push up because there are capex left because of that; there will be a few loans would be coming in the books. So it will slightly push up from here and so on.

items.statement: Promoter and non-promoter warrants fully subscribed
items.quote: Yes, the entire warrant has been subscribed promoter and non promoter, all.

items.statement: Added new customers in Middle East and India for larger diameter welded pipes
items.quote: It's a mixed bag, see. It's a new geography in Middle East also. Again, in India also, a few new customers have been added. Again, primarily on the bigger size welded pipe, it started deploying.

items.statement: 5-7 bidders typically compete for power sector tenders; high entry barriers via approvals and quality
items.quote: See, there are many products what need to be supplied and each have their own set of buyers, but we believe, more than 5-7 numbers of buyers are there who bid in these type of contracts

items.statement: Volume growth >20% YoY on blended basis in Q2 FY26
items.quote: for the year -on-year quarter, the volume growth is also on a blended basis more than 20%, at-least.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 56.3% seamless, 38.9% welded, 4.8% others; welded grew 48% YoY
items.quote: Revenue bifurcation for the quarter was 38.9% from welded pipes, 56.3% from seamless and 4.8% from others. Growth in Seamless segment was 25% on a year -on-year basis and Welded segment registered a strong growth of 48%

items.statement: Working capital cycle for new fitting/seamless verticals expected similar to current
items.quote: Seems similar to what we are currently operating.

items.statement: US export uncertainty due to tariff clarity; Europe CBAM standards not yet finalized
items.quote: You're rightly on the site of US, there's a lot of uncertainty, so that is slightly declining at our side.

items.statement: Employee costs rising due to new plant commissions; expected to stabilize post FY26
items.quote: currently each quarter, there is a new expansion coming in, a new plant started. That's why those costs are increasing. I think post this year, this should stabilize.

items.statement: Wine Tourism delivered record quarter with 8% growth in Q2 and 15% in H1
items.quote: The biggest bright spot is our Wine Tourism business, which delivered yet another record quarter in Q2, reporting 8% growth in Q2 and 15% growth in H1.

items.statement: Launched third resort The Haven by Sula with 30 keys and convention center in October
items.quote: Our new resort, which I had spoken about in the last earnings call as well, features 30 keys and for the first time, we have a state-of-the-art convention center.

items.statement: Adding 20 more keys in Phase 2 of The Haven by Q4, taking total capacity up nearly 50% to 154 keys
items.quote: I'm also very pleased to announce that we are already in development of Phase 2 of The Haven, and we will be adding another 20 keys in Q4. So overall, by year-end, that takes our room capacity up by nearly 50% to 154 keys versus 104 keys just 6 months back.

items.statement: Maharashtra market showing signs of recovery and growth in Q2 after challenging 12 months
items.quote: Maharashtra, our most important market, after going through a pretty challenging phase over the last 12 months has shown signs of decent recovery coming back to growth in Q2, which bodes very well for H2 as well as the coming years.

items.statement: Own Brands declined marginally in Q2 due to Telangana route-to-market disruption from retail license expiry
items.quote: Own Brands showed a marginal decline in Q2, which was primarily due to the temporary route-to-market disruption in Telangana, which emerged recently as our third largest market.

items.statement: Excluding Telangana, Own Brand sales grew mid-single digits YoY with 8 states delivering double-digit growth
items.quote: Encouragingly, excluding Telangana, our Own Brand sales grew by mid-single digits year-on-year. This was supported by strong double-digit growth across 8 of our states, including Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Pondicherry, among others.

items.statement: CSD segment revenues more than doubled YoY in Q2 benefiting from expanded label listings from 5 to 9
items.quote: Our CSD segment, which we've talked about even in the last earnings call, also saw robust growth with sales more than doubling year-on-year in the second quarter, so more than 100% growth, reflecting the benefits of the expanded label listings from the previous 5 to now 9.

items.statement: Sula gaining market share in overall wine market in H1 despite lower S&D spend than competitors
items.quote: Moving on, we believe that Sula has continued to gain market share in the overall wine market in H1 despite having lower S&D spend than our key competitors as indicated by the early industry data that has come in for some of the key corporation markets.

items.statement: Elite & Premium share stable at 78% in Q2; The Source range clocking double-digit growth and now 10% of own brands revenue
items.quote: Moving on to our portfolio mix. The share of Elite & Premium remained pretty stable at about 78% in Q2. Within this, The Source, as I touched on earlier, continued to be the standout, clocking healthy double-digit growth.

items.statement: The Source brand share expected to double in a couple of years; expanding national footprint with new labels in Haryana and Delhi
items.quote: We fully expect The Source to be our key driver of growth going forward. And we would not be surprised if its share of own brands doubles in a couple of years.

items.statement: Sula Muscat Blanc launched as India's first premium low alcohol wine with positive response; expanding Muscat acreage for FY27 supply
items.quote: Our latest wine launch, the Sula Muscat Blanc is India's first premium low alcohol wine, which has received a very positive response from the market in its first quarter of launch, and this is also showing really good potential for future.

items.statement: Popular portfolio rebounded from degrowth to healthy growth in Q2 led by Samara and Port 1000 after outsourcing Maharashtra distribution
items.quote: Our efforts here can now show clear results with our popular portfolio rebounding well from degrowth and delivering healthy growth in Q2, led by the well-known value-priced brands, Samara and Port 1000.

items.statement: Wine Tourism Q2 occupancy improved 350 bps to 77%; footfalls up 2% to ~78,000 guests; spend per guest up low single digits
items.quote: Average room occupancy improved by 350 basis points year-over-year to 77%, while average room revenue increased by 1%. Visitor footfall rose by 2%, reaching approximately 78,000 guests.

items.statement: Capex for current fiscal and going forward expected to taper to INR30-35 crores annually, nearly half of previous years
items.quote: Importantly, major investments have already been made and capex in current fiscal and going forward is expected to taper down to INR30 crores to INR35 crores, which is nearly half of what we have been doing in the last few financial years.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted ~900 bps YoY due to adverse mix, wine tourism sourcing change, and high-cost inventory carryover; all factors transient
items.quote: Our gross margin contracted by around 900 basis points year-over-year. This contraction was driven by 3 key factors: First and foremost, adverse market and product mix, which I touched base earlier.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined 530 bps YoY primarily due to gross margin impact; operating costs reduced 8% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin declined by 530 basis points year-over-year primarily due to gross margin impact. However, through disciplined cost management, we reduced operating costs by 8% year-on-year, helping to contain the adverse impact on EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Expect 250 bps YoY improvement in operating margins in H2 FY26 driven by higher WIPS accrual, wine tourism traction, and phasing out high-cost inventory
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect to see a year-on-year improvement of 250 basis points in our operating margins in second half of this year. This improvement is expected to be driven by a combination of a higher WIPS accrual, sustained traction in wine tourism and phasing out of high-cost liquid inventory from last year.

items.statement: Net debt INR350 crores at Sep 2025 vs INR315 crores YoY; increase due to lower profitability and higher receivables from slow Telangana collections
items.quote: Net debt at the end of September 2025 stood at around INR350 crores compared to INR315 crores in September last year. The increase in debt is primarily attributable to lower profitability and higher receivables, with receivables expanding due to slow collection from Telangana in quarter 2.

items.statement: Collections normalized starting Q3; debt-to-EBITDA comfortably around 2.5x trailing 12 months; cash from operations post tax positive INR4 crores in H1
items.quote: I'm pleased to report that collections have normalized starting quarter 3, and we expect further improvement going forward. Despite these challenges, our debt-to-EBITDA ratio remains comfortably around 2.5x trailing 12 months EBITDA. And cash generated from operations post tax stood at a positive INR4 crores in H1.

items.statement: WIPS outstanding INR80 crores at Sep 2025 vs INR72 crores at Mar 2025; accrued INR20 crores and received INR13 crores in H1; extra INR11 crores received in Oct bringing outstanding to ~INR70 crores
items.quote: Our outstanding balance at the end of September stood at INR80 crores compared to INR72 crores when we closed March 2025. We accrued WIPS of INR20 crores and received a payout of INR13 crores in H1. Additionally, we received an extra payout of INR11 crores in beginning of quarter 3, which is in October, bringing our current WIPS outstanding to approximately INR70

items.statement: Expect EU FTA to reduce minimum import price likely in line with Australia FTA first phase; vast majority of Own Brands portfolio not impacted
items.quote: With the EU, we do expect that there would be some reduction in the minimum import price likely in-line with the price that was negotiated most recently in the first phase of the Australia FTA. However, we are confident that even given such an outcome, the vast majority of our Own Brands portfolio will not be impacted.

items.statement: Actively exploring expansion of imported wine distribution business as duties and MIP expected to come down; currently distribute 2 global brands
items.quote: Given that duties are expected to come down and the minimum import price is expected to come down, we are now actively exploring to once again step back in and expand our imported wine distribution business.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given for FY27; see immense potential from expanding distribution breadth across states
items.quote: No. So, Nishita, first and foremost, we do not give a revenue guidance per se. But looking at our efforts in terms of expanding the breadth of distribution of wine across the states in the country, we do see that there is immense potential.

items.statement: Capacity utilization just below 60%; ample capacity built for next 2-3 years; Own Brand business fixed asset turnover above 2x
items.quote: Also, Keshav, it's worth noting here that right now our capacity utilization is just below 60%. And so, you're not seeing the full revenue yet coming from the capacities that we have put up.

items.statement: Sustainable ROE of 17-18% achievable once operating leverage returns with demand recovery
items.quote: Once that is back, we do see that the 17% to 18% of ROE, which we were clocking earlier, that is something which is a sustainable one.

items.statement: Telangana disruption expected to recover from December 1 as license auctions conclude and supply transitions to new holders
items.quote: As far as we are aware, this is going to start from December 1 itself. So, we would get a good benefit of that within Q3 itself. Fingers crossed.

items.statement: No further resort expansion planned for FY27; front-loaded Phase 2 of The Haven into FY26; other Wine Tourism expansions planned
items.quote: Right now, we have no further plans for FY '27. In fact, we front loaded a little bit. We sped up our construction of The Haven Phase II, which was supposed to come in '27. We brought it into '26.

items.statement: Battery storage at ~2 MW with recent 0.9 MW installation; battery costs coming down; committed to increasing storage; solar limited by roof space
items.quote: I'm very pleased to say that, yes, we are more or less already at 2 megawatts. So, we installed, I must say, I don't have this right in front of me, but our most recent installation was about 900 kilowatts, so 0.9-megawatt battery was our most recent installation.

items.statement: Maharashtra Q2 shows turnaround beginnings; gaining market share in Premium & Elite despite competitors' higher unsustainable discounts
items.quote: Q2, I do believe, is the beginnings of a turnaround. And yes, we have not been hit with the tax rise. And as such, I'm sure you would be aware that Maharashtra in other segments has faced a decline in excise revenues. Wine, however, in Q2, at least in Sula's case, that is not the case. We have positive news there. And I would also like to say that our market intelligence says that we are gaining m

items.statement: EU FTA likely to come in at lower level than Australia's $5 CIF threshold; cannot give more visibility; leave to government to protect Indian farmers and industry
items.quote: We do believe EU will probably come in at a lower level than $5 but I'm sorry, we can't give you more visibility than that and we leave it into the capable hands of our government and commerce ministry to protect the interests of the Indian farmers and our fledgling industry.

items.statement: Revised full-year FY26 EBITDA growth guidance to 8-12% YoY
items.quote: Looking forward, looking ahead for the full year, we revised our EBITDA growth guidance to 8% to 12% growth Y-o-Y in FY '26.

items.statement: CDMO-CMO on track to exceed earlier 30-40% YoY sales growth target for FY26
items.quote: We are on track to achieve and exceed the earlier estimated sales target which is 30% to 40% growth Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Atali plant inaugurated in September; trial batches started; full operational contribution expected from FY27
items.quote: We inaugurated the Atali plant in September and have started operations. Currently, we are in the process of taking trial batches of a few products for customer qualifications. More products are planned in upcoming months. We expect the facility to be fully operational in two to three quarters, thus contributing meaningfully to the revenue from FY '27.

items.statement: Atali project adds ~440 KL capacity; ~340 KL commercialized; expenses to hit P&L from next quarter
items.quote: Basically, see Atali project has close to 440 KL of capacity which will get added and out of which we have almost commercialized worth of capacity of almost 340 KL.

items.statement: Xanthine capacity expanded from 5,000 to 9,000 MT/annum by end of FY26; currently operating ~500 MT/month
items.quote: Xanthine expansion is ongoing as planned. We are now operating around 500 metric tons per month. The incremental capacity will get operationalized in phases, and we expect to reach 9,000 metric tons per annum installed capacity by end of this financial year.

items.statement: API business saw high margin pressure due to skewed mix toward lower-margin APIs and second-year genericization of prior launches
items.quote: The API business saw high margin pressure. Moreover, the API sales mix in this quarter wa s skewed towards lower margin APIs

items.statement: CDMO business structurally higher margin; overall EBITDA margin depends on mix
items.quote: Yes, CDMO business has structurally higher margins. How it impacts the overall mix is depending on how other mixes are also growing and how much is the percentage of CDMO vis-a-vis the others.

items.statement: CDMO has 21 customers, 59 active projects (39 commercial, 20 development); 7-8 projects moved to commercial recently
items.quote: The number of active projects is now 59, of which 39 projects are in commercial stage and 20 are under different stages of development, both at customer's end.

items.statement: API H2 FY26 expected to normalize and improve over H1; new launches in lifestyle and anti-cancer segments
items.quote: So, we will improve on our first half's performance in second half for the API business.

items.statement: Xanthine pricing has bottomed out and stabilized
items.quote: I think the pricing has bottomed out, basically. And of course, it has not moved from bottom significantly, but it has stabilized.

items.statement: Inventory buildup in H1 due to CDMO preparative manufacturing; expected to normalize as sales booked in H2
items.quote: So, for the CDMO business, the inventory gets built up over a few months because the manufacturing is spread across many months. So, it goes up and then it comes down when the sales is booked.

items.statement: Forex loss of INR 7.4 cr in Q2 from INR 3+ rupee depreciation on USD 24M long-term loans and USD working capital loans; loans kept unhedged as strategic choice
items.quote: On the first question on the Forex loss, it is coming basically, as we all know, because of the sharp depreciation of rupee of almost more than INR 3 in this quarter, 30th September as compared to 30th June. And this is coming basically on the loan that we have foreign currency long-term loans that we have. We have 24 million of long-term loans.

items.statement: Xanthine export share 59%, domestic 41% in Q2
items.quote: In terms of geographical split, the export sales was 59% and the remaining 41% was local sales.

items.statement: API mix: 55% regulated markets, 31% rest of world, 14% non-regulated; Xanthine volume split 71% beverage, 29% others
items.quote: The sub -segment wise breakup is 55% regulated market, 31% rest of the world and 14% non -regulated market.

items.statement: CDMO commercial projects increased to 39 from development stage; 7-8 products moved up recently
items.quote: And we have actually shifted almost seven, eight products there. And which have re sulted in basically launches or approvals which have come in this last couple of quarters

items.statement: API growth challenging due to customer inventory correction and competition on prior launches; recovery depends on new launches
items.quote: But I think growth will be a little bit more challenging, it looks like, because last year's launches, on which we had earlier promises, the customers are a little bit slow with higher inventory.

items.statement: Ganesh Polychem JV: H1 rough due to shutdowns and cost-reduction projects; profitability expected to normalize in H2 and return to ~80-100% of FY25 PAT in FY27
items.quote: Yes, at least it will be near FY '25 level. It will be 80% to 100% of FY '25.

items.statement: Opened Europe CDMO BD office; planning dedicated North America BD hire to expand funnel
items.quote: So, basically, in the CDMO -CMO segment, basically, we have started an office in Europe. So, we have a representative in Europe which is promoting Aarti Pharmalabs' CDMO activity in Europe. And now we plan to put one person exclusively for the CDMO BD in North America.

items.statement: Anti-cancer block debottlenecking planned H2 FY26 / early FY27 to support FY27-28 launches
items.quote: Yes, actually, we are looking at debottlenecking our anti-cancer block as well in the second half of the, you know, later part of this year, early next year, which will be enabling us to further look at meeting the targets of these launches.

items.statement: H2 FY26 EBITDA target ~INR 300 cr implied by 8-12% full-year guidance after Atali costs
items.quote: Yes, Dhwanil. That is what we are basically targeting. An d we are working hard to achieve it

items.statement: Long-term 15-20% EBITDA growth target disavowed; PAT/PBT growth more realistic
items.quote: No, no, 15% to 20% EBITDA growth is quite steep. I think that is the number that we have not stated. Overall, I think, profit growth, PAT growth or PBT growth, we can target a good number.

items.statement: Q2 standalone revenue INR 417 cr (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR 75 cr, PAT INR 31 cr (incl. INR 7.4 cr forex loss)
items.quote: The top line for the quarter was INR 417 crores, which was INR 377 crores a year back, which is an increase of 11% EBITDA stood at INR 75 crores as compared to INR 85 crores in the corresponding period of the previous year. The profit after tax for Q2 FY '26 was INR 31 crores as compared to INR 48 crores a year back. In this quarter, PAT had an impact of Forex loss of around INR 7.4 crores.

items.statement: Q2 consolidated revenue INR 418 cr, EBITDA INR 75 cr, PAT INR 28 cr
items.quote: The top line stood at INR 418 crores as against INR 458 crores in Q2 of FY '25. The EBITDA for the quarter, that is Quarter 2 FY '26 stood at INR 75 crores as compared to INR 94 crores in Q2 of last year. The profit after tax for the quarter was INR 28 crores as compared to INR 55 crores a year back.

items.statement: CDMO priority over intermediate manufacturing; fungible plants used for both; qualifying outside suppliers for intermediates to free capacity
items.quote: Yes, Prakashji, you know, the CDMO sales always ge t first priority. And then we look at the intermediate manufacturing. See, the API manufacturing has dedicated manufacturing blocks and that is where we continuously do the production. It is just a question of intermediate manufacturing, how it shifts, bas ically, because we are backward integrated in our intermediates that we manufacture for our

items.statement: API generic launches face intense competition in first two years; market share and inventory swings cause volatility
items.quote: So, first two years of the launch are volatile. After several years, we had this kind of a mega launch of few products which saw this kind of up-down.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth guidance of 75-85% YoY for FY26
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we will grow our revenues year-on-year between 75% to 85%. So, on a full year basis, our revenues on a standalone basis should be 75% to 85% over last year.

items.statement: Target 15% closure of $45 million qualified pipeline within FY26
items.quote: we target to do 15% closure of the $45 million pipeline tha t we spoke about within this year

items.statement: PSBXchange pipeline target of Rs 3,000-3,500 crores in transactions/approvals by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect to have between Rs. 3,000 crores to Rs. 3,500 crores worth of transactions or approvals on the pipeline by the end of the year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 25% for FY27
items.quote: At a consolidated level we can expect a EBITDA margin of 25%.

items.statement: Long-term blended EBITDA margin target of 30-35% over next 3-4 years
items.period: next three years, three to four years
items.quote: On a steady state basis, which we will hit, you should be expecting a 50% EBITDA margin on the product side of the business. So, when you add the product margins and the service margins on a blended basis, you should be looking at a 30%, 35% on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Qualified pipeline of $45 million (Rs 400 crore) across 85 deals in 24 countries
items.quote: We have close to $45 million or close to Rs. 400 crore worth of pipelines. And this is qualified pipelines. Qualified pipelines across 85 deals in 24 countries.

items.statement: Supply chain finance now less than 50% of pipeline; trade, cash, corporate/retail internet banking 30%+; lending 20%
items.quote: From product pipeline perspective, till last year, bulk, or I would say 90% of our business, our pipeline used to be only supply chain financing. But this year you will see our supply chain finance has come now to less than 50% in terms of pipeline. A very large 30% plus pipeline now is trade, cash, corporate internet banking, retail internet banking.

items.statement: Geographic pipeline mix: 40% India, over 50% across Africa, Asia, MENA; Europe and Americas next frontiers
items.quote: Geographic mix also, you will see India continues to be strong in India. 40% is India. But we are now hedging ourselves and we have a large part, over 50% of our pipeline now is across the world. Across Africa, Asia, and MENA.

items.statement: Supply chain finance business at 54% EBITDA margin (steady state 50%+); standalone profitable post-capitalization, loss-making pre-capitalization
items.quote: The first thing that you will see is that our core of Veefin is our supply chain finance business, and that core is working extremely well. We are showing 54% EBITDA profitability in the supply chain finance business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 18% in H1 FY26 (before NCI PAT margin 7%, post NCI 6.5%)
items.quote: Our consolidated PAT margin before NCI is 7% and post NCI is 6.5% and our EBITDA margins are 18% on console.

items.statement: Heavy IP investment in 6 enterprise products simultaneously on Veefin 4.0 shared architecture; capitalized per IGAP/AS26, amortized over 10 years
items.quote: We have now embarked on a journey of building six enterprise-grade products simultaneously. And all of this are being built on the Veefin's 4.0 shared architecture.

items.statement: IP investments to remain heavy for next year then taper down
items.quote: Some IP investments will continue being heavy for the next year and then they start tapering down.

items.statement: DSO improving: standalone from 149 to 130 days YoY; consolidated from 138 to 105 days YoY
items.quote: On an annual basis, our DSOs are improving year-on-year. So, from the year before, from our 149 days, we have now come down to 130 days, our DSOs. Okay. And this is not just on a standalone basis, even on a console basis, our DSOs are improving. Last year, we had 138 and we have come down to 105.

items.statement: Preferential round of Rs 94.32 crore raised; BSE approval pending, expected in few days
items.quote: We have also raised a preferential round. BSE approval is pending. Should be coming in the next few days, we are assuming. For Rs. 94.32 crore, this sets us up very well for fueling our continued IP investments as we speak.

items.statement: No IPO funds used for acquisitions; acquisitions funded via subsidiary-level capital raises
items.quote: We have not used any IPO funds till date on acquiring any companies. So, all the acquisitions which have happened, they have happened through raising that we had done in the subsidiary.

items.statement: Voluntary attrition next to nil; 600 product-side employees, 900 services-side, 35-40 sales people on product side
items.quote: We have our attrition levels on the voluntary side are next to nil. We will come to more on this later.

items.statement: Restructuring manpower for efficiency; delivering same work with fewer people
items.quote: We are looking at our manpower very closely. Then we are seeing opportunities of enhancing our productivity. We are letting go. We are restructuring our people. We are making do with lesser manpower to deliver the same work which we have been doing.

items.statement: Transitioning from single-product (supply chain finance) to multi-product platform; 6 new enterprise products on shared 4.0 architecture
items.quote: We are very clearly transitioning and we are in the throes of this transition from a single segment product company into a multi-product platform.

items.statement: 30+ banks across 15 countries using supply chain finance; 70% recurring SaaS revenue; strong cross-sell traction with existing and new larger customers
items.quote: Thirty plus banks are using this across 15 countries. We are talking now only of supply chain financing. Thirty plus banks are using this. Our renewal rates are high. Most of these are SAAS products. 70% of our revenues just from supply chain finance are recurring.

items.statement: New customers in new product lines much larger in size than existing customers
items.quote: Our pipeline, which you see, there is a fair mix of the pipeline between existing customers and new customers. And the new customers are much larger in size. Much, much larger.

items.statement: Only company globally with entire transaction banking/working capital suite on single micro-services chassis; zero legacy advantage vs incumbents (Temenos, FIS, Fiserv, Finastra, Intellect)
items.quote: we are the only company globally, mind you, we are the only company globally with t he entire transition banking, working capital products on one single chassis. All with micro-service architecture

items.statement: SaaS pricing model shifting to annual recurring/pay-as-you-grow across all products; moving away from upfront licenses + AMC
items.quote: The pricing model that we have is all around SaaS based pricing, recurring pricing. It could be pricing based on transaction. It could be pricing based on AEM. But what we a re seeing a lot now is annual recurring. So, the market also is moving away from the old school of upfront, big licenses, and then AEM fees

items.statement: PSBXchange revenue model: ~45 bps blended (10 bps sourcing + 20 bps tech usage + 15 bps onboarding) on transaction volume
items.quote: The revenues that we generate from them, net revenues will be 10 b ips on the sourcing. There will be a net 20 b ips on the technology usage with some of the banks, the PSBs and the non- PSBs will use. And the 15 basis points on the onboarding. So, in effect, close to 45 basis points is what one can look at earning from these

items.statement: Run rate of $40 billion annual disbursements on Veefin platform
items.quote: And we had last year, or last six months, the numbers that we have seen, our run rate is $40 billion worth of annual disbursements.

items.statement: Enterprise sales have high acquisition cost, long sales cycles; success depends on ability to speak bankers' language and land-and-expand strategy
items.quote: First thing to remember, high cost of acquisition, a very long sales cycle. People get bored, people get scared and they leave this business. It takes time, it takes patience and one big differentiator, going back to the leadership team, going back to our sales team that we have, is the ability to talk the language of the bankers.

items.statement: Quarterly reporting to start from December 2025; eligible for main board migration by July 2026
items.quote: From December onward, we start showing our quarterly results and start doing that. Because as you know, next year by July' 26, we'll be eligible to move to the main board.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at around Rs 700 crore
items.quote: It'll be around 700 only

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%
items.quote: I am giving about 15% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11-12% for FY26
items.quote: The guidance given to the recycling plant is the same, 11-12%.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected between Rs 15-20 crore
items.quote: The capex will be between 15 to 20 crs in the next year. Not more than that.

items.statement: Production capacity increased 22% to 75,754 metric tons per annum as of Q2 FY26

items.statement: Q2 FY26 capacity utilization at 66%, lower due to Wada plant ramp-up
items.quote: Reflecting sustained growth momentum, capacity utilization for the quarter stood at 66%.

items.statement: H2 FY26 capacity utilization expected at 80%

items.statement: H2 FY26 exit utilization expected between 68-70%
items.quote: It is between 68 and 70.

items.statement: Recycling plant expected to reduce raw material costs by 10-12% annually
items.quote: The recycling plant is expected to reduce raw material costs by 10 to 12% annually, further boosting our margins.

items.statement: Solar plant to save Rs 15 crore annually in power costs with 4-year payback
items.quote: 15 crore is yearly saving.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 solar savings estimated at Rs 3-3.5 crore
items.quote: Almost 3-3.5 cr will be saved.

items.statement: MS drum automation expected to expand EBITDA margin by 800-900 bps as volumes scale
items.quote: Page no. 19. Yes, it is correct sir.

items.statement: Demand is good; whatever is produced is being sold
items.quote: The demand is good sir, whatever is being made is going.

items.statement: Export demand to US reviving after a 1-2 month pause
items.quote: Yes, that is also reviving. We are giving it to the US as well, it didn't go for a month or two, now that is also going.

items.statement: New product line planned in industrial packaging, announcement expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: It is in industrial packaging.

items.statement: Receivables cycle around 90 days; collections average 75 days
items.quote: It stays for around 90 days. In 62-63 days, if we add the total amount, it returns in 75 days.

items.statement: Long-term debt repayment on 5-year tenure to start next quarter
items.quote: We have taken it on a tenure of 5 years. And the repayment will start from the next quarter.

items.statement: Recycling plant commissioned Oct 3 with 5,000 MT capacity meeting 10-12% of raw material needs
items.quote: We have set up a new recycling unit. This area is around 4,400 square meters of land in Bharuch with an investment of around 10 crore. The 5,000 metric ton annual capacity will meet our 10 to 12% of raw material requirement.

items.statement: Solar plant 6 MW commissioned Oct 30; full 15 MW expected by month-end
items.quote: By this month end it should get done. Because we have already started with 6 MW. So the balance will be done by month end.

items.statement: IBC volume grew 42% YoY in Q2; 10% growth despite tariff headwinds
items.quote: IBC massive volume growth of 42% and 30% revenue growth year on year.

items.statement: No discounts given; MS drum price increases expected to reflect next quarter
items.quote: No, no, there is no discount. The goods are sold according to the market rate but there is no discount.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue Rs 325 crore, up 22% YoY
items.quote: The revenue stood at 161 crore, up by 21% year-on-year for the quarter and 22% half-year to 325 crore

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA Rs 27 crore; full-year EBITDA target Rs 70 crore maintained
items.quote: I'm telling you that in today's date, it's more than 70 crores.

items.statement: Tariff issues normalizing; chemical companies negotiating with US buyers

items.statement: FY26 guidance: presales INR125 billion, revenue recognition INR48 billion, launches INR170 billion, collections INR60 billion
items.quote: we are very much confident to achieve our FY '26 guidance, which includes presales of INR125 billion, revenue recognition of INR48 billion and steady growth across other key operating metrics.

items.statement: Reiterated FY26 guidance: launches INR170 billion, sales INR125 billion, collections INR60 billion, revenue recognition INR48 billion
items.quote: we stand firm on our guidance on launches of INR170 billion on sales of INR125 billion on collection of INR60 billion and revenue recognition of INR48 billion for this financial year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 presales INR46.6 billion (37% of FY26 guidance), sold 3 million sq ft at INR15,700/sq ft, 1,338 units at avg INR3.5 cr/unit
items.quote: during the first year, we've achieved about INR46.6 billion of sales, which is a little short of 40% of our annual guidance of about INR125 billion

items.statement: H1 FY26 collections INR18.6 billion; 47% to construction, 25-27% to SG&A/brokerage/taxes, balance to land/approvals
items.quote: We've achieved total collections of about INR18.6 billion for the first half of the year.

items.statement: Launched 2.45 million sq ft worth INR43 billion in H1 FY26; planning ~8 million sq ft launches in H2 FY26 with GDV INR13,000-14,000 crore
items.quote: during the second half of the year, we are planning launches almost close to 8 million square foot which will be in 2 of our 3 key markets

items.statement: Cumulative launches since Feb-Mar '24: 17+ million sq ft, GDV >INR234 billion, >80% sold, unsold inventory ~INR50 billion
items.quote: We launched close to 17-plus million square foot since February, March '24 until about September '25, which has a GDV potential in excess of INR234 billion.

items.statement: Forthcoming launch pipeline: 24 million sq ft land-based inventory, GDV >INR420 billion; total launched + forthcoming ~41-42 million sq ft, GDV >INR650 billion
items.quote: cumulatively, there's almost like 24 million square foot of development potential of land-based inventory, which we are sitting on. Now this forthcoming launch inventory has a GDV potential in excess of INR420 billion.

items.statement: H1 FY26 GP margin 29% vs 23% YoY; EBITDA margin dipped due to lower revenue recognition, expected to recover in H2
items.quote: Our GP margin stood at about 29%, which is much higher than the previous half -- previous financial year's first half. The EBITDA margin dipped because of lower-than-anticipated quantum of revenue recognition

items.statement: GP margin improvement driven by higher proportion of low-rise floors vs affordable housing; only 5-6 affordable projects left to deliver
items.quote: The portion of middle-income home completion is getting higher. And hence, the GP margin is improving. So if we do a like-to-like comparison with the previous year, our GP margin has gone up to 29% versus 23%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 construction spend INR940 crore; H2 FY26 expected INR1,000-1,100 crore; full year ~INR2,000-2,050 crore
items.quote: We spent about INR900-plus crores during the first 6 months, INR940-odd crores during the first 6 months on construction. I think that number should be between INR1,000 crores and INR1,100 crores for the second half of the year.

items.statement: Delivered ~16 million sq ft; ~9 million sq ft near completion (similar to last quarter); heavy rains in Q1 impacted construction momentum
items.quote: On the overall portfolio level where we stand as of today, we've delivered close to 16 million square foot. There's another 9 million square for which is getting close to delivery

items.statement: Sector 71 portfolio sales potential revised up to 18.5 million sq ft from 17 million sq ft due to refined planning (no new land added)
items.quote: our estimate as of today stands at about 18.5 million. So almost 1.5 million square foot of additional planned area, something which we are envisaging out of the Sector 71 portfolio

items.statement: New launches in Sector 37D and Sector 71 with smaller unit sizes (~1,800 sq ft vs earlier 2,200-2,300 sq ft) to keep ticket sizes attractive
items.quote: We are now launching projects with starting apartment sizes about 1,800-odd square foot. we've tried to ensure that the ticket size remains attractive, and it's affordable for the end user to participate in these launches.

items.statement: H1 FY26 sales across all key micro-markets: 500+ units in Sohna, 450+ in SPR Sector 71, 300+ in Dwarka Expressway (Sectors 37D & 84)
items.quote: roughly, 500-plus units got sold in the Sohna region, about 450-odd units were sold in the Southern Peripheral Road Sector 71 micro market. And about 300-plus units were -- 300-plus units was sold in the Dwarka Expressway market

items.statement: Net debt ~INR9.7 billion; target to reach zero net debt in 12-15 months; raised INR8.75 billion NCDs from IFC (A+ stable rating by CARE)
items.quote: There's a net debt, which is quite modest, which is, by and large, range bound, but yes, less than INR10 billion, so about INR9.7 billion of debt is something which is still in the company.

items.statement: Raised INR8.75 billion (~$100 million) via private placement of NCDs to IFC (World Bank arm); first listed debt transaction for company
items.quote: we recently raised INR8.75 billion, which is almost $100 million through the private placement of nonconvertible debenture to the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank lending arm

items.statement: H2 FY26 collections expected: INR4,000-4,500 crore from ongoing/recent projects, INR1,500 crore from new launches; total FY26 target INR6,000 crore
items.quote: ongoing and recently launch will give us numbers anywhere between INR4,000 crores to INR4,500-odd crores whereas INR1,500 crores will come out of the new -- the launches for the year

items.statement: Revenue recognition H1 FY26: INR12 billion; full year guidance INR48 billion
items.quote: during the first half, we've done a recognition of about INR12 billion

items.statement: No geographic expansion plans currently; focused on NCR key markets (40 million population); will update if new market entry considered
items.quote: No plans as of now. So we wish best of luck to everyone who is entering new markets, whether it's people from NCR going to the Mumbai market or other players coming to the Gurgaon market

items.statement: Onboarded Bain & Company to improve construction efficiency; target to complete INR10,000 crore inventory over next 18-20 months
items.quote: We've also now onboarded Bain & Company, which will further help us in improving construction-related efficiency across various projects which are nearing completion.

items.statement: Onboarded quality contractors: Ahluwalia Contracts, Capacit'e, Arabian Construction Company; now added Bain & Company for efficiency
items.quote: we've been working with good quality contractor, we've onboarded contractors like Ahluwalia Contracts, Capacit'e, Arabian Construction Company. But just as an additional layer of efficiency improvement. We've also now onboarded Bain & Company

items.statement: Among few large supply creators in Sector 71; confident on sales offtake; Dwarka Expressway infrastructure supports demand
items.quote: we are amongst few large supply creators in the Sector 71 market. And hence, we are very positive as far as the sales offtake is concerned.

items.statement: Delhi-NCR residential market strong: 62,000 units (INR1,530 bn) in 2024; 26,795 units (INR934 bn) in H1 '25; Gurugram micro-markets seeing price appreciation 98-151% over 5-6 years
items.quote: Delhi-NCR residential market remained strong recording sales of about 62,000 units worth INR1,530 billion in 2024 and around 26,795 units of worth INR934 billion in the H1 '25.

items.statement: Management maintains FY26 revenue guidance of INR 700 crores and PAT guidance of INR 45 crores, declining to revise despite H1 PAT of INR 26 crores
items.quote: Let us not revise it. Let us understand Quarter 3, how is it rolling out? It is pretty good, actually, in terms of retail , it is going very strong. So, let us hold on to the next quarter until any other revisions.

items.statement: Retail demand strong in Q3 with ticket size upgradation despite high gold prices; B2B volumes flat YTD but Q2 volumes grew 20% YoY to 380 kg
items.quote: We are witnessing encouraging demand trends and expecting robust consumer traction during the upcoming wedding season in retail, particularly led by strong interest in occasion wear category.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded 766 bps YoY to 19.5% driven by job work share rising to 65% of sales mix; margins fluctuate quarterly based on job work proportion
items.quote: Margins are clearly dictated by the rise in job work volume. So, right now in my sales mix, if you check Quarter 2, 65% is job work.

items.statement: Q2 B2B volumes (wholesale + job work) reached 300 kg vs 220 kg YoY; Q3 job work expected muted due to early season, retail momentum strong
items.quote: So, if you see the volume data, you can see that the customer preference can change. We are not sure that in Quarter 2, we expected the wholesale to actually grow very strongly.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity scales with gold price; 10 karigars now represent INR 125 crores capability vs INR 50 crores at lower gold prices; integrated manufacturing supports retail margins
items.quote: Now, that same 10 Karigarswill not produce less because the gold prices has gone up. They will produce the same amount. Right now, my manufacturing capability would be INR 125 crores.

items.statement: Making charges increased slightly in H1 to test price sensitivity, then readjusted; occasion wear dominates 22 carat, daily wear shifting to 18 carat
items.quote: We took a little bit on, we lifted the making charge a little bit up. We checked the consumer response. The consumer response was good in terms of revenue, but they were still hesitant.

items.statement: Experimenting with 18 carat occasion wear inventory; occasion wear remains 22 carat dominated, daily wear seeing strong 18 carat preference
items.quote: we are experimenting in 18 carats. We are building up inve ntory in occasion where also 18 carat, that is new for us also. But we are certainly seeing the demand coming up

items.statement: B2B customer base expanding through exhibitions, new designs, caratage experimentation; preferred supplier to corporates; job work volumes surged 53% YoY to 249 kg in Q2
items.quote: Continuous practice of exhibitions will be there, launching of new designs will be there, understanding market dynamics, experimenting in different caratage, like 18 carats and all will help us in actually penetrating the market more.

items.statement: CC limits at 9% interest; not using Gold Metal Loans (3%) due to margin requirements and cash reserve constraints; evaluating GML/hedging gradually for future
items.quote: CC, we are paying, let us say, 9%. On the GML, we could have got it by 3%. But I think that is a decision to take, whether we go on GML or on the gold buying.

items.statement: Volume growth key KPI: Q2 volumes up 20% YoY to 380 kg despite 50% gold price rise; H1 volumes flat YoY at 542 kg; management suggests evaluating performance via volume x weighted average gold price
items.quote: The strongest progress that you can see is that we have not lost on volumes in the first half of the season. And in the Quarter 2, we have grown the volumes to 380 kg from 317 kg.

items.statement: Cautious on revenue trends due to global precious metal price volatility; geopolitical tensions noted; book value of gold protects against downside risk
items.quote: However, while the overall demand remains positive, we are also cautious on the revenue trends given the recent volatility in global precious metal prices.

items.statement: Management emphasizes systematic retail operations (no bargain system, policy-driven); 11-year-old store grew from INR 24 crores to INR 323 crores retail revenue
items.quote: We are purely running this retail store on the basis of right marketing that we are doing. You can check our Instagram page, Harit Zaveri Jewel lers. You will understand

items.statement: Confident competing with established players (Indriya etc.) in Surat/Rajkot due to demographic alignment, merchandise strength, and proven Ahmedabad execution
items.quote: Will it hamper us? They are already there in Ahmedabad also. Why it has not hampe red us? We are still growing in Ahmedabad fairly well

items.statement: Marketing spend 2-3% of sales for new stores, 0.75-1% for mature stores; Surat store maturity target INR 500 crores, Rajkot INR 400 crores by year 4-5
items.quote: Generally the marketing budget would be in the new store expansion, it will be somewhere around 2%-3%. On the maturity of the store, it will be generally from 0.75%-1%.

items.statement: Management targets 10,000 machine deliveries in FY27 with 8,500-9,000 as realistic range
items.quote: Next year, we have already committed to our customers to close to 10,000 machines.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 6,000 to 16,000 machines per annum by September 2026
items.quote: We are scaling our production capacity from 6,000 machines per annum to 16,000 machines per annum by September '2026.

items.statement: Huron capacity doubled from €30-32M to €70-75M top line capability
items.quote: And now with this capacity expansion, we have reached out to close to €70 million to €75 million top line we are able to execute it over there based on the model mix there.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 4,546 crores, well-diversified across sectors
items.quote: It remains healthy and well-diversified at Rs. 4,546 crores, reflecting steady demand and continued customer confidence.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 order intake of Rs. 619 crores with 44% from aerospace and defense
items.quote: Our order intake for Q2 FY '26 stood at Rs. 619 crores. This includes 44% from aerospace and defense, means Rs. 272 crores.

items.statement: Strong demand from Indian defense (Rs. 180 crores in H1) and European defense customers
items.quote: In these two quarters, and particularly in the last quarter, we have received close to Rs. 180 crores worth of orders only from the Indian defense area there.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin at 24.5%, in line with near-term guidance despite higher employee costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 24.5%, which is broadly in line with our last year, primarily due to the increase in employee expenses and other expenses, but still it is in line with our near-to-guidance over there.

items.statement: HUMA controller development expected to add 4-5% gross margin once fully integrated
items.quote: And we are expecting gross margin to be increased close to a 4% to 5% over there.

items.statement: Total planned capex of Rs. 450 crores, 75-80% to be spent in FY26, balance in H1 FY27
items.quote: So, CapEx, what we have planned for a total Rs. 450 crores. And I think largely we will finish, let's say, 3-4% we will finish this year itself.

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned positive in H1 (Rs. 50+ crores vs -Rs. 100+ crores last year), meaningful improvement expected in H2
items.quote: In last year, let's say it was minus Rs. 100 crores, 100 plus. So, this first half, we have crossed Rs. 50 crores. Incrementally, it will be more than this basically.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue increased due to large 5-axis machines with long cycles and milestone billing
items.quote: So, you see that this quarter, the numbers of 9 machines and 164, these are the very large machines. It is partially built up like that.

items.statement: Q2 revenue mix: 36% aerospace/defense, 26% auto, 21% general engineering, 17% others
items.quote: In terms of revenue contribution across the industries in Quarter 2: 36% came from aerospace and defense, 26% from auto and auto components, 21% from general engineering, and the remaining 17% from the other areas.

items.statement: Machine sales breakdown: 1,237 entry-level (Rs. 252 cr), 69 mid-level (Rs. 69 cr), 9 high-value (Rs. 164 cr)
items.quote: So, value-wise, Rs. 252 crore. Machine-wise, 1,237 machines. It is an entry-level product. Mid-level is close to 69. And at 69, number of machines also close to 69. Average value is Rs. 1 crore. A high value is 164 machines with the machine is 9, and average machine is Rs. 18.26 crore.

items.statement: 30% of procurement still imported (CNC controllers, drives, motors, precision bearings, sensors)
items.quote: Still, in our total purchase, we have close to 30% is imports. Particularly, there is still, let's say, the CNC controllers, drives, motors, specific bearing elements.

items.statement: 80-90% of hiring for expanded capacity already completed, salary arrears paid in Q2 caused cost spike
items.quote: Almost 80% to 90% people are already on the roll there now.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 88% in Q2, targeting 90-100%+ in H2 FY26
items.quote: The capacity utilization for Q2 FY '26 was 88%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue grew 15.8% to Rs. 918 crores, Q2 grew 17.9% to Rs. 508 crores
items.quote: Our performance for this first half of the year was also strong, with consolidated revenue of Rs. 918 crores in H1 FY '26 compared to Rs. 792 crores in H1 FY '25, reflecting a growth of 15.8%.

items.statement: Applying under PLI scheme for controller, drive, and motor development
items.quote: We are under the PLI scheme. We are also going to be applying for that.

items.statement: European customers primarily defense-focused (French companies), Indian defense orders from ordnance factories
items.quote: But largely in Europe right now, all the French companies and everyone, those of our customers are mainly on the defence side there.

items.statement: Delivery timeline for complex machines exceeds 2 years, capacity constraints limit near-term growth
items.quote: Right now, we are tied up and we are not able to give the delivery for this kind of a special machine less than two years like that.

items.statement: Tumakuru land acquisition for demo centers, warehouses, service support - not for large capacity expansion
items.quote: We are not looking to be any furthermore large capacity expansion over there, but rather we are going near to the customers to have some small assemblies and to have some fixturing, some solutions, and R&D activity near to my customers over there basically.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment development underway, targeting commercialization within 2 years
items.quote: We are designing and developing one or two products right now. It is a very high precision zone for all of us. This is the first time it is happening in India also. So, we are learning and we are expecting within two years it should be commercialized over there.

items.statement: Targeting 40%+ corporate EBITDA margins in H2 FY26
items.quote: we should start trending towards the normal 40% EBITDA margins that we set out as a target going forward. So, I think we are expecting the second half to be very, very strong, and we should start trending towards 40% plus margins as we go forward.

items.statement: Domestic travel, corporate mobility, and forward bookings for festive and wedding seasons are healthy
items.quote: Domestic travel continues to anchor performance. Corporate mobility is steadily expanding, and forward bookings are for the festive season and wedding season are looking very healthy.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 36% from 30% YoY driven by ARR growth, green energy savings, and lease rental flowthroughs
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income for the second quarter came in at INR82.6 crores, representing a 28% year -on-year growth and a margin of 36% in the current quarter compared to 30% in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Capex of INR1,800-1,900 crores between now and FY28-29, majority from FY27 onwards, funded by mix of project debt and equity
items.quote: The capex requirement to deliver this key count remains at around INR1,800 crores to INR1,900 crores between now and FY '28 and '29. And that would come through a mix of debt and prudent project level debt.

items.statement: Green energy share increased from 25% to 29% of total units consumed, driving HLP cost savings
items.quote: Key drivers for this expansion are a, ARR growth. Second is HLP cost savings due to the rising share of green energy as part of our overall units consumed. The green energy share has grown from 25% to 29%.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai shifting mix toward higher-ARR transient and group business away from low-ARR airline contracts
items.quote: In Mumbai, we've kind of invested the money into Grand Hyatt upgrade because we wanted to look at specific strategy of capturing more transient in group business, which are normally at a higher end of the ARR than the traditional contract of the airline business, which are at the lowest end of the ARR.

items.statement: Showroom revenue INR8 crores in H1 FY26, expected to more than double in H2; classified under F&B
items.quote: We are at around INR8 crores incremental. That's where we are right now for Showroom. We anticipate as we get into the second half, we would more than double that in the second half given the business on hand.

items.statement: Central government sanctioned INR44,859 crores for Northeast infrastructure; 978 industrial units registered; 5,000+ km road projects; 10 Greenfield airports in 11 years
items.quote: Projects worth INR44,859 crores have been sanctioned in the region, and 978 industrial units have been registered in Northeast Special Infrastructure Development scheme. With over 5,000 kilometres of road projects undergoing now and 10 Greenfield airports being built in the last 11 years.

items.statement: INR7 crores notional forex provision on ECBs in Q2; natural hedge via forex earnings; evaluating rolling hedging strategy
items.quote: in the quarter gone by, we've taken a INR7 crores delta. It's a notional provision as part of the finance cost, and that's one of the reasons that you would see that in the results. We have a natural hedge. We have forex earnings as well. And this is primarily on account of ECBs, which had come in over the past years from promoters, and that is what has been taken as a provision. We are looking at

items.statement: Employee cost stable at 20.6% of operating revenue; headcount added for F&B enhancement (chefs, showroom staff) not Bangalore pre-opening
items.quote: But if you were to again look at just as a percentage of the total kind of operating revenue, my employee cost has remained stable at around 20.6% for the quarter as a percentage of operating revenue only. So, on a quarter -on-quarter, Y-o-Y basis, sorry, there has been no increase in the manpower cost as a percentage. But in the absolute term, my manpower that I've taken in is for improved produc

items.statement: Service apartment revenue dipped 5% sequentially due to high base effect from Mumbai room refurb last year; engaging corporates to improve occupancy
items.quote: And that is also because of a high base effect last year where when the rooms were under refurb, we kind of reallocated some of the demand for the rooms into the apartments. And that's pushed the occupancy for apartments artificially up. So, it's a stronger, larger base that you're looking at. And I think we are now engaging with -- as we speak, the team is engaging with corporates to get in more

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue guidance INR 1,100-1,200 crores with EBITDA margin 18-20% and PAT margin 10-12%
items.quote: Looking ahead to financial year 2026, we are confident of achieving revenues in the range of INR900 to INR1,000 crores, with EBITDA margin firmly in higher double-digit zone.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR 2,000-2,200 crores with margins maintained at FY26 levels
items.quote: 2027 will be -- we have given, I think, sub stands at 2000 to 2200. I may be a little bit here or there, but I think it's 2000 to 2200 for FY2026-2027.

items.statement: Order book INR 1,552 crores as of September 2025; H1 FY26 order inflow INR 174 crores; pipeline INR 3,668 crores
items.quote: As of September 2025, the company's order book stood at INR1,552 crores, comprising INR999 crores worth of orders from roads and bridges, INR142 crores from tunnels, and INR. 411 crores worth of projects from slopes.

items.statement: Current order book INR 1,635 crores; expect INR 700 crores more by mid-January reaching INR 2,400-2,500 crores
items.quote: Yes. This time, right now, order book is INR1,635 crores. As of today, we are just speaking. So, by December, we are expecting to grow by something like -- December or 15th January, we are expecting another INR700 crores projects.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.49%, PAT margin 10.15%; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.48%, PAT margin 19.71%
