items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 18-20% and PAT margin 10-12%
items.quote: Yes, Yes, it will be 18%-20% and the PAT will be around same 10% --12%.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan INR 70 crores, of which INR 48 crores already spent in H1
items.quote: We further plan to incur a capex of INR70 crores in financial year 20, out of which INR48 crores of capex is already done in first half of financial year 2026.

items.statement: HAM project equity requirement 15-20% of project cost; INR 70 crores for INR 500 crore project
items.quote: Yes, definitely. We have to put something around 15% to 20% of the total cost of the project as a promoter in the HAM project. So we are bidding for INR500 crores projects, I did almost INR70 crores for that particular one project only.

items.statement: Planning QIP of around INR 110 crores for domestic projects
items.quote: It will be around INR110 crores, I think.

items.statement: Acquired 51% stake in Maccaferri Infrastructure Private Limited (MIPL) in Q1 FY26; full consolidation from Q3
items.quote: To further strengthen our capabilities in this niche, we acquired a 51% stake in Maccaferri Infrastructure Private Limited, a subsidiary of Officine Maccaferri S.p.A Italy, enhancing our expertise in geotechnical and environmental engineering solutions.

items.statement: MIPL revenue FY25 INR 155 crores; FY26 target INR 350-450 crores; full consolidation from Q3
items.quote: For Maccaferri, this year we will be achieving a number of INR350 crores, roughly. Management: 350 to 450 range.

items.statement: SRM order mix ~60-65% roads, ~30% slopes; MIPL 100% slopes; combined ~52% roads, ~48% slopes
items.quote: So, road will be now almost 60 to 65%. And slope will be another 30% because in tunnel, we are doing only one single project as of now. So, if they come to MIPL, then 100% is slope. So combined, it will be something like 52% road and 48% slope or 53% road and 43%, something like that.

items.statement: Working with NHAI, MSRDC, MSIDC in Maharashtra; BRO in Northeast; 60-day receivables cycle
items.quote: We have a 60-day cycle almost. So whatever work we do, 30 days we do work, then we make our bid and everything. So we are investing in only those projects which have ready cash available.

items.statement: Unutilized bank guarantee limit INR 76 crores out of INR 225 crores sanctioned; additional INR 75 crores enhancement sanctioned
items.quote: The unutilized limit as of date is INR76 crores out of the total sanction limit of INR225 crores. Additionally, INR75 crores of enhancement already being sanctioned by the bank from Bank of Baroda and Yes Bank.

items.statement: Using insurance bonds instead of bank guarantees; cost equivalent to BG commission but no collateral required
items.quote: Since our credit rating is A minus, we are getting a lot of insurance bonds. And most of the organizations are accepting insurance bonds in lieu of BGs. So, that problem is, we are not facing any such problems.

items.statement: International expansion via Abu Dhabi branch targeting GCC and Africa; bid submitted in Uganda; no revenue included in FY27 guidance
items.quote: This INR2,000 crores, I have not taken any international exposure so far. Chirag Shah: Okay. Sanjay Mehta: Because we have this -- yes. We have to already quoted, but we have not held one so

items.statement: Collaborating with Maccaferri International for projects in Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh
items.quote: We are collaborating with certain agencies in Saudi. We are collaborating in Sri Lanka. We are collaborating in Bangladesh and finalizing few projects with the help of Maccaferri International and SRM will be executing those projects.

items.statement: Puneet Pal Singh appointed Managing Director for India expansion; Sanjay Mehta moved to Non-Executive Director for international growth
items.quote: As part of this diversification strategy, we have appointed this year Mr. Puneet Pal Singh as Managing Director. He will be focusing on accelerating our business expansion within India. I have transitioned to the role of Non-Executive Director, where I will lead our international growth initiatives.

items.statement: Geographic diversification from J&K/Ladakh to Uttarakhand, Himachal, Nagaland, Gujarat, Maharashtra leveraging MIPL offices
items.quote: This year, acquisition of MIPL, Maccaferri Infrastructure Private Limited has given us a leverage to assess PAN India opportunities for the growth. So, as you see, last year we were confined to Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, but this year we have diversified into various states like Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Gujarat and Maharashtra also in the road sector.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in Maharashtra (INR 300 crore won, INR 500 crore bid) and Northeast (BRO road projects); cluster strategy for cost efficiency
items.quote: Already we have got a project in Palghar area, which is INR300 crores, which was in October. That's why it was not in presentation. And we have again quoted for another INR500 crores project in this area. So let's see, Maharashtra is in our focus, North East is in our focus.

items.statement: Cherry-picking projects with good margins across geographies; not competing on low-margin projects
items.quote: No, because I told you that we have our standard policy of not bidding for these projects which have low margins. So, that is what I call cherry picking. So, we are doing only those projects which have good margins, whether they are in whichever geographical area of India.

items.statement: HAM project bidding initiated due to changed qualification criteria; better margins than EPC with dual income (EPC + interest)
items.quote: Because, if you have seen the recent developments, the criteria -- qualification criteria, Government of India has changed for HAM projects. So we're making it more restrictive now. So since we have not taken any HAM projects, now it is our time to go for HAM projects, and they have a better margin than EPC projects as of today.

items.statement: Auditor changed due to Indian accounting standards adoption; previous auditor retained for joint ventures
items.quote: What was the reason behind the change of auditor? Okay, because we moved to India as an Indian standard and our earlier auditor was not doing that. And it's a better group. Nothing more. He's still our auditor on the joint ventures, the earlier one.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margins expected to stay stable at 14-15%, with positive upside next financial year as blended occupancy increases
items.quote: for the current year, financial year, we expect margins to stay stable between 14% to 15%. Next financial year, we expect a kind of a positive upside on the margins as the blended occupancy increases a bit.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance revised to around INR220 crores from earlier INR180-200 crores range
items.quote: initially, we had given a guidance of around INR180 crores to INR200 crores. So it would be in the range of around INR220 crores.

items.statement: FY26 seat addition guidance maintained, H2 will be heavier for supply acquisition similar to last year
items.quote: H2 of FY '26 is where we are also pushing more on the supply acquisition and H1 was more of a consolidation phase around for us.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 operating EBITDA margin at 36.1%, H1 FY26 at 36.9%, up 180 bps YoY
items.quote: The operating EBITDA stood at INR132 crores, which is a growth of 32% on Y-o-Y basis. The margins stood at 36.1% for Q2FY26.

items.statement: Premiumization impact on margins expected in 4-6 quarters as premium centers grow as percentage of portfolio
items.quote: directionally, premiumization is going to help us with respect to improving the margins. But the impact of it would require at least four to six odd quarters and a bit more a larger portfolio of premium centers.

items.statement: Pipeline of 22 new centers under LOI adding ~24,000 seats and 1.1 million sq ft chargeable area
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have a pipeline of centers under fit-out, along with signed LOIs for 22 new centers, adding approximately 24,000 seats and 1.1 million square feet of chargeable area.

items.statement: H1 FY26 signed contracts for ~30,000+ new seats vs ~25,000 in H1 FY25, Q2 alone 15,000+ seats
items.quote: On the demand side, we signed contracts for 15,000-plus new seats in Q2 FY 2026 and approximately 30,000 plus for H1 of FY 2026 compared to almost about 25,000 seats in H1 of FY 2025, reflecting a robust revenue pipeline.

items.statement: Total capacity 170,000+ seats across 247 centers covering 8.4 million sq ft; operational seats 147,000 as of Sep 2025
items.quote: Our total capacity now stands at over 170,000 seats across 247 centers, covering an expansive 8.4 million square feet. As of September 2025, our exit month occupancy stood at 74%.

items.statement: Added 14,000 new seats in Q2 FY26, 33% YoY growth in operational seats
items.quote: On the supply side, during the quarter, we added 14,000 new seats, bringing our total capacity to around 147,000 operational seats pan-India as of September 2025, a 33% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Strong demand from GCCs and large enterprises; 61% occupier seats from large corporates/MNCs, 34% from 500+ seat segment
items.quote: Approximately 61% of our occupier seats are taken by large corporates and MNCs, 23% by SMEs, 15% by start-ups and remaining share by freelancers.

items.statement: India flex market at 80M sq ft across top 8 cities, largest in APAC, on track to cross 100M sq ft by 2026
items.quote: By Q2 2025, India's office footprint stood at about 80 million square feet across the top 8 cities, the largest in APAC region and on track to reach about 85 million square feet by year-end, and looking at crossing about the 100 million square foot milestone by 2026.

items.statement: 70% of new supply from Grade A+ assets, 100% from Grade A; 26 premium centers (21 Gold, 5 Elite)
items.quote: now in terms of the new additions over the last 1 year, 70% of properties which we have sourced is under Grade A plus supply and 100% across Grade A.

items.statement: Managed aggregation remains ~65% of pipeline; straight lease for Elite centers, MA for Grade A buildings
items.quote: the current pipeline of new centers, which you see with respect to managed aggregation is almost about 65%-odd.

items.statement: 9+ large corporate MNCs signed in H1 taking 5,000+ seats; existing Fortune 500 IT client expanded 1,000 seats across 2 Tier 2 cities
items.quote: In H1 FY 2026 also saw us sign 9-plus large corporates MNCs, taking up 5,000-plus seats. An existing Fortune 500 IT client, who currently has a portfolio with us across 5 locations, signed further expansion of 1,000 seats across 2 Tier 2 cities.

items.statement: Average capex INR1,700-1,750/sq ft super built-up; Gold centers 15-20% higher, Elite another 20% above Gold
items.quote: the average capex on super built-up area is about INR1,700 to INR1,750 on a super built-up area. The premium center, a Gold center would cost about 15%, 20% higher. So that would be another INR200 to INR250 more. And then the Elite would be another 20% from Gold.

items.statement: Gross debt INR21 crores in Q2 FY26 vs INR28 crores YoY; debt-equity 0.04, net debt-to-equity -0.18
items.quote: Our gross debt stood at around INR21 crores in Q2 FY '26 as against INR28 crores in Q2 of last year, resulting into a debt-equity ratio of 0.04, a notable improvement from 0.07 in Q2 of FY '25.

items.statement: Contract assets INR77 crores represent D&B work-in-progress with 45-60 day receivable cycle
items.quote: Contract assets for us are the D&B project assets. So typically, what we have is around 45 to 60 days kind of a receivable on that side, the assets till the time they are billed to the customer.

items.statement: Planned subsidiarization of Awfis Transform (design & build) to enable focus, capital flexibility, expansion into retail/hospitality
items.quote: A significant milestone in our strategic journey is the planned subsi diarization of Awfis Transform. Our high potential design and build business. We believe this vertical represents a key growth engine for Awfis and tracking it separately will enable greater focus, strategic clarity and scalability

items.statement: Blended occupancy 74% exit month Sep 2025; centers >12 months at 84% occupancy
items.quote: As of September 2025, our exit month occupancy stood at 74%, while centers operational for over 12 months achieved a robust 84% occupancy.

items.statement: Operating breakeven: 30-35% occupancy for MA centers, 55-60% for straight lease centers
items.quote: in a managed aggregation center, where we have a profit share model with a space owner along with a minimum guarantee situation, the operating breakeven at the center is about 30% to 35% of occupancy. For a straight lease center, the similar operating breakeven is at about 55% to 60-odd percent kind of occupancy.

items.statement: Annual center closures of 2-3 centers expected; INR3.5 cr FA write-off in Q2 from ~900 seats closed
items.quote: every year, there could be two or three centers that will get closed down every year. And every 6 months in terms of hygiene, we are basically taking the write-off for the fixed assets and their written-on value.

items.statement: ESOP 2024 scheme charge of INR2.4 crores in Q2 from annual appraisal process
items.quote: as part of the annual appraisal process, there are ESOPs issued to the employees under the ESOP 2024 scheme. So there's an additional charge which has happened on the ESOP side. So that is around INR2.4 crores approximately.

items.statement: Furniture business: partnerships curated, phased plan, growth expected over next 3-6 months
items.quote: over the next 3 to 6 months, you will see us obviously growing that segment. Last few months were obviously around curating the partnerships, setting the portfolio, the kind of product offering we were enabling.

items.statement: Flex segment (co-working <100 seats) growing strongly with network effects; enterprise segment driven by mid-sized GCCs
items.quote: Both the flex and the enterprise segment of our business continues to grow at a strong pace. The enterprise segment is propelled by the entry of new midsized GCCs setting up operations in India.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 1,000 crore within 3.5-4 years from IPO (thousand working days)
items.quote: We have been very clear that we will take a thousand working days. So you can say almost between 3.5 years to 4 years from the date of IPO. So when you look at thousand working days, that is the target we have. And I think we will definitely reach that in the next whatever within the next 3 years.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 140 crore for FY26 in line with prospectus
items.quote: Yes, we are very much in line with that.

items.statement: Capex per store: luxury INR 7-10 cr, premium INR 3-5 cr, value premium INR 1.5-2 cr
items.quote: So it depends on the three different formats. The luxury format can take anywhere between 7 crores to 10 crores. The premium format will take between 3 crores to 5 crores, and the value premium can take anywhere between 1.5 crores to 2 crores.

items.statement: Plan to open 15 stores in FY26; 8-9 already opened in H1
items.quote: We plan to open about 15 stores in all in the current year, '25-'26. Out of that, we have already opened 8 or 9 stores.

items.statement: Superlative large-format store (1 lakh sq ft super built-up) in Hyderabad launching Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our new store format Superlative, which is being built in Hyderabad, is expected to be launched in Q4. The work is progressing as planned and it would house all our premium as well as luxury segment. The store spans almost 1 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Target 6-8 exclusive FOFO stores in Sri Lanka over 3 years via Singer partnership; first store Q4 FY26
items.quote: We plan to open 8 stores in Sri Lanka over the next three years, making Stanley's first step towards becoming a global Indian luxury brand.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 550 bps YoY to 23.5%
items.quote: I am pleased to share that our EBITDA margins expanded significantly by 550 basis points to 23.5% this quarter, compared to 18% in the same period last year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 320 bps YoY to 22.1%
items.quote: The EBITDA margins expanded by 320 basis points to 22.1% in H1 FY'26 compared to 18.9% in H1 FY'25.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross margin improved 330 bps YoY driven by procurement efficiencies, localization, insourcing
items.quote: Our gross profit margin improved by 330 basis points over the same period last year, supported by better procurement efficiencies, greater localization and increased insourcing of the manufacturing process, all of which helped us deliver a richer and more efficient product mix.

items.statement: Leather localization at 45-50%, targeting 70-80% in next 12 months; ~15% BOM saving so far, 20-25% at full localization
items.quote: As of now, we have been fairly successful and that also shows in our gross profit improvement in the H1 of this year. We continue to source, but we have to be extremely careful not to kind of compromise on the quality. So, that is a long drawn process. A lot of Indian tanneries do not have the capabilities. So, we are getting in Italian expertise and going about in an organic manner, but we remain

items.statement: Leather is ~50% of BOM; further 5-8% leather cost saving possible, supporting 2-3% gross margin improvement to 62-63%
items.quote: Maybe we can get another 5%-8% further in the leather cost, which we can get the benefit.

items.statement: COCO revenue grew ~23% YoY in H1 FY26; retail now ~70% of total revenue
items.quote: Our COCO business is significantly grown, even this H1 by almost 23%. So, that is where the real change is coming.

items.statement: Shift from loose furniture to complete home solutions: Level Next avg ticket INR 25-30 lakh vs INR 2 lakh in 2020
items.quote: But now in Stanley Level Next with complete home solutions, it is pivoted to almost about 25-30 lakhs. That is because of the changing dynamics in the Indian residential construction industry.

items.statement: Perfume pilot (UD perfumes INR 7-20k) in Level Next stores; high margins, no major marketing spend planned for 1-2 years
items.quote: We are just piloting it. It's in a very early stage and we will not have any major time or money spent on this. We are piloting it in our own stores. And it's just a pure brand extension into the what is known as the not the usual deodorant or cologne market. It is called as UD perfumes. These are expensive perfumes starting at about 7,000-8,000 going up to almost 20,000.

items.statement: Men's shoes and belts also piloted as lifestyle extensions to attract younger customers (30-45 age)
items.quote: We have men's shoes also we have started. That is also been there for a while now. That also has passed the proof of concept. It's a highly profitable business.

items.statement: ~80%+ revenue from direct B2C; building business development team for architect/designer channel next year
items.quote: Largely 80% of our business still comes from, probably even larger, comes directly from B2C. But now we are introducing a strong business development team starting next year. So eventually we will also be attracting a lot of good talent in terms of architecture, interior designers coming into our foray.

items.statement: Branded furniture model is cash-and-carry; one trading item switched to cash-and-carry, receivables improving steadily
items.quote: So, our model has for the branded business of furniture, it's always been cash and carry. There was one particular trading item where we were giving credit, that now we have changed to cash and carry and we are seeing a meaningful increase in that going steadily, but we are still maintaining the cash and carry policy as of now.

items.statement: No further fund raise needed to reach INR 1,000 cr target; existing funds adequate as store cohort matures
items.quote: We have adequate funds. We will not need any funds because now the age and maturity of the stores has started.

items.statement: Stanley brand IP transferred to company pre-IPO for INR 37.5 cr; capitalized as intangible asset in H1 FY26
items.quote: Before the IPO, they had paid INR 37.5 crores and acquired all the Stanley brand. And this was pending to be approved by the agency of transfer to the Company name. This happened during the current H1 and they have capitalized that as part of intangible assets.

items.statement: Moat: customization, after-sales service, 30-year brand trust; imports from Europe/Dubai/China are a challenge but lack service capability
items.quote: But we are expecting the COCO to cover the finished product. Hopefully that will give us a stronger moat. But otherwise also, I think our moat has always been customization and furniture being a product that people enjoy for years to come, maybe even decades to come, they need an after-sales service. So a trader can bring in anything from anywhere, but they will not be able to give a service.

items.statement: Store maturation curve: 50-60% potential in Year 1, 70-75% in Year 2, 80-90% in Year 3, full maturity Year 4; breakeven within 6 months, ROI within 24-30 months
items.quote: From our experience, it is understood that the new store normally delivers about 50% to 60% of its true potential by the end of the first year, goes up to about 70%-75% second year and only after the third year it comes to its optimum level. So, that's how we measure our store matrix and that's how we keep an eye on our store breakeven as well as store profitability.

items.statement: Superlative Bangalore store (1 lakh sq ft super built-up) delivers ~INR 50 cr annual throughput; Hyderabad target higher
items.quote: This store easily gives about INR 50 crores of throughput. The Hyderabad store, our target is to reach a much higher number going forward.

items.statement: Real estate availability and high rentals in Mumbai/Delhi delaying large-format store rollout in those cities
items.quote: Unfortunately, we are not getting desired real estate, especially in cities like Mumbai. Unfortunately, the rental expectations are extremely high. So we are a little shy. We will not just rush into it. We are negotiating for built-to-suit properties. It might take a little longer, but we will make meaningful investments.

items.statement: Festive season sales (Sep-Nov, Feb-Mar) drive footfall via floor-stock promotions; all three formats participate
items.quote: Normally in the festive season period between September and December, we always go on what I call as a sale. But those sales are technically for floor stocks that are there and they are always refurbished with new products. That's how we generate footfall into our stores.

items.statement: Festival discounts (2-5%) do not hurt margins; volume increase improves manufacturing efficiency and localization benefits
items.quote: We don't see any impact of the price reduction happening on our margins.

items.statement: Structural HR and technology upgrades (Salesforce, SAP HANA) post-IPO; SAP HANA completion by year-end FY26
items.quote: We have Sales force and we have SAP HANA being introduced in our Company. That's a work in progress that will complete by this yearend.

items.statement: Management guided for base EBITDA margin improvement of ~150 bps in FY26, excluding Sanofi and Novo deals.
items.quote: what we have guided for is we expect this year the base margins to improve by about 150 basis points. I think we'll be on track for that.

items.statement: Management expects to become debt-free by end of FY27 (18-24 months) after Zuventus stake purchase.
items.quote: So I think with post that acquisition, we expect now to be debt-free by end of next year. So it'll take about 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Domestic organic growth targeted at industry growth plus 100-200 bps.
items.quote: I think what we've continued to guide is that organically, we would look to be at industry growth rates plus 100 to 200 basis points.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin was 19.3%, up from 19% in Q2 FY25 and 19.2% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 19.3% versus 19% in Q2 FY '25 and 19.2% in Q1 '26, supported by our operating leverage and productivity gains.

items.statement: Gross margin was 60.8% in Q2 FY26 vs 60.6% in Q2 FY25, driven by product and business mix.
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 60.8% versus 60.6% in Q2 of FY '25. The change was driven largely by product and business mix.

items.statement: Domestic business grew 10.6% YoY in Q2 FY26, above industry growth of 11%, with growth across gynec, cardio, derma, consumer and diabetes.
items.quote: The domestic business grew by 10.6% YoY to INR 1,031 crores, this is led by strong performance across all key therapies.

items.statement: International business grew 15.8% YoY in Q2 FY26; Europe up 22.7%, Canada up 17.5%, emerging markets up 8.6%.
items.quote: International markets maintained strong growth momentum, growing 15.8% YoY, INR 1,238 crores.

items.statement: ARV order book provides visibility for current year and large part of next year; South Africa tender won.
items.quote: we have quite a good, healthy order book. So we have visibility for the current year and even the next year.

items.statement: Inventory increased in H1 FY26 to support anticipated H2 launches in Europe and Canada; expected to normalize over next 6 months.
items.quote: for the European market, we are anticipating some new launches and even the Canadian market, and that's where the inventory has gone up.

items.statement: Amphotericin B launched in UK (last year) and Italy (recently); further launches in France, Germany expected in H2 FY26.
items.quote: We should have launches in some of the other Western European countries like France, Germany in the remaining part of this financial year.

items.statement: Chronic portfolio (cardio, diabetes, semaglutide) and women's health are key growth pillars; in-licensing deals targeted at mid-teens EBITDA margins.
items.quote: if we can do deals that are somewhere in the ballpark of mid -teens EBITDA margins and then has a rub -off effect on our entire portfolio, I think that would be sort of a high-level threshold.

items.statement: Novo Nordisk partnership for semaglutide brand Poviztra in India; exclusive distribution with no territory restrictions within India.
items.quote: We'll be able to sell where Novo is also selling.

items.statement: Early entry with Novo's semaglutide brand ahead of patent expiry (Mar '26) to shape obesity market vs crowded generic competition later.
items.quote: post -LOE, we anticipate a very crowded market in India. And so the ability to partner with Novo and launch this brand ahead of the competition and allowing ourselves to shape the market and have brand recall versus being lost in the crowd probably 4, 5 months down the line is something that we feel strongly will allow us to succeed

items.statement: Bevacizumab biosimilar Phase III completed; filing with SEC expected in next few weeks.
items.quote: We have completed our Phase III of Bevacizumab. We believe it's gone up very well, and we should be submitting our file for evaluation by the SEC and subsequent approval by the regulators in the next few weeks.

items.statement: ARV pricing stable in recent tenders including South Africa; no significant pricing pressure observed.
items.quote: the pricing has been largely stable. I think even in the new South Africa tender s and all, we haven't seen much impact on the pricing.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR 837 crores in Q2 FY26 due to partial payout for Zuventus minority stake purchase.
items.quote: Net debt for the quarter was at INR 837 crores. The debt has increased primarily due to partial payout of the ZHL stake purchase.

items.statement: Zuventus minority stake purchase completed in early October; full consolidation from Q3 FY26.
items.quote: We have now completed the purchase of the minority stake in Zuventus, which allows us to fully consolidate the business.

items.statement: M&A focus on domestic market (portfolio gaps and strengthening strong segments) and bolt-on acquisitions in key international markets (Canada, UK, Europe).
items.quote: M&A will continue to be an important part of our growth strategy. And to that extent, domestic market, which is our single largest market, we will definitely be active in looking for M&A opportunities there.

items.statement: Domestic organic growth (ex-Sanofi) was 8.5-9% in Q2 FY26; Sanofi diabetes portfolio contributed ~1.5 months.
items.quote: Yes, except that, it has been at 8.5%-9%.

items.statement: Tenecteplase gaining approvals in emerging markets for myocardial infarction; stroke indication seeing doctor-initiated demand in some markets.
items.quote: most of the approvals that we're getting in the emerging markets is for the original myocardial infaction.

items.statement: No plans to locally manufacture semaglutide in India; will rely on imported global product from Novo Nordisk.
items.quote: In fact, this is the re global product. So they will continue to be importing the product for us to market and distribute in India and no plans to locally manufacture.

items.statement: Sanofi field force joining Emcure after retirement, supporting diabetes portfolio ramp-up.
items.quote: Sanofi people also joining post their retirement or whatever, in Sanofi, it is obviously helping our products as well.

items.statement: Sanofi cardiac portfolio back to industry growth levels; diabetes portfolio tracking better than initial targets.
items.quote: the cardiac portfolio is now back starting in line with the industry growth. So there, I think, as we had even last quarter mentioned, we are seeing normalization now.

items.statement: Inventory build-up for H2 FY26 export launches; expected to normalize over next 6 months.
items.quote: Over the next 6 months, we see inventory normalizing.

items.statement: Overall revenue grew 13.4% YoY to INR 2,270 crores in Q2 FY26; PAT grew 24% YoY to INR 251 crores.
items.quote: Revenues from operations for the quarter grew 13.4% YoY to INR 2,270 crores, up from INR 2,002 crores in quarter 2 of FY '25.

items.statement: H2 FY26 CDMO margins expected to mimic H1 (~12% EBITDA margin)
items.quote: I think blended rates, I think H2 should largely be similar as H1 as an overall year, given obviously the current market dynamics, while it remains for the Q3 as well, we are seeing a decent volume growth, some pockets, as I said, of APIs have started stabilizing, which looks in control, I think

items.statement: API business full-year losses expected lower than last year
items.quote: So we think that by the year-end, our EBITDA will be better than what it is showing. So the EBITDA for the quarter was negative INR14 crores. It was very similar to Q2 FY'25. But this has been something that by the year-end, we should be better based on our cost optimization, and we expect the full-year losses to be lower than last year.

items.statement: International branded formulations expected strong in H2 FY26
items.quote: This revenue was largely impacted by seasonality issues and is expected to be strong in the next half year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex INR 107 crores; H2 FY26 capex expected INR 100-125 crores
items.quote: Till now, for the first six months, our capex is close to INR107 crores. We would probably, depending on the future requirement, foresee just a similar or slightly lower capex in the next six months.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~40%; peak operational capacity 55% for oral solids, 60-65% for injectables/oral liquids
items.quote: 55% is the peak. So we are operating at 40%. So we report our total operational capacity that we can reach, right, of which 55% is the operational capacity broadly. We are currently at 40.

items.statement: European CDMO contract: 6-year commercial supply starting April 2027, portfolio across multiple SKUs/packaging, single base molecule
items.quote: This is a six-year commercial supply contract. And yes, broadly -- and on your point on product, this is a portfolio across multiple SKUs and packaging types. The base molecule here remains the same.

items.statement: European dossier pipeline: 10+ dossiers, Dapagliflozin and Rivaroxaban commercial supply in Q3 FY26, others over 2-2.5 years
items.quote: There are 8 to 10 other dossiers in pipeline, which are across multiple dosage forms, product types that we will subsequently launch over the next 2, 2.5 years.

items.statement: CDMO gross margin improved to 37.6% in Q2 FY26 from 37.1% in FY25; EBITDA margin declined due to API price drop and new plant overheads
items.quote: If you really look at it, what went is if you look at the gross margins in this business in FY '25, we had a gross margin of 37.1% in the CDMO business. If I look at just the Q2, where the margins were low, the gross margins are still at 37.6%. So we have improved our gross margins from the last year, right?

items.statement: API gross margin fell to 9.3% in Q2 FY26 from 12.8% in FY25 due to cyclosporin price decline
items.quote: If I really talk about the gross margins in FY '25, we had a gross margin of 12.8% in the API business. With the continued downward trend of the larger cyclosporin business in Q2, the gross margins of the business were only 9.3%.

items.statement: CDMO volume growth >7% YoY in Q2 FY26 despite flat IPM volume growth
items.quote: Our CDMO business witnessed a healthy volume growth of over 7%, even though the IPM volume growth was flat.

items.statement: Domestic branded formulations revenue grew 5.3% YoY and 13.5% QoQ to INR 122 crores in Q2 FY26

items.quote: And next year, the full -- they are planning to achieve $7 million in Beryl. And this -- our regular turnover also may go up to $20 million. So $27 million is internal target for next '26, '27 financial year.

items.statement: Civil engineering work on hand ~$4.2-4.3M; MES work on hand ~$600K (up from $150K last quarter).

items.statement: Beryl EBITDA margin expected to rise from 7-8% to 15-20% over next few quarters as 25-30% of work offshored to India; standalone margins to improve with operating leverage as top line grows.
items.quote: from the current level of 7%, 8% EBITDA, they can easily go up to 15% to 20% EBITDA levels. And with the top line also growing at least 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Standalone model has high operating leverage: fixed cost base means incremental revenue drops largely to bottom line.

items.statement: US civil engineering demand recovering post-election/tariff clarity; Q2 revenue up 20.85% YoY to INR40.23 crore; EBITDA up 144.5% to INR5.96 crore; PAT up to INR3.24 crore.

items.quote: the sales have gone up by 20.85% from INR33.29 crores to INR40.23 crores, a significant increase by 20%. And the EBITDA was shot up by 144.5% from INR2.44 crores to INR5.96 crores and the profit after tax was shot up by 2% from INR0.68 crores to INR3.24 crores

items.statement: Beryl adds residential & semi-commercial permit/approval/inspection services (2 FL counties, expandable to 3,000+ US counties) complementing Mold-Tek's industrial/commercial steel detailing; AI-based plan review tools to be leveraged offsho
items.quote: these are residential buildings wherein Beryl provides right from permits, approvals, inspections and additions, if any, which any decisions takes place in the 2 counties in Florida, and they will provide even on-site inspection support.

items.statement: Mechanical engineering diversifying from automotive (Tier 1 body manufacturing) into utility (power transmission substations), industrial machinery & special purpose machines, and plant engineering.
items.quote: we have been working towards diversifying further to derisk ourselves from the automotive so that we have more predictable and [inaudible 0:33:55] scope of growth. So these are like the broad categories of segments which we are working on.

items.statement: AI tools from Beryl (automated plan review, permit processing) to be deployed at Mold-Tek India to accelerate permit approvals and improve quality inspection.

items.statement: Beryl team visiting India for 2 months from January; Mold-Tek senior engineers visiting Florida in December for knowledge transfer on residential permit/inspection processes.
items.quote: we are also sending a couple of our senior engineers in December, this month itself, to Beryl, Florida so that they will be catching up with the ways and means and methods followed by Beryl in executing these projects.

items.statement: US tariff policy uncertainty remains a key risk for civil/commercial construction demand and PEB export model; Europe civil not pursued due to different standards and lower pricing attractiveness.

items.statement: Aspirational revenue target of INR 2,500 crores by FY31

items.quote: The Lifetime Nominations, the value of which is INR 600 crores for international business and INR 150 crores for Indian business, totaling INR 750 crores, is over and above the increases of the existing platform that we supply to.

items.statement: New aerospace plant under construction at Waluj; acquisition planned to speed certification by 3.5 years
items.quote: We have already engineered plain spherical bearings. And NRB has a best-in-class plant under construction as part of an earlier plan to cater to the aerospace industry... items.statement: PAT margin improved to 12% in Q2 FY26 from 10% last year; target ROE 17-18%

items.statement: Industrial expansion to maintain margins via high-entry barrier products; not growing at expense of margin

items.quote: Will we have more than our competition? Yes. Will we have as much inventory as we have today? No. It will come down step by step, but it will not come down to the level of our competitors.

items.statement: Debt-equity under 20%; AA- Crisil rating; cash reserves and real estate at book value provide funding headroom
items.quote: Given that our debt-equity ratio is under 20%, you can see that we have preserved huge cash reserves and have borrowing ability which ensures that CAPEX is not going to be an issue at all.

items.quote: All these initiatives we are talking about are like INR 50 crores to INR 75 crores, I mean, just to give you a rough number. It is not going to be INR 100 crores or INR 200 crores or something like that

items.quote: It's stable around INR140 to INR150.

items.quote: We have applied for the pharma grade PG. So the moment we get the license, we'll start the manufacturing of the pharma grade.

items.statement: Recognized as Great Place To Work in US, Canada, Colombia, Philippines
items.quote: We have been recognized as a 'Great Place To Work' in four geos to date: the US, Canada, Colombia, and the Philippines.

items.statement: AM Lens reduced false positives ~60% and increased investigation throughput 3x for BFSI client
items.quote: They have been able to reduce false positives by around 60% and they have been able to increase the throughput of their team by 3x with the number of transactions they have been able to investigate for anti-money laundering.

items.statement: Interaction Intelligence cut agent time-to-proficiency from 10-12 weeks to 2-3 weeks
items.quote: We have seen that the time to proficiency for agents has been reduced significantly, from 10-12 weeks to 2-3 weeks.

items.statement: Pricing models evolving to outcome-based, per transaction or outcome
items.quote: As we go through this exercise, our pricing models will evolve into outcome-based pricing, charging per transaction or per outcome with customers to create a sustained revenue base.

items.statement: Aggressively renegotiating with input service providers, vendors, partners to cut costs
items.quote: We are renegotiating aggressively with our input service providers, vendors, and various partners. This is why, across the board, our margins have improved quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Media business faces strong headwinds from OTT, free dish, free TV services
items.quote: There is no doubt that the media business continues to face challenges in India, whether from OTT, free dish, or free television services.

items.statement: BAGO initiative targeting 1,000-2,000 smaller ISPs for partnerships and deals
items.quote: The idea is that many of these providers are facing growth challenges and are looking for strong partnerships and relationships. We have created this cell called Broadband Accelerated Growth Opportunities at the head office with a central team.

items.statement: FY26 D2C revenue target of 305 crores
items.quote: With this momentum we remain confident of achieving our FY26 direct to consumer revenue target of 305 crores.

items.statement: Expect 40-60% growth in D2C business and low double-digit growth in license and customer brands
items.quote: We expect to continue 40% to 60% growth in our direct-to-consumer business. The license brands and customer business will be sort of low double-digit kind of growth.

items.statement: Net debt target around 200 crores, debt-to-equity at 0.25
items.quote: As the business continues to generate cash the gross debt number will continue to go down. We plan to manage debt prudently keeping it currently at 0.25 debt to equity, which we feel is a healthy number.

items.statement: Jean Dousset store investment of 6 crores each, planning 2-3 stores in CY26
items.quote: Our Jean Dousset store requires an investment of about Rs. 6 crores and does sales of around 25 crores with a gross margin delivered of 70%.

items.statement: UAE manufacturing facility expected to come on stream around December 10
items.quote: Our own manufacturing facility is expected to come on stream sometime around the 10 th of December

items.statement: US D2C brands grew 60% YoY, D2C overall grew 43% YoY
items.quote: This performance was especially robust in our US D2C brands which grew 60% year over year supported by deeper consumer engagement and strengthened brand presence.

items.statement: D2C EBITDA margin expanded from 8.8% to 12.1% YoY, D2C EBITDA grew 96% to 7.2 crores
items.quote: D2C EBITDA for Q2 FY26 grew 96% to 7.2 crore s, with EBITDA margins expanding from 8.8% in Q2 FY25 to 12.1% in Q2 FY26

items.statement: UAE manufacturing adds 1% cost dilution, margins would be 10% without it
items.quote: I mean, it has maybe a 1% impact on our cost structure. So, I think that the margins that you're seeing now of 9% have an impact of 1% dilution due to the cost of manufacturing in UAE.

items.statement: Jean Dousset New York flagship contributes 25 crores annually, 30% of brand sales
items.quote: The New York flagship continues to contribute roughly 25 crores annually, 30% of the brand's total sales demonstrating robust profitability and impressive retail productivity.

items.statement: Bullion sales of 70-80 crores to UAE subcontractors for country of origin, compresses gross margin
items.quote: So, the number is somewhere in the range of 70 to 80 crores. So, while the customer brands show a growth of 47%, there is an element of bullion sale to third party contractors for casting purposes in order to have country of origin, UAE.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by 100 crores YoY, expect positive operating cash flow for FY26
items.quote: I mean, if you see year-over-year, we have now managed to reduce inventory by about 100 crores. And we will see positive cash flow from operations for this year.

items.statement: Trade payables reduced by 80 crores, paying faster to save costs
items.quote: If you see in this quarter, we have been sort of buying in much shorter duration. So, our trade tables are lower by about 80 crores.

items.statement: Net debt improved to 0.24x from 0.27x, interest costs lower due to lower utilization
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to strengthen, with net debt improving to 0.24 compared to 0.27 last year, reflecting better working capital management and improved cash generation.

items.statement: No plans to scale India business, focus on US D2C expansion
items.quote: Currently, there is no immediate plans to scale up in India. For now, we are trying to figure out the unit economics of our India business.

items.statement: Further 15 crores annual cost reduction expected between Q3 and Q4
items.quote: We expect that run rate to accelerate in Q4 to about 60 crores annually. So, there's a further 15 crores of annual cost reduction that will happen between Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Customer brand margins 7-8% for B2B, D2C lab grown margins 13-14%
items.quote: Our margins in lab grown are now approaching 13%-14% for our direct-to-consumer business. And they would be maybe in the seven to eight percent for the B2B business.

items.quote: I think most of the banks MCLR, 1 -year MCLR is around 8.65 to 8.75, 8.8. That will be the, because we are taking term loans, it's all linked with 1-year MCLR.

items.statement: No knee-jerk reaction to new AAA-rated NBFC entrants; focused gold loan model with branch network and customer trust seen as moat
items.quote: There are people coming AAA or AA or whatever A rating, etc. with deep pockets, maybe coming into the business. But then we have been focused on this business. We are focused on gold loan or branches are also focused on gold loan.

items.statement: Adding ~4.2 lakh new customers per quarter; incremental new customer count stable with minor variations
items.quote: So, answering Shreya's question on number of customers, every quarter we are adding a new set of customers, which is around 4.2 lakhs.

items.statement: Non-gold portfolio 12%-15% of consolidated AUM; expanding microfinance and vehicle finance via subsidiaries
items.quote: This non -gold loan portfolio is about 12 %-15% of the consolidated loan board portfolio.

items.statement: Loan book split: >3 lakh 44%, 1-3 lakh 33%; average ticket size >Rs 1.17 lakh
items.quote: So, above 3 lakh is 44%. 1 lakh to 3 lakh is 33%.

items.statement: No quantifiable loss from retail investor complaints case; exchange filing detailed and unrelated to Muthoot Finance
items.quote: Love, please go through that exchange filing. This has nothing to do with Muth oot Finance, no loss incurred by the investors.

items.statement: Employee costs rising due to Onam bonus, incentives, increments and branch expansion hiring
items.quote: This is a bonus season. So, Onam bonus etc. payments come, incentives are paid. Of course, increments are also paid. I am not sure that may be one of the reasons. Of course, we are adding people also.

items.statement: Will continue current three-entity gold loan structure (Muthoot Finance, Belstar, Muthoot Money); no structural changes planned
items.quote: We will continue with this structure.

items.statement: Record order booking of ₹6.52 billion in Q2 FY26, up 14% YoY, driven by domestic orders
items.quote: We're also pleased to report a record order booking of ₹6.52 billion during this quarter, which is 14% hig her on a year -on-year basis, driven primarily on robust domestic order booking

items.statement: Closing order book at all-time high of ₹22.20 billion, up 24% YoY as of 30th September
items.quote: As a result of which, the closing order booking as of the 30th of September stood at, again, an all-time high of ₹22.20 billion, up 24% year-over-year.

items.statement: Domestic order booking grew 52% YoY to ₹4.07 billion, contributing 62% of total order booking
items.quote: On the order booking, the company achieved record order booking, and this was largely driven by the domestic order booking, which grew at a very rapid pace of 52% year-over-year to ₹4.07 billion and now contributes 62% to the overall order booking in the quarter.

items.statement: Domestic outstanding order book at all-time high of ₹10.96 billion, up 55% YoY; export outstanding order book at ₹11.23 billion, up 3% YoY
items.quote: Domestic outstanding order book is also at an all-time high of ₹10.96 billion, which grew 55% as compared to the previous year. At the same time, the export outstanding order book stood at ₹11.23 billion as on the 30th of September, up 3% and contributes 51% of the closing order book.

items.statement: Enquiry book remains extremely healthy, providing good visibility for order booking in near and medium term across sectors and geographies
items.quote: Our order booking is a reflection of our enquiry book, which remains extremely healthy and gives us good visibility in terms of order booking, not only in the near term, but in the medium term.

items.statement: Domestic demand growing in steel, cement, sugar, utility power drive turbines; export demand resilient in Europe, Middle East, energy transition markets
items.quote: We've had some good successes, and we believe that there is enough impetus for these segments to grow in the coming quarters and coming years as well.

items.statement: FY26 growth will be back-ended with higher growth rates in Q3 and Q4; revenue decline in H1 to be made up in coming quarters
items.quote: The outlook for the company, as I said, remains very confident. As we've stated in the Q1 earnings conference call, the growth for financial year FY 2026 will be back ended. Q3 and Q4 will represent higher growth rates in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Management not giving formal guidance but expects growth better than single-digit; not satisfied with single-digit growth
items.quote: I think it's better we don't really give guidance as such. But I think you have an idea of where our order book sits and you could interpret that in whichever manner. I think I'm happy to say that it would be growth. A single-digit growth number is very little, and I won't be particularly satisfied with that.

items.statement: Margins not expected to be materially impacted despite higher domestic execution; overhead absorption benefits and value engineering to offset lower domestic margins
items.quote: While domestic margins are slightly lower, I think that the company's robust product mix and the fact that we have done intensive work in value engineering means that we do not foresee any pressure on margins.

items.statement: NTPC energy storage project margins in line with expectations; no surprises as all purchase orders placed and costing accurate
items.quote: As far as margins go, there's been no surprises or pretty much all the purchase orders that have to be placed have been placed, and so the costing is quite accurate.

items.statement: Aftermarket turnover at record ₹1.78 billion, up 8% YoY; contribution enhanced to 35% from 33% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: However, the Aftermarket turnover was a record ₹1.78 billion during the quarter, an increase of 8% year-over-year. As a result, the Aftermarket segment contribution to turnover enhanced to a robust 35% in Q2 FY 2026 as compared to 33% in Q2 FY 2025.

items.statement: Aftermarket order booking at record ₹1.99 billion, up 15% YoY, including new marquee orders
items.quote: During the quarter, the segment reported a record order booking of ₹1.99 billion, which included new marquee orders and led to a growth of 15% year-over-year when compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Export sales increased 27% to ₹2.82 billion; export contribution to sales rose to 56% from 44% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Domestic sales declined by 20% to ₹2.24 billion, while export sales increased 27% to ₹2.82 billion. Export contribution to sales increased by 56% in the second quarter of FY 2026 as compared to 44% in the second quarter of FY 2025.

items.statement: U.S. product order finalisation delayed due to tariff uncertainty; refurbishment business in U.S. buoyant with good enquiries and orders
items.quote: One of the larger markets, which has disappointed on the product ordering has been the United States, which we believe given some of the trade uncertainties going away would lead to finalisation.

items.statement: Capex in current quarter around ₹30 crores including heat pump setup and new offices; no plans for new factories; Sompura expansion to be capitalised by end of year
items.quote: The CapEx is in this current quarter was somewhere in the region of about ₹30-odd crores, but that included setting up a heat pump and setting up new offices, etc.

items.statement: Not capacity-constrained; expanding vendor base and supplier ecosystem to meet volume growth; fourth test bed commissioned at Sompura
items.quote: We are today in a position to take up shorter lead time orders. We are able to take up orders which have longer gestation period because we have broad-based our vendor base.

items.statement: Acquired remaining 30% stake in TSE Engineering Pty Ltd, South Africa for ZAR 10.97 million (₹56 million); TSE to become wholly owned step-down subsidiary
items.quote: We recently announced the acquisition of the remaining 30% equity stake in TSE Engineering Pty. Limited in South Africa for a cash consideration of ZAR 10.97 million, which is ₹56 million.

items.statement: Utility boiler feed water pump drive turbine market estimated at 50-55 turbines (~8 GW) over next 2-3 years; Triveni approved vendor with major developers including NTPC
items.quote: This market will be something like around 50, 55 turbines market there. And we are approved vendor with all these major developers as well as like NTPC and all these sorts of things.

items.statement: Heat pump demo unit at Peenya facility delivering 126°C hot water (world's first CO2-based); strong enquiry pipeline building
items.quote: One demo unit we established at our Peenya facility. This is the world's first when it comes to the temperature wise. We are giving a hot water at 126 degrees, CO2-based heat pump.

items.statement: MVR (mechanical vapor recompression) commercial orders picked up; first delivery expected Q1 FY27; 8-9 compressors in first purchase order
items.quote: We picked up commercial order s and we'll be delivering first MVR sometime quarter one of the next financial year. That enquiry pipeline is also building up

items.statement: Investor Relations head Surabhi Chandna leaving; Amit Shah taking over IR responsibilities
items.quote: Ms. Surabhi Chandna, who has led the Investor Relations & Value Creation function at Triveni has decided to pursue external opportunities and today is her last working day.

items.statement: Inventory significantly higher on six-month basis due to deferred revenue from Q1; receivables higher due to API and export order billing norms; cash flow not a problem
items.quote: If you look at our balance sheet on a six-month basis, you'll see that inventory is significantly higher also, which is what will give you the confidence into the revenue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Advances from customers typically 10-30% of order value depending on customer and industry standards
items.quote: It would be anywhere between 10% to 30%. Now it will depend from customer-to-customer.

items.statement: Domestic market primarily served by Siemens and Triveni; market share gains in high-spec API turbines and utility drive turbines; market also growing
items.quote: The majority of the domestic market is catered to by Siemens and us in the industrial space. And so, people coming and going, you're talking about a few turbines here and there.

items.statement: U.S. tariff uncertainty (currently ~56%) delaying product order finalisation; Southeast Asia underperforming; geopolitical issues caused Q1 inspection deferrals
items.quote: Currently, our tariff is somewhere in the region of about 56-odd percent for our product range. And that's quite large, as you would imagine.

items.statement: U.S. regulatory approvals for water and environmental concerns delaying combined cycle projects; simple cycle with combined cycle add-on later more common
items.quote: Because the availability of regulatory approval for water and other environmental concerns, I think takes a little bit more time.

items.statement: Management not providing specific revenue or EBITDA margin guidance for FY26; aims for high double-digit sales growth and double-digit EBITDA margins
items.quote: So, unfortunately, at the moment, we are not providing any specific guidance. But generally, we have been growing at high double-digit even on the sales number and we are also working on improving margins as we scale. We will continue to aim to have similar kind of growth in the future as well, you know, at least for the coming financial year.

items.statement: Capex not sizable; capacity expansion at Solapur plant targeting ~20% capacity growth over next six months
items.quote: So, generally, our business is not very CAPEX driven. It is more OPEX driven. There is continuous CAPEX that we do to increase the capacities available to us, specifically in our Solapur plant. However, it is not very sizable. It is basically to add about so that it grows at about 20% in terms of capacity over the next six months.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 14.94% driven by price increases due to price-insensitive demand, festive pickup and GST rate cut; targets double-digit EBITDA margins going forward
items.quote: So, this quarter was a bit peculiar in the sense that what we saw was the GST rate cut being announced after which there was deferred purchases. So, our pricing models that we use, they realized that the customer is not price sensitive. Rather, I would say it is price insensitive.

items.statement: Strong demand recovery by end of Q2 FY26 supported by improved consumer sentiment and GST rate cut coming into effect
items.quote: By the end of the quarter, we witnessed a strong recovery in demand as asset buying picked up, supported by improved consumer sentiment and the GST rate cut coming into effect.

items.statement: Thomas Scott own brand revenue Rs 22 crore (+77% YoY); licensed brands Rs 33 crore (+23% YoY); contract manufacturing Rs 3 crore (+40% YoY)
items.quote: Our own brand, Thomas Scott, delivered revenues of Rs. 22 crore, up 77% year-on-year, reflecting the growing strength of our direct-to-consumer franchise and improved assortment planning. The licensed and other brands that we support also maintained steady traction with revenues of Rs. 33 crore, an increase of 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Offline exclusive stores in Bangalore increased to six with new store at Gopalan Mall; offline pilot phase testing return on capital employed
items.quote: During the quarter, we also strengthened our offline presence with the opening of a new exclusive store at Gopalan Mall in Bangalore, further enhancing visibility and reach in the market in the South. With this addition, our total number of exclusive outlets in Bangalore now stands at six.

items.statement: Trade receivables ~Rs 71.5 crore; inventory ~Rs 77.1 crore; inventory building for H2; receivables typically 60-75 days
items.quote: Currently, as it stands, we have about Rs. 71.5 crore approximately in trade receivables and we have an inventory of about Rs. 77.1 crores. Now, in terms of inventory, obviously, the inventory increases are there to accommodate greater sales in H2.

items.statement: Manufacturing cycle 30-45 days; target sales cycle ~100 days; current inventory days below target cycle as supply catching up to demand
items.quote: Because we are manufacturer to customer, that is, we are truly direct to customer, we have a manufacturing cycle, which is typically about 30 to 40 days in terms of manufacturing. Sometimes, for some products, it could be as high as 45 days as well. And then we have the sales cycle where the finished good is actually sold to the customer. Generally, we target to keep that at about 100 days.

items.statement: Marketing spend typically 7-10% of top line; performance marketing with ROI focus; pricing and marketing levers adjusted multiple times daily
items.quote: We typically target to keep that somewhere between 7% to 10% of our overall top line. Sometimes we have to go more aggressive, but in both cases, our pricing is also higher. But these things are very evolving.

items.statement: Catalog AI improved kids wear conversion by ~80 bps from 1.1-1.2% base to ~1.9-2%
items.quote: Generally, we have applied this in our kids wear segment for the brands that we do kids wear and we have seen a good success on application of this model, resulting in improved conversion by at least 80 basis points in total. So, and that is against the base of, say, 1.1% to 1.2%.

items.statement: Online and offline retail (e.g., Zudio) target different customer profiles; both growing at healthy double-digit rates
items.quote: I would look at them as different customer, different target audience, different customer profiles, to be very honest. And both of these areas, the one that you mentioned, such as video or even e-commerce online, are receiving very healthy double-digit growth. So, both are high growth areas.

items.statement: Online products available pan-India; offline pilot focused only on Bangalore based on sales data
items.quote: For online, as I said, it is Pan India. For offline, currently, we are focused on Bangalore.

items.statement: No plans to launch own premium brand this financial year; focused on Thomas Scott and premium licensed brands
items.quote: So, at the moment, there are no specific plans. It is an interesting proposition because we do have learnings in the premium segment. However, at the moment, at least for this financial year, we are focused on our own brand, which is Thomas Scott and our other brands specific with greater emphasis on the premium brands that we are working with.

items.statement: Revenue mix guidance: Thomas Scott 30-40% of top line; licensed brands remainder; contract manufacturing ~5% (could decline to 4%)
items.quote: Yes. So, generally, Thomas Scott would be between about 30% to 40% of the top line and the remaining would be other brands. About 5% would remain B2B. That 5% could go to 4% as well.

items.statement: Gurgaon handbag facility fire in Q2; production resumed in ~1 month; outsourced manufacturing interim; insurance claim filed; impact not material
items.quote: The impact that it had was primarily on handbags category because the specific facility in question manufactured handbags for us. The production is resumed, about and the first assumption happened in about a month. First set of assumptions happened in about a month from the fire.

items.statement: AI/tech team ~5-6% of workforce; not expected to expand rapidly; focus on internal applications for conversion, restocking, pricing, planning
items.quote: Generally, our investment in AI is investment in our overall technology team or tech partners who support us in creating these applications. This is not a very sizable investment. Again, it is a 5% or 6% team that does the development.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin target 13-14%, similar to FY25 level
items.quote: Our intention is to close the year with the EBITDA margin similar to last year's level, and we remain confident in that goal.

items.statement: Expect consistent quarter-by-quarter EBITDA margin upswing rather than sudden spike
items.quote: As Mr. Sagar mentioned, we anticipate a consistent quarter-by-quarter upswing rather than a sudden spike.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 operating EBITDA INR 111 crores at 10.7% margin, up 7% sequentially
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA for Q2 FY '26 reached INR111 crores, reflecting an EBITDA margin of 10.7%. On an absolute basis, this marks a 7% improvement over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Flow Control margin improved from 21% in Q1 to 23% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: First of all, flow control, as I said earlier to answering to somebody's question, we are still good. Q1 '26 was about 21% margin. And now this quarter, it is 23% margin.

items.statement: Dalmia subsidiary EBITDA margin improved from 8.7% in Q1 to 11.4% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Comparative to last quarter which was 7 -8%. So we have improved , last quarter was 8.7% EBITDA and this quarter, it is 11.4%.

items.statement: Steel and cement demand expected to hover around 4-6% growth in H2, similar to H1 outlook
items.quote: Demand, after talking to many big players of steel and cement, should be hovering around 4% to 6%. And outlook is almost similar to first half.

items.statement: Order book remains robust for upcoming quarters, particularly in steel sector with major mills confirming substantial capex plans
items.quote: Our order book remains robust for the upcoming quarters, particularly in the steel sector, where major mills have confirmed substantial capex expenditure plan.

items.statement: Cement segment shows strong momentum supported by upcoming large-scale expansions and scheduled plant turnarounds
items.quote: The Cement segment also shows strong momentum supported by upcoming large-scale expansions and scheduled plant turnarounds.

items.statement: FY26 capex budget INR 150 crores, INR 60 crores spent in H1, remainder in H2 with some spillover to next year
items.quote: So we had budgeted INR150 crores. We have spent INR 60 crores in H1. We aim to do the rest in the H2.

items.statement: Target 80-85% capacity utilization in next 2 years from current ~72%, no new plant expansion planned
items.quote: Yes, you're right, and we are having a planning to reach to a level of 80% to 85% capacity utilization in next 2 years' time. As of now, we will not do any capacity expansion.

items.statement: Received single-digit price increases in Flow Control (~28% of revenue) on long-term contracts, expected to sustain for next year
items.quote: We received mostly price hikes in the area of flow control, which is approximately 28% of our revenue. We are -- I mean, we basically got, let's say, single-digit price increases, and these are long-term contracts.

items.statement: Alumina inventory at high cost will clear by November, lower alumina prices to benefit next 4 months; magnesia prices up but recipe optimization to offset from December
items.quote: For margins, now onwards, alumina prices will be the market prices, whatever high alumina inventory was there, it will vanish in November numbers. So next 4 months, we will have advantage of lower price of alumina.

items.statement: Expect better product mix in upcoming quarters with higher-margin industrial orders and ladle business performance bonuses
items.quote: The second part is we are also expecting a better product mix because in the current quarter, we had cement high volumes. So this will also help us to improve our realization rates better.

items.statement: Gained market share in Flow Control from 22% to 30%+ in a major group from July, 8-10% market share gain in second half
items.quote: We got market share gain from July onwards, I would say, in one of the biggest group from 22% to 30+% now So likewise, in other groups also. So there is, I would say, 8% to 10% market share gain in Flow Control in second half of this year.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA 0.45x, higher due to working capital tied to revenue growth; record collections in October recovered Q2 shortfall
items.quote: Our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio is at 0.45x, which is higher than last quarter, majorly due to working capital tied to revenue growth.

items.statement: Key account payment delay resolved with record collections in October, H2 cash flows expected to normalize
items.quote: So then Sensitivity: Internal everything was streamlined. And fortunately in October, I think we have recovered everything. It was a record collection. I would not say the number, but it was a record collection ever

items.statement: Expect interest expenses to trend downward with continued impact of last year's debt reduction efforts
items.quote: We consider this to be manageable and with continued impact of last year's debt reduction efforts, we expect interest expenses to trend downward in the period ahead.

items.statement: 12% safeguard duty on specialty steel ended around 30th October, contributing to steel margin squeeze
items.quote: In addition, the 12% safeguard duty on specialty steel, which the Government of India had implemented about six months ago, is now over. As of around 30th October, there is no safeguard duty for steel industry.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue INR 1,035 crores (highest ever quarterly), up 8% QoQ and 19% YoY; shipment volume 141 KT, up 9% QoQ and 18% YoY
items.quote: Despite market headwinds, we achieved highest ever quarterly revenue from operations of INR 1,035 crores. This reflects a sequential growth of approximately 8% over Q1 FY '26 and a year-on-year increase of nearly 19% versus Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Dalmia subsidiary revenue INR 264 crores in Q2 FY26 vs INR 216 crores YoY; shipments 42 KT vs 35 KT QoQ
items.quote: To clarify the number, Q2 FY '26 was INR 264 crores and Q2 FY '25 was INR 216 crores. So there is a substantial increase in the revenue and also on the shipment, as we mentioned, 3 5 kilotons to 42 kilotons is what we have done.

items.statement: Ashwath Technologies integration progressing well; ANKRAL and Radex cement bricks product transfer from group technology completed
items.quote: We are also pleased to report that we have successfully completed the product transfer of ANKRAL and R adex cement bricks from our group technology into India. This will provide opportunities that will unlock further value for our shareholders. Our integration with Ashwath Technologies is also progressing well.

items.statement: Chinese steel overcapacity continues despite 2% annual production cuts; cheap subsidized exports via Southeast Asia persist
items.quote: Government of China has decided to reduce their steel production 2% every year. And by 2035, they want to reduce their steel production from 1 billion to 700 million, 750 million tons. But their own consumption is much lower than this. So in spite of reducing 2% steel production every year, it will not have any impact. They have overcapacity, still they keep on exporting the steel at a very cheap

items.statement: Induction furnace segment sluggish with 150 of 500+ customers reducing production due to monsoon and cheap imports from Vietnam, Thailand, China
items.quote: But that market is sluggish. I would say, in the last 4 -5 months out of, say, 500-plus customers, 150 customers have reduced their production temporarily because of monsoon and Cheap import from Vietnam, Thailand, China, etc.

items.statement: Green/eco-grade products (UREX, Resistal) at trial stage, material impact expected in 2-3 years; technology transfer to unlock value via capacity utilization, working capital, margin improvement
items.quote: It is a very initial stage as of now, Eco or green. These are trial stage things. It will not have a material impact on anything. It will take another 2 years to 3 years when we have a substantial business of these type of products.

items.statement: FY26 AUM target INR970 crore and disbursement target INR400 crore
items.quote: Financial year '26's AUM target was INR970 crore and the disbursement target is INR400 crore.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursement target INR150 crore each quarter
items.quote: Our target is INR150 crores, INR150 crores in both the quarters. Then whatever happens, we will do. We will disburse INR150 crores, INR150 crores in both the quarters as per the current situation.

items.statement: AUM target INR1,500 crore achievable by FY28
items.quote: We can reach in 2028.

items.statement: AUM target INR2,000-2,500 crore at peak branch productivity
items.quote: So the book will be around INR2,000 crores, INR2,500 crores

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to fall 2-5% over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So, it will fall around 2%, 5%. So, it will take 2, 3 quarters.

items.statement: Yield expected around 9-9.5% going forward
items.quote: It will be around 9. And this is also double digit. This is at 9.67 present. It will be around 9.5.

items.statement: Gross and Net NPA expected to remain around current levels by year end
items.quote: So we will not expect too much that it will go down, it will go around. It will be around this level.

items.statement: Loan book grew 33.21% YoY to INR867 crore in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our loan book, with a growth of 33.21% has become INR867 crore which was INR651 crore in Q2 of the previous year.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 85% YoY to INR117 crore in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Disbursement with a growth of 85% was INR117 crore which was INR 63 crore in Q2 of the previous year.

items.statement: New geographies contributed INR34 crore (Maharashtra), INR20 crore (Andhra Pradesh), INR18 crore (Karnataka) in last 6 months
items.value: 34 crore Maharashtra; 20 crore Andhra Pradesh; 18 crore Karnataka
items.quote: In the last 6 months, we have made a book worth INR34 crores in Maharashtra, INR20 crores in Andhra Pradesh, and INR18 crores in Karnataka.

items.statement: Borrowing cost 10.99%, lending rate 20%, spread 9%, NIM around 9%
items.quote: Borrowing cost has been 10.99% which was 11.03% in the previous Q2FY25. Credit cost has been 1.66% in Q2FY26, which was 1.81% in the previous Q2FY25. Lending rate has been 20% and spread has been 9%.

items.statement: Yield declined due to shift from LAP to housing loans (16-18% HL rate)
items.quote: Earlier, we had a higher percentage of LAP. Now that we have focused on HL, we do HL business between 16% to 18%. So, the rate has fallen a bit.

items.statement: Gross NPA 1.88%, Net NPA 0.64% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Gross NPA was 1.88% which was 1.96% in Q2FY25. Net NPA was 0.64% which was 0.59% in Q2FY25.
Our overall DPD is 1 plus DPD which is around 12%. And 30 plus DPD is 7.32%.

items.statement: Credit cost 1.66% in Q2 FY26 vs 1.81% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Credit cost has been 1.66% in Q2FY26, which was 1.81% in the previous Q2FY25.

items.statement: Issued INR50 crore NCD in Q2 and INR26 crore NCD this quarter; mutual fund invested INR50 crore in NCD
items.quote: In Q2, the company has issued INR50 crore NCD and in this quarter INR26 crore NCD. It is a matter of great joy that the mutual fund has also invested in the NCD of INR50 crore.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to decrease 2-3% to around 62%; PBT around 22%
items.quote: By reducing cost-to-income by 2%, 3%, we can do around 62%. PBT is around 22%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 disbursement target Rs.1,100-1,150 Cr; Q4 FY26 target Rs.1,350-1,400 Cr; FY26 AUM target Rs.16,200 Cr
items.quote: For December quarter, we are targeting a disbursement of close to about Rs.1,100 Crores to Rs.1,150 Crores. And March, we are targeting a disbursement of close to Rs.1,350 to Rs.1,400 Crores. With that I am confident of achieving Rs.16,200 Crores AUM price by this financial year end.

items.statement: GNPA target Rs.450 Cr by end of Q3 FY26; stage 2 assets target Rs.1,275 Cr; maintain PCR, spreads, NIMs at current levels
items.quote: And we are having a plan to reduce our GNPA from Rs.475 Crores to Rs.450 Crores in current quarter. And we are expecting reduction in stage two assets, Rs.1,275 Crores from Rs.1,325 Crores as end of September 2025. We i ntend to maintain provision coverage ratios, spreads and NIMs at level what we reported in the current

items.statement: FY28 AUM target Rs.25,000 Cr inclusive of organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: Yes, we have aggressive growth plans on both disbursement and A UM. That is on the organic side. We are also looking at going ahead with some book purchases, which is in the early stages. So, by and large, we should be reaching the guidance of 2028.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 disbursements Rs.1,069 Cr (highest ever); sanctions Rs.1,206 Cr; loan book Rs.15,033 Cr, up 8% YoY
items.quote: We have disbursed Rs.1069 Crores in the Q2 of current financial year as against Rs.867 Crores in Q2 of FY2025 and Rs.829 Crores in the previous quarter. I am happy to say that this is the highest ever disbursement in a quarter we have achieved in the history of our company.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 NIM 5.5%, spread 3.4%, yield on assets 12.1%; housing loan yield 11.17%, non-housing 13.55%
items.quote: Our NIM for quarter Q2 FY 2026 was at 5.5%. The company has been able to maintain a spread of 3.4% by rising yield to 12.1% despite its stiff competition at our pricing levels.

items.statement: Reduced MLR to 10% from 10.10% effective July 1, 2025; benefit passed to customers at end of June 2025
items.quote: We have reduced our benchmark lending rate, it is called marginal lending rate to 10% from 10.10% with effective from July 1, 2025. Since our assets are re-priced on a quarterly basis, the benefit of the MLR cut passed on to all the customers at the end of June 2025.

items.statement: Rs.6,000 Cr of bank borrowings due for re-pricing in next three months; expect 10-15 bps reduction in cost of funds over Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: Approximately Rs.6,000 Crores of bank borrowings are scheduled for re -pricing over the next three months. And as a result, we anticipate further reduction in overall cost of funds.

items.statement: GNPA Rs.475 Cr (3.16%) vs Rs.552 Cr YoY; NNPA Rs.225 Cr (1.50%); PCR 52.54%; stage 2 assets Rs.1,323 Cr vs Rs.1,422 Cr QoQ; new book GNPA ~1.2%
items.quote: GNP A amounted to Rs.475 Crores as end of September 2025 at 3.16% as against Rs.552 Crores as of September 2024 and Rs.485 Crores as of June 2025. The net NPA stood at Rs.225 Crores at 1.50%. We have a total provision of Rs.375 Crores with the provision coverage ratio of 52.54% for stage three assets.

items.statement: COVID restructured book Rs.790 Cr; Rs.121 Cr slipped to NPA; Rs.408 Cr in various stages; recovery Rs.6 Cr from written-off accounts in FY26, expect Rs.8-9 Cr more
items.quote: During the COVID period, we restructured loans about close to Rs.790 Crores, of which Rs.121 Crores already slipped in the NPA, remaining Rs.408 Crores are various stages of asset.

items.statement: Plan to add 10-15 branches in FY26 (4-5 in West, 2-3 in Karnataka, rest in Tamil Nadu, AP, Telangana); currently 234 touch points (203 branches, 31 satellites, 2 recovery)
items.quote: Sir, we are looking at another 10 to 15 more branches , which is already in the offing. So this financial year, we may be adding another 10 more branches.

items.statement: Prepaid Rs.200 Cr to Repco Bank in Q2 FY26; plan to repay Rs.300-400 Cr more in H2 FY26 to reduce exposure; issued Rs.150 Cr commercial paper in June; NHB refinance sanction Rs.150 Cr utilized; fresh proposal Rs.500-750 Cr submitted
items.quote: In last quarter, we repaid about Rs.200 Crores to them. We have requested them to reduce the cost of funds. We are having a plan to reduce exposures with Repco Bank by availing lower costs from other banking system.

items.statement: Revised incentive policy effective April 1, 2025 aligned to industry; silver jubilee honorarium; 32-35 branches added in 24 months; promotions after 2-2.5 years; hired experienced sales, recovery, collections staff
items.quote: Yes, we have realigned what you call incentive policy in line with industry practices to motivate employee to do more business, more sales, more recovery, more disbursements, which has resulted in the numbers. This quarter we disbursed about Rs.1060 Crores, which is our all -time high disbursements.

items.statement: ROA 2.9% Q2 FY26 (guidance 2.9-3% for FY26); ROE 13.5%; cost-to-income 28.4% (26.34% adjusted for one-offs); average ticket size incremental Rs.23-24 lakh
