items.quote: Our ROA stood at 2.9% and ROE at 13.5% for Q2 FY 2026. Cost to income ratio for the quarter stood at 28.4%.

items.statement: Interim dividend declared for silver jubilee year; board to consider higher payout (currently ~Rs.20 Cr on Rs.400 Cr PAT)
items.quote: Mr. Mundra, we have already declared interim dividend for this year for silver jubilee.

items.statement: Book purchases early stage; FY26 inorganic minimal Rs.30-40 Cr; FY28 target Rs.25,000 Cr includes inorganic; prior experience with three tranches performing well
items.quote: We are not going for any book buying for current financial year. It may around Rs.30 Crores to Rs.40 Crores kind of book we are planning to buy, not in a big way. We want to start that, we want to explore that avenue also.

items.statement: Portfolio runoff increasing due to higher non-housing share (shorter tenor 6-6.5 years vs 8.5-9 years for housing); must run faster to maintain growth
items.quote: You are right Rajiv. That is a challenge we are facing on day in and day out. Going forward also, yes, my book attrition will happen, but we will have to run fast even to be in the same place. Yes.

items.statement: NHB reclassification: loans for reimbursement and >2 kitchen units now non-housing; non-housing share up due to regulatory changes
items.quote: So net fee also , couple of months before they came with the clarifications that loans given for the purpose of a re imbursement thing, we should classify as a non -HL. Earlier, we used to classify such loans as a housing loan. Now, as per the NH B clarifications and advices, such loans are classified as a non -HL.

items.statement: Issued Rs.150 Cr commercial paper in June; positive response for CPs and NCDs from banks, MFs, institutions
items.quote: In June, we successfully issued Rs.150 Crores of commercial paper. Following our entry into the capital market after a long time, we received a positive response from banks, mutual funds and other institutional investors for both commercial papers and NCDs.

items.statement: Sanctions Rs.1,206 Cr vs disbursements Rs.1,069 Cr in Q2 FY26; Rs.150 Cr gap from sanctioned-but-not-disbursed (construction-linked)
items.quote: during the September quarter ended our sanctions was close to about Rs.1206 Crores w hereas we have done only disbursement of about Rs.1070-odd crore. So there is a gap of about Rs.150 Crores gap is there. Sanctioned but not dispersed in September quarter alone

items.statement: Expect ~30% QoQ disbursement growth from branches opened in last 24 months; BT-outs under control, in line with prior quarters
items.quote: The branches what I opened in last 24 months started to giving substantial amount of disbursements. I am expecting around another 30% of increase in quarter -on-quarter disbursements.

items.statement: ESOP discussion started at board level; will update on progress
items.quote: Thank you so much. Thank you. Akash for supporting us this ESOP matter also premium discussion started at board level. Let us see how it goes. We will keep you posted on the update.

items.statement: Management targets around 15% revenue growth for FY26 and 15-20% for FY27 if products click and monsoon behaves
items.quote: We are trying to clock 15% over last year. That is our internal target.

items.statement: Management expects to cross INR400 crore revenue in FY26 and target INR500 crore in FY27 with 15% and 20% growth respectively
items.quote: If this year, we cross INR400 crores, then maybe next year, we can buy for INR500 crores, but that would mean 15% this year and 20% next year.

items.statement: Cotton volumes grew 6% YoY to 1.11 million packets with 26.3% value growth driven by premium products
items.quote: cotton reported a steady growth of around 6% Y-o-Y in volume, reaching 1.11 million packets, while the growth in value is almost 26.3%

items.statement: Maize volumes grew 7.3% YoY in H1 with 17% recovery driven by government focus on corn for fuel and strong hybrid performance
items.quote: Maize, a major crop even during this H1 shows a strong growth of 7.3% in quantity Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Vegetable seeds segment grew 25% YoY in value driven by expanding market reach and strong farmer demand
items.quote: vegetable seeds continue to be our fastest-growing segment, delivering almost 25% Y-o-Y value growth

items.statement: Bajra volumes declined 5-6% due to erratic rainfall timing but government focus expected to drive future growth
items.quote: It's hardly 5% or 6% decline in the bajra market. And in future, the way government is focusing on bajra crop, right, definitely, we are sure that bajra will go up significantly.

items.statement: Gross margins maintained at 52-54% average; EBITDA margin compressed due to enhanced marketing schemes to drive sales
items.quote: We have always been maintaining the gross margins around 52% to 54% on an average moving left, right, okay? But in order to clock enhanced sales, our marketing people hav e to give enhanced schemes to the

items.statement: EBITDA margin reduction is temporary; expected to improve once new products stabilize and marketing credits reduce
items.quote: once the marketing gets stabilized with new products, automatically, the credit that goes to the market, reduces and as a result, the EBITDA and the net profit margin go up

items.statement: INR100 crores of advanced bookings lying in books not yet adjusted against receivables
items.quote: we have around INR100 crores of advanced booking lying in our books, which has not yet been adjusted against our debit balances receivable

items.statement: Working capital increased to INR4,134.69 million from INR2,837.45 million due to higher receivables and inventory; expected to normalize with Rabi sales and advanced booking adjustment
items.quote: The working capital increased from INR2,837.45 million in H1 FY '26 '25 to INR4,134.69 million in H1 FY '26, primarily due to increase in receivables from the customers and the increase in the inventory.

items.statement: Debtors to reduce through recoveries and INR100 crore advanced booking adjustment; inventory to deplete with Rabi and Kharif 2026 sales
items.quote: the debtors will be reduced 2 ways: one, by recoveries from the market. Secondly, we have around INR100 crores of advanced booking lying in our books, which has not yet been adjusted against our debit balances receivable.

items.statement: Cotton and paddy together account for 74% of H1 revenue; management aims for 60-40 Kharif-Rabi split but portfolio tilting toward 70-30 H1-H2
items.quote: cotton and paddy together accounted for almost 74% in H1 revenue

items.statement: Hybrid paddy mix approximately 40% volume, 60% value; non-hybrid 60% volume, 40% value
items.quote: quantity-wise, it will be, say, 40-60 and value-wise, it will be 60-40

items.statement: No bad debt risk as company sells to distributors who handle farmer collections; distributors are prudent in shifting goods
items.quote: there is no question of bad debt because we are dealing not with farmers we are selling the seeds to our distributors and distributors then take care of the sale and also collection from the farmers

items.statement: Illegal BT and RRF cotton spreading, undermining organized sector; industry urging government to regularize RRF trade
items.quote: the industry continues to be impacted by the spread of illegal BT cotton, illegal RRF cotton, which Nath Bio-Genes ( undermines the organized

items.statement: Nath Bio-Genes gained 10-15% market share in Maharashtra and grew in Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka despite organized sector decline
items.quote: we, along with other 2, 3 small companies, we have only grown. Other companies are not growing because of our product performance, right? So our market share has been increased. And definitely, whatever we had -- I'm not sure about the numbers, but we have grown around 10% to 15% in Maharashtra only.

items.statement: GM cultivation in India only permitted for cotton since 2006; no new traits approved; GM import for consumption separate from cultivation approval
items.quote: the last approval for GM trait was in 2006. There has been not even a new trait in cotton allowed since 2006. So that's a different process. This is to allow GM -- it's a grown commodity to be imported into the country

items.statement: Aurangabad land not for sale; retained for seed cultivation operations
items.quote: Aurangabad land is not for sale. It is with us. It is going to continue with us. It is only appreciated and valued not to be put to any other use.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV progressing well with product testing, seed production, and marketing structure development; expansion into new crops planned
items.quote: Some of our products which are tested last season have performed exceedingly well. Now we are going for parallelly production of the same seed also in Uzbekistan. We're also now working on creating a marketing structure to take these seeds to the farmers there.

items.statement: R&D team has 12 products under Plant Varieties Protection Act registration; strategy to register all demo-stage products
items.quote: There are about 12 under registration, sir. And we have planned -- we have made a strategy now, whichever is going to enter in demo stage, we will send them for registration.

items.statement: R&D focusing on heat tolerance, abiotic stress (no spray/no irrigation trials), biotic stress hotspots; breakthroughs in okra, tomato, gourd disease resistance
items.quote: we also have a very specialized program on heat tolerance because Nath B io-Genes considers heat tolerance as a trait of global importance and we are working on that. In addition to that, with the international institutes, we are working with them to develop and get the germplasm for seed tolerance

items.statement: Extended monsoon impacted cotton sentiment negatively; maize benefited; bajra uncertain due to rainfed nature; no major cropping pattern shift observed
items.quote: cotton was impacted a little negatively in terms of sentiment. Maize was impacted positively. Bajra continues to be uncertain crop all around because it goes into areas where rainfall is not sure all around.

items.statement: Cost of production rising 5-10% annually; cotton prices government-controlled compressing margins; diversified portfolio offsets impact
items.quote: cost of production is definitely increasing, and it increases constantl y. The reason being that the land available is always less than the demand of the cotton production

items.statement: Company paying dividends for 4-5 consecutive years; dividend percentage may increase with profit improvement
items.quote: the company is giving dividends year after year. I think this was the fourth or fifth year in which we have given dividends. And if the profits improve, maybe the dividend percentage will also increase.

items.statement: H2 FY26 expected positive for vegetable seeds (next 5-6 months) and PNS due to good rainfall and water levels
items.quote: next 5 months will be vegetable seed sales. And definitely, it will help and it will increase the vegetable sales next 5 months.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 20.4%, up 460 bps YoY, driven by favorable product mix, higher capacity utilization, disciplined pricing and plant efficiency gains.
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved sharply to 20.4% up by 460 basis points from 15.8% in Q2 FY '25. This expansion reflects a favorable product mix, higher capacity utilization, disciplined pricing and efficiency gain at the plant levels.

items.statement: Management targets full-year FY26 EBITDA margin of 20% after achieving 20.4% in Q2, up from earlier 17-18% guidance.
items.quote: Yes, considering the results what we have got after implementing our product mix and better margin -- product offerings, we will definitely be achieving the EBITDA margin of 20% for the whole year.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book for windows, doors and modular furniture stands at over INR125 crores, with INR127 crores current book split as INR32 crores modular furniture and INR95 crores windows/doors.
items.quote: Even today also we are having more than INR125 crores of unexecuted order book for the window and doors and Modular Furniture division.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline is 18-24 months; all contracts are fixed price.
items.quote: About 60% of our revenue comes from the day-to-day B2B distribution business where there is long-term orders. So, execution time for this order as per the current stages of different sites, maybe around 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: FY26 capex projected at INR15-18 crores, focused on new product offerings like WPC doors and southern India expansion, not existing capacity.
items.quote: This year, we are projecting around INR15 crores to INR18 crores spending in this financial year.

items.statement: WPC door manufacturing facility implementation underway in Q3 FY26, commercial launch preponed to Q4 FY26 from earlier Q1 FY27 target.
items.quote: Regarding the capex front, as we mentioned in earlier calls also, we are initially working on the WPC doors production lines and which is going to be implemented in this quarter. And the product is expected to be launched commercially. And in the fourth quarter of this financial year, we are planning to launch this product.

items.statement: PVC extrusion capacity 24,000 MT/annum at 60%+ utilization; uPVC windows/doors fabrication capacity 30 lakh sq ft at 35-40% utilization.
items.quote: Yes, it's up to 60% plus in this quarter because this quarter has been better capacity utilization as compared to the previous quarters.

items.statement: PVC extrusion expected to reach 80-85% utilization by end of FY27; windows/doors fabrication timeline for 80% unclear but growing at 20-25% annually.
items.quote: By end of the next financial year, the kind of the growth what we are getting and the market response for all our current existing offerings. So end of the next financial year, we can be at that level.

items.statement: Healthy demand from residential real estate momentum in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, renovation-led refurbishments, and structural shift to uPVC windows/doors and modular furniture.
items.quote: The residential real estate sector maintained its momentum with sustained project launches and strong sales in Tier 1 cities, along with healthy activity in the mature Tier 2 micro markets. This steady pace of the development has continued to drive demand for the interior building materials and finishing solutions.

items.statement: Modular furniture contributed 18% of H1 revenue; PVC profiles, uPVC windows/doors fabrication 82%. Fluted/soffit panels done >INR25 crores in H1, targeting INR50 crores+ for full year.
items.quote: See, H1, the Modular Furniture contributed about 18% of our overall business and remaining 82% came from the PVC profile distribution and this fabrication of uPVC windows and doors.

items.statement: Premium product focus across all verticals: fluted/soffit panels, uPVC furniture profiles, end-to-end modular solutions for high-end bungalows, premium uPVC/aluminum system windows.
items.quote: In all three product verticals of our company, we have added certain solutions. The first one in the extruded PVC profile distribution that, especially that fluted and soffit panels and uPVC furniture profiles. And Modular Furniture, that offering our end-to-end solutions to the interior designers and architect connects.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable at current levels, no major hikes foreseen near-term; Q2 margin driven more by product mix than input cost benefit.
items.quote: See, the input prices remain stable, I would say. In the first quarter, it was purely -- majorly because of the price benefit which we got. But in the second quarter, it is more from the product mix strategy which we opted to go into the premium segment for certain products.

items.statement: Expanding dealer/distribution network across all Indian states, aggressive trade exhibition participation driving lead generation in retail and project channels.
items.quote: We are already placed in almost all the states throughout India, and we are aggressively participating in the trade exhibitions to expand our brand visibility and to attract more and more large distributors.

items.statement: Two new Studio Arezzo outlets planned in H2 FY26: one in Bangalore (work started, completion by end H2), second location undecided.
items.quote: outlets are being planned in H2. So we are still on, on that. So, South India... Dharmil: And where will that be? Hitesh Agrawal: Yes, one is the South India, basically in Bangalore, we are planning. And second one is not yet decided

items.statement: No new competitive pressure from large players like Supreme Industries; revenue growth shortfall due to selective approach avoiding low-margin segments, not competition.
items.quote: To be very frank, till now we have not come across with any kind of a competition with the new entrants. Revenue front pressure or say that non -achievement of the projected or targeted revenue growth is not linked to any kind of competition.

items.statement: Exports ~2.5% of revenue, limited to modular furniture; dedicated export team appointed, targeting results in H1 FY27, no overseas exhibitions booked yet.
items.quote: Exports is not a big bite for us. In fact, for the last year also, it was just around 2.5% of total revenue. So it's on the almost same level, because export, we are doing only in the Modular Furniture division.

items.statement: Receivables spike in H1 is interim; full-year working capital cycle expected to improve vs prior year, managing inventory/debtors growth below revenue growth.
items.quote: Yes, it would be better than the last previous year basically. We are continuously working on the better working capital management. So with the increase of the top line, we are focused on not allowing to increase the inventory or the debtors in the same ratio.

items.statement: No specific top-line guidance for FY26, but confident of achieving 20%+ growth; targeting 20-25% annual growth for next 3-4 years including FY27.
items.quote: we are targeting the growth percentage what we have discussed earlier of 2025 year's annual growth for next 3 to 4 years. And we are on the right track and continuous working is happ ening on the top line front also

items.statement: Fluted and soffit panels revenue >INR25 crores in H1 FY26, targeting INR50 crores+ for full year FY26.
items.quote: For fluted and soffit panels, we have already done more than INR25 crores in first half. And for the whole year, we are targeting INR50 crores plus.

items.statement: NSE listing planned once eligibility criteria met, potentially by end of FY26; will consult merchant bankers thereafter.
items.quote: Yes, we mentioned in past also, we are having the plan. Once we are eligible for that -- NSE is having certain criteria. Maybe by end of this financial year, we will fulfill the criteria set by the NSE.

items.statement: No winter-related construction restrictions seen so far in Q3 FY26; optimistic no repeat of last year's extended winter impact on Delhi NCR activity.
items.quote: Not at this stage. Even today also, we have already passed half of the quarter as there is no restrictions we have faced. So, activities are normally happening and we don't forecast at this stage.

items.statement: Open to contract manufacturing for other brands in modular furniture given sufficient capacity, but no active discussions currently.
items.quote: To be very frank, as of now, we are not into any discussion. But yes, we are open because we have sufficient capacity in that front also. If some good opportunity comes, so we can take a call on that at that time.

items.statement: D-Stona brand (profiles, moldings, embossed panels) performing well, integrated with PVC extrusion capacity, new solutions added regularly.
items.quote: See, D-Stona is also doing good. It's a part of Polywood basically. It comes from the extrusion business vertical. So in D -Stona, we make the different type of profiles, basically that in the shape of the seats or the moldings.

items.statement: Company was first in India to launch fluted panel manufacturing 2 years ago and soffit panels; regular new product development ongoing.
items.quote: We have been doing this regularly. In fact, that we were the first one to launch the fluted panel manufacturing in India when we launched 2 years back in India. Then soffit also, we were the first one to start manufacturing in India.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 10-15% for FY26; margin expansion of at least 200 bps expected
items.quote: And now as you rightly mentioned about the progress of winter, it is doing good as far as Northern and Central and Eastern India is concerned. And there is every possibility that we may revise ow guidance in the third quarter once we have winter salcs in our hand, but that we can only do in the third quarter con call. As of now, we stand at our guidance of 10% to 15

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded to 16.73% from 12.88% YoY driven by sales growth, raw material price stability, price hikes, and reduced discount sales
items.quote: No, no. Basically, there have been 2 reasons for the margin cxpansion. The first reason, as you rightly mentioned, is the sales growth. And the second reason is that the raw material price was stabilized, but we took the hike in our product prices. So that is also reflecting in the margins. And thirdly, we took some steps to reduce our discount sales and refurns also

items.statement: Expect at least 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion for FY26 vs FY25; may revise guidance after Q3
items.quote: And we expeet that over the last year, we should have at least 200 basis point margin cxpansion as far as this current year is concerned. But again, this guidance can be revised once we have third quarter sales in our hand, which is doing very well

items.statement: Apparel summer-winter mix shifting toward 46:54 from 60:40 six years ago; targeting 50:50 in 1-2 years
items.quote: So this year, we should be touching ~- on apparels, I'm talking about, it should be around 46 summer's and 54 winter. And we see that going ahead. In next 1 or 2 years, it should even out, 50-50, summer and winter contribution.

items.statement: Strong summer trade show bookings with mid-teens volume growth; winter secondary sales and repeats indicate good season progress
items.quote: And as far as trade show for summer, which happened almost 2 months back, we got a very strong demand in summer. I a double-digit volume growth in summer as well. So that is giving us the confidence to revise our guidance going forward in the next quarter.

items.statement: Targeting at least 10% reduction in working capital days by end of FY26 via increased distributor sales (30-day payment) and merchandising rationalization
items.quote: Yes. So we arc pretty sure that this year, there would be at least 10% reduction in the working capital days as we end this financial year. So we are working on the working capital as well as debtor days also

items.statement: Cloak & Decker at 17 stores with 8 in pipeline; targeting 25 stores by end FY26 and 25-30 more in FY27; aim INR 100 crore brand in 3-4 years
items.quote: Yes. So there have been inquiries. Already, we have around 17 stores of Cloak & Decker and another 8 are in pipeline. So we'll have 25 stores by the end of this financial year. And for next financial year, we intend to open another 25 to 30 stores.

items.statement: Winter inventories nearly empty at warehouses; secondary sales strong; expecting fewer returns and less EOSS this year
items.quote: So let me give you a very good news that our inventorics are almost cmpty as far as our warchouses are conceed and sccondary sales are happening. So we're pretty sure that the inventory at our EBOs, inventory at our LFS channel would be least as compared to many of the previous years

items.statement: Cotton prices stable for 1.5 years; took 7-8% price hike benefiting margins
items.quote: Fortunately, cotton prices are very stable, and they have not moved much in the last 1.5 years. And even today also, the prices are almost same, which was last financial year. But we have taken a hike of around 7% to 8%.

items.statement: MBO/SIS payment cycle ~75 days; LFS/online/EBO sales-based payment within 30 days; no returns from MBO/SIS
items.quote: MBO is around 75 days. And LFS, online EBO, sales-based. When they sell it, then they give within 30 days.

items.statement: Dividend-paying company since inception; will continue dividends and invest in solar capex; aim to generate returns on cash and distribute to shareholders
items.quote: We have been a dividend-paying company since inception. So definitely, one part would be to give dividend or whatever Board decides. And scoondly, as I said carlicr also that we'll be investing some money in the solar power also. So that would also nced some capex

items.statement: Main competitors: Madura, Raymond, Arvind brands; some new entrants but some brands shut down; no significant new competition in category
items.quote: Sir, yes, competitors are basically Madura brands, Raymond brands and Arvind brands and some of the new cntrants also, but there are some brands which have shut down also. So the comptition is basically more from these brands only

items.statement: No concrete government policy support for textile/apparel sector despite high labor intensity and low capex needs
items.quote: t think government has taken any initiative to support textiles or apparels as of now. No policy - 1o good policy has come as of now. And believe me, we have been telling this government a lot of times that this is the most least capex and high labor-intensive industry

items.statement: Volume-value growth split expected at 60:40 for FY26; volume guidance for winter to be given after January sales end
items.quote: But overall, we already have told that we should be growing 10% to 15% in this financial year. And the volume and value growth should be around 60% to 40%, 60% volume and 40% value.

items.statement: Increased distributor sales with 30-day payment terms (vs 75 days for some retailers) to reduce working capital days
items.quote: what we did is that we actually increased our distributor sales, and we take payment from distributors in 30 days, which we used to take from 75 days in some of our retailers

items.statement: Committed to open 40-45 EBOs across India with emphasis on Western and Southern regions
items.quote: We remain focused on expanding our retail footprint and firmly committed to open 40 to 45 EBOs across India with a strategic cmphasis on Western and Southern

items.statement: Partnered with quick commerce platforms Blinkit, Swiggy, Zepto for 30-minute delivery; Salesforce collaboration for digital transformation
items.quote: To enhance customer convenience and reach, we have partnered with quick commerce platforms such as Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto to enable quick deliverics within 30 minutes. Additionally, our strategic collaboration with Salesforce is helping us streamlining our operations, elevate our customer experience and building long-term brand loyalty through digital transformation

items.statement: Rockit brand consistent performance; Home Textile robust growth across categories; online sales strong momentum via own website
items.quote: We saw a strong rebound in the sales across most categorics. Our Rockit brand delivered yet another quarter of consistent performance. The Home Textile segment also maintained its robust growth trajectory, supported by healthy demand across all

items.statement: Merchandising rationalization enabling inter-location stock transfers to reduce stuck inventory and improve payment cycles
items.quote: And secondly, what we did is that we rationalized our merchandising also. So carlier, Wwe were not transferring goods from one location to another location when it was needed. So that will again -- otherwise, our goods kept stuck on one location and that reduced basically payment cyele also

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross profit margin expanded 197 bps YoY to 24.1% due to stable raw material prices
items.quote: Gross profit margin stood at 24.1%, expanded by 197 basis points over year-to-year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross profit margin expanded 233 bps YoY to 25.3%
items.quote: Gross profit margins increased by 233 basis points to 25.3%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 82 bps YoY to 10.4%
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 10.4%, expanded by 82 basis points on year-to-year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps YoY to 11.1%
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 FY '26 was INR134.9 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.1%, an increase of 70 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread declined INR7/kg YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: So cotton yarn spread year-on-year, I think it has gone down by almost INR7 a kg, the spread.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread was INR120/kg in Q2 FY26 vs INR125/kg in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So yarn spread -- the cotton yarn spread for this quarter was about INR120 vis-a-vis INR125 in the last quarter.

items.statement: Cotton yarn realization was INR272/kg in Q2 FY26 vs INR277/kg in Q1 FY26
items.quote: It was around -- cotton yarn was around INR272 in this quarter and about INR277 in last quarter.

items.statement: Expect similar or slightly better margins in H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26
items.quote: And about the margins, we expect similar or slightly better margins in the next 6 months.

items.statement: Odisha plant expected to be 4-5% more competitive at EBITDA level
items.quote: So we expect that Odisha to be more competitive by 4% to 5% at the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Odisha capex on schedule, land possession obtained, ground breaking expected in 30-40 days
items.quote: We have got the possession of land, and we have applied for all the requisite permissions and we expect to break ground in the next 30 to 40 days.

items.statement: Solar capex on schedule, 40 MW power expected from 1st March
items.quote: Our solar capex is also going as per schedule, and we expect to start getting 40-megawatt power from 1st March onwards.

items.statement: Odisha capex estimated at slightly less than INR1,000 crores
items.quote: Yes, a little less than that, but in the ballpark.

items.statement: No significant capex plans beyond Odisha plant, only INR20-30 crores modernization
items.quote: There will be like small changes, small modernization capex, maybe INR20-INR30 crores, which will be happening other than the normal scheduled maintenance.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 capacity utilization at 96%, among highest in industry
items.quote: As of Q2 FY '26, we stand at capacity utilization of 96% among the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Odisha plant to add 40% incremental spindle capacity, commissioning targeted Sep-Oct 2026
items.quote: That's the plan. That's the plan right now. So once we break the ground and start in the earnest, then we can have more tighter deadlines.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 11% YoY to INR334.2 crores in Q2 FY26, export share rose to 53% from 46%
items.quote: Shares of export in the revenue is approximately INR334.2 crores, delivering a growth of 11% in export front for the quarter with the share of export sales rising to 53% in Q2 FY '26 from 46% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: H1 FY26 export revenue grew 15% YoY to INR675.4 crores
items.quote: The export contribution increased from INR 589.5 Crores in H1 FY25 to INR 675.4crores in H1 FY '26, an increase of 15% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Domestic demand muted due to higher US tariffs and global macro uncertainty
items.quote: Domestic demand was muted because of higher U.S. tariffs and uncertainty about the global macro situation.

items.statement: Export demand held up but at cost of lower margins
items.quote: Export demand held up in the last quarter, but at the cost of lower margins.

items.statement: Demand flat in Q3 FY26 so far, small domestic bump-up in last 15-20 days, export slightly sluggish
items.quote: So yes, so demand has been pretty flat, I would say, like we generally see a lot of bump up in demand in these times, but the demand has been pretty flat. We see a small bump up in domestic demand in last 15, 20 days, which generally happens after Diwali. And we are seeing that play out. But export demand is slightly sluggish than what it was a month back.

items.statement: Bangladesh demand consistent for last year, may be muted for 2-3 months due to elections
items.quote: Demand from Bangladesh has been pretty good for last 1 year. Every month is almost a record from India. So the demand has been pretty consistent for last 1 year, and we expect the demand to remain same, maybe a little muted going forward for 2, 3 months because of the election.

items.statement: Power cost 7-8% higher in Q2 FY26 due to seasonal tariff changes, expected to normalize in Q3
items.quote: The night tariff, which is withdrawn during these times and peak hour is more because of that, power is slightly higher by 7%, 8% in this quarter. I think we will come back to the normal level in this quarter.

items.statement: Rooftop solar saving ~1% of revenue, SPV solar to start from 1st March
items.quote: And the saving from the rooftop, which we already have is around about 1% of the revenue.

items.statement: Government removed import duty on cotton, lowering Indian prices and reducing disparity with international prices
items.quote: There was a welcome step by the government to remove the import duty on cotton, which has been a big relief. As a result of this, Indian prices have also come down and the disparity between international and Indian prices have significantly lowered.

items.statement: Cotton crop estimated 2-3% lower YoY, consumption down 3-4%, imports up 30%, closing stock 80-85 lakh bales
items.quote: And we are expecting a good closing stock of about 80 lakh to 85 lakh days, which will be a historic high barring the COVID year.

items.statement: Cotton inventory higher than usual in Sep due to preponed stocking from duty-free import window until Dec
items.quote: So this year, the inventory was a little higher than usual because of higher imports because the government had relaxed the duty on cotton for until December. So we -- some stocking, which we generally do in November, December, January, February was preponed because of that.

items.statement: GST on garments lowered, expected to boost domestic garment demand
items.quote: Another positive step by the government was lowering of GST on garments. We are expecting this to give a boost to the demand for garments in the coming future.

items.statement: GST rationalization on polyester fiber (18% to lower) and 100% synthetic (12% to 5%) positive for synthetic consumption
items.quote: It was just that the polyester fiber was taxed at 18%, which has been rationalized, which brings down the investment -- brings down the investment in the polyester fiber. And if you talk about the 100% synthetic, yes, the cut has been almost from 12%, it has come down to 5%.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing reduced ~INR50 crores vs Mar'25, gross debt/equity improved to 0.48 from 0.58
items.quote: Company continues to work on reducing the interest outlay going forward as short-term borrowing reduced by approximately INR50 crores as on date as compared to March '25. The gross debt to equity now stands at 0.48 as opposed to 0.58 as of March'25.

items.statement: Plan to repay INR70 crores long-term debt in next 1 year, INR140 crores in next 15-16 months from existing ~INR300 crores
items.quote: We'll be paying off around INR140 crores in next 15 to 16 months from the existing, I think, around INR300 crores.

items.statement: Odisha capex funding: INR300-350 crores internal accruals, rest debt
items.quote: So it's around INR300- INR350 crores of internal accruals which we are planning to deploy in this new project, and rest will be through debt.

items.statement: Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales merger to formalize by end of FY26
items.quote: That will be formalized by -- before the end of the year -- this financial year.

items.statement: Expect flattish revenue in H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26 (no incremental revenue due to full capacity)
items.quote: So we expect to -- the revenue we expect to be the same as it was in this half -- in first half. We don't see any incremental revenue coming in because most of our -- we are working at full capacity.

items.statement: Expect flattish top line for next 12 months barring price increases
items.quote: So top line, we don't see any much improvement other than maybe if the prices go up. So we see a flattish top line for next 12 months other than any bump up in the price.

items.statement: US tariffs at 50% on India biggest dampener; if removed, margins would improve
items.quote: See we think the biggest dampener right now is the tariff from India, which are at 50%. So we are giving this guidance based on that it remains like that. But if the tariffs go, then things will definitely improve.

items.statement: Import duty relief on cotton until Dec only, 50% chance of extension, US-India trade deal may bring cotton exemption
items.quote: there is a 50% chance that this might get extended. And there is another thing that with the U.S., India trade deal, it might happen. So there might be some exemption from U.S. cotton

items.statement: Bangladesh accounts for ~60% of exports
items.quote: I don't have the figure right now, but it should be around 60%.

items.statement: Interest cost increased due to INR3 crores forex fluctuation (Ind AS), actual outflow INR9 crores, expected reversal next quarter
items.quote: So yes, you're right, but that was mainly because of the forex fluctuation. So our actual outflow was less than last quarter. It was about INR9 crores, but INR3 crores was the forex fluctuation, which was put into this account because of the Ind AS entry. If the forex is stabilized and it will be -- the entry will be reversed in the next quarter.

items.statement: Fabric/garmenting only 6-7% of top line by year-end, margins better but small scale
items.quote: It would be like 6%, 7% of our top line once -- by the end of the year, I think when we own those companies.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement approved by shareholders; MCA approval expected by December 2025
items.quote: We are expecting approval of the scheme by December 2025.

items.statement: Domestic PNG customers grew to 23.28 lakh; added 0.27 lakh commissioned and 0.34 lakh registered in Q2 FY26
items.quote: GGL has added 0.27 lakh commissioned customers in Q2 FY '26 and registered 0.34 lakh customers in Q2 FY '26 despite of monsoon season.

items.statement: Signed gas sales agreement with Bathinda Military Station for PNG supply to 11,300 residential quarters
items.quote: GGL has signed a gas sales agreement with Bathinda Military Station, which is one of the largest military bases in India, for the supply of PNG to over 11,300 residential quarters.

items.statement: Industrial sales volume 4.34 MMSCMD in Q2 FY26, down 8% QoQ; Morbi volume 2.13 MMSCMD, non-Morbi 2.22 MMSCMD
items.quote: In the industrial segment, sales volume was 4.34 MMSCMD for the quarter ended 30th September 2025, whereas the sales volume during the previous quarter was 4.71 MMSCMD, an overall decrease of approximately 8%.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial volume grew 1% QoQ and 8% YoY to 2.22 MMSCMD
items.quote: The non-Morbi volume of 2.22 MMSCMD for the quarter ended 30th September 2025 has grown from 2.20 MMSCMD during the previous quarter. That is an increase of approximately 1%.

items.statement: Reduced industrial gas price by INR 3.25/SCM effective August 1, 2025; maintained gas premium over propane at INR 4-5/SCM
items.quote: The reduction in spot RLNG prices and crude prices during the quarter enabled GGL to reduce the prices in the industrial segment, which was by INR 3.25 per SCM, with effect from August 1, 2025.

items.statement: Morbi volumes expected to remain lower in short term due to propane price competition in winter months
items.quote: However, in the short term, the Morbi volumes are expected to remain lower.

items.statement: CNG sales rose 13% YoY in Q2 FY26; Gujarat up 11%, outside Gujarat up 26%; CNG volume hit record 3.934 MMSCMD
items.quote: CNG sales rose by 13% year-over-year, with Gujarat recording an 11% increase and areas outside Gujarat delivering a notable 26% growth, underscoring GGL's success in deepening its presence across all geographies.

items.statement: CNG vehicle base reached 16.22 lakh in September 2025, up 15% YoY; CNG 45% cheaper than petrol, 23% cheaper than diesel
items.quote: As of September 2025, the CNG vehicle base across GGL's network reached approximately 16.22 lakh compared to 14.12 lakh a year earlier, reflecting a solid 15% growth.

items.statement: Invested INR 282 crores in gas infrastructure in H1 FY26; full year capex guidance INR 800 crores
items.quote: For the full financial year, we plan to incur a capital expenditure of approximately INR 800 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance for PNG business INR 800-1,000 crores; rest to be disclosed later
items.quote: If you only look at PNG , the guidance would be along the same. INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores will be investments in this area.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at INR 4.5-5.5 per SCM
items.quote: For the financial year 2025-2026, we estimate an EBITDA margin in the range of 4.5 to 5.5 per SCM.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gas sourcing: APM 2.03 MMSCMD, New Well Gas 0.44 MMSCMD, long-term contracts 3.44 MMSCMD, short-term/spot 2.85 MMSCMD
items.quote: Yes, the APM volume was close to 2.03. New Well Gas was close to 0.44. The long-term contracts were 3.44, and the short-term contracts were 2.85.

items.statement: New Well Gas allocation down from 0.54 MMSCMD in Q1 to 0.44 MMSCMD in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The allocation of the New Well Gas for the Q2 for the Financial Year '25-'26 was approximately 0.44 MMSCMD, down from 0.54 MMSCMD in the Q1.

items.statement: Priority sector APM shortfall 51% overall in Q2; CNG shortfall 64%, domestic 100% allocation
items.quote: During the 2nd Quarter, we received 100% allocation for the domestic segment. However, there was a 64% shortfall in the CNG segment, resulting in an overall shortfall of 51% in the priority segment.

items.statement: Expect industrial volume increase of 2-3 lakh SCMD in new GAs (Ahmedabad Rural, DNH, Thane) over 18 months
items.quote: I think we are expecting in the range of 2-3 lakh SCMD in these areas in at least 18 months.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with port capacity providers (Pipavav, Kandla), fleet providers, and international propane suppliers for propane distribution entry
items.quote: We are currently in discussions with capacity providers for the port, Pipavav and Kandla. And we are in very advanced discussions with these service providers.

items.statement: Q2 Morbi PNG industrial price INR 44/SCM without VAT; propane-gas differential INR 4-6/SCM in Q2, currently less than Q2, expected to increase to INR 5-6/SCM
items.quote: Present price in Morbi without VAT is INR 44.

items.statement: FY26 volume likely sub-9 MMSCMD if conditions unchanged; FY27 9-10 MMSCMD range
items.quote: Yes. Looking at the present conditions, if nothing changes, yes, that is right. But if prices or things change, then it will change.

items.statement: GSPC signed 1 MTPA LNG deal with Qatar Energy starting 2026 for 17 years; will help competitive pricing and margins
items.quote: As the press release says, the volumes are up to 1 MTPA, and the volumes begins in 2026, and the term for the contract is for 17 years.

items.statement: Expect spot LNG prices to settle at $7-8/MMBtu by end of 2027; but linkage to Brent may remain less competitive in near term
items.quote: Spot in terms of absolute numbers may come down to single-digits, $7- $8. That is what we understand.

items.statement: DK Saraf committee report endorses higher APM allocation for CGD industry; company supports but realistic about limited domestic production
items.quote: CGD industry on its own has been asking for higher APM allocation. And the industry expert committee report further endorses the requirement to give a higher APM allocation for the CGD industry, particularly for the CNG and PNG segment.

items.statement: Digital transformation: expanding ERP ecosystem, implementing SCADA for centralized monitoring, identifying automation opportunities
items.quote: We have planned to strategically expand our ERP ecosystem to incorporate additional key business functions and achieve the benefit of seamless integration across verticals.

items.statement: Pipeline network spans 43,900 km; added 42,400 domestic PNG connections in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our pipeline infrastructure now spans approximately 43,900 km of PE and steel networks, which continues to be the key driver for our growth.

items.statement: Maintains AAA rating from CRISIL, CARE, and India Ratings
items.quote: Gujarat Gas continues to maintain a strong credit profile with a AAA rating from CRISIL, Care, and India Ratings.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target approximately Rs 1,500 crore with EBITDA margin around 13-14%
items.quote: Moving into the second half of FY'26, our primary focus will be on returning to profitability in Q3 and Q4. We are aiming to achieve an EBITDA margin of around 13% to 14%, with an approximate turnover of around Rs. 1,500 crore for the fiscal year.

items.statement: Khareef season demand disrupted by excessive rainfall and floods across key regions
items.quote: Overall, we have seen the demand for agrochemicals being disrupted.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 15% vs 19.7% YoY; sequential improvement noted
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 77.5 crore as against Rs. 147.1 crore in the same period last year, translating into an EBITDA margin of 15% compared to 19.7% in Q2 FY'25. Sequentially, however, margins have shown improvement, reflecting the impacts of tighter cost controls and efficiency measures.

items.statement: Patented products now contribute more than half of brand portfolio
items.quote: Another major strength this year has been our growing portfolio of patented products. Patented products now contribute to more than half of our brand portfolio.

items.statement: Gajraula plant expansion delayed 3-6 months; no other capex planned
items.quote: So, the plan was only for this addition in our Gajraula plant. So, as we said we are going slow because the focus is more on stabilizing the business. We do not want to focus another part on the CAPEX immediately. So, that we have put on a second priority. So, it would take anywhere from three to six months for us to start this project. Other than this, we do not have any other CAPEX.

items.statement: Inventory reduced 24% YoY from Rs 873 crore to Rs 666 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: Inventory levels have decreased by Rs. 207 crore from Rs. 873 crore in H1 FY'25 to Rs. 666 crore in H1 FY26, marking a 24% year-on-year reduction.

items.statement: Africa business ~$1M targeted; China subsidiary $6-8M revenue target; Rupee-RMB trade as natural hedge
items.quote: Export is an area of focus and our business in Africa is continuing. As previously stated, after the successful completion of three consignments, we have been awarded further orders based on our quality. The feedback from the customers has been overwhelmingly positive. This year, we hope to do around $1 million business with this customer alone. We have started generating revenue from our China su

items.statement: OPEX reduced 13% vs Q2 FY25 and 11% vs H1 FY25 through regional restructuring
items.quote: Through strategic restructuring across regional operations, the company has achieved an OPEX reduction of 13% compared to Q2 FY'25 and 11% compared to H1 FY'25.

items.statement: Sales return provision Rs 80 crore for September; actual returns expected ~Rs 60-70 crore vs Rs 140 crore last year
items.quote: For September, we have done provision of Rs. 80 crores and what we are expecting is our returns would be around Rs. 60 crores. But same thing last year was actually around close to Rs. 140 crores of sales return. So, from about Rs. 140 crores last year, we are going to have less than 70, around Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores for which we made a provision of Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: Rabi sowing delayed by ~1 month due to extended monsoon; herbicide sales in Q3, insecticide/fungicide in Q4
items.quote: Rabi season in Q3 for the herbicide that is going on as of now. Thatis a delay for one month. But still we can say which was the sales in October and that will be in November end. But definitely it will come under Q3 only if we talk about the herbicide of the Rabi season. And if we talk about insecticide or fungicide, that will come in the quarter 4

items.statement: Preferential warrant Rs 150 crore at Rs 640; 25% (Rs 37.5 crore) received; balance Rs 112.5 crore due within 18 months
items.quote: In fact, you are talking about the preferential which we have done in January, February. So, definitely there is an 18 month of time as per the guideline. And | think till that time it should be okay because all the participants had said it was 25%, which was Rs. 150 crore. So, we have already got Rs. 37.5 crore. So, Rs. 112.5 crore. It has to come through that and thereis a time

items.statement: Maximum two new product launches planned for next financial year
items.quote: No, maximum two products we will launch in next financial year.

items.statement: Patented product registrations progressing in Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Vietnam; active ingredients and formulations in approval process in Taiwan, Mexico, Thailand, Vietnam
items.quote: Our patented product registration in Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Vietnam are progressing. Our active ingredients and formulation products are moving through the approval process in Taiwan, Mexico, Thailand, Vietnam and other key markets.

items.statement: ECL provision Rs 8.5 crore temporary; expected reversal in December as collections peak in Nov-Dec
items.quote: For the second question, it is just a temporary provision which has been done because we have put a formula that beyond a certain number of days we need to provide for the debtors. But November and December being the key collection months, we will be able to collect those and these provisions will be reversed. So, you will see in December that there will be a reversal because we use a certain form

items.statement: Management aims to surpass prior-year visa application volumes for full-year FY26 but does not provide a specific numeric target.
items.quote: Our objective is to achieve more numbers than we did last year. Right now, in terms of volume, we don't know how many volumes is expected in third quarter and fourth quarter. We definitely wish to surpass whatever we have achieved in the last few years.

items.statement: Aadhaar Seva Kendra contract valued at INR 2,000 crores to be executed over 6 years, implying ~INR 350 crores annual revenue at full ramp-up.
items.quote: Correct. When the project is fully ramped up, we expect that revenue to come in.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target is to sustain the current 28-29% level.
items.quote: Correct. These are the consolidated margins. As you know, more than 40% EBITDA margins we are doing in the visa business, our immediate and long-term objective is to sustain the margins that we have achieved.

items.statement: Revenue mix target of 70% Visa and 30% Digital Services over time, subject to new contracts and acquisitions.
items.quote: I think it should get to that 70-30 range somewhere over the period. Again, it is subject to how the new business comes in, as well as the acquisition.

items.statement: Visa volumes grew 12% YoY to 11.3 lakh applications in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Visa volumes increased by 12% during Q2 FY'26, rising to 11.3 lakh applications compared to 10.1 lakh applications in Q2 FY'25.

items.statement: Digital BC business processed 3.5 crore transactions with gross transaction value of INR 27,300 crores in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: In our BC business, we processed around 3.5 crore transactions during the quarter, with gross BLS International Services Limited November 12, 2025 transactional value crossing INR27,300 crores

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin stabilized at 28.9% in Q2 FY26, up from 28.9% sequentially.
items.quote: On a sequential basis, we have maintained our EBITDA margins at around 29% in the second quarter, and we feel the margins have now stabilized at these levels.

items.statement: Visa segment EBITDA margin improved 549 bps YoY to 42% in Q2 FY26 driven by self-operated model shift and cost optimization.
items.quote: EBITDA for the segment rose by 26% to INR192 crores with a margin of 42%, an improvement of 549 basis points from 36.4% margin last year.

items.statement: Digital segment EBITDA margin at 7.4% in Q2 FY26 due to Aadifidelis consolidation; management aims to stabilize and improve over time.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR21 crores, a 72% rise with a margin of 7.4%. This growth was primarily driven by the consolidation of Aadifidelis.

items.statement: Won 3-year MEA mandate to operate India Visa centers in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, China.
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured a 3-year mandate from the MEA, Government of India to operate India Visa application centers across key cities in China, including Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou.

items.statement: Awarded contract by Government of Cyprus to establish visa application center in Kazakhstan.
items.quote: In addition, we were awarded a contract by the government of Cyprus to establish a visa application center in Kazakhstan, thereby further enhancing our international presence.

items.statement: Won INR 2,000 crore UIDAI contract to establish 250-300 district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendras over 6 years, starting December.
items.quote: In a major milestone, we also won a prestigious and large-scale contract valued at around INR 2,000 crores from the Unique Identification Authority of India to establish district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendra. The long-term agreement reinforces our proven capability in executing large-scale e-governance and public service delivery projects, while strengthening our role in India's digital ecosystem. Th

items.statement: Hotel investment was a small, one-time investment from cash reserves to learn asset-light managed hotel model; no further property purchases planned.
items.quote: we did a very small investment, if you see from our cash reserves that we have, to understand this, which itself gives us a 10% to 12% return on our investment. Our objective is that once we learn, our objective is not to invest, but to acquire the expertise so we can run our own brand name. Our objective is to run an asset-light model as in the visa business

items.statement: Digital partnerships added with Aditya Birla Capital, Piramal Finance, and Grameen Foundation in July 2025.
items.quote: We entered into key partnerships with Aditya Birla Capital and Piramal Finance in July 2025, followed by many other companies. In the same month, we also partnered with Grameen Foundation for Social Impact.

items.statement: BC network expanded by 15,000+ channel service partners to over 45,400 BCs as of Sep 30, 2025.
items.quote: We further strengthened our distribution network by adding more than 15,000 channel service partners, taking the total to over 45,400 BCs as of September 30.

items.statement: Management estimates 15-17% global visa outsourcing market share; 50% of market already outsourced, 50% potential future outsourcing.
items.quote: What we feel is that we currently have 15% to 17% global market share, and 50% of the market is outsourced. 50% is yet to be outsourced, which is what the numbers we had showed; there's no proper study that is out there, but this is what our assumption is.

items.statement: MEA temporary ban on new tenders due to SLA complaints on waiting times; existing contracts unaffected; working to resolve soon.
items.quote: There were some SLA-driven complaints regarding waiting time, etc., that is normal when you're processing millions of applications. We had already announced that. We are working towards resolving the matter and are hopeful that it will be resolved soon. There is no impact on our financials or revenue.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 1,306 crores as of Sep 30, 2025, up from INR 928 crores on Mar 31, 2025.
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a strong cash flow and a healthy balance sheet with net cash of INR1,306 crores as on September 30, 2025, compared to INR928 crores as on 31, March 2025.

items.statement: No immediate plans to repatriate overseas cash; funds retained for foreign acquisitions.
items.quote: Last year, if you look at, we did about INR900 crores of investment in new acquisitions outside India. It all happened from the cash there. In the current year, we are also looking at more acquisitions. As and when they get crystallized, we will need cash outside India rather than in India for those.

items.statement: Actively pursuing acquisitions; focus on EBITDA-multiple valuations, ROI, and synergies with existing business.
items.quote: We have a couple of targets we are working on, and we hope to increase our pipeline of target companies, which we can review and take them forward. We are quiet, I would say, aggressively looking at decent acquisitions over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Dividend policy raised to 30% of surplus cash after funding needs; buyback limited by small free reserves under SEBI rules.
items.quote: Earlier, it was 15% of our consolidated cash generated amount. Now we have raised it to 30% of our surplus cash after taking into account any funding requirements, the net cash. The Board have the flexibility of increasing the dividend going forward.

items.statement: Majority of visa centers now self-operated; some countries remain partner-operated for feasibility reasons.
items.quote: The majority are operated by us independently. This is the objective right now.

items.statement: Net revenue per visa application improved 12% YoY to INR 3,223 in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Net revenue per application improved by 12% from INR2,883 in Q2 FY'25 to INR3,223 in Q2 FY'26, supported by enhanced service offering and favorable business mix.

items.statement: iDATA subsidiary processed 1.8 lakh visa applications in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Our subsidiary, iDATA, continued its strong growth momentum, processing around 1.8 lakh applications during the quarter, demonstrating sustained demand and operational efficiency.

items.statement: MEA ban on new tenders is temporary; management expects resolution soon with no financial impact.
items.quote: This tender we had already won. We are currently operating all government contracts BLS International Services Limited November 12, 2025 for the Indian government as well as across the world, so there's no issue on that. As we said, we are working to resolve soon, and we are hopeful of resolving the matter soon. There should be no issue or any impact on our financials

items.statement: Revenue and EBITDA guidance remains unchanged from earlier guidance
items.quote: The guidance remains the same, as we have said earlier.

items.statement: Finalized acquisition in international curriculum space for ~US$1.5m, expected to close in Q3 FY26
items.quote: So, yes, we have finalized one acquisition, which is in the international curriculum space. I can't share anything beyond that, but this should be completed in Q3.

items.statement: Acquisition to be funded partly via foreign currency debt despite cash availability
items.quote: And, we might do some part of it as debt, although we have cash, but foreign currency debt is always easier.

items.statement: No divestment planned for investee companies Smartivity and ixamBee for next two years unless significant liquidity event
items.quote: Not in the near future. Not for the next two years. Unless there is a significant liquidity event.

items.statement: Identified portfolio gaps in international curriculum, regional segments, supplementary books, test prep, computer sciences; will acquire if opportunities at decent valuation
items.quote: We have some gaps in, I would say, like in international curriculum expansion. We have some gaps in, I would say, school regional segments. We have some gaps in, I would say, like non-core textbook area, which is like supplementary books area, Test Prep area. So, we have gaps in computer sciences. We have gaps in 4-6 areas.

items.statement: Full adoption of new NCERT syllabus books for Classes K-12 expected by FY27; staggered adoption over 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect the full adoption of the new syllabus books for Classes K-12 by FY27 and are fully equipped to utilize this opportunity over the next 2 sales seasons.

items.statement: NCERT curriculum benefits expected to start from next year (FY27) after staggered release caused confusion
items.quote: So, this year we might get some benefits. But, we feel that those benefits will start coming in from next year onwards.

items.statement: Entered partnerships for content and licensing including Allied (ICSE), Discovery, Amar Chitra Katha, Money Prep, Speedlabs to expand school catalogue
items.quote: We have entered multiple partnerships for content and Licensing including Allied (ICSE Books), Discovery, Amar Chitra Katha, Money Prep (Financial Literacy), Speedlabs (JEE and NEET Foundation) etc.

items.statement: Digital initiatives SmartK and TestCoach seeing higher adoptions and enrolments
items.quote: The Digital initiatives SmartK and TestCoach continue to move forward with higher adoptions and enrolments.

items.statement: Gross margin percentage reduced in H1 FY26 due to lower pricing in AI Datasets licensing vs H1 FY25 despite higher volumes
items.quote: We saw a reduction in the Gross margins percentage during 1H due to a change in the content licensing (AI Datasets) revenues vs. H1FY25.

items.statement: AI Datasets revenue Rs142m in H1 FY26 vs Rs160m in H1 FY25; pricing lower but volumes improved
items.quote: On an absolute basis, we delivered content licensing (AI Datasets) revenues of Rs142m during H1FY26 vs. Rs160m in H1FY25.

items.statement: AI Datasets deal mix shifted to 75% perpetual and 25% renewal deals this year vs 50-50 last year
items.quote: So, for last year, I would say, it was 50-50. But this year, it's gone to 25% being renewal ones and 75% being perpetual.

items.statement: Third-party content licensing carries lower margins as substantial percentage passed to publishers
items.quote: Of course, since we have to pass substantial percentage of it down the line, so there, of course, our margins would be lower on third party content.

items.statement: AI Datasets customer count increased to 4 from 2 in previous period; speaking to fifth customer

items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA surged 109% year-on-year to INR504 million, translating to a healthy 20% EBITDA to gross margin ratio.

items.statement: Google Cloud Platform migration causing incremental costs; expect INR1-2 crore reduction in coming quarters
items.quote: we will see approximately anywhere between INR1 crore to INR2 crore kind of reduction in this cost in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Plan to optimize 75 heads by end FY26 and 200 heads by end FY27 via AI automation
items.quote: we are looking at least 75-odd heads being optimized by the end of this fiscal year. And I think this has the potential to optimize about 200 heads from a headcount point of view by end of next year.

items.quote: The cost increase that you see on the employee side, that is a little bit of addition that we've done on increasing the sales force on the corporate side and adding a few more people on the MICE and expense management sales front.

items.statement: Value-added products attach rate 15-20%; significant headroom for growth
items.quote: the attach rate still of value-added products and services hovers between 15% and 20%. So there's a lot of headroom for growth on that going forward.

items.quote: our air ticketing passenger volume declined 3% year -on-year to INR1,329,000. However, gross air bookings grew 12% year -on-year to INR1,4811 million.

items.statement: Hotel room nights grew 9% YoY; gross bookings up 40% YoY
items.quote: hotel room nights grew by 9% year-on-year to INR504,000 million. Gross bookings increased 40% year-on-year to INR5,142 million

items.statement: B2B share ~67-68% of business in Q2 FY26
items.quote: This would be around 67%, 68% 67%.

items.quote: third quarter is seasonally a weaker quarter for corporate travel. We see with the Diwali and the Dussehra break in October and then with the Christmas break second half of December, corporate travel will be relatively slow in this quarter.

items.statement: October organic revenue less service cost growth expected 15-20%; EBITDA growth 25%+
items.quote: We would expect revenue less service cost growth to be between 15% to 20%, and we would expect EBITDA growth to be upwards of 20%, 25%-25% plus.

items.statement: EBITDA growth indication of 25-30% for FY27 (not formal guidance)
items.quote: we would expect EBITDA numbers to continue to improve at least 25% to 30%. This is not a formal guidance that I'm putting out right now, but just giving you an indication, right?

items.statement: ROCE improved from ~5% to ~8%+ in H1 FY26; targeting 13-14% in FY27
items.quote: next year, we should be around the 13%, 14% mark in terms of ROCE.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 12-15% and EBITDA margin 22-23% excluding other income
items.quote: So I think we are on track to achieve this 12% to 15% and for the year. If this kind of momentum continues, which we have seen in the last quarter, we should reach there pretty easily. Yes.

items.quote: So, I think at about 70%, 75%, we will start looking at good margins coming in. Before that, we might not have very good margins, though we are not going to lose any more money, we are going to make a little money.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR150 crores including steel plant ~INR75 crores; FY27 capex ~INR75 crores maintenance
items.quote: Yes. So, I think this year would be a capex of about 150 crores around. That includes, of course, the steel plant expansion, which is close to about INR75-odd crores with land and building. And the rest is, of course, maintenance capex.

items.statement: FY27 capex around INR75 crores maintenance
items.quote: Going forward, this will be -- I think next year, it should be around INR75-odd maintenance.

items.statement: Glassware plant utilization ~60% in Q2 FY26, breakeven achieved; Opalware ~85% utilization
items.quote: Year-to-date, our glassware plant had a utilization close to 55%, whereas we saw about 60% utilization levels in Q2 of this financial year. I'm pleased to share that our glassware plant has achieved breakeven during this current quarter.

items.quote: Our steel plant will commence production from December of 2025. Once operational, it will significantly strengthen our supply chain. items.statement: Unomax facility has 30-35% spare capacity; can expand writing instruments via machines and molds
items.quote: Yes. So already, we had about 30%- 35% capacities that were empty in our Unomax facility. And these -- this is not very difficult to expand. It's more expansion of machines.

items.quote: CPIW, a member of the Promoter Group of Cello World Limited, the umbrella entity holding the Cello brand in other classes as well will acquire the trademark for stationery and writing instruments. That is Cello brand from the big group.

items.quote: So they're very close. I think this should close within this month itself. And we should ideally start seeing revenues in Cello World by January, so by the last quarter, we should see revenues in Cello World.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 24% including other income; ~22% operational EBITDA margin
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR141.3 crores with a healthy EBITDA margin of 24%. Our PAT stood at INR85.7 crores with a margin of 14.6%.

items.quote: So gross margin, when I spoke about the contraction, there are two to three factors, as I said. One is that the glass plant -- the glass sales are higher, which is from the new plant, which currently has higher costs.

items.quote: Our steel category experienced a decline during the current quarter due to supply constraints. We had to source steel wares from other OEM manufacturers at a slightly higher cost, which affected profit margins during this quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 saw healthy 20% top-line growth; festive demand strong across categories; channel stock low, secondary sales higher than primary
items.quote: During Q2 financial year '26, we recorded a healthy 20% top line growth to reach revenues of INR587 crores. items.quote: But other than that, it seemed like this thing is back, as we have seen in the last -- because this has been by far the best quarter in terms of demand. It seems -- still we don't -- the festive demand, I feel, we got a bit of October also.

items.statement: Consumerware 71.9% of revenue, Writing Instruments 13.8%, Moulded Furniture 14.3% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Speaking of the revenue mix, over 71.9% of revenue came from the consumer ware, 13.8% from the writing instrument and the remaining 14.3% from moulded furniture & allied products.

items.statement: Glassware SKUs to expand from 110 to ~150; focus on import substitution in tumblers and storage
items.quote: Currently, we have around 110 SKUs in this vertical, and we plan to expand the portfolio to about 150 SKUs going forward.

items.quote: The GST rate has been reduced from 12% to 5% for approximately 10% of our product portfolio, primarily within the hydration category. GST rates for all of the other products remain unchanged.

items.statement: Solar-based cost optimization at glassware plant to reduce energy costs
items.quote: We are also undertaking solar-based cost optimization initiatives at the plant, which will further enhance operational efficiency and reduce energy costs.

items.statement: General trade 73.3%, online 11.6%, modern trade 8.4%, exports 6.7% of sales in Q2 FY26; e-com and quick-com shift helping working capital
items.quote: Sales contribution of both the general trade and exports are on the downturn at 73.3% and 6.7%, respectively. Contribution of online sales was about 11.6% and modern trade at 8.4%.

items.statement: Inventory reducing trend, channel stock easing; October collections strong, outstandings cleared quickly
items.quote: The inventory is on a reducing trend with channel stock easing out. E-com and quick com both saw a major shift in terms of channel mix, which is also helping us in this respect.

items.statement: October collections very good; dealer payments improved leading to better distributor channel payments

items.statement: Healthy net cash position maintained as of H1 FY26
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we continue to maintain a healthy net cash position.

items.statement: Chinese dumping pressure in glassware; new entrants in Opalware but no market dent yet; competitive intensity to increase
items.quote: Despite active dumping pressure from Chinese suppliers, we have successfully scaled up production and gained market share.

items.quote: Currently, of course, it's been very premature. They have not really made any dent in the market as of now. But going forward, competitive intensity in this segment will increase a little bit.

items.quote: I think export has actually come back to its previous levels where it was. It had declined a little bit. But having said that, I think we will continue at this level. It should -- it will not dip, I feel, for the year.

items.quote: In terms of segment-wise margin, writing instrument led by a 55% gross profit margin followed by consumer ware at 50.2% and moulded furniture at 40.9%.

items.quote: So basically, in terms of the brand, CPIW, which is the entity that holds the Cello brand as well. We'll be acquiring it. So it's -- there is no royalty post that and it will be leasing it out to Cello World at no additional cost as with other -- and no royalties as well.

items.quote: We'll, of course, do justice to both by having separate teams working on this, although there will be shared infrastructure and other efficiencies that are to be gained from this transaction.

items.quote: unless the US kind of -- because we have not been hit by the tariffs as yet. The orders have not slowed down. But we have a decent amount that we sell to the US as well. So if nothing gets hurt there, I think we should continue to do these numbers.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margin at least at the current 7% range in coming quarters.

items.statement: Company continues to operate in negative working capital zone.

items.statement: Target positive quarterly ROA in FY26, aiming for Q3 or Q4
items.quote: Based on the current trend in business and delinquency levels, we expect to achieve positive quarterly ROA in FY '26 since the operating performance strengthens and provisions are expected to normalize.

items.statement: Target cost-to-income ratio of 60-65%

items.statement: Target loan book growth of 20-25% YoY in FY27

items.quote: Directionally our ROA and ROE target is 2 percentage and 20 percentage.

items.quote: On the unsecured side, for the current year guidance, we have given a 35%and it will then moderate to around 30% business.

items.statement: Target steady-state credit cost around 4%

items.quote: The net interest margin at 5.9% also remained stable sequentially. items.statement: Gold loan incremental lending rate at 15%, average portfolio yield 13.5%
items.quote: And the current lending rate for gold is 15%.

items.quote: However, if you see from a cost of deposits point of view, last year, the whole 4 quarters, we were at 7.5%. This year, we come down to 7.3% and last quarter it was 7.2% . So we've been rationalizing the deposit rates.

items.statement: Average cost of savings deposits 5.1%, average cost of fixed deposits ~8%
items.quote: The average cost of savings deposits is about 5.1% and the average cost of fixed deposits is about 8% or so.

items.statement: Gold loans 39% of loan book, target ~40% going forward

items.statement: Microfinance disbursements picking up since August 2025 after quality-focused restraint

items.statement: RBI draft ECL framework not yet applicable to SFBs but signals convergence to universal bank standards
