items.statement: CASA grew 14% YoY to INR 6,046 crores, CASA ratio improved 180 bps to 26.4%
items.quote: CASA balances remained the key pillar of our deposit profile, reaching INR 6,046 crores in Q2 FY '26 as compared to INR5,319 crores in Q2 FY '25 translating to a growth of 14 %. CASA ratio improved strongly by 180 basis poin ts to 26.4 %.

items.statement: Retail deposits 96% of total deposits (up from 93%), INR 22,082 crores, up 11% YoY
items.quote: The share of retail deposits in total deposits improved further from 93% in FY '25 to 96 percentage in Q2 FY '26, a clear reflection of the stickiness and quality of our franchise.

items.statement: Kerala microfinance stress declining, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka remain key stress states but Karnataka improving
items.quote: In terms of stress in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Kerala definitely has been coming down. We are seeing a major uptick in that. And that is why we have the confidence to start lending again, with the guardrails in place. In terms of Tamil Nadu, Tamil Nadu is actually where we have the bigger stressed book as of date. Tamil Nadu and Karnataka ar e the 2 big states over there

items.statement: Single NBFC account of ~INR 40 crores slipped to SMA-1, under negotiation
items.quote: But in the NBFC book there is 1 account where it has slipped into SMA 1 in the last quarter. And we are negotiating with them, and we are as of now hopeful that we'll be able to get it under control before the quarter end. Shailesh Kanani: Sir, can you quantify that

items.statement: Acquired R.K.S Motors Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana via slump sale for ~INR90 cr (ex-inventory), 19 locations, 27 touchpoints, 1,039 employees onboarded, co-branding license up to 36 months
items.quote: Effective 15th October, we have acquired the authorized Maruti Suzuki dealership of R.K.S Motors Private Limited through a slump sale transaction. The transaction value is approximately INR90-odd crores, excluding the inventory.

items.statement: Acquired Globe CV BharatBenz dealership in Punjab via slump sale for ~INR12 cr, 8 facilities (7 integrated 3S, 1 parts), 37 service bays, Prabal Motors now exclusive BharatBenz dealer in Punjab
items.quote: Similarly, we had also completed the acquisition of BharatBenz's dealership of Globe CV Private Limited in the state of Punjab through a slump sale. The total consideration for this transaction was approximately INR12 crores.

items.statement: Divested Piaggio (Kuttukaran Green) and Honda (Vision Motors) subsidiaries to sharpen portfolio focus and reallocate management bandwidth to higher growth businesses
items.quote: Lastly, during the quarter, we completed the divestment of the 2 subsidiaries, Kuttukaran Green Private Limited, which operated our Piaggio business and Vision Motors Private Limited, which operated our Honda business.

items.statement: Target Kerala revenue share below 50% by FY27 through geographic diversification
items.quote: All these initiatives are in line with our strategic objective to diversify our geographic presence and reduce the revenue contribution from Kerala to below 50% by FY '27.

items.statement: LOI received for NEXA workshop at Perumbavoor and Thodupuzha with 2 service bays, 3 bodyshop bays, ~500 vehicles/month throughput, ~INR2 cr investment
items.quote: We have received an LOI to set up NEXA workshop at Perumbavoor and Thodupuzha in Ernakulam and neighboring district. This facility will have 2 dedicated service bays and 3 bodyshop bays, with an expected monthly throughput of approximately 500 vehicles. The investment for this workshop is estimated to be around INR2 crores.

items.statement: Incorporated ZPAREX Digisolutions as step-down subsidiary for e-commerce spare parts platform, starting with Maruti, Tata, BharatBenz, Ather parts
items.quote: In addition, we have taken a step towards building a stronger digital and retail parts ecosystem by establishing an e -commerce platform for spare parts and accessories under the entity ZPAREX Digisolutions Private Limited, which has been formed as a step -down subsidiary under Popular Mega Motors Private Limited.

items.statement: GST rate cut announcement in mid-August caused purchase deferrals, mass segment PV sales declined YoY but grew in August; deferred demand expected to flow through Q3, Arena portfolio showing renewed traction
items.quote: during mid - Popular Vehicles and August, the discussions around a potential GST rate revision created a wait-and-watch approach among customers. The rate cut was announced in early September and became effective at the end of the month. This led to postponement of purchases, particularly in the mass segment

items.statement: Demand environment supportive, expect sustained recovery across key segments with momentum from acquisitions and network expansion
items.quote: Looking ahead, the economic environment remains supportive, aided by GST rate reductions and improving consumer sentiment. We expect a sustained recovery in demand across key segments with the momentum from our recent acquisitions, continued network expansion and disciplined operational execution.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA INR49.4 cr (3.2% margin), down 16.5% YoY; adjusted EBITDA INR53 cr (3.5% margin) after INR3.5 cr cess provision, down 10.4% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR49.4 crores, up 29.1% quarter-on-quarter from INR38.3 crores in quarter 1 of FY '26 and down 16.5% year -on-year from INR59.2 crores in quarter 2 of FY '25. EBITDA margin stands at 3.2% for quarter 2 FY '26.

items.statement: Service gross margins improved to ~59% in Q2 from ~56% in H1 FY26 due to revenue-per-car programs with Accenture; labor margin ~8%, spares margin 17-18%
items.quote: So we are trending at close to around 59% on an average, which was actually close to around 56% in the first half of the year. So we are seeing improvements on those aspects.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 4.2-4.3% (ex-inorganic), FY27 target 5%; service volume growth 2-3% organic + ~4% inorganic = 7-8% total; revenue growth higher than current ~3%
items.quote: EBITDA margins, I think we should be able to do about 4.2%, 4.3% from the current 3.5% margins that we are at. Preet: 4.2%, 4.3% except -- keeping aside the inorganic part

items.statement: FY26 PV organic volume growth ~6%, inorganic +2,500 units (~6-7%), combined double-digit growth; FY27 also double-digit growth expected on small car inquiry strength
items.quote: FY '26 overall growth of our passenger car business would be about -- organic growth would be about 6%. We would end up approximately 6% gro wth because of the GST cuts, et cetera, with Q3 and Q4 being very strong. Add to that, the inorganic, we should be adding probably approximately 2,500 vehicles, which would give us another 6% to 7% growth

items.statement: Telangana acquisition: loss in first year due to pre-op expenses, breakeven by Q1 FY27; Punjab BharatBenz: breakeven/low profit in FY26, was profitable for last 2 years
items.quote: The first year that we are actually looking at the operate -- because of the preoperative expenses that we actually have, we are expecting this -- the first year to have kind of a negative in terms of the margins that we will have, but we are -- we will actually try to breakeven towards the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Maruti inventory down to ~33 days by Oct end (from 45-47 days Sep end, 75-85 days earlier); all businesses combined under 30 days by Oct-Nov; interest cost nearly halved
items.quote: We started correcting in April, May. We had bought it down. Popular Vehicles and And in July, August, because of the festive, we had picked up a bit of stock. But by September end, we were down to about approximately 45, 47 days. And October end, we are down to about 33

items.statement: Dealer discounts on Maruti down from INR14k (H2 FY25) to INR9k (H1 FY26) to INR5-6k (Nov); further reduction expected as demand exceeds supply and stock normalizes
items.quote: The discount that we were putting from our hand from the dealer side in H2 of last year had gone up to about closer to INR14,000. And earlier part of this -- so H1, we've been able to bring it down to INR9,000. But in November, as we speak, it has come to about INR5,000, INR6,000.

items.statement: Maruti service ASP grew 12% in Q2 despite volume degrowth; service revenue per car programs driving labor (~8% margin) and spares (~17-18% margin) improvement
items.quote: Even more heartening thing, that's what I'd like to add on a point here is that the ASPs have grown by 12% in service for Maruti business, while the overall volumes have de-grown.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 PV volumes 8,498 units (+48% QoQ), revenue INR664 cr (+37% QoQ); CV volumes 2,797 (+13% QoQ), revenue INR452 cr (+6% QoQ); EV volumes 1,717 (+30% QoQ), revenue INR28 cr (+14% QoQ)
items.quote: New vehicle volumes stood at 8,498 units, up 48% quarter -on-quarter from 5,736 units in quarter 1 of FY '26. Total income from this segment stood at INR664 crores, up 37% from INR484 crores in quarter 1 of '26.

items.statement: Impairment losses reduced to INR1.7 cr from INR3.4 cr QoQ due to improved collections and lower ECL provisions; focus on aged collections continues
items.quote: Impairment losses reduced to INR1.7 crores from INR3.4 crores in quarter 1 FY '26, driven by lower debt or provisions and improved collections during this quarter.

items.statement: Cess provision INR3.6 cr taken (INR2.5 cr PVSL, INR1.2 cr subs) for ECL ledger balances; FADA writ petition in Supreme Court; government in dialogue with OEMs; total industry impact ~INR2,500 cr
items.quote: On the cess front, we are still awaiting the final clarity from the government, writ petition has been filed in the Supreme Court by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Association. However, we have taken a provision of INR3.6 crores for compensation sales for the amount lying in the electronic credit ledger during this quarter.

items.statement: JLR cyberattack from late August paused production and spares supply through September and part of October, impacting Q2 luxury business; JLR guidance: Nov-Dec decent, Jan-Mar back to regular deliveries
items.quote: JLR faced a massive cyberattack from the end Popular Vehicles and of August, which paused the production and continuity in supply of spares for most of September and part of October, which impacted our business performance in Q2

items.statement: FY26 closing debt lower than FY25 despite festive stock build; inventory correction from Oct onwards reducing interest cost; FY27 PAT expected to cross FY24 level of INR70-80 cr
items.quote: No, FY '26 closing debt would be lower because, as I said, for the festive season, we had built up stock, but the GST announcement came as a complete surprise to us.

items.statement: Nagpur JLR facility opening by mid-December FY26; evaluating another luxury brand acquisition by end-December; consolidation of 6-state presence over next 12-18 months
items.quote: FY '27, for us, we would see a growth because by December second week or third week, we would be opening up our Nagpur facility. And hopefully, we would be able to acquire a new brand by the end of December.

items.statement: Popular Mega Motors certified Great Place to Work; CARE upgraded Popular Autoworks rating to CARE A- Stable from BBB+; CRISIL reaffirmed CRISIL A/Stable and A1
items.quote: Popular Mega Motors India Private Limited, company's wholly owned subsidiary is certified as a Great Place to Work. The credit ratings update, CARE Ratings Limited have upgraded the rating awarded to the subsidiary company, Popular Autoworks Private Limited for the long-term bank facilities from CARE BBB+; STABLE to CARE A -; STABLE.

items.statement: State revenue mix Q2 FY26: Kerala 59%, Tamil Nadu 25%, Karnataka 11%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 1%; 6-state presence after Telangana and Punjab additions
items.quote: The state-wise revenue breakup for quarter 2 of FY '26 is Kerala at 59%, Tamil Nadu 25%, Karnataka 11%, Maharashtra 5%, and Punjab at 1%.

items.statement: Tata ACE Pro gaining strong traction, expected to add 15-25% volumes; Ather EV 2-wheeler presence expanded in Maharashtra (Chandrapur, Kamptee, Nagpur, Waluj) and Chennai
items.quote: During the quarter, Tata Motors also introduced ACE Pro, which has been gaining strong market traction and is expected to contribute an additional 15% to 25% in terms of volumes.

items.statement: Service volume growth guidance: FY26 ~2-3% organic, FY27 double-digit growth expected as new car sales feed service pipeline with 4-6 month lag
items.quote: So as Naveen mentioned earlier, this full year, we are expecting to close the service volumes closer to about 2% to a max 3%. But as you rightly said, with the volumes coming in towards the second half of this year, next year, for example, you can see, when you -- while you must be very clear in terms of the national growth in volumes.

items.statement: Digital spare parts platform (ZPAREX) targets higher EBITDA margin than physical retail (currently 7-8%) over 3-5 years by eliminating store/manpower costs; spare parts gross margin ~18%
items.quote: We are looking at -- not in the first 2 years, but over the next -- over a 3 - to 5 -year period, we are expecting a higher EBITDA margin than the physical thing because we don't need physical stores, the costs associated with that, manpower, etcetera, in the digital model.

items.statement: Targets 25% top-line growth and 25% bottom-line growth for FY26, aiming to restore pre-2025 profitability levels
items.quote: We are looking at about 25% growth from the last year's number, which unfortunately did not happen last year because of the business- one particular business, which was for INR 80 crores, which we did not get last year because it did not get operated.

items.statement: Targets PAT margin of 12-13% for FY26, comfortable with that range
items.quote: We are comfortable at a figure which is about 12% to 13%, 14% in fact. This is the kind of figures which we are comfortable with.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 97.08 crore, PAT INR 7.82 crore; PAT margin improved marginally despite top-line dip
items.quote: Now as you would be aware, our, consolidated revenue was INR 97.08 crores with a PAT margin of INR 7.82 crores. I repeat, INR 97.08 crores were the revenue from sales and PAT was INR 7.82 crores.

items.statement: Medical conference business (Travexel) has significantly higher profitability than regular MICE; order book INR 22-25 crore this year and INR 20-22 crore next year
items.quote: What I can tell you is that the medical conferences company, their profitability is much higher than a regular MICE company. There are various reasons to it, but I cannot get deeper into those reasons.

items.statement: Order book currently looks very healthy; H1 orders virtually all executed; INR 40 crore new mandates secured in 15 days during H1
items.quote: Currently, our order book looks very healthy. But unfortunately, I cannot share the numbers here. So, this is about it.

items.statement: Government/institutional tender division launched; empanelled with 2-3 ministries and associations; won INR 80 lakh business at higher margins than corporate MICE
items.quote: In the past 2 months - 3 months, we have now got into the institution and government tender business. We have started the process of getting empanelled into a lot of government agencies.

items.statement: MICE constitutes 80-85% of business; cruises, weddings, religious tourism make up remainder; Book My Yatra OTA portal 90% ready, targeting December launch
items.quote: If I talk about the bifurcation, then, MICE will be about, I could be extremely wrong, but about 80% - 85% would be MICE and some would be cruises, some would be weddings, some would be religious tourism, but majorly it is MICE only.

items.statement: Acquired Travexel for doctor conferences (pharma vertical); NEOCON in November, APICON (8000 doctors) in February in Patna
items.quote: We acquired a company a few months back, Travexel, which was into doctor conferences, the pharma business. So, that company we had acquired and that company already has two businesses.

items.statement: Moved to 13,000 sq ft single-plate office (3x previous size) in Sector 73 Noida on 9-year lease; 250-275 seat capacity for OTA team expansion
items.quote: In order to expand, we have moved into an office which is three times bigger than the current one or the one where we were about two months back, from 4,600 square feet, two plate offices. In order to generate synergy, we have moved into 13,000 square feet, one plate office.

items.statement: April-May impacted by India-Pakistan conflict causing cancellations; recovery from June onwards; international destinations stabilizing; strong query flow in H2
items.quote: The first half, we were able to marginally increase the PAT margins from last year, although the top line and the bottom line took a dip. And basically, the reason of this is April and May were affected due to the India-Pakistan war.

items.statement: Focus on blue-chip corporates; not pursuing Tier II/small dealer trips due to profitability and payment concerns; IT sector has low incentive travel; pharma limited by regulations
items.quote: For us, mostly our corporates, our clients are the bigger companies which are there in India. So, in terms of regional offices or Tier II cities, in most of the cases, the decision comes to their zonal office or it comes to their regional office.

items.statement: Government payment cycles managed via strict documentation and compliance; confident payments won't delay if paperwork is clean
items.quote: In terms of payment cycle, I very frankly do not want to comment on it. But what happens if the documentation is no problem, if there is no service issue, in 100% cases, I am sure the payment would not be delayed.

items.statement: Promoters buying shares from market at low prices, confident in long-term value
items.quote: We, do not do any hanky panky and are buying share from the market. Because we are confident that if we take this share at a low price today, then we do not have to go anywhere, nor do we have to go to Dubai, nor do we have to go to Goa.

items.statement: April-May force majeure (war) caused revenue dip; peer comparison difficult due to different business models (asset-light vs asset-heavy)
items.quote: Had it not been this war scenario, April-May, then we would have shown you a growth. We would have shown you a growth in top line and in bottom line also.

items.statement: Average revenue per event not a meaningful KPI for MICE; top-line and PAT margin are the correct health metrics
items.quote: One basic simple formula is the top line and the PAT margins, there is nothing better and easy for calculation. Yes, there are bifurcation which I do not have right now and but this is the easiest and the safest way to check the health of the company.

items.statement: Target 76-78 stores by March 2026 and 150 stores by March 2028
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of 76 to 78 stores by March 2026.

items.statement: Plan to add 30-35 stores over next two years after FY26
items.quote: And then we will be adding another 30-33-35 stores in the next two years. So, by end of March 2028, the company aims to reach 150 stores.

items.statement: H2 FY26 store additions of 13-15 stores, mix of PNG and LiteStyle, COCO and FOCO
items.quote: Our PAN-India expansion program is progressing well, with around 13 to 15 new stores planned in the second half of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 5.5-6% for full year FY26
items.quote: So, broadly, at EBITDA level, close to 5.5% to 6% can be expected as a EBITDA margin for the year?

items.statement: Marketing spend capped at 1.25-1.5% of revenue for full year
items.quote: So, what we are thinking is that it should not cross 1.25 to 1.50 of the 1.5% of the total revenue, the entire marketing spend.

items.statement: Studded jewellery ratio target 12-13% in next two years
items.quote: The company aims to reach 12%-13% in the next two years.

items.statement: Plan to add one international store per year, starting with North America West Coast
items.quote: But yes, we will be adding, we will look at adding one store a year on the international front, right now, looking at North America as the region.

items.statement: Record festive sales of INR 428 crores on Navratri, up 66% YoY; October sales over INR 1,800 crores
items.quote: Early festive demand, particularly during Navratri, resulted in record-breaking sales of INR 428 crores, an exceptional 66% rise year-over-year.

items.statement: Positive volume growth despite 50% YoY gold price increase; 55-60% of wedding purchases use old gold exchange
items.quote: But we have also seen positive volume growth at the company level. Consumer interest in jewellery remains strong and now with the upcoming wedding season in the month of December-Jan, the road looks pretty positive.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin 11.9% (+510 bps YoY), EBITDA margin 6.6% (+327 bps YoY), net margin 3.6% (+190 bps YoY)
items.quote: Gross profit rose by almost 91% year-over-year to INR 258.1 crores, with the gross margin expanding by 510 basis points to 11.9%. EBITDA grew by almost 117% to INR 142.9 crores, reflecting an EBITDA margin improvement of 327 basis points to 6.6%.

items.statement: Retail segment EBITDA margin 9.1%, PAT margin 5.1% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our retail segment, which accounts for around 72.2% of total sales continues to be our largest growth engine with a revenue growth of 29% year-over-year, with EBITDA margin of 9.1% and PAT margin of 5.1%.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement expected in Q3 FY26 vs Q2 due to festive season
items.quote: Now, the real improvement you will see in quarter three.

items.statement: Gold schemes: Golden Gain 53 kg, Suvarna Lakshmi Labh 63 kg (total 115 kg), fully hedged on MCX
items.quote: So, as on September current financial year, we have a Golden Gain Plan of almost 53 kgs and Suvarna Lakshmi Labh Plan is almost for 63 kgs. So, totaling 115 kgs, which is completely hedged on the MCX.

items.statement: Scheme sales contribute ~7-8% of annualized revenue (~INR 700 crores)
items.quote: So, total contribution would be around 10% from this scheme because we have schemes in quantity and schemes in value. So, the total sale from this would be in tune of around INR 700 crores, which would be on the range of around 7% to 8% of the annualized sales.

items.statement: New store capex increased to INR 47-50 crores (incl. INR ~2 cr capex) due to higher gold prices
items.quote: Now, that because of the incremental in the gold prices, that minimum investment is around 45 crores and the capex is roughly 2 crores. So, around in between 47 crores to 50 crores is the amount that required need to be infused for opening of new store.

items.statement: Total store count 63 at end Q2 FY26 (8 added in Q2: 5 COCO, 3 FOCO); entered Indore, Lucknow, Kanpur
items.quote: We launched eight exclusive stores during the quarter, five company-owned COCO stores and three franchisee-owned FOCO outlets, taking our total store count to 63 at the end of Q2.

items.statement: H2 FY26 plan: add 14-16 stores (6-7 PNG, 7-8 LiteStyle; 50% COCO, 50% FOCO)
items.quote: We plan to add another 14 to 16 stores in the coming six months before March end. Out of that, we have targeted that we should be looking at around six to seven PNG stores and same around seven to eight LiteStyle stores.

items.statement: LiteStyle stores: 1,500-2,000 sq ft, inventory INR 8-10 cr, target 2.5-3 stock turns, gross margin 20-25%, breakeven 12-18 months
items.quote: in these stores would be in the range of around INR 8 crores to INR 10 crores. And we expect that these stores should contribute once they mature to around 2.5 to 3 stock turns. So, around INR25 crores is what we expect these stores to reach at. The margins would range -- in the range of around 20% to 25

items.statement: Studded jewellery ratio rose to 9% in Q2 FY26; launched Polki, Kundan, Colourstone collections
items.quote: We also saw a significant increase in the studded jewellery mix, taking the stud ratio to 9%, reflecting a clear shift in the consumer preference towards more design-led aspirational products.

items.statement: Transaction volume +18% YoY, avg ticket ~INR 1 lakh; footfall +20%, conversion 93%
items.quote: On the customer front, engagement continues to strengthen. Our transaction volume were up by 18% with an average transaction value of almost INR1 lakh. Footfall grew by 20%, supported by a conversion rate of 93%.

items.statement: Payables elevated at Sep-end due to festive stocking; cleared post-festival
items.quote: The thing is, since we are closing on 30th September and we have to gear up for, since that's right on 2nd of October and plus the festival season also in the month of October. So, yes, there is slightly improvement in the payables on 30th September, but because after the festival, whatever the credit days we have, we have already cleared entire payment cycle.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed long-term rating CRISIL A Positive, short-term CRISIL A1
items.quote: CRISIL has reaffirmed our long-term rating as CRISIL A positive and our short-term rating as CRISIL A1, underscoring our strong financial discipline and prudent capital management.

items.statement: 100% effective hedging on gold month-on-month; silver hedged only during festive season, else replenishment model
items.quote: Yes, so we are doing 100% effective hedging on a month-on-month basis. So, that's the same thing we are keeping continued for the last almost nine months after the IPO.

items.statement: SSSG: volume flat YoY, +29% QoQ; value slightly up YoY; 24 new stores added since H1 FY25
items.quote: So, year over year, if you see there, then the SSSG in terms of volume is more or less same, but quarter over quarter, there is 29% growth in the SSSG.

items.statement: No demand impact seen from high gold prices; gold viewed as emotion/tradition, not just investment
items.quote: In India, gold is not just, you know, jewellery or fashion, it's also emotion, it's a religion, it's a part of a tradition. So, people are using old gold as a currency to buy new gold.

items.statement: No consumer pressure from lab-grown diamonds; company not entering that category
items.quote: See, studded jewellery sale has seen a very, very steady rise. There has been no pressure from lab-grown. So, as a company, we have not seen any pressure from the consumer side demanding lab-grown.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~85% gold, ~10% silver, ~5% diamond (stone cost only)
items.quote: Yes. So, when I see my total 100% revenue, almost 85% is coming from gold, and 10% is coming from silver, and remaining 5% is coming from diamonds.

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 revenue outlook of INR 500 million including inorganic businesses, subject to shareholder approvals; base business guidance of INR 400 million
items.quote: We are very confident and we are willing to reiterate our 2028 guidance for INR400 million on the base business, and then with the inorganic businesses that are also performing strongly to now reiterate our INR500 million outlook for FY 2028 subject to shareholder approvals.

items.statement: Expect to start consolidating new businesses from next financial year subject to approvals
items.quote: We expect to start consolidating from the next financial year the new businesses that we have announced subject to, like I said, the regular approval process.

items.statement: Pro forma combined H1 revenue of almost US$110 million at 30% EBITDA margin for OneSource and incoming businesses
items.quote: On a pro forma basis, the combined revenue for the first half of the year of both the incoming businesses and OneSource are almost US$110 million, at a very healthy 30% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Accelerating Phase 2 capacity expansion for DDC business to support FY27 commercialization; capacity expansion progressing in full swing
items.quote: We are pulling forward our Phase 2 capacity expansion plans, and it is progressing in full swing to support our FY '27 commercialization plans for DDC business.

items.statement: Will be fully ready by end of calendar year 2026 with over 200 million units capacity for pens, almost a year ahead of previous schedule
items.quote: We are rapidly expanding our capacity installations, and we will be fully ready by the end of calendar year '26, almost a year ahead of our previously announced schedule in terms of readiness for over 200 million units of capacity for our pens.

items.statement: Installed biologics capacity of 4,000 liters (4 kL mammalian + 1 kL microbial) expected to be fully utilized and need instant expansion
items.quote: We believe that our installed capacity of 4,000 liters will not only be taken fully, but will need instant expansion as we meet increased demand for both mammalian and microbial on the drug substance.

items.statement: DDC order book remains solid with 8-10 customers launching next year across multiple global markets; several customers provided take-or-pay and reservation fees
items.quote: We will have almost eight to 10 customers actually launching next year across multiple global markets so that will be a key driver and that's what gives us great confidence for it.

items.statement: Added 26 new RFPs this quarter across all modalities; 12 customers common across modalities demonstrating cross-selling success
items.quote: This quarter, we added 26 new ones. And these are apart from the wins which we have had in MSAs and licensing agreements which we have signed.

items.statement: Biologics funnel almost 4x of FY25 driven by US Biosecure Act and simplified biosimilar approval pathways by FDA and Europeans
items.quote: In fact, today our biologics funnel is almost 4x of what it was in FY '25.

items.statement: Significant demand growth seen in emerging markets as innovator supplies arrive; expect markets to expand significantly in quantities and capacity utilization
items.quote: We believe that not only the markets will expand significantly with quantities in terms of demand, but in also in terms of our capacities being fully occupied.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA grew 37% to INR 1,065 million with margin expansion of 506 bps to 28%; H1 EBITDA INR 1,950 million at 28% margin
items.quote: In terms of profitability for the quarter, we grew 37% on EBITDA, reaching INR1,065 million, and the margin expanded to 28%, which is a 506 business points improvement versus prior year.

items.statement: Working capital elevated at INR 5,936 million due to planned inventory buildup for long-lead items for upcoming DDC launches, backed by customer advances or purchase orders; expect normalization over medium term
items.quote: As of September 30th, moving on to our working capital, we had a working capital of INR 5936 million. It is currently elevated, and this includes planned buildup of inventory for long-lead items that we are preparing for upcoming future DDC launches.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR 9,033 million (up INR 4,326 million from March 2025) due to accelerated capex; effective interest rate down 140 bps to single digits; multiple credit rating upgrades to A family since listing
items.quote: Our net debt currently stands at INR 9033 million, which is an increase of INR 4326 million compared to March of 2025, which is a year-end last. This increase is largely demonstrated in the ongoing capital expansion that we are doing, which we are actually accelerating in terms of our capex investments.

items.statement: Over 20 customers total; 9 customers launching products in markets outside Canada; customers are regional/national champions across Canada, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, India
items.quote: We have constantly been increasing our customer base and we now have over 20 customers. We have over nine customers who will launch product in several markets on outside of Canada.

items.statement: No known competitor globally has device assembly capacity across 10-11 platforms; capacity addition takes ~2 years lead time; market is access-driven not price-driven for next couple years
items.quote: No one that we know. And that's what -- not just in India, even globally. And that's the differentiation which we offer. And

items.quote: With 2 wheelers as you mentioned 17,300 and in 4 wheelers with commercial vehicles it was around 30,000, but with H-One coming in, it has gone up to 45,000.

items.quote: So the inventory has seen a sharp rise in H1 FY '26 as we have stocked up seeing the demand in H2 FY '26, so we expect the inventory levels to go down from Q3 FY '26.

items.quote: Our order book as of 30th September 2025 stands at INR2,069 crores, providing strong execution visibility for the next several quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 order inflow of nearly INR789 crore, including INR463 crore for renewable energy sector
items.quote: In quarter 2, we secured orders totaling to nearly INR789 crores, out of which orders worth INR463 crores are for supply of transformers for the renewable energy sector.

items.statement: INR300 crore of order book is 400 kV class to be executed from Vadod facility
items.quote: About INR300 crores order book is 400 kV class, and that is supposed to be executed from the Vadod facility, which is now commissioned.

items.statement: Order execution timelines: 220 kV class 15-24 months, 400 kV class 18-30 months
items.quote: Typically, 220 kV class orders last between 15 months to 24 months. 400 kV class lasts between 18 to, say, 2.5, three years.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline estimated between INR12,000-18,000 crore
items.quote: It will be close to anywhere between INR12,000 crores to INR18,000 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.3%, H1 FY26 16.4%, backed by operating leverage, favorable product mix, and improved procurement efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the period Q2 FY '26 and H1 FY '26 stood at 17.3% and 16.4% respectively. Mainly, backed by operating leverage benefits, a favorable product mix, higher contribution to power transformers, and improved procurement efficiency of key raw materials like copper and CRGO and steel.

items.statement: High voltage transformers (400/765 kV) expected to have structurally higher margins, but difficult to quantify before first prototype
items.quote: A couple of basis points higher is what we anticipate for the near future, because entering into these segments is something where it takes lot of technology cost, research and development cost, once stabilized, the margins turn out to be better.

items.statement: Startup costs for new facilities denting Q2 margins temporarily, expected to normalize as plants stabilize
items.quote: It's only for the temporary or one-time cost which we are incurring for amalgamating the plants, newer facilities or this thing, and the startup cost for the newer plant, which is making some dent on the margins at the moment.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through via price variation formulas in utility orders (70%) and hedging practices for private orders (30%)
items.quote: Utility orders come with the price variation formula, which provides us a natural hedging against any variation in the raw material prices. For the rest of the 30% orders, which comes from the private payers, EPC, IPPs, etcetera, we certainly have raw material price hedging practices in our organization.

items.statement: Raw material sourcing largely domestic; CRGO, insulation, RIP bushings, tap changers for high kV class imported with long-standing supplier relations
items.quote: The sourcing of raw material is largely domestic. Of course, some of our vendors, when we talk about CRGO, may be relying more on the import cycle for the CRGO steam. However, majority of the material is sourced domestically. There are certain components that are specifically imported for higher KV class, like insulation material, RIP bushing, tap changers.

items.statement: No supply constraints faced for CTC or CRGO; strategy of placing orders well in advance with suppliers
items.quote: We are pretty secure on that, on all fronts, including these two fronts.

items.statement: First sizable export order of INR20 crore for 132 kV class transformer; export pipeline expanding with potential for meaningful contribution over next 12-18 months
items.quote: On the export front, we have made a strong start, our first sizable international order of INR20 crores for the supply of 132 kV class transformer, which aligns with our vision to diversify to our geographical presence.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced to INR125 crore after repaying INR130 crore for Vadod and INR85 crore for BTW from IPO proceeds
items.quote: Now, long-term debt in our books stood at INR125 crores as on debt.

items.statement: Working capital interest rate 8.5-9%, term loan rate 10-10.5%
items.quote: So working capital plant, we have an interest rate of 8.5% to 9%, whereas for term loan, it is around 10%, 10.5%.

items.statement: Finance cost to be significantly lower in H2 FY26 due to debt repayment, but working capital needs for new plants will persist
items.quote: So -- and another INR85 crores, which was taken for the acquisition of BTW facility. Now, long-term debt in our books stood at INR125 crores as on debt. This means that finance cost will be significantly lower in the H2 numbers.

items.statement: Target to maintain 70/30 power transformer to T&D ratio by FY30; aim to be dominant player in 400 kV and 765 kV class by FY30
items.quote: By FY30, we see ourselves as a very dominant player of 400 kV class. We see a very dominant player of 765 kV class also by FY30.

items.statement: Order book well-diversified across PSUs, IPPs, EPCs, and private industrial plants; engaged with large private developers for data center transformers
items.quote: Overall, our order book stands at a healthy, well-diversified, across PSUs, IPPs, EPCs, and private industrial plants, providing clear execution visibility into FY '26 and FY '27.

items.statement: No advantage expected from competitor TARIL's World Bank blacklisting; export strategy independent
items.quote: We don't see any of such advantages that will be coming in, in the near future.

items.statement: Payment solutions revenue share fell to 50% in H1 FY26 from 67.5% in H1 FY25 due to lower card issuance volumes driven by PMJDY slowdown, unsecured lending stress, and lower COVID-era renewals.
items.quote: In H1 FY26, the payment solutions contributed about 50% of total revenue as compared to 67.5% in H1 FY25. This moderation is largely a result of lower card issuance volumes by banks, primarily external program-driven and regulatory factors, rather than any change in customer relationships or share of wallet.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 to be stronger than H1 FY26 due to seasonal BFSI pickup, customer forecasts, and new project wins in payments and IoT.
items.quote: Historically, the second half of the year tends to be stronger for BFSI spends and card issuance, and we expect the same pattern to play out this year as well.

items.statement: IoT solutions revenue grew 31% YoY to INR654 million in H1 FY26 driven by wallet share gains in renewables and new customer additions; SIM card supplies to telecom operators to start in H2 FY26.
items.quote: Our IoT business contributed about 10% top line in H1 FY26. We witnessed a strong growth of 31% to INR654 million in H1 FY26 versus INR500 million last year in the same period.

items.statement: Sizable IoT projects close to closing expected to contribute significantly in H2 FY26 and FY27; renewable customer base expanding from 3-4 to double-digit by year-end.
items.quote: There are some sizable projects which are pretty close to closing and which will have a very sizable contribution for us in H2 and also in FY27.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin improved 336 bps QoQ to 26.9% and 9 bps YoY; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved 54 bps YoY to 25.3%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 95 crores with an EBITDA margin of 26.9, an improvement of 336 bps sequentially, and 9 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement to ~46% driven by favorable product mix (metal cards, renewable solar tags with in-house inlays, high-volume communication fulfillment project), operational efficiencies, better procurement terms, lower import costs
items.quote: Primarily, we have benefited from a favorable product mix across the verticals. Additionally, operational efficiencies have also kicked in in this quarter with the volume growth as you rightly said.

items.statement: Payment card pricing remained static at last year's levels; RFID pricing unchanged; IoT chip costs may optimize with new generation chips but benefit not yet seen.
items.quote: On the payment card side, we've seen the price change remain more or less static as per the last year's levels.

items.statement: INR200 crore capex plan over 18 months per IPO objects for equipment and infrastructure expansion; INR42 crore assets added in H1 FY26 before IPO funds.
items.quote: So, basically, the capex plan of INR200 crores was spread across a period of 18 months. If you see the capex plan that has been mentioned as part of the objects of the IPO, has been expansion of the existing infrastructure and capacities of the company.

items.statement: INR300 crore debt repaid in second week of October 2025 from IPO proceeds; interest cost savings to reflect from Q3 FY26 onwards.
items.quote: Around the second week of October, about INR300 crores of debt was repaid completely as per the IPO proceeds plan.

items.statement: Export initiatives include existing relationships in Nepal and Sri Lanka, approved products in Africa, shortlisted for global metal card RFPs, and qualification with a large global player; no plans for overseas personalization bureaus.
items.quote: We are working with some partners in the African continent where our products have been approved and we should be seeing some business coming in there. On our high-end products such as metal cards, as we stated earlier, there's one global RFP that we've been shortlisted with.

items.statement: IoT expanding into BLE, sensor-based RFID, special purpose tags, cold chain monitoring, anti-counterfeiting, and hybrid RFID-BLE solutions; multiple POCs underway.
items.quote: Beyond RFID, we are investing in adjacent and next-generation IoT technologies, including Bluetooth Low Energy, which is BLE, sensor-based RFID, and Special Purpose Tags.

items.statement: Selective acquisitions made in IoT space to accelerate innovation and reduce time-to-market in BLE and sensor-based technologies; integration enhances RFID roadmap synergy.
items.quote: To strengthen our position, we have also made selective acquisitions in the IoT space. These have been strategically aligned to accelerate our innovation cycle and reduce time-to-market in high-potential solution areas.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contributed 63.5% of Q2 FY26 revenue; over 98% revenue from existing clients; no customer churn, order cancellations, or renegotiations in payment solutions.
items.quote: The top 10 customers contributed almost 63.5% of our revenues, and more than 98% of our revenues came from existing clients, demonstrating the depth of our client relationships and the stable base that we have built.

items.statement: Payment solutions vertical revenue INR272 crore (69%) in Q2 FY25 vs INR352 crore total revenue in Q2 FY26; communication fulfillment INR94 crore (24%); IoT INR27 crore (7%).
items.quote: payment solution was about INR272 crores, communicat ion & fulfillment was about INR94 crores. IoT was 7%, was about INR27 crores

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 better than H1 FY26 on volume and value; confident of good growth in FY27 but declines to give specific revenue or margin guidance.
items.quote: We expect H2 FY26 to be better, supported by seasonal pickup in BFSI volumes, steady momentum in communication fulfillment, and continued traction in our IoT business.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and tariff uncertainties delayed international expansion; Middle East project abandoned due to strategic misalignment with national interest.
items.quote: We had one unfortunate situation that we had deeply engaged with one customer in Middle East, but because of geopolitical equations post this skirmish that we had with the neighbor in April-May, we had to kind of take a step back in that relationship because it was not strategically aligned to our national interest.

items.quote: We've traditionally been in a 25%, 26% range over the last couple of years.

items.quote: Tech spending on our business is predominantly, as I said, symmetric. So if revenue goes up by 10%, headcount will also go up -- billable headcount will also go up by 10%. So we are targeting 25% to 30% CAGR. So that is what you can take as headcount growth also.

items.statement: Key risk: vendor consolidation by large customers; mitigation through proximity and making client stakeholders successful
items.quote: Now the challenge or the bigger risk is not winning this consolidation, but not being invited for a seat on the table. And that is what I said earlier by saying that we have to be very close to the customer. We have to be always aware of this exercise before it begins so that we are able to prep ourselves as well as the customer to select us.

items.statement: No H1B dependency, non-issue for the company
items.quote: No, H1B, we are not H1B dependent at all, Vikas. So that's a non-issue as we speak.

items.statement: Dividend policy ~10% of consolidated profit payout, will continue
items.quote: So we've always f ollowed about a 10% consolidated profit payout as our dividend policy. So we would like to stick to that because for some shareholders, dividend is a reward

items.statement: Tax rate expected 24-25% effective for FY26
items.quote: The tax rate should be between 24% to 25% effective.

items.statement: Other income comprises realized and unrealized exchange gains
items.quote: The other income major constituent is the realized gain and the unrealized gain, both will be there. Both are as component. The main component. The exchange gains basically.

items.statement: Vision 2030 target $500M revenue via 25-30% organic CAGR plus 1-2 large acquisitions
items.quote: But what we are trying to do is grow 25%, 30% year-on-year, and we are confident that we'll have 1 big or 2 reasonably large acquisitions along the way, which will help us get to the $500 million. So that's our plan to get there. Very much on the cards. We still have a few years to get there.

items.statement: Acquisition capacity currently limited to $10-15M revenue targets; larger deals possible later with war chest
items.quote: All our acquisitions are typically capability acquisitions. And we look at anything between $10 million to $15 million in top line because that's all we can afford. We don't want to dilute capital. So $10 million to $15 million top line with an EBITDA which is better than where we are at is our normal yardstick to determine whether we want to go in for an acquisition or not.

items.statement: Small IT firms gain from AI disruption while large incumbents lose; not specific to tech industry
items.quote: Whenever there's a disruption in any industry and AI is a disruption in the tech industry. Whenever there's a disruption, the biggest loser is the market leader. The small guys always gain. So that's what's happening here. The big guys are losing out because of the disruption, okay? And the small guys are winning.

items.statement: Launched SakMod (legacy modernization), SakCelerate (AIOps/FinOps), Conversational AI, Emergency Care Agent
items.quote: Under intelligent p roducts, our portfolio has been expanded by 2 major accelerators, namely SakMod, which is a composable framework for legacy modernization and system integration; and SakCelerate, which is a unified AIOps and FinOps automation platform for enterprises. Under intelligent platforms, our recent releases include Conversational AI, which enables voice- driven customer and employee ex

items.statement: Centers of excellence (6) building capabilities and accelerators to demonstrate use cases to customers
items.quote: For this, almost a couple of years ago, we had started this concept of centers of excellence where we have 6 centers of excellence, which is led by senior leaders and their role is only building capabilities and accelerators and demonstrating to our customers what we can do for them in terms of use cases for their business.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 8-10% in H2 FY26; Hero to outperform and gain market share
items.quote: Based on these encou raging trends, we expect the 2 -wheeler industry to grow 8% to 10% in the second half of FY'26 with Hero poised to outperform the overall market and continue to gain market share

items.statement: Festive retail growth 17% YoY; post-festive momentum sustained with lowest inventory and receivables in years
items.quote: During this year, festive season starting from ONAM i.e. from 23rd August '25 until yesterday, November 13, 2025, the growth in ICE VAHAN registration stood at 16.2%, ahead of industry growth of 14.7% over the comparable period in the previous year, leading with a 40 bps market share gain.

items.statement: Rural demand recovering strongly post-harvest; marriage season supportive for Q4 and Q1
items.quote: But as we have progressed late into festive towards Dhanteras and then early part of November, we are seeing all this crop harvesting proceeds reaching the market and it's now responding really well.

items.statement: ICE EBITDA margin 17.7% (+121 bps YoY); overall EBITDA margin 15% (+54 bps YoY) after EV investment of ₹252 cr
items.quote: The EBITDA margin during the quarter for ICE business improved to 17.7%, up 121 basis points year-on-year, driven by lower material cost, cost efficiencies and mix improvement, while we continue to invest behind brand building, new businesses and new I: products

items.statement: Commodity inflation expected 1-2% in Q3; LEAP cost savings program offsetting aluminum price increases
items.quote: A bit on quarter 3, yes, aluminum continues to really -- we see inflationary trend there. So there will be -- quarter 3, broadly, the expectation is there will be some level of commodity inflation, but will be more range bound within 1% to 2%.

items.statement: October VAHAN market share 31.6% (+3.7% YoY); nearly 1 million retail units in October
items.quote: Our VAHAN market share in October expanded by 3.7% year-on-year to 31.6%.

items.statement: Global business dispatches grew 77% (3x industry); now present in 52 countries including Europe and UK
items.quote: The company's Global Business continued its upward growth trajectory during the quarter with dispatch growth of 77%, which is 3x the industry growth, led by Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Colombia.

items.statement: Scooter share (ICE+EV) ~40%; new sub-segments emerging; 12 new models/variants launched for festive
items.quote: You're right. I think overall, ICE plus EVs put together, the scooter contribution has been pretty robust. In fact, ICE alone also has done really well.

items.statement: EV market share 11.7% (+6.8% YoY); #1 or #2 in 50+ towns; 20%+ share in 48 towns
items.quote: The EV business delivered its highest ever quarterly market share of 11.7%, which is up 6.8% year-on-year, riding on the success of Vida VX2.

items.statement: Average selling price up 4.2% YoY and 2.4% QoQ driven by mix and pricing; EV price increase effective Nov 5
items.quote: The average selling price increased 4.2% year-on-year and 2.4% quarter-on-quarter, driven by mix and pricing.

items.statement: Receivables reduced to ~12 days from 30 days YoY; highest ever festive collections; lowest inventory in years
items.quote: we've also seen the highest ever c ollections during the festive period, thereby bringing our receivables in the Indian business to close to 12 days compared to what it was 30 days in the previous years, right

items.statement: Continued investment in Premium, Scooters, EV portfolio, brand building, Hero 2.0 and Premia
items.quote: Moving forward, our journey of investment behind growth will continue. We remain consistent in our commitment towards investing in Premium, Scooters, EV portfolio, brand building and to improve customer service in store with Hero 2.0 and Premia.

items.statement: Harshavardhan Chitale appointed new CEO effective January 2026
items.quote: We are delighted to announce the appointment of Mr. Harshavardhan Chitale, our new Chief Executive Officer effective January '26.

items.statement: GST reduction announced pre-festive significantly uplifted consumer sentiment and retail momentum
items.quote: At the outset, I would like to express our sincere gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Bhai Modi ji and Honourable Finance Minister for announcing the GST reductions ahead of the festive season.

items.statement: ABS mandate discussions ongoing with government; positive conclusion expected shortly
items.quote: We are in talks with the government. And I think shortly, we should come to a very positive conclusion, which will be far more effective technological intervention.

items.statement: First-time buyers rose to 81% during festive vs 70-72% average; entry segment share expanded from 7.9% to 9.2%
items.quote: A numerical indicator, first-time buyers generally hover around 70%, 72% on an average. In the festive, it went up to 81%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow ₹4,111 cr in H1 FY26; parts/accessories revenue ₹1,533 cr (+5% YoY)
items.quote: Our continued focus on cash management resulted in delivering strong cash from operations, strengthening our financial performance, operating cash generated in first half is ₹4,111 crores.

items.statement: Gained market share across all segments - Entry, Deluxe, Premium, Scooters, EVs, Global Business
items.quote: We gained market share dispatch across all key segments - Entry, Deluxe, Premium, Scooters, EVs and even our Global Business.

items.statement: Industry growth may taper from festive peak but fundamentals strong; no decline expected in H2
items.quote: It could possibly not sustain at the October, November period that you have seen, industry did 30 lakhs in October, right. So from there on, you might possibly see a decline, but from -- but I mean, clearly, we expect a much better H2.

items.statement: Global business premium contribution 40%+; 80-20 strategy focusing on top 10 markets yielding 12% share
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that our premium product contribution is 40% + in the global markets, right. And the premium portfolio, therefore, continues to really outgrow the markets.

items.statement: Financing penetration stable for full year; temporary festive shift to cash customers
items.quote: So overall, from a full year perspective, financing largely is stable. Of course, we'll see temporary ups and downs. I mean some cash customers have come out more in the festive.

items.statement: Dow Jones Sustainability Index score improved to 75 in FY25 from 69 in FY24
items.quote: Dow Jones Sustainability Index score further improved to 75 in FY'25 from 69 in FY'24, reflecting HMCL's leadership towards sustainable business growth.

items.statement: Netherlands 3Q realisation expected ~€30/t lower QoQ; coking coal consumption cost €5-10/t lower QoQ; 4Q expected much better
items.quote: As far as the Netherlands is concerned, 3Q guidance just now is about €30 per ton lower in 3Q compared to 2Q but we expect 4Q to be much better because of what I said earlier. Coking coal consumption costs in Netherlands will be down about €5 – €10 per ton

items.statement: UK 3Q prices seen flattish QoQ; EBITDA breakeven in 4Q FY26 unlikely without government policy action
items.quote: If there are no actions from the government, it will be difficult to get EBITDA breakeven by 4QFY26. But if there is some action similar to what is being done in Europe, then of course we can move closer to that

items.statement: India standalone EBITDA margin improved ~80 bps QoQ to 24% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Tata Steel Standalone Revenues for the quarter stood at Rs 34,680 crores and EBITDA was Rs 8,394 crores, reflecting a QoQ improvement in EBIDTA margin of ~80 bps to 24%.

items.statement: Neelachal Ispat EBITDA margin 20% in Q2 FY26, up 17% QoQ
items.quote: Our wholly owned subsidiary, Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited recorded ~Rs 260 crores of EBITDA for the quarter, up 17% QoQ and reflecting an EBIDTA margin of 20%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 280 bps in H1 FY26 to ~15%
items.quote: Our consolidated revenues for the half year were Rs 1,11,867 crores and EBITDA was Rs 16,585 crores at a consolidated EBIDTA of Rs. 11,037 per ton reflecting an EBITDA margin of about 15%. The EBIDTA margin expanded by 280 bps in the first half of this financial year

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex ~Rs 7,000 cr; Netherlands decarbonisation project major spend not in next couple of years even after FID
items.quote: During the half year, we generated ~Rs 10,000 crores of operating cashflows after interest, tax and working capital. Of this, we spent about Rs 7,000 crores on capital expenditure

items.statement: India safeguard duty notification expired Nov 2025; awaiting government advice; industry seeks support for continued investment
items.quote: The notification I think has expired in November and we are waiting for advice from the government on safeguard. We are working with them and let's see where it takes us

items.statement: Richer mix: Kalinganagar cold rolling mill ramping, 1 of 2 galvanising lines commissioned (2nd by Dec), combi mill 0.5 MTPA commissioned last quarter; BlueScope acquisition adds downstream synergies
items.quote: The cold rolling mill has just started ramping up in Kalinganagar. The galvanising line, one of the two lines has come in, the other one will come by December. We have a combi mill, which is a state-of-the-art long products plant of half a million ton which has just got commissioned last quarter

items.statement: Netherlands phase 2 decarbonisation has no government funding commitment; timing and technology at company discretion
items.quote: The answer is yes. This tailor-made agreement is specifically towards phase one and our commitment is to do the phase one. The phase two is left to the Company to decide as to when and as far as timing, the technology to be used, the project cost to be done etc.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Rs 11,037/t in H1 FY26; India Q2 EBITDA margin 24%; Neelachal EBITDA margin 20%
items.quote: Our consolidated revenues for the half year were Rs 1,11,867 crores and EBITDA was Rs 16,585 crores at a consolidated EBIDTA of Rs. 11,037 per ton reflecting an EBITDA margin of about 15%

items.statement: H1 FY26 operating cashflow after interest, tax and working capital ~Rs 10,000 cr
items.quote: During the half year, we generated ~Rs 10,000 crores of operating cashflows after interest, tax and working capital

items.statement: Netherlands cost transformation delayed on people restructuring timeline due to ongoing Central Works Council discussions
items.quote: However, we are delayed on the people restructuring timeline an d the consequential benefits of the same in this year, as the discussions with the Central Works Council are ongoing

items.statement: UK EAF cost position to improve by £150 per ton; UK business should be EBITDA positive long-term
items.quote: when we did the EAF, the larger point was, we said the cost position of UK will improve by about £150 per ton, okay, because we were taking out a lot of fixed costs, we were using locally available scrap instead of imported iron ore, coal et c.

items.statement: Kalinganagar volume effect benefit of Rs 2,500 crore targeted by end of FY26
items.quote: by the time we exit this year, we should be able to get there and that's our target on the volumes anyways.

items.statement: Net Debt to EBITDA target maintained at 2.75-3x on sustained basis
items.quote: between 2.75 and 3 is where we would like to maintain ourselves on a more sustained basis.

items.statement: No major price increase factored for December; operating close to November levels
items.quote: We've not factored in major price increase in December. We are saying that we operate close to November levels.

items.statement: TSN EAF engineering capex estimate expected by May-June; FID pending policy clarity and new government
items.quote: Engineering will be known on capex somewhere around, say, May or June. That's my best estimate at this point of time.

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF acquired for ~Rs 3,000 crore for ~1 million ton capacity
items.quote: you're getting almost a million ton for Rs 3,000 crores or less.

items.statement: UK EAF capacity of 3 million tons with 10-15% exports considered optimal
items.quote: 3 million tons with maybe 10 -15% exports is fine. And optimally also, that was the right capacity for us.

items.statement: Pipe business heading towards 1.5 million tons including leased capacity; ambition to reach 4 million tons
items.quote: today, I think the pipes business is heading towards 1.5 million tons, which includes the pipe business that we acquired through Bhushan plus all the leased -out capacities.

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF typical EBITDA Rs 5,000-7,000 per ton; lower than integrated operations but logistics savings help
items.quote: Typically, an EAF kind of operation in the Indian context, I would say, is more of Rs 5,000 to 7,000 EBITDA per ton kind of thing.

items.statement: Cost transformation target unchanged at Rs 5,450 crore achieved in H1; Netherlands compliance lower due to employee restructuring delays
items.quote: our target is the same. I mentioned when we started this that it is a n 18-months program. Obviously, the work that can be done is being pursued across the geographies.

items.statement: India steel demand growing at double-digit (10%) vs GDP 6.5-7%; supply additions causing near-term price pressure
items.quote: demand is quite strong and India is the only major country which is showing double-digit growth in steel consumption.

items.statement: UK metal-over-margin shrunk significantly due to cheaper imports flooding market
items.quote: that metal over margin is an important thing , that has shrunk significantly and that's purely because of the fact that cheaper imports are flooding the market.

items.statement: Iron ore security: 500-600 mt captive reserves beyond 2030; engaging OMC/NMDC for long-term arrangements; Canada mine optionality
items.quote: we already have some iron ore. We have maybe about 500-600 million tons of iron ore with us today, which is available beyond 2030 based on our existing mines.

items.statement: UK government needs to realign import quotas to domestic consumption; EU quotas tightened but UK quotas unchanged
items.quote: the quotas have not been changed even though the demand has shrunk over the last few years, unlike EU where the quotas have been 15 changed and have been tightened further

items.statement: TSN decarbonization JLoI bipartisan; new Dutch government expected to honor commitments; tailor-made agreement pending
items.quote: it is certainly the assumption that we are working in, that the government will continue to work on it because it's of national importance and it is something of a commitment.

items.statement: Ferrochrome unit sold due to Sukinda mine underground capex and MDPA changes; exiting mining lease to rebalance sources
items.quote: our call was to exit the mining lease of Sukinda because of the high underground capex. And once we took that decision, it was necessary to rebalance the sources of mining.

items.statement: BlueScope 50% stake acquired at ~7x underlying EBITDA; strategic for downstream consolidation and product mix enrichment
items.quote: if you look at it from an underlying EBITDA perspective, it is 7x, which from a value-added downstream perspective is what the numbers will effectively look at.

items.statement: Significant cash outflow on dividend this quarter; any deleveraging opportunity will be pursued but balanced with growth investments
items.quote: This quarter we had a significant amount of cash outflow on our dividend, which is an obligation that we are clearly focused to fulfil as part of servicing investors.

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF CO2 footprint 0.2-0.3 t/t vs Jamshedpur 2.1-2.2 t/t and Netherlands 1.6 t/t; carbon pricing to improve economics
items.quote: Ludhiana is going to be at 0.2 tons of CO2 per ton of steel , because it will use green energy.

items.statement: UK profitability challenged if current abnormal market conditions persist; expecting resolution in next few months
items.quote: If today's situation continues forever, of course, there's a challenge. But we don't expect today's situation in the market to continue forever.

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF output primarily for retail market with higher realisations; future EAFs could target alloy steels for automotive in West/South
items.quote: pretty much all that is produced there is going to the retail market where our realisations are higher than it is in the project market.

items.statement: UK downstream network tied to base grade HRC for value addition; capacity cannot be lowered due to integrated downstream needs
items.quote: we have a very tied -in downstream network of our own, which uses the base grade HRC or the quality of HRC for further value addition.

items.statement: India capacity additions in big chunks (5mt Tata, JSW, JSPL) creating near-term supply overhang; medium-term balance expected
items.quote: we've added 5 million tons, JSW has added something, JSPL has added something. So, you will go through years when a lot of new capacity is coming on stream.

items.statement: Balance sheet managed well with focus on working capital and profitability across geographies
items.quote: we are managing our balance sheet pretty well under the circumstances in the context of our operating cash flows, with all geographies being focused on working capital and profitability.

items.statement: Netherlands employee restructuring slower than planned affecting cost transformation compliance; working with CWC to resolve
items.quote: The compliance in Netherlands is lower, as I mentioned, because of the employee restructuring going slower than what we had planned.

items.statement: Thailand EAF profitability surged post-earthquake due to quality-driven closure of local competitors; Tata Steel Thailand seen as quality leader
items.quote: Tata Steel Thailand is seen as one of the best quality producers of steel in Thailand, has a good name, we have the Tata Tiscon brand operating in Thailand as well and they got the benefit of that.

items.statement: Management targets mid-teen EBITDA margin in the mid-term and expects H2 FY26 volumes and margins to improve over H1.
items.quote: We will continue to make our best efforts to progress on our strategic goal of delivering profitable growth and reach mid-teen EBITDA in the mid-term.

items.statement: MHCV industry grew 7% YoY and LCV 2-4 ton grew 15% YoY in October, indicating strong H2 momentum.
items.quote: The industry momentum has further built up in October, with MHCV and LCV 2-4 ton industry growing Y-o-Y by 7% and 15% respectively.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY to 12.1%, a record level, driven by cost savings and price realization.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 12.1%, higher by 50 basis points against Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Switch India bus order book stood at 1,650 units at end of H1 FY26.
items.quote: Order book for the buses at the end of H1 FY '26 stood at 1,650 units.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 capex guided at around Rs 1,000 crore; H1 capex was Rs 658 crore with no subsidiary investments.
items.quote: You can expect around Rs. 1,000 crores of CAPEX which is getting incurred.

items.statement: LCV capacity to be raised from 80,000 to 110,000-120,000 units in 6-9 months via process changes; bus body-building capacity to reach 20,000+ units/year after AP and Lucknow ramp-up.
items.quote: Our current capacity is close to 80,000 units on the light commercial vehicles. But we have already laid out a plan to increase this capacity to 110,000-120,000 units without much of an investment.

items.statement: AC cabin cost increase has been passed on to customers, protecting margins.
items.quote: In fact, your question on this AC cost hike, in fact, we have passed it on to the cu stomers. That is why the margins are holding out, Chandru

items.statement: Non-truck businesses now contribute ~50% of revenue (buses 13%, LCV 12%, spares 10%, exports 7-8%), down from 55-58% truck share a few years ago, and are margin-accretive.
items.quote: Now, roughly 50% of the revenue comes from the non-truck businesses. With buses, about 13%; light commercial vehicles, about 12%; spares, about 10% and exports, about 7%-8%.

items.statement: Receivables reduced by ~Rs 500 crore YoY; operating working capital brought down ~50% YoY; inventory maintained to support demand.
items.quote: at the receivables in particular , I think there is a Rs. 500 crore reduction in receivables only in the last 1 year from September 24 to September 25

items.statement: Net cash position of ~Rs 1,000 crore at end of Q2, a positive swing of ~Rs 1,500 crore YoY.
items.quote: Our cash position net of debt continues to be positive at the end of Q2 at roughly Rs. 1,000 crores, reflecting a positive swing of roughly Rs. 1,500 crores on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance merger with NXT Digital cleared by RBI; listing expected minimum by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Timeline, we said in the earlier conference call that it could take a minimum of the Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Export volumes grew 45% YoY in Q2 and 38% in H1; FY26 target 18,000 units; mid-term target 25,000 units at 20% CAGR.
items.quote: This year, Balaji told you that we have grown more than 35%+ so far in H1. And therefore, to achieve 18,000 units over a base of 15-15.5 should be achievable.

items.statement: GST rate cut from 28% to 18% on trucks and buses reduced ownership cost; broader GST rationalization expected to boost freight demand.
items.quote: GST 2.0 added cheer to the festive season on two accounts , the rate rationalization from 28% to 18% brought down the cost of owning new trucks and buses, while GST rate reduction in several other categories of goods is expected to increase the overall freight demand.

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduction underway; management states promoters committed to further reduce pledged shares.
items.quote: They are trying to reduce the pledge shares. Some reduction has already happened, I think in the recent past, but they are committed to reduce it further.

items.statement: OHM operating 1,100+ electric buses with 98%+ fleet availability; added 250+ buses in Q2; targets 2,500+ buses in next 12 months.
items.quote: OHM, our eMaaS subsidiary is now operating more than 1,100 electric buses with fleet availability of 98% plus. During the quarter, OHM added more than 250 buses to the operating fleet and is progressing well on its target of operating 2,500 plus buses within the next 12 months.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 1 per share recommended by Board.
items.quote: Due to continued improvement in company's fiscal performance and better outlook for the ongoing years, the Board of Ashok Leyland has recommended an interim dividend of INR 1 per share.

items.statement: Festive season demand was robust with record bookings and sustained consumer confidence.
items.quote: The festive season has been particularly very encouraging for us, driven by robust demand, record bookings and the sustained consumer confidence and a clear reflection of brand strength and the market trust we have built over the period of time.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward percentage guidance but sees demand holding up well into November.
items.quote: In terms of percentages, we don't give the forward guidance, Chandramouli, but I can tell you, post the GST, the demand and the inquiry and the demand is holding up really very well for us.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 327,067 motorcycles in Q2 FY26, up from 225,317 in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: During this quarter, we sold 3,27,067 motorcycles as against 2,25,317 in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Domestic sales were 292,703 units in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Out of this, in India alone, we sold 2,92,703 units.

items.statement: International volumes were 34,364 units in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: In our international markets, our volumes stood at 34,364 units during this quarter.

items.statement: Royal Enfield holds ~84% market share in the midsize motorcycle segment.
items.quote: We continue to gain market share across board, particularly in the midsize motorcycle segment, where Royal Enfield has been able to continue its dominance at about 84% market share.

items.statement: Festive months (Sep-Oct) retail sales reached ~2.49 lakh motorcycles, best ever.
items.quote: And with over about 2.49 lakh motorcycles we sold during the festive months of September and October, our best ever festive performance, we have achieved a milestone that speaks volume about our momentum and unwavering love riders have for the brand.

items.statement: Commodity cost pressure of ~40 bps (precious metals, aluminum alloys) offset by ~50 bps price increase benefit.
items.quote: We have had a 40 basis point impact as far as commodity prices, mainly led by both precious metals and aluminum alloys and all that. And overall, I think it's been offset. We've also had a bit of price increase, which has also given us a positive impact of about 50 basis points.

items.statement: Inquiry-to-booking conversion improved ~10 percentage points to 29-30% post-GST cut.
items.quote: Our walk-in conversion has gone up, our tele conversion has gone up, our online conversion has gone up. So the E2B, we normally say enquiry to the booking conversion has actually seen a 10 percentage point growth during this point of time. It used to be about 20%, 21%. It has gone to about 29%, 30%.

items.statement: Rural retail growth slightly higher than urban during festive; South and East regions showed strong pickup.
items.quote: During the festive time, the rural had been slightly higher than the urban. But once again, we have to wait for some more time. But for us, one good thing which has happened during this time is that the South has not been doing very well for us. Now South also has picked up. We have seen very good growth. And East has done really, really well for us during this time.

items.statement: VECV Q2 FY26 sales 21,901 units (+5.4% YoY); H1 sales 43,511 units (+7.5% YoY).
items.quote: I'm very happy to share that at VECV, we recorded our highest ever second quarter sales of 21,901 units exceeding our previous record of 20,774 units in Q2 of financial year 2025 with a growth of 5.4%.

items.statement: VECV #1 in light & medium duty trucks with 34.8% market share (10,096 units in Q2).
items.quote: We are now at number 1 position in light and medium duty trucks with sales of 10,096 units in Q2 and a market share of 34.8% in this segment.

items.statement: VECV heavy-duty truck market share 10.5% in Q2; H1 volumes flat at 9,961 units.
items.quote: Our heavy-duty truck volumes grew 3.5% in Q2 in the same quarter of previous year. Our market share in this segment in Q2 stood at 10.5%.

items.statement: VECV bus sales 3,217 units in Q2; H1 sales 9,222 units (+1.9% YoY).
items.quote: We made sales of 3,217 units in our bus division. And with this, our first half sales are 9,222 units with a growth of 1.9% against 9,053 units in first half '25.

items.statement: VECV parts business (Eicher + Volvo) grew 11.8% QoQ.
items.quote: In our parts business, both Eicher and Volvo combined, we recorded a robust growth of 11.8% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: VECV electric truck (Pro X) deliveries 244 units in Q2, 436 in H1; ~24% share in small 2-3.5T EV market.
items.quote: Sales of Eicher Pro X electric trucks continued to gain traction, even though the overall electric vehicle market has continued to be very small. It is just 1.5% of the 2 to 3.5 tonne market. And within that, we have delivered 244 units in Q2 and 436 units in H1. In some of the months, our market share in this small market has been 24%.

items.statement: VECV exports 1,823 units in Q2 (+61.3% YoY); H1 exports 3,259 units vs 2,322 prior year.
items.quote: Eicher tractor and buses exported 1,823 units in Q2, up 61.3% over Q2 of previous year. Despite political disruptions in Southeast Asian markets, YTD exports stand at 3,259 units against 2,322 units in H1 of previous year.
