items.quote: I would say most of the auto components are not inc luded. And lately, when he introduced the new tariff for commercial vehicles, on that, he's -- from 10%, he's taken it up to 50% on commercial vehicles. So what we supply to come in, which was at 10% earlier, that will go to 50%, but the customer is bearing that cost

items.statement: Long-term debt increased to INR 330 crores for Hosur greenfield project; consolidated debt stable at INR 670 crores; repaying INR 100 crores annually
items.quote: Simultaneously, you would have noticed that in shor t-term borrowings, there is a reduction. And in fact, there are 2 reasons why long-term borrowings have risen because there is a greenfield project that is undergoing in Hosur. So for that, we have taken the loan that is for capacity expansion and new business. And at consolidated level, if you see at the total debt level, it stays at the same le

items.statement: Long-term borrowings to increase this year for Hosur project but decrease from next year onwards
items.quote: So this year, you will see some increase in the long-term borrowi ngs. But next year onwards, it will come down

items.statement: Working capital reduced continuously over last 4-6 quarters
items.quote: You would have noticed for last 4 to 6 quarters, we have been reducing on working capital front.

items.statement: Land monetization of 26-27 acres targeting >INR 1,500 crores; rejected INR 400 crore offer; shifting costs and timeline of 1-1.5 years
items.quote: But we told them that we want to cross INR1,500 crores in any case.

items.statement: GST reduction from 28% to 18% in September 2025 improved auto affordability and demand
items.quote: Retail inflation softened to around 0.25% in October and the GST rate reduction from 28% to 18% in September '25 contributed to improved affordability in the automobile, supportin g the overall industry demand

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy across key auto segments; OEMs announcing large investments in India
items.quote: On the domestic front, demand remained healthy acr oss the key automotive segments. Our long-standing OEM partnership and foc used education helped us to capture momentum in the

items.statement: Revenue guidance conservative due to potential customer project delays
items.quote: If some customer delays it, then we normally cut the probably figure there. So I'm taking a little conservative and say 3,000 plus.

items.statement: Reiterated guidance of approximately USD 275 million revenue from utility bedding and US brand business over next 3 years
items.quote: On our 2028 guidance ; we reiterate our earlier guidance of achieving approximately USD 275 million in revenues from the utility betting segment and the US brand business over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Guidance of approximately USD 175 million annual revenue from utility bedding business by 2028
items.quote: We remain confident in our previously stated guidance of achieving approximately USD 175 million in annual revenues from the utility bedding business by 2028.

items.statement: Expect core business margins to return to 15-16% levels in 6-9 months as markets stabilize
items.quote: As markets stabilize, hopefully in the next, I would say, 6 to 9 months, then margins will go back to 15% to 16% levels on our core business.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan of approximately Rs 200 crores, with Rs 80-85 crores spent so far; only maintenance capex planned for FY27
items.quote: If you go to our investor deck, we had a total CAPEX plan this year of approximately 200 odd crores, out of which 100 crores or 99 crores was our Greenfield project in North Carolina, where we have spent half of that money right now.

items.statement: North Carolina Greenfield facility (USD 15 million investment, 18 million pillows annual capacity) expected operational late Q3 or early Q4 FY26
items.quote: Regarding our third manufacturing facility in North Carolina in the United States, which was initially scheduled to commence operations in September 2025, there has been a minor delay. The facility is now expected to become opera tional during late Q3 FY26 or early Q4 FY26

items.statement: Utility bedding facilities at approximately 60% capacity utilization across two US manufacturing facilities
items.quote: Despite the challenging backdrop, we maintained approximately 60% capacity utilization across both the existing US manufacturing facilities.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 volumes expected to be similar to Q2 FY26 (25.2 million meters) based on rolling forecast and purchase orders ~50 days before shipment
items.quote: So, at this point of time, our 3rd Quarter looks very similar to our 2nd Quarter in terms of volume . So, there are similar numbers.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11.4% in Q2 FY26 from 12.3% in Q1 FY26 due to tariff impact; margin pressure expected to continue until end of year
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was 11.4% versus 12.3% in the previous quarter. We expect margin pressure to continue until the end of this year.

items.statement: Utility bedding target EBITDA margin 15-16%; brand business target 17-18%; expect breakeven by Q4 FY26
items.quote: On the pillow business, we expect an EBITDA margin of 15% to 16%. And on the brand side, 17% to 18% is our internal target.

items.statement: US retailers are nimble-footed, evaluating product mix and inventory levels; situation fluid with holiday season approaching
items.quote: As we see it right now, we are seeing the retailers being very nimble -footed and trying to find what is the new normal. This is new for everybody for whatever product portfolios they are selling.

items.statement: 50% tariff on India imposed late August 2025 impacted export competitiveness; additional 25% Russian oil penalty led to temporary customer support on case-to-case basis
items.quote: The tariff challenge persists in our core business. The 50% tariff imposed on India in late August 2025 has impacted India's export competitiveness in the US market.

items.statement: Product mix shifts and down-trading observed since Q4 FY25; average selling pressure continued but expected to stabilize
items.quote: We have been observing product mix shifts and down-trading since Q4 2025, and we have proactively navigated these changes to support our partners and maintain business continuity.

items.statement: Signed licensing agreement with Tommy Hilfiger (sixth licensed brand, four added in last 2 years); Wamsutta relaunch sold in all 50 US states
items.quote: For our utility betting segment, we are very pleased to announce the signing of a licensing agreement with the Tommy Hilfiger brand. This marks our sixth licensed brand with four added in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Added 700 new retail counters for Boutique Living and Layers in Q2 FY26; expanded product portfolio in bath and top of bed segments
items.quote: We have also expanded our retail footprint for both Boutique Living and Layers, adding 700 new counters during Q2, which has enabled deeper penetration in key domestic markets.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by Rs 175 crores in H1 FY26; net debt to equity ratio at 0.34x in September 2025
items.quote: There has been around Rs. 175 crores of debt reduction in H1 FY26. Net debt to equity ratio stood at Rs. 0.34X in September 2025.

items.statement: Cotton below 32mm duty-free until Dec 31, 2025; expect continuation but no official news yet; most imported cotton is 32mm+ which was already duty-free
items.quote: However, cotton below 32 mm in length is duty -free up to 31 st December this year. We do expect it to continue but there is no news as of now.

items.statement: India FTAs with Japan, Australia, Middle East signed; UK FTA done but needs UK Parliament ratification; EU FTA expected by end of year or early next year
items.quote: India has never been in a better position than before with having a free trade agreement done with Japan in the recent past, Australia, Middle East and now two more. UK is done but has to get ratified by the UK Parliament and then EU hopefully will be done by the end of this year, early next year.

items.statement: Core non-US business now contributes 30% of overall revenue mix; expanding footprint in Australia, Japan, Middle East, Europe, UK
items.quote: Our core non- US business now contributes to 30% of our overall revenue mix for the core business.

items.statement: Utility bedding and US brand segments combined contribution increased to 17% of revenues in Q2 FY26 from 13% in Q1 FY26 (~40% QoQ increase); run rate ~USD 85 million per annum
items.quote: Our utility bedding and USA branded segments continue to scale with their combined contribution increasing to 17% of revenues in Q2 FY26 compared to 13% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Sales volume grew 7% QoQ to 25.2 million meters in Q2 FY26; total income grew 12% QoQ to Rs 1,082 crores
items.quote: Sales volume for Q2 FY26 stood at 25.2 million meters versus 23.6 million meters in Q1 FY26, a growth of around 7% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Tariff-related challenges may continue for next 1-2 quarters; full tariff impact just setting in; consumer reaction to price increases uncertain
items.quote: Tariff-related challenges may continue for the next one or two quarters. Until the environment stabilizes, we continue to f ocus on operational efficiency, sustainability, and maintaining our market share

items.statement: Net debt to equity ratio at 0.34x in September 2025 after Rs 175 crores debt reduction in H1 FY26
items.quote: Net debt to equity ratio stood at Rs. 0.34X in September 2025.

items.statement: Invested significantly in human talent and infrastructure for US subsidiary; doubled New York showroom to 20,000 sq ft; added performance marketing for D2C brands
items.quote: We have invested a fair amount and you can see that even if you compare our employee cost of previous 6 months, first half to this 6 months, the numbers are there.

items.statement: Finalized purchase price allocation for two US units acquired last year; balance sheet numbers for March 2025 reinstated retrospectively
items.quote: We have also reinstated the balance sheet number for March 2025. This is due to finalization of the purchase price allocation of our two units which we acquired in US last year.

items.statement: Utility bedding ~2/3 and brands ~1/3 of USD 85 million run rate; brand business includes Waverly, Gaiam, Wamsutta; utility includes Beautyrest, Tommy Hilfiger
items.quote: Just from a thumb rule perspective, at this point of time, approximately it's two-third, one-third. That means utility is two-third of that number and one-third is brands, roughly.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin was 14.9% vs 16.3% last year; excluding 1.2% impact from strategic initiatives, margin is close to prior year.
items.quote: So, the EBITDA in its current value is 14.9% of revenue compared to 16.3% last year and if I add this 1.2%, which is our initiatives that we're running, our EBITDA percentage is very close to last year.

items.statement: Management targets ~16% EBITDA margin excluding special initiatives, in line with five-year-old guidance.
items.quote: Well, right now if I remove the special initiatives that we are running, we know we are doing that deliberately, we are currently at around 16%, which is what we said we will achieve as a guidance that we gave five years ago right.

items.statement: Management will provide updated revenue and EBITDA guidance by Q3 or full-year FY26 call.
items.quote: So why don't you give me a little bit of time till the either the third quarter call or the full year call for me to give you a much more well thought through guidance on revenue over what period and EBITDA over what period.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 600 cr over 5 years on track; INR 250 cr firmed up but delayed ~12 months due to hard rock at site.
items.quote: We said INR 600 crores over the next five years. We said INR 250 crores, but INR 250 crorea out of the INR 600 crores is firmed up. The balance INR 350 crores we are thinking through it.

items.statement: INR 250 cr capex tranche delayed by approximately 12 months due to hard rock encountered during execution.
items.quote: Yeah, yeah, so probably 12 months.

items.statement: India industrial products growing faster than construction/mining; inquiry pipeline strong but conversion slower; textile segment muted due to tariffs.
items.quote: So, what you're seeing, Ravi, is a growth consolidated across all products. So, if you look at the industrial products, the growth has been higher compared to our construction and mining and whatever, yeah?

items.statement: Europe demand muted; management assumes H2 similar to H1 and has resized cost structure accordingly.
items.quote: So, we are planning on the basis that the second-half will be roughly similar to the first half even though our performance towards the end of the second quarter was actually better than the prior months.

items.statement: North America grew well across verticals except distribution; Q3 expected to be strong with green shoots in distribution.
items.quote: North America has grown very well for us across all verticals of the business except our distribution operation. But, there also we are beginning to see some green shoots. We think the third quarter will be strong.

items.statement: Middle East demand strong; pricing challenges corrected. Australia and Southeast Asia small contributors.
items.quote: Middle East continues to remain strong. We had some pricing challenges, which we have corrected, but otherwise the demand profile looks quite strong, and we are continuing to grow.

items.statement: Tariff impact fully mitigated at consolidated P&L level via cost reductions, price increases, and overhead savings; $9M annual EBITDA impact at steady state if no action taken.
items.quote: So just to summarize, if you look at a steady state one year, so let's take for example next financial year which is 2026-27, assuming a certain growth rate, the impact of tariff both from the exports from India to the US as well as from Italy to the US, the combined impact would be $ 9 million at an EBITDA level if we didn't do anything.

items.statement: If US tariffs drop from 50% to 25%, estimated $3M EBITDA benefit at consolidated level.
items.quote: So $ 3 million would be the benefit. That's my guesstimate. I don't have the numbers in front of me, yeah.

items.statement: Power and fuel optimization and renewable energy shift expected to save INR 5-6 cr annually.
items.quote: We have done an initiative on our power and fuel. We are not a very high-power consuming company, but nevertheless there is a significant chunk that is there and we are already having a significant part of our power as renewable. We're going to over index on that and that's going to give us about INR 5 to 6 crores of savings every year, right.

items.statement: In-house motor production to reach 75-80% of global volume by FY27.
items.quote: Close to 75 to 80% of the volume of motors, we will be making ourselves globally, right?

items.statement: Demand Match (stabilizer) launched in India as standard offering on new machines; retrofit program for 3-4k units/year planned for Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We think there is an opportunity for at least 3-4 thousand machines a year. Now, like I said, we have not prioritized that business now, we are now focusing mainly on launching the product built in the factory. Maybe in the third, fourth quarter we will start looking at the retrofit business.

items.statement: Low-cost compressor range (vs Chinese imports) in field validation; target launch by April 1 or Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We have an internal target to get it launched by the 1 st of April but definitely by the first quarter of next year, we should have the products in the market.

items.statement: Europe and US strategy shifting to hybrid direct+distributor model to increase customer-facing time and win rates; no acquisitions planned.
items.quote: We believe that a hybrid model of going direct in partnership with distributors is going to get us, put us more often in front of the customers and we have found that when we are in front of the customers, we win, right.

items.statement: Cash position improved in H1 FY26 driven by receivables reduction; inventory management gains expected in H2 via internal project.
items.quote: The bigger contributing factor in this particular quarter and the first half has been the reduction in our receivables. We managed our receivables well and we've brought it under control, and we expect that inventory management in Europe and in India will start gaining momentum by virtue of the project, one initiative that we are running internally.

items.statement: Cumulative Europe investment loss ~EUR 25M (~INR 250 cr) since inception.
items.quote: The total investment has been in the form of losses. We have lost close to 25 million euro, which is roughly about INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Europe headcount reduction underway; exit costs to hit P&L in H2 FY26, lower cost base from FY27.
items.quote: So those costs are going to be taken out during the rest of the quarters of this year, but we will not see an immediate P&L impact because there is a certain, you know, cost of letting people go and you know, the resettlement Costs are going to be involved.

items.statement: Aftermarket revenue share scales with installed base: ~30% in India (base 100) vs ~12% in newer markets (base 25); growth velocity key to profitability.
items.quote: In another country the aftermarket contribution is about 30% to revenue, yeah. Now if the installed base is 25 in another country, then the aftermarket contribution is around 12%, So as 25 moves to 100, 12 will start moving towards 30, right?

items.statement: Textile sector investment muted due to tariff uncertainty; broader industrial caution delaying capex decisions.
items.quote: Textile continues to remain a little muted. They were getting into the year itself with challenges, now with the tariff, their challenges have been even more. So, they are very muted in terms of investment.

items.statement: Europe and US growth rate insufficient; strategy reset underway to achieve higher market share (target 6-7% in US).
items.quote: The current strategy that has taken us to a 3% to 4% share of the European market is not going to take us to, let's say, to go to 6%, 7% share of the US market and we are looking at what should be the revised go to market strategy for ELGi in Europe, similarly in the US as well.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA negative in H1 FY26; North America near break-even at EBITDA level (excl. one-offs).
items.quote: I don't have the number in front of me, Harshit, but Europe was negative, and North America was almost break even, yeah.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 PAT INR 947M including one-off US property sale gain; ex-one-off PAT similar to prior year.
items.quote: So, if I include the one-off gain on sale of property, PAT is about INR 947 million for the quarter, which is roughly similar to what it was the previous year, previous quarter.

items.statement: Employee cost up 15% in Q2: 6% normal increment, 4% forex impact, 3% headcount addition; strategic initiatives consumed 1.2% of EBITDA.
items.quote: Employee cost seems to have gone up by 15%, but there is some explanation to that; 6% is the normal increase, increase in the euro exchange and the dollar exchange has contributed 4% to the employee cost increase and we have added 3% in headcount.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 722 crores as of 30 September 2025
items.quote: Our order book remains robust at around INR 722 crores as on 30th September 2025, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Omeras Global business via wholly owned step-down subsidiary HLE Surface Technologies GmbH, funded entirely through internal accruals
items.quote: The quarter marked an important milestone for HLE Glascoat as we completed the acquisition of the Omeras Global business through our wholly owned step-down subsidiary, HLE Surface Technologies GmbH, along with the shares of Omeras Store GmbH.

items.statement: NCLT approved scheme of amalgamation of Kinam Enterprise Private Limited with HLE Glascoat Limited effective 7 August 2023
items.quote: Further, we are pleased to inform you that the scheme of amalgamation of Kinam Enterprise Private Limited with HLE Glascoat Limited has been approved by the Honorable NCLT, Ahmedabad Bench, effective 7th August 2023, being the appointed date.

items.statement: Expect overall EBITDA margins of roughly 16% for H2 FY26, with second half historically contributing 55-60% of annual revenue
items.quote: On the business other than Omeras, I think our second half of the year should see improved EBITDA margins. We are expecting EBITDA margins for the overall business at about between -- roughly about 16%, which will be far more healthier than what we have declared in the first half.

items.statement: Expect Omeras business to reach breakeven or above by Q4 FY26
items.quote: I think on the Omeras business, we do not have a guidance for this particular year, except to say that by the end of the year, we should be at breakeven or above because as we said, we will need about 2 to 3 quarters to stabilize and grow this business.

items.statement: Expect full-year FY26 PAT margin in excess of 6.5% to 7%
items.quote: And I think at the PAT level, we would be -- it would be fair to say that number should be at a net for the year basis in excess of between 6.5% to 7%.

items.statement: Glass line segment EBIT margins currently 5-6% excluding Omeras; expect double-digit EBIT margins for entire glass line business by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect to be in double digit for the entire Glass-line business as a whole by quarter 4.

items.statement: Heat exchanger business stable annual EBIT margins expected at 20-22%; oil and gas orders at ~18% EBIT margin
items.quote: So the oil and gas -- to answer your question on the margins, our, let's say, stable annual margins for the heat exchanger business should be in the range of between 20% and 22%. The oil and gas margins are slightly lower given the higher volumes and are likely to be at about 18% is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Omeras gross margins in 50% range; expect healthy double-digit EBIT margins at optimal volumes
items.quote: The margins are in line with what you said. We are having gross margins in the 50% kind of a range. So it is only about building the volumes to an optimal level at which level we should see healthy double-digit margins.

items.statement: Glass line India capacity utilization at 60-65%, targeting ~80% by Q4 FY26; Filtration & drying at 80%, targeting 85-90% by Q4; Heat transfer at 65-70% by Q4
items.quote: We are currently -- in the glass line business, we are currently at between 60% and 65% capacity utilization. We are hoping to take that up to about 80% by quarter 4.

items.statement: Steady inquiries across all segments; pharma/API and techchem improving, agrochemicals under pressure; some US tariff uncertainty slowing capex decisions
items.quote: We continue to witness steady inquiries across all business segments, reflecting the strength of our offerings and growing market acceptance.

items.statement: Thaletec well positioned for US pharma capex opportunities; expanded US team and service capabilities
items.quote: Thaletec is very well positioned in the U.S. As you know that we have now been renewing our efforts in U.S. in the last 2-2.5 years in the U.S. market. And we have a track record now much bigger track record, I would say, than last time.

items.statement: Filtration & drying revenue INR 252 crores in H1 FY26 (60% annualized growth); Heat transfer revenue near INR 100 crores in H1 FY26 (>40% annualized growth)
items.quote: Filtration and drying revenue for the whole of FY '25 was at about INR 314 crores. For the first 6 months of this financial year, the revenue from filtration and drying is already at INR 252 crores, which is -- if you were to just annual numbers on an equated basis, still represents almost a 60% growth in business.

items.statement: Omeras Store order book EUR 4-4.5 million; delivered EUR 1.8 million in first 45 days; cancelled ~EUR 0.5 million non-viable orders
items.quote: The Omeras Store order book currently, as we said, is a very marginal order book, which is hardly about $4 million, $4.5 million – EUR 4- EUR 4.5 million, sorry.

items.statement: Omeras inquiry pipeline ~EUR 28 million and growing; conversion awaited on large projects and relationship building with new management
items.quote: At Omeras and Omeras Store, we had a very healthy visibility of inquiries, which was in the tune of 28 million 45 days ago, and that has only grown by a couple of million as we speak today.

items.statement: Kinam order book in excess of INR 100 crores as of September 2025; pipeline building for petrochemical/energy segment
items.quote: So the Kinam order book as of today as of September, sorry, is in excess of INR100 crores. So again, Kinam order book also looks very positive.

items.statement: Margin impact from competitive pricing on large high-value orders accepted in prior quarters, not from higher material costs
items.quote: The material cost impact that we discussed was not so much from a perspective of higher cost of material, but it was from a more competitive pricing that we had offered on some of these large projects that we have won in the past.

items.statement: Inventory days improved from 121 to 110 days; receivable days back to FY22 levels
items.quote: The inventory is actually on a number of days basis, we have actually reduced the number of days inventory from 121 days to 110 days. So there is an improvement in the inventory.

items.statement: Debt reduction strategy unchanged; prioritizing efficient working capital management, disciplined capital allocation, internal accrual funding
items.quote: Our debt reduction strategy for the full year remains unchanged from what we had outlined in the previous earnings concall. We continue to prioritize efficient working capital management, disciplined capital allocation and internal accrual funding to further strengthen our balance sheet.

items.statement: No further acquisitions planned currently; evaluating inbound opportunities but nothing on horizon
items.quote: Currently, there is nothing on the horizon in terms of any further acquisition. We obviously keep coming up with -- we keep getting approached with some interesting ideas. But for the moment, no, we are not looking at anything.

items.statement: Thaletec Germany and US order book >9 months; India glass line order book >5 months
items.quote: And for the Thaletec Germany and Thaletec U.S. business, it is in excess of 9 months, which is again very, very healthy.

items.statement: US tariff situation causing some players to delay capital investment decisions
items.quote: Some decisions or some players have been going slow in terms of capital investment. But other than that, the situation is encouraging overall, except for agrochemicals, as you mentioned.

items.statement: Expect Thaletec GLE business to grow at more than double-digit rate annually; India GLE rebuilding volumes; Omeras meaningful contribution expected in FY27
items.quote: They are looking good, and think we are looking at more than double-digit growth rate in Thaletec, GLE business on an annual basis. And this comes on the backing of a relatively large base of revenues already there.

items.statement: Competitive intensity lower in heat exchanger business due to larger addressable market across chemicals, pharma, metals, food, paints, energy
items.quote: So I would say the competitive intensity is lower in the heat exchanger business relative to the other 2 purely because we are looking at a larger addressable market size

items.statement: Thaletec capacity sufficient for 2-3 years at current 60% utilization; no major capex needed for peak revenue targets
items.quote: The comment on the capacity was from perspective to say that it's unlikely to require very large capex for may be 2 or 3 more years to come because we already have substantial capacity.

items.statement: Oil & gas heat exchanger order executed worth ~INR 60 crores spread over Q4 FY25, Q1 FY26, Q2 FY26
items.quote: The order size that we executed not just in quarter 2, but even partially in quarter 1 as well was an aggregate value of roughly about INR60 crores. I think it was -- the entire execution was spread over Q4, Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 margins impacted by initial losses at Omeras (INR 3.6 crores EBIT loss) and competitive pricing on prior orders; transient impact expected
items.quote: Initial losses incurred at the newly acquired business at HLE Surface Technologies GmbH Germany. These are factors which have led to this transient impact on the margins for this quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 booking value Rs 88.1 cr vs Rs 102.9 cr YoY; H1 FY26 bookings Rs 309 cr up 91% YoY
items.quote: The booking value for the quarter stood at Rs. 88.1 crores against Rs. 102.9 crores in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: H1 FY26 bookings Rs 309 cr up 91% YoY driven by Q1 launches
items.quote: H1 FY26 booking stood at Rs. 309 crores up 91% year on year supported by the successful launches in Q1.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 collections Rs 91.3 cr up 76% YoY
items.quote: Collections stood at Rs. 91.3 crores for the quarter up 76% year -on-year, driven by strong bookings in previous quarters and timely construction progress.

items.statement: Delivered 90 homes (1.19 lakh sq ft) in Q2 FY26, up 95% YoY
items.quote: We delivered 90 homes in Q2 FY26 totalling 1.19 lakh square feet, a growth of 95% year -on-year.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 construction spend Rs 37.3 cr up 11% YoY; H1 FY26 Rs 76.6 cr
items.quote: Construction spend for the quarter was Rs. 37.3 crores, up 11% from last year and H1 FY26 construction spend was Rs. 76.6 crores, indicating consistency in execution across projects.

items.statement: Eldeco Solano Gardens (50 acres, GDV Rs 1,000 cr) launch expected this year after environment clearance and RERA registration
items.quote: We are now preparing for the launch of our new township project Eldeco Solano Gardens on New Jail Road in Lucknow later this year. The project is spread over 50 acres with a n estimated gross development value of Rs. 1,000 crores and is expected to be a key growth driver for the coming years.

items.statement: Solano Gardens launch expected this month or next after RERA registration; villas to start this financial year
items.quote: Once the RERA registration comes, which I expect, I don't see any impediment there. Should be this month or next month and within 3-4 weeks of that, we should be launching that project.

items.statement: Solano Gardens average realization expected at Rs 5,000-6,000 per sq ft over project life
items.quote: As far as the average realization goes, I think over the life of the project, it will match the realization that we are currently having in the other projects. We declare that every quarter. So that's about Rs. 5,000-6,000 a square foot.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.7%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 5.5 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.7%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin 30% over next 12-18 months driven by Imperia Phase II revenue recognition
items.quote: So, about 30% is what you should be looking at over the next 12 to 18 months. Because Imperia 2 is the main project which is going to get recognized.

items.statement: Next quarter EBITDA margin could be 35-40% due to Imperia Phase II
items.quote: But next quarter, it could be as high as 35% or 40% because of Imperia 2.

items.statement: Imperia Phase II revenue recognition expected to start in Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: I think in the quarter that we are in right now, Q3 and Q4 is when the revenue recognition starts.

items.statement: Q2 realization drop to ~Rs 6,000/sq ft due to mix shift including EWS/LIG project Saksham
items.quote: This quarter, we recognize more of EWS which is economically weaker section kind of product that we did. And next qua rter, I think it will revert to normal

items.statement: Trinity current realization ~Rs 8,200/sq ft (super area); carpet ~Rs 12,000; sample apartment ready by February to drive price uptick
items.quote: It's around 8,000 plus some change, sir. 82 or something like that.

items.statement: Brand premium assessed at 20-30% vs peers due to trust and delivery track record
items.quote: What used to be 5% or 10% is now as much as 20% to 30%, which if you look at it, is a phenomenal premium, which one gets for the same product.

items.statement: Lucknow market undersupplied in Rs 60L-1.5Cr segment; absorption upside larger than pricing upside
items.quote: I think it's an undersupplied market. There is a lot of demand for quality housing, but that's in the region of Rs. 60 lakhs to Rs. 1.5 crores. items.statement: Management expects recovery from Q4 FY26 on exports and a good Rabi season for domestic, but keeps guidance muted due to weather uncertainty
items.quote: No, we had said that looking at how the H1 has gone, and I think we had a conversation as you rightly gathered, we expect the positive trajectory now coming from Q4 FY26 on Exports. On the Domestic business, we expec t a good Rabi , but I would put a cautious statement given the fast -changing weather conditions. So i f things go well, we should do well, but I would keep the guidance muted

items.quote: We expect the ETR to be in the range of 22%-23% for the next 2-3 years.

items.quote: However, it is also important to highlight that the growth of new products commercialised over the last three years has regis tered a decent 38% Y-o-Y growth in H1. We remain on track to commercialise 8 to 10 new molecules in the current fiscal, having commercialized 5 in H1

items.statement: H1 FY26 commercialised 5-6 new products in CSM with mix of agrochemical and non-AgChem; another 5-6 planned in H2

items.quote: In terms of late-stage programs, we have six.

items.quote: As you know, the increase in contract asset is in line with the customer delivery schedules, which are lined up for H2. items.quote: For this quarter, we reached to 55% capacity utilization for the paracetamol from the new plant, which was commenced in March this year. And by the end of this year means by March end, we expect to reach about 65% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Government targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030; PSU capex up 21% to Rs 86,000 cr in FY26 budget; 11 river interlinking DPRs ready
items.quote: India's target of 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 would double the current capacity. This would mean huge spends by government in this segment and the government has proposed to increase investment in power sector through its 9 PSUs by 21% to INR 86,000 crores in 2025-26 budget.

items.statement: Promoter pledge targeted to reduce to 50-60% post-March if lender discussions go well
items.quote: So, if discussions with lenders go well, we are targeting around pledge going down to around 50-60%.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR2.60 per share (par value INR5), taking total FY26 dividend to INR4.20 (84% of par value)
items.quote: At the outset, I am glad to announce the dividend approved by Board of Directors, INR2.60 on a share of par value of INR5. That makes a total dividend this year of INR4.20, which is 84% of the par value of share.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 throughput hit record 1.44 million TEUs; H1 FY26 throughput 2.73 million TEUs, up 11% YoY (EXIM +10.2%, domestic +13%)
items.quote: And the performance of the company in Q2 has been the ever highest throughput of 1.44 million TEUs, ever highest operating income and ever highest PAT in the history of the company in any quarter.

items.statement: Domestic demand was below expectations in H1 due to weak cement (monsoon), gunny bales and tiles; demand now picking up from Q3
items.quote: Domestic demand, domestic throughput has been slightly less as per our expectations. The main reasons were the less demand in cement due to monsoon season, which is now picking up. Then Gunny Bales also, there was less demand and tiles traffic also, there was less demand. Now demand has picked up, and we are having good loading in domestic.

items.statement: Rail freight margin improved from 26.17% to 27.80% YoY in H1; operating margin rose from 30.47% to 31.44%
items.quote: And at the same time, we have increased our margin also. So rail freight margin has increased from 26.17% to 27.80%. Operating margin has increased from 30.47% to 31.44%.

items.statement: Signed MOUs with UltraTech Cement and Adani Cement for bulk cement movement in tank containers; agreement with UltraTech for ~1 lakh tonne/month
items.quote: In domestic, we have achieved a big breakthrough by signing MOUs with 2 giants in cement sector. First is UltraTech Cement and second is Adani Cement for movement of bulk cement in tank containers.

items.statement: H1 capex spend INR420.35 crore vs budget INR860 crore; Board likely to increase budget for more infrastructure spending
items.quote: Capex, we have already spent INR420.35 crores as against a budget of INR860 crores. Board of Directors have deliberated and most probably, we will be increasing the budget because we have to increase more infrastructure spending.

items.statement: Commissioned 21 new high-speed rakes in H1 (total ~410); procured 3,000 containers (total ~56,000); 1,000 tank containers ordered (200 received, 500 more by mid-Dec)
items.quote: In the first half, we have commissioned 21 rakes, new rakes, high-speed rakes and which takes us total count to around 410 rakes. We have procured 3,000 containers, which takes our total count to around 56,000 container fleet for CONCOR.

items.statement: FY26 volume guidance unchanged: EXIM 10%, domestic 20%, overall 13% (on handling basis); EXIM already at 10.2% in H1, domestic at 13% needing 26-27% in H2
items.quote: Then guidance, I would like to keep them unchanged at 13%, EXIM 10%, domestic, 20%. We are quite optimistic and positive that we will achieve this guidance.

items.statement: WDFC connectivity to JNPT expected by March 2026 (delayed from Dec 2025); will double rail coefficient at JNPT within 1 year
items.quote: WDFC, connectivity to JNPT is likely by March 2026. Initially, it was December 2025, but it has been pushed by some accounts.

items.statement: Rail coefficient increased at all three major ports: JNPT 15.68% to 15.83%, Mundra 23.82% to 24.9%, Pipavav 57.42% to 58.14%
items.quote: See, rail coefficient is seeing an increase in all the 3 main container ports. JNPT also, it has increased from 15.68% to 15.83%. Mundra, it has increased from 23.82% to 24.9%. Pipavav, it has increased from 57.42% to 58.14%.

items.statement: EXIM realization ~INR27,000/TEU (originating); domestic realization INR57,000-58,000/TEU (up from INR56,000); EXIM lead down 2.5%
items.quote: If you see in EXIM, it is not INR14,000. It is in the range of INR27,000 per TEU, if you see the originating volume. As I already explained, EXIM, there is a drop of lead by 2.5%. So this is the basic reason for drop in realization.

items.statement: H1 empty running cost: EXIM INR52 crore (down from INR63.47 crore), domestic INR132.53 crore (down from INR142 crore); total INR184.53 crore vs INR205.47 crore YoY
items.quote: Similarly, empty running is for EXIM, first half, it is INR52 crores and domestic, it is INR132.53 crores. Total, it is INR184.53 crores. Last year, it was EXIM 63.47 crores; domestic INR142 crores, total INR205.47 crores.

items.statement: New EXIM reefer road-cum-rail service started from ICD Baddi to Mundra via Dadri; DPD movement from Khemli grew from nil to 275 TEUs
items.quote: We have commenced new EXIM reefer, road cum rail service from our ICD at Baddi to Mundra Port via Dadri. DPD movements will get a further boost, which will increase our volumes, and we have come up with a new liberalized policy of DPD, which will further bring us more business and more revenue.

items.statement: EXIM market share fell from 55.9% to 54.1%, domestic from 58% to 55.7%, total from 56.5% to 54.5% in H1; consciously avoided low-margin/low-lead business; lost wastepaper volumes at Mundra to competitors
items.quote: In EXIM, it has dropped for first half of the financial year. It has dropped from 55.9% to 54.1%. In domestic, it has dropped from 58% to 55.7%. And total, it has dropped from 56.5% to 54.5%, almost 200 basis points, it has dropped in total.

items.statement: Signed MOU with Vadhvan Port as common rail operator on nomination basis (port capacity ~24 mn TEUs, commissioning by 2030); MOU with Bhavnagar Port to operate container terminal (senior partner, functional from 2030)
items.quote: First is we have signed MOU with Vadhvan Port, where they have appointed us common rail operator on a nomination basis. We'll be designing the rail yard, managing the rail yard, everything rail operations at new Vadhvan Port which is coming on north of JNPT and it will be on DFC.

items.statement: Entered shipping sector: containers moving to Middle East (200 deployed, both-way loaded), >30% margin/container; Far East services starting soon
items.quote: Already 200 containers have gone to Middle East and most of them have come back loaded. So we are getting both way loaded direction, loaded traffic, which is a very big boost to our business. We are in talks with some companies in Far East and we will very soon starting our Far East services also. This is also a very high-margin business. We are getting more than 30% margin on every container.

items.statement: Double-stack trains grew 7.4% YoY in H1 (3,083 to 3,312); EXIM empty running down 18%, domestic down 6.7%, overall down 10.2%
items.quote: Then there has been a good growth in double-stack handling, almost 7.4% growth. Last year, we have handled 3,083 double-stack trains. This year, it is 3,312 in the same year-on-year basis.

items.statement: EXIM export growth H1: rice +41%, auto parts +18%, buffalo meat (reefer) +18%, aluminium ingots +13%; import growth: solar panel glass 5x, raw cotton 100%, auto parts +46%
items.quote: The export growth for the first half is very good in rice, almost 41% growth, auto parts, 18% growth, meat, that is buffalo meat, reefer, which goes in reefer containers, we have seen 18% growth and aluminium ingots, 13% growth.

items.statement: Indian Railways launched three end-to-end logistics initiatives with CONCOR as integral partner: assured transit train Delhi-Kolkata (80% occupancy, targeting 100%), Sonik goods shed development (4-year pilot), parcel service Mumbai-Kolkata
items.quote: CONCOR has been an integral part of new initiatives of end-to-end logistics launched by Indian Railways. Three initiatives have been launched by Honorable Minister of Railways for which CONCOR is an integral part.

items.statement: LLF payout ~INR400-420 crore/year, increasing 7% annually; Q2 LLF INR105 crore vs INR66 crore YoY; net LLF expected to remain in same range as terminals surrendered offset 7% increase
items.quote: See, LLF, as you know, it is increasing 7% every year, and our LLF is in the range of INR400 crores to INR420 crores every year. So in this year also, you may be seeing an increase in LLF for this particular quarter from INR66 crores to INR105 crores.

items.statement: Depreciation lower in Q2 due to LNG truck useful life change (8 to 15 years); Q1 had one-time depreciation from DR site retrospective capitalization
items.quote: You have rightly said depreciation, we have changed the rate for LNG trucks, which has some impact in this quarter. And in the last quarter, there was some capitalization, which was done retrospectively for our DR site, which was commissioned.

items.statement: Contingent liabilities rose from INR1,377 crore to INR2,120 crore in FY25, mainly court cases, claims, custom bonds; some LLF demands contested but not actual payable liability
items.quote: So these are related to various court cases and claims mainly and some custom bonds and all that. So maybe on account of that. The details, I'll have to see, but it is mainly -- our contingent liabilities are related to these elements only.

items.statement: Medium-term infrastructure target unchanged: 100 terminals, 500+ rakes, 70,000 containers by 2028
items.quote: Target for infrastructure for 2028 remains the same, 100 terminals, 500-plus rakes and 70,000 containers for CONCOR.

items.statement: Bulk cement opportunity: 63 million tonnes moved by road (bulkers) vs 7 million tonnes by rail; tank containers offer door-to-door, multi-drop, 20-30 days free time as warehouse
items.quote: Out of this 70 million tonnes, railway is moving 7 million, only 10% of the bulk cement is being moved as of now by Indian Railways in their specialized wagon, we call it BCCW and BCFC, okay? So the remaining 63 million is moving by bulker on road.

items.statement: Bulk cement tank container margins higher than existing domestic margins; shipping margins >30% per container; goods shed logistics and parcel service also high-margin
items.quote: Actually, it will be certainly -- I mean our margin will increase because as of now, we are not moving much of cement. We are moving just bag cement that is to 50 containers with whatever we are allowed. So in that, our margins are very limited. But with bulk cement, whatever 3 streams we are running from I mean as of now, our margins are certainly on the higher side and which are likely to increa

items.statement: Dahej plant capacity utilization at 65-70%, expected full utilization by end of year; Roha at 100%
items.quote: Let me inform you that the current capacity utilization at the Dahej plant is about 65% to 70%, and we expect full capacity utilization by the end of this year and Roha is currently being utilized at 100% utilization.

items.statement: Two capex programs planned: Dahej (new land 16,834 sqm) and Roha Phase-II (4.5 acres); total anticipated outlay INR100 crore plus INR18 crore already spent at Dahej and INR14-15 crore at Roha
items.quote: See, you know, this question is, right now, our anticipated capex flow is the region of INR100 crores, but as you know, everybody would know that when you start a project and when you finish it, there are always certain cost escalations in each project, you know.

items.statement: High-value products currently 15% of revenue, targeting 50% in next few quarters; new R&D products have gross margins >50%
items.quote: So, the high value, high margin products currently constitute of around 15%. And we would like to increase that to around 50% in the n ext few quarters

items.statement: EBITDA margin 23.6% in Q2 FY26 vs 16.6% in Q2 FY25; management expects 200-300 bps improvement in next 3-4 years, more over 5 years
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q2 FY '26 was at 23.6% as compared to 16.6% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: US sales impacted ~10% in Q2 FY26 due to tariff chaos; current quarter expected nil to negligible impact; global demand sluggish but revival expected first in food color industry
items.quote: Overall, the revenue generated by the company from the U.S. market was affected roughly by around 10% in the September quarter and the remaining can be attributed to other markets.

items.statement: Building inventory at both plants to improve service levels and reduce lead times; inventories will be utilized in current and next quarter as demand improves
items.quote: We would like to build some stocks. So eventually, when the demand is at full potential, earlier on we had certain lead times which we were offering to our customers, which they were not liking.

items.statement: New high-value products priced >US$25/kg; pricing power demonstrated by not reducing prices despite 50% tariff on US exports; rupee depreciation benefits export-heavy revenue
items.quote: The newer products are of an expensive nature around more than US$25 per kilo upwards.

items.statement: No major competitor capex expected due to uncertain geopolitical environment; high entry barriers (decades for MNC approvals, stability testing, trust) protect market position
items.quote: Not from any of our competitors, no, at this moment. In fact, a lot of the industry players are being very judicious with their capital because of the uncertain geopolitical environment.

items.statement: Non-food industrial shift from carcinogenic dyes to food-grade colors driven by health/safety concerns and regulatory testing for heavy metals (lead 2ppm limit); voluntary but compliance-driven
items.quote: Part of it is also driven by regulatory wherein, crops, etc., are being tested for such presence of such lead, arsenic contamination. So, in order to comply with those requirements, they have to -- they are taking these steps.

items.statement: 95% revenue from exports; evenly distributed across North America, South America, Europe, Southeast Asia, Australasia; strong in Europe and Americas
items.quote: Now as far as Vidhi is concerned, we have a very evenly distributed sales geography -wise. So we are present very -- we are in the North American continent, South American continent, European continent, Southeast Asia, etc., Australasia, this is where we find our demand from.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to dual-plant operations (Roha 100%, Dahej 70%) and strategic stock-building for faster deliveries; raw materials, WIP, finished goods all higher
items.quote: So the higher inventory comes from operations running at two plants, so we are inviting raw materials, in-process stocks, and finished products.

items.statement: Future capex funded by mix of internal accruals and debt; R&D investment continues without capital constraints
items.quote: See, the ongoing expansions, etc., would be a mix of our internal accruals as well as some debt.

items.statement: Declared second interim dividend of INR1.50 per share (150% on face value INR1) for FY26
items.quote: Accordingly, the company has also declared a second interim dividend of INR1.50 per share i.e. 150% per equity share having a face value of INR1 each for the financial year 2025-'26.

items.statement: Deepening wallet share with existing MNC clients and distributors; cross-selling new products through global distributor network; exhibiting monthly at global trade shows
items.quote: We have excellent rela tions with all the top MNCs, et c. So whenever we introduce any new products, the first and obv ious customer base for us would be to target our own distributors who are present in all those industries, which we wish to target

items.statement: Global tariff chaos, US government shutdown, recession in 26 US states, job losses creating demand uncertainty; but ground reports from distributors show sales looking good ahead
items.quote: There was also a survey very recently that 26 out of the 50 states are already in a recession in the US. And California and the state of New York, which were so far not in recession, were also, I think this was a survey by the -- there was a report by the Moody's, you

items.statement: Confident of improving EBITDA performance quarter-on-quarter; expect double-digit growth from non-food business (currently 2.5-5% of revenue); non-food shift driven by fertilizer, ink, sanitation, personal care, healthcare industries
items.quote: I assure you that the EBITDA performance, which the company has achieved in the se cond quarter, we are confident of improving on that in the next few quarters to come

items.statement: Natural colors face cost (20x higher), stability, availability, shelf-life challenges; synthetic colors preferred for industrial applications replacing carcinogenic dyes
items.quote: Just for your explanation and understanding, natural colors are expected to increase the coloring budget of any company by at least 20 times.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; R&D team developing forward-integrated products for pharma and higher-value industries
items.quote: Since I am very closely working with the R&D team in our company, we are continuously developing forward integrated products which find a wider application in certain higher category of industries.

items.statement: Dahej plant commercial since Dec 2023; capacity doubled from 325 to 675 MT/month (7,200 MT/annum); new Dahej land allotted April 2025; Roha Phase-II construction starting in 2.5-3 months, completion ~10 months
items.quote: The Dahej plant, which began commercial operations in December 2023, following a successful trial phase, has significantly increased the company's total production capacity from an earlier 325 metric tons per month to 675 metric tons per month.

items.statement: Chairman retired by rotation without majority; two independent directors stepped down; board reconstitution targeted before Q3 results
items.quote: Our chairman, who was retiring by rotation, did not receive the requisite majority and consequently ceased to be a director. Following this, two other independent directors hav e also stepped

items.statement: New head of sales appointed based in Europe; legal and HR leadership being hired as part of broader reset
items.quote: I've appointed a new head of sales. He's based in Europe. He brings extensive international experience, strong sales leadership, deep domain expertise in t elco and technology

items.statement: Operational profitability achieved for first time since June 2022; PAT positive without exceptional items
items.quote: we have achieved operational profitability. We are PAT positive without any exceptional items. So, I would say that in the truest sense, we have returned to profi tability this quarter driven by operations and not one-time

items.statement: Management committed to sustaining PAT positive trend going forward
items.quote: So definitely, the effort is to maintain the trend now, see, because we got to this after a lot of like, I've been telling my team last quarter in tears. So, we are here now, so we wanna keep it sustained from here on.

items.statement: Announced deals worth $15 million this quarter; renewed long-standing partnerships with leading operators in APAC and Europe for 5-6 years
items.quote: In the last few months, we have announced deals wor th $15 million that we announced to stock exchanges and I think most of you got it. So, we ha ve renewed long-standing partnerships with our leading operators in APAC, Europe, and over for fiv e and six years respectively

items.statement: Won major deal with leading APAC operator to upgrade revenue assurance and fraud management via HyperSense platform including AI use cases
items.quote: We also won a major deal with leading APAC operator to upgrade and enhance their revenue assurance and fraud management capabilities through Subex's HyperSense platform, including AI use cases.

items.statement: Secured new engagement with leading telco in Netherlands for unified MVNO billing and wholesale partner settlement platform
items.quote: And we have also secured new engagement with a leading telco in Netherlands to deliver a unified platform for MVNO billing and wholesale partner settlement.

items.statement: Upgraded existing fraud management system to HyperSense for Middle-East operator leveraging AI
items.quote: Another significant win came from Middle-East, wher e we'll upgrade an existing fraud management system to HyperSense. Again, we'll leverage AI to enhance operators' fraud management capabilities

items.statement: Deal conversions faster this year; some geographies remain slow with orders pending PO for multiple quarters
items.quote: are definitely seeing much faster flips than I saw last year, and I would say a few previous quarters. So definitely, this has been a good quarter for us. In terms of deal conversion, what we are seeing truly is that there are geographies that have become a little bit more agile, and I would say faster for us. But there are still one or two geographies which are slow

items.statement: All products being made GenAI native; rethinking product suite for lighter versions with shorter implementation cycles
items.quote: So, what we are doing is we are making it all GenAI native. All the products will be GenAI native right now. So how do we make it? Obviously, every product is going to be a little different. Like, assurance is different from fraud management, which is different from our billing system. So, we are seeing what are the opportunities to make a GenAI native, more lighter version of products that don't

items.statement: Revenue INR 68.9 crore vs INR 66.4 crore previous quarter; Normalized EBITDA INR 7.3 crore vs INR 4.3 crore; Normalized PAT INR 3.9 crore vs INR 12.8 crore
items.quote: Revenue for t he quarter stood at INR 68.9 crores against INR 66.4 crores for the previous quarter. Normalized EBITDA for the quarter is at INR 7.3 crores against INR 4.3 crores for the previous quarter. Normalized PAT for the quarter is at INR 3.9 crores against INR 12.8 crores for the previous quarter

items.statement: Not actively pursuing M&A; focus on cap table stabilization
items.quote: M&A, again, I mean, we are not actively honestly in market. The one effort that we want to definitely make is, and I've said that in past as well, is tha t we do want to make sure that we can get some stabilization to our cap table

items.statement: Recognized in Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI in CSP Operations for second consecutive year; one of few Indian product companies in quadrant
items.quote: Subex has been recognized for the second cons ecutive year in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for AI in CSP operations. So, this is an acknowledgment of our position as a trusted innovation partner to telco leaders worldwide

items.statement: Cash position INR 135 crore; cleanup efforts not cash-related
items.quote: Which I think is good. You would agree. Right? If we have INR 135 crores in bank right now. So, I think we have strong liquidity position.

items.statement: Pursuing recovery of Sectrio provision aggressively through all means including legal; one contract nearly closed, other in recovery process
items.quote: we are pursuing it aggressively in all forms, I would say all means available to us right now to go and see what we can recover. So, all the efforts are on. I'm very aware that, th at needs to be recovered. So, we are taking all recourses, including legal where available

items.statement: Internal push for INR 100 crore quarterly revenue; hopes to achieve next year given robust order book
items.quote: INR 100 crores? This has been my internal push as well to all my teams that I really truly, truly do want to see INR 100 crore quarter. It's not just an aspi rational thing. When can we get there? Honestly, if I knew it, I would tell you. But there is a strong push, Abhishek. , internally also, there is a strong push

items.statement: Monthly recurring revenue broadly flat; subscription conversion delayed by large implementations; may resume reporting in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Currently, it's more or less flat because sti ll we not really converted the entire revenue to th e subscription and all because there is bulk of the implementations that is still on. And as we explained earlier also, it's the large implementations that a re there. So, once you finish the implementation cycle, then only the subscriptions or support services

items.statement: Sales team changes underway; head of sales replaced last week; further downstream changes planned as part of comprehensive reset
items.quote: We have actually. Right? I mean, the sales side has been on-boarded as of I think last week. So, the head of sales himself has been changed. And I think we are making some other changes as well on downstream.

items.statement: Operates in duopoly market with one big competitor; competitors unlisted and under no disclosure obligation; order book details withheld for competitive sensitivity
items.quote: funnel and things like that -- see, this is a small market that we are in, Mahesh. The truth is that the market that we are serving, we are working in a duopoly situation. So we are there , and there is one big competitor. And then everyone else is a distant third force. Right? And they are all unlisted. So, they are under no ob ligation. See, my competition is all unlisted. They are all private.

items.statement: H1 FY26 was good on order book and profitability; H2 typically slightly better than H1 and momentum expected to continue
items.quote: I think H1 has been fairly good. I think we ended Q2 on a good note in terms of order book and the profitability. We are looking to continue the momentum in H2. Typical ly, H2 ends up being a little -- if you have been with us, you will know that H2 ends up being slightly better than H1

items.statement: Order book strong; large orders of 4-5 years with renewals and implementation revenue
items.quote: So, typically, this order, which is when we reporte d, it is a large order, ranges from four years to f ive years. And in that, there are certain renewals orders. So, basically, like, our annuity wise is strong. We keep winning that

items.statement: Pipeline funnel targeted at INR 180-200 million for the year
items.quote: So, see, in terms of funnel, we are typicall y targeting in a for instance, in this year, we are targeting a funnel of INR 180 million to INR 200 mi llion, if that answers your question

items.statement: Fraud is pervasive and growing with AI agents; betting on fraud management across telco, fintech and financial sectors
items.quote: Right from your delivery frauds to your WhatsApp frauds to your SMS, the fraud is all pervasive. And the more that AI agents come into play, this is only going to get worse, actually.

items.statement: Focus on telco adjacencies like fintech wallets and OTT; horizontal scaling of fraud management into financial sector; not pursuing legal, education, defence as new verticals
items.quote: The challenge of going into entirely new domain. Right? Let's take, for example, legal, is truly that, the GTM, the cost of actually cracking a market open is extremely high when you do not have domain knowledge in a certain domain

items.statement: 150 customers with active billing and AMC; sales team builds 4-5x pipeline; quarterly business reviews with top customers
items.quote: when we say 150 customers, it would be that num ber. The way we calculate that number is that do they have an install base? Are they working with one or more of our products? And do we have an AMC coming from there? And do we have an active billing going on with those

items.statement: Negative retained earnings prevent buyback or dividends; cash deployed in treasury investments and reinvestment for growth
items.quote: So basically, yes, there's a regulatory hurdle beca use the company retained earnings is still negative . So, there's a buyback provision is there whereby it has to be funded out of the retained earnings. So unfortunately, we are not there

items.statement: No active licensing conversations with partners like Tech Mahindra; products require development effort to horizontally scale, not designed for lift-and-shift licensing
items.quote: Are we actively thinking of licensing? We haven't really had those conversations, to be honest, because the way our products are built, it can be horizontally scaled, but that's not without actually production, I would say, development effort.

items.statement: Board reconstitution targeted before Q3 FY26 earnings call; seeking technocrat profiles with industry renown
items.quote: So, I said in the opening, Ajay, that before the Q3 call, we should have board reconstituted. The point I was making was that I have received a lot of ques tions offline as well from the shareholders saying that why haven't you appointed the Board yet

items.statement: Legacy goodwill of INR 196 crore from RAFM IP subject to annual impairment testing; potential non-cash impairment surprises possible but procedural
items.quote: So, INR 196 crore, which you're talking about, it's a goodwill. Correct? Because we barely hear you correctly. Yes. So, the goodwill, that it's coming out from our main IP, which is the RAFM IP. So, that is there in the balance sheet.

items.statement: US H-1B visa fee hikes and law changes have not directly affected business; minor on-site deployment visa hiccups but nothing insurmountable
items.quote: US laws, actually, honestly, it hasn't directly affected us too much because most of our -- my bill team is actually sitting in Bangalore next to us. So, we haven't had major challenges

items.statement: Investor Day planned with product roadmap, adjacencies, TAM; investor relations agency onboard; shareholder outreach and roadshows to follow
items.quote: Again, as in when we announce the Investor Day, I look forward to seeing most of you here. Please d o come. We will share the information on the products, on adjacencies, on new areas, on the TAM, everything that you have been asking for, for a

items.statement: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY26 to remain muted, with clear upside from Q1 FY27 driven by movie releases and digital B2B order book
items.quote: quarter 3 and quarter 4 will remain muted to that extent. And quarter 1 from the next financial year, you will see a clear upside and the numbers which you are looking for.

items.statement: Management does not provide formal guidance but indicates FY26 will end in the same zone as H1 FY26
items.quote: We generally don't give any guidance or forward -looking statement. But what I can tell you is whatever you have seen in quarter 1 and quarter 2, I think we will remain more or less in the same zone when we end this year.

items.statement: Digital B2B order book stands at approximately INR300 crores with leading OTT platforms
items.quote: Moreover, our order book of -- for our digital B2B business stands at approximately INR300 crores with various leading OTT platform.

items.statement: Digital B2B order book includes INR250 crores+ with Netflix, INR42 crores with Zee Studios, and others with Amazon, Sony, Star
items.value: INR250 crores+ with Netflix, INR42 crores with Zee Studios
items.quote: currently, we have INR250 crores plus order book with Netflix, INR42 crores order book with Zee Studios. And there are others with Amazon, Sony and Star.

items.statement: Capital allocation: INR150-175 crores for Motion Pictures, INR20-25 crores working capital for digital, TV funded internally
items.value: INR150-175 crores for Motion Pictures, INR20-25 crores for digital
items.quote: The total capital, if you ask me, INR150 crores to INR175 crores will be into Motion Pictures. Television doesn't need any capital, so it is totally funded through internal accrual. On digital space, close to INR20 crores to INR25 crores working capital is needed for us.

items.statement: INR131 crores raised last year; INR65 crores for Motion Pictures, INR33 crores for music rights/movie distribution/digital content, INR32.5 crores general corporate purposes; none deployed yet
items.quote: So primarily INR65 crores will go into Motion Pictures, INR33 crores will go i nto music rights, movie distribution, digital content space and general corporate purposes is INR32.5 crores. As of now, we have not used a single rupee from this fund.

items.statement: TV episodic revenue under pressure at INR24-25 lakhs per hour; direct variable cost margin ~30%
items.quote: TV business episodic revenue will continue to be under a little pressure because broadcast is also looking at cutting cost and the content cost has been reduced drastically by the leading broadcast. So unless somebody comes up and take the punt of kind of investing heavily into this content, we will continue to be in the range of INR24 lakhs, INR25 lakhs per hour episodic revenue.

items.statement: TV revenue was INR28-29 lakhs per hour; direct variable cost margin ~30%

items.statement: Kutingg targets mass audience, family-oriented, not edgy; offers binge, episodic, vertical, AI-led content

items.statement: Cash reserves strong at INR137 crores providing comfortable liquidity for growth plans
