items.quote: On the demand front, apparel imports in the U.S. during the period January to July 2025 continue to witness a decent growth of 5%, while retail sales grew by 7%. Imports from U.K. and EU continued to show higher growth of 8% and 9%, respectively, in the period January to August 2025.

items.statement: Expect some demand contraction from spring 2026 if 4-6% price increases passed to consumers
items.quote: Going forward, I think from early '26, you would see price increases, and that could have some bearing on demand. Demand is very price sensitive. And if there is a 4% to 6% price increase, which is passed on to the consumers, which is most likely to happen, I think there could be some degree of demand contraction.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA INR84 crores flat YoY; PBT declined due to higher finance and depreciation from new capex and Ind AS lease treatment
items.quote: The company reported an EBITDA of INR84 crores with flat Y-o-Y growth after being impacted considerably by tariffs. Prudent cost control and productivity gains offset some of these effe cts. However, the PBT declined on account of higher finance and depreciation costs

items.statement: Q3 margins may be worse than Q2 if 50% tariff continues; Africa improvement to offset partly
items.quote: Q3, if the 50% tariff continues through Q3, the performance at the bottom line level may be top line may grow -- will grow over Q2 levels, but bottom line may show a lower performance than Q2 level.

items.statement: Africa revenue drop of 25% in Q2 caused operational deleverage and 280bps EBITDA margin decline QoQ
items.quote: That is primarily because of Africa business. Our Africa business has fallen by about 25% in Q2, which is correcting itself in Q3 and Q4. So that drop results in operational deleverage, right? So, when the revenue falls, there is -- your cost does not fall in proportion as there is a lot of fixed costs we carry.

items.statement: India order book INR900+ crores; Africa order book INR240-250 crores; both confirmed with additions coming
items.value: INR900-plus crores for India. And for Africa, it will be almost INR240 crores, INR250 crores
items.quote: So I mean, when I look at the order book for -- first of all, the order book stands full. So when I look at the order book for India, almost INR900-plus crores for India. And for Africa, it will be almost INR240 crores, INR250 crores

items.statement: Africa H2 FY26 revenue expected to exceed USD 50 million; new customers added
items.quote: So I believe for next half, that is Q3 plus Q4, our Africa revenue should exceed USD 50 million. I'm saying exceed. So this is the base level, and we could do better than that.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex INR110 crores: INR75 crores for 3 new India facilities (Bhopal, Bangalore, Jharkhand) and Kenya expansion; INR35 crores modernization
items.quote: Out of INR110 crores, the INR75 crores is for the new capacity additions. There are 3 new facilities. One is in Madhya Pradesh in Bhopal Unit-2, which the work is in progress. The other one, is a new plant coming up in Bangalore and one more unit in Jharkhand. All -- these put together in India, we have invested close to INR50 crores for the new capacity additions. And about INR20 crores is the in

items.statement: H2 FY26 capex ~INR40 crores committed for new units in final completion stage; focus on Kenya
items.quote: Now with reference to H2, whatever we have already committed, especially for the new units which are in the final stage of completion , we shall ensure the same is completed.. Our investment focus is more in Kenya because of the incremental order flow anticipated.

items.statement: At 50% tariff, India bears up to 15% burden share with some customers; passed partly to supply chain; impact INR12-15 crores in Q2
items.quote: In number terms, the impact came to about INR12 crores to INR15 crores here in India.

items.statement: If tariff settles at 20%, India burden share drops to sub-5%; part pushed to fabric suppliers, part absorbed
items.quote: But once the 50% comes to somewhere in the range of 20%, then the cost impact on us will be sub-5%. And that -- again, part of that will be pushed back to the fabric suppliers, part of that, we will absorb.

items.statement: Strategic investment in BTPL fabric processing unit for integrated play, superior margin and larger market access
items.quote: Our strategic investment in BTPL, a fabric processing unit, positions us for future success. An integrated play enables a supe rior margin and provides access to a larger market

items.statement: Africa revenue share ~22%; international revenue expected to grow to 30% of total in years ahead
items.quote: So currently, Africa could be about 20 -odd percent, 22%. But in my assessment, if we look at the years ahead, we would see international revenue probably grow faster than India and would contribute to as much as 30%, just given the traction that we are see ing across the different geographies.

items.statement: AGOA expired Sep 30 2025; Kenya now has 10% reciprocal tariff vs Bangladesh; AGOA restoration would widen tariff delta to ~30%
items.quote: At the moment, without AGOA, Kenya enjoys a tariff delta of 10% vis-a-vis Bangladesh. However, if AGOA is restored, the tariff and duty differential with Bangladesh will widen to almost 30%.

items.statement: No government support for tariff impact yet; discussions ongoing but nothing factored in
items.quote: For now, there is no government support whatsoever, and we have not baked anything from the government as a relief or a support measure in this.

items.statement: US tariff impact adjusted against top line as FOB discount; other expenses declined 6% QoQ flat YoY
items.quote: The U.S. tariff impact is normally -- it is taken -- adjusted against our top line itself because it's a discount offered on the FOB.

items.statement: Higher finance costs from new capex and Ind AS lease treatment; depreciation run rate INR23 crores normal + INR20 crores Ind AS
items.quote: The current run rate of depreciation, INR23 crores is on account of normal depreciation at a consol level. Another INR20 crores is Ind AS depreciation.

items.statement: Q2 consolidated volume 12.97M pieces at INR700 avg realization; H1 25.58M pieces at INR697
items.quote: In total, for the Q2, we ended up with 12.97 million at n average realization of INR 700. For H1, it was 14.91 million in Gokaldas, 6.97 million by Atraco and 3.7 million in Matrix, totalling to 25.58 million for the company at a consolidated level. Realization for Gokaldas, it is @ INR 847, Atraco at INR 444 and Matrix is at INR 568. Overall average realisation is @ INR 697

items.statement: If 50% tariff persists through H2, Q3 bottom line worse than Q2; Q4 better on Africa; tariff resolution would flip margins up from Q4
items.quote: If the U.S. penal tariff on India continues through the entire second half of this financial year, we could see some margin erosion. The company, like the rest of the industry, is hopeful of an early resolution of the tariff impact and could see ourselves tiding through this withou t much ramifications

items.statement: FY26 production target on track despite 40-day pellet plant shutdown
items.quote: GPIL is well on track to meet its FY '26 production target despite the loss of production of pellet for about 40 days due to the incident that took place on 26th September.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 22% and PAT margin 14% despite soft realizations
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margins stood healthy at 22% and 14%, respectively, despite soft realization across the product range.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 20% and PAT margin 12%
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margin continued to hold firm at 20% and 12%, respectively.

items.statement: Ari Dongri iron ore mine expansion from 2.35 to 6 MTPA; environmental approval expected by end of December 2025
items.quote: we have been able to move forward on getting much-awaited regulatory approvals for expanding the capacity of Ari Dongri iron ore mines from 2.35 million tons to 6 million tons per annum, and we have successfully completed the public hearing for environmental approval.

items.statement: 2 MTPA pellet capacity expansion pre-commissioning trials underway; commissioning targeted by end of November 2025
items.quote: The 2 million ton pellet capacity expansion is progressing as planned. The pre-commissioning trials are underway and commissioning is targeted by the end of November '25.

items.statement: 0.7 MTPA cold rolling mill complex project cost INR900 crores (INR600 crores debt, balance internal accruals)
items.quote: The total cost of project for CRM project is INR900 crores, of which INR600 crores is financed through debt and the balance remainder funded by internal accrual.

items.statement: 10 GW battery energy storage system project in Maharashtra; land acquisition of 112 acres completed; project cost INR700 crores (60% debt, 40% equity from GPIL)
items.quote: Godawari New Energy Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of GPIL, has planned to set up a 10 gigawatt battery energy storage system project in Maharashtra, for which land acquisition of 112 acres has already been completed. The cost of the project is INR700 crores, which is proposed to be funded by a debt of 60% and balance from internal accrual out of equity contribution from GPIL.

items.statement: Additional 250 MW solar power capacity approved for captive use in CRM and integrated steel plant; commissioning expected by Q4 FY27
items.quote: The Board in its last Board meeting has approved setting up an additional 250-megawatt solar power capacity in addition to the earlier announced capacity of 125 megawatts for captive use in the CRM project and integrated steel plant. The project is expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY '27.

items.statement: Ari Dongri mine ramp-up: targeting 4.5-5 MTPA in FY27, full 6 MTPA from January 2027
items.quote: Our idea is to reach 4.5 million to 5 million tons next year and then full throttle 6 million tons from January '27.

items.statement: New 2 MTPA pellet plant expected to reach 80-85% capacity utilization from Q4 FY26
items.quote: From Q4 onwards, we're expecting close to 80% to 85% of the capacity for the new pellet plant.

items.statement: CRM complex and BESS plant commercial production targeted for April 2027 (FY28)
items.quote: we're looking at the commercial production of April '27, which is FY '28 for both, for BESS as well as for the CRM.

items.statement: CRM and BESS plants expected to reach 80%+ utilization from second year of operation
items.quote: From the second year onwards, we will be at 80% plus in both the plants for sure.

items.statement: Domestic pellet demand strong; H2 FY26 pellet prices expected to remain stable around INR9,000-9,750/ton
items.quote: the pellet H1 has been close to INR9,000 on average. Looking at the current demand and supply, we feel H2 will also be on the same similar level because pellet demand in the domestic market is still quite strong.

items.statement: Indian steel demand forecast at 9% growth in FY25 and FY26 driven by infrastructure and construction
items.quote: Indian steel demand remains strong with the World Steel Association forecasting 9% growth both in FY '25 and '26, driven by sustained expansion across infrastructure and construction.

items.statement: Pellet prices stable around INR8,500-10,000 band, currently ~INR9,750/ton; DRI ~INR22,000-23,000; Billets ~INR35,000; Finished steel ~INR38,000-39,000
items.quote: Pellet prices have also been stable around INR8,500 to INR10,000 band, currently at around INR9,750 a ton, and likely to follow a similar trend in H2.

items.statement: Imported coal (RB1 6000 GCV) landed cost ~INR11,000/ton in Q2; expected INR10,500-11,000 in Q3
items.quote: It was about -- so Q2, it was about INR11,000 landed to my plant, RB1 coal, 6000 GCV coal.

items.statement: 250 MW solar project IRR ~24% vs grid tariff of INR7.70-8/unit; solar cost ~INR5.50/unit at steel plant
items.quote: This 250-megawatt solar, if you compare with the rate of INR7 and net cost to the steel plant at about INR5.50, the internal rate of return is about 24%.

items.statement: Galvanized fabricated products volume surge due to PGCIL approval for transmission-grade structures and new strip capacity for pipe segment
items.quote: We are. So additional capacity, we got all the approvals from PGCIL now. We are ramping up the capacity of our rolling mill. We have also started taking strips, which are used for the pipe segment.

items.statement: Billet sales declined 40% in H1 due to 2-month power plant shutdown for pollution norm upgrades
items.quote: we had taken a planned shutdown of one of our bigger turbines. There were modifications required to meet the new norms. Basically, the State Pollution Board has recommended to all industries to revise their pollution norms.

items.statement: Pellet sales primarily within 100 km radius of Raipur; expanded capacity will first displace external supply from Odisha
items.quote: we sell close to about say a periphery of say about -- maximum is about 100 kilometers in and around Raipur, that's it.

items.statement: BESS market competitive with Adani, Ola, JSW, Reliance; GPIL targets top 5 in India, focusing on container supply not SECI tenders
items.quote: Firstly, whether it's Adani, Ola, or JSW, there will be stiff competition in this, and we are very well prepared for that. We don't want to be a capacity design such that we want to be probably one of the top 5 in India in terms of volumes.

items.statement: PGCIL approval received for supply of steel billets for transmission-grade galvanized steel structures
items.quote: GPIL received PGCIL approval for the supply of steel billets for transmission-grade galvanized steel structures, recognition the high quality of GPIL billets now comparable to those of India's leading steel producers.

items.statement: No intention to invest in fossil fuel thermal plants; committed to renewable energy due to expected carbon tax benefits
items.quote: We have no intention of going back into that. We are very much happy in moving forward because sooner or later, I'm very sure with new government norms, new carbon tax mechanisms which India has proposed, things will get beneficial for us in the longer run.

items.statement: Merchant iron ore purchases of ~50,000 tons/month to continue until expanded mining capacity ramps up
items.quote: We have been a buyer in the market for about 50,000 tons every month. And with the new pellet capacity, there will be additional mine, till mining capacity ramps up.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR100 crores (>50% subscribed by promoters) to fund BESS and CRM projects without additional debt
items.quote: This INR100 crores of preferential issue does not fund my entire steel plant project. But definitely, this will help meeting requirements for BESS and CRM projects.

items.statement: Pellet production target FY27: bare minimum 4 million tons with new plant at 80% utilization from January
items.quote: Pellet for next year, 4 million will be the bare minimum. It might be on the higher side. Probably we will analyze during the planning of the next year, but 4 million will be the bare minimum for sure.

items.statement: Pellet plant incident on 26 Sep 2025 caused 6 fatalities, 6 injuries; 35-40 day shutdown; financial assistance provided to families
items.quote: we are deeply mourned and grieved by the unfortunate and unforeseen incident, which took place on 26th September '25 in one of our pellet plants in which six of our colleagues lost their lives and six others were injured.

items.statement: Store addition target raised to 130 stores for FY26 and 150 stores for FY27
items.quote: So our initial target was 100 stores, 100 new stores. And we've already added 86 this year. So we have actually increased that 100 number to 130 stores. So I think we'll add around 130 stores this year. And if our store operating and profitability metrics remains robust and as strong as it is, we will open 150 stores next year.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at 8% for next 2-3 years due to high new store additions
items.quote: So I think we did pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 8% last year. So that is our future guidance for the next 2 to 3 years because we are adding so much new area.

items.statement: Targeting 8-10% SSSG for mature stores going forward
items.quote: That is what we target. So even for mature stores, I think 8% to 10% SSSG is our target. And if we do our execution well, if we plan our assortment well, I think it is possible.

items.statement: Cash flows cover growth till end of FY28; no immediate fund raise plans
items.quote: But right now, looking at the cash flows, we are covered till the end of FY '28.

items.statement: Capex plus inventory investment of INR350 crores and warehousing cost of INR25-30 crores needed for 150 stores next year
items.value: INR350 crores capex + inventory, INR25-30 crores warehousing
items.quote: So to open 150 stores, we would need a capex plus inventory investment of around INR350-odd crores and additional warehousing cost would be around INR25 crores to INR30 crores.

items.statement: Total store count reached 259 with 28 lakh sq ft; 16 net new stores added in Q3 so far taking total to 275
items.quote: We opened 43 new stores during this quarter and achieved a net addition of 70 new stores in the first half of the financial year, taking our total store count to 259 stores with 28 lakh square feet of retail space. Additionally, we have added 16 net new stores so far in the current quarter, taking the total of 275 stores as of today.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin improved to 6.3% in Q2 from 2.1% YoY; H1 margin 7.2% vs 5% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin grew from 2.1% to 6.3% and the PAT grew from INR70 lakh to INR25.3 crores, which is a growth of 3,561%.

items.statement: Gross margin target 28-29%; company prefers passing benefits to consumers for higher sales per sq ft over higher gross margin
items.quote: Our target gross margin is always 28%, 29%. We want to pass on everything to the consumer because we feel it is the time to get the maximum market share and maximum per square feet sales.

items.statement: Bill discounting benefit of 1.5-2% per month expected to reflect in gross margin from Q3
items.quote: So you should start seeing it from the third quarter.

items.statement: Momentum continuing in Q3; beating internal expectations; very bullish outlook
items.quote: I can just say that the momentum is continuing, and we are very, very happy with the kind of response we're getting both from our old stores and all the newer regions and the newer stores that we've opened. And we are beating our own expectations.

items.statement: Early winter onset boosted winter contribution from 40% to 55% of sales; 5% sales delta and 3% gross margin delta vs non-winter
items.quote: So we have seen our winter contribution increase from about 40% on the last year same day to almost 55%. So that is very healthy for us because winter is, number one, you have extra margin, extra gross margin. Second, the ASP is higher. So it translates into much better sales numbers. So there's a delta of around 5%.

items.statement: Apparel contribution increasing; apparel ASP only up 3% YoY; overall ASP rise driven by mix shift not price hikes
items.quote: So whenever you want to see whether it's an actual price increase, you should only compare ASP of apparel from last year to ASP of apparel now. So that ASP increase is only 3% because we have increased the contribution of apparel and apparel ASP is much, much higher than general merchandise.

items.statement: Own design share increased from 25% to 35%; targeting 40-45% by next summer; increasing 5% per season
items.quote: So we are only taking it a gradual increase and increasing it by 5% every season. So I think we moved up from 25% to 35%. And hopefully, next year, summer, it will be around 40%, 45%.

items.statement: South India focus: 18 stores in Karnataka, 2 in Goa, entered Andhra Pradesh; aim to be national in 2-3 years including Tamil Nadu
items.quote: Our aspiration is to be a national level retailer. Our aspiration is to be in all the states of India in the next 2 to 3 years. So definitely, we will be present in Tamil Nadu as well.

items.statement: New stores in new geographies performing at 72-73% of old store throughput; only 2% difference vs new stores in core markets
items.quote: So they are currently at around 72% to 73%. So they are well within the range. And in terms of new regions, so new stores in old regions versus new stores in new regions, the difference is only 2% in terms of per square feet sales.

items.statement: QIP proceeds used: INR135 cr debt repayment, INR165 cr working capital, INR100 cr general corporate; creditor days to drop from 50-55 to 30-35
items.value: INR135 cr, INR165 cr, INR100 cr
items.quote: So we have raised QIP primarily to repay the debt of INR135 crores. We are using INR165 crores for our working capital and INR100 crores for general corporate purpose.

items.statement: Paying vendors early yields 1.5-2% per month bill discount; vendor count up from 180-190 to 250; 15-20 exclusive vendors
items.quote: So we get around 1.5% to 2% per month bill discount from them. So that is di rectly added to the bottom line if we pay them their bills earlier

items.statement: QIP raised INR400 cr; INR135 cr used to repay debt; cash flows cover growth till FY28 end
items.quote: So we have raised QIP primarily to repay the debt of INR135 crores.

items.statement: Store-level attrition 40-50%; mitigated by process automation, retention bonuses, variable pay (10-40% of salary); head office attrition <15%
items.quote: So what we have done is we have completely moved awa y from being manpower -oriented to being process oriented. So we've automated a lot of processes at our store where even a new guy within a day or 2, he can get trained and he can start giving an output

items.statement: Plan to hire CEO to focus on long-term strategy; most leadership promoted internally (retail head from floor manager, BD head from store manager)
items.quote: And me and my father both, we want to hire a CEO so that we can spend more time in the long- term strategy of the business because the plan is big, and we want to gro w multiple times and exponentially over the next 10

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS ROE 22.9% in H1 FY26; target >20% ROE; last year pre-Ind AS ROE ~27%
items.quote: Our ROE continues to show consistent impr ovement, standing at 22.9% in the first half of this year, reflecting disciplined capital allocation and strong operational leverage

items.statement: SSSG: reported 23.4% in Q2, normalized 10.3% (Durga Puja shift); H1 SSSG 13.3%; volume growth 58% in Q2
items.quote: Reported SSSG for quarter 2 stood at 23.4% and normalized SSSG adjusted for the Durga Puja shift from quarter 3 to quart er 2 stood at 10.3%. The same -store sales growth for the first 6 months of the financial year stood at 13.3

items.statement: New store breakeven at INR500/sq ft; new stores start at INR750-800/sq ft and break even from month 1; mature in 2-3 years
items.value: INR500/sq ft breakeven, INR750-800/sq ft start
items.quote: So our stores -- our new stores start from around INR750 to INR800 per square feet and the breakeven point is around INR500 per square feet. So our stores start from the first month itself, and it breaks even from the first month itself.

items.statement: Unit economics: capex INR1,100/sq ft, inventory INR2,500/sq ft (90-100 days), total investment INR2.4-2.5 cr/store, cost INR190/sq ft
items.quote: So our store economics, so capex required for the store is around INR1,100 per square feet. And the inventory required at the company level for that store is around INR2,500 per square feet, out of which -- so that's around 90 to 100 days of inventory.

items.statement: Cost per sq ft reduced by INR6-7 YoY; further scope for reduction with scale
items.quote: Yes, definitely. So we've already seen our costs come down by INR6 to INR7 per square feet if we are comparing it year-on-year.

items.statement: Key risks: inventory risk (managed via data-driven assortment, >1yr inventory down from 24% to <4%), location risk (4-5 layer site approval), execution risk at scale
items.quote: So the biggest risk is inventory risk. So that is why we have a lot of checks an d balances around aging of inventory, inventory management. So I think no other retailer puts their slow movers on discount within 2 weeks of introduction

items.statement: GST rate reduction benefit not yet seen; yarn prices offset fabric GST cut; any future benefit will be passed to consumers via MRP cuts
items.quote: So we haven't seen any benefit till now because whatever GST benefit was there, the price has increased that much of the yarns. But people are saying we should start seeing the benefit from around March onwards.

items.statement: Omnichannel exploration: leveraging store inventory for online sales in same city; no suitable tech partner yet; target launch next financial year
items.quote: Yes, we are expl oring different technologies where we can leverage the same store inventory and add another channel, which is online to sell to the customers in that particular city so that it doesn't have any additional costs and we can leverage the existing inventory an d cater to more customers. But we haven't found a suitable technology partner yet. But hopefully, soon, we'll be able to do th

items.statement: Care Health Insurance expects no price hike this quarter but will re-evaluate portfolio continuously
items.quote: For this quarter, we are not looking for any price hike, but this is a continuous journey, and we'll keep on reevaluating or keep on relooking at our portfolio.

items.statement: Religare Housing Finance targets four-digit AUM franchise in next few years from current INR245 crores
items.value: four digit kind of a franchise
items.quote: if we look at the overall intended equity base and the leverage we can easily target a four digit kind of a franchise in few years to -- in next few years.

items.statement: Religare Broking targets industry-plus growth in next few quarters and years with additional capital and competitive bank lines
items.period: next few quarters and few years
items.quote: We are looking at an industry plus kind of a growth in next few quarters and few years with the impetus being provided by the additional capital and availability of lines at a more competitive rate.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance invested INR322 crores capital infusion in September 2025
items.quote: Our investment book has grown by INR900 crores compared to March 2025 driven by business growth and capital infusion of INR322 crores in the month of September.

items.statement: Religare Enterprises allocated INR600 crores for Care Health, INR200 crores for Broking, INR250 crores for Housing Finance, INR75 crores for loan repayment from preferential issue proceeds
items.quote: we have earmarked INR600 crores for CARE, we have earmarked INR200 crores for broking business, INR250 crores for housing finance business and another INR75 crores for that loan repayment which was due at REL

items.statement: Care Health Insurance operates 271 branch offices and 22,000 hospital network
items.quote: they operate their operations through 271 branch offices and have a network of 22,000 hospitals under their belt.

items.statement: Religare Broking has 1,400+ touch points across 400+ cities serving 12 lakh+ customers with 2.5 lakh active clients
items.quote: The company has 1,400 plus touch points across 400 plus cities and towns serving 12 lakhs plus customers and active customer base is 2.5 lakhs.

items.statement: Religare Housing Finance has presence in 8 states with 15 branches
items.quote: The company has presence in eight states with 15 branches.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance combined ratio improved to 100% in Q2 FY26 from 102% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our combined ratio for the quarter 2 is 100% compared to 102% in the quarter 2 same period last year.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance claim ratio was 65% in Q2 FY26 vs 64% in Q2 FY25; H1 claim ratio 68.1% vs 65.1%
items.quote: Our claim ratio for quarter 2 is 65% as compared to 64% in the previous year. And on an H1 basis it is 68.1 against 65.1.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance profitability increased over 100% to INR177 crores in H1 FY26 from INR83 crores in H1 FY25 on N basis
items.quote: Our profitabil ity for this H1 on an N basis has increased by more than 100%, touching a number of INR 177 crores against INR 83 crores in the previous year's same period

items.statement: Religare Broking reported PBT of INR3.3 crores in Q2 FY26 vs INR18 crores in Q2 FY25
items.quote: RBL during the quarter has reported a top line of INR89.6 crores against the last year number of INR110.5 crores and the PBT of INR3.3 crores in the quarter 2 FY '26 against INR18 crores last year.

items.statement: Religare Housing Finance reported PBT loss of INR4.49 crores in Q2 FY26 vs INR3.66 crores loss in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The company currently is having a PBT loss of INR4.49 crores versus a INR3.66 crores for the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance GWP over INR9,200 crores in FY25; H1 FY26 top line INR5,100 crores with 19% growth on N basis
items.quote: In this,H1 we achieved a top line of INR5,100 crores with a growth of 19%. These numbers are on N basis.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance retail business grew 28% in H1 FY26; October retail book grew 39%
items.quote: Our retail business grew by 28%. In the month of October also, the growth journey continues and our growth is 22% with retail book growing at 39% for the month of October.

items.statement: Religare Finvest core SME book reduced to INR95 crores; cash balance INR423 crores; collection efficiency 98%
items.quote: RFL now has a core book of SME, which is now reduced substantially to about INR95 crores and all the assets have been converted into cash, so we are carrying a cash balance of about INR423 crores.

items.statement: Religare Housing Finance AUM INR245 crores; product mix 70% home loans, 30% loan against property
items.quote: Currently the AUM of the company is around INR245 crores and the basic products that we do are affordable home loans and affordable loan against property with a product mix of 70% to 30% each.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance took 8-10% price hike on retail portfolio in past 12 months
items.quote: So in the past 12 months, we have taken a price hike on the retail portfolio in the range of close to 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance passed GST distribution cost to distributors; expects zero-sum impact from GST changes
items.quote: So this is we have taken a call. We are very mindful of watching the industry. And we are looking at this on a continuous basis. But as of now, we have passed this cost to the distribution.

items.statement: RBI lifted Corrective Action Plan on Religare Finvest in July 2025; banks removed fraud classification
items.quote: Because of this, RBI lif ted the CAP in July 2025, and all banks also removed the fraud classification of RFL this year.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance migrating to IFRS; early trends show better numbers than current reporting
items.quote: We are migrating slowly and gradually to IFRS. And what we are seeing that the results on the IFRS, they are almost what we are seeing on a 50% basis.

items.statement: Religare Finvest is debt-free; all legacy debt settled with lenders
items.quote: The entire debt has been settled with all the lenders and there is no debt now on the books of RFL

items.statement: Religare Enterprises repaid INR75 crores loan; now debt-free at HoldCo level
items.quote: REL has already repaid its loan to the tune of INR75 crores, so REL today is debt free.

items.statement: Preferential issue of warrants INR1,500 crores completed; promoter group and marquee investors contributed INR750 crores each; 25% received

items.statement: Group General Counsel Babu Rao joined from Bajaj Finance; Group CHRO Indranil Choudhury joined from UTI Mutual Fund
items.quote: we have onboarded Group General Counsel Babu Rao. He has joined us from Bajaj Finance Ltd. And we have also on-boarded Indranil Choudhury as Group CHRO from UTI Mutual Fund.

items.statement: Three Burman family members expected to join board soon subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: three members of Burman family are expected to join the board soon, subject of course to regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Care Health Insurance solvency ratio 1.89x vs minimum 1.50x; market share 9.9% in health insurance, 22% in SAHI
items.quote: The solvency ratio is 1.89, against the minimum control level of 1.50. Our market share is 9.9% among the health insurance space including all the GI and standard health insurance. Within SAHI, our market share is 22%.

items.statement: Religare Finvest CRAR 197.6% vs regulatory 15%; net NPA ~1%; net worth INR812 crores
items.quote: Our net NPA ratio has continued to be very stable at about 1% and CRAR which is the regulatory ratio requirement of 15% against that we are at about 198%.

items.statement: Religare Housing Finance CRAR 142.4%; NNPA 3.3%; collection efficiency 97.34%
items.quote: The company has a very strong CRAR of 142% with investable ratings of BBB - Stable from both ICRA and CARE.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue and profit growth expected at 7-8%
items.quote: for the full year, we do expect an increase in revenue and profits in the range of about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Capex under implementation is about INR230 crores
items.quote: So it is about INR230 crores. That is now already under implementation.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR8,789 crores as of 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: The consolidated orders booked during September 2025 quarter are INR1,461 crores against INR889 crores in the quarter ended September 2024. The orders in hand as on 30th September 2025 on a consolidated basis are INR8,789 crores against INR7,066 crores as on 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR7,754 crores as of 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: The standalone orders booked during September 2025 quarter are INR1,208 crores compared to INR831 crores in the quarter ended September 2024. The orders in hand as on 30th September 2025 are substantially higher at INR7,754 crores compared to INR6,160 crores as on 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Export orders in hand at INR1,644 crores on standalone basis
items.quote: This includes export orders in hand of INR1,644 crores.

items.statement: Order book split: INR6,004 crores projects and INR2,785 crores manufacturing (consolidated)
items.value: INR6,004 crores projects, INR2,785 crores manufacturing
items.quote: So in that, the projects business is INR6,004 crores and manufacturing is INR2,785 crores.

items.statement: Standalone manufacturing order book INR1,817 crores (domestic INR1,125 crores, export INR692 crores)
items.quote: On a standalone basis, the manufacturing domestic orders is INR1,125 crores and manufacturing export is INR692 crores. So about INR1,817 crores is manufacturing out of the stand-alone order book of INR7,700 crores, and the balance is projects.

items.statement: Overall demand trends encouraging with robust inquiry position and export inquiries picking up
items.quote: The overall demand trends continue to be encouraging, and the inquiry position continues to be robust. Export inquiries have also picked up.

items.statement: Healthy pipeline across metals, steel, oil & gas, automobiles, cement, core infrastructure; sugar muted; air pollution control curtailed
items.quote: we are seeing a healthy pipeline across most industries. We expect that sugar may be a little muted now because as you know, the sugar is probably in a little bit of a downturn right now. But otherwise, we are getting orders from metals, including steel, oil and gas, automobiles, cement, the core infrastructure sectors are healthy.

items.statement: New Bhartoli facility for Machine Building division expected completion by July 2026, adding INR225 crores annual revenue
items.quote: Presently, the shops being set up at Bhartoli are for expanding manufacturing capacity in the Machine Building division. This is expected to be completed by July 2026 and when completed, we expect an additional annual revenue of INR225 crores.

items.statement: Dahej SEZ skids & modules facility approved: Phase 1 INR65 crores for INR160 crores revenue, Phase 2 INR22 crores for INR275 crores total revenue
items.quote: Our Board has yesterday approved an investment of INR87 crores in setting up a new facility for manufacturing of skids and modules at our existing land within the plot at SEZ in Dahej. The investment will be done in 2 phases, involving investment of INR65 crores in the first phase and INR22 crores in the second phase. The expansion when completed is expected to give an annual revenue of INR160 cro

items.statement: All announced manufacturing expansions to complete in ~12 months, potential INR400 crores+ revenue increase; consolidated manufacturing revenue could reach INR3,200-3,300 crores from current INR2,500 crores
items.quote: So the expansions that we have announced and which I just spoke about, they should be completed in another 12 months, all the expansion that I've spoken about. And we have said that those expansions are in the manufacturing area, and we are talking potentially of about INR400 crores increase in revenue from manufacturing because of that.

items.statement: Project business margins currently 5-7%, expected to improve with higher export share (26% of order book) and focus on core engineering skills
items.quote: The margins in this segment continue to be unless you continue to be around 5% to 6% to 7%. That's how the project business seems to be for us as well as for other companies, other competitors. There is scope to improve if we concentrate only on areas where our specific engineering skills, for example, in the boiler business. But also exports is normally an area which gives higher margins.

items.statement: Legacy FGD orders (INR300-400 crores) to complete by June 2026; milestone-based retention payments of ~INR400 crores expected largely in current year
items.quote: So legacy orders, you're probably referring to the FGD orders and those kind of things. So we do expect that they will all be completed within June 2026.

items.statement: INR80-90 crores of manufactured goods ready for dispatch but held due to customer site unreadiness; customers paying 95% plus storage charges
items.quote: In the manufactured items, we do have certain clients and some equipment that are ready for dispatch worth about maybe INR80 crores or INR90 crores, which the customer is not able to lift because the site is not ready.

items.statement: Cavite Biofuel (Philippines) held for sale at INR1,076 crores; seasonal operations Dec-Apr on sugarcane, then molasses; quarterly holding cost ~INR10-11 crores plus interest and FX; full-year revenue expected INR470-480 crores with INR30-40
items.value: INR1,076 crores assets held for sale
items.quote: So total investment, as you can see from the published results, assets held for sale is about INR1,076 crores.

items.statement: Boiler demand good, competitive landscape fine; process equipment facing temporary competitive pressure on margins but expected to normalize with strong capex cycle ahead
items.quote: Boilers, the demand is good. Boilers also is our largest product line. There is always competition, but I wouldn't describe it as pricing pressure. There's always competition. We have a large part of our project business order book is from boilers.

items.statement: Export orders 26% of consolidated order book; active export inquiries and negotiations ongoing; no significant US exposure or tariff impact currently
items.quote: About 26% of the consolidated order book is from exports. We also have a lot of very active inquiries, which we are pursuing negotiations with certain customers.

items.statement: Government guidelines have significantly curtailed FGD demand, impacting air pollution control equipment order book
items.quote: we are seeing a growth in all our product lines, except for air pollution control equipment because the recent government guidelines have curtailed the demand for FGDs very significantly.

items.statement: Always evaluating inorganic opportunities; will disclose if something concrete materializes
items.quote: We are always evaluating. And if something fructifies, we'll get back to you.

items.statement: Philippines plant sale process ongoing with parties doing due diligence; no specific timeline; not desperate to sell at discount
items.quote: We are engaged with a few parties. Obviously, we can't talk about specific names or the discussions or even the time line. So there are some parties who are doing some amount of due diligence on the potential transaction.

items.statement: Consolidated manufacturing revenue FY25 was INR2,500 crores; target INR3,200-3,300 crores post capacity expansions
items.quote: if you notice from our consolidated results, our manufacturing revenue for the past year, 31st March '25 year end is about INR2,500 crores. So I would expect that once all these expansions and the capacity is done, so we should be reaching close to INR3,200 crores, INR3,300 crores a year.

items.statement: Targets India Domino's revenue growth of 12-17% YoY, with 5-7% LFL and 7-10% store expansion
items.quote: So, together if you really see, the number can vary from 12% to 17%, right? The upper end and lower end ranges. So, that is how we model and within 5% to 7% like-for-like growth, there should be 1% to 2% improvement in pricing or mix.

items.statement: Commits to 200 bps EBITDA margin improvement over three years from FY24 base
items.quote: I think we stand by our guidance that we have given or that what Suman gave during Investor Day that we should improve 200 basis point, right, Suman?

items.statement: Plans to open 900 Domino's stores over three years
items.quote: We are committed to about 900 stores, like we said, in the three years, right? So, that target does not change.

items.statement: Sees strong demand for Domino's; surprised by sourdough pizza uptake in Tier-2/3 cities
items.quote: I am ac tually surprised by the uptake of sourdough pizza in Tier-2, Tier-3 cities. I would have never imagined that. So, therefore, it is indicating the demand does exist in India for a brand like Domino’s

items.statement: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin improved 37 bps YoY in Q2; expects continued improvement from mix, pricing, operating leverage
items.quote: On a standalone basis, our pre-IndAS EBITDA margins have improved during the last two quarters, up by 37 basis points versus the same quarter last year.

items.statement: GST rate cut on inputs like cheese and sauces provides ~50 bps margin benefit; partially passed to consumers
items.quote: And therefore, the weightage of that in our mix is about 50 basis points in terms of margins.

items.statement: Added 93 stores in Q2 across brands and markets; total network near 3,500 stores with ~2,500 Domino's
items.quote: We continue to expand our network footprint with a run rate of approximately one new store per day, and we have added 93 stores during quarter two across brands and markets.

items.statement: Domino's India added 88 stores in Q2 (81 Domino's); YTD Domino's additions at 149; entered 16 new cities reaching 500 cities
items.quote: In Q2, we expanded the store network in India by 88 stores over previous quarter. Out of which there were 81 new Domino's store. YTD number for Domino's is now 149 in the financial year.

items.statement: Popeyes added 8 stores in Q2 (4 in Mumbai marking West entry); double-digit SSG; ADS and profitability improving
items.quote: Along with this, we opened 8 new Popeyes stores out of which 4 were in Mumbai, marking the entry of Popeyes into Western part of the country.

items.statement: COFFY in Turkey added 5 stores in Q2; now operates 172 cafes
items.quote: We added five new stores for COFFY during the quarter and now operate 172 cafes.

items.statement: H1 capex of Rs 415 crore primarily for store expansion, technology, and delivery bikes; supply chain capex minimal
items.quote: The materiality of the number fits on two accounts. One is our store CAPEX's, which is quite significant. The second is tech. And the third is in terms of our existing stores where we continue to put in maintenance CAPEX to ensure the stores are up and running to support the high LFL growth that are coming through.

items.statement: Mumbai commissary to be commissioned by Q3 or early Q4; completes major supply chain investment cycle
items.quote: With our last big investment on commissaries, which is the Mumbai one, which will get commissioned by this quarter or early next quarter, we will be done with our large supply chain cycle of investments.

items.statement: Took selective price increases on Cheese Volcano pizza and packaging charges; targets 1-2% price/mix contribution to LFL
items.quote: Like I said, we have taken price increases in Cheese Volcano pizza. W e have increased packaging charges in a few places. And some other products also, we have gone and increased the

items.statement: Reduced Big Big Pizza price from Rs 899 to Rs 799 post GST cut; passing input savings to consumers selectively
items.quote: Like for example, in Big Big Pizza, we had taken the price increase to Rs. 899. We have brought it down post-GST reduction to Rs. 799.

items.statement: Launched sourdough pizzas and breads in Q2; Big Big Pizza, Chicken Burst, Flavor Burst launched in prior quarters; Popeyes launched Flavor Burst Burgers
items.quote: During Q2, we launched sourdough pizza and breads, a new product form which is already gaining traction among customers.

items.statement: Domino's app is largest new customer acquisition channel; new customers start at lower ticket size but repeat rates stable at ~3x/year
items.quote: Today, Domino's app is the largest channel for new customer acquisition. So, therefore, from that perspective, new customers come in at a lower average ticket size, but we are seeing no dilution in the repeat rates.

items.statement: GST on inputs like cheese and sauces reduced from 12% to 5%; company remains on 5% output rate with no input tax credit
items.quote: Having said that, we are thankful to the government to bring down the GST on some of the input like the ingredients like cheese and sauces that we get from 12% to 5%.

items.statement: Consolidated interest costs declined 23.5% YoY due to efficient refinancing of Turkey acquisition debt
items.quote: Post IndAS, interest costs declined by 23.5% year-on-year, largely due to efficient refinancing of the acquisition debt in Turkey.

items.statement: Domino's India LFL 9.1% (delivery LFL 16.5%); Turkey LFL 5.6% inflation-adjusted; Sri Lanka LFL 81%; Popeyes double-digit SSG
items.quote: Domino's across geographies had a strong, positive, like-for-like growth, with India growing at 9.1%, Turkey at 5.6%, adjusted for inflation, and Sri Lanka at 81%. Popeyes also grew double-digit SSG.

items.statement: Domino's India order volume grew 15% YoY; revenue grew 15.5%; delivery channel revenue growth over 20%
items.quote: Domino's India saw strong order growth 15% year-on-year and revenue growth of 15.5%. Like I said, like-for-like growth was 9.1% and delivery like-for-like growth was 16.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Turkey revenue Rs 5.9 billion with 10.4% PAT margin; COFFY ramping up with strategic pricing
items.quote: The business reported Rs. 5.9 billion in revenues and a PAT margin of 10.4%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 19.7% YoY to Rs 23.4 billion; EBITDA grew 19.5% to Rs 4.8 billion; PAT from continued ops grew 53.7% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations grew 19.7% year-on-year to Rs. 23.4 billion and reported EBITDA grew at 19.5% to Rs. 4.8 billion.

items.statement: App traffic grew 28%; loyalty members exceed 40 million; ad monetization platform launched with Apple, Tata Neu, Flipkart
items.quote: the app. The app t raffic grew 28% and loyalty member base rose to more than 40 million

items.statement: Cheese inflation spiked post Maharashtra elections due to milk price increases; impacts gross margins
items.quote: There is some inflation that we have been hit on the cheese prices, because milk prices post the Maharashtra election have really shot up.

items.statement: Turkey hyperinflation accounting (IAS 29) causes P&L volatility from inventory revaluation; expects steadier margins going forward
items.quote: Depending on how much inventory they are holding at a certain point in time, right, and how that gets revalued into the P&L, there could be some seasonality impact of that.

items.statement: Targets ad monetization to contribute at least 50 bps of revenue over time; currently in early launch phase
items.quote: My ambition would be to get at least 50 basis points of the revenue to flow in from th is, but it will take time, right? It is not going to happen

items.statement: No plan to roll back free delivery; experimenting with packaging charges to find sweet spot; will integrate costs into product pricing without losing value proposition
items.quote: Delivery charge, no, there is no plan to roll back. However, we will continue to tinker with packaging charges as experiments and see where the sweet spot is.

items.statement: Indian auto industry posted healthy growth across all vehicle categories in Q2 FY26 driven by steady demand, GST relaxation, easing supply chains and festive season tailwinds
items.quote: During this quarter, the Indian automobile industry continued to post healthy growth across all vehicle categories, supported by, steady demand momentum, GST relaxation, easing supply chain constraints and festive season tailwinds.

items.statement: Capex guided at INR70-75 crores excluding further new order wins
items.quote: Currently, what we've guided for capex is INR70 crores to INR75 crores. That's, of course, excluding any further new order wins.

items.statement: Two new lightweighting orders for control arms and links with combined annual value US$14 million and lifetime value US$70 million, SOP expected Q1 FY28
items.value: US$14 million annual, US$70 million lifetime
items.quote: We are happy to announce 2 new orders in lightweighting vertical for control arms and links having combined annual value of US$14 million and lifetime value of US$70 million with SOP expected in Q1FY28.

items.statement: Global business vertical added order with annual value US$4.8 million and lifetime value US$24 million from Q1 customer, SOP expected Q4 FY27 with gradual ramp-up over 2 years
items.value: US$4.8 million annual, US$24 million lifetime
items.quote: Our global business vertical established last year also continues to gain traction with another order with annual value of US$4.8 million and lifetime value of US$24 million from a customer added in quarter 1. SOP expected in Q4 FY27 with gradual ramp-up over 2 years post SOP.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.8% in Q2 FY26 and 12.9% in H1 FY26, compression due to product mix, higher catalyst prices, and increased employee and other expenses from growth investments
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA margins, these are broadly in the range of 13% to 14%. In Q2, these were at 12.8%. And in first half, if you look at, these were 12.9%. Now this appears slightly lower primarily due to product mix and higher prices of brick which were as a result of upward movement in the prices of the noble metals.

items.statement: Catalyst cost increase due to higher noble metal prices passed through to revenue but lowers margin percentage mathematically
items.quote: Catalyst is a pass-through element. It doesn't affect our profitability. However, it affects the margin percentage. So if you have a higher denominator, because of higher catalyst sale, either as a result of those products which have catalysts with them or if the price of the catalyst goes up, as a percentage, purely mathematically, the margin percentage appears lower.

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical currently ~10% of revenue; exports very small percentage; both expected to become more significant
items.quote: And the lightweighting part of it is roughly 10% of revenues. As you'll see from the order wins that we've already had now in exports, the previously announced plus the one announced right now in this quarter, plus lightweighting, both would become more significant as a percentage of sales.

items.statement: Export margins very good but working capital intensive so gross level neutral; lightweighting margins too early to indicate
items.quote: On the export side, the margin profiles are definitely very good. At the same time, exports is also going to have a lot of working capital involved, right? So on a gross level, it should be neutral. And on the lightweighting side, I think, we're just getting going. It's too early to indicate yet.

items.statement: TREM5 notification remains 1 April 2026 but change very likely given timeline; nature of change difficult to guide without formal communication
items.quote: TREM5, the notification remains to be 1st April '26 by the government. However, a change seems very likely given that we are less than a quarter or maybe 4 months away from that. So I think a change is very likely. The nature of the change is very difficult to guide right now because there's no formal communication.

items.statement: Open to M&A in lightweighting vertical for localization of powertrain agnostic components; multiple conversations ongoing but not at disclosure stage; mindful of ROCE and margins
items.quote: we are always -- we are open towards M&A. And specifically, as I said, for the next 5 years we spoke about, we are talking about a preferential M&A in the lightweighting vertical. Currently, what we've guided for capex is INR70 crores to INR75 crores. That's, of course, excluding any further new order wins.

items.statement: Capacity utilization around 80% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: So capacity utilization this quarter was around 80%.

items.quote: We expect that order to start 2 quarters after previously announced. So there should be around a 2-quarter delay, and that is not much to do with tariffs. The end product SOP is going to start 2 quarters later than planned by the end customer.

items.statement: Export traction surprisingly good across US, Europe and Middle East; new order announced and good RFQ pipeline
items.quote: It is surprisingly good. And that is indicative that we just got another big order, which we announced as part of this call. And this is of course, not limited just to the U.S. market, also the Europe market. And now Middle Eastern market, ther

items.quote: So in the lightweighting vertical, whatever we have shared is powertrain agnostic, right? So they sometimes use the same parts for ICE, EV and that's interchangeable.

items.statement: Donghee technology license agreement includes royalty percentage and one-time payment; manufacturing footprint to be optimized with co-use of facilities or new facility based on significant order wins
items.quote: Regarding the terms, it's a general TLA, which has a royalty percentage and a onetime payment, right? The exact numbers of course, we can't share. Coming to the manufacturing, we want to really look at our entire ma nufacturing footprint wherever we can co -use the facility. And if an order win which is significant requires a new facility, we can look at it based on the customer that we win

items.statement: JV (ETPL) had marginally negative contribution in Q2 due to delays in in-warding by end customers; one-off and small relative to consolidated numbers
items.quote: There is a marginally negative contribution from the JV for this particular quarter. That was primarily on account of certain delays in in-warding by the end customers towards the end of the quarter. This was marginal only.

items.statement: Export business involves significant working capital; gross margin neutral despite good margin profile
items.quote: On the export side, the margin profiles are definitely very good. At the same time, exports is also going to have a lot of working capital involved, right? So on a gross level, it should be neutral.

items.statement: Augmented global business development, lightweighting, M&A, strategy teams and business development consultants leading to higher employee costs
items.quote: And additionally, we have also augmented our global business development team and team for lightweighting, plus there were marginal increments also, which have resulted in rise in the overall employee costs.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR787.2 crores in Q2 FY26 (11% YoY); H1 FY26 revenue INR1,543.5 crores (11% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter ended Q2 FY26, on a consolidated basis, we reported revenues of INR787.2 crores, reflecting a Y-o-Y growth of 11%.

items.statement: Gross profit INR194.9 crores in Q2 FY26 (4% YoY); H1 FY26 gross profit INR384.4 crores (4% YoY) in line with industry growth
items.quote: Gross profit, which is a better indicator of our performance for the quarter came in at INR194.9 crores, up 4% Y-o-Y, which is in line with the industry growth for the same period.

items.statement: EBITDA INR101 crores in Q2 FY26 (4% YoY decline); H1 FY26 EBITDA INR199.4 crores flat YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 FY26 stood at INR101 crore, translating to a Y-o-Y degrowth of 4% and EBITDA margin stood at 12.8%.

items.statement: Filed one patent in Q2 FY26, total 16 patents filed to date

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix: emissions 88%, suspensions 9%, supply chain management 2%, other 1%
items.quote: So overall, in FY '25, if you see the overall contribution of emissions business was to the tune of 88%, 9% came from suspensions, 2% from supply chain management and 1% from other miscellaneous.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 5% over FY25 base of Rs. 5,500 crore, implying ~Rs. 5,800 crore
items.quote: With all these reasons, now we are revising our guidance from 15% to 20% to 5% over the previous year. That is the guidance kind of a thing.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance at 20% over FY26, aspires for 30%
items.quote: But as of now, since FY '26 has not been completed and the base needs to be established, so still we maintain 20% growth for FY '27 as of now.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance 12.5-13% for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: It should be. 12.5% to 13% margin should be doable in the current financial year. And next year also, it will be around 13% margin should be there.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands over Rs. 20,000 crore as of 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: As of 30th September 2025, the company's unexecuted order book stands over Rs. 20,000 crores, which includes EPC value of Bhopal Bypass HAM Project of MPRDC and newly secured high level bridge project of BSRDC, in Bihar.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY26 maintained at Rs. 12,000-15,000 crore; Rs. 6,000 crore secured so far
items.quote: we had mentioned in the beginning of the year and the last quarter of the last year, our order book for FY '2 6 would be between Rs. 12,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores. We still maintain the same kind of guidance for FY '26

items.statement: Identified 76 projects worth over Rs. 1,00,000 crore for bidding in next 1.5-2 months; expects Rs. 6,000+ crore new orders by FY26 end
