items.statement: FY27 capex expected around Rs. 250 crore
items.quote: '27, around Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: Appointed dates received for 3 HAM projects (Varanasi Kolkata Packages 2, 3, 6) and 1 EPC project (Bharatpur flyover) in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Company has received appointed dates for 3 HAM projects: Varanasi Kolkata Highway Packages 2, 3 & 6. During the quarter, Company also received appointed date for an EPC project in Rajasthan for Construction of Flyover in Bharatpur City.

items.statement: MPRDC HAM project (Bhopal Bypass) appointed date delayed due to land/alignment issues; uncertainty on timing
items.quote: There are issues. The land and alignment issues are still persisting. There is a bit of uncertainty for the term. So, we would not be able to share what would be the likely appointed date.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 13.9%; H1 FY26 13.1%; consolidated Q2 22.4%, H1 24.3%
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for the 2 nd quarter of FY26 is Rs. 136 crore. Standalone EBITDA margin for the quarter is 13.9%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin decline attributed to fixed costs on lower revenue
items.quote: See, the fixed cost being the same, there is a decline in the turnover. So, the fixed cost will be largely same, similar to this one because of the overheads and other things which we cannot suddenly reduce it. That reflected in the marginal reduction in the EBITDA.

items.statement: NHAI awarding subdued for 2.5 years; NHAI FY26 target 6,300 km; pipeline of 120+ projects worth Rs. 3 lakh crore
items.quote: NHAI has set an ambitious target of 6,300 km length of new projects award for FY26, which is expected to generate substantial new business for the industry players going forward.

items.statement: Water sector: JJM and irrigation revenue guidance Rs. 900 crore for FY26 (H1: Rs. 235 crore); completion targeted by FY28
items.quote: See, under J JM, in the H1, we achieved Rs. 235 crores apart from certain revenue from the irrigation project and we still maintain Rs. 900 crores from the JJM and irrigation for FY '26.

items.statement: Received 3 LOAs in Q2: BSRDC (bridge), AAI (Varanasi Airport), NHPC (Solar+BESS)
items.quote: During Q2 FY26, Company received three Letters of Award o from Bihar State Road Development Corporation for High -level bridge construction on High Level Bridge along with approach road on Hathouri - Aurai, in Bihar o From Airports Authority of India (AAI) for the development of Varanasi International Airport. o from NHPC for the Solar Power-Cum-BESS project

items.statement: Received Rs. 2,200 crore net of debt from 11 monetized assets; Rs. 38 crore received in Q2, balance on back-to-back basis from NHAI
items.quote: For the 11 asset, the net receivable net of debt was Rs. 2,200 crore, which we have received. Shravan Shah: The entire money has been received? Pankaj Agarwal: Yes. The entire money has been received. And out of Rs. 200 crore, some money has received in this quarter, which is around Rs. 38 crore and the balance will be received as and when received from NHAI on back-to-back

items.statement: Credit ratings upgraded for 4 subsidiaries: Hathras (A to AA+), Hardoi (A to AA+), Yamuna (A to AA), Awadh (A to A+)
items.quote: I am happy to share, during the quarter, credit ratings of four of Company's subsidiaries have been upgraded significantly : 1. Hathras Highways (Mathura Package 1C): Upgraded from CARE Single A to CARE AA Plus 2. Hardoi Highways (Hardoi Bypass): Upgraded From CARE Single A to CARE AA Plus 3. Yamuna Highways (Mathura Package 1B): Upgraded from CARE Single A to CARE AA 4. Awadh Expressway (Kanpur L

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: ~Rs. 900 crore from water/irrigation, ~Rs. 4,000+ crore from highways/coal mining/others
items.quote: See, in FY '26, we are expecting total Rs. 900 crore turnover from water, drinking water supply, and irrigation projects. Aniket Madhwani: And remaining from the highway. T. R. Rao: And the remaining Rs. 4,000 plus crore s from highways and other projects

items.statement: Agra Bypass arbitration award Rs. 485 crore contingent; NHAI contemplating challenge
items.quote: See, this arbitration award is a contingent kind of a thing. Now, see, the award, what we understand is that NHAI is contemplating challenging the award.

items.statement: CIDCO order matter sub judice; no update available
items.quote: See, matter is still sub judice. So, we can't say anything now. We are not in a position to share the further details. Matter is still sub judice.

items.statement: No buyback planned; capital earmarked for HAM/TBCB/BESS equity infusion
items.quote: No. As of now, we are not considering the buyback of this thing. But that could be, see, as we are actively bidding the HAM projects in the next two -three months, the high -value HAM projects would be requiring equity infusion in these HAM projects.

items.statement: India business to outperform IPM by 100-150 bps; double-digit growth assuming market grows 8-8.5%
items.quote: So we gave an overall guidance of a double-digit kind of growth, assuming the market grows at around 8% to 8.5%, which looks like the plausible scenario.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expected at 19.5-20% despite H2 opex from US CDMO and GST impact
items.quote: And even from the EBITDA guidance perspective, I see somewhere between 19.5% to 20% should be our EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Non-US international business targeting high-teens to 20% growth for FY26
items.quote: We are expecting that looking at even the second half projections, we should be easily upwards close to around high teens of 20% kind of growth from the non-U.S. markets.

items.statement: US business expected to grow low double-digits (10-11%) for FY26 vs earlier mid-single-digit guidance
items.quote: I think it's getting close to a low double-digit kind of growth. So somewhere between 10% to 11% is what I expect.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to reach 4-5% of revenue in H2 FY26 as filings concentrated in Q4
items.quote: Most of our filings are in Q4. So I think it's more of a phasing thing, and we expect the R&D to be within 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Medium-term target of at least 1% annual EBITDA margin improvement from FY27 onwards including planned investments
items.quote: I've always maintained that year-on-year, we should look at least a 1% improvement in our overall margins.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 35-38% for FY27 as company exits MAT after March 2026
items.quote: FY '27 will be 35% to 38%, you can say, because we'll be coming out of MAT after March '26.

items.statement: US CDMO plant operational from September; opex of INR50 cr/quarter from Q3; revenue INR20 cr/quarter; targeting INR300 cr annual run-rate in 12-18 months
items.quote: The opex expense will be around INR50 crores per quarter going forward because we just started this facility in the month of September.

items.statement: Medtech opex INR8-9 cr/quarter with EBITDA loss INR5.5 cr; breakeven expected by FY28
items.quote: So for the quarter, Medtech opex was around INR8 crores to INR9 crores. So there is an EBITDA loss of around INR5.5 crores in Medtech.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO revenue INR40-45 cr booked in H1; expect INR20 cr/quarter in H2; targeting INR70-80 cr for FY26
items.quote: We have already booked around INR40 crores to INR45 crores of revenue from CDMO business in U.S. And going forward for the next 2 quarters, again, we see around INR20 crores per quarter of revenue.

items.statement: Enzene Pune operations at INR25-30 cr/quarter; H1 revenue INR180-185 cr including US business from Pune
items.quote: In H1, we are around INR180 crores to INR185 crores of revenue, including the U.S. business, which we do from Pune.

items.statement: Gross margin stable at 65% despite strong growth due to API price decline offset by higher international mix
items.quote: But our international business growth was higher than domestic in quarter 2. And whenever international business will grow at a higher rate than domestic, there will be impact on gross margin because our gross margin for domestic business is better than international.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance 64-65% for H2 and full year FY26
items.quote: Yes, 64% to 65%, you can.

items.statement: GST revision positive for affordability; one-time trade impact INR10-12 cr; recurring Sikkim benefit loss INR50-60 cr in H2 (INR25-30 cr/quarter)
items.quote: And second is the benefit that we used to get from Sikkim. So I think that's a substantial impact, which is going to hit us in -- from now on. So I think that impact in H2 alone is close to around INR50 crores to INR60 crores.

items.statement: Domestic Q2 growth 12.4% YoY; outperformed IPM in 6 of 11 therapies; became #1 in Acute segment per IQVIA
items.quote: According to IQVIA SSA data for Q2 FY '26 in the Acute segment in domestic market, Alkem became the number one company.

items.statement: US sales grew 28% YoY driven by sacubitril/valsartan launch; 4 launches in Q2
items.quote: I think the most meaningful launch in U.S. has been sacubitril/valsartan that we have done in Q2. And that has really done well for us.

items.statement: GLP-1 CT for diabetes completed; SEC approval received; awaiting formal MA; expect to be among first players at patent expiry
items.quote: Our India application, our CT for diabetes indication is already completed. We presented to the subject expert committee. And we have got approval that's a public information.

items.statement: Tolvaptan (Jynarque) launch slated for FY27-28 pending litigation; Mirabegron launch after patent expiry per settlement
items.quote: So in tolvaptan, you are talking about the Jynarque approval, so that is slated for FY '27-28.

items.statement: Government reportedly considering MIP on penicillin G; impact speculative until notification; inventories sufficient
items.quote: So this is speculative, Bansi, at this point in time. And any hypothesis that I build on any speculation won't hold true. So we are waiting for some notification to come.

items.statement: Other expenses for Q3 and Q4 guided at INR900-905 cr/quarter including Enzene and Medtech opex
items.quote: The other expense will be for quarter 3 and quarter 4 will be in the range of, say, INR900 crores, INR905 crores.

items.statement: Acquired Bombay Ortho and Adroit in April 2025; intangible assets and goodwill increased from trademark and technical know-how capitalization
items.quote: So we acquired 2 companies in April '25, one was Bombay Ortho and other one was Adroit. So other intangible assets also includes the trademark and the technology -- technical know-how, which we got from the company when we acquired them.

items.statement: Continuously evaluating domestic brand acquisitions; good cash on balance sheet; will pursue right opportunities at right value
items.quote: I think India is our core market. And I've always said that we are continuously on the lookout now we have good cash on our balance sheet as well.

items.statement: Adroit business merged into domestic operations; no longer tracked separately
items.quote: It's -- it will now be merged with our domestic business. So we'll run it as a part of the middle.

items.statement: US price erosion inevitable on new launches like sacubitril/valsartan; timing uncertain (3-6 months); base business flat with volume growth offset by price erosion
items.quote: See price erosion in a new launch in U.S. is a market phenomenon, right? This is only first quarter of players entering. So the question is whether price erosion will happen, price erosion will happen.

items.statement: Constant currency growth for non-US international business ~28% in Q2 (reported 32% with 4-4.5% currency gain)
items.quote: Overall, I think we have had a currency gain of close to 4% to 4.5% in the range of 4% to 4.5%.

items.statement: US CDMO plant asset turnover target of 1x; currently in development phase not commercial manufacturing
items.quote: This is all development work. It's not a commercial scale manufacturing.

items.statement: Management expects Q3 FY26 volumes and EBITDA per ton to be similar to Q2 FY26 levels; declines to provide full-year FY26 or FY27 guidance due to volatility
items.quote: I'd be very happy if we are able to end our numbers on similar lines as Q2

items.statement: Management does not want to assign any guess for Q4 FY26 or full year FY26/FY27; will reassess after Q3 results
items.quote: I don't want to be assigning any guess there because I do see Q4 we can have a lot of positives. But if I look at Q3, I would like to restrict my listing to Q3

items.statement: India volumes flat YoY and QoQ in Q2 FY26; Tier 1 volumes declined due to GST-driven inventory adjustments and reformulation, offset by non-Tier 1 market share gains
items.quote: overall flat volume performance for India on both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis

items.statement: AMET region volumes declined high-single-digit YoY and single-digit QoQ in Q2 FY26 due to Egypt market share loss to backward-integrated local players; Türkiye grew double-digit
items.quote: The AMET region recorded a modest single-digit volume decline quarter-on-quarter and a high-single-digit decline on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Rest of World volumes grew double-digit YoY in Q2 FY26 driven by Latin America and Asia Pacific; North America declined due to reciprocal tariffs
items.quote: Latin America and Asia Pacific maintained their strong growth trajectory with posting double-digit year-on-year gains

items.statement: Management expects India demand recovery from Q4 FY26 as GST inventory adjustments ease and reformulation approvals come through; Q3 FY26 likely similar to Q2
items.quote: We're seeing the first signs of the same in November and basis the discussions with our large customers, we do expect the same to continue

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA declined 5% YoY to INR 251 crores; EBITDA per metric ton ~INR 18,700 for H1; Q2 FY26 EBITDA per metric ton INR 17,300
items.quote: Our EBITDA declined by 5% year-on-year at INR 251 crores vis-a-vis INR265 crores in H1 FY '25 and consequently, H1 FY '26 EBITDA per metric ton stood at INR18,700 per metric ton approximately

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA per metric ton was INR 17,300
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR17,300 per metric ton

items.statement: Cumulative full-year FY26 EBITDA impact from US tariffs estimated at 3-5% of FY25 EBITDA; projects delayed and customers building inventory slowly
items.quote: Cumulatively, the impact for the whole year was in the range of 3% to 5% of our FY '25 EBITDA

items.statement: Fatty alcohol prices remain elevated with historically high spread vs crude petroleum; lower-than-expected palm kernel oil production keeping feedstock prices high into October-November
items.quote: Despite the harvest season, lower-than-expected palm kernel oil production has kept feedstock prices elevated, and this trend is expected to continue and persist into October and November as well

items.statement: Freight costs eased compared to previous quarters but shipment delays persist due to port congestion and blank sailings
items.quote: Freight costs eased compared to previous quarters, offering some relief. However, shipment delays continue due to ongoing port congestion and blank sailings

items.statement: Reformulation from oleochemical to petrochemical surfactants accelerated in Q2 FY26 due to high fatty alcohol prices; Galaxy developing petrochemical-based alternate surfactants for commercialization in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect the requisite approvals to come in this quarter and business to comme rcialize from Q4 FY '26

items.statement: Reformulation impact estimated at 3,000-4,000 tons volume loss in India in Q2 FY26; management views this as cyclical not structural, with reversal typically in 12-15 months after oleochemical prices correct
items.quote: we could have done in the quarter, about 3,000 to 4,000 tons higher volume if this reformulation had not happened

items.statement: US customers unhappy with tariffs and seeking to diversify vendor base; Galaxy working on Egypt plant approvals to service US demand and building pipeline in LatAm, APAC, Europe
items.quote: every customer would want to have a diversified vendor base and also more dependable vendors. So they are not in a good situation where they are looking at the earliest opportunity where they can get back to business with us

items.statement: Egypt market share erosion due to aggressive local backward-integrated competitors; reformulation also occurring in AMET markets as customers reduce active ingredient content
items.quote: continued market share erosion in Egypt by the Tier 1 segment due to intensified competition from aggressive local players who are backward integrated

items.statement: US imposed 50% tariffs on Indian exports from August 1, 2024, impacting existing business and pipeline projects; India GST rate reduction on FMCG products caused inventory adjustments
items.quote: additional 50% tariffs not only had adverse impact on our existing businesses where the tariff is applicable but also had a continuing effect on our projects in the pipeline

items.statement: CWIP of ~INR 260 crores as of FY25; most new capacity in India, some in Egypt, from projects initiated 1.5 years ago
items.quote: Most of them will be in India, some of it in Egypt, but most of it will be in India in terms of what projects we initiated 1.5 years back

items.statement: US capacity expansion under review on drawing board; awaiting tariff sustainability clarity and cost competitiveness assessment; balance sheet ready to move quickly
items.quote: we are preparing our plans on the drawing board to be ready, okay? And we are also very clear that we need to set up capacity that can be cost competitive

items.statement: Consolidated volumes flat YoY and QoQ in Q2 FY26; Performance Surfactants high-single-digit decline; Specialty Care double-digit volume growth driven by non-US geographies
items.quote: consolidated volumes for the quarter remained flat year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter, while Performance Surfactants registered a high-single-digit decline, mass specialties despite tariff uncertainty, clocked double-digit volume growth driven by non-US geographies

items.statement: Near-term outlook muted due to global challenges and margin pressures; US tariff inflationary impact on consumer demand uncertain; fatty alcohol price correction timeline unclear
items.quote: the near-term outlook appears muted, reflecting global business challenges and margin pressures across both segments

items.statement: Reformulation reversal typically takes 12-15 months after oleochemical prices correct; first signs of palm kernel oil price decline seen in last two weeks but need to wait and watch
items.quote: the reversal typically, what I've seen is that those reversals happen probably in about 12 to 15 months

items.statement: Launched five second-generation sunscreen molecules at in-cosmetics Bangkok in November 2024; healthy pipeline building across APAC, Europe, US for Sun Care and skin formulation products
items.quote: Organically, the recent in-cosmetics in Bangkok, we launched five products, all in the Sun Care range, the latest second-generation sunscreen molecules

items.statement: EPC project revenue recognition spread over more than a year; progressing well per timeline but no specific FY25 recognition guidance given
items.quote: it's more than a year project. So it will be spread over a period of more than a year

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR1,300 crores and EBITDA margin 23-25% maintained
items.quote: Our target is to reach INR1,300 crores and many of the things as I told you, they are under WIP, and we will be processing in Q3 and Q4, we will be working harder to reach the target.

items.statement: Medium-term growth target at least 10% year-on-year, potentially higher after capex
items.quote: are having certain kind of facilities currently we are operating. And as your point, I appreciate we are having a lot of plans for increasing our revenues and we are having the strong capex plans okay? And we will be targeting every year at least 10% growth, okay

items.statement: Order book INR2,220 crores as of Oct 2025, plus INR500 crores pipeline expected by March 2026
items.quote: So actually, if you look at our order book, 70% of the orders are from defense and our total order book as on today is INR2,220 crores, out of which about 70% of the orders are from defense, 20% are from space and about 10% that includes energy and other current standing.

items.statement: INR600 crores titanium and INR450 crores super alloy orders in current book
items.quote: And instantly, I wish to inform you that we have INR600 crores worth of titanium order book currently. So we'll be executing them and to reach that INR1,300 crores business. And we have about INR450 crores of super alloys or ders currently

items.statement: Expect INR2,000 crores opening order book for FY27
items.quote: Actually, we are thinking even some more order will come. The first April 2026, we expect at least INR2,000 crores opening balance will be there minimum.

items.statement: Non-defense share growing from energy, space, exports; defense currently 70% of order book
items.quote: We expect at least maybe 10% to 15% maybe exports in the coming 2 to 3 years. That is what we are expecting. And there will be increase both from space as well as other. Energy, we are expecting because once this order fructifies, the ultra-supercritical order, that will have significant increase in the energy side.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 21.82%, PAT margin 6.73%; full year EBITDA margin target 23%
items.quote: The EBITDA and PAT margins for the first half stood at 21.82% and 6.73%, respectively.

items.statement: Confident of achieving 23% EBITDA margin once INR1,300 crore revenue target met
items.quote: Definitely, once INR1,300 crores as come, 23% EBITDA is not an issue and it will definitely come. It will -- we are confident of that.

items.statement: Capex plan under finalization, details expected by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: We are in discussion with our ministry and we should be ready with maybe by end of Q3, we'll be able to make those plans and probably in the next con call, we can give you detailed figures.

items.statement: Bottleneck is infrastructure; capability exists for 500 grades including 100 aeronautical grades
items.quote: It is not the question of capability. Capability exists. We have a very strong R&D team in Midhani. We have wealth of knowledge. We have profit sheets for so many grades. It is only question of infrastructure.

items.statement: Metal bank MOU signed Nov 10, 2025 for 6 critical raw materials; customer-owned, Midhani-operated; operational in 6-8 months
items.quote: Midhani has entered into Memorandum of Understanding on November 10, 2025 for creating a metal bank at Midhani to ensure uninterrupted production and supplies of projects of national importance.

items.statement: Virgin to scrap ratio typically 60:40; limited by customer requirements (e.g., Gaganyaan human-rated)
items.quote: So typically, the ratio of the virgin material to scrap will be in the ratio of 60% to 40%. So sometimes when huge orders are there where virgin materials have to be used, scrap generated cannot be put back into production line and there will be accumulation.

items.statement: Revenue mix: specialty steel 37%, super alloys 21%, titanium alloys 19%, maraging steel 15%, other grades 8%
items.quote: Super alloys, for example, we have -- so we have total percentage of super alloys is 21%, titanium alloys is about 19%, maraging steel is about 15% and specialty steel is about 37%. A nd all other grades, minus all the above 4, it comes to about 80%. So this is a revenue hit of 8

items.statement: Empaneled for all ISRO launch vehicles (PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV) and Gaganyaan human-rated mission
items.quote: Midhani's material is what you see in the -- when the launch vehicle lifts, whether it is PSLV, GSLV or LVM3 or any of these SSLVs. You see the Midhani's rocket motor casing that is what gets ignited on the ground.

items.statement: Supplying materials for Tejas Mk2 program; grades under type testing and qualification
items.quote: Okay. See, luckily, we are the company producing materials for the Tejas Mk2. Yes, there are number of grades in that and we have already started processing these materials.

items.statement: Supplying special steels to shipyards (Hindustan Shipyard, Mazagon Dock); indigenizing imported grades
items.quote: We are working with Mazagon Dock Limited for some of the indigenized steels. There are grades which are currently being imported. So we are discussing with them on indigenization of steel and we'll be soon developing these steel grades.

items.statement: Exports INR95 crores last year; targeting INR100-150 crores annually post NADCAP certification by Q4 FY26
items.quote: If you look at our exports last year, we have exported orders worth of INR95 crores, about INR94 crores, okay. So currently, we have already supplied to the tune of INR 21 crores, okay, till now, till second half.

items.statement: NADCAP certification for export eligibility to be completed by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Midhani is going for NADCAP certification, which is essential for export orders. So by Q4, we'll be completing this NADCAP certification also, which will enable us to export the materials.

items.statement: Value of production H1 FY26 INR497.67 crores, up 3.9% YoY
items.quote: Value of production during the second quarter of FY '25-'26 stood at INR256.38 crores, and VoP for firs t half of FY '25-'26 was INR497.67 crores, registering a growth of 3.9% against the value of production of INR479.01 crores recorded in the corresponding period of previous year

items.statement: MOU for ABHED bulletproof jacket technology transfer from DRDO and IIT Delhi signed Nov 2025
items.quote: And another important thing is we have signed a MoU for a bulletproof jacket, its name is ABHED. And it is a technology developed by DRDO and Indian Institute of Technology Delhi and this will significantly increase the forthcoming orders for bulletproof jackets.

items.statement: Metal powder plant for additive manufacturing: PO placed, targeting installation in 6 months
items.quote: we have already initiated, there is a purchase order. Okay? So we are pursuing with the company to supply this equipment. With this, the advantage is Midhani is also producing metal powders for additive manufacturing

items.statement: Raw material supply chain disruptions caused deliberate non-booking of some export orders
items.quote: One of the reasons why we are falling short is because there were some raw material constraints for processing of some of the titanium alloys. We need to import materials from abroad. So where we are having currently some geopolitical situation is not so good. So we are not getting -- some supply chain disruption was there.

items.statement: Order execution timeline 12-18 months; developmental grades take longer
items.quote: The time line for executing the current order book, okay? So currently, we are having about INR2,200 crores, and we expect another -- anyway, we are moving towards something like -- yes, we should be able to complete by 12 to 18 months, whatever orders currently we are having.

items.statement: Visioning exercise for 2030 and 2047 underway; aligned with Viksit Bharat
items.quote: Already, we are into the exercise of 2030 and 2047. And we are a significant partner in Viksit Bharat, proposed by Honorable Prime Minister.

items.statement: Expect mid-teens RevPAR growth in Q3 FY26
items.quote: If we continue on this trajectory, then mid-teens is the minimum expectation for revenue growth for Q3.

items.statement: Target net EBITDA margin of at least 59% by FY28 excluding extraordinary expenses
items.quote: But going forward, our forward thinking is that we would be very disappointed if by FY28, our net EBITDA without extraordinary expenses is less than 59%.

items.statement: Expect FY26 EBITDA margin to be same as FY25 despite higher renovation spend
items.quote: I think in FY26, our EBITDA margin will be the same as FY25, which means effectively that the increase in spend, we will make up with a double increase in revenue.

items.statement: Plan to spend Rs. 130-140 crore on renovation in FY26 including capex
items.quote: In 2025, for example, this year, I think we are going to spend about Rs. 130 crore, Rs. 140 crore, including capex in the renovation of our hotels.

items.statement: Total renovation spend of Rs. 450 crore across portfolio with Rs. 300 crore already spent over last 2-2.5 years
items.quote: When we finished the renovation, we will have invested Rs. 450 crore across the portfolio.

items.statement: Renovation OPEX, technology OPEX and ex-gratia together accounted for 8% of revenue in Q2 vs 5% last year
items.quote: if you look at renovation OPEX, TFS OPEX, ex-gratia and so on, it put together is a bout 8% of revenue in this quarter v/s 5% last year

items.statement: Renovated 3,000 out of 4,600 rooms needing renovation; 1,600 rooms remaining to be renovated by end of next calendar year
items.quote: We have renovated about 3,000 out of 4,600 rooms. Some more will be renovated in H2. Many, many more will be renovated in H1 next year.

items.statement: Operational portfolio at 121 hotels and 10,956 rooms as of September 30, 2025; total inventory 242 hotels and 20,074 rooms
items.quote: As of September 30, 2025, the total inventory for the group stands at 242 hotels and 20,074 rooms with 10,956 rooms and 121 hotels being operational and the rest in pipeline.

items.statement: Signed 15 new management and franchise contracts adding 1,138 rooms to pipeline; operationalized 5 hotels adding 272 rooms in Q2
items.quote: In Q2, we signed 15 new management and franchise contracts, adding 1,138 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 5 hotels, adding 272 rooms to the operational portfolio.

items.statement: Target pipeline of 35,000-40,000 rooms in next 2.5 years including operational rooms
items.quote: We think that we should be closer to 35,000 to 40,000 rooms as a pipeline that is double the pipeline in the next 2.5 years, including operational.

items.statement: Expect managed hotel openings of 5,000 rooms next year and 7,000 rooms the following year
items.quote: So I think we should do 5,000 next year, maybe 7,000 the following year.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 net EBITDA margin at 43%, down 306 bps YoY due to renovation, technology and ex-gratia expenses
items.quote: Net EBITDA grew 1% to Rs. 132.4 crore, translating to a net EBITDA margin of 43%, which decreased by 306 bps YoY, primarily due to increased investments in renovation, technology and a onetime ex-gratia payment to employees due to salary cuts during COVID.

items.statement: Expect renovation, technology and ex-gratia expenses to reduce from 8% to 5% of revenue next year and stabilize at 2% by FY28
items.quote: While these expenses/investments accounted for 8% of revenue in this quarter, we expect all these 3 expense heads to reduce to 5% of revenue in the next year, before stabilizing at 2% of revenue by FY28 onwards.

items.statement: GST rate cut impact assessed at 3-3.5% of revenue loss from input credit; expect to offset by next year as more rooms priced above Rs. 7,500
items.quote: For us, the impact then assessed was 3% - 3.5% of revenue because that was the loss of input credit and your expenses would go up that much.

items.statement: Red Fox Aerocity rebranded as Lemon Tree Hotel Aerocity enabling repricing from Q3 onwards
items.quote: Post these upgradations, for example, the Red Fox Aerocity Hotel has been rebranded as Lemon Tree Hotel Aerocity, which will now allow us to reprice the hotel from this quarter onwards and capture significantly higher revenue.

items.statement: First fully renovated Keys hotel in Pune showed 47% RevPAR improvement YoY
items.quote: As an example, we have seen a significantly improved performance in the first fully renovated Keys hotel in Pune, which has now shown an increase of roughly 47% in RevPAR YoY.

items.statement: Expect industry demand growth of 15-18% annually driven by airline capacity doubling and airport expansion from 140 to 260
items.quote: What does this tell you that demand is going to grow at 15%-16%-18% a year.

items.statement: Q2 demand muted due to high base effect, floods, airline crash, geopolitical tensions and festival timing shifts
items.quote: Last year, Q1 was muted because of elections and pent-up demand moved to Q2. So last year, Q1 base was low, Q2 base was high.

items.statement: Debt reduced to Rs. 1,610 crore as of September 30, 2025 from Rs. 1,822 crore a year ago; credit rating improved to A+ from A
items.quote: The debt for the company stood at Rs. 1,610 crore as of 30th September, a fall of Rs. 212 crore vis-a-vis the Rs. 1,822 crore on 30th September last year. Lemon Tree has also improved its credit rating to A+ from A.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings reduced to 7.72% in Q2 FY26 from 8.68% in Q2 FY25 due to rating upgrade
items.quote: which has significantly reduced our cost of borrowings over the year to 7.72% in Q2 this year as compared to 8.68% in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Won Letter of Award for 2.25 acres in Nehru Place, Delhi for 500-550 room Aurika hotel; initial approvals and design underway

items.statement: Cloud-based platform with AI/ML for personalization, analytics, automated processing; ML-driven intelligent orchestration for dynamic service selection, pricing, consumption

items.statement: International presence in 100+ countries, 3,000+ touchpoints spanning lounges, wellness, golf, meet & assist; global lounge revenue doubled QoQ
items.quote: Internationally, we now enable access in 100+ countries through 3,000+ touchpoints, spanning lounges, wellness experiences, golf access, meet & assist and other premium services.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with net worth INR333.1Cr up 25.8% YoY; cash and equivalents INR141Cr; no debt details disclosed
items.quote: We continue to have a strong balance sheet with our net worth currently at INR333.1 crores, up by 25.8% compared to the same time last year. Our cash and cash equivalent balance as at quarter end stood at INR141 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 20-25% YoY; EBITDA margin to increase 1-1.5% from FY25's 8% to 9-9.5%
items.quote: our guideline is for 20 to 25% overall increase, and the EBITDA margin, which was 8% last year, will increase by 1 to 1.5%, staying around 9 to 9.5% overall.

items.statement: FY26 technical plant revenue INR 250-260 cr; FY27 technical plant revenue INR 300-310 cr (20-25% growth)
items.quote: For FY '26, our revenue for technical plant will be around INR 250 crores to INR 260 crores. And after that, it will be increased by again 20% to 25%, what guidance we are giving. So on that parameter.

items.statement: FY26 segment revenue targets: B2C INR 220-230 cr, B2B bulk & formulation INR 630-650 cr, exports INR 70-80 cr, technical INR 250-270 cr; total INR 1,150-1,200 cr
items.quote: Our internal revenue target for the current year for B2C, it will be around INR 220 crores to INR 230 crores. It will be increased by, as we already told, 20% to 25% increase of our last year sale. Our B2B bulk and formulation will be around INR 630 crores to INR 650 crores. Our export will be around INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores and our technical business will be INR 250 crores to INR 270 crores

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 715 cr, up 26% YoY; Q2 revenue INR 347 cr, up 12% YoY but sequentially lower due to early monsoon pulling Kharif demand into Q1
items.quote: For the first half of financial year '26, revenue reached INR 715 crores, registering 26% year -on-year growth. This year, our Q2 revenue was sequentially lower than Q1, which is the uncommon trend of our company. The primary reason fo r this divergence was an early onset of monsoon, which arrived nearly 20 days ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Rabi season outlook positive with full reservoirs and good moisture; confident of surpassing last year's Rabi performance and achieving 20-25% growth in H2
items.quote: Looking forward to the upcoming Rabi season, with favorable moisture and reservoir level nationwide, we are optimistic about the good demand momentum, we are con fident of our ability to surpass last year's Rabi performance and remain firmly on track to achieve our growth objective for financial year '26.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved slightly YoY due to scale and operating leverage; Q2 margin compressed sequentially and YoY due to lower brand formulation share, higher active ingredient/export mix, appraisal costs, headcount rise, and MTM f
items.quote: However, on an H1 FY '26 to FY '25 comparison, margin improved slightly, driven by higher scale and operating leverage. This improvement is inflected in our net profit, which stood at INR 49.9 crores for H1 FY '26, up from INR 36.1 crores H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Technical prices stable most months; slight 5-10% decrease in some products in last 1-2 months due to erratic rainfall; formulation prices follow technical with lag, B2C less immediate
items.quote: The price trend was good until now. Now, maybe in the last one or two months, a slight decrease is visible in some products. Otherwise, in all other months it was good

items.quote: So, mainly in technical, our key products are Cypermethrin, Alphamethrin, and Permethrin. And the second line that we have developed for our captive consumption includes Hexaconazole, Metalaxyl, and Chlorantraniliprole. The maximum we will use in captive consumption.

items.statement: Trade receivables grew 30% vs 26% revenue growth in H1 due to monsoon delay; expected to normalize in H2 and come down on YoY basis
items.quote: This trend was actually it is agrochemical industry normally if you see, so in H1, inventory and receivables are always high actually. So, it is the trend thing. However, by 50 to 20 days because there is a delay in monsoon, so some receivables has increased, but it will be taken care in H2.

items.statement: Kheti Point online platform sold off earlier; no current role
items.quote: We are not talking about that. We closed that. We sold it off earlier. Currently, Kheti Point has no role in this.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth guidance of 75-85% YoY for FY26
items.quote: over the next six months again, on a standalone basis, we will grow our revenues year-on-year between 75% to 85%.

items.quote: We expect to have between Rs. 3,000 crores to Rs. 3,500 crores worth of transactions or approvals on the pipeline by the end of the year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 25% for FY27
items.quote: At a consolidated level next year we can expect a EBITDA margin of 25%.

items.statement: Qualified pipeline of $45 million across 85 deals in 24 countries with 35 active deals
items.quote: we have close to $45 million or close to Rs. 400 crore worth of pipelines. And this is qualified pipelines. Qualified pipelines across 85 deals in 24 countries.

items.quote: Geographic mix also, you will see India continues to be strong in India. 40% is India. But we are now hedging ourselves and we have a large part, over 50% of our pipeline now is across the world. Across Africa, Asia, and MENA.

items.statement: Supply chain finance business at 54% EBITDA margin (post-capitalization)
items.quote: We are showing 54% EBITDA profitability in the supply chain finance business. And this is taking into account whether it i s capitalized or not capitalized, there is a 54% EBITDA in the supply chain finance business

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA jumped over 300% YoY post-capitalization
items.quote: And as you can see, our EBITDAs have jumped over 300%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 18% in H1 FY26 (before NCI)
items.quote: Our consolidated PAT margin before NCI is 7% and post NCI is 6.5% and our EBITDA margins are 18% on console.

items.statement: Product side steady-state EBITDA margin target 50%+
items.quote: on a steady state basis, which we will hit, you should be expecting a 50% EBITDA margin on the product side of the business.

items.statement: Heavy IP investment in 6 enterprise products simultaneously on Veefin 4.0 architecture; investments to continue for next year then taper
items.quote: Some IP investments will continue being heavy for the next year and then they start tapering down.

items.quote: So, from the year before, from our 149 days, we have now come down to 130 days, our DSOs. Okay. And this is not just on a standalone basis, even on a console basis, our DSOs are improving. Last year, we had 138 and we have come down to 105.

items.statement: Preferential round of Rs 94.3 crore raised; BSE approval pending
items.quote: we have also raised a preferential round. BSE approval is pending. Should be coming in the next few days, we are assuming. For Rs. 94.3 crore, this sets us up very well for fueling our continued IP investments.

items.statement: Acquired Epik and Regime (26% stake via Estorifi); services business (20% stake); Veefin Capital (no business yet)

items.statement: Plan to increase stake in acquired companies per existing agreements
items.quote: in terms of taking over a higher stake in the acquired companies, yes, that is a part of the plan that we have. So, those were the agreements that we had in place when we acquired these companies.

items.quote: We, on the product side, we have close to 600 across the group. We have around 900 people on the services side of the business. And on the sales team, only on the product side, we have close between 35 and 40 people.

items.quote: We are looking at our manpower very closely. Then we are seeing opportunities of enhancing our productivity. We are letting go. We are restructuring our people. We are making do with lesser manpower to deliver the same work which we have been doing.

items.statement: SaaS pricing model: recurring, transaction-based, AUM-based, pay-as-you-grow; moving away from upfront licenses
items.quote: The pricing model that we have in our quiver is all around SaaS based pricing, recurring pricing. It could be pricing based on transaction. It could be pricing based on A UM. items.statement: Supply chain finance run rate $40 billion annual disbursements
items.quote: our run rate is $40 billion worth of annual disbursements.

items.statement: Enterprise sales have high acquisition cost, long sales cycles; execution risk in simultaneous multi-product development

items.statement: Targets loan book growth of ~25% over next 2-3 years with secured lending share >50%

items.quote: The Bank aims to maintain a NIM of around 8.5% and deliver a return on equity of about 15% supported by efficient operations and moderated growth towards the end of FY '28.

items.statement: Expects steady-state credit cost up to 2% on combined secured and unsecured portfolio

items.statement: Current equity raise of Rs 950 crore sufficient for next 24 months till September 2027
items.quote: So broadly speaking from our side, the current raise of Rs. 950 crore is good enough for next 24 months. You can say till September ‘27.

items.statement: Expects normal JLG disbursements to resume in next 2-3 months as guardrail impact stabilizes
items.quote: My sense is next 2-3 months’ time, we should see almost regular type of disbursement. It is very difficult to predict the exact quantum, but disbursement will become very regular in next 2-3 months’ time.

items.statement: NIM target of 8.5% by FY28 driven by lower cost of funds, higher retail yields and normalized slippages
items.quote: If I take combination of all combined, we should be looking again sometime FY '28 at 8.5% NIM is what our execution plans are.

items.statement: MBBL portfolio grew 39% YoY to 13% of micro-banking book; penetration below 6%

items.statement: Expects credit cost to improve meaningfully in Q3 and normalize from Q4 onwards

items.statement: Total deposits flat QoQ but up 10% YoY; retail TD +29% YoY, CASA +17% YoY; CASA+retail TD ratio 78%

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 17.2% as of Sep 30 2025; raised Rs 950 cr via rights issue in Nov 2025 for Tier-1 capital

items.statement: Reverse merger of holding company with bank: all statutory approvals secured; assessing NCLT petition timing

items.quote: We are very near to the port. If we get that opportunity, definitely, we'd like to have it.

items.statement: Container manufacturing: ~15,000 units produced since 2021; INR420 crores forex saved
items.quote: The company has so far manufactured almost 15,000 containers and saved around INR420 crores of foreign exchange in four and a half years.

items.statement: JV discussions ongoing for non-railway products; Dubai JV deferred; no commitment until materialized
items.quote: We have both planned formation of JV for some other products, not for the railway products. So, when the things will materialize, then we will declare it as of now. It is just into the thinking stage only.

items.statement: Container pricing under pressure due to steel rates; stainless steel containers reduce tare weight and increase payload
items.quote: This is the basically incremental -- steel rates meaning we have to offer a low price for our containers.

items.statement: Demand driven by innovation and customer conviction; no predictable seasonality; solutions sold for steel coil, slab, sheet transport
items.quote: We keep on developing, we keep on innovating, we keep on searching the market, we keep on convincing our customers to go for it, to go for it. Some people get convinced, some people may not get convinced.

items.statement: Not competing on standard containers or wagons; differentiated via specialized designs; private maintenance of wagons may be allowed in 6-12 months
items.quote: I think I told you my strategy. I am not into the red race.

items.statement: Domestic demand remains robust supported by pharma and personal care sectors; international markets face headwinds from consumption softness and geopolitical issues
items.quote: Domestic demand remained robust, supported by strong manufacturing activity and steady consumption in pharma and personal care sectors.

items.statement: Expect demand momentum in India to remain firm while global conditions should gradually stabilize
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect demand momentum in India to remain firm, while global conditions should gradually stabilize.

items.statement: Optimistic of growing volumes in H2 FY26 on same basis as Q2 over Q1; expect Q3 and Q4 to be slightly better
items.quote: In the same lines, ma'am, we expect we are optimistic of growing in the same basis as we've grown in Q2 over Q1, and we expect Q3 and Q4 to be slightly better.

items.statement: Texol UAE branch expected to reach full capacity utilization in 1.5 to 2 years
items.quote: Texol, it will still take about 1.5 years to 2 years to reach full capacity utilization.

items.statement: No capacity expansion planned for next 2-3 years; need to catch up with capacity utilization first
items.quote: Ma'am, we've just enhanced capacity towards the end of last year. I don't see us enhancing capacity for the next 2 to 3 years at least.

items.statement: Silvassa capex for automobile lubricants expected to increase volumes by ~19,000 kL per annum with highest gross margins
items.quote: Ma'am, Silvassa capex is mostly for automobile lubricants. Once it comes on stream, it is expected to increase automobile lubricants volumes by close to 19,000 kL per annum and automobile lubricants has the highest gross margins.

items.statement: EBITDA per KL expected to increase by INR 5-6 in FY27 driven by volume growth in PHPO and transformer oils
items.quote: Perfect. EBITDA per ton only, let me check. Yes, it will go up to INR5, INR6, per litre.

items.statement: Price pass-through contracts with major marquee customers mitigate crude oil price fluctuation risks
items.quote: Yes. So with the major marquee customers of ours, we have price pass-through contracts, and they do mitigate the risks.

items.quote: But it is not a one-to-one correspondence. There is a delayed, say, generally a movement in crude price takes about 45 to 60 days to take effect in the base oil prices. items.statement: Working capital days increased to 85 from 77 as of March 2025 due to higher inventory (58 days) and receivables (68 days) from longer export lead times; creditor days improved to 41
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, working capital days increased to 85 from 77 as of March '25, primarily due to higher inventory days at 58 and receivables at 68, reflecting longer lead times in exports. Creditors days improved to 41, providing some offset.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio negligible; finance cost reduced by converting overseas suppliers to non-LC terms and SOFR declining to sub-5%
items.quote: The finance cost reduction is basically because our finance cost is mostly represented by way of discounting for import LCs, which we do from Indian branches of foreign banks. Second, SOFR also has come down in this quarter, it has

items.statement: Cash on hand in range of INR 70-80 crores including fixed deposits; open to inorganic growth and currently evaluating options
items.quote: Cash on hand is somewhere in the range of INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores. This includes the fixed deposits of the bank of the company. But inorganic growth, yes, we are open to it. We have, in the past, evaluated a few options, which have not worked out. We are currently evaluating some options.

items.statement: BHEL transformer oil contract strategically important for breaking into their requirements; expect supplies to grow
items.quote: So I will not be able to give you details about how much in terms of contribution. But this is a very important contract for us because it has allowed us to break into that BHEL's transformer oil requirements. And going forward, we expect our supplies to them also.

items.statement: PHPO segment at 49% of H1 FY26 revenue; four initiatives to strengthen: new geographies, additional products to existing customers, newer customers, increasing wallet share
items.quote: Yes. So basically, there are 3 or 4 initiatives which we're looking over there. One is, like I mentioned, new geographies. Second is additional products to existing customers. Third is newer customers in this field. And fourth is increasing our wallet share with them.

items.statement: Automobile lubricants has highest gross margins; transformer oil is biggest growing segment due to DISCOMs and electricity transmission
items.quote: automobile lubricants also has higher gross margins. Transformer oil is the biggest among the growing segments in the country because of DISCOMs and electricity transmission. So that is also a huge growth driver for

items.statement: Red Sea disruptions have more or less stabilized; freight costs still high but able to pass on enhanced freight costs to most customers
items.quote: Ma'am, the Red Sea issues have more or less stabilized. Freight costs are still high, but we have been able to pass on this enhanced freight cost to most of our customers.

items.statement: Consolidated manufacturing volumes in H1 FY26 at 261,524 KL, up ~9% from 240,318 KL in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our consolidated manufacturing volumes of H1 FY26 stood at 261,524 KL, up approximately 9% from 240,318 KL in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: EBITDA for Q2 FY26 at INR 658 million, up 43% sequentially from INR 460 million in Q1 FY26 and significantly higher than INR 403 million in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 FY '26 came in at INR 658 million, a strong 43% increase over INR 460 million in Q1 FY '26 and significantly higher than INR 403 million in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Headwinds faced by industry believed to be behind; expect upward trend in capacity utilization and profitability margins going forward
items.quote: We are hopeful that the headwinds that we were facing, the industry was facing is behind us. Things are looking up on the global geopolitical issues also. The currently completed quarter results are much better than the previous quarter results and year-on-year. So we expect going forward, we will have an upward trend in the capacity utilization and in the profitability margins.

items.statement: R&D continuously engaged with buyers' R&D; newer products in pipeline but too premature to announce; premium products like derma grade oils being targeted
items.quote: Yes, too premature to tell you right now, but it is a continuous process. Our R&D department is in constant engagement with the buyers' R&D department and newer products are definitely in the pipeline, and they will be announced as and when they happen.

items.statement: Bid for various transformer oil tenders; looking at additional geographies for PHPO and other products; automobile lubricants growing
items.quote: Yes. So we've bid for various tenders of transformer oils. We are looking out for additional geographies for our PHPO and other products. Even automobile lubricants are growing. So yes, things will work out, partnerships will break in and hopefully, the tariff issue will also get resolved.

items.statement: Inventories managed on just-in-time basis; no significant inventory losses despite base oil price reduction
items.quote: Contrary to most of our peers, we don't carry significant inventories. Our inventories are more or less on just-in-time basis, okay? So in spite of the reduction in prices of base oil, we have not had any significant inventory losses.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue at INR 10,599 million, up 17% sequentially from INR 9,030 million in Q1 FY26; H1 FY26 revenue at INR 19,629 million vs INR 19,299 million in H1 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue for Q2 FY '26 stood at INR10,599 million, up 17% sequentially from INR 9,030 million in Q1 FY '26 and higher than INR 9,351 million in Q2 FY '25. For H1 FY '26, revenue was INR 19,629 million compared to INR 19,299 million in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Targets 50 operational hotels by end of FY26

items.statement: Groundbreaking for Kolkata EM Bypass mixed-use project in January 2026, completion within three years

This mixed -use development gets underway in January '26 and is likely to be completed within three years of the start of the construction.

items.statement: Acquired 90% stake in Zillion Hotels & Resorts (Juhu, Mumbai) for ~INR 206 crore; finalizing acquisition of 31 rooms in Kochi
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have successfully completed the acquisition of 90% stake in Zillion Hotels & Resorts Private Limited, which owns the Juhu Mumbai property for approximately INR 206 crore. items.statement: Plan to add ~588 keys in H2 FY26 (400 management, 144 lease, 31 ownership), taking portfolio to ~3,024 keys
items.quote: We plan to open 102 keys in December, about 70 keys in the month of January, 100 keys are going to open in February FY '26. And then in March, we plan to open 243 keys. items.statement: ICRA rating A+ with outlook revised to positive from stable; net worth INR 1,305 cr
items.quote: We continue to maintain a superior financial position with net worth of about INR 1,305 crore and an ICRA rating of A+. In fact, ICRA has revised the outlook from stable to positive.

items.statement: Zillion acquisition funded via INR 105 cr line of credit on Zillion books (ICICI) + INR 80 cr creditor takeover + INR 50 cr equity
items.quote: We have taken a line of credit of which is one line of credit for Zillion of INR 105 crore on the books of Zillion from ICICI Bank. That is big money has gone. And towards acquisition, we have also invested another INR 130 crore; so INR 80 crore on this line of creditors and takeover of creditors and the balance INR 50 crore is towards the equity thing of the Zillion.

items.quote: About INR 15 crore has been earmarked this year for AI-led initiatives such as web check -ins, digital identity, AI -based chatbots and concierge services across our hotels. items.statement: Sustainability targets: 100% EV transport by FY26, 95% landfill diversion, waste neutrality by 2025, water neutrality by 2028, carbon neutrality by 2032; multiple IGBC certifications
items.quote: We are now targeting 100% electric vehicle case transport by FY '26 and 95% landfill diversion, taking us closer to our milestone of waste neutrality by 2025, water neutrality by 2028 and carbon neutrality by 2032.

items.quote: Significant progress has been made in all our new -build projects at Kolkata, Visakhapatnam, Pune and Navi Mumbai and groundbreaking in Kolkata will be as in January 2026.

items.quote: Moving on to EBITDA, the EBITDA for the quarter was INR 395 crores, which is a 30.5% growth over last year. And the EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% vis -à-vis 12.4% last year.

items.quote: Our quick commerce expanded to 695 stores across 460 cities in the country and the registered users on quick commerce have increased to 1.08 crore people.

items.quote: Our data suggests at this point in time, with a caveat that in some cities we are there for long and in some cities, we've just recently entered, about 20% of our e-commerce customers are coming to the Vishal franchise for the first time through the e-commerce route.

items.statement: Private brands offer 20-50% price advantage over third-party brands; GST impact relatively smaller; competitiveness unchanged
items.quote: The price benefit that our private brands offer over the third-party brands are very significant. They could be in the range of 20% to 45%, 50%. Obviously, different for different private brands. The GST impact is relatively much smaller, the GST benefit. So, I'm not certain whether the competitiveness of our private brands will get impacted at all.

items.quote: So, Prerna, as you heard from GK, as far as the existing cost is concerned, that will keep coming down depending upon the phasing. But as GK also said that we can't comment on the future expenses on ESOPs.

items.quote: Now we are very confident that we will surely touch EUR220 million and probably something more could be an added sugar to the entire revenue that we have.

items.quote: So, 11% could be 10.9%, 10.85%, something like that. But we are not looking at something very dramatic reduction. And we are hopeful because all other parameters are positive for us.

items.quote: From the 17%, 18% that we were anticipating, I don't have the real market numbers, but the feelers I have got is the four-wheel drive market has touched close to 24%, 25%, which we were expecting it next year.

items.quote: On the other hand, the domestic construction equipment market declined by around 9% in H1 FY26 versus last year with backhoe loader volumes down 12% mainly due to a prolonged monsoon and the slower adoption of higher cost BS-V models.

items.statement: Export order book stable for H2 FY26; no spike or big reduction expected
items.quote: The order books for exports are more or less stable. There is no spike in the second half, nor there is a big reduction. So I would say we would sustain more or less at the same level.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.4% vs 10.9% YoY; mix shift to lower-margin 4WD axles pressuring near-term profitability
items.quote: The growth in domestic four-wheel drive axles, though very encouraging was concentrated in a lower margin family of products within the agriculture segment. As a result, we are experiencing some near-term pressure on profitability.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by localization (78% now, targeting 80%), efficiency gains, and spare parts growth
items.quote: Also, on the localization front, we have made steady progress with localized raw materials now accounting to 78% of our total requirement and expected to touch 80% by the end of this year, thus strengthening our cost structure and supporting long-term profitability.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex INR211 million for furnaces, machining center, test bench; phased expansion over 30 months starting FY27
items.quote: During H1, we invested INR211 million into our world-class facility at Ranjangaon with two new sealed-quench furnaces and 800 mm pallet Mazak machining center. We also installed the TLB test bench in July and a robotic washing machine in September.

items.statement: Maintenance capex in FY26; significant expansion capex phased over 2-3 years for EUR350 million revenue target
items.quote: When we look at the future, we know, we have always said it, that if we want to reach our target of EUR350 million, more important capex and real expansion capex will be required. We are starting this.

items.quote: We are adopting a very step-by-step approach. You have seen we have spent over INR20 crores this year. We have introduced the Mazak machine, horizontal machining center. We have introduced two sealed-quench furnaces, test benches.

items.statement: Mix shift: domestic 4WD axle growth concentrated in lower-margin family; teleboom handler and backhoe loader exports growing
items.quote: The growth in domestic four-wheel drive axles, though very encouraging was concentrated in a lower margin family of products within the agriculture segment.

items.quote: A major highlight this half was our INR17.5 crores agreement with Montra Electric for industrialization and supply of e-transmissions for electric-powered agriculture tractors.

items.quote: Revenue from our engineering services business was INR50 million in Q2 FY26, up from INR17 million a year ago.

items.quote: Exports delivered an even stronger growth of 31% year-on-year, largely driven by teleboom handler axles.

items.statement: Tractor emission norms (Stage V) delayed beyond 2027; no impact on 4WD conversion trend

items.statement: Balance sheet strong with healthy liquidity; funding operations and strategic investments comfortably
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with healthy liquidity levels that enable us to fund operations comfortably, support strategic investments, and remain agile in capturing growth opportunities.

items.quote: When something gets advanced like this, then a lot of our cost-saving initiatives in terms of plant efficiencies, purchasing efficiencies, all these things get overridden because our target is more on achieving the revenue because we need to feed the market.

items.statement: Received Caterpillar SER award for third consecutive year; highest global recognition for operational excellence
items.quote: We are delighted to share that Carraro India received for the third consecutive year the Caterpillar SER award, the highest global recognition for operational excellence, quality and customer commitment.

items.statement: Targets 35-40% revenue and PAT growth in FY26, with FY26 revenue of INR700-750 crore and FY27 revenue of INR900 crore

So, we are expecting around INR400 crores to INR450 crores turnover in H2.

items.statement: Targets FY26 EBITDA margin of 11-13% and FY27 EBITDA margin of 13-14%, potentially 15-20% with better water-infra orders
items.quote: So, this time we are expecting EBITDA margins to be somewhere between 11% to 13% on a consolidated basis. In blended, there will be a mix of TCC and EPC.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR2,500 crore submitted, expecting INR500 crore conversion at 15-20% strike rate; targeting INR2,000 crore order book by Mar 2026

items.statement: Workforce of over 1,100 employees; asset base of 222+ construction machines and vehicles

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR 700-800 crores with EBITDA margin around 20%

items.quote: I think, I don't have the exact numbers, but I think the Mehru is in slightly excess of INR 375 crores. Quality Power is, if I'm not wrong, around INR 285 crores or INR 290 crores. And the rest would be Endoks.

items.quote: Mehru has delivered a significant improvement in operational margins this quarter to about 12%, driven by higher capacity utilization, product mix optimization and operational discipline.

items.statement: Strong sustained demand globally driven by energy transition, renewables, grid modernization
items.quote: The high-voltage electrical equipment industry continues to experience strong sustained demand across global markets, driven by the energy transition, renewable energy integration, and grid modernization.

items.quote: The HVDC magnet wire capacity, we should be able to have the first stage of capacity, feeling about demand by Q3 of next year.

items.statement: Near zero net debt; excess cash >INR 200 crores

items.statement: Added 140-150 people last quarter to ramp up for new facilities
items.quote: We have also added more than 140 or 150 people in the last quarter, to be able to what we say, ramp-up and train them for when we shift to the new facilities.

items.statement: Biggest risk: Chinese competitors focused on volume over profit, not domestic/European/US rivals

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 413 crores (+126% YoY); EBITDA INR 97.7 crores (+67% YoY); gross margin 40%

items.statement: BIS license requirement for HVDC magnet wires slowing imports; Indian capacity booked for next year
items.quote: HVDC magnet wires now require BIS license, which has slowed import approval since the Indian capacity is already booked out for the next year.

items.statement: Less than half a dozen global competitors outside China for GIS instrument transformers; market INR 2,000-3,000 crores
items.quote: Globally the markets are between INR 2,000 crores to INR 3,000 crores for this product, again with less than half a dozen competitors outside of China.

items.quote: Presently means that 30%-35% may be challenging because of this impact of quarter 2. But I definitely foresee that we will be one of the effective and promising performers as far as industry peers are concerned.

items.statement: Biologicals gross margin ~70%; plant nutrients gross margin ~52%.

items.statement: Backward-integrated four plants manufacturing base supports supply reliability and margins with higher utilization year-to-date.

items.statement: Domestic B2C strong: Haryana +60%, Uttar Pradesh +25%, Maharashtra +26%, Andhra Pradesh +22% YoY in H1; Bihar, Karnataka, Rajasthan significant growth on lower base.

items.statement: INR 14 crore raised in IPO for capex; deployment minimal in Q2, full deployment from Q3.
items.quote: Of the INR 14 crores raised for capex in the IPO, utilization in Q2 was intentionally minimal as our focus was on seasonal sales.

items.statement: Return on capital employed for H1 FY26 stands at 14.1%.
items.quote: The return on capital employed for H1FY26 stands at 14.1%.

items.statement: Q3 demand expected to pick up from mid-December to February; Q4 historically stronger and expected to be even better this year.

items.statement: FY26 guidance: 25-30% revenue growth, EBITDA margin 10-11%, PAT margin 6-7%

items.quote: Globally, we are witnessing a shortage in chipsets, sensors and storage, largely driven due to the DDR and Flash prices going up, as well as the supply constraints.

items.statement: Pro Series launch next quarter targeting global brands; multi-brand strategy to maximize market share and serve diverse customer needs
items.quote: In CP PLUS brand, we are also focusing on multiple series to capture the value on SMB market, as well as launching soon the Pro Series next quarter to target global brands, which will go live in the coming quarter.

items.quote: So in terms of Q3 and Q4, we should be able to operate the capacity that somewhere around 80%-85% above our installed capacity and we should see a similar trend in terms of or rather a little improved trend in terms of the bottom line.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect production momentum to strengthen as most premium automakers are nearing completion of their platform transitions and are all set to roll out a series of new models. This optimism is also reflected in the upwardly revisioned global production forecast for the full year, now converging around the 90 million plus mark.

items.statement: Consumer electronics and aerospace booked business at $3 billion, up from $2.7 billion in March 2025
items.quote: Booked business between consumer electronics and aerospace is already now at a whopping 3 billion up from 2.7 billion in March 2025 and is further expected to see a sharp ramp-up by the time we next report this figure to you.

items.statement: Plan to add more than 5,000 engineers in next five years, new building coming in latter half of year
items.quote: We are wanting to add more than 5,000 engineers in the next five years, building and bolstering our competency with global business services that we have built in -house and our AI platform. A new building will be coming up in the latter half of the year to support this growth.

items.statement: Consumer electronics business grew 36% QoQ in Q2 based on September run rate, two plants operational, largest coming in H2 FY27
items.quote: Based on the September run rate revenue, Q2 demonstrated a 36% growth over the first quarter. This will further pick up pace in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Consumer electronics business expected to be profitable in first full year of operations
items.quote: We also expect this business to be positive in profit in the first full year of operations.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue grew 37% YoY in H1 FY26, became Tier 1 to Airbus, in advanced discussions for complex high-value packages
items.quote: Aerospace business delivered a 37% revenue growth in the first half of FY'26 on a year-on-year basis. We became Tier 1 to Airbus earlier this year and that is already giving us desired results. We are in advanced discussions for complex and high -value large packages.

items.statement: Emerging business profitability improved to 9.5%, up 110 bps QoQ, driven by Atsumitec assimilation and consumer electronics ramp-up
items.quote: As the ramp-up of the consumer electronic business has happened together with some improvement in the Atsumi tec business, you are seeing the trajectory move up.

items.statement: Tariff-related costs of ~$10 million on P&L this quarter, engaging with OEMs for pass-through with lead-lag effect
items.quote: We continue to engage in constructive discussions with our OEMs, and as of this quarter, there is about $10 million of tarif f-related costs on our P&L, which will flow, albeit with a lead-lag effect.

items.statement: Net effective debt to EBITDA stable at 1.1x at end of Q2, Rs 2,600 crores CAPEX spent in H1
items.quote: Despite the large growth capital, inflated working capital and transitory impacts on profitability in the first quarter of the fiscal year, our leverage at the end of the second quarter remains s table at 1.1x net effective debt to EBITDA.

items.statement: Yutaka acquisition revenue $1.2 billion, open offer pending, likely closure around Q1 FY27, not yet in current numbers
items.quote: I mean, if it helps, Jyoti, I think the revenue is 1.2 billion. The open offer remains pending. It is a likely closure somewhere around Q1 of FY '27. So Yutaka is still not in the numbers that you are seeing right now.

items.statement: EV share in revenue currently 11%, order book EV share dipped from 24% to 22% due to new non-EV platform launches and recalibrated EV volume trajectory
items.quote: Our EV revenues right now is 11%. And in the order book, you see a dip from 24 % to 22 %, which is largely reflective of what Vaaman was saying in terms of new launches that are happening along with non -EV powertrains as well.

items.statement: Transformative measures in Western/Central Europe 75-80% complete, further acceleration expected in H2 especially modules and polymer
items.quote: The majority of the transformative actions are in place with some bids to follow in the second half of the year. We do anticipate further acceleration of improvements in performance during the second half of this year, especially in the modules in polymer business division.

items.statement: Complete management team change in Europe, new head Christophe now fully in control of modules and polymer division
items.quote: We also had a complete management team change over there. And that management team is now fully in grip of the complete operation. We will have Christophe in the subsequent calls coming up, because now he has completely taken control of the modules and polymer division as the new Head over there.

items.statement: Chip shortage situation mixed, some improvement reported but uncertainty remains, customers proactively working on solutions

items.statement: ROCE at 14.2% as of September 2025, impacted by Q1 transition, greenfield ramp-ups, and inflated working capital, expected to creep up as performance normalizes
items.quote: On ROCE, we are at 14.2% as at the end of September 2025, impacted by the transitionary impact on profitability in the first quarter, early stage ramp ups of all the new green fields as well as the inflated working capital. This should creep up again as performan ce normalizes in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Bulk division EBITDA turned positive to INR1.2 crores in H1 FY26 from loss of INR1.5 crores in H1 FY25 due to lower inventory model, tighter inventory management, and disciplined procurement.

items.statement: Consumer demand remains encouraging; expanded distribution across general trade, modern trade, and quick commerce driving volume growth despite GST disruption in late Q2.

items.statement: Environment clearance fast-track for ethanol plants (B2 category) sunset in March 2024; new plants now require full EC process with public hearings, creating bottleneck for further capacity additions.

So, new plants will have to undergo the entire process of getting environmental clearance, public hearing, etc. So, I think that will pose a significant bottleneck to further capacity enhancements.

items.statement: GST rationalization caused short-term pricing and inventory challenges in Q2 but creates stable ecosystem for branded players medium-term.
items.quote: Meanwhile, regulatory changes such as GST rationalization have posed short-term challenges in pricing and inventory, but in the medium term, they create a more stable and transparent ecosystem for branded players.

items.quote: We don't see any reason why this division should not get to about INR500 crores number. And contributing from oil as well as foods. So, that is our long-term vision.
