items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 69 crore and INR 142 crore for the half year, translating to margins of about 15% and 16%, respectively.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure of ~200 bps sequentially attributed to inventory fluctuations and slight raw material price increase, not a major factor.
items.quote: There is no major reason that we can point to. It is more like just inventory up down. And also, there is a slight increase in raw material prices, but that is not a major contributing factor.

items.statement: INR 100+ crore capex budgeted for FY26, over half already spent; includes land, building for future expansion, new cylinder factory commissioning this quarter, balancing and specialty equipment.
items.quote: Yes. So we have about INR 100-plus crore of capex budgeted this year. And a lot of it is going into land, building for enabling future capex.

items.statement: Carton business at ~70% overall utilization with room for top-line growth; flexible packaging has free capacity, no immediate capex planned except balancing equipment and building expansion.
items.quote: In the carton business, we are more at like – I had say, overall, we are at about 70%-odd utilization. So, there is a good room for further expansion in the top line without much capex.

items.statement: Chennai Greenfield plant ramping up well at 40-50% utilization; large account approvals progressing; expects good utilization over next few quarters.
items.quote: Chennai is going quite well. The overall working, quality and everything in the plant is very stable. We are slowly entering into more and more customers and some of the large accounts where there is audit and approval and trials and everything which is required, which takes some time. Those are also progressing quite well.

items.statement: Bank borrowing rate 8-9%; interest expense as percentage higher due to lower top-line growth but debt ratios under control; MTM loss on euro loan ~INR 4 crore in Q2 after INR 10.6 crore in Q1.
items.quote: Generally, our bank borrowing rate is bet ween 8% and 9%. So that continues. And obviously, if the top line growth does not translate then the interest portion as a percent will be a little higher side

items.statement: Aspiration for mid-double-digit top-line growth with better bottom-line improvement; both carton and flexible packaging to grow at similar rates, flexibles faster from lower base.
items.quote: Our aspiration is mid-double-digit sort of growth rate in top-line with better improvement in bottom-line and our carton and flexible should both grow at a similar kind of rate.

items.statement: US export development pipeline stalled due to tariffs but existing business continues; if trade deal announced, could ramp up increased business by end of financial year within a couple of months.
items.quote: So although it is small now, if the trade deal is announced and the tariff, even if it drop s to half of what it is now, it could be even lower. But even if it is half, it could bring about significant scope for business. So it should not take a very long time and say, if it is announced in November sometime, we should be up and running with increased business by the end of the financial year

items.statement: Innofilms (now integrated) developing specialized innovative films with good R&D traction; recyclable film adoption slow due to lack of government mandate but qualified for when demand picks up.
items.quote: On the Innofilms, we are quite encouraged by the developments that our team is doing in the R&D, and there is some good traction on some specialized products, which we are developing with that capacity.

items.statement: Customer engagement strong; approvals from several large accounts progressing; no comment on specific clients like iPhone-related business.
items.quote: Overall, customer engagement has been strong and approvals from several large accounts are current ly progressing, which will further aid the scale up as they come through

items.statement: Creative Offset subsidiary revenue growing with loss narrowing and cash flow improving but still below expectations; working on new customers and product lines to reach profitability.
items.quote: On the Creative side, also there is a growth in the revenue and therefore, a drop in the loss and improvement in the cash flow and all that. But still, it is way below our expectation, to be frank.

items.statement: Global tariff volatility, war and disruption creating gloomy export markets; China dumping present but not major concern in their industry.
items.quote: Obviously, all the mess up going on globally because of the tariffs and the volatility and there is so much war and disruption everywhere. So overall global markets are a bit gloomy.

items.statement: GST slab revision caused short-term trade channel recalibration and inventory correction; transition largely normalized, rationalized structure expected to support demand improvement.
items.quote: The revision in GST slabs during the quarter resulted in short-term recalibration across parts of the trade channel, which contributed to softer demand in September. This transition has largely normalized, and we expect the rationalized structure to support improvement in underlying demand in the coming period.

items.statement: Inventory fluctuations contributed to gross margin pressure; no specific debtor or inventory days disclosed.
items.quote: There is no major reason that we can point to. It is more like just inventory up down.

items.statement: Investor suggested market placement of 10 lakh shares at INR 3,000 to raise INR 300 crore for debt reduction; management will take suggestion into advisement.
items.quote: Thank you very much for your suggestion on the raising capital, we will take that into advisement.

items.statement: Targets FY26 presales of about INR2,000 crores, dependent on Amaya and Aaroham launches
items.quote: FY '26 presales, the outlook is about INR2,000 crores is what we are targeting. We want to cross that threshold this year. And yes, that's the outlook for it. A lot of it depends on how the 2 project launches go.

items.statement: Expects net profit margins in low double digits (around 10-11%) for FY26
items.quote: So I said the full year profit should be in the low single digits, let's say, 10-odd percent, maybe 11% kind of net profit margins is what I think we will look at for this financial year.

items.statement: Expects to cross 20% ROE threshold by FY28 as per current plan
items.quote: FY '28, I think we should definitely cross the 20% ROE threshold if you go as per the plan that we have right now for derivatives.

items.statement: Net profit margins expected to reach low double digits in FY26, improve further in FY27, and reach mid- to high-teens by FY28
items.quote: I would not like to give exactly, but definitely in the teens. Mid, low, high teens, I don't want to get into but definitely, teens would be there, let's say, mid- to high teens is where they would land at in FY '28, if we go as per plans

items.statement: Revenue visibility of INR11,000 crores up to FY30 includes ongoing projects (INR6,300 crores), Aaroham (INR1,500-1,800 crores), Amaya (INR300 crores), Oma (INR700 crores), and future phases (INR2,000-2,500 crores)
items.quote: So we have INR7,000, plus INR2,000 crores, plus INR2,500 crores, this about comes in around INR11,000 crores. Is that a good number to get there, Rohit, or anything else you would like specifically?

items.statement: Acquired 22.7 acres on perpetual lease at MWC Chennai for senior living project with sales value potential of approximately INR1,200 crores
items.quote: We acquired 22.7 acres on perpetual lease at MWC Chennai to develop a senior living project. This project has a sales value potential of approximately INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Targets Chennai senior living project launch by end of FY27; project spans 15 lakh sq ft over 6-7 years
items.quote: We are targeting for end of next financial year launch but the approval process in Chennai is a little longer than elsewhere for us in that market. That said, after launch, I would say it's a 6- to 7-year project, 15 lakh square foot.

items.statement: Disproportionate capital allocation toward senior living; land prices more viable due to pricing premium and ability to choose less competitive micro-markets
items.quote: So one part where we have definite clarity is that a large substantial chunk will get delivered towards senior living. And in senior living, we are finding viable land parcels.

items.statement: Increasing prices in most markets but pace of increase slower than before; land prices remain high in Gurugram and Jaipur
items.quote: So we are increasing prices in most places. We don't have pricing pressures anywhere. But the pace of price increase is slower than what it was before.

items.statement: Referral bookings contribute 60-70% of sales in non-Gurugram/Pune markets; channel partners dominate in Gurugram and Pune
items.quote: If you exclude those 2, between 60% and 70% of our bookings in different projects come through referrals.

items.statement: Gurugram market no longer secular; differentiation by product quality and brand emerging; Ashiana positioned in middle tier
items.quote: I think what is happening in the Gurugram market is that it is now not a secular sales market for every developer. I think it is getting split a little bit between the development quality, the product quality, the positioning, the sales engine, the marketing engine, the brand positioning in the market.

items.statement: Aaroham launch delayed due to building bylaw interpretation differences; RERA application filed, approval expected by end of month
items.quote: We got stuck in some approval issues in our interpretation of the building bylaws and other building code and fire codes. Our interpretation and the town planning interpretations were different. So we had to recalibrate our drawings a little bit.

items.statement: Pre-tax operating cash flow of INR122.62 crores in Q2 FY26 driven by better collections
items.quote: The company posted pre-tax operating cash flow of INR122.62 crores during the quarter. Cash flow continues to be healthy, driven by better collections.

items.statement: Ashiana Aaroham funded by IFC through INR100 crores listed NCDs
items.quote: Ashiana Aaroham got funded by International Finance Corporation through allotment of INR100 crores of listed Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs).

items.statement: Land deals in Jaipur, Panvel, Bangalore pending condition precedents; government approval-linked CPs may resolve or be dropped in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Neither the condition precedents have not been satisfied in either of the 3. Jaipur, Panvel and Bangalore, we are still waiting for the landlords to complete certain conditions that they are supposed to do for the transaction to fully go through.

items.statement: 226 customers filed consumer forum case against Ashiana Town seeking INR50 crores; company contesting claims, maintains overall customer satisfaction is high

items.statement: Equivalent area constructed in Q2 FY26 at 7.25 lakh sq ft, up 18% QoQ
items.quote: Equivalent area constructed for Q2 FY '26 at 7.25 lakh square feet, higher by around 18% versus 6.15 lakh square feet in the first quarter.

items.statement: Value of area booked in Q2 FY26 at INR303.43 crores vs INR430.97 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We achieved value of area booked of INR303.43 crores for the quarter, vis-à-vis INR430.97 crores in the first quarter.

items.statement: Amarah Phase 4 & 5 sold 76,000 sq ft in Q1 and 47,000 sq ft in Q2; 3 lakh sq ft remaining over 10+ quarters
items.quote: Amarah, we sold like in Q1, 76,000 square foot, Q2, 47,000 square foot. Any number above, let's say, 30,000 square foot a quarter, I think we are good in Amarah.

items.statement: Aaroham Phase 1 pricing in INR3-5 crore ticket range; Amaya pricing around INR7,500-8,000/sq ft after discounts
items.quote: So Ashiana Aaroham is in the INR3 crores to INR5 crores range, I think, bulk, exact pricing is not yet concluded.

items.quote: We thought we could do an analyst meet at one of our senior living projects. We plan to do one at Talegaon, Ashiana Amodh within the next, let's say, 30 to 60 days.

items.quote: IndyAstra is a very unique MOU. There is a restriction in sharing of details around this because there is a MOU signed between Ind yAstra and defense, where we a re working something very -very important for the country's security

items.quote: HEAL – on observability, which is we have already done in all banks like most of these public sector private box are are are customers under these labels for almost close to more than a decade on technology predictability.

items.statement: Broad-based demand recovery seen across markets, especially India and Asia, after ~10 flat quarters
items.quote: We have seen an improvement in demand occurring across markets and more so specifically in India and Asia, as you correctly pointed out. We see that there is a growth in demand currently.

items.statement: First quarter of healthy growth after ~10 flat quarters; cautiously optimistic for sustained recovery
items.quote: This is the first quarter where we've seen such healthy growth after close to about 10 quarters of flat movement. So we are a little cautiously optimistic right now.

items.statement: Expect ~INR30 cr revenue from EU regulated markets in FY26
items.quote: We have already started selling in the EU. And in fact, we have given a guidance that we are hoping for up to INR30 crores revenue to come from the EU in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 15-18% as scale improves
items.quote: We hope that we should be back to our EBITDA -- targeted EBITDA rate of between 15% and 18%.

items.statement: Ongoing capital projects on track for completion by Q4 FY26, commissioning Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our ongoing capital projects remain on track for completion by Q4 FY '26 with commissioning scheduled for Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: New plant opex estimated INR1.2-1.5 cr per month after commissioning
items.value: INR1.2 crores per month to INR1.5 crores
items.quote: With regard to the new plant, which we will commission next year, we expect opex to be in the range of about INR1.2 crores per month to INR1.5 crores.

items.statement: Additional depreciation from expansion estimated INR6-8 cr full year in FY27
items.quote: I would say between INR6 crores and INR8 crores would be the full year depreciation -- additional depreciation next year, which will come from the expansion.

items.statement: New plant EBITDA breakeven expected in FY28, not FY27
items.quote: EBITDA breakeven, we expect from the new plant in FY '28, not in FY '27 because -- FY '27 is going to be basically getting all registrations done for us.

items.statement: 15-20% of production currently outsourced; outsourcing to continue for lower-margin ROW markets
items.quote: Currently, roughly between 15% to 20% of our production is outsourced. The rest is all in-sourced by us.

items.statement: First US FDA API registration filed Sep 2025; audit expected H2 CY26; commercial production H2 FY27 if audit successful
items.quote: We successfully submitted our first API registration to the U.S. FDA in September 2025. We anticipate regulatory audits to begin in the second quarter of the next financial year with commercial production expected to commence in the latter half of FY '27, assuming successful audit outcomes.

items.statement: 3 CEPs granted and 5 ASMFs approved in Europe; 3 more CEPs and 3 ASMFs under process
items.quote: Currently, we have about 3 CEPs already granted in Europe and 5 ASMFs. We have applied for a grant of further 3 CEPs in Europe, which are currently under process and 3 more ASMFs are being filed separately.

items.statement: 15 products in validation pipeline for US/EU; 3 validations done, 4th ongoing, target 15 by Dec 2026
items.quote: We have got a total of 15 products, which are in the pipeline for which validation batches are being done. Out of that validation for 3 products is already completed. The fourth one is going on right now. By December next year, we hope to complete 15 validations.

items.statement: Fluralaner commercial launch May 2025 post-patent expiry; strong growth in domestic and export markets
items.quote: With regard to fluralaner, the launch -- commercial launch has taken place in May this year after the expiry of the patent in March 2025. Customers have already launched the product. And it's definitely one of our star products with a good grow

items.quote: Our gross margins are better though with lower realizations currently. We have had an increase in the cost with the new plant going on stream, but it's a very small plant with just one small pilot clean room, which we have commissioned.

items.statement: Regulated market (US/EU) gross margin expected 55-60% vs current ~50-55%
items.quote: We expect that to be in the range of around 55% to 60%.

items.statement: Working capital currently ~INR45 cr, expected to grow to ~INR60 cr
items.quote: Currently, our working capital is around INR45 crores. We expect it to grow to about INR60 crores.

items.statement: Long-term debt sanctioned INR95 cr; used ~INR45-46 cr so far; peak debt expected INR75-95 cr
items.quote: So we have got a sanction for INR95 crores debt. We hope to not utilize this debt completely. We hope to curb it. Worst-case scenario is a max at INR95 crores, best scenario probably at around INR75 crores.

items.statement: 15-20 Indian and ~double Chinese veterinary API manufacturers; competitor count grown in last 2-3 years
items.quote: With regard to competitive dynamics, there are good 20 players, roughly about, I would say, between 15 and 20 manufacturers here in India, who are manufacturing veterinary products and probably double the number in China.

items.statement: Working with 5 of top 10 animal health companies in non-US markets; receptive to US supply
items.quote: Out of the top 10 animal health companies, we are currently working with 5 of them, not in the U.S. market, but in other markets. And they were receptive to the idea of having us in as a supplier for the U.S. market.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from supply-demand imbalance; sustained demand growth needed for price recovery
items.quote: The pricing pressure was created mainly by the supply-demand imbalance. Demand has been subdued for a significantly long time now. It first started with the inventory unwinding post-COVID. And then generally, demand has been muted in many markets. And supply has been strong with capacity being created.

items.statement: Export sales ~70% of revenue; export growth ~3-4% from FX, rest volume
items.quote: On the export front, which is about 70% of the sales, we have a top line growth of probably about 3%, 3.5% on account of exchange fluctuation, probably 4%. The rest is all volume growth.

items.statement: Outsourcing cost up ~30% in H1 due to higher volumes; job work charges separate from material cost
items.quote: Current half year, we have seen our cost of outsourcing go up by close to something like 30% because a large quantum has been outsourced.

items.quote: Typical history has shown that a best case scenario takes a U.S. filing to actual audit in about 12 to 15 months, worst-case scenario can be even longer.

items.statement: EU registration cost ~EUR18,000 per product; US filing costs not yet determined

items.quote: So, we expect our run rate to be around Rs 750 to 800 crores of revenue, and a PAT should be around Rs 135 to 150.

items.quote: So it's not the focus on the listing revenue. It's more on the commission -based revenue is the focus. That's the shift we are m aking on wedding services.

items.statement: AI chatbot launched in one domain; will expand to all domains after fine-tuning
items.quote: We launched AI Chatbot in customer service in one of our domains, and we will launch it for all the domains once we fine-tune our Chatbot.

items.statement: AI-based astrology product launching end of month with free first question
items.quote: We are launching an AI-based astrology product because we will be end of the month , we'll be launching the product. We will be answering one question powered by AI using Vedic Astrology free.

items.statement: Expect double-digit EBITDA margin by March 2026 and ~10.5% in FY27
items.quote: Yes, our efforts are to a double-digit margin. At least we close a double-digit margin by March '26. So, as sir has said in the beginning of the call, quarter 3 and 4 would have a, I mean, backup of a strong demand.

items.statement: Target 11% EBITDA margin over next 2 years with 50 bps annual improvement
items.quote: So, basically, as we promised and we discussed with the market in earlier calls, we want to go up to a margin of 11% in the next 2 years of time with the improvement of around 50 bps, I mean 10-50 bps every year.

items.statement: Target 18% pre-tax ROCE in first phase, then 18% post-tax
items.quote: And ROCE, we intend to achieve 18% pre-tax in the first phase and then later on followed by 18% post-tax in the coming period of time.

items.statement: Expect overseas business to breakeven by Q4 FY26 and return to 12.5-13% margins
items.quote: We are expecting our quarter 3 to be better, followed by quarter 4 to be neutral in terms of margins and losses. We expect to be in greener. This is our prime desire.

items.statement: Order books extremely strong for Q3 and Q4 due to elongated festive season
items.quote: The lucky thing is that even in the case of December, November and December, because of the festive season, the elongated festive season, our order books are extremely strong. So, we do expect a strong third quarter. And of course, as always, a very, very strong quarter 4.

items.statement: India business normalized EBITDA margin 10.44% in Q2 FY26 vs 10.16% in Q2 FY25 after adjusting for INR11.21 cr impact from new projects
items.quote: If I look at the impact that I gave you of 11.21%, our EBITDA is 10.44% versus 10.16%. In fact, higher than the quarter 2 of 2025.

items.statement: Sundaram-Clayton business at 4.48% EBITDA margin for H1 FY26, near 5% in Q2; expected to reach 9-10% from April 2026 after relocation
items.quote: But as we shared our plans earlier, like along with the machining, we expect something 11%, 12%. And in terms of S-cost, the margins are expected to be around 9.5% to 10%, 10.15%, that's all.

items.statement: Overseas business margins improving QoQ; were 12.5-13% historically and expected to return shortly
items.quote: In fact, if you look at our overseas business in the past, our margins there are higher than those of the Indian business. They were at about 12.5%-13% of margins. We expect those margins to come back very, very shortly.

items.statement: EV business generated INR6.94 cr revenue in H1 FY26; expect INR15 cr for full FY26
items.quote: And we generated a revenue of INR6.94 crores in the first half of the current financial year. And we expect to do a business of around INR15 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: Sundaram-Clayton revenue INR198 cr in H1 FY26 (INR102 cr in Q2); annual run-rate INR400 cr
items.quote: Sundaram-Clayton, the effective sale is now INR198 crores for the half year. Rajit Aggarwal: Okay. Yashpal Jain: So, yes, it was around INR95 crores last quarter. 102-103, roughly, I mean 92.5 and 102.5

items.statement: INR300 cr capex planned for FY26 including Sundaram; major capex cycle largely done; future capex INR150-200 cr/year for maintenance, safety, incremental growth
items.quote: In the beginning of the year, we have said that around INR300 crores of capex would be there, including the Sundaram one also. So, and the debt is around 858 in the month of September.

items.statement: No major capex required in next 12 months; capacity from recent expansions sufficient for growth
items.quote: So, in short, there doesn't seem to be any major requirement of capex in the next 12 months at least. We are well within our framework to grow at the rate at what you've been seeing us grow without further capex required on a large basis.

items.statement: Debt ~INR858 cr in September 2025; working capital needs increased due to rolled-back payment terms; term loan repayment INR45 cr in H1
items.quote: And the debt is around 858 in the month of September. But yes, our working capital requirement has increased. There is a reason that that has gone up. Earlier, we were having some favorable payment terms from some of the customers, which has been now rolled back to the earlier levels.

items.statement: Debt expected around INR850-900 cr; working capital portion rising with business growth
items.quote: I think it should be around 850 to 900 something, keeping in view the working capital requirements as our business is going up, we need to maintain inventories also and the receivables also.

items.statement: Pune die casting and cabin fabrication projects to reach full production by April 2026; customer consent received for Pune die casting
items.quote: In the Pune die casting, we have received now the customer consent also. And from next year, April, the volumes will gradually start. So, that's the reason this new business, which is dragging us down, would again be in the same profit trajectory.

items.statement: Sundaram-Clayton relocation to new premises by March 2026; INR40-50 cr additional capex for shift
items.quote: Majority of the same will be coming up in by the month of March while we shift to our premises. And then there's another die casting coming up in Pune and the cabins and fabrication again in Pune.

items.statement: ADC share ~32% in Q2 FY26; Vision Systems revenues doubled; Sheet metal grew from <INR200 cr to targeting INR1,000 cr
items.quote: So roughly in this quarter, the ADC business has been about 32%, right? So, yes, which includes a revenue of INR198 crores from Sundaram-Clayton business despite that India business standalone quarter 2 has given INR177 crores of revenue to us.

items.statement: HMSI share 4.2% in Q2 FY26 (up from 3.7%); new projects in pipeline across sheet metal, castings, locks, mirrors, helmets
items.quote: For the current quarter, I mean quarter 2, the HMSI share is 4.2%. And for half year also, it is 4.2%. Whereas in the corresponding year, it was 3.7%. So, 0.5% we have gained.

items.statement: 4-5 new European customers in pipeline; onboarding may start Q4 FY26 / Q1 CY27
items.quote: There are 4-5 new customers coming in the pipeline. So, as sir has also answered previously in this session, we are going to see a new customer base also starting might be quarter 4 of our financial year and quarter 1 of their financial year, which is effective Jan '27 -- '26.

items.statement: Assembly (spokes) business declining as premium segment shifts to alloy wheels; combined with sheet metal to utilize capacity
items.quote: Otherwise, I mean with the passage of time, the spokes will be largely replaced by the alloy wheels in the coming period of time. As of now, the mopeds and some segment of the bikes are being run on the spokes wheel. So that's the reason it is going down.

items.statement: Cabins & fabrication business recovering after emission norm transition; green shoots of new orders in Q3/Q4 FY26
items.quote: Yes, to a large extent, yes. We have started green shoots of new orders coming in. The cabin and fabrication business, like you said, was affected a lot. With the change in the emission norms, there was a lot of inventory lying with the customers.

items.statement: Europe volatile; Romania operations improving; power costs down from peak but above pre-war; new projects routed through Romania
items.quote: Gradually, it started to come down. It is still not at the level as what was there before the war, but it has come down dramatically because of operations in Romania are lower than those in Spain by a significant margin.

items.statement: Euro strength and rupee depreciation caused translation losses on overseas business
items.quote: The European business, you also have to consider the fact that with the depreciation of the rupee and the euro becoming stronger, we have had translation losses. And when the overall business is in a loss, in the Indian context and in translation to the Indian rupee, that has a double whammy impact.

items.statement: Collection period 45 days; supplier terms 30-45 days; working capital debt rising with business growth
items.quote: The collection period is 45 days, while suppliers in some of the cases is 30 days also or 45 days also. This is how we need to maintain capex.

items.statement: QIP of INR500 cr approved as backup for inorganic opportunities; no acquisition finalized yet
items.quote: In fact, the point that you mentioned, the QIP was to be kept as Voucher (Backup) in case any such opportunities were to arise. We still haven't finalized on any so far.

items.statement: India auto industry grew 6.1% in Q2 FY26; 2-wheeler +7.4%, PV -1.5%; Sandhar India revenue +33%, consolidated +29%
items.quote: Let me begin by first of all, saying that the auto industry, the domestic auto industry grew by about 6.1% in quarter 2 of 2026, out of which the 2-wheeler segment has grown by 7.4%. The passenger vehicle segment growth -- actually witnessed a degrowth of 1.5%.

items.statement: Overseas turnaround dependent on Europe-US trade resolution; targeting breakeven in Q4 FY26 despite flat volumes
items.quote: Even though the revenues might be in the same range, because till the time we see a final arrangement between the European Union and US markets and other markets. But at least plan is that we should not incur the losses and we turn around to a breakeven in the first phase.

items.statement: Revenue target INR 5,400 crore for FY26 and INR 7,600 crore for FY27 with PAT margin 4.25%
items.quote: We have delivered a strong performance for H1 FY26 and we are on track to achieve our target revenue of INR 5,400 crore by FY26 driven by new client acquisition operation efficiency and enhanced management capabilities.

items.statement: Export revenue target 10-12% of sales from Q3 FY26, 15-20% by March 2027
items.quote: And again, going ahead to 15%-20% by 2027 March.

items.statement: Volume target 650-700 kg/month exit rate for FY26, 900 kg/month for FY27
items.quote: So, we have taken the average rate of 90,000-95,000. If rates goes up and stand to 1,20,000-1,25,000, then the numbers will go up. But let's see how the gold rates go, it comes down or whatever, how it plays. So, where does the stability come? But we every time take the conservative number and we will stick on to 7,600 crores.

items.statement: Advanced gold business at 7% of revenue, studded jewellery doubled to 1.5% driving gross margin expansion
items.quote: So, you can see we have improved our gross margin by 20 basis points. So, our advance gold business has improved from 5% to 7%. And our studded natural diamond jewellery has gone up from 0.7% to 1.5%. It has doubled the sale in this quarter. That's why our gross margin has gone up.

items.statement: Gold metal loan at 4% cost vs 9.5% CC limits; 8-10% of borrowing shifted to GML in Q2, targeting 75-80% conversion
items.quote: The gold-metal loan is available for 3%, 3.5% of interest cost. And other expenses come up to 4% versus 9.5% for the CC limits. So, we will save 5.5% of interest going ahead on the borrowing cost.

items.statement: Exports doubled to INR 150 crore in Q2 FY26; Dubai office operational from November 2025
items.quote: I am pleased to share that our exports have doubled this quarter, reaching around INR 150 crore, reflecting the early success of this initiative and reinforcing our confidence in continued global growth.

items.statement: Malaysian client volume expected to rise from 30-35 kg/2 months to 40 kg/month in Q3, 50-70 kg/month by March 2026
items.quote: now from November, you can see the average of the Malaysian customer, which was 30 kg or 35 kg in two months, it will go up to 40 kg per month in this quarter, because they were also Sky Gold & waiting that we can avail the goods from Dubai office

items.statement: Current capacity 1.2 tons/month across three subsidiaries; new facility construction starts April 2026, completion end 2028
items.quote: So, we are planning to start the construction of the facility from April 2026. And it will take three years to make the facility. And in 2028, we are planning to open, end of the 2028, when our 1.2 ton of facility will be exhausted.

items.statement: New facility capex INR 150 crore construction + INR 100 crore furniture/fixtures over 3 years; funded from internal accruals (INR 50 crore/year) and term loan for fixtures
items.quote: So, we will need INR 150 crores for construction basis and INR 100 crores for furniture fixture and machinery which will be needed in 2028. So, in three years, we will put 50-50 crores from internal accruals, as we are expecting extra 50 crores in each year.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient despite high gold prices; consumers shifting to lightweight, lower-carat (18Kt 7%, studded 1.5%) and daily-wear jewellery
items.quote: Despite the elevated good prices, Indian consumer has been resilient and continues to stand strong in the festive season. The demand for gold is not dampened. Instead, people are adjusting budgets by exploring lightweight designs, lower-carat gold like 9Kt, 14Kt or diamond stud pieces.

items.statement: Wedding season orders for Jan-Feb 2026 very strong; Q3 FY26 expected to be best quarter for revenue and volume
items.quote: So, this quarter, we are having good orders of wedding season is going on for January, February and all. This quarter, wedding orders are very nice placed by the customers. So, this quarter also is very good by volume also and revenue also.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved by 7 days in Sep'25 vs Mar'25; targeting cash flow positive after March 2027 when PAT exceeds INR 300 crore
items.quote: Surely, we will be cash flow positive after '27 March. We will be short in '27 Mar by INR 70 crores-INR 80 crores-INR 100 crores that will, we have already raised the debts for that. So, we will be shortly cash flow positive after '27 March when our profits will be above INR 300 crore and above.

items.statement: Advanced gold business (job-work only) at 6% of volume, targeting 10-12% by FY27 to improve working capital cycle
items.quote: we are targeting to be at 10% to 12% by '27 for advance gold business. And that will again help us to reduce our working cycle and we will be cash flow positive by '27 March

items.statement: Net debt INR 450 crore; GML facility sanctioned INR 170 crore (INR 40 crore utilized at 4% cost), targeting INR 350 crore GML limit
items.quote: So, at this point of time, we have got INR 170 crore of sanctioned GML facility. We are negotiating with other bankers as well to sanction the GML facility. We expect that this INR 170 crore, considering the current set of bankers, can go up to INR 350 crores.

items.statement: Acquired Speed Bangle (ex-Ganna N Gold) in Aug 2025; 41 kg in Q2, 50 kg/month from Q3; 100% advanced gold model with Section 115BAB tax benefit
items.quote: This business will adopt 100% advanced gold business which is expected to strengthen the working capital cycle. Also this company has tax incentive benefits under Section 115BAB, resulting in improved PAT margins.

items.statement: Non-binding term sheet for majority stake in Shri Rishab Gold (mangalsutra specialist) to onboard large retail client via Star Mangalsutra subsidiary
items.quote: To further expand our customer portfolio and deepening market penetration in the high growth traditional jewellery segment, we have entered into a non-binding term sheet to acquire a majority stake in the Shri Rishab Gold, a reputed Mumbai-based jewellery firm.

items.statement: Top 3 clients 25-27% of revenue, top 5 clients 30-35%; new clients CaratLane 10-12 kg/month, Aditya Birla 3-4 kg, P.N. Gadgil 6-7 kg, Reliance onboarding
items.quote: So, top 3 is 25% to 27% and top 5 will be 30% or 32% something. Siddharth Sipani: 35

items.statement: Dubai B2B office (Sky Souk Jewellery Trading LLC) opened Oct-Nov 2025 to serve UAE, Singapore, Malaysia; exports targeting 15-20% of sales by March 2027
items.quote: To expand our international footprint, we have established a new B2B sales office, Sky Souk Jewellery trading LLC in Dubai, UAE. This move is aimed at strengthening our foot-fold in the Middle East, a region identified for its robust demand for premium jewellery, particularly in UAE.

items.statement: Siddharth Sipani promoted to CFO (16 years experience); Virupakshi Kolla appointed independent director (36 years banking, ex-Kotak Mahindra Bank Gems & Jewellery head)
items.quote: To support our growth, we have strengthened our team by promoting Mr. Siddharth Sipani as the CFO, who previously headed the finance department as a group finance controller Sky Gold & and brings over 16-year of expertise in finance and accounts, global fundraising, due diligence. compliance, auditing across diverse industry sectors. This will help me to focus on strategic business initiatives. Al

items.statement: Gold price outlook: management expects 20-25% annual appreciation over next 3-4 years driven by ETF and central bank buying
items.quote: So, I think we are seeing from last 20 years, we have seen a huge amount of investment routing to ETF and sovereign gold bond, which was not there 5 years-10 years back, ETF was not there so much. So, ETF is buying like 150-200 ton per year and central banks are buying. So, I think gold is, I think we will appreciate it. I am seeing next 3-4 years gold appreciating by 20%-25% yearly basis.

items.statement: Promoter share sale execution issues in prior quarter; no further dilution planned for 3-5 years; funded via internal accruals
items.quote: We have already done for 2-3-5 years from here. So, we have appointed a good branded merchant banker for the execution two quarters before. But there was some execution lag from the merchant banker side. I accept and apologize for that, but there is no plan for 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Volume 544 kg/month in Q2 FY26 (+20% QoQ); advanced gold 6% of volume, studded 1.5% of revenue; 18Kt at 14-15% of sales
items.quote: Volumes have been increased to 544 kgs per month for this quarter, registering a 20% growth versus Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: 22Kt remains 80% of India market; 18Kt at 14-15% of company sales; 9Kt/14Kt below 1% but growing; studded jewellery doubled to 1.5% of revenue
items.quote: So, lower caratage is very low volume, you can see India 80% is 22Kt, and 15% is 18Kt and this 9Kt, 14Kt is below 1%. So, it will take time to grow 5-10 years to come up at 4%-5% of the sales. So, right now we are at 14%-15% of 18Kt sales and 80% at 22Kt sales.

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed from WDV to SLM across group; H1 FY26 PAT higher by 0.08% due to change
items.quote: During the quarter, we re-aligned the accounting policy for depreciation across Sky Gold Group. The same as we re-aligned from WDV to SLM so as to better match the business expenses with the expected pattern of usage of assets. This change has resulted into currently half a year PAT to be higher by 0.08%.

items.statement: Signed MOU with Universal Autofoundry for 7-year machining alliance starting January 2026 in Rajasthan
items.quote: Kranti has signed an MOU with Universal Autofoundry Limited (UFL) for a long-term machining alliance in Rajasthan. This partnership begins in January 2026 for a seven-year term and focuses on integrated manufacturing for the automotive and engineering

items.statement: Received new purchase order from Ingersoll-Rand US for 10 housing components with estimated annual business of USD$438,000
items.quote: We have also received a new purchase order from Ingersoll-Rand US in August 2025 for 10 new housing components w ith a sample order worth USD$9,763 and an estimated annual business of USD$438,000

items.statement: Expects monthly sales revenue of ₹8-8.5 crores currently, with Jaipur facility adding ₹4-4.5 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Current order book-wise, we are right now at a monthly sales revenue rate of somewhere around ₹8 crores - ₹8.5 crores. This is what we have currently monthly. But future projection for January from Q4 onwards is there. In addition to this, our Jaipur facility will be started in January. That will add up to the further revenue of around ₹4 crores - ₹4.5 crores.

items.statement: Jaipur facility expected to add ₹20-22 crores revenue in next financial year
items.quote: Not ₹100 crores. It will add to around ₹20 crores - ₹22 crores in next financial year. This ₹4 crores I said is the contribution in the next quarter, Q4. It is close to around ₹1.5 crores per month.

items.statement: Pune facility at 65-68% capacity utilization, expected to reach 75-78% by end of FY26; Jaipur facility adding 48 machines starting January 2026
items.quote: Right now, in Pune facility, we are at a capacity utilization close to around 65% to 68%. With the new products that we have added, we expect this to go to close to around 75%-78% by the end of this financial year. Jaipur facility, it is yet to achieve. But right now, the capacity utilization for whatever the plant is running, which is somewhere around 50% -55% may be the capacity utilization.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 18.7% in Q2 FY26; expects to stabilize at 16.5-17% long-term
items.quote: The margin expansion from 15.9% to 18.7% underscores our operational efficiencies we have been able to implement.

items.statement: Conservative long-term EBITDA margin target of 16.5-17% with all operations in place
items.quote: What we are optimizing, because of few product mix and few new product development additions, as well as some export order additions, what we expect on a conservative basis also, we will be somewhere around 16.5%, 17% margin in the long run with all the operations in place.

items.statement: Tractor segment contributes 65-68% of revenue; expanding into EV, commercial vehicles, non-automotive (Ingersoll, Bonfiglioli)
items.quote: Segment-wise, actually we do not have a different segmental revenue that we are monitoring. If you go with market segment-wise, definitely, tractor is our major segment. There are close to 65% - 68% revenue comes from tractors. Another by then EV and commercial vehicles are there. Considering future, we have a few non -automotive segments where we have grabbed some big orders , like from Ingersoll

items.statement: Lease rental for Jaipur facility approximately ₹1.5 crores for first financial year; 48 machines being added
items.quote: No, it is much less than the initial first two years, it is lesser, because we have worked out the MOU accordingly, and it will be close to somewhere around ₹1.5 crores for the financial year.

items.statement: Preferential issue of ₹12.8 crores nearly complete; only ₹1.5 crores remaining to be received; no immediate fundraising plans this financial year
items.quote: Yes, the total preferential issue was around ₹12.8 crores. Out of that, only last ₹1.5 crores is yet to be received from the investor. The balance has been received and the utilization has been in, as well as the details are already given, as well as for the working capital and few CAPEX margins and CAPEX addition which we have done in last year.

items.statement: Targeting net debt-free by 2030-2032; balancing CAPEX with equity and debt
items.quote: Debt consolidation is the plan. We are targeting to be a net debt -free company by 2030 -2032. But being a heavy CAPEX industry, for the last two years we are balancing our further CAPEX in the combination of equity and debt.

items.statement: Expects minimum double-digit revenue growth annually for next three years with EBITDA stabilizing at 16-17%
items.quote: Overall, yes, what I said is on the blended level on the conservative with all types of product and everything. We expect that we will be stabilizing EBITDA margin of 16.5% to 17%. Revenue wise, we expect at least double digit, minimum double-digit growth and all next coming to three years.

items.statement: Preciso Metall at ~40% capacity utilization, 12-13% EBITDA margin; expects strong recovery from Q4 FY26
items.quote: Right now, we are at close to around 40% capacity utilization. So, we have a good potential to increase the business. We are banking on a few products also, which are recently under development, as well as a few samples which are submitted. The development process is going on. So, we expect a strong recovery in Preciso Metall starting from Q4 onwards, as well as the next financial year.

items.statement: Secured order from Pune-based EV commercial vehicle manufacturer Eka Mobility; expanding across domestic, global and tractor segment OEMs
items.quote: Our footprint in the EV segment continues to expand. This quarter, we have secured another order from a Pune -based electric commercial vehicle manufacturer, Eka Mobility, further validating our capabilities in the clean mobility space.

items.statement: Plans to enter select non-automotive engineering segments leveraging group company's foundry; pursue strategic partnerships with OEMs and technology companies
items.quote: Additionally, we aim to enter the select non -automotive engineering segment, leveraging our group company's foundry to broaden our revenue base.

items.statement: Will scale renewable energy adoption, enhance water recycling, deploy energy-efficient equipment to reduce costs and carbon footprint
items.quote: On the sustainability front , we will scale renewable energy to adoption, enhance water-seed recycling system, deploy energy -efficient equipment and improve overall resource utilization to reduce both our costs as well as our carbon footprint.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% after gold price impact, original target 45-50% in next 6-8 months
items.quote: We are expecting to grow to 20%-25% this year. Our target is to achieve 45%-50% in the next 6-8 months.

items.statement: Booked INR102 crores fresh domestic orders at IIJS 2025 plus INR5.41 crores premium Aneya orders
items.quote: Operationally, it has been a defining quarter for us, as we have also booked INR102 crores of fresh domestic orders at IIJS 2025, and additionally, we have secured INR5.41 crores orders of our premium line of diamond and polki jewellery collecti on under our brand name, Aneya

items.statement: In talks with two national chains for orders, preparing for January IIJS Signature exhibition, expect order book to rise in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: Yes, 100% we are currently in talks with two national chains for the orders to confirm and in January IIJS signature new exhibition is also coming. We are preparing for that in a huge segment. So, we will expect order book to rise and can confirm in quarter 3 and quarte r 4 as well you can see the numbers

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin doubled to 11% (540 bps expansion) driven by higher volumes, premium product mix, design innovation and gold price
items.quote: Total income grew by 18% year -on-year to INR102 crores, while EBITDA margin is doubled more than INR11.47 crores we have achieved, doubled than the last quarter, resulting in 540 bps margin expansion to 11%.

items.statement: Aim to maintain stable margin with gradual upward bias supported by manufacturing efficiency and volume from national chains
items.quote: our focus is also on improving product mix, scaling branded segments, w hich will structurally support margin. And again, we aim to maintain stable margin with gradual upward bias supported by manufacturing efficiency and volume of orders from the national chains

items.statement: Current capacity 750 kg (up from 500 kg), can expand to 1 ton; 1.5 ton total premises capacity with 3 floors of 500 kg each
items.quote: So, current capacity we have increased 250 kgs from 500, 750 kgs is the current capacity. And we are sufficient to fulfill the orders for the current time. In case if we receive more order we can increase up to 1 ton.

items.statement: Can expand production capacity in 40-60 days using acquired land; 93% utilization on first 500 kg floor
items.quote: So, as I mentioned before also th at we have factory unit where we have over 1.5 ton production capacity to expand space. We have acquired the land. So, when we have order flow, we need 40 to 60 days to expand our production capacity.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 60-65% from big-box corporate chains, 30-35% from big-box singular stores; separate teams for each segment
items.quote: So, currently around in terms of kgs I would mention 60% to 65% of the revenue mix is coming from big box corporate clients and 30% to 35% is coming from big box singular stores.

items.statement: Target 45-day working capital cycle; 60% of IIJS orders delivered, 70-75% of diamond collection orders released
items.quote: The collections we launch, we focus on the order cycle. Our capital is not blocked in inventory. The capital cycle will obviously increase. We target to focus on 45 days of working cycle in terms of collections.

items.statement: Hedge 100% of gold inventory against fixed sales rates; procure bullion from established vendors, Gift City and local players
items.quote: So, we are hedging almost 100% hedge. Whatever sales booked by a company in every transaction on fixed sales, fixed rate cut, type of rate cut, we are hedging 100% against the fixed rate cut.

items.statement: Consumers shifting to lighter weight and lower caratage (18K, 14K) due to rising gold prices; company developing capsule collections for this trend
items.quote: So, there are 2 -3 different trends I am able to see right now. So, because of the rising gold prices people are focusing on lighter weight jewellery and clients are also focusing on reducing the caratage also. We are also working on capsule collections of 18 carat jewellery and 14 carat jewellery also in diamond and polky collections.

items.statement: Broad-based demand across national and regional chains; 20% volume growth sustainable due to design-led offerings and premium collections
items.quote: Yes, because we believe that this trajectory is sustainable because the demand is broad-based across national jewellery retail chains plus regional jewellery chains which we have different brands to cater to them. And again, we are focusing also on our premium collection categories.

items.statement: Gold price rose 40-50% in 6 months impacting revenue growth guidance; volume growth target maintained at 20%
items.quote: But in quarter 1 and quarter 2, as we have seen, the gold price has risen to Ashapuri Gold Ornament Limited November 18, 2025 over 40 %-50% in just last 6 months. Through that gold price also, we have sustained a revenue margin of 20%. We are expecting to grow to 20%-25% this

items.quote: There is a product difference, sir. The making cycle of our product is more now. Rather than the difference in product, small product, casting product, they are producing casting and chain product. So, there is more turnover in them compared to our antique product. This is our whole designing and wedding segment. So, the production cycle is a little big in that. And if we do a comparison in that,

items.statement: Target 500 operational Care Home beds by November end; scale AGEasy to breakeven by late FY27 or early FY28; develop 1.5 million sq ft residences annually
items.quote: target 500 beds operational by November end and then go on to build out the rest over the next 4 years. Scale AGEasy to reach and drive breakeven by early FY '28 or late FY '27.

items.statement: Preferential issue of convertible warrants raised INR80 crore; INR40 crore received, balance next year; primarily for residence vertical
items.quote: we also raised INR80 crores through preferential issue of convertible warrants. Half of the proceeds, the partial payment, INR40 crores has already been received. The rest will come next year. This will primarily be used for residence vertical for existing as well as future projects.

items.quote: Due to the geopolitical situation in India, the government has reviewed all high clearances, all projects which were within 20 kilometers radius of all important airports. Our project was 20.1 kilometers from the Chandigarh Airport. So that is still not cleared.

items.statement: Noida Sector 150 OC pending; Supreme Court hearing on 18 Nov 2025; project falls in Category 2; all dues paid, sports city obligation constructed
items.quote: the matter is lying with the Supreme Court. Our hearing is on the 18 th Nov’25. The Noida Authority in the last hearing has presented 3 categories in Sector 150 and 78, 79, which they want to resolve. We fall in Category 2

items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA at negative INR26 crores. The focus continues on cost optimization, high utilization and efficient treasury management.

items.quote: AGEasy achieved a net revenue of INR20.9 crores. So we're now already at a monthly run rate of INR7 crores to INR8 crores already, marking a 1.5x growth QoQ. The H1 revenue now stands at INR35 crores, which is about 3.3x same period last year. We have had a 2.4x QoQ growth on the off-line sales of AGEasy products.

items.statement: Net debt INR105 crore repaid; liquidity INR208 crore earmarked for growth
items.quote: On liquidity, we're at about INR 208 crores, Our net debt of INR105 crores has been repaid. So this is net of that debt and it is primarily earmarked only for growth.

items.quote: You may have seen that many players are now entering the Senior Living segment, including some marquee names as well. So, we are glad that at least the entire category gets a push.

items.quote: The gross margins remain stable at 41.2%, and I would like to draw your attention, despite the growth and other headwinds, we were able to maintain this gross margin ratio.

items.quote: Gathering consumption waves following changes in the GST rate, the domestic auto industry is expected to grow at a healthy pace. The entry-level motorcycle segment and PV segment is poised for a strong volume expansion, and the overall PV segment is also expected to perform well.

items.quote: On the global side, stricter regional value content, RVC requirements, are accelerating the shift towards localized manufacturing, especially in the U.S., and sourcing within the U.S., Mexico, Canada, and Florida.

items.quote: This performance has come despite the introduction of tariffs, which are causing some pressure on the sales offtake, especially in the U.S. and European markets, also impacting our margins in certain cases.

items.quote: After the monsoon, we see a very good opportunity. We have got a lot of work at hand. We are also expecting a few more large-sized orders, which will be announced as soon as we have received them. Very soon, we will come up. And we are hoping for a good season in H2.

items.quote: working capital cycle keeps, by and large, though we say it is about 90 days, but on a few projects because of various things, generally, it lies about 90 to 120 days.

items.statement: Dependent on workforce, government portfolio, cyclic operations and short-term project life making business high capital intensive

items.quote: Given the performance that we've had in H1, we will continue to aim for a full year margin improvement.

items.quote: I think the demand environment continues to remain challenging. Notwithstanding that, we have a strong set of plans to drive growth.

items.quote: On the profitability front, Q2 adjusted EBITDA crossed Rs. 100 crores for the first time ever with a lifetime high margin of 13.1%. Our EBITDA margin expanded 162 basis points YoY during the quarter.

items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for H1 was Rs. 168.5 crores, resulting in a growth of 20% YoY. Our margins are up 70 basis points on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Gross margins at 56.5% in Q2, range bound vs 56.3% last year, up 25 bps YoY
items.quote: Our Q2 gross margins at 56.5% were range bound versus 56.3% last year and 25 basis points higher on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Service AMC bookings grew strong double-digits in value driven by volumes and ASPs
items.quote: AMC bookings growth accelerated and grew by strong double-digits in value. This was driven by both, volumes and ASPs.

items.statement: Multiyear AMC mix improved helping customer retention
items.quote: Within that, the multiyear AMC mix improved, which helps in driving customer retention.

items.statement: Inaugurated revamped R&D centre in Bangalore to add muscle to product innovation capabilities
items.quote: I'm also pleased to share that we have recently inaugurated our revamped R&D centre in Bangalore, and this will add more muscle to our product innovation capabilities.

items.statement: Robotics now contributes nearly 60% of VC sales, cleaning category emerged as powerful growth engine
items.quote: With the growth and the growing salience of robotics, which now contributes to nearly 60% of VC sales, the cleaning category has now emerged as a powerful growth engine for us.

items.statement: Premium portfolio share increased in water purifiers over 3 years, mid-price segment shrunk as people upgraded
items.quote: Our mix of economy has remained the same, increased marginally. Our mix of premium has increased, and the mix of the mid-price segment has shrunk a little bit because people have upgraded to premium.

items.quote: In robotics, our growth has come also from a premium end of our portfolio, the fully automatic cleaning station as also the auto bin station, which come at higher gross margins and which are, therefore, more P&L accretive.

items.quote: Our app now has more than 1.5 million monthly active users who come to us for transacting, who come to us for looking at products and of course, for service interactions.

items.statement: First-party data of nearly 15 million customers with privileged access to homes through direct sales and service network
items.quote: We have, as we speak now, a first-party data of nearly 15 million customers. We reach our customers through both, our direct sales channel and through our service network.

items.statement: No impact on market share from new entrants; e-commerce share recovered to highest ever
items.quote: Indeed, in e-commerce, where there was some ear ly competitive activity a couple of years ago, we have managed to recover and grow share to the highest ever across both our e-commerce platforms

items.statement: Welcome competition as it creates category awareness and growth; market big enough for all
items.quote: We welcome all competition because we believe it's going to be creating this virtuous cycle of higher growth.

items.statement: Debtors increased due to seasonal monsoon/pre-festive billing, e-commerce and modern trade terms, and GST 2.0 order back-ending; will unwind in H2

items.quote: I think that process has already started, and I would say it started nearly a year back. And the key trigger for that was the fact that the business had seen and continues to see good volume growth. So that is something which gives us a very, very important lever in negotiating costs.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment remains mixed across sectors and economy; could impact demand
items.quote: I think the only callout that I would have is that as you would have noticed, the consumer sentiment does continue to remain mixed and that is still getting reflected in various sectors and parts of the economy.

items.statement: Customer SAT scores reached all-time highs; edge case resolution improved with special escalation desks, proactive teams, spares availability

items.statement: Dividend or buyback remains an option given healthy cash position; bias towards growth investments at this transformation stage
items.quote: I think that remains an option. Having said that, our bias at this stage of the transformation would be towards looking at growth opportunities, and that is an ongoing process.

items.statement: Expect normalization in upcoming quarters as seasonal challenges are temporary
items.quote: However, these challenges are temporary, and we expect normalization in the upcoming quarters.

items.quote: Further, we commissioned our new hospital in Rajahmundry in east Godavari district of AP.

items.quote: We are now gearing up for the commencement of two new spoke hospitals in Bengaluru — Electronic City and Hennur — further expanding our presence in this key metropolitan city.
