items.statement: Secured nomination from leading Japanese OEM for transfer case on iconic pickup platform with SOP H1 FY28
items.quote: We have secured a nomination from a very leading Japanese OEM that is a market leader globally and in particular, in Southeast Asia, to develop the transfer case for their iconic pickup truck platform with SOP starting from H1 FY '28.

items.statement: Expect to surpass FY24 transfer case volumes and accelerate growth in coming quarters
items.quote: We expect to surpass FY '24 transfer case volumes and are well positioned to accelerate further growth in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect 20-25% improvement in EV transmission volumes in H2 FY26
items.quote: Broadly, we are expecting about a 20% to 25% improvement in volumes on EV transmissions.

items.statement: Evaluating feasibility of US manufacturing footprint, study conclusion by March 2026
items.quote: As part of our long -term strategy, we are al so evaluating the feasibility of establishing a manufacturing footprint in the U.S. market to support future growth and deepen our global presence. We expect this study to reach some sort of a conclusion before March end '26.

items.statement: Transfer cases grew 42% YoY in H1 FY26 driven by Mahindra, Tata, Force Motors
items.quote: On transfer cases, we delivered a strong performance in the first half, growing 42% year-on-year and demonstrating continued momentum in this vertical.

items.statement: Components segment grew 113% YoY in H1 FY26, primarily export-led to BorgWarner and Magna
items.quote: The components segment continued its robust performance, growing 113% in H1 FY '26 compared to H1 FY '25. This exceptional growth was largely export led despite global market uncertainties.

items.statement: Exports contributed 16% of total income in H1 FY26, over 20% in Q2 FY26, targeting 20-25% medium-term
items.quote: Exports, this was most encouraging, contributed nearly 16% in H1 and more significantly, over 20% in Q2 FY '26, helpi ng us make progress towards our medium-term target of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Volume-led price correction on transfer cases based on contractual threshold reflects sustained demand
items.quote: During the quarter, we also saw a volume -led price correction based on the agreed contractual threshold, which you could interpret as a healthy sign that reflects sustained demand and strong long-term volume visibility.

items.statement: US tariffs limited to 25% on light-duty applications, India remains competitive vs China at 50%
items.quote: Coming to U.S. tariffs, I want to highlight that we do not foresee any short-term impact of these actions on our components business. India, despite this action, continues to remain competitive in the light-duty application segment in the United States, where -- and I want to emphasize this, the duty structure is not 50%, but limited to 25%.

items.statement: Prefer organic growth and technology acquisition over strategic acquisitions to protect quality focus
items.quote: Our approach -- preferred approach is that we will grow sort of organically. We will aggressively acquire technology. So acquisition can take many different forms and which is how we are looking at this 8 -speed technology from Europe.

items.statement: Decided to leapfrog to 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmissions for passenger segment
items.quote: And in order to sort of leapfrog this dynamic market, we have made a decision to go straight to 8-speed transmissions instead of 6 or 7 -speed transmissions. And given the commonality that exists between -- to a significant extent between manual transmission -- the manual transmission ecosystem in India and what is needed for dual-clutch automatic transmissions, we have elected to work with dual -

items.statement: Received significant RFQ for 5-speed manual transmission from India's largest commercial vehicle OEM
items.quote: As mentioned in our previous earnings call, we have received a significant RFQ for a five-speed manual transmission from one of India's largest commercial vehicle OEMs.

items.statement: Engaged with Ford, Tesla, Toyota for EV transmission opportunities in US and Europe
items.quote: On the export front, we are expanding our global reach to engage with international OEMs like Ford and Tesla, also Toyota, aligning with their evolving platform requirements and strengthening our presence in key geographies.

items.statement: Components export contracts typically 5-7 years, often extend as carryover to next-gen platforms
items.quote: So typically, our contracts go from 5 to 7 years, sometimes longer. It depends upon the life cycle of these Tier 1 aggregates. What I would like to -- the insight I would like to offer you is that with electrification coming in, OEMs are reluctant now to do major surgery on the legacy products because there's not much growth globally that they are expecting. Therefore, the legacy -- whatever resid

items.statement: Several new export products in approval stage, expect conversion to firm orders in FY27
items.quote: Several new products are currently in the approval stage, and we anticipate many of this to be converted into firm orders in FY '27.

items.statement: EV plant utilization below desired level, targeting 20-30% volume improvement via Tata portfolio broadening
items.quote: But in the immediate near future, what I can tell you is broadening the portfolio just at Tata Motors will give us at least a 20% to 30% improvement in volumes. Overall, the utilization at the end of this will still remain below what we desire.

items.statement: Marketplace unpredictable, but exports recovered from 1.5% to 20% of sales in 2 years demonstrating resilience
items.quote: The reality is the marketplace continues to remain a little unpredictable. And so our approach now is to take advantage of where we are right now and continue to strengthen the resilience of our business model. And hopefully, you've seen that we have the ability to bounce back. And the strongest indication of this, I would say, is that if you looked at our exports in FY '24, they had fallen to jus

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance of 18-20% for rest of FY26; with 25% YTD growth, full year likely to cross 22%
items.quote: And we have given a guidance of around 18% to 20% growth for the rest of the year, which means that 25% plus 18% to 20% for five months, we would be crossing 20% growth for sure for the whole year.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 7.2-7.4% for full year FY26
items.quote: will continue to reinforce the fact that this year also we should also be clocking an EBITDA between 7.2% to 7.4% on a whole year's level

items.statement: Target to increase stud ratio to 13-13.5% by FY27
items.quote: So, to give answer to your question, yes, we are looking at 13%, 13.5%, for FY '27.

items.statement: October sales grew ~55-60% YoY to INR 1,700 crore, highest-ever monthly sales; current growth momentum upward of 20%
items.quote: We had clocked the highest-ever sales in any single month of INR 1,700 crores in the month of October, compared to about INR 1,100 crore s of sales in the previous year's October month of the festive

items.statement: YTD value growth ~25% YoY; volume growth minimal in low single digits due to high gold prices
items.quote: We are currently seeing year-to-date (YTD) value growth of almost 25% year-on-year. However, despite this strong value growth, volume growth is minimal remaining in the low single digits or almost zero primarily due to rising gold prices.

items.statement: Q2 consolidated EBITDA margin 6.9% (+340 bps YoY); H1 blended EBITDA ~8.5%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter and for the whole year has been range bound. So, you would see an EBITDA margin improvement of 340 bps from 3.5% to 6.9% on a consolidated basis

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin normalized to 7.4% vs Q1 10.1% which included ~INR 20-25 crore hedging gain
items.quote: In Quarter 1, it was 10%. In Quarter 2, it is around 7.4%. We clearly stand by our guidance of the range bound of, let's say, 7.1% to 7.4%.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month sales crossed INR 7,400 crore; YTD revenue crossed INR 5,000 crore
items.quote: So, when we published that TTM number as well, we are very happy to inform you that the trailing 12 months sales have crossed INR 7,400 crore.

items.statement: Launched 6 showrooms in Q2, 16 in H1 (11 franchisee, 5 COCO); pipeline of 4-6 more franchisee stores
items.quote: We have launched six showrooms in Q2 and a total of 16 showrooms we have launched in H1

items.statement: Average ticket size increased 16% to INR 86,200; stud ratio strong at ~12%; no discounting on making charges
items.quote: In terms of average selling price and average ticket price in an increasing gold scenario, we have seen that it has almost gone up by 16% to INR 86,200.

items.statement: Old gold exchange rose to 42-43% of transactions from 35% YoY; consumers shifting to lighter weight, 18k/14k/9k jewellery
items.quote: The other aspect that we need to take note of is that the old gold exchange in the overall transactions that we do with the consumers, that has gone up to 42% to 43% from a 35% a year back

items.statement: Diamond jewellery volume growth in low single digits; natural diamond realisation per carat stable
items.quote: The volume caratages have also gone up by, I would say, low double digits. So, there is some amount of caratage growth. And the gold aspect of it in the overall diamond jewel lery has also played a role

items.statement: ~65% business from loyal/repeat customer base; focus on middle/upper-middle class budgets with lightweight designs
items.quote: And also, amongst our consumer base we must keep in mind that almost 65% of the business that we get is from our loyal customer base and our repeat customers.

items.statement: Inventory increased from INR 3,500 crore to INR 4,200 crore for Dhanteras preparedness and gold price impact; payables increased for festive stocking
items.quote: Similarly, if you look at the balance sheet, you will find an increase in the inventory level from around INR 3,500 crore level to INR 4,200 crore level, which we have explained. This has got two reasons one is the Dhanteras preparedness, and secondly, the gold price rise impact.

items.statement: GML mix dropped to ~51% in H1, currently ~54-55% to avoid margin calls from gold volatility; using CC instead
items.quote: Although GML availability had improved in Quarter 2, but once again, as you are aware, GML is on an unfixed basis. And d ue to the extreme volatility in the gold prices, we were receiving a lot of margin calls. So, to avoid the margin call pressure, we resorted to CC instead of GML

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity at 0.75x; debt elevated in Sept for Dhanteras, comes down by INR 300-400 cr by Dec; working capital limits increased to INR 2,400 cr for Mar'26
items.quote: The net debt to equity is also in the range of 0.75. Overall, we are very confident that the business is showing its resilience despite competitive pressure in the market, but we maintain our strength in the market.

items.statement: SSSG: Q2 -4%, H1 +8%, YTD October +17%
items.quote: So, first, in terms of SSSG growth of Q2 has been -4%. SSSG growth for six months, H1 has been +8%, and SSSG growth for YTD October has been 17%.

items.statement: Hedging: Sales hedged 90-100% (effectively 105% with replenishment); inventory hedged 65-70%, can increase to 80-90% if gold prices fall
items.quote: From hedging perspective, I would like to say that when it comes to hedging in terms of the sales that we are doing, we are almost hedging 90% to 100%. That is buying as much as we are selling. And if we are looking at the hedging levels of the inventory that we have, as we ended Q2, our hedging percentage has been in the range of 65% to 70%.

items.statement: GML rate differential vs CC ~6% (3.5% vs 9-10%) but manageable; margin call risk forces dynamic hedging management
items.quote: While our ideal target to take the GML to 75% remains there, but as of now, we are again seeing volatility for the last three, four days. So, going forward, we have to see. But in terms of impact, the differential impact is Around 6.5, let's say the GML interest rate is 3.5% and CC is around 9%, 6% on the differential will not be a huge amount.

items.statement: Q2 inventory gain ~INR 5-8 crore vs INR 20-25 crore in Q1 due to lower hedging ratio
items.quote: It is around INR 5 crore to INR 6 crore. In the opening remark itself, sir had said that it is around 50 basis points on INR 1,500 crore. So, that is the number.

items.statement: Maintains pricing power without discounting; peers offering discounts on gold but Senco focuses on designs and offers
items.quote: As you are aware, there are a lot of discounting happening in the market, but we maintain the brand image perfectly. We don't indulge in discounting either in the making charges, we rather play in attracting our customers with more new designs and attractive offers.

items.statement: GST rate change (GST 2.0) caused purchase deferment in Q2; Durga Puja timing also impacted Eastern region sales
items.quote: GST 2.0, where customers have suspended their purchases for the purchase of capital goods. So, the cultural pattern varies from region to region. I think that could be one of the reasons.

items.statement: Franchisee interest growing due to gold as asset class confidence; Everlite model (INR 6-8 cr capex) for lightweight jewellery in tier 2/3/4 towns
items.quote: Also, our Everlite model, which is the INR 6 crore to INR 8 crore of capital required to open a store focusing on lightweight jewellery, is very much there as well.

items.statement: PAT jumped ~300% YoY to INR 48.8 crore in Q2; adjusted PAT up 43% excluding customs duty impact
items.quote: So, in terms of PAT, we have increased our PAT by almost 300% compared to Q2 of last year, from INR 12.1 crore to INR 48.8 crore. And if we take the adjustment of the customs duty impact that was there, still there would be an increase in PAT of 43%.

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY26 expected around H1 level with slight upside
items.quote: I think what we closed the H1 margin for, I think somewhere around that would be a realistic number for the whole of the end year also, maybe 0.5% up and down here.

items.statement: ARPOB growth target of 8-10% annually for next 3 years
items.quote: Also, for last 2, 3 years, clearly, we have shown 8% to 10% ARPOB growth. And I think for next 3 years also, we do expect 8% to 10% ARPOB growth clearly.

items.statement: CGHS rate revision to add 2.5% revenue upside and 1.75% EBITDA upside in FY27
items.quote: So we are looking to the upside of CGHS revenue that will be around 1.5% in this FY '26 with the benefit on EBITDA to around 1% in this financial year, which may go up to 2.5% in the next year on the revenue front and nearly around 1.75% on the EBITDA front.

items.statement: Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 hospitals to reach EBITDA breakeven in 15-17 months
items.quote: And we are pretty much sure with the next 15 months to 17 months, both hospitals will be EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: Agra hospital to be consolidated from Q4 FY26 and be EBITDA positive from day 1
items.quote: Agra facility will be on our books from quarter 4 fully. So somewhere from the first week of the new year, we should be starting the facility.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 1,500 crores over 4.5-5 years inclusive of acquisitions and greenfield
items.quote: I think we have already given the guidance for the next 4, 4.5 years of INR1,500 crores of capex. I think we'll just stick to that.

items.statement: Added 700 beds in Q2 FY26 via Model Town Delhi (300) and Faridabad Sector 20 (400)
items.quote: During the quarter, we have added 700 beds with commencement of our New Delhi and Faridabad hospital.

items.statement: Agra acquisition adds 250 beds, integrated from Q4 FY26
items.quote: Continuing our expansion strategy, we also, this quarter acquired Shantived Hospital in Agra, having an expanded capacity of 250 beds.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions at Greater Noida (15 months) and Noida Extension (17-18 months) underway
items.quote: Both these 2 hospitals capacity should be available for us to be utilised somewhere 15 months from the date today. So 15 should be Greater Noida and maybe 17, 18 months from today should be the Noida extension.

items.statement: Target to double bed capacity from ~2,550 to ~5,000 in next 3-4 years via brownfield, acquisitions and greenfield
items.quote: We feel that probably in the next 3 to 4 years, there is still scope in the company to even close to double this capacity in next 3 to 4 years, including all these brownfield expansions that are already in place, the upcoming acquisitions and 1 more greenfield that the company is planning very soon within the NCR region.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 26.7% excluding new hospital losses
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA was INR737 million, up by 35% year-over-year, while our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at healthy 26.7%.

items.statement: Mature hospitals have scope for margin expansion as occupancy can rise from ~65% to 75%
items.quote: For example, both Noida extension and Greater Noida can reach optimised utilization of 75% of occupancy. So still a 10% room way for occupancy to grow, which will directly flow to the EBITDA.

items.statement: Group ARPOB at INR 32,015 in Q2 FY26; mature hospitals up 9% YoY, new hospitals up 19% YoY
items.quote: Our strategic focus on high-value super speciality care and continued investment in cutting-edge medical infrastructure has resulted in an increase in consolidated ARPOB to INR32,015 in quarter 2 FY '26.

items.statement: Occupancy at 66% in Q2 FY26 despite 700 bed addition; Noida at 89%, Greater Noida 69%, Noida Extension 64%, Jhansi 71%
items.quote: However, despite the bed addition, our occupancy stood healthy at 66% during the quarter. As far as, hospital-wise occupancy is concerned, our Noida facility achieved an occupancy of 89%, Greater Noida at 69%, Noida Extension at 64% and Jhansi-Orchha at 71% during the quarter.

items.statement: International patients yield 45-55% ARPOB premium over domestic
items.quote: See, I think there is always upward of around anything between 45% to 55% that's up from your domestic. So even you can extrapolate from there.

items.statement: New hospitals seeing increasing footfalls; Delhi at 13-14% occupancy in first 2-3 months
items.quote: But I think 13%, 14% of already Delhi is operating as of now. Faridabad, we just started. But as said earlier, we are expecting both these hospitals to have a breakeven reaching in 15, 16 months kind of.

items.statement: Super speciality focus driving ARPOB growth; Noida Extension at 70% super speciality mix with ARPOB INR 40,800
items.quote: Our Noida Extension Hospital achieved its highest-ever ARPOB of INR40,800, up by 7% year-over-year, given its approximately 70% contribution from super speciality services.

items.statement: Income tax authorities unfroze provisionally attached properties and fixed assets, restoring financial flexibility
items.quote: A key positive milestone this quarter has been the order from income tax authorities unfreezing the provisional attached properties and fixed assets of the company, restoring full financial flexibility for expansion initiatives.

items.statement: CGHS rate revision effective Oct 13, 2025 with tier-based higher reimbursement for accredited super-specialty providers
items.quote: I would also like to take this opportunity to highlight a key industry-wide development this quarter with the long-awaited central government health scheme (CGHS) rate revision after more than a decade, effective October 13, 2025.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with net cash position of INR 3,692 million
items.quote: Our balance sheet position continues to remain robust with a strong net cash position of INR3,692 million, providing ample financial headroom to capitalize on suitable growth opportunities.

items.statement: Acceptable borrowing cost 7.5-8% from PSU banks if debt taken in future
items.quote: As on date, we do not have any kind of debt in the books. However, if in future we take up the debt, then generally it comes to around 7.5% to 8% on a rate coupon from the PSU banks.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced by 8-10 days in Q2; targeting similar reduction by March 2026
items.quote: So if you see our debtor days has been reduced. So what we have given the projections earlier also in our earnings call. So this time also, we have reduced the debtor days by 8 to 10 days.

items.statement: OCF/EBITDA at 58% due to salary payment policy change; normalized would be ~78%
items.quote: Regarding cash flows. So OCF to EBITDA currently we are 58%. So we have changed the policy. Earlier we have paid salaries on net cumulative of a month, now we are matching the salaries payment as per the competition, as per the peers, okay. Now we are making a bit on the same -- last day of a month, okay. If we neutralise that effect, so our OCF to EBITDA will be around 78%.

items.statement: GST rate cut on consumables/reagents to benefit revenue by 0.3-0.5% and EBITDA by 0.3-0.5%
items.quote: So there are change in GST that will definitely help us. So that will lead to around 0.3% to 0.5% of the overall revenue. That will change only 0.3 to 0.5% in EBITDA.

items.statement: Payor mix: ~37% government, rest split equally between private insurance/TPA and self-pay
items.quote: Payor mix is somewhere around 37% roughly is the government business. And the rest is equally divided between private insurance, TPA as well as self that is the cash payor.

items.statement: Doctor cost at 21.5% of revenue
items.quote: So overall, we are at 21.5% in the doctor share -- doctor cost percentage of revenue.

items.statement: Acquired Shantived Hospital in Agra (250 beds); integration by H2 FY26, revenue/EBITDA from Q4
items.quote: We expect this integration to be completed by H2 of this fiscal itself, and we should be adding revenues and EBITDA of this hospital from quarter 4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Plan to add 300-400 beds via acquisition/project in H1 FY27 within INR 1,500 cr capex
items.quote: And then we also remain committed post that. That means somewhere around H1 of the upcoming next financial year '27, we should also be looking to add somewhere around 300 to 400 beds through an acquisition or an upcoming project that we are working on.

items.statement: Opened representative offices in Baghdad and Tashkent; expanding into Cameroon; targeting 5-6 info centres this FY
items.quote: In this financial year, I think that the strategy is very, very clear that we will open around 5 to 6 information centres.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 18-20% YoY over FY25
items.quote: we are still promising for the delivery of the 18%, 20% annual growth in comparison to FY '25.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin guided at 18% +/- 1%
items.quote: Our margins have remained historically intact. That is from 17%, 18%, 19% or we can say 18 plus/minus 1% type of thing

items.statement: Q2 revenue declined 26-27% due to pan-India heavy monsoon halting underground works
items.quote: As far as this quarter is concerned, in this quarter, we have a decline of about 26%, 27% in our figures because of the obvious reason of pan-India rains.

items.statement: Q2 PAT margin shrank ~2% due to idle labor and resources during rains
items.quote: even then, our margins have shrink only with 2% for this quarter, not more than that.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book INR 2,388 cr; tender pipeline INR 4,000 cr; expect INR 500-600 cr new orders in FY26
items.quote: our unexecuted order book is precisely INR 2,388 crores, which we are having in our hand. And we have the tenders in pipeline of about INR 4,000 crores, and we are expecting minimum INR 500 crores, INR 600 crores further orders to be added in this financial year.

items.statement: Procured critical materials during monsoon; procurement not yet recognized as revenue due to item-rate contracts
items.quote: we have procured a lot of material for which we have not received anything because from government department, supply and laying is the only item.

items.statement: Ramped up execution post-monsoon; expect strong Q3 and Q4 to deliver full-year 20% growth
items.quote: We have ramped it up since October or the rain stopped whenever it happened. And now it is dead sure that we will give it in December and in March quarter.

items.statement: Eligibility criteria (turnover, solvency, experience) act as entry barriers; cannot bid for large tickets without prior similar execution
items.quote: if suppose you have to take INR 500 crore bidding, you want to do INR 500 crore bidding, you must have completed at least one work of INR 300 crores. So, that is a technical eligibility criteria.

items.statement: H.K. Kansal (IIT Roorkee, 40-yr govt water sector veteran) appointed CEO; 75-78 in-house engineers
items.quote: Mr. H. K. Kansal, who did his B.Tech from IIT Roorkee, and then worked in the water sector for 40 years as an engineer in the government department and reached till HOD position. After that, we have appointed him as the CEO of the company.

items.statement: Brijbihari renamed EMS Industries, now wholly owned subsidiary of EMS Limited
items.quote: Brijbihari has been renamed as EMS Industries, and it is already subsidiary of EMS Limited. Brijbihari is EMS Industries now and it is a wholly owned subsidiary of the EMS Limited.

items.statement: Targets 14 crore PAT for FY26 and 18 crore PAT for FY27, aiming for 30 crore PAT by FY28
items.quote: So, down the line what we see is like this year we are targeting 14 crores of PAT and plus above and next year we are targeting around 18 crores of PAT because in last quarter we can get margin from our dying unit also. And for FY28 we see to grow it from here around 30 crores also.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to improve from current 3% to 7-8% by FY28 driven by integration, efficiency and scale
items.quote: Collectively, these initiatives place us firmly on track to improve EBITDA margins from the current 3% to 7% to 8% by FY28, driven by integration, efficiency, and scale.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY26 revenue of around 350 crores, maintaining H1 run rate
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we expect around 350 crores of revenue from H2 also. 350 plus only. So, this run rate I t hink will be maintained. The consolidated 382 numbers will be maintained, I think

items.statement: Plans 55 crore capex for backward integration dyeing unit, work to start in 3-4 months
items.quote: The third is a dying unit which we are planning to start work in next three to four months. So that will be an integration for the next capex will be around 55 crores.

items.statement: Plans 8-9 crore capex for green energy in Q1 FY27 after dyeing unit expansion
items.quote: For that capex will be around 8 to 9 crores.

items.statement: Backward integration dyeing unit expected to commercialise by December 2026 or January 2027
items.quote: Backward integration we are expecting to commercialise by December'26 or January'27.

items.statement: Current capacity utilisation at 89.9%, highest in history, on 19.2 million meter platform
items.quote: The capacity utilization was 89.9%, the highest in our history, reflecting at maturing operating engine and more consis tent execution across our 19.2 -million-meter platform

items.statement: Teesta Spintex finishing unit capacity utilisation around 75%, with 15-20% spare capacity
items.quote: Exact numbers I don't have Sir, but somewhere around what I presume it must be around 75% or so. And around 15 to 20% of the capacity, I think there is still spare.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA 10 crores at 2.6% margin, margins expanded 32 bps subsequently as integration benefits began
items.quote: EBITDA of H1 -FY26 stood at 10 crores with a margin of 2.6%. Subsequently, however, margins expanded by 32 basis points, an early sign of recovery as integration benefits began to take shape.

items.statement: Forward integration through Teesta Spintex contributed 3.37 crore PAT in H1, expects 4 crores in H2
items.quote: So, from the finishing unit, the profit from Testa Spintex standalone is around, I will give the exact number. 3 crore 37 lakhs is from the acquired unit. And in H2 we see around 4 crores from here.

items.statement: Weaving margins declined due to pricing compromise to maintain working capital cycle
items.quote: So weaving margins are declined because of the prices I said. So that is completely reflecting in the standalone, right? So, the prices which we have altered s omething to maintain the working capital cycle. So that is reflecting in the weaving standalone results

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to improve by up to 2% from integration benefits
items.quote: So, the margins are definitely that this EBITDA margin we see to improve by the integration we are doing because as I said the revenue part you can just expect 7 to 8 percent of growth but the main thing will be the increase in the profits by integration. So, the margins percentage if you see this will improve from up to 2 to 3 percent. Up to 2% EBITDA margin will improve.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue 382 crores, highest ever half-yearly performance, driven by healthier product mix and improved realisation
items.quote: We closed the period with 382 crores of Revenue, our highest ever half yearly performance. This growth was supported by our healthier products mix, improved realization and stronger wallet share from key customers.

items.statement: Domestic denim market growing due to young population and older generation adoption; export US tariff impact minimal
items.quote: So, Saket Ji, the market, if you see, apart from the export market, the domestic market is very good. In India, if you see, there is a good consumption of denim. If you see a lot of young population, even the older generation is now converting and comfortable wearing denim. So, the market is growing in India itself.

items.statement: Compromised slightly on pricing to maintain working capital cycle and strict payment terms
items.quote: Sir, if you see the pricing, the margins might have been impacted a little bit because we are still very strict on our payments and working capital cycles. So, we are not willing to hold these stocks or increase our debtors in the market. So, pricing, little bit we have compromised in that pricing.

items.statement: No price hike expected in H2 FY26 due to competition and US tariff pressure; may consider after tariff clarity
items.quote: H2 we don't see any price hike because there is little b it of competition because of this global reasons also like US Tariff so there is somewhat pressure in domestic market also however, we have able to maintain our sales so there is no drop in that so price hike once this tariff thing is more clear so we can think of after that but before that price hike is seems to be little difficult

items.statement: Reduced working capital days from 19 in FY25 to 15 in FY26; considers 15 days as sustainable standard
items.quote: At present, I think this is the best working capital days we are managing. Going low below this, I think it's not very much practically possible now. So, this working capital days I think we can expect to be, we can make a standard to maintain this cycle now.

items.statement: Net debt to equity reduced to 0.11x; no bank debt in company; finance cost minimal
items.quote: With continued cash generation, we further reduced leverage, bringing net debt equity down to 0.11x, reinforcing our financial resilience ahead of upcoming capex.

items.statement: No bank debt available; power cost very low due to 65% renewable energy
items.quote: If you see, we don't have any bank debt available. Power is renewable. So, our power cost is very less. So, these are the advantages.

items.statement: Other income of 2.07 crores from bond investments and AIF equity investments due to reduced working capital cycle
items.quote: So, other income is from the investment in bonds so interest has been received from investment in bonds and this we are able to do because there is a reduction in the WC cycle so this we have invested in bond market and some investment was done in AIF so some income has been received from there.

items.statement: Product mix similar between FY25 and FY26; no significant change in premium SKU share

items.statement: Industry consolidation increases competition as fewer customers concentrate supplier focus

items.statement: No long-term debt, financial capability to fund future expansion from reserves if market need arises

items.statement: Large BRO order executed at aggressive pricing, impacting Q2 margins
items.quote: This was a very marquee project and given the size of the contract and such a large order volume, there was competitive pricing and AJAX felt that it's in its best interest that it contributes to the nation building and also forms a grip on these large orders. This was done at, let's say, far more aggressive pricing.

items.statement: H1 FY26 SLCM volume grew 20% YoY (2,300 units); ~5 pp boost from single 110-unit BRO order
items.quote: If you look at H1-to-H1, we went up by 20% SLCM. I'm talking about SLCM specifically, and 2,300 machines were sold. I mentioned that about 100 or 110 odd machines came from one single order, which obviously added about five percentage points to the growth.

items.statement: Large BRO order of 110+ SLCMs executed fully in Q2 FY26; no spillover to H2
items.quote: See, the large order was executed completely in Q2. There is no spillover which is expected in the second half of the year. It was for SLCMs and 110 plus machines were as part of quasi government authority tender.

items.statement: Smaller SLCM variant tested in beachhead market; initial distribution in 4-6 key markets planned for H2
items.quote: We now feel confident that look the product can be extended across at least four, five, six key markets in the country and we are preparing ground to make sure that we start initial distribution of some of these in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Non-SLCM focus on boom pumps, concrete pumps and batching plants; building customer connect and conversion
items.quote: As far as the non-SLCMs are concerned, I think our focus has been on pumps, which is both boom pumps and concrete pumps and on the other side in batching plants. We hope that we will continue in terms of building connect and also conversion with our customers across the country.

items.statement: Hosahalli fourth plant CWIP INR 35 cr; expect additional INR 10-15 cr in FY26; targeting H2 completion
items.quote: You will see that the CWIP is about INR 35 crores already. We expect another INR10 crores to 15 crores for the full year, for Hosahalli, which is the fourth plant. The rains have been a bit of a dampener in terms of progress, and we are still targeting H2 closure.

items.statement: CEV4 inventory entirely sold out before June 30, 2025 regulatory deadline
items.quote: The CEV4 inventory was entirely sold out before the regulatory deadline of the 30th of June 2025.

items.statement: Customer mix roughly one-third each: first-time buyers, rental companies, mid-size contractors; high repeat demand from existing base
items.quote: It is in the ratio of almost one-third each, in each of these categories. Lakshminarayanan: Got it. And the last… Shubhabrata Saha: We have a very large, because we've been the pioneer in this business, and we are happy to say that a lot of demand actually originates from there, because the people love the machines that they use, and because of the strong operating performance of the machine, as w

items.statement: Competitors engaged in unsustainable practices: excess CEV4 liquidation at substandard pricing/commercial terms
items.quote: Some of the other competition had a different take on it. They showed lot more CEV-4 and they were running against time. And the kind of pricing strategy they, and commercial strategy adopted to get these machines liquidated were not only, let's say, substandard from margin corridors or commercial acumen.

items.statement: Price premium vs competition ~3-5%; resale value premium 10-15%
items.quote: Now, if you go into that border, obviously, the differences will be quite substantial, right? But in general, I think we have consistently alluded that anywhere around 3% to 4%, 5% differential exists between what prices we sell and what price our competition sells at.

items.statement: Cash and investments ~INR 710 cr; liquid cash ~INR 35-37 cr; strong balance sheet maintained
items.quote: Cash balance in investments, we have about INR 710 crores and our liquid cash balance was about INR 35 crores, INR 37 crores.

items.statement: First fill rate (on-time in-pull) running 90-92%; dealer touchpoints expanding
items.quote: I have to say this that our on-time in-pull, which is called the first fill rate, is being tracked here almost on a day-to-day basis. So to that extent, we are running upwards of 90%-92%.

items.statement: GST rate cut on auto components has no impact (positive or negative) on business
items.quote: If only, sir. No impact to us, positive or negative. So, it's completely business as usual.

items.statement: Liquidity challenges at retail level seen as transient; expect improvement as year progresses
items.quote: The only negative surprise could be just the liquidity challenges which we are seeing on the retail, but that's transient and that should get better as we progress.

items.statement: Return on invested capital upwards of 40%; financial discipline and efficient capital allocation maintained
items.quote: Our return ratios continue to be resilient. Our return on invested capital is upwards of 40%. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue target lowered to INR825 crore from earlier INR860 crore due to tariff uncertainty and delayed dispatches
items.quote: As I said, I am now not that confident of achieving INR860 crore. We feel INR825 crore should be okay in case of INR825 crore, we have not included the additional revenue which will come from the acquisition of WesTech as well as from Penstock UK.

items.statement: FY26 PAT guidance range of INR75-85 crore despite H1 revenue of only INR293 crore
items.quote: However, it will still be in the range of INR75-85 crore, and I think we will still pos t relatively good results

items.statement: Long-term target of INR1000 crore revenue by FY27 with EBITDA 22-25% and PAT 10-14%
items.quote: Our target is to become a dominant player for such products in many markets in the world and at the same time maintain a good profitability, have EBITDA between 22-25% and PAT between 10-14% that is what we are aiming at.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at INR890 crore with strong pipeline of INR40-70 crore monthly
items.quote: Our consolidated order book, as I have already shown before is INR890, crore. You can see all the companies have a strong order book, Waterfront included.

items.statement: Gross margins compressed in H1 due to tariff impact on US exports, low-margin screw generator project (INR7-8 crore), and higher employee cost ratio
items.quote: On the gross profit and margin, though we have had growth, but margins as a percentage have come down. EBITDA, profit before tax and profit after tax, all have been hit hard because of the factors, which I have already stated before.

items.statement: Expect margin recovery in H2 as fixed costs absorbed over 1.8x revenue (INR530 crore vs INR293 crore in H1)
items.quote: In the second half, we are expecting to achieve INR530 crore, which is like 1.8 times of what we have achieved in the first half. That means that the fixed was being same, we would have lot of spill over towards the bottom line in the second half of the year.

items.statement: INR60-70 crore capex planned across India units (Unit 1,2,3) this year to support INR1000 crore revenue target
items.quote: In unit one, unit two and unit three together, we are going to invest close to INR60-70 crores in this year, so that we have capacity in house for production and achieve revenue of INR1000 crore.

items.statement: Houston plant expansion targeting USD4.5-5 million investment, construction start by April-May, commissioning by March 2027
items.quote: We expect to submit all for final approval of the city in January, and generally the approvals are received within two months. So, we should be in a position to start the construction activities by April-May and we shall commission the plant by March 27.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia plant planned with USD2-4 million investment, targeting establishment by mid-2027 for Middle East market access
items.quote: We are also planning to invest in a new plant in Saudi Arabia. This is still on the paper, but the decision has been taken. So we would be, opening up a company in Saudi Arabia to target the markets of Middle East, and we hope to establish this company by mid of 2027.

items.statement: Acquiring Penstocks (UK) Ltd for Midlands presence and framework agreements; acquisition expected to complete by December 2025
items.quote: We have already entered UK, but we will now like to strengthen the UK market. And for that we are acquiring another small company having 3-4 people, Penstocks (UK) Ltd.

items.statement: Acquiring WesTech for industrial process equipment business (INR55 crore revenue last year) with relaxed controls expected to boost growth; completion expected by December 2025
items.quote: In the same spirit we are acquiring WesTech. WesTech brings to us a new market, which is the industrial process equipment business. Wes Tech has very strong technology and the industrial process equipment business in hand of Wes Tech was around INR55 crores last year.

items.statement: Shivpad merger with Jash expected to complete by January 2026 pending NCLT procedural issues
items.quote: It is only procedurally some issues are left, and it is not because of us, but because of NCLT bench not being established. So, we expect by January 26 the merging of Shivpad will Jash to be completed.

items.statement: Global decision-making slowdown due to tariff uncertainty across countries, not just US-India; Vietnam order (INR10 crore) delayed due to World Bank funding issues
items.quote: There is a lot of unease due to the tariff not only at India but in many countries and so things have slowed down in many countries. We have equipment worth INR10 crore, nearly ready for last five months for Vietnam but it's not leaving because Vietnam is not taking World Bank loan.

items.statement: Perceptible slowdown in capital investment decisions globally due to tariff uncertainty; expects resolution in few months
items.quote: It is slow down. If you see, every country is troubled by the tariff and no one is safe from it. So, everyone is re-evaluating the decision on how to go for capital investments, what to invest, what not to invest.

items.statement: New orders being quoted with tariff factored in; old order book bears tariff cost (50% on some products) with no pass-through possible
items.quote: Since then, we have been costing our products to include tariffs, so that tariff does not hurt us in the new orders. On the old orders, there is nothing that we can do.

items.statement: Legal opinion suggests no duty on cast iron gates to US; INR20-30 crore of such exports potentially tariff-free; refund claim possible for past payments
items.quote: Our lawyers in USA have concluded that on the casta and products, there cannot be any duty. So, our casta and gate business, which was going from India to America there would be no duty on that.

items.statement: Chennai plant production commenced; team building ongoing, full contribution expected from April 2026
items.quote: We commence the production in Chennai. We are putting up a team in place, I think next few months would be spent putting the right team in place, and from April 26 onwards this plant would be able to contribute fully once the team is in place.

items.statement: Unit 5 (SEZ expansion) expected commissioning March-April 2026; adjoining Unit 4
items.quote: It is expected to be commissioned in March April. Unit five is expansion of unit four. A new plant adjoining unit four, but it is part of unit four.

items.statement: Export focus on gates, screens, knife gate valves; process equipment push post-WesTech acquisition; disc filters gaining traction (8-9 machines ordered)
items.quote: initial focus is on Gate, Screens and Knife gate valves for export market. Kunal: So, process equipment also since we will be having WesTech acquired. Pratik Patel: We have still not acquired. We are going to acquire it, and then we have to use their strength to see how we can push process equipment in the

items.statement: Target revenue mix: 35% India, 30% US, 15% Europe, 15-20% rest of world to reduce single-market dependence
items.quote: In time to come as I said, I want UK, which is within Europe and Africa, to grow more stronger and have something like 35% Indian business, 30% US, 15% from Europe, and 15-20% from rest of the world.

items.statement: BABA Act orders already being received for 3-4 years; not a new opportunity but ongoing
items.quote: BABA is not an issue, we are already getting orders for there. BABA is very old, its not new. We have been taking order for this BABA for last 3-4 years now.

items.statement: Saudi operations small scale (USD2-4 million); getting LCs and payments on initial orders; no working capital issues reported
items.quote: We are getting LC and payments so it's not an issue. Your experience, I don't know concerns which type of industry or product we have had no such issues about getting payments and working capital and things like that.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty (not tariff itself) causing global project delays and decision paralysis; expects policy consistency eventually
items.quote: The problem is not tariff the problem is uncertainty. No one knows what will happen tomorrow and so this uncertainty is not allowing people to take decision and move forward.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue target INR530 crore (1.8x H1) driven by historical Q3/Q4 seasonality (40-45% in Q4) and order book visibility
items.quote: If you see last five years, it has been the same pattern the Q1 is around 12-15%, Q2 is around 20%, Q3 is around 25% and last quarter is around 40-45%. It's not something new.

items.statement: Targets triple-digit revenue by FY27-28 with 50-50 nuts/ice cream split
items.quote: We envision a strong growth runway ahead with a clear roadmap to achieve triple-digit revenue growth by FY '27-'28.

items.statement: Ice cream plant to reach 100% utilization by March 2028
items.quote: By March '28 we will be 100% utilization of the ice cream segment.

items.statement: Ice cream PAT contribution to match nuts by FY27-28
items.quote: FY '26-'27-'28 the PAT contribution will be equal from ice cream and nuts.

items.statement: Expanding nut facility by 2 lakh sq ft adding 30 MT/day in two phases over next two years
items.quote: this facility with new two lakh square foot facility coming up on Company's own five acre land parcel just adjacent to the existing plant which will add 30 metric ton per day capacity in two phases and this will lead to total capacity increase 40 metric ton per day. This will happen over the period of next two

items.statement: Nut processing capacity to quadruple from 10 to 40 MT/day over next three financial years
items.quote: As I mentioned, we are developing two lakh square foot plant and expanding capacity from 10 metric ton per day existing to 40 metric ton per day capacity over the period of next three financial years, coming financial years.

items.statement: Ice cream plant at 1 lakh litre/day currently 25% utilized in H1 FY26
items.quote: In ice cream current capacity of the plant is one lakh liter per day production of the ice cream and current capacity utilization is almost 25% we can say current, first half of the financial year.

items.statement: Singapore export revenue expected >1M SGD this year, targeting 5x growth
items.quote: So, almost current financial year we expect almost more than 1 million Singapore dollar as a revenue from export over there and which will next couple of years we are we are thinking of increasing it for almost five fold.

items.statement: Singapore exports yield 5% extra margin vs India, room to reach 10-15%
items.quote: Singapore export gives us almost 5% extra margin. India the margins which we are getting is a pretty good margin, India. And Singapore adds 5% to that margin. But in Singapore there is a room for expanding this margin, we can take it to 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Nuts segment contributes ~90-95% of PAT currently; ice cream PAT positive but not substantial
items.quote: If you see as of now last financial year and first half of current financial year at PAT level there is a 100% contribution, almost 95% it PAT is coming from nut segment, right? Till this first half.

items.statement: Passed 100% of GST cut benefit to consumers (nuts 12% to 5%, ice cream 18% to 5%)
items.quote: So, obviously customers are getting the same product at a lesser cost and we have ensured across both the segment to pass on the benefit 100% to

items.statement: GST cut to 5% will drive organized play and market expansion in ice cream
items.quote: Now at the GST rate has come to 5% the organized players will have a larger opportunity to grow the market. So, next couple of years will be a very crucial period for Melt N Mellow to expand the market and expand the capacity and the GST rate cut is a very important tailwind is a very important fo rce multiplier for expansion of the ice cream

items.statement: Nuts B2C sales: 5-8% from e-commerce/quick commerce, rest from 100+ Tier-2/3/4 towns
items.quote: As far as e-commerce, quick commerce are considered almost 5% to 8% sale comes from e-commerce and quick commerce.

items.statement: Ice cream sold through 25,000 retail touchpoints, 200+ distributors, 25+ super stockists across 4 states
items.quote: Meanwhile, in Melt N Mellow ice cream, products are available through 25,000 retail touch points and these are supported by 200 plus distributors and 25 plus super stockis ts across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Goa and Telangana

items.statement: Ice cream to launch on online channels by March 2026
items.quote: Ice cream is as of now not available on online channels, it will be available by March 2026.

items.statement: Launched Kaju Katli 4 months ago, full-scale rollout next calendar year
items.quote: So, in that segment, we have launched Kaju Katli four months before and we did its testing in pilot sale in Diwali also we got good response. So, in Kaju Katli we are going a full throttle in next calendar year.

items.statement: Nuts: 90% imported raw nuts from 9 countries; milk prices fluctuate seasonally but secured supply at competitive rates
items.quote: No, in nuts almost 90% is import like pistachios from USA, almonds from USA and Australia and cashew nuts from West Africa, East Africa, Cambodia like that almost 90% is from import.

items.statement: Milk procurement secured at competitive prices through scale leverage despite seasonal fluctuations
items.quote: Prices fluctuates but if we have , if one has a assured supply line , right, supplier arrangements then you can have if market rate is 100 you can get it at 100 minus x that is possible so that leverage comes for the if you have consistent procurement and procurement at s cale so that we are leveraging

items.statement: Export focus on Singapore (300+ outlets), Japan, and USA pending tariff clarity
items.quote: Regarding the expanding export to other territories we will be focusing on Japan. We are working on the on Japan, making our product available in Japan and also we are waiting for dust to settle for US tariffs.

items.statement: Rights issue planned, in-principle application to exchanges in December 2025
items.quote: Yes, so right issue we are contemplating and in the month of December we are thinking of applying to in principle application to exchanges.

items.statement: Two CEOs: Nana Mhaske (nuts division) and Abhishek Purani (ice cream division)
items.quote: I thank our CEO nuts division Mr. Nana Mhaske and CEO ice cream division, Melt N Mellow division Mr. Abhishek Purani for participating in this call along with me.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue Rs 66.67 crore (+50% YoY), EBITDA Rs 9.65 crore (+26%), PAT Rs 5.8 crore (+17%)
items.quote: In quarter 2 of FY'26, Krishival Foods delivered a strong momentum. The revenue stood at Rs. 66.67 crore up 50% year-on-year driven by sustained growth across both business segments. EBITDA improved to Rs. 9.65 crore which is 26% up reflecting operating leverage as we scale. And PAT rose to Rs. 5.8 crore which is 17% up.

items.statement: H1 FY26 total income Rs 120.71 crore (+60% YoY), PAT Rs 10.20 crore (+23%)
items.quote: Looking at the first half of FY '26, performance remains equally strong. Total income stood at Rs. 120.71 crore up 60% year-on-year while PAT grew 23% to Rs. 10.20 crore.

items.statement: Nuts segment Q2 revenue Rs 53 crore (+20% YoY); Ice cream Q2 revenue Rs 13.62 crore
items.quote: Breaking it down, the Krishival Nuts segment contributed Rs. 53 crore in revenue which is 20% up year -on-year led by wider distribution, new product launches, and strong festive demand. EBITDA also improved due to higher volumes and disciplined cost control. Meanwhile, Melt N Mellow contributed Rs. 13.62 crore in Quarter 2 of FY'25 underscoring the success of brand building and

items.statement: GST reduced to 5% for nuts (from 12%) and ice cream (from 18%), fully passed to consumers
items.quote: In the nuts segment for major majority of nuts like pistachios, almond, flavored nuts the rates were 12% those have been brought to 5%. In the ice cream the rates were 18% those have been brought to 5%.

items.statement: US export expansion waiting for tariff clarity after pilot $5,000 shipment in April
items.quote: We are waiting for some rate clarity to come fortunately today only some good news is coming on certain food products rates have been brought to the earlier level so once US rate this confusion settles then we are very confident on going full throttle in USA.

items.statement: Promoter stake at 37%, will maintain or increase via rights issue participation
items.quote: Promoter stake is at 37%. The reason is simple as we grow the Company initially so as in the growing company equity getting debt for the financing had certain limits, so in that process the proportion of promoter equity has reduced but going forward we are working on maintaining the same like in rights issue also promoters will participate to maintain their these shareholdings.

items.statement: No plans for large-scale retail outlets or franchise model; asset-light distribution approach
items.quote: But as far as physical retail expansion we don't have any bigger plan. So, we will follow asset light approach for distribution so that focus remains on ensuring the production of quality products and distributing it through physical distribution or through online distribution but having retail outlets at a scale is not in our pipeline.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 50-60% with medium-term CAGR 30-35%
items.quote: For financial '26, we are targeting revenue growth in the range of 50% to 60% with a medium-term goal of maintaining a CAGR of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 operating EBITDA margin target 25.5-26%
items.quote: We believe we should end Q3 with an operating EBITDA margin in the range of 25.5% to 26%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA margin target 26.25-26.75%
items.quote: And Q4 with an operating EBITDA margin in the range of 26.25% to 26.75%.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin target 17.5-19%
items.quote: We expect PAT margins to be in the range of 17.5% to 19%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 operating EBITDA margin 23.7%, down 3.68% QoQ due to 7.5% tender price drop and one-time items
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 24.7% and our operating EBITDA margin stood at 23.7%, reflecting a quarter-on-quarter decline of 3.68%.

items.statement: One-time items caused 1.8% operating EBITDA margin decline, expected to recover in Q3 FY26
items.quote: These factors together caused an estimated 1.8% decline in operating EBITDA margins, which we expect to recover in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Backward integration and value engineering projects to add 1% operating profitability from Q4 FY26
items.quote: we are progressing toward the completion of several key backward integration and value engineering projects, which will positively impact our operating profitability by another 1% from quarter 4 FY '26.

items.statement: Order book exceeds 18,800 pumps with near-term pipeline of over 30,000 pumps across major states
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have a strong order book exceeding 18,800 pumps consisting of direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM and export orders, and a near-term pipeline of over 30,000 pumps across major states including Maharashtra, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Solar module expansion project shifted to adjacent 28,000 sqm land parcel leased for 15 years, phased execution commenced, no timeline impact
items.quote: Separately, we proposed shifting the solar module expansion project to a land parcel located adjacent to our existing plant. This proposed change is driven by several practical and strategic considerations as outlined below.

items.statement: Target 5 lakh pumps capacity by H1 FY27, currently at 2 lakh, solar module 0.75 MW operational this FY and 0.75 MW next FY
items.quote: we will achieve this capacity up to 5 lakh by H1 '27. And this capacity is achieved so that the visibility that we are getting in FY '27, '28, '29, we do not miss any portion due to our capabilities and capacity.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 2 guidelines received, expected launch by January, industry and government bullish on aggressive volumes
items.quote: regarding KUSUM 2, we have received a guideline from the government and MNRE. There has been a discussion that in the month of Jan is expected to come and in KUSUM 2, all of us, the entire industry is very bullish.

items.statement: Tender prices fell 7.5% on average impacting 80% of core revenue; value engineering mitigated 2.85% margin impact
items.quote: The primary reason was the L1 price in PM KUSUM and Magel Tyala tenders, which fell by an average of 7.5%, impacting the margin of over 80% of our core revenue.

items.statement: Receivable days increased to 138 from 126 due to extended monsoon delaying RMS data and Magel Tyala bank loan disbursement delays, expected to improve in Q3
items.quote: Our receivable days stood at 138 days as of September 2025, compared to 126 days at the end of June 2025. This increase was primarily driven by two reasons.

items.statement: Net debt position INR38 crores at quarter end; IPO proceeds INR842 crores, INR478 crores deployed; no extra borrowing expected due to cash generation
items.quote: So, we reported a net debt position of INR38 crores as on quarter end.

items.statement: Executed 48,000 total pumps in Q2 FY26 (23,000 solar, 25,000 non-solar); Q1 FY26 51,000 total pumps
items.quote: In quarter 2, we have supplied 48,000 pumps. And, in quarter 1, we have supplied 51,000 pumps. Both solar and non-solar.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix 70-75% solar pumps, 20-25% non-solar pumps
items.quote: See, in FY '25, if we see, 70%-75% of our revenue is from solar pumps and 20%-25% is from non-solar pumps.

items.statement: Aggressively expanding private network, export market and non-government channels; significant increment expected in FY27
items.quote: Definitely in the coming time, you will see that our private network, export market and other than government network, you will see a lot of increment in FY '27.

items.statement: State tenders attracting more EPC players causing price pressure; strong backward integration provides entry barrier and margin protection
items.quote: if more and more participants come, our execution will be at a higher level, and our farmers will benefit more. So, that was the primary reason.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 1 scheme stops by March 2025; state governments running localized tenders under central norms with 30% central subsidy
items.quote: till 31st March '25, till this calendar year, the total scheme of PM KUSUM 1 will be stopped by the government. It will not be continued. This is clear.

items.statement: Export orders part of 18,800 pump order book; export pump average value INR 10,000-20,000
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have a strong order book exceeding 18,800 pumps consisting of direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM and export orders

items.statement: Solar pump realization and margins better than non-solar; backward integration covers both solar and non-solar pumps
items.quote: Definitely, today, I'll say that the complete set of solar that we supply to the government, definitely, our realization is better in that. And definitely, for many years, for the past few years, we have worked a lot on solar, and we have worked on solar backward integration, we have worked on solar technology. So, the margin of our Oswal's is comparatively more than that of non-solar pumps.

items.statement: Raw material prices increasing but value engineering minimizing impact; further raw material price increases expected
items.quote: the prices of raw materials are also increasing and the prices of tenders are also decreasing. But, as we have said, our team has worked a lot on value engineering and is still working.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 2 delay would impact entire solar cell industry and DCR cell demand; government committed to aggressive launch
items.quote: PM KUSUM getting delayed due to any reason means that the entire solar cell industry is put in uncertainty. That's the number one point.

items.statement: Indian aviation passenger traffic expected to grow at 8-9% CAGR over next decade driven by structural factors
items.quote: Over the next decade, passenger traffic is expected to grow at a CAGR of 8% to 9% in India.

items.statement: Passenger traffic temporarily impacted in H1 FY26 by India-Pakistan conflict and Air India crash leading to reduced flight schedules
items.quote: While the long-term industry growth drivers remain intact, passenger traffic during the first half of the current financial year was temporarily impacted by two major external events, the India-Pakistan conflict in May and reduced flight schedules that were implemented for maintenance and safety reasons, following the unfortunate Air India airplane crash in June of this year.

items.statement: Passenger traffic showing recovery signs from end of September with improving week-on-week trend
items.quote: Encouragingly, passenger traffic has shown signs of recovery in the past few weeks, and this recovery trend reaffirms the underlying strength of India's aviation sector and its strong demand fundamentals.

items.statement: System-wide sales grew 18.4% YoY in Q2 FY26 to INR 7.3 billion driven by 9.2% LFL growth and 9.3% net contract gains
items.quote: Against this challenging backdrop, TFS has performed well and delivered a strong quarter with system-wide sales of INR 7.3 billion and PAT of INR 979 million, which equates to growth of 18.4% Y-o-Y in system-wide sales and 15.3 % growth in consolidated PAT on a comparable basis, after adjusting for last year's deconsolidation of the Semolina business.

items.statement: H1 FY26 system-wide sales grew 22.4% YoY with 10.4% LFL growth and 10.0% net contract gains
items.quote: For the first half, system-wide sales growth was 22.4%, supported by like-for-like sales growth of 10.4% and net contract gains of 10.0%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated PAT grew 17.2% YoY on adjusted basis
items.quote: Additionally, consolidated PAT has grown by 17.2% year-on-year in the first half , on an adjusted basis.

items.statement: Operating over 500 travel QSR outlets and lounges system-wide; mobilized 50 QSR outlets and 4 lounges in last 12 months
items.quote: TFS is now operating over 500 travel QSR outlets and lounges at a system-wide level, thereby reinforcing our leadership position in the sector. We mobilized 50 travel QSR outlets and four lounges in the last 12 months, and our joint ventures are progressing well, with timely mobilization of new units and steady progress on execution.

items.statement: Brand portfolio expanded to 135 brands system-wide with 16 new brands added in last year including Gordon Ramsay Street Burger
items.quote: Our brand portfolio as well has expanded to 135 brands as of September 25 at a system-wide level, after the addition of 16 exciting new brands in the last one year. For example, in August, we launched India's first outlet of Gordon Ramsay Street Burger at Delhi Terminal 1, which received a very positive response from traveler s and great coverage on social media.

items.statement: Secured contract for 11 travel QSR outlets and 1 lounge at Cochin International Airport; started 14 travel QSR units at Delhi IGI Terminal 2
items.quote: We also secured two new contracts, one to operate 11 travel QSR outlets and 1 lounge at the domestic terminal of Cochin International Airport, which is the 8th busiest airport in India. With this importantly, we will expand our presence to 14 of the top 15 airports in India. Second , is the recently reopened Delhi IGI Airport Terminal 2, where we have started operating 14 travel QSR units as well.

items.statement: Noida and Navi Mumbai International Airport units ready for phased opening; Cochin units going live from January
items.quote: We're also looking forward to commencing the travel QSR and lounge operations and the recently won F&B concessions that I mentioned, as well as at the Noida and Navi Mumbai International Airports, which are expected to open soon.

items.statement: Gross margin typically in 80-82% range impacted by product mix and new concepts; managed costs at optimum level without compromising customer experience

items.statement: EBITDA margin to remain range-bound as new units take 12-18 months to reach efficiency levels of mature business
items.quote: So, our EBITDA margin will remain in a range -bound manner, because as we bring in new concepts and mobilization of units, and which is part of our industry, it typically takes us 12 to 18 months to bring the new mobilized units to the same level of efficiency as the rest of the business.

items.statement: Price hikes typically pass on inflation to consumers at 2-4% range for H1 FY26
items.quote: So, Nihal, the element of price hike, typically we tend to only pass on the inflation to the consumers. So, roughly, it would be in the range for the first half of the year to be around 2% to 4%,, which would be the price hike which would have been passed on.

items.statement: Balance sheet strong with zero debt; cash balance grew by INR 1.2 billion from INR 6.3 billion in March 2025 to INR 7.5 billion in September 2025
items.quote: Our balance sheet is strong with zero debt. Cash balance has grown by INR1.2 billion from INR6.3 billion in March 2025 to end at INR7.5 billion as on 30th September 25.

items.statement: LFL growth driven by improving penetration and upselling through new brands, concepts like 5-minute quick commerce menu, and lounge marketing activities
items.quote: In terms of LFL growth, yes, while it was a weak quarter in terms of the passenger growth, our endeavor always is to work on a couple of factors.
