items.quote: Additionally, at our lounges, we enable the technology platform to provide direct integration to banks and card networks for a smooth lounge access for their customers through our wholly owned subsidiary, Elite Assist Technology and Services. We have alrea dy entered strategic partnerships with multiple partners for this lounge access solution and more collaborations are underway.

items.statement: Joint venture model with Adani Airports (roughly 120 units) mitigates risk of vertical integration; long-term contracts and shared expertise create strong partnership
items.quote: The slight difference, probably to that as well is, many of these units we do run through joint ventures. We already are in a joint venture with Adani Airports. By doing that, our skill set in terms of operators, a lot of their learning, their expertise as airport operators, they run multiple airports, and very strong teams there. So, that skill set coming together is what creates , that's why you

items.statement: Delhi Terminal 3 contract up for renewal this financial year; other renewals listed in DRHP
items.quote: The one in this financial year is the Delhi Terminal 3 contract, that does come up for renewal for us.

items.statement: Revenue mix of 54% partner brands and 46% in-house brands not a strategic target; focus on optimal basket delivering best IRR and sales
items.quote: So, internally, there'll never be a target, say, let's do more percentage of in-house or more percentage of third-party brands. It's always that let's do a basket that ultimately delivers the best IRR for us, and ultimately that's linked to the most sales, logically to drive.

items.statement: New units target required IRR and ROCE; payback in set number of years but 12-18 months to reach mature efficiency levels
items.quote: Nonetheless, what we do try to do is that we get a certain payback in a set number of years, in the early start of the contract. But it typically takes us 12 to 18 months to get those units mobilized and operate at the same level of efficiency as the rest of our business.

items.statement: Highway expansion opportunity with government planning 1,000 wayside amenities over next few years; TFS sees this as long-term opportunity leveraging multi-brand F&B hub capabilities
items.quote: The government has particularly called it a 1000 wayside amenities over the next few years, which would be access control F&B areas. And we see that playing to our strength, where we can actually go in, multi-brand, build out, fuel, non-fuel retail, play that opportunity.

items.statement: Delhi Terminal 2 contract is short-term (3 years) concession model unlike JV with GMR at Terminal 3; reopened due to transition needs
items.quote: Delhi Terminal 2, currently, which is opened in terms of the contract as well that we're doing there, is a short-term contract. So, what we do operate, the joint venture with GM R, GHL, that does operate in other markets as well. But this particular contract is a short-term contract, which we have for three years.

items.statement: Technology subsidiary Elite Assist (EATS) rolling out lounge access management solution with bank/card network integration; too preliminary for quantification
items.quote: So, EATS is actually rolling out technology solutions for our various business lines. So the first initiative is the lounge access management solution which we've done, which is actually, we've enabled the technology platform, which gives direct integration for banks and card networks for lounge access to their customers.

items.statement: Loyalty programs include senior citizen, student, and family lounge packages; deeper loyalty strategy in development for frequent flyers
items.quote: So, for example, we have, I'll give you one example. We have lounge packages , which are discounted or special for senior citizens. We have a student package. We even have a family package. We have young kids going to a lounge. Not everyone may be traveling business class or they don't have a car d. So there's a way we actually allow them at a discounted as a family package.

items.statement: Targets FY28 revenue of Rs 1,050-1,100 crore and EBITDA margin of 16-18% at company level
items.quote: our eventual goal post is in FY '28, at the company level, we are going to be in the range of about Rs. 1,050-Rs. 1,100 crores at the EBITDA of about 16%-18%.

items.statement: Dahej Phase-II project investment of around Rs 250 crore funded through internal accruals and debt
items.quote: the Dahej project represents an investment of around Rs. 250 crores funded through a combination of internal accruals and debt.

items.statement: Phase-II at Dahej adding 10,829 MTPA capacity to be commissioned by November 30, taking total capacity to over 16,000 MTPA
items.quote: The Phase-II of our new plant at Dahej will be commissioned by the end of November with an additional capacity, as mentioned earlier, at 10,829.

items.statement: Cooling Agents capacity of 500 MTPA at Dahej Phase-II, production starting November 30
items.quote: It will house India's largest Cooling Agent's unit capacity of over 500 metric tons per annum, along with dedicated lines of Phenol derivatives and Citral derivatives.

items.statement: US tariff impact caused customers to defer orders and use inventory; demand expected to return around Q4 FY26
items.quote: we do see this demand regardless to come back about Q4.

items.statement: GST rate changes caused domestic customers to reassess blends and delay purchases; pent-up demand expected back around Q4 FY26
items.quote: there has been some degree of pent-up demand officially coming back around Q4.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 3.4% due to lower Mint realizations, high raw material cost, unfavorable mix, higher expenses and inventory adjustments
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 3 crores, reflecting an EBITDA margin of 3.4%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.1%; depreciation increased to Rs 4.8 crore from Rs 3.5 crore YoY due to Krystal asset capitalization
items.quote: EBITDA for the period was Rs. 17.9 crore with an EBITDA margin of 10.1%.

items.statement: Menthol prices down ~10% YoY; company plans to forward integrate Menthol into Cooling Agents to control value chain
items.quote: the prices have come down from last year by about 10% or so in the actual gross value of that particular product.

items.statement: Able to pass on large part of raw material volatility to customers under normal scenarios; inventory holding model manages costing
items.quote: we were able to pass on a large part of the RM volatility to our customer given the normal business scenario.

items.statement: Mint portfolio was 70% of FY25 revenue; fast-tracking value-added specialty products from FY27-28 pipeline to FY27 to replace Mint revenue
items.quote: we had about 70% for total revenue in FY '27 was the Mint portfolio. Aashish Upganlawar: Right. Yash Parekh: I am sorry, my apologies. 70% as of FY '25

items.statement: Phenol derivatives, Cooling Agents, Citral derivatives at Dahej Phase-II; BHA production fast-tracked from FY28 to FY27
items.quote: one of the examples of this would be, for example, there is a situation in the Phenol chemistry where BHA was effectively planned for FY '28, now for now. We have fast-tracked that and we are going to be starting that particular production in FY '27.

items.statement: Serve 269+ customers across 18 countries including leading F&F houses and major FMCG companies
items.quote: We now serve more than 269 customers across 18 countries, including several leading flavor and fragrance houses and major FMCG companies.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with multiple confectionary and pain management segment customers for Cooling Agents cross-selling
items.quote: There are advanced level discussions going on with multiple customers in this particular object.

items.statement: Repaid Rs 140 crore (Rs 97.4 cr long-term debt at Krystal + Rs 42.6 cr working capital borrowings); net debt/equity down to 0.3x from 0.8x
items.quote: The company repaid Rs. 140 crores split into Rs. 97.4 crores of long-term debt pertaining to Krystal Ingredients and an additional of Rs. 42.6 crores of working capital borrowings at G EM Aromatics.

items.statement: US imposed 50% tariff in late August; customers accepted pass-through but slowed demand, depleting inventory
items.quote: The 50% tariff imposed by US led many customers to defer orders utilizing their existing inventories, which impacted export volumes.

items.statement: GST Council changed rates Sept 2: Natural Menthol 5% (from 12%), Synthetic Menthol 18% (from 12%); customers reworking formulations
items.quote: On September 2nd, the GST Council announced the change in the GST rate, where Natural Mint and Menthol primarily was moved from 12% to 5%, and synthetic was moved into 18%.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility and new plant ramp-up create uncertainty; better visibility expected by Q4 FY27 for Krystal utilization
items.quote: as the situations are extremely volatile at a geopolitical level as well, plus this entire brand-new plant is coming up. So, as we completely streamline this particular plant over the next one quarter, I think there is going to be much better visibility towards Q4 for FY '27.

items.statement: Cash PAT Q2 FY26 Rs 0.5 crore; H1 FY26 Cash PAT Rs 10.3 crore
items.quote: Cash PAT for the first half was Rs. 10.3 crores.

items.statement: R&D center led by 13 scientists focusing on new molecules, yield improvement, green chemistry
items.quote: The center is led by a team of 13 scientists who focus upon developing new molecules, improving yields and advancing green chemistry processes.

items.statement: Krystal Ingredients eligible for 15% corporate tax rate and government incentives in perpetuity
items.quote: Krystal Ingredients is also eligible for a 15% corporate tax rate and government incentives, a benefit that continues in perpetuity and supports long-term profitability.

items.statement: Capex purchases of trailers and containers to start end of Q3 FY26 and complete within Q4 FY26
items.quote: And the purchase will start from end of Q3 FY26. And as per our plan, what we have initially communicated, it will start from end of Q3 FY26, which means, like, from December onwards consolidation is happening. And we will start releasing the POs and add the assets into the facility.

items.statement: INR 130 crore capex planned for trailers and containers, to be completed within Q4 FY26
items.quote: Now, we are going capex heavy as per you like it is like we are involving this INR 130 odd crores in capex, buying containers and trailers.

items.statement: Trailer purchases in tranches of 30-35 vehicles per PO starting December; 1,000 containers in 2-3 tranches
items.quote: So, trailers purchase, we will be having in fragmented way. So, which will start from end of Q3 FY26, which is like from December, and which will be in different tranches like 30-35 vehicles in one PO could be the numbers. And the other asset purchases like containers, 1,000 containers is what we are trying to do. That will be done in two or three tranches.

items.statement: Backward integration via trailers expected to add 15-20% to top line; container purchase to reduce vendor cost by 20-22% at EBITDA level
items.quote: With the trailer purchase, when we do this backward integration, we are focused, roughly around 15% to 20% from the top line, especially on this trailers. And container purchase, we will be reducing our vendor cost, especially close to 20%, 22% from the existing levels.

items.statement: TEUs handled in H1 FY26 were 47,032 vs 53,407 in H1 FY25; management expects FY26 to close with good incremental TEUs
items.quote: So, TEUs which we have handled is almost close to the numbers what we have been achieving from in the last year, compared with the last year. And we are positive ahead and we will close FY26 with good number, good incremental TEUs.

items.quote: The sea import contributed the largest share at 81% of the revenue in Q2 FY26. The air segment recorded meaningful traction, with the air import revenue increasing 17.3% year-on-year, taking its contribution to 2.11% in Q2 FY26 from 1.37% in Q2 FY25. And air export revenue more than doubled year-on-year in Q2 FY26 to INR 14.3 million, increasing its contribution to 0.66% from 0.22% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contributed 41% of Q2 revenue vs 39% in Q1, driven by higher wallet share and repeat assignments
items.quote: Revenue contribution from our top five customers increased to 41% in Q2 FY26, compared to 39% in Q1 FY26, driven by higher wallet share and a larger share of repeat assignments.

items.statement: Renewable energy sector accounted for 46% of Q2 revenue vs 43% in Q1; battery segment emerging as new opportunity
items.quote: From the industry vertical perspective, the renewable energy sector accounted for 46% of the revenue in Q2 FY26, compared to 43% in Q1 FY26. The sector continued to expand capacity in India and globally, and our long-term relations in this segment are enabling consistent business.

items.statement: Diversification push into automobile, fashion, and pharma verticals to grow top line in coming quarters

So, automobile is one of the vertical, which we are trying to, we already do, but we are trying to enhance this portion of automobile spread. And we are also trying to push more on like this fashion and we are also trying to push more on the pharma sectors.

items.statement: Sales team expansion planned in West (Gujarat, Maharashtra) and New Delhi; hiring to start end of Q3 or early Q4 FY26
items.quote: And going forward we are just looking to improve the sales base in the West, especially in Gujarat, Maharashtra and New Delhi. These regions, the sales force will be implemented. I think the number of people, sales team, new sales team will come up in these regions. And we also expect much better number from these regions, sir.

items.statement: Export share increasing gradually; cross-selling to import customers to boost exports; major trade corridors include China, Vietnam, Malaysia, Europe, Thailand, North America

So, we are targeting, if you can see, in the last two years, the percentage of exports, ocean exports have increased a little bit. And we are very positive on targeting more of export customers going forward and majority of our inbound customers also do exports.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to customer base expansion and slight liberalization; expected to come down in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Not actually, but there is an increase in the trade receivables actually, but we are increasing the customer base. So, that is the one of the reason for increase in the credit terms. And we are also wanted to increase the customer base going forward. So, there is a little bit of liberalization, but at the same time, we are holding all the working capital, we are managing it properly and it is well

items.quote: So, this freight levels in Q2 has increased. So, that has given a higher level of top line, but if at all we had done 21,000 odd TEUs, the levels, the top line has increased because of the freight. The freight has increased for Q2. That is the reason.

items.statement: GST payment made following inspection for previous year based on department workings and company clarifications
items.quote: So, we got one inspection was going on for the previous year. And based on the workings and the detailed clarifications given by the department. So, we have made one payment, which is actually based on the workings given by both the department as well as our working based on that we have made that payment.

items.statement: Group company Glottis Shipping Private Limited handles liner agency business from Vietnam and Malaysia to India; relationship at arm's length; similar activities planned for Glottis Limited
items.quote: So, I'll just give you a heads up on the company, Glottis Shipping Private Limited, which is like, it is a liner agency business. So, we are handling agency business from Vietnam into India and from Malaysia into India. We handle vessels on behalf of the principal. So, that is the principal activity of that company. And for Glottis, we have been using some of their services also. And going forward

items.statement: GST rates reduced on batteries from 28% to 18% and solar combo packs from 12% to 5% effective 22nd September
items.quote: The GST rate on batteries were reduced from 28% to 18% effective 22nd September and for solar combo packs from 12% to 5%.

items.statement: Company passed on entire GST rate reduction benefit to end consumers
items.quote: The company is fully aligned to the government's goal of reducing burden to the end consumer, and we have passed on the entire benefit of GST rate reduction to the end consumer during this period.

items.statement: Nearly 88% of business grew ~7% in H1 FY26; aftermarket, automotive, solar and IUPS contributed to growth
items.quote: Nearly 88% of our business has grown by about 7%. Within this, aftermarket, automotive, solar and IUPS continue to contribute to the growth.

items.statement: Remaining 12% of business declined due to weaker demand in exports, e-rickshaw and telecom
items.quote: Remaining 12% of the business witnessed a decline in revenues, impacted by a weaker demand scenario, majorly in businesses like exports, last mile, which is the e-rickshaw business and our telecom business.

items.statement: Q1 grew 5%, Q2 degrew 2.1%, overall H1 modest 1.3% growth
items.quote: The company started the year on a strong note with Q1 registering about 5% growth, but showed a 2.1% degrowth in Q2, overall resulting in a modest 1.3% growth during H1.

items.statement: Distributors and retailers destocked and postponed buying after GST rate cut announcement on 15th August
items.quote: However, we suddenly saw a shift in momentum once the GST rate cuts were announced on 15th of August. Our distributors and retailers started destocking and postponed their buying in anticipation of receiving new stocks with updated prices.

items.statement: Company took production cuts in August and September to manage cash and reduce inventory
items.quote: The company took production cuts in August and September, the second half of August and the full of September with focus on cash management.

items.statement: Efficient working capital management generated incremental cash flow of INR 500 crores plus by end of September
items.quote: However, it helped us to reduce our inventory to a large extent, and therefore, we generated an incremental cash flow of INR 500 crores plus by efficient working capital management.

items.statement: Input material cost pressure continues; company yet to fully pass on input cost inflation to market
items.quote: Operating profitability was also impacted due to continuous pressure on input material cost. The company is yet to fully pass on the input material price impact to the market.

items.statement: Price corrections paused after GST announcement to pass full benefit to customers; may resume in Q4
items.quote: However, once the GST rate cut was announced, we decided that we will put a stop to our price correction of the market because that sends a wrong signal to the market, we wanted to pass on the entire benefit to the customer.

items.statement: Operational improvement initiatives on cost excellence and manufacturing technology upgrade showing results; full potential in coming quarters
items.quote: On the operational front, the various operational improvement initiatives on cost excellence and manufacturing technology upgrade that we had taken up and we have been informing to you since last 2 quarters, are showing results.

items.statement: Substantial part of 2-wheeler battery production moved to Punched Grid Technology; full motorcycle capacity to move by end of December
items.quote: For example, we have moved a substantial part of our 2-wheeler battery production to Punched Grid Technology. All such initiatives have started delivering results and its full potential will be realized in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Domestic auto replacement demand robust in H1; auto OEM demand expected to see uptick in Q3
items.quote: Domestic auto replacement demand was robust in H1, and auto OEM demand is expected to see uptick in Q3 as well.

items.statement: Industrial UPS and solar witnessed decent growth; solar declined in Q2 but strong rebound expected in Q3 with GST cuts and PM Surya Ghar incentives
items.quote: Industrial UPS and solar witnessed decent growth in demand, though there was a decline in Q2 for solar, but with the GST cuts and GST being brought to 5% and with PM Surya Ghar incentives that are in place, we believe there would be a strong rebound in Q3.

items.statement: Home UPS remained soft due to extended monsoon and GST rate cut announcement; solar, home UPS and industrial UPS are aspirational purchases
items.quote: Home UPS remained soft due to an extended monsoon season until August in this year. And home UPS has a double whammy impact because of the extended monsoon and then the GST rate cut announcement. So 3 businesses, solar, home UPS and industrial UPS, these are aspirational in nature.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainties heavily impacted export business for second consecutive quarter; expect similar trend until geopolitical tensions subside
items.quote: Tariff uncertainties have heavily impacted the export business for the second consecutive quarter, as you know. We expect the situation to continue in similar trend until geopolitical tensions subside.

items.statement: New geographies and portfolios identified; expect export uptick from Q4 (January) and steady state in Q1 next year
items.quote: And Q4 onwards, we will report you again, an uptick in the export business because we have found out additional markets, additional portfolios. The trials are over. So from Q4 onwards, we hope that from January onwards, we'll again see a marginal tick -- positive tick on exports and thereby we'll reach a steady state in Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Outlook for lead acid business positive across most verticals in H2 FY26 due to expected auto OEM demand uptick from GST reduction
items.quote: As we enter second half of FY '26, the outlook for the lead acid business remains positive across most business verticals due to expected uptick in auto OEM demand due to GST reduction.

items.statement: October retail data shows passenger vehicle growth 11% vs H1 4%; 2-wheeler retail sales growth 52% indicating destocking and primary production pickup in Q3
items.quote: Just to give you some color, the retail data for October, a typical growth scenario for a passenger vehicle was -- October was 11% against the H1 growth of 4%. And accordingly, the primary production numbers have also increased as published by SIAM recently for October.

items.statement: Invested INR 580 crores in H1 FY26 and INR 65 crores in October in lithium-ion cell manufacturing; total equity investment in Exide Energy stands at INR 3,947 crores
items.quote: We have invested about INR580 crores in H1 in FY '26 and further INR65 crores, we have already invested in the month of October. With this, the total equity investments made into Exide Energy, which is our 100% subsidiary, till date stands at INR3,947 crores.

items.statement: Equipment installation and commissioning nearing completion; expect to start production towards end of FY26; process validation and sample preparation underway
items.quote: Equipment installation and commissioning works in Exide Energy is nearing completion. The company expects to start production towards the end of FY '26. At this moment, we are going through process validation and sample preparation for some of our customers.

items.statement: Engaging with various OEMs of 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler, 4-wheeler and stationary energy providers across key end customer markets
items.quote: And we are also meanwhile, engaging with various OEMs of 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler, 4-wheeler as well as stationary energy providers across key end customer markets.

items.statement: First lithium-ion line (NCM cylindrical) for 2-wheeler OEMs; preparing samples for two large 2-wheeler OEMs; second line (LFP prismatic) for stationary applications
items.quote: So as we mentioned earlier also Vibhav, that we will be starting with our first line, which is basically for 2-wheeler application. This is the NCM line, with cylindrical cells, which we will be commissioning first. And we are talking to large OEMs for the offtake already.

items.statement: Lithium-ion margins targeted similar to current lead acid margins at steady state (80-90% utilization); focus now on utilization ramp-up to 60-80%
items.quote: But if you look at global benchmarks, that's the only benchmark available. In India, we do not have an industry benchmark on this. But if you look at global benchmark, I think on a steady-state level, the margins will still be similar to our current lead acid margins. That's our aim.

items.statement: Lithium-ion cell pricing will be mix of import parity and cost-plus; expect OEMs to value Make in India cells over Chinese imports
items.quote: pricing of the cells, obviously, will be a mix of both, depending on how we end up into negotiation with the customers. Of course, we expect that the customer to give value to Make in India cells over import Chinese cells.

items.statement: Lead acid margins expected to demonstrate plus 12% to plus 13% corridor in coming quarters once volume growth returns, assuming lead prices stable
items.quote: Going forward, we still feel that in coming quarters, though we do not give a guidance, but I feel we will be substantially able to demonstrate our margins, plus 12% to plus 13%. That's the corridor what we are looking at.

items.statement: China export restrictions on rare earth magnets, equipment and raw materials; equipment and know-how already received; raw material restriction delayed to November 2026; suppliers expect manageable impact
items.quote: On the third, raw material, as you know, they have already announced, they have relaxed -- delayed the import restriction by 1 year, to November '26. So until November '26, we should not worry.

items.statement: Battery waste management regulations (EPR) compliance required; accruals made in Q2; will become regular cost; aim to pass on cost via premium for 100% recycled product
items.quote: You know, we had to comply with the new battery waste management regulations, which was not there last year or the year before last. And yes, we had made accruals to fulfill the obligations in quarter 2.

items.statement: Lithium-ion Phase 1 (6 GWh) focus; land and utilities for 12 GWh; Phase 2 investment much lesser than Phase 1; will decide after seeing faster adoption in 1-2 years
items.quote: The land which we have purchased, we have purchased for 12-gigawatt hour. The utilities, what we have invested is for 12 gigawatt hours. Only the shed and machine we have installed for 6-gigawatt hour. So we can very quickly ramp up at much lesser cost, means the Phase 2 investment will not be same as Phase 1 investment.

items.statement: Solar business ramped up to ~INR 800 crores last year; plans to cross INR 1,000 crores this year; target INR 1,500 crores in 2-3 years driven by PM Surya Ghar, channel network and GST reduction
items.quote: I think last year, they reached about INR800 crores very quickly. And this year, they have plans to cross INR 1,000 crores. So we are really looking forward that 2 to 3 years' time, we wan t to make this franchise about INR 1,500 crores

items.statement: Lithium-ion not prioritized for solar currently; lead acid preferred for solar backup due to footprint and fast charging less relevant; lithium-ion focus on EV OEM segment
items.quote: For solar installation, unfortunately, footprint is for battery is not so much of an issue because footprint is decided by solar panels, not by batteries. You see what I mean? And also, since it's a backup power application, the fast charging is not as relevant as possibly EV.

items.statement: Aftermarket replacement growth strong double-digit in Q2 (4-wheeler and 2-wheeler ~10-11%); H1 growth 12% and 11% respectively; OEM growth expected robust in H2
items.quote: In the replacement market, Kapil, our growth for subsequent two quarters were all strong double-digit. In 4-wheeler, we are still double-digit. This must be news to you. But as I see the numbers in front of me, both 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler at around 10% to 11% in Q2.

items.statement: Manufacturing technology upgrades (Punched Grid, continuous casting) and automation initiatives delivering cost savings, quality improvement and operating leverage; full motorcycle capacity to Punched Grid by end of December
items.quote: I think we have gone public by announcing -- I think it's still there in the annual report as well that we have invested half of our motorcycle capacity to Punched Grid and the balance half is being invested this year, which means by end of December calendar year, our full motorcycle manufacturing will move to Punched Grid technology.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers EBIT margin sustainable range 35% to 40%
items.quote: It should be in the same region, 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand growth for polyester film driven by EPR and GST reduction
items.quote: The demand growth is actually very strong for polyester film in the domestic industry. And like Vaibhav mentioned a few questions ago, because of the imposition of the requirement of use of PCR content in film, there is a shift from other substrates to pol yester film, which is further fueling demand growth for polyester

items.statement: Polyester Films spread compressed to INR19-20/kg in Q2, improved to INR22-23/kg currently
items.quote: So in the September quarter, the value addition, the difference between selling price and raw material cost was about INR19 to INR20 a kg. In the month of October, it improved marginally to INR22. And currently, we are in the range of about INR22 to

items.statement: Specialty Polymers EBIT margin expanded 146 bps to 37.03% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: EBIT increased 45% year -on-year to INR21.24 crores, with margins improving by 146 basis points to 37.03%.

items.statement: Multiyear offtake agreements secured with Nike, Taro Plast, and Hyosung TNC for ELITe recycled polyester
items.quote: A multiyear offtake agreement has been secured with Nike, making it the anchor customer for the Infinite Loop India facility. Under this agreement, ELITe will supply to Nike TWIST TM, Loop's branded virgin quality sustainable polyester resin made exclusively from textile waste, featuring full traceability through Loop's proprietary chemical tracer technology.

items.statement: ELITe chemical recycling project capex INR1,600 crores, equity INR500-600 crores, debt INR1,000-1,100 crores
items.quote: Loop project, yes, the ELITe. So that is a project of about INR1,600 crores capex. It is going to be implemented by Ester Loop Infinite Technologies, which is a 50-50 joint venture company between Ester and Loop. And it's going to be funded by about INR500 crores to INR600 crores of equity and the balance INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores of debt.

items.statement: rPET capacity of 20,000 metric tons per annum commissioned in September 2025 at Hyderabad plant
items.quote: We are pleased to report that the rPET capacity of 20,000 metric ton s per annum has been commissioned in September 2025 at our Hyderabad plant.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech capacity utilization 85% in Q2 FY26 vs 61% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: During Q2 FY '26, capacity utilization stood at 85% as compared to 61% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Import pricing at INR93-94/kg forcing domestic price parity; raw material cost pass-through in commodity films
items.quote: See, import pricing was in the region of about INR93, INR94, and our pricing had to match that. Otherwise, imports would continue. If we start charging more than the import pricing, the volumes will increase. So we are restricted in increasing our prices because of the imports.

items.statement: Raw material pricing is pass-through; margins depend on demand-supply not raw material cost
items.quote: Yes. But as I've always mentioned before, raw material pricing is not really significant in our business. Raw material is a pass -through. The margins depend on demand and supply. So basically, even if raw material pricing has come down, yes, the prices will come down.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers volume growth driven mainly by existing accounts; new customers to ramp in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: So right now, the majority of volume growth came from the existing accounts, but we also saw development of new customers, which are going to pick up volumes in coming 3 to 4 quarters.

items.statement: Approximately 25,000 tonnes of polyester film imported in Q2 FY26 at predatory pricing
items.quote: Okay. So the total imports of Polyester Film, it's very difficult to give an exact number, but approximately 25,000 tonnes of material was imported in the quarter -- in the second quarter. That is a huge number when you're talking about a market size of ou rs. And more than the volume, it is the price at which it is being imported.

items.statement: DGTR initiated antidumping investigation on polyester film imports from Bangladesh, China, Thailand, USA
items.quote: Basis petition by domestic polyester film industry, Director General of Trade Remedies has initiated investigation for imposition of antidumping duties on imports of polyester film originating from Bangladesh, China, Thailand and U.S.A.

items.statement: EPR obligation deferral to March 2026; 20% PCR content requirement expected to drive BOPET demand from Q1/Q2 CY2026
items.quote: So what it means is that in FY '25- '26, the obligation was 10% of the flexible packaging and '26-'27, it was 10% and then thereafter, 20%. So those who have not complied with the 10% in FY '25-'26 have to comply to 20% instead of 10% in '26-'27. And we are seeing a strong momentum in the market wherein many big brands have already started gearing up for addressing the 20% obligation next year. So

items.statement: US tariffs substantially impacted value-added polyester film exports; Specialty Polymers unaffected due to IP protection
items.quote: See, basically, all our value-added films go to America. And because of the tariffs, this got substantially impacted. So we lost a lot of sale in the value -added segment, the real profitable segment, we lost a lot of sales because of the U.S. tariffs in Polyester Film. But this was not the case as far as Specialty Polymers was concerned because of IP.

items.statement: Euro loan MTM losses due to EUR/INR appreciation from 88 to 103; USD loan also impacted
items.quote: So first of all, the loss from foreign currency is not INR20 crores in quarter 2. It is around INR10 crores, both companies together. So as we have been mentioning in our previous calls also, in our subsidiary, that is Ester Filmtech, we have taken a euro loan from OLB Bank Germany. And as you know that euro has significantly appreciated against rupee in the last 1 year, if you remember, at the st

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt INR740 crores; net debt ~INR650 crores; expected to reduce to INR600-610 crores by year-end
items.quote: Our current debt is around INR740 crores, which is on the gross basis. So you can adjust the... Arvind Singhania: Consolidated. Sourabh Agarwal: Consolidated debt. So you can -- after adjusting for the cash and cash balance, it will be roughly around INR650 crores. And at the end of the year, we will be around INR600 crores to INR610 crores

items.statement: Term loan repayment maturity ~INR40 crores for next 6 months
items.quote: So our repayment schedule -- repayment maturity for the next 6 months will be roughly around INR40 crores.

items.statement: Share warrants INR175 crores raised for Loop project; INR85 crores received so far; 18-month period has 6-7 months remaining
items.quote: So the total value of the share warrant that we have issued is INR175 crores against which we have received till date around INR 85 crores for the -- as you are aware that in case of share of warrants, the total period available for investing is 18 months. Those 18 months have not yet expired, and we will call for the balance amount of money as per the requirement.

items.statement: ELITe acquired ~90 acres land in PCPIR zone Surat, Gujarat for chemical recycling project
items.quote: ELITe has entered into an agreement with a group of sellers for acquisition of 90 -- approximately 90 acres of project land in the PCPIR zone, strategically located in Surat, Gujarat, providing direct access to abundant polyester textile waste, skilled workforce and streamlined permitting process.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers sales volume 1,161 metric tons (+51% YoY); revenue +39% YoY
items.quote: In Specialty Polymers business, we recorded significant volume growth of 51% and revenue growth of 39% year-on-year with total sales reaching 1,161 metric tons in Q2 FY '26, indicating robust demand despite U.S. trade tariff.

items.statement: Polyester Films sales volume 21,329 metric tons (+8.72% YoY); revenue +2.34% YoY
items.quote: Polyester Films sales stood at 21,329 metric tons, reflecting a growth of 8.72% over Q2 FY '25, a reflection of continuous growth in demand. Revenue increased from INR290 crores to INR296.82 crores, an increase of 2.34%.

items.statement: rPET sales volume 1,046 metric tons (+219% YoY) in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Sales of rPET increased significantly to 1,046 metric tons in Q2 FY '26 as compared to 328 metric tons in Q2 FY '25 as the company continues to scale up its sustainability -focused product portfolio.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech sales volume 10,374 metric tons (+39.7% YoY); total income INR119.73 crores (+20.5% YoY)
items.quote: For Ester Filmtech, we reported a robust 39.7% year -on-year growth in sales volume, reaching 10,374 metric tons, up from 7,425 metric tons in quarter 2 FY '25. This was accompanied by a 20.5% increase in total income, which stood at INR 119.73 crores compared to INR99.4 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting an improved operational scale.

items.statement: ELITe project debt to be funded in SPV with natural FX hedge from 100% export orientation
items.quote: As far as the Loop project is concerned, the risk of foreign exchange loans will be far lower. because 100% of the production is going to be exported, which provides a natural hedge.

items.statement: Government ethanol blending policy confirmed at 20% until October 2026; potential increase to 27% thereafter
items.quote: the government is clear that the policy of 20% blending is up to October 2026. Beyond 2026, the government is looking at the possibility of increasing it to about 27%.

items.statement: Biofuels demand steady with 20% blending mandate; OMC allocations for next year not yet complete
items.quote: The traction overall is good because the 20% blending is going to stay. There is no doubt. And further traction will happen as and when the blending program is enhanced to possibly order more.

items.statement: Chemicals EBIT margin expanded from 8.1% to 10.9% in Q2 FY26 due to favorable product mix shift toward performance chemicals
items.quote: For Chemicals, EBIT margins have expanded from 8.1% to 10.9% or nearly 11%.

items.statement: Potable Spirits EBIT margin improved from 20.5% to 21.4% in Q2 FY26 driven by premiumization and Amrut partnership
items.quote: For Potable Spirits, EBIT margins have increased from 20.5% to 21.4%.

items.statement: Biofuels EBIT margin increased from 5.1% to 6.9% in Q2 FY26 supported by blending program and multi-feedstock capacity
items.quote: Biofuels EBIT margins have increased from 5.1% to 6.9%.

items.statement: Ethanol supply year runs to October 31; OMC allocations for next year partially received, clearer picture in couple of months
items.quote: the ethanol supply year is up to 31st of October. So, we are on track to supply based on the order book. Yes, so that is okay. I think, subsequently, the allocation that we have got, the OMCs have given not complete allocations.

items.statement: Incremental capex of INR 10-50 crore expected over next year for specialty chemicals; modular brownfield expansion approach
items.quote: I think you will continue to see some incremental CAPEX based on how our projects and how our customers are scaling up, which will be we are talking about in the range of maybe INR 10 crores to INR 50 crore kind of CAPEX to start with.

items.statement: Excess ethanol capacity in industry as blending at 20% while capacity caught up; potential for 27% blending
items.quote: the capacity has also caught up with the demand because the blending program is right now at 20%, while there is discussion on how it can be increased beyond 20% to maybe up to 27%. There is now some excess capacity in the industry.

items.statement: Crude at ~$60 pressured glycol ethers pricing vs petrochemical alternatives; expect crude hardening as India/China shift from Russian oil
items.quote: crude has been close to $60, which has meant that some of the other products like MEG have been lower on cost and some other petrochemical-based alternatives to our products have been lower on cost and we have had to struggle on price as well as margins in areas like glycol ethers.

items.statement: Performance chemicals revenue doubling on small base; bio-based amines commercial sales starting this and next quarter with L'Oreal, BASF, Dow partnerships
items.quote: we started with new performance chemicals, which is doing well. I am quite confident about the strong pipeline that we have. That business quite small is doing well, with very strong partnerships starting to merge with significant players like BASF, Newpark, Dow, etc.

items.statement: First globally to make bio-based amines; commercial sales starting this quarter and next with customers like L'Oreal
items.quote: We have also become the first ever company globally to make bio-based amines. Whilst we are to start commercial sales in this quarter and the next quarter, but nevertheless, it is an achievement where we worked with customers like L'Oreal and others.

items.statement: Amrut partnership exclusive in agreed whisky markets (UP, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Kerala, Tamil Nadu); first right of refusal on renewals
items.quote: Amrut's understanding with us is exclusive. They cannot give the brand which we are doing to anyone else. And since we are manufacturing them, we are selling them, we are putting investments into them, so the understanding is very clear from a long-term perspective, we have the first right of refusal, even after a long term, once the agreements are there for renewal.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma pursuing US FDA approvals and branded nutraceuticals contracts with US/European companies targeting 40-50% margins
items.quote: in branded nutraceuticals, we have some development. And if we talk about the branded nutraceuticals, it means that we are having our own brand, which will go to the formulation as an active agent with the name of our brand. So, we are in the process of having some contract with the U.S. companies and European companies to use our branded nutraceuticals. And you know the margin, as Saket, you aske

items.statement: UP molasses reservation policy clarified: B-heavy molasses reservation converted to C-heavy equivalent; no impact on Country Liquor supply
items.quote: B heavy molasses has 25% more sugar than C heavy molasses. So, that is the translation, which in terms of ethanol quantity does not mean that it will produce more ethanol. It is equivalent.

items.statement: 50% US tariff impacting JV directly and indirectly; some products sold directly to US, some customers slowed down
items.quote: 50% tariff in the U.S. has impacted to some extent the joint venture, some of our products directly and some of our products indirectly.

items.statement: INR 1,400 crore long-term debt as of Sep 2025; INR 467 crore preferential allotment + INR 180 crore normal repayment = INR 640 crore reduction
items.quote: Actually, the company is having about INR 1,400 crores long-term debt as on date. And the normal repayment for the remaining period in this year is about INR 180 crores in next five months, means November to March. Apart from this, whatever we are raising, this INR 467 crores will also be utilized for the repayment or you can say the prepayment of the existing debt.

items.statement: Debt split post-demerger: INR 600 crore India Glycols, INR 800 crore IGL Spirits; prepayment to reduce both proportionally
items.quote: in these two companies, India Glycols and IGL Spirits, the segregation what we have done as of date is about INR 600 crores and INR 800 crores. INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.

items.statement: Average long-term borrowing cost 10%, working capital 9.25%; expect INR 60-70 crore annual interest savings from next year after prepayment and rating improvement
items.quote: our average cost of borrowing is about 10%, while for the working capital, it is about 9.25%. So, we are also looking at something like, you can say, the improvement in the outside credit rating, which will help us to reduce the interest rates, as well as we are all focusing for the prepayments. So, that overall, the company's on long-term basis, I will say that the interest will come down by say

items.statement: Preferential allotment of INR 467 crore equity at INR 915/share to promoters, friends & relatives approved by Board and EGM; awaiting BSE/NSE approval
items.quote: the Board has already approved the issuance of 467 crores equity at the rate of INR 915 to the promoters, friends and relatives. The EGM has already approved, means the investors have rather blessed that resolution. And we are expecting the approval from the BSE and NSE shortly.

items.statement: Ethanol blending reached ~20% in FY26 from 5% in FY20; INR 40,000 crore farmer payments and INR 43,000 crore forex savings in FY25
items.quote: the blending program has more or less progressed as per plan from nearly 5% blending in '19-'20 to an expected blending of close to 20%, which is expected in this year, which is the year '25-'26.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma under pressure: nicotine sales hit by low-cost competition and Russia-Ukraine war; Thiocolchicoside disrupted by Gloriosa seed shortage
items.quote: in nicotine, the low-cost production by the new manufacturing facilities has dented the volumes and the value both. And apart from this, the Russia and Ukraine war has impacted negatively to nicotine business also. But in branded nutraceuticals, we have some development.

items.statement: JV investment increased from INR 381 cr to INR 411 cr due to minimal capex funded by JV's own funds, not IGL
items.quote: investment, there are certain minimal CAPEX are being taken up by the JV itself. We have not invested directly into the JV by India Glycol Limited. Whatever the investment has been taken, they are taken by JV itself by their own funds.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved steadily from ~11% in FY22 to ~15% in H1 FY26 reflecting business quality improvement
items.quote: we had a relatively lower year in the year 2022, at an EBITDA margin of close to 11%. And that has improved steadily from 11% to close to 15%, as you would see now, which has been a steady, you would say, recovery for the business or growth in the business, not only in terms of top line, but also in terms of the quality of the business.

items.statement: Monthly average order intake for YTD September 2025 is ₹254 crores, driven by Supercritical, Conventional Energy, Export, and Water Waste Water segments.
items.quote: A quick glance at order intake, so generally as we provide this, this is a monthly average and you can see a very good growth, that is ₹254 crores, that is a monthly average for YTD September 2025.

items.statement: Orders on hand total ₹26,392 million, comprising ₹13,254 million without nuclear and ₹13,138 million nuclear.
items.quote: Coming to orders on hand, again, a good growth story, you can see without nuclear, we are ₹13,254 million; and nuclear alone, it is ₹13,138 million. So total, it is ₹26,392 million.

items.statement: Export order intake YTD September 2025 is ₹390 crores, representing 17% of total order intake.
items.quote: A good export performance , as I mentioned, which have been our discussion in last couple of Investor Meeting , so you can see YTD September ₹390 crores, and we are 17%, which is an export percentage to total OI.

items.statement: Non-nuclear order intake grew at 16% CAGR year-on-year, showing comfort in standard and project segments.
items.quote: So, the yellow highlights which you see is the order intake that has come without nuclear. So, there has been a growth of 16% CAGR of a non-nuclear business year-on-year and that also gives a comfort that we are not only dependent on the nuclear, but we are also dependent on standard and project segments, which form the core and the largest share of our business.

items.statement: Water segment is the largest at 29% of sales, followed by General Industry 23%, Energy 18%, Petrochemical and Chemical 21%, Building Services 8%, Mining 1%.
items.value: Water 29%, General Industry 23%, Energy 18%, Petrochemical and Chemical 21%, Building Services 8%, Mining 1%
items.quote: So, you can see that the W ater is the one, which is the biggest of the lot of all the segments that we cater to, which is 29% of our sales. General Industry constitutes around 23% of our sales; Energy constitutes about 18% of our sales; Building Services, 8%; Petrochemical and Chemical, 21%; and Mining is 1%.

items.statement: Firefighting business is close to ₹625 crore with ~12,000 units sold annually, growing at ~50% CAGR since 2021.
items.quote: If I'm asked how exactly you look at the firefighting business out of – this is close to around ₹625 crore of a business and close to around 12,000 units are being sold annually.

items.statement: Solar business expected to grow at least 50% from last year, expanding pan-India with new state entries, but cautious due to working capital intensity.
items.quote: I would say we would, let's say, grow from our last year at least 50% of the business. We are being careful here not to go too aggressively, because this business involves a lot of working capital and involves a lot of long period for cash to cash cycle.

items.statement: Export should grow robustly as more acceptance and references are developed.
items.quote: Yes. Export should grow definitely, because step by step more and more acceptance is happening. We are developing references. So, I see no reason why we should also grow in that.

items.statement: Valves division investing in imported grinding machine, laser welding technology, and hybrid cell for bigger size valves handling and throughput improvement.
items.quote: We are also investing continuously on the bigger size valves handling, including the imported grinding machine that's helped for the valve seating arrangement. We also invested on laser technology for the welding technology which is overlay, which is a heart of the valve, I would say.

items.statement: Valves division continuously increasing capacity through efficiency improvements and lean concept implementation.
items.quote: The plant is equipped with continuously working on increasing on the capacity, which we do by our own efficiency improvements, and also lead concept implementation.

items.statement: Key customer additions: L&T (biggest energy order this year), Haryana Renewable (solar government customer), Swastik Trading (dealer), ArcelorMittal, Hindalco, JSW (mining), Reliance (Nagothane and Dahej plants), Tata (Sanand data centre).
items.quote: In Energy, Larsen & Toubro has, as Mr. Bhave talked about, this is one of the biggest order which we got this year ; and Thermax and ISGEC are the OEMs to which we supply our energy pumps.

items.statement: Valves division obtained Chinese TSG certification first among valve plants, enabling export to China; also pursuing API Monogram and Saudi Aramco qualifications for Oil & Gas market entry.
items.quote: And, proud to say, the Chinese market is one big market for us in the exports, and they came up with the TSG certification, which is an entry, if you have to supply to them, I think we were the one of the first valve plant that could get this certification.

items.statement: Valves business grew at 22% CAGR on order intake and 21% CAGR on sales over last 5 years.
items.quote: And just to give you the growth of the valves business, I think we have been growing at CAGR of 22% on the order intake and 21% on the sales over the last 5 years.

items.statement: Solar business involves high working capital and long cash-to-cash cycle, so growth is managed step-by-step.
items.quote: We are being careful here not to go too aggressively, because this business involves a lot of working capital and involves a lot of long period for cash to cash cycle.

items.statement: Valves division has 325 permanent employees; extensive employee engagement programs to keep team motivated.
items.quote: The total permanent employee strength is 325 and it's spread over 28,000 square meters.

items.statement: PM-KUSUM scheme continuation announced, supporting solar pump business growth.
items.quote: There is continuation of the PM-KUSUM scheme also announced. And we are doing well.

items.statement: Revenue growth slowed to 7-8% in last 9 months due to delay in nuclear pump dispatches (Gorakhpur, Haryana, Kudankulam projects), but order book grew 22%.
items.quote: It's only a matter of delay of this nuclear order. In the order book is sitting, the orders from Gorakhpur, Haryana project and also Kudankulam project, which due to the nature of that business is a bit slow. We expected this to happen in this year, but it may not happen in this year, a very small portion may happen this year.

items.statement: Acquired Bharat Pumps & Compressors Limited (BP&CL) technology knowhow in 2023, now supplying spares and services for reciprocating pumps.
items.quote: BP & CL, Bharat Pumps & Compressors Limited , we acquired this company, the technology knowhow in 2023 earlier, and then we started this business, the entire range of parts and services what we cater for on our own pumps. This has been done for the BP & CL pumps also.

items.statement: Dividend for 2024 declared at 200%.
items.quote: And dividend, which is for 2024, that is 200%.

items.statement: Revenue grew from ₹18,067 million to ₹19,117 million; PBT from ₹2,282 million to ₹2,485 million; 20% revenue CAGR, 25% PAT CAGR, 19% EBITDA CAGR; ROCE 23.45%; net cash ~₹300 million.
items.quote: Revenue, you can see again a sustained and very good growth from ₹18,067 million to ₹19,117 million. And so, as in profit before tax, we have grown from ₹2,282 million to ₹2,485 million.

items.statement: SupremeServ expanding mechanical seal repair centre and 5-axis machine; Chinchwad plant has rooftop solar generating majority of power.
items.quote: We are expanding this actually the repair centre as well as the 5 Axis machine, which we have recently bought. It's really speeding up the mechanical seal manufacturing line.

items.statement: SupremeServ aftermarket growing at 18%+ driven by spares, services, digitization (KSB Guard, Sonolyzer), reverse engineering, and BP&CL reciprocating pump business.
items.quote: The result here you see, actually, we are growing at 18% or plus in last few years, mainly with these initiatives which we have recently taken.

items.statement: SupremeServ has 76 industrial spare parts service partners and 200+ submersible service partners; central warehouse with 14,000 bin locations.
items.quote: We have actually got 76 different service partners for the industrial spare parts, and for the submersible, those are more than 200.

items.statement: Ethanol/distillery business supplied 1,200+ pumps in last 2-3 years, trend expected to continue for next 2-3 years unless government stops blending mandate.
items.quote: We have been quite successful in this particular distillery business, where we have supplied close to more than 1,200 odd pumps in last 2, 3 years. And we see this trend still continuing for next 2, 3 years, until unless we see a stoppage coming from the government side.

items.statement: Data centre demand growing; supplied pumps for Tata project in Sanand, expecting more from Assam, Dholera and other locations.
items.quote: We have been successful as well, where we have supplied the pumps, especially for this Tata project in Sanand and we are quite hopeful that for the further projects which are coming up in Assam as well as in Dholera and other places, means we will be also getting more and more requirements.

items.statement: Petrochemical expansions expected in 2026-27 at Reliance, BPCL Bina, IOCL Panipat, HCL Mumbai refinery.
items.quote: definitely 2026 and 2027 looks quite positive with the new expansions coming up in Reliance as well as BPCL Bina, uh IOCL Panipat for m aleic acid and HCL Mumbai refinery expansion

items.statement: Management targets minimum double-digit top-line growth for non-nuclear business, potentially better than double-digit, with consistent EBITDA margins of 13-14%.
items.quote: In general, I would answer that is in our strategy that at least minimum double-digit if not more. And if we look at it , it should be more than double-digit.

items.statement: Solar business order book estimated at more than ₹250 crores.
items.quote: It will be somewhere , order book would be around, let 's say, I would say more is on the sales revenue, order book is converted into sales revenue. So, we should be able to do something similar more than ₹250 crores or something like that.

items.statement: Capacity expansion at Shirwal (14,000 sq m) and Sinnar (4th/5th shed) to be commissioned by March 2026.
items.quote: So, yes, first of all, you must be seeing that in Shir wal, we are expanding, the land we had taken, that 14,000 square meter, that will be commissioned by March next year. The fourth or fifth shed in Sinnar , which got delayed a bit, that will be also commissioned by March 2026.

items.statement: Current plant utilization close to 85%; debottlenecking ongoing, further capacity expansion under evaluation but no decision yet.
items.quote: I think this is what we have been debating internally. There is internal push to have capacity expansion and we debate a lot and we have an exchange that let's try to see how much we can extract more out of our things

items.statement: Engineered pump business expected to grow faster due to new thermal policy (43+ GW) and petrochemical expansions; standard pumps to maintain growth pace.
items.quote: Yes, engineered pump business definitely is likely to grow as compared to what it has been past few years. As rightly said, yes, both in Petrochemicals as well as in Energy, we see a big thrust coming because of the new thermal policy that has been announced where we are talking of more than 43 gigawatts coming up.

items.statement: Nuclear pump deliveries for Gorakhpur expected to start next month or first half of January; Kudankulam few pumps this year; Kaiga after Gorakhpur completion.
items.quote: So having said that, I think, we are hopeful that the pumps should start somewhere in next month or first half of January. And then after that it is testing of 500 hours, customer has an option to increase it to 500 hours more. So, I think next year first half we should definitely see.

items.statement: Nuclear order book delivery extensions officially received for GHAPV: 4 pumps by mid-2026, remaining 4 by 2027; Kaiga to follow.
items.quote: The delivery extensions which we have officially received for GHAPV are 2026 and 2027. Four pumps by made of 2026 and remaining by four pumps of 2027.

items.statement: Gross margin improved this year due to favorable product mix; EBITDA margin steady at 13-14% range; internal efficiency improvements offset mix pressure.
items.quote: A gross margin is of course, as we know, it’s a product mix and in fact this year gross margin is better off , because of the favourable product KSB Limited (KSB) Institutional Investors’ Meet November 17, 2025 mix. And when we come to EBITDA, it depends on the interest income and other

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 13-14% consistent level; not aiming for 15-16% unless nuclear contributes.
items.quote: EBITDA margin is also on a consistent level, I would say, 13% to 14%. This is something similar. Unidentified Analyst: Around that level. Rajeev Jain: And as I said, this is our range which we want to more important is the growth top-line and keeping this EBITDA margins on this level

items.statement: SupremeServ currently 16-17% of revenue; target to grow beyond 20% to 25-30% over time, driven by nuclear, mechanical seals, and engineered pumps.
items.quote: At the moment, total SupremeServ would be close to 16%, 17% of the total business. And with these initiatives, surely, we will grow further. The way the standard industry is growing, it will be really challenging for us to meet that percentage , because, for example, say, submersible pumps, those are quite big in number . But in that ratio, the spare parts may be sold, may not be sold, but as you

items.statement: KSB leads in Energy (conventional & nuclear) and Valves (gate, globe, check in Energy); top 3 in Industry; top 3-4 in Agri; low share in Building Services, Mining, Firefighting. Overall pump market share ~12-15%.
items.quote: Overall, we would say that our market share in pumps would be somewhere 12% to 15% is something on an average, on a broader scale.

items.statement: Nuclear PCP competitive moat strong: KSB only major global player currently producing primary coolant pumps; new entrants face high barriers.
items.quote: So, I think we should already have a head start with the fact that KSB is the only major player worldwide having produced a primary coolant pump. So, I don't know when the last the name , you said when they have produced the last PCP. So, I think that should give us a head start

items.statement: API Monogram certification targeted for Q1-Q2 next year as entry requirement for Saudi Aramco approval; localization requirements also emerging.
items.quote: I think we are targeting to get that done in the first and second quarter of next year. And that's an entry requirement for us to apply for Aramco approval.

items.statement: Export momentum to continue outgrowing domestic business, subject to geopolitical situation and tariffs.
items.quote: Yes. I can confidently say, yes, subject to geopolitical situation. That is the only hurdle which we will have, otherwise no other hurdle, we will grow.

items.statement: Working capital days increased due to solar business cash-to-cash cycle; nuclear has advances offsetting WIP; inventory efficiency improved overall.
items.quote: capital, yes, as we have been talking due to solar business, a cycle of working capital , as Mr. Jain also mentioned, cash to cash cycle. That is definitely on the higher side

items.statement: Boiler feed pump lead time 12-14 months; L&T has 8 units of Adani for ordering this or next quarter; visibility positive for next 4-5 years.
items.quote: Yes, these pumps are usually, you don't have your lead time of close to 12 to 14 months from the date of placement of orders and getting the approvals. And definitely we see a positive scenario, because L&T that sources have got 8 units of Adani for which the boiler feed pumps will come for ordering either this quarter or maybe next quarter.

items.statement: Data centre identified as high-potential sub-segment; OEM cell created with parent to adapt products; dedicated slide planned for next meeting.
items.quote: Data centre is one of the smallest sub- segment which we are focusing on, but it has a very good potential. And we are adapting our products also to their requirement.

items.statement: Parent KPIs for Indian management: minimum double-digit top-line growth, consistent EBITDA margins (13-14%), continuously increasing dividend.
items.quote: KPI is given mainly for the Indian market. So, it is as you see in the performance, they see.
