items.quote: We're not going to give make projections yet because we need to get to a stable, consistent revenue stream before we start making projections.

items.statement: Cross-border UPI integration with 10 countries completed by RS Software; revenue being earned from NPCI launch
items.quote: The integration of UPI with the 10 countries you're referring to with their real time payment rail. Has all been done by RS Software, so we are gaining revenue from the launch by NPCI of UPI integrated cross-border transactions.

items.statement: Active bids for cross-border product technology; at least a couple of bids where RS technology is being proposed
items.quote: We have been working at our Payments Innovation Lab on the cross-border product technology and. I am pleased to say that there are at least a couple of bids right now where our technology is being responded with for building cross-border products.

items.statement: Transaction-based pricing model exists in 3-4 cases; strategy to move toward transaction-based revenue
items.quote: There are already three or four cases where we do gain by transaction, a pricing per transaction.

items.statement: NPCI remains important client with 10-year relationship; all major digital payment infrastructure enhancements done by RS Software
items.quote: We do not report you know project by project revenue. We report our overall revenue and NPCI is an important client. We've got a 10 years relationship starting with these building of UPI.

items.statement: Customer segments are central banks, major banks, financial institutions including NPCI, Interac, The Clearing House
items.quote: Our customer segments, Abhijit, are across the central banks, across the major banks. And the financial institutions.

items.statement: Partnership with Retachi Payments gaining traction to leverage UPI transaction growth in India
items.quote: For us to leverage the growth of UPI transactions in India, we have a partnership in place. With which I mentioned before, with retachi payments and I'm glad to say that finally we're getting more and more traction through that partnership.

items.statement: Payments Canada and Interac are prospects, not clients; no execution work currently; full-time sales rep appointed in Canada last month
items.quote: Payments Canada is a prospect for us. When we continue to have a sales activity there, we are not executing anything for Payments Canada.

items.statement: RS Software focused on central bank payment infrastructure (real-time rails, overlays, fraud risk); Volante works mostly with banks only
items.quote: We are, we are focused on central banks that you know central payment infrastructure. Volant works mostly with the banks only.

items.statement: EFRM product (RS IntelliEdge) holds IP; products target payments modernization at central bank level with long sales cycles
items.quote: The our the EFRM product of NPCI. Is RS Software's RS Intelliage product where we hold the IP?

items.statement: All products aligned with AI strategy for 8 years; RS IntelliEdge incorporates deep machine learning and AI
items.quote: All of our products are aligned very well to the AI strategy. One of our products, RS Intelli Edge, which has been repurposed to be India's broader risk platform, incorporates a significant amount of deep machine learning and a I with it.

items.statement: Significant investment in product development while building India's digital payment infrastructure; profit and cash flow positive for past 3.5 years
items.quote: We are profit positive, cash flow positive in spite of the fact that we have invested significantly into into enhancing our products.

items.statement: New COO Samik Roy appointed in early July with 24 years experience from Microsoft and Oracle; proving effective
items.quote: We have recently in early July this year appointed a new Chief Operating Officer. Samik Roy. He comes from a 24 years of solid background and success with Microsoft and with Oracle.

items.statement: Talent attracted globally; Calcutta/West Bengal education institutions provide quality talent; new COO focused on people pillar for retention
items.quote: We attract our talent from across the world. By the way, a lot of our technology talent comes here. Calcutta, West Bengal has got some great education institutions.

items.statement: Cash position increased over last 3 years; current fiscal aberration due to project delays; dynamic decisions based on cash burn
items.quote: If you look at our last three years performance, overall we've added more cash to the company and now we haven't gone down.

items.statement: No fundraising or equity dilution plans as of today; additional capital for growth always on agenda but no current plans
items.quote: That is always on the agenda for any company. We do not have any plans as of today.

items.statement: Product companies take 6-8 years to demonstrate real revenue; consistency not yet achieved; will take more time
items.quote: In every single case, the product companies are taking 6 to 8 years before they even start to demonstrate any real revenue.

items.statement: Current fiscal performance impacted by couple of projects delayed in decision making; may open in Q4 FY26 or move to FY27
items.quote: This year's performance is impacted because couple of our projects are delayed in their decision making. So that's got delayed. It might some of them might open in the last quarter of this fiscal, otherwise they move in next fiscal.

items.statement: Sales cycles for central bank payment infrastructure are long and unpredictable, making revenue consistency difficult
items.quote: These are typically long sales cycles and we sell into central banks both directly as well as through our channel partners along with our channel partners. So because these cycles are unpredictable from a closure timing perspective, which is why. It is difficult for us to be able to define consistency in our revenue acquisition.

items.statement: Asian region prospects may mature faster than other geographies; Middle East also has pipeline
items.quote: I think we got some good prospects going on in the Asian region. And we also have some of the Middle East region.

items.statement: Three major initiatives: strengthening management pillar, expanding sales coverage in North America with new hires and board involvement, channels in Asia/Middle East picking up momentum
items.quote: Firstly, you look at the management pillar and that is where we are very highly focused on strengthening that for for active implementation #2 is. In terms of our sales coverage, we have, we have decided now, sorry, we are implementing already recruiting salespeople in the geographies in North America.

items.statement: Conscious strategic pivot from services to products in 2015 driven by digital payments advent; card networks uninterested in cannibalizing card revenue
items.quote: on the part of our software for for a strategic pivot of what we do. V inodchandra Agrawal 11:49 Sure, sure. R aj Jain 12:03 And the major factor influencing that was we could see the advent of digital payments starting to take place where the major payment networks like Visa, MasterCard, American Express were not really interested because they were card networks primarily

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue around previous year level, give or take a few percentage points
items.quote: We expect this year to be around the previous year's numbers, give or take a few percentage points in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Targets H2 FY26 revenue of INR750-800 crores
items.quote: All things being equal, we should do something around INR750 crores to INR800 crores in H2 and take the number close to previous year level.

items.statement: Order book of INR300 crores revenue, expects INR200 crores realization in FY27
items.quote: Going forward, beyond that, we have an order book of around INR300 crores revenue with us, and that is expected to realize around and we expect to realize about INR200 crores in FY '27.

items.statement: Capex plan: INR100 crores in H1 FY26, INR70 crores or less in H2 FY26, INR100-120 crores in FY27
items.quote: This year, we plan to invest next - first half, we've invested about INR100 crores. Second half, we'll do INR70 crores or less. And next year is likely to be around INR100 crores to INR120 crores overall.

items.statement: Capacity utilization headed to 75,000 tons, expects 80,000-90,000 tons in FY27
items.quote: If we look at the forging space, we stand at about - we are headed for about 75,000 tons of capacity utilization. And this year and next year, we expect to push it to anywhere between 80,000 to 90,000.

items.statement: US Class VIII truck market inventory depletion, purchases restarting from November, recovery by June 2026
items.quote: Now the Class VIII truck market is beginning to wake up and we are seeing purchases starting from November onwards. Last 3 months have been particularly bad and we see this picking up by June of next year, it should be at a reasonable level.

items.statement: Domestic CV market stagnant due to shift from multi-axle to tractor trailers reducing front axle demand
items.quote: Domestic market looks to be holding its own. As I've said, TIV has gone up, but unit sales has dropped because multi-axle vehicles are being replaced by tractor trailers. So the addressable market for MMF products in that zone has come down.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 19% vs 21% previous period, operational EBITDA 17.5% vs 19.5%, expects improvement from current levels
items.quote: EBITDA for this period stands at 19% as against 21% for the previous period. EBITDA -- operational EBITDA stands at 17.5% versus 19.5% for the previous year.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve from current levels if sales bottom reached in Q2
items.quote: If we hold that we have hit bottom in terms of sales, then margin should be improving. But whether this is the bottom or not, it's not a question that I can answer right now. But we expect -- from what I said earlier, we expect Q2 to have been our worst quarter.

items.statement: US tariffs currently borne by customers, unsustainable beyond March, may trigger resourcing
items.quote: So far, we are not affected. The tariffs are borne by the customers. And going forward, I would say, until March, probably they would absorb. Beyond March, they would definitely look at resourcing or at negotiating for sure.

items.statement: Net debt INR855 crores at Q2 vs INR843 crores FY25, expects INR50-75 crores inventory reduction
items.quote: We are compressing our inventories now and we see scope for a reduction of at least INR50 crores in our inventories.

items.statement: Peak debt at INR850 crores, no significant reduction expected in next 2 years, may consider equity infusion
items.quote: we will -- I would say, there will not be any significant reduction in debt in the next 2 years. 8) M M Forgings ... What we will do, let me explain. For sure, we don't want to borrow anymore. We have seen peak debt and God willing, I would like to hold it there

items.statement: Converting rupee debt to foreign currency loans, targets interest run rate INR50-60 crores vs INR70-80 crores
items.quote: I would expect our interest to be pegged within INR60 crores, maybe if we get our act together, maybe even INR50 crores. Somewhere between INR50 crores and INR60 crores, we'll target run rate of interest.

items.statement: DVS Industries merger into MM Forgings at NCLT, expected anytime
items.quote: The wholly owned subsidiary, DVS Industries will be merged into MM Forgings. Those proceedings are on at NCLT, and we expect the merger any time now.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton INR38,300 vs INR40,500 previous half year
items.quote: The EBITDA per ton stands at INR38,000 as against INR40,000 -- INR40,500 at the previous half year. For this year, it stands at INR38,300.

items.statement: Sales realization per ton improved from INR1.8 lakhs to INR1.93 lakhs due to higher value-add in machined parts
items.quote: More machined parts have gone. But overall, the sales of machined parts has not increased. It's only come down. But the extent of machined - the value add that we are doing in machined parts has gone up.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty, customer project delays, market volatility may impact growth trajectory
items.quote: Nobody can hazard a guess on where we will be. But overall conditions, India is positive and U.S. is not. Europe is middling. South America is slightly bustling.

items.statement: EV subsidiary Abhinava Rizel close to first sales, INR20-30 crores annual potential, developing controllers for 3-in-1 solution
items.quote: Overall, this customer holds about INR20 crores to INR30 crores of potential and has committed that they would like to work very closely with us. So one good news is that Abhinava Rizel is slowly seeing end of the light and will start its manufacturing very shortly.

items.statement: Targets portfolio EBITDA margin north of 30% near-term and 40% long-term after full renovation
items.quote: So with that, with having those rooms operational for us, the target is that at a portfolio level to have an EBITDA margin that is North of 30%.

items.statement: Aims to beat industry growth, targeting 5-7% growth for next financial year despite ongoing renovations
items.quote: So if the industry is growing at 7%, we would always aim for a 10% growth. But having said that, because for the next couple of financial years as well, our existing portfolio will continue to be seeing some sort of renovation in a phase wise manner. In spite of that, we still want to continue to have that 5-7% growth.

items.statement: Total three-phase renovation budget INR120 crore; INR50-55 crore spent on Phase 1 (Courtyard), balance INR70 crore for Marriott upgrades
items.quote: So, the total budget for all the three phases put together was around INR120 crores. And today the spend is, we have completed spending around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Phase 2 Convention Center work starts April 1, 2026, completes in six months by September 30, 2026; budget INR30-35 crore
items.quote: Phase two the Convention Center -- phase two split again into two parts. Phase two, the first part is the Convention Center, where we are going to take it out in April on April 1 of 2026. And we aim to complete it in six months, which is by 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Phase 2 room refurbishment: 168 of 295 Marriott rooms to be upgraded by March 31, 2027 in batches of 20-30 rooms
items.quote: So, basically, this, we aim by the end of next year to do those many rooms in a phased manner, because we won't be able to do 295 rooms in one year. So, that's why we have put an estimate of...(inaudible)

items.statement: Madhapur Greenfield project at conversion and design stage; ground-breaking awaits government permissions for land-use change
items.quote: The Madhapur update is that we are in the process of converting the land from residential to commercial and taking the permissions. So parallelly we have also initiated design, what do you call, appointments for like the architect and interior designer.

items.statement: Phase 1 added 56 new rooms at Courtyard; spa, gym, rooftop restaurant and pool to be completed by end of December 2025
items.quote: We are happy to announce that 56 new rooms have been added and are open to guests from this month. And the other two floors, which are the gym and spa and the rooftop restaurant, will be completed by the end of December.

items.statement: Phase 2 expands Convention Center from 10,000 to 20,000 sq ft and upgrades existing 10,000 sq ft
items.quote: And the phase two involves expanding the Marriott Convention Center from 10,000 square feet of Convention Center to 20,000 square foot. And also upgrading the existing 10,000 square foot Convention Center to a modern facility.

items.statement: Hyderabad demand growing 10-12% annually with minimal supply addition (3-4% for weaker brands), creating favorable demand-supply gap
items.quote: So what we know is that supply at a city level is increasing at about 10% to 12% per year. Sorry, demand is increasing at 10% to 12% per year, with little to no increase in the supply.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 27.7%; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 23.4%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR8.82 crores. So, the EBITDA margins came in at 27.7%, reflecting strong cost discipline and operational efficiency.

items.statement: ADR up 9% YoY at Marriott (INR6,620) and 13% YoY at Courtyard (INR6,837) in Q2 FY26; H1 ADR up 11% and 14% respectively
items.quote: For Q2 FY26, the ADR for the Marriott property stood at INR 6,620, up 9% year-on-year, while for Courtyard, it was INR 6,837, a growth of 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: New Courtyard club-level rooms to be priced 25-30% above existing inventory
items.quote: And this is just a start because the new rooms that we are adding, we intend to market those as a premium like club level sort of room, where the ADR will be a significant 25% to 30% higher than the rest of the inventory.

items.statement: F&B and banqueting contribute 45-48% of revenue; new Pan-Asian restaurant will increase restaurant count to six
items.quote: So essentially, if you look at our business, typically about 45% of our revenue comes from F&B, which basically includes the banquet and the restaurants that we have.

items.statement: MICE revenue currently under 30% of total; expected to reach close to 50% after Convention Center expansion to 20,000 sq ft
items.quote: So the MICE business that right now contributes like under 30% of our overall revenue, we expect that to go close to 50%.

items.statement: Marriott Bonvoy loyalty program contribution to occupancy increasing quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: And as we speak, quarter-on-quarter, the contribution of occupancy in our hotels from this loyalty program only keeps increasing, which is why we want to continue to invest in a relation with Marriott.

items.statement: Operating cash flows improved in H1 despite lower profits due to ADR growth offsetting occupancy decline from renovation
items.quote: In spite of that, you see the difference in the EBITDA or the EBITDA margin is very, very minimal. This is because we have managed to push the envelope with the ADR.

items.statement: Refinanced promoter loan with Kotak at 8.25% interest rate; most interest cost capitalized as borrowing cost on expansion
items.quote: We have repaid the promoter's loan and refinanced from the Kotak. And most of the interest cost is being capitalized because it is a borrowing cost on the expansion, on capitalization and interest rate is also 8.25%.

items.statement: Rights issue raised INR37.5 crore; open Kotak credit limit of INR70-80 crore available for balance capex
items.quote: we had raised around INR37.5 crores from the rights issue. And that continues accruals from the ongoing running hotel. And this phased wise renovation has also helped us keep that good healthy EBITDA, which is contributing to cash flow and the cash in the company. So this can easily be funded through that and also, we have an open limit from Kotak for another INR70 to INR80 crores

items.statement: Actively evaluating Brownfield acquisitions in Hyderabad and leisure destinations (tiger reserves, vacation spots); no deals crystallized yet
items.quote: We are concentrating a little bit on Hyderabad for looking for more Brownfield and existing hotels. And we are actively looking and we would like to announce something once something is concrete and crystallized. And other than Hyderabad, we are looking at other destinations, more like touristy and like vacation type of destinations to add to our portfolio.

items.statement: Madhapur land leased from promoter relatives on 25% EBITDA revenue share; no lease payments until property generates healthy EBITDA
items.quote: The land is owned by the wife of the managing director and the brother-in-laws of the managing director. And they have leased the land to the company on a 25% EBITDA lease rental basis. So until the property is up and running and making a good healthy EBITDA, there would be no lease payments to the related parties of the management.

items.statement: Convention Center renovation (Apr-Sep 2026) will impact MICE revenue and associated room occupancy; Courtyard completion expected to offset gap
items.quote: You see it will surely impact the revenue because the convention center will be unavailable to be leased out, rented out. And that will also have an effect on the room occupancy, because a lot of the convention center usage contributes to the room occupancy.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 combined RevPAR INR3,794; H1 FY26 combined RevPAR INR3,803
items.quote: For Q2 FY26, the RevPAR for Marriott was INR4,726 and INR2,156 for Courtyard with the combined RevPAR at INR 3,794. For H1 FY26, the combined RevPAR was INR 3803.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 occupancy: Marriott 71.4%, Courtyard 31.5% (renovation impact), combined 56.9%; H1 combined 56%
items.quote: For Q2 FY26, occupancy was 71.4% at Marriott and 31.5% at Courtyard, with a combined occupancy of 56.9% across the complex. In H1 FY26, the combined occupancy stood at 56%.

items.statement: Outsourced laundry operations to third party to reduce cost burden on margins
items.quote: And also one major thing which we did was we outsourced the laundry. The laundry was putting a little bit of cost on the margins. So we actually got a third party to run the laundry for us and we created the facility from that.

items.statement: Invested in back-of-house MEP upgrades (generators, chillers, piping) to lower future maintenance costs and improve margins
items.quote: The MEP is something which we really concentrated for the past two years after taking over this property, didn't really upgrading these amenities so that the cost outlier tomorrow is very less as compared to having older equipment.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth minimum 10% year-on-year
items.quote: And going forward, if you see the sales growth, and it will be 10% from the last year's, minimum.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue target around INR150 crores
items.quote: So, we are looking like INR150-odd crores revenue next year, sir? Ashwani Khemka: Exactly. Correct

items.statement: SPL Infusion full-year revenue potential INR90-110 crores
items.quote: The full year operation, we can INR90 crores to INR110 crores, we can do.

items.statement: SPL Infusion optimal capacity utilization by Q2 FY27
items.quote: By say -- in the second quarter of FY '27.

items.statement: SPL Infusion FY27 revenue contribution around INR70-80 crores
items.quote: So next year, sir, then what we are saying is that maybe INR70 crores can be contribution from this plant alone in the full year FY '27, sir? Ashwani Khemka: Yes

items.statement: Alevia Healthcare FY26 bottom-line contribution INR1-1.5 crores
items.quote: And from a only bottom-line perspective, we expect around INR1 crores to INR1.5 crores of contribution to our bottom line. That is only our share of the venture for FY '26.

items.statement: Alevia Healthcare FY27 bottom-line contribution minimum INR3-3.5 crores
items.quote: A minimum of growth 100% from this number. So, minimum of INR3 crores to INR3.5 crores we should achieve in FY '27, it will go way up north as well.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex INR1.04 crores
items.quote: During the H1, we did a capex of INR1.04 crores.

items.statement: SPL Infusion commercial production started, revenue booking from Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have started the commercial batches, and we should start booking revenue in Q3 FY '26. That is the quarter ending December.

items.statement: SPL Infusion Q3 low volume, Q4 substantially higher volume
items.quote: Q3 will have less volume and Q4 will have a substantially good volume.

items.statement: Nepal unrest held back export orders worth nearly INR1 crore in Q2
items.quote: In Nepal, prolonged local unrest prevented execution of export orders worth nearly INR1 crore.

items.statement: Inventory of INR6+ crores held back due to regulatory scrutiny
items.quote: And you can be seen our inventory levels are a round INR6 crores plus, which we could not export because of this reason.

items.statement: SPL Infusion has healthy order book from government, semi-government, open market and exports
items.quote: And we have a very good healthy order book in place.

items.statement: LatAm regulatory scrutiny delaying approvals and dispatches, moderating near-term growth
items.quote: In LatAm, product issues raised against unrelated Indian exporters led to tighter FDA scrutiny for all suppliers, slowing clearances and dispatches.

items.statement: Antibiotic market declining 8-10% globally due to resistance, but company exposure only 7-8%
items.quote: Last 3, 4 years after the COVID pandemic and the infections -- the antibiotic growth is down by 8% to 10% in most of the cases.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.5% vs 17.9% YoY due to lower margins
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was at 15.5% versus 17.9% in Q2 FY '25. The year-on-year contraction in EBITDA margin was due to lower margins during the quarter.

items.statement: SPL Infusion margins similar to base business, potentially slightly better
items.quote: Yes, yes, similar. A little better also.

items.statement: IV fluid prices revised upward by government
items.quote: Yes. The prices have been revised.

items.statement: Revised Schedule M deadline extended by 2 months to February 2026
items.quote: As you must be aware, the revised schedule M guideline, which was to end on December '25 has been extended only for 2 months.

items.statement: Exports 81.6% of revenue; core markets CIS, Middle East, Africa, LatAm
items.quote: Exports constituted 81.6% of the total revenue. The core markets of CIS, Middle East and Africa, Latin America accounted for 81.6% to INR12.6 crores.

items.statement: French Africa registrations expected 6 months after January sample submission
items.quote: In the month of Jan, our samples are to be submitted, and we should be receiving registrations maybe 6 months from that.

items.statement: Held back shipments in Q2 already dispatched in Q3
items.quote: This has already gone and it is on the way.

items.statement: Net debt INR6.7 crores as of September 2025
items.quote: the net debt position as of September was at INR6.7 crores.

items.statement: Future PPP projects may require market fundraising if above INR30-40 crores
items.quote: But if something requires maybe INR30 crores, INR40 crores, then we might go to the market to raise funds.

items.statement: Exploring 1-2 new PPP ventures similar to SPL Infusion model
items.quote: And very soon, we may tie up with 1 or 2 like similar venture, which will be disclosed to the stakeholders.

items.statement: Employee costs stabilizing due to modernization and AI-driven efficiency
items.quote: We have done certain modernization in our facilities. And with the help of AI, we have quantified and work everything is the modernization is going on in a very high speed in the plant.

items.statement: Aim to deliver double-digit EBITDA growth in H2 FY26
items.quote: As margin pressures ease gradually, we aim to deliver double digit EBITDA growth in the second half.

items.statement: Expect double-digit EBITDA growth on 2-year CAGR basis into FY27
items.quote: One needs to look at a double digit profitability growth over a 2-year CAGR basis which we are pretty confident about.

items.statement: Operating margin to improve by at least 200 bps in FY27
items.quote: Depending on where we end at this year, we are confident that next year, operating margin will definitely see an improvement of at least 200 basis points.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio ARR target 2.5x FY24 by FY27
items.quote: We are on track to reach 2.5x of FY '24 ARR in FY '27 in line with our aspiration.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio targets double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27
items.quote: We remain sharply focused on profitability and aspire to achieve double digit EBITDA margins in this portfolio by FY '27.

items.statement: Foods portfolio to return to higher growth trajectory by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are extremely confident that by Q4, we will get back into higher growth rate on Foods.

items.statement: India volume grew 7% in Q2 FY26 despite GST disruption
items.quote: We have delivered a 7% volume growth in India in spite of the disruptions in September.

items.statement: GST disruption caused ~2% volume impact in Q2 FY26
items.quote: You can take around 2% during Quarter 2.

items.statement: Quick commerce nearly doubled year-on-year
items.quote: Quick com has nearly doubled on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Gross margins have bottomed out and will improve from here
items.quote: Gross margins definitely have bottomed out and as we move ahead, we only improve from here.

items.statement: VAHO margin higher than company level, significantly higher in focus areas
items.quote: The margin at VAHO level is higher than the company level margins, significantly higher and especially the things we are focusing in.

items.statement: Parachute margin compression drove large part of H1 margin erosion
items.quote: A very large part of the margin erosion is because of Parachute margin compression.

items.statement: Copra prices down 15% from July 2025 highs, expected to settle further from March 2026
items.quote: On Copra prices, it has come down actually from 15% from the highs seen in July 25. Current forecasts and our crop estimate outlook suggest that Copra market is likely to settle down over the course of the next few quarters and start coming down March onwards.

items.statement: VAHO premium segment grew double-digit; franchise gained 150 bps value market share MAT
items.quote: The franchise gain ed 150 bps in value market share on a MAT basis. The mid and premium segment s of the portfolio continued to record double -digit volume growth in this quarter.

items.statement: Foods portfolio crossed Rs 1,100 crore ARR; Saffola Oats gaining share, Honey and Soya Chunks scaling well
items.quote: The Food portfolio has crossed Rs. 1,100 crore ARR. Saffola Oats continue to gain market share while the Honey and Soya Chunks continue to scale up well.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio exited Q2 FY26 with ARR over Rs 1,000 crore
items.quote: The digital first portfolio exited the quarter with an ARR of over Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Plix personal care focus to drive profitability; hero SKUs contribute 50-60%+ of sales
items.quote: Our effort is focused on ensuring that, for a successful digital business, hero SKUs contribute at least 50–60% of sales and in our case, the contribution is even higher.

items.statement: Project SETU enabling range selling, reducing wholesale dependency, expanding direct coverage
items.quote: Project SETU has enabled range selling, which has directly contributed to a significant improvement in the trajectory of VAHO growth.

items.statement: Organized trade, especially quick commerce, leading growth; quick commerce nearly doubled YoY
items.quote: Organized trade, specially quick commerce continue to lead growth for the business. Quick com has nearly doubled on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: VAHO industry growth entering double digits in value; category building and premiumization driving growth
items.quote: If I have grown say 16% and gained share, you can derive a number. So, it should be in double digits, a little bit, entering double digits definitely in value.

items.statement: GST rate rationalization benefited ~30% of India business; benefits passed to consumers via price cuts or grammage increases
items.quote: About 30% of our India business have benefited from the GST revision. Consistent with the government's objective, we have passed on the benefits of the reduced GST rates to the consumers across relevant categories, either through price cuts or grammage increase in price point packs.

items.statement: BTL spend to be converted to ATL over next 2-3 years via Project SETU
items.quote: Another important outcome is that we are controlling resource allocation—a lot of below-the-line spend that was wasted will now be converted to above-the-line over the next 2–3 years.

items.statement: Saffola Foods organic growth (ex-discontinued) ~8% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The Organic Saffola Foods ex of some of the discontinued products in the base has grown by about 8%.

items.statement: VAHO 2-year CAGR (ex-Shanti Amla) ~9%; premium non-Shanti Amla volume in double digits
items.quote: The 2-year CAGR minus Shanti Amla, because as I said that we are defocused by LUP of Shanti Amla, the value is around 9%. And if you take this year also, the volume for the premium part which is the non-Shanti Amla portfolio, is in double digits.

items.statement: Copra price outlook uncertain; margin recovery depends on commodity deflation from March 2026

items.statement: All products manufactured per BIS standards, quality certified by authorized hallmark center

items.statement: Medium-term target of 4% PBT by Q4 FY27

items.statement: Project One annualized savings INR110-120 crores, in-year savings INR50-60 crores

items.statement: Net debt INR285.7 crores as of September 2025 vs INR232.2 crores March 2025

items.statement: GST rate reduction expected to boost consumption and volumes in India
items.quote: I think the reduction of GST rates should make consumption go up. So we believe that there should be great opportunities, both on the production side and also on the distribution side.

items.statement: GFS segment under severe macro stress globally, peers also under pressure
items.quote: if you look at it across the Board, we benchmarked peers with the leading GFS companies and they are all under severe stress. So this segment is something which we need to keep a watch on.

items.quote: the tariff is probably impacting only a very small portion of the India GFS business. So it doesn't have an overall significant I thought I said that to Disha's question also that it doesn't impact the business of TVS Supply Chain Solutions as a wh ole.

items.statement: European markets remain subdued with soft demand in industrial automation and power infrastructure
items.quote: The broader Europe market continues to remain subdued as the region moves through a gradual recovery, demand remains soft across industrial automation and power infrastructure, and government priorities have shifted towards defence spending.

items.statement: Strong export demand and deeper customer engagement driving standalone growth
items.quote: This growth was driven primarily by robust export demand that we had, deeper customer engagements, and successful conversions of some of the new opportunities which we were working in the last quarter.

items.statement: Close to 1,000 orders booked for single-phase inverter at exhibition

items.quote: So, the whole procurement has been challenged, and we have taken out about 4%-5% cost out of procurement cost. So, this is for good and sustainable.

items.quote: With sustained momentum from new product launches, the expanding geographical coverage, we remain confident of achieving about 12%-15% topline growth in this electronics business by end of this year.

items.quote: We have got many distributed customers. Unlike the Aluminum business, where it is focused with 6-7 or maybe 7-8 major customers, the electrical business, both in Lumel and in Rishabh is very well spread out.

items.statement: White labeling accounts for 18-20% of total turnover with two long-term customers
items.quote: We have two major customers for whom we white label, and I think it will not be more than 20%, maybe 18%-19%.

items.quote: I am pleased to report that our consolidated revenue grew by about 7.7% in Q2 FY '26 and 9.9% in H1 FY '26 on the year-on-year basis compared to the last year.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 12.1% YoY in Q2 FY26 and 14.6% in H1 FY26
items.quote: Our standalone business delivered a strong performance with revenues increasing by 12.1%, as you heard, during the quarter and 14.6% during the first half of the year, on a year-on-year basis.

items.quote: We have grown our revenues by 33.6% in Q2 FY '26 over Q1 FY '26, reflecting a robust and progressive growth. On a year-on-year basis, the revenue grew by 10.4%.

items.quote: US obviously has been a challenge for eve ryone, likewise for Rishabh, but we have found out a solution between our customers and our office in the US on how to address the issues which Trump has created over the last couple of

items.quote: Further, the planned phase-out of loss-making contracts will temporarily weigh on revenues in the coming quarters, which we have told you repeatedly and Q3-Q4 may reflect some losses, consistent again with our guidance which we had given earlier.

items.statement: Building strong management team, filling gaps with external experts and good hiring

items.statement: Aspiration for 20-22% topline CAGR and 25% bottomline CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: So, I would say realistically, if we plan about 20% and deliver 22%, I will be very happy, 22% CAGR on the topline and maybe 25% in the bottomline.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin for core zinc oxide business is 10%-11%; consolidated margin expected to reach 13%-14% in 2-3 years as non-rubber share grows to ~30%
items.quote: we have always maintained that the steady-state EBITDA margins in our core manufacturing business of Zinc oxide is 10% to 11% range. And we expect the margins to inch up to about 13% to 14% on a consolidated level as the share of non-rubber applications increase in the overall revenue stream.

items.statement: Tyre industry expected to grow 7%-8% annually; GST cuts may push growth slightly higher
items.quote: the tyre industry is expected to grow between 7% and 8% in the next couple of years. That is what the projections from the certain independent bodies. And that time we were not aware of the GST cuts which were going to happen. Now, with the current GST cuts, etc., the tyre demand seems to be quite good. And we are witnessing a good quarter demand. And hopefully this will translate to a certain sli

items.quote: on a year-on-year basis, on a half-year basis, the company has recorded more than 20% growth in revenues in the Zinc sulphate segment.

items.statement: Q3 seeing good demand after flat Q2; tyre industry growth expected 7%-8% with upside from GST cuts; non-rubber applications (pharma, cosmetics, ceramics, specialty chemicals) showing steady traction
items.quote: after a flat Q2, with GST rate implementation, the new GST rate pushed purchases, the current Q3 is seeing good demand. The tyre industry in general is expected to grow well in the coming year. And the company is very well positioned to capture this growth also.

items.quote: We are also expanding proactively into non-rubber applications and aim to increase the non-rubber share from the current 15% to over 30% in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.94% (down 0.7% YoY) due to higher-cost inventory from shipping delays; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.29%; margins expected to normalize and improve with logistics stabilizing and zinc prices rising
items.quote: The very marginal 0.7% decline in EBITDA margin during the quarter was primarily due to the consumption of higher cost inventory arising from shipping delays in the previous period. This was a temporary factor, and we are already seeing normalization. With logistics stabilizing and zinc prices showing improvement, we expect margins to be much better in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Total working capital cycle (incl. finished goods and raw materials) 60-90 days; zinc inventory (raw + finished) roughly two months
items.quote: our total working capital cycle, including finished goods and raw materials, is roughly about close to 90 days, 60 to 90 days, depending on how the situation is. So, that is a broad idea for you.

items.statement: Paid dividend of Rs 1 per share for FY24-25; expect to continue dividend payout in future years
items.quote: I am also happy to mention here that the company recently paid a dividend of Rs. 1 per share for the FY '24-25. We expect to continue the dividend payout in future years.

items.quote: As far as the technology for processing scrap is concerned, this is 100% an internally developed technology. It is an IP that is internally owned. And this has been done over the last two decades of trials, errors, learning, and continuous R&D.

items.quote: if there is a very, very sharp swing in prices of zinc, upward or downward, there could be an impact on our margins. But if the movement in zinc prices of the same quantum is over a longer period, that will not have much impact on our margins.

items.quote: the trials will start from Q4. Currently, we have set up a pilot line for the same and we will be working very closely with some of our established customers to develop grades for this recycled rubber which tailor makes their requirement.

items.quote: At present, the mix is 50-50. Going forward, we are planning to keep it at 30-70, 30-internal and 70-extra.

items.quote: So, small, small additions will do. For that, I don’t think we’ll have to go to the capital market. items.quote: We have already received approval from Rajasthan, Punjab, and Chhatt isgarh and permission from Bihar and Karnataka are expected shortly

items.quote: We have signed MOUs with Delta Electronics India for collaboration in the battery energy storage system, green hydrogen, and EV charging infrastructure, as well as green am monia, JV with AHES, Korea, and GH2 Solar, India

items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA was ₹ 254.8 crore, up 50% year -on-year, and EBITDA margins were at 46% , an expansion of 7 percentage points year-on-year.

items.statement: India hospitality EBITDA margin expanded 9 percentage points YoY to 41% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our India hospitality business delivered an EBITDA of ₹ 78.5 crore, up 47% year-on-year. EBITDA margin was at 41% , an expansion of 9% points over Q2 of last year.

items.statement: International hospitality EBITDA margin expanded 7 percentage points YoY to 14% in Q2 FY26

items.statement: Annuity business maintains 90% EBITDA margins with 98% committed occupancy

items.statement: Pune benefits from limited new luxury supply for next 5 years and strong corporate demand

items.statement: Maldives solar installation program commenced across all 3 resorts to reduce diesel dependency and stabilize power costs
items.quote: Our solar installation program is now commenced across all 3 resorts, helping reduce diesel dependency, stabilize power costs, and strengthen our long-term margin profile.

items.quote: We plan to invest ₹100 crore in a phased manner for refurbishment of existing rooms, development of additional keys, new F&B outlet and spa.

items.statement: Total capex of ₹2,000-2,200 crore over next 5 years for owned assets including Bangalore refurbishment, Sri Lanka resort and Varanasi hotel
items.quote: So altogether, we will spend around ₹2,000 - ₹2,200 crore over the next five years.

items.statement: Acquired 76% stake in 104-key Hilton Goa Resort at ₹320 crore enterprise value with ₹120 crore initial cash outflow
items.quote: With the Hilton Goa Resort, we have acquired 76% in a running hotel with an enterprise value of ₹ 320 crores, FY25 revenue of ₹50 crore and EBITDA of ₹18 crore, with a minimal initial cash outflow of only ₹120 crore.

items.statement: Proposed acquisition of 51% stake in Soho House India for ~₹60 crore including operational Juhu property and Delhi development
items.quote: Moving on to proposed investment in S oho House India, we plan to invest approximately ₹60 crore for a 51% stake in Soho bo Pvt Ltd , which holds exclusive development and operating rights for Soho Houses and cities without houses in India.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to ₹1,646 crore as of Sep 30, 2025 with cash balances of ₹484 crore

items.quote: Same-store EBITDA rose 91%, with EBITDA margin up 5 percentage points to 13%.

items.statement: Sri City factory Phase 1: RAC line operational by Oct 2026, compressor line by Q4 FY27; washing machine and refrigerator lines thereafter; full capacity by FY29
items.quote: The first product line of operations will be room air conditioners, which will be operational by October 2026, followed by aircon compressor line in Quarter 4 of Fiscal Year ' 27. Thereafter, washing machine and refrigerator line will begin in a phased manner.

items.statement: Exports contribute 5-6% of revenue; H1 FY26 exports reached almost 7% vs 6% full year FY25; 54 countries served
items.quote: Exports to 54 neighboring countries, including Nepal, Bangladesh, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia, contribute to 5 % to 6% of LGEIL's revenue.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 8.9% vs 12.4% YoY due to commodity prices, festive GTM investments, recycling costs; price hikes of 1.5-2% taken in Oct for refrigerator and washing machine
items.quote: During the quarter, we recorded a quarterly EBITDA of INR 5.48 billion, with an EBITDA margin of 8.9% compared to INR 7.57 billion and a margin of 12.4% in Quarter 2 of previous year.

items.statement: Price increase of 1.5% to 2% implemented in October for refrigerator and washing machine; promotional intensity rationalized post-Diwali
items.quote: Regarding margin normalization, we have also taken a little bit price increase of 1.5% to 2% for our refrigerator and washing machine case. We have also rationalized our promotional intensity, and our ongoing localization is already happening.

items.statement: Q2 demand impacted by cool summer, early monsoon, currency volatility, US tariffs, Indo-Pak tensions; GST rate cut announcement Aug 15 and implementation Sep 22 revived consumer confidence
items.quote: The first half of the year witnessed muted momentum across the consumer durable sector, shaped by a combination of external headwinds. Demand was notably impacted by an unexpected cooler summer, early monsoon, currency volatility, U.S. tariffs, and geopolitical tensions, particularly the Indo -Pak situation, leading to a cautious consumer sentiment.

items.statement: B2B contributes ~6% of sales driven by HVAC and information display; win rate strong, healthy pipeline; timing shift due to US tariffs, no structural demand issue
items.quote: Our B2B business is contributing roughly 6% of our business, and it is majorly driven by IT and information display panel and HVAC. Currently, we have seen there is a pressure on this segment due to U.S. tariff changes that led to the budgetary allocation and key segments like IT and display solution.

items.statement: Working capital cycle INR 2.2bn as of Sep 30 2025 vs INR 2.0bn Mar 31 2025; increase due to compressor-led inventory and extended credit to trade partners
items.quote: As of 30 th September 2025, our working capital cycle stood at INR 2.2 billion, as compared to INR 2.0 billion as of 31st March 2025 last year. The increase was primarily due to incremental inventory in compressor-led products and temporary credit support to extend additional payment days to our trade partners.

items.statement: Localization at 55.8% in Q2 FY26, improved 2-3% annually over last 3 years; target ~70% in 3-4 years; in-house compressor production since FY23, OLED TV and side-by-side localized at Pune
items.quote: Localization rose to 55.8% in Q2 FY '26, thanks to in-house side-by-side and compressor production. Under the Make in India initiative, we are committed to drive our localization further.

items.statement: GST rate cut announced Aug 15, implemented Sep 22 boosted demand; recycling target FY26 70% vs 60% FY25; BEE star rating for HVAC coming soon; Sri City gets 100% capital subsidy over 20 years
items.quote: However, a key development during the quarter was the GST rate cut announcement on August 15. This timely policy intervention helped revive consumer confidence and supported the demand outlook. The implementation of the revised rates on September 22 gave a strong and positive push to sales in key categories.

items.statement: Exports 5-6% of revenue to 54 countries; Global South strategy to expand premium exports from Sri City factory; government tariff agreements with US expected to help
items.quote: Under the Global South initiative to expand business in the emerging market, LGEIL now stands at the center of LG HQ's export strategy. LGEIL plans to identify new export destinations from our third manufacturing facility to expand exports of premium products to wider markets.

items.quote: We are using the plant at optimum capacity. We are running it at 90% to 95% level.

items.statement: Surat Greenfield plant nearing completion, expected to commence operations in H2 FY26

items.statement: Existing plants running at 70-80% average utilization, some lines at 100%
items.quote: On an average, I think 70 % to 80% is utilized and new capacity will also get added in this coming quarter now.

items.statement: Surat plant will take 3-4 quarters to ramp to full capacity of INR 250 crore revenue potential
items.quote: Surat will take some time to ramp up to that capacity, right? I think in terms of, like, of course, capacity will be available, but we will take at least three quarters, four quarters to reach the full capacity.

items.statement: Sales mix shifting toward higher-margin frozen products, driving margin expansion
items.quote: But within standalone also, our sales mix has changed towards frozen, more of frozen where the gross margin is higher. And the EBITDA is also higher for us.

items.statement: Retail store count grew from 1,600 to 2,000 driven by Safeway Albertsons (200+ stores) and Costco (75 stores)
items.quote: That is correct. Only Costco works on an in and out. The rest of them are normally permanent listings. So, the jump from 1,600 to 2,000, as you know, most of these guys are pan-US, Costco was a large part of it, Costco was about 7 5 stores. But when you get listings, I think the major jump happened with Safeway Albertsons, which I think was about 200- odd stores.

items.statement: No price increases taken; tariff costs passed to distributors and consumers; rupee depreciation improves realizations
items.quote: As far as tariff is concerned, right now, we have passed on. We are not taking anything. Basically, we are selling at the same price at which we were selling it before to the distributors. And then onwards, they are also selling it. So, basically, any tariff which will be borne by the distributors will be passed on to the consumers into this market.

items.statement: Freight cost at ~8% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: Yes, it will be in a similar range, around say 8% on a consol basis.

items.statement: Volume growth contributed ~70% of revenue growth, price growth ~30%
items.quote: So, volume growth will be almost 70% of the total growth which you have seen, and the rest will be the price growth.

items.statement: Net debt-free balance sheet with robust net cash of INR 89 crores
items.quote: The company's financial position also remains strong, with a net debt free balance sheet and robust net cash balance of INR 89 crores.

items.statement: India market entry targeting INR 100 crore revenue in 3-4 years via quick commerce and modern trade
items.quote: Our strategy for India is more on the quick commerce and modern trade side. We do not want to get into general trade. Our product range is more for urban India. And in terms of goal, we are looking at building about INR 100 crore business in the next three years to four years in a gradual phase manner.

items.statement: US tariff situation dynamic, monitoring competition; government expected to close trade deal in couple of weeks
items.quote: So, tariff as of now, I mean, the situation is dynamic in nature and we are monitoring closely to see what competition is doing. But as of now, we have maintained our prices. items.quote: Currently, we pay, we pay duties in the range of 4% to 15%. Once the FTA comes in, it will effectively go down to zero, which we will pass on 100% to the consumer.

items.statement: Forex gain of ~INR 4 crores in other income, additional gains embedded in revenue from rupee depreciation
items.quote: I will say in terms of right now, around INR 4 crores of forex gain is sitting in other income and maybe couple of crores will be in top line itself, because that is a number which you cannot really identify as such.

items.statement: H1 FY26 demand and installation impacted by incessant rains from May to October; Q2 revenue flat year-on-year
items.quote: The incessant rains from May to as late as October impacted micro irrigation demand as well as installation. Hence, Q2F26 was affected.

items.statement: Unrecognized work order pipeline for irrigation projects stands at about Rs.76 crores
items.quote: Today, we have got an unrecognized work order pipeline of about Rs.76 crores for irrigation projects, and besides this, we are also exploring export markets in coordination with Mahindra and Mahindra's international operations.

items.statement: Non-subsidy business contribution reached 37.8% of total revenue in H1 FY26, up from 3% in FY20
items.quote: In fact, you will be happy to note that we have reached a 37.8% contribution of the non-subsidy business to the total business in H1 FY26, compared to a mere 3% contribution in FY20.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain non-subsidy revenue share at around 37% for the rest of FY26
items.quote: So, we think, frankly, that we have done very well to get it to 37%, 37%-plus already and we would be hoping to maintain it at these levels for the rest of this year.

items.statement: Receivables increased by Rs.9.4 crores versus FY25 but debtor days improved by about six days
items.quote: The receivables in H1FY26 were higher versus FY25 by about Rs.9.4 crores. This was on account of an increase in receivables during H2FY25, and the skew towards certain opportunity states with longer collection cycles, and the delayed fund release in these states also led to increased receivables. However, it is noteworthy to mention that the receivables in terms of days of sales has gone down by a

items.statement: Management expects cash flow improvement in H2 FY26 due to better subsidy release likelihood
items.quote: We do expect an improvement in the next six months. So, obviously, the mix that we have of the different states impacts us on an ongoing basis. And in the following six months, we do expect an improvement because we are seeing a possibility of better cash flow, we are seeing better likelihood of subsidy release, and we think some momentum is definitely building there.

items.statement: Non-subsidy business currently has lower margins than subsidy business but is not loss-making; margins expected to improve as brand establishes
items.quote: Yes. So, Aditya, I just want to confirm that we are definitely not losing money on our non-subsidy business. So, there is definitely no negative impact on our total margin in terms of loss-making because of our non-subsidy business. I just want to clarify that.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable in H1 FY26; strategic sourcing and better mix delivered 1.7% total material cost saving versus H1 FY25
items.quote: During this period, raw material prices were stable. That, along with our strategic sourcing initiatives, has enabled your company to deliver material cost saving of 0.4% versus H1FY25. The rest of the total 1.7% material cost saving versus H1F Y25 can be attributed to the impact of a better mix, a better mix in terms of businesses, states, and products

items.statement: Distributed manufacturing with satellite units and main unit in Nasik improves asset utilization and controls freight and processing costs
items.quote: For a better control over freight and processing costs for the last few years, we have been efficiently managing distributed manufacturing with satellite units, while our main unit continues to be in Nasik. This also has improved our asset utilization.

items.statement: Revenue in Uttar Pradesh now in double-digits and expected to grow further; focus on establishing foundation before aggressive expansion
items.quote: In UP, our revenues are now in double-digits and we expect them to grow further. We would obviously want our foundation to be well established before we go aggressively in the new states.

items.statement: Export opportunities being explored in Africa leveraging M&M tractor division relationships; early stage with both government and private sector opportunities
items.quote: We have got a very big tractor business as you know, and they have a strong presence in many parts of the world, in Africa, for example. And a lot of the opportunities that we receive in terms of export are through the existing relationships that our tractor team has, both with end customers as well as with the trade.

items.statement: GST on micro irrigation reduced from 12% to 5%, expected to positively impact demand in medium-to-long-term
items.quote: The recent GST changes, i.e. the reduction of GST on micro irrigation from 12% to 5%, is likely to have a positive impact on demand in the medium-to-long-term.

items.statement: Government targets 2 million hectares annually (10 million hectares over five years) versus ~1 million hectares in FY25
items.quote: The Hon'ble Prime Minister is pushing for 1 crore hectares to be covered in the next five years, which translates to an average of 2 million hectares a year versus about 1 million hectares in the FY25.

items.statement: Extended monsoon suppressed demand and installation across industry in Q2 FY26; farmer loan waiver requests in Gujarat being monitored
items.quote: The incessant rains have definitely impacted the industry. And that is really something that is by way of suppression of demand, suppression of installation, etc., So, it is a direct linkage there. And Gujarat is not an exception in that sense. That is a phenomenon that we see across the country.

items.statement: Manpower cost for FY25 was Rs.31.8 crores, single-digit growth versus FY20 despite six years of inflation
items.quote: Just to quote a few examples, manpower cost for FY25 was Rs.31.8 crores, which is a single-digit growth compared to FY20 levels, despite inflation over these six years.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward revenue guidance but aims to grow faster than industry
items.quote: We do not give forward guidance, but what we are always focused on is growing faster than the industry. And that is what we really want to do and we will keep working on.

items.statement: R&D spend target 2-3% of PAT over medium term
items.quote: But going forward, maybe we can reach 2%-3% of PAT, which we think is sufficient for the size of our Company and the kind of business we are in.

items.quote: Our production volumes are fully committed for calendar year FY'26.

items.quote: In 2nd Quarter, which is normally is always affected with the monsoon season but however, in this quarter, we have done export of 1.33 million tons of bauxite which is almost double when compared to the previous corresponding quarter of last financial year.

items.quote: The recent commissioning of our 9-megawatt solar plant, which is linked to this bleaching clay plant under the group captive model, has helped to lower cost and reinforce our sustainability goals. items.quote: So, being a converter, our margins are fixed. The fluctuation in the metal is , we cover the fluctuation via MCX or LME. So, we are 95%-98% hedged on the commodities. Our margins are fixed once we have a conversion fixed with the customer.

items.quote: We are focused on OEMs. We are focused on auto. We are focused on high -end solar products. So, where the customer is quality conscious. So, once we saw this, we said, okay, now it may be the right time.
