items.quote: This first half year that is quarter one and quarter two. The sales are mostly affected by a monsoon. Prolonged monsoon had affected our sales but the trend is now on the growing side.

items.statement: Distribution business down 30% in H1 FY26 due to commoditization; pivoted to new product basket
items.quote: In distribution, though it may seem you know a trading type of business, there are many industry specific constraints that came up because commoditization of certain products that we were doing for few years.

items.statement: Employee cost 23% of revenue in H1 FY26 (up from 21%); 950 employees on payroll; high due to on-site deployment for monitoring and O&M services
items.quote: Our employee cost has increased from 21% to 23%

items.statement: Competition from small startups breaking prices without delivering service levels creates margin pressure
items.quote: There are many small startups, people who leave larger companies can do small, small things on their own and they end up spoiling the market because they break pricing, they don't deliver service at that level

items.statement: Demerger of construction chemicals and water treatment business completed in FY25; post-demerger compliances on track
items.quote: We completed our demerger/merger activities in this financial year in last financial year. So all the post demerger compliances where are on track now

items.statement: Targeting Rs 350-360 Cr revenue in FY26
items.quote: Sir, we are targeting around 350 Cr.-360 Cr. like revenue in this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 500-600 Cr revenue next year and Rs 1,000 Cr in two years with same PAT margins
items.quote: So, we are targeting at least Rs. 500 Cr. in the next financial year Rs. 500 Cr. to Rs. 600 Cr. and Rs. 1,000 CR in the next two years with more or less same PAT margins.

items.statement: Targeting order book of Rs 1,000 Cr by FY26-27
items.quote: We are targeting an order book of Rs. 1,000 crores by FY26-27.

items.statement: Expecting 80% capacity utilization by September 2026
items.quote: I think by the end of September, we will be like 80% capacity, you can say it will be in 80% capacity within September, like next September.

items.statement: Expecting EPC revenue of Rs 150-200 Cr in FY27 and Rs 500-700 Cr thereafter
items.quote: In FY27, again, it depends upon the order we achieve. Most of the tenders are coming in January, February, March period only. So, it depends upon the order book order, like how much orders we get. Then we are targeting around at least, say, 150 Cr.-200 Cr, like revenue to be booked in the next financial year. And after that, like a major 500 Cr.-700 Cr.

items.statement: Expecting EPC EBITDA margins of 8-9%
items.quote: Say, it's around like 7%-8%-9%. It should remain in that range only.

items.statement: Expecting consolidated EBITDA margins around 15-16% for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margins should remain around 15% or 16%, like something like that only.

items.statement: Spent Rs 16.45 Cr on existing facility; further Rs 6-7 Cr for cables division; total Rs 160-170 Cr needed for Rs 1,000 Cr revenue target
items.quote: So, Rs. 16.45 Cr. to be precise, we have already spent on the existing facility, including the land and building cost and the plant and machinery cost. And we will be like further spending around Rs. 6 Cr. to Rs. 7 Cr. in the upcoming few days only for the cables division.

items.statement: Conductor division at new Dankuni facility to start by December 2025 or January 2026; cable division to follow; capacity to double by March 2026 and target 4-5x in 2-3 years
items.quote: We are expecting the Conductor Division will be installed in December only. So, we will be getting the handover of property on 12 th or 13 th December, and we have already placed the machine. By that time, all the machines will be at our place only and we are trying to start the Conductor Division within December or maybe in January 1 st week. And then after that, we will be installing our cables

items.statement: Order book at Rs 286.21 Cr as of Sep 30, 2025 (2.36x H1 revenue); execution over 1.5 years
items.quote: Order book stands at a robust Rs. 286.21 Cr. as of September 30, 2025, about 2.36x H1 revenue, providing strong visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.85% vs 13.62% in FY25; PAT margin 9.82% vs 8.84%
items.quote: For FY'25, we did an EBITDA margin of 13.62% and for half-year FY'26, our EBITDA margins are around 15.85% and our PAT margins for FY'I25, it was 8.84% and for half-year FY'26, it's 9.82%.

items.statement: Government tenders have price variation clauses linked to LME; debit/credit notes raised accordingly; inventory and supplier relations managed for competitive pricing
items.quote: First of all, all the major projects which are going on have PV, price variation clauses in the government tenders because it's not possible for the contractor to work at the same price for the next upcoming 18 months or 24 months. So, normally all the major contracts are having price variation clauses. So, we raise debit note or credit note depending upon the LME prices of the raw materials.

items.statement: Majorly supply to EPC contractors; also participating directly in government tenders; vendor approvals from Himachal Pradesh and Punjab secured; Rajasthan approvals expected soon
items.quote: First of all, we are majorly supplying to EPC contractors and we are also participating in direct government tenders also. We are aggressively participating right now in government tenders for supply of cables also.

items.statement: Plan to add HTLS conductor, MVCC, AL-59 conductors, 11kV HT cables at new facility; exploring data center, solar cables, house wires via distributorship
items.quote: We are also adding new products also in that facility, like HTLS conductor, MVCC, AL-59 conductors, and module 11kV cables HT cables, etc. We will be adding new products also in that unit.

items.statement: Created dedicated EPC division headed by Whole-Time Director Rajesh Jhunjhunwala for forward integration; participated in Rs 60 Cr tenders; targeting Rs 1,000 Cr order book in two years
items.quote: We are aggressively expanding our presence in EPC projects and have created a dedicated EPC division headed by Mr. Rajesh Jhunjhunwala, our Whole-Time Director, which will provide a strong forward integration advantage. We are targeting an order book of Rs. 1,000 crores by FY26-27. We have already participated in tenders aggregating approximately Rs. 60 crores and are awaiting the results, and we

items.statement: Trade receivables at Rs 68 Cr; government payments via EPC contractors with minor 10-20 day delays; IPO proceeds to optimize working capital
items.quote: We are mainly supplying right now to major EPC players and like we have good understanding with them and like some of them are quite a big name. So, we are supplying regularly to them. And like suppose the delay, maybe if it's say 10-15-20 days, like but not a major delay normally.

items.statement: Internal accruals insufficient for EPC expansion; equity infusion needed in 6-12 months for EPC project capital requirements
items.quote: We need equity in the further six months or one year. Because we are expanding to like EPC contracts as well, where there will be a fund requirement. And if we will win, like say a good sizable amount of order, we will be needing a sizable amount of capital for executing those projects.

items.statement: H1 FY26 total income Rs 121.44 Cr (+13% YoY); EBITDA Rs 19.24 Cr (+25% YoY); Net profit Rs 11.92 Cr (+16% YoY)
items.quote: The first half of financial year 2026 has been an encouraging period for JD Cables where we saw total income grew 13% year-on-year basis to Rs. 121.44 Cr. EBITDA increased 25% year-on-year basis to Rs. 19.24 Cr. with margins expanding to 15.85%. Net profit rose 16% year-on-year basis to Rs. 11.92 Cr. maintaining strong profitability at 9.82%.

items.statement: Strong demand in transmission and distribution; government-led investments (RDSS, grid expansion) driving growth; data center and solar cable opportunities emerging
items.quote: There is a lot of opportunity in the data center as well. We will definitely like to explore data center and solar cables in the near future, very soon And yes, our products are being used for electrification only for transmission and distribution.

items.statement: Competition exists across segments; major players like KEC, Polycab, Laser, Lumino, Cabcon also do EPC for forward integration
items.quote: Like see, competition is already in each and every segment, sector there is a competition. And like if you see the major players like KEC, KSC, Polycab, and then Calcutta-based, there are many companies like Laser, Lumino and Cabcon, all are into manufacturing cables as well as they are taking the EPC, because it gives you the forward integration advantage.

items.statement: Revenue split roughly 70% derivatives, 30% cash; derivatives pricing INR20 per order
items.quote: If you look at the pricing is very simple. We charge INR20 on the derivative side. The rest is on the cash. The split is actually very similar. Roughly, you can say 70% odd will be on the derivative side and 30 odd will be on the cash side

items.statement: 80% of customer acquisition is organic, rest primarily performance marketing and small word-of-mouth referral
items.quote: So for us, see organic is the biggest channel and almost I think we reported also almost 80% people come organically. The other channel is primarily the performance marketing, which is digital marketing that happens. And a very small part of it is referral, but we are not running a commercial referral.

items.statement: MTF book growing well; targeting double-digit market share over 3 years by expanding market rather than taking share
items.quote: And what we are expecting in the future is that we have a fair share that we want to kind of reach. And it will take at least three years to probably reach there. And the fair share is significantly higher than where we are today, probably like a double digit number on the market side

items.statement: LAS (loan against mutual funds) in early stage; loan against securities not yet launched; growth will scale as product features added
items.quote: So it is very -- LAS is very early stage today. So if you look at LAS is actually not even fully LAS. It is just loan against mutual funds as of now. Loan against securities is yet to be launched.

items.statement: Personal loan book INR1,140 crore, LAS book INR60 crore; credit loss INR70 crore on ~INR1,250 crore book; provisioning cost stabilizing
items.value: INR1,140 cr personal, INR60 cr LAS
items.quote: Our personal book size is INR1,140 crores. And our LAS book is about INR60 crores.

items.statement: Credit loss INR70 crore on book closer to INR1,250 crore; cost of provisioning has come off vs last quarter, book stabilizing
items.quote: I think from a book perspective, I think we are more closer to 1,250 odd. And hence, this number is slightly lower in percentages. And some of these are like variable in nature, we are still in a phase where we are stabilizing our book from a vintage perspective.

items.statement: Wealth management (Fisdom) contributing ~3% of revenue; distribution income across mutual funds, PMS/AIF, insurance, unlisted securities; PMS of mutual funds recently launched
items.quote: So on the wealth side, I think we are very early today. We did the acquisition on the Fisdom side, which got the balance sheet got consolidated as of 30th of September, but the P&L will start getting consolidated soon. And roughly 3% revenue is coming from that business.

items.statement: Derivatives share of revenue to fall below 50% as cash, MTF, commodities, wealth grow faster
items.quote: So I think it is beyond 50, definitely it can come below 50. But that is like output number in the way to look at where if everything else goes or grows faster, this definitely can come off.

items.statement: MTF contributes 3-4% of cash ADTO, adding ~INR2 per order to realization; each 3% MTF penetration adds another INR2
items.quote: So, roughly today, MTF as a percentage of cash ADTO is around 3% to 4%, because the pricing on MTF is different. Prayesh Jain: Right. Ishan Bansal: And hence, it is adding to a INR2 rupees of realization extra per order

items.statement: Commodities DTU 20,000-30,000; first-time users larger component than switchers; expect to reach fair share faster than MTF
items.quote: So, already I think we are seeing a good growth. We had a DTU of around 20,000 to 30,000 also happening on this product. And I think this will keep on growing in the future as well.

items.statement: Technology cost optimizations reduced cost-to-serve QoQ; still running at higher capacity for uptime, further optimization possible
items.quote: We have done some optimizations in last quarter, which has helped us to reduce this cost. And we've been kind of running at a significantly higher capacity just to maintain good, you can say, uptime for our customers.

items.statement: 832 core product employees, ~300 customer service, ~500 from Fisdom acquisition (including ~180 sales)
items.quote: So, we have 832 core employees who are involved in product business building and about 300 odd employees who are doing our customer services. And on the Fisdom side, we have acquired about 500 odd employees which have come with part of the acquisition.

items.statement: No specific regulatory risk foreseen over next two quarters; business-as-usual
items.quote: From a regulatory standpoint, I think it is BAU for us. There is no specific risk which we are foreseeing, Saket.

items.statement: Revenue per order up QoQ due to: 1) average ticket size growth, 2) June pricing action fully baked in, 3) cash/derivatives mix shift
items.quote: So there is a mix of multiple, I think, three reasons. One is the average ticket size helps us increase the revenue per order. The second thing is the pricing action one we took in June last year, June this year, was fully baked in in this quarter.

items.statement: FNO active users flat at ~1.4M for 2-3 quarters post-regulation churn; but average order per user up 10-20% as low-quality users exit, high-quality users grow
items.quote: But the quality of the user is like doing really well. So if you look at the average order per user have significantly grown, some of those numbers, you can look at it, will be kind of in the range of like 10% to 20% growth on average order per user

items.statement: CAC varies quarterly due to branding fixed cost and variable acquisition; full-year spend not expected to differ significantly from past; depends on market conditions
items.quote: So, Prayesh it is difficult to predict for the future, but I would say that it is not going to be very different from the -- the overall spends are not going to be very different from the previous times and acquisition overall numbers also depends on the how the market conditions are.

items.statement: MTF pricing (14.95%) not primary driver of platform choice; customer experience matters more; competition at 7.99% not seen as threat
items.quote: Our pricing is simple. It is 14.95%. Other than that, the growth rate I think it's not very -- we don't see competition from an MTF perspective specifically because it is a second product typically that customer is using.

items.statement: Disbursement via partners declined in Q2 due to market concerns on unsecured lending and transition to separate credit app; now recovering
items.quote: One is obviously the market related reasons where there was concern on unsecured lending itself. The second piece actually was more specific to us where we actually created a separate app for credit business and as we were moving customers from our existing product to that, there was a transition period which led to that drop for a intermittent time.

items.statement: Fisdom acquisition balance sheet consolidated Sep 30; P&L consolidation starting soon; currently near breakeven but negative contribution
items.quote: So currently, like I said, roughly, their run rate from a revenue perspective is around 3%. And on the contribution side, I think they're still negative. More we like breakeven, closer to breakeven, but still negative.

items.statement: AMC revenue INR17.99 million (insignificant); personal loan book INR1,140 cr; LAS book INR60 cr; MTF yield 14.95%
items.quote: It is about 17.99 million, very insignificant at this stage.

items.statement: Focus on wealth management as customers become affluent; broking to continue growing; new products: MTF, commodities, more to come
items.quote: Next 2 to 3 years, I think we are kind of super focused on few of the products that we have taken up, like, as one big data point that we are seeing, and we are also elaborated in our documents earlier that a lot of our customers now are kind of becoming affluent, and they need wealth management.

items.statement: New user quality similar to past vintages; ARPU viewed on annualized basis, not quarterly
items.quote: But you're right. The quality of the user that we are getting today looks similar to what we were getting earlier as well. It's not like significantly different from in the past as well.

items.statement: Unsecured loan disbursement 100% digital; collections mix of digital and physical
items.quote: So collection obviously is a mix of digital and physical. But on disbursement side, it is 100% digital. And that's how we operate both on book as well as on the distribution side.

items.statement: Pull-based product discovery; no push incentives or community building; enable seamless customer discovery
items.quote: Yeah, so Jayant, see I think again, like we are building more pull -based platform. So, customers kind of re-enable the discovery which is very well. So, customers find what they are looking for and we avoid any push-push.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of ~20% over FY26 and EBIT margin improvement of 1.5-2%
items.quote: say, top line would be, you know, about 20% growth over this year, and margins also should be higher because of operational, operational efficiency, because that is what has been holding us back. Otherwise, our value addition is quite good, but this additional turnover should help us to improve, margins by, anywhere between, 1.5% to 2% at EBIT level.

items.statement: Malur plant commenced operations, proving 1,000+ parts for Caterpillar; transition to complete by end of November
items.quote: Our new plant at Malor has successfully commenced operation. Facility has already begun proving over 1,000 parts for Caterpillar, which we previously supplied from our Bhamsundra plant.

items.statement: Paint shop at Malur plant expected to be commissioned in Q4 FY26; first phase deliveries started this month
items.quote: the entire system orders have been placed. And the... it will come in two phases, so some of the deliveries of parts and all that have started coming this month itself, and it will come into the factory, and it will be implemented in two phases.

items.statement: Pune and Vadodara plants operating at ~50% capacity, utilization improved ~10% this year; combined potential ~4 crore/month additional revenue in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Current capacity utilization, as we've talked about in the past, our capacity utilization has been quite poor at Pune and Vadodra, where we've been operating at around 50% capacity. But in this current year, both these plants have picked up and is doing better than last year, significantly better, I would say, more in terms of profitability than in turnover, but turnover also, utilization has gone

items.statement: Combined revenue potential at 80% utilization across all plants (including Malur) estimated at Rs 250 crore
items.quote: Ganesh Agrawal: 250 crore rupees. Harshad Patel: Okay, right. Yeah.

items.statement: Caterpillar indicated 25-40% volume increase from Jan 2026; Volvo ramping up significantly with new models
items.quote: customers are all ramping up. Now, they have given us indications that from January onwards, a significant improvement in offtake should be there. anywhere between 25% to 40% increase in volumes from the existing customers, including Volvo and a couple of others also, who are all in this earth-moving.

items.statement: Malur plant break-even at Rs 60 crore annual revenue (Rs 5 crore/month) including existing business; new revenue from Jan 2026, significant ramp-up from Q1 FY27
items.quote: In terms of value, it would be 60 crore rupees. 5 crore rupees a month. Harshad Patel: 5 crore rupees a month, but that is... that is including the existing business.

items.statement: Malur plant target Rs 100 crore annual revenue in 2-3 years; ~Rs 3.5 crore shifted from Bamsundra, additional Rs 6-6.5 crore to be added over 2 years
items.quote: the potential, for, for that particular plant, we were, we are talking about, was, something like 100 crores, coming out of that plant over a period of, next 2-3 years. Out of that, if we say that about 4 crores of... three... three and a half crores of business has moved from the old plant, so it... Additional 6, 6.5 crores revenue has to be generated from there, which will happen over the course

items.statement: Bamsundra plant capacity reset to Rs 48-50 crore/year (Rs 4 crore/month); currently at 40-45% utilization after Caterpillar shift; targeting fill-up within next year
items.quote: I would say that the existing Bangalore facility, the old one, should... I mean, we should keep that capacity as something like, you know, 48 to 50 crores. About 4 crores a month is what it should be able to run in a nice and a proper manner.

items.statement: Onboarding ~2 customers/month at Bamsundra plant including EV and food processing equipment MNCs
items.quote: So, now that that capacity has been vacated. So we are onboarding, you know, something like two customers a month. And, some businesses have started either in EV segment and, some other food processing equipment, and some customers have been added.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.93% vs 9.1% YoY, driven by better product mix; H1 FY26 margin up ~100 bps
items.quote: EBITDA improved from 3.57 crores in Q2 25 to 4.6 crores in 26, with margins growing from 9.1% to 9.93%, primarily due to better product mix. On half-yearly basis, revenues for 6 months, FY26 increased to 84 crores, up from 76 crores in the previous year, and EBITDA went up from 6.5 crores to 8.25 crores, with margins improving by about 100 basis points.

items.statement: Gross margins at 49% in Q2 FY26, in 47-49% band for last 4 quarters; management expects to maintain at least this level
items.quote: Margin-wise. I would say that even if we maintain margins at this level, it should be good. Last year, I mean, this quarter, margins were better because of some product mix, especially at the Puna facility, and that has helped because if you will see from the quarterly statement, the employee cost has gone up very significantly.

items.statement: Margin pressure in Q3 FY26 due to duplicate costs from running both Bamsundra and Malur plants; normalization expected by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: And that, I would say, by first quarter of next year, that should be okay. Last quarter also, there'll be revenue from this plant. So, to that extent, our margins will come back towards normalcy either in the fourth quarter of this year, or definitely in the first quarter of next year.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by raw material consumption ratio improvement, complex/high value-add orders, and threshold for order acceptance
items.quote: Primarily, our raw material consumption, that means the operating margin, raw material consumption to sales ratio, that has been improving. That is due to better processes, and more than that, I would say that the kind of orders that we are executing are of a little bit more complex nature than what we used to do in the past.

items.statement: Shift toward complex, engineered, high value-add parts including specialized welding jobs; automation enabling higher complexity
items.quote: the kind of orders that we are executing are of a little bit more complex nature than what we used to do in the past. So that is leading to better kind of margins than before. And we have kept a threshold also for accepting orders. If there is a lower than a certain value addition, we try not to get into that.

items.statement: Caterpillar aftermarket opportunity 4-5x current size; mining equipment pickup expected Q1 FY27; export tariffs expected to drop to 15-20%
items.quote: their aftermarket business, is, is, that market, that we are, sort of supplying from Pune facilities. And that is a very large opportunity, and there, it is up to us how much we can grab. So the challenge is more from our side than from theirs. They can go, you know, even four, five times higher than what we are currently

items.statement: Paint shop at Pune plant: CFE permission received, equipment orders not yet placed; needed for Caterpillar aftermarket ramp-up
items.quote: The permission, the first, permission, that is CFE, consent for, establishment, has come. Yeah, okay, yeah. We haven't placed order for equipment as of yet.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue Rs 42.9 crore (+9.8% YoY, +4.65% QoQ); H1 FY26 revenue Rs 84 crore (+10.5% YoY); EBITDA Rs 4.6 crore (Q2), Rs 8.25 crore (H1)
items.quote: In Q226, revenue was at 42.9 crores, as against 39.14 crores in Q225. And 41 crores in Q126. This was a marginal growth of 9.8% and 4.65% over the previous respective quarters.

items.statement: Personnel cost to sales at all-time high in Q2 FY26 due to dual-plant staffing during transition; profit still improved
items.quote: in fact, even in the... in this last quarter, for the results for which we have declared, our personnel cost to sale has been at an all-time high, because we've added more people, and revenues have not got generated. But despite higher personnel cost, profit has still been a little bit better.

items.statement: Paint shop delayed due to red-category pollution control approval; now received for both Malur and Pune
items.quote: the government approval, because, you know, these paint facilities, once you put, it is coming in red category under the pollution control laws. And that, that permission, has unfortunately got very... it was very much delayed

items.statement: Caterpillar export parts for mining equipment; tariff concerns expected to resolve with duties falling to 15-20%
items.quote: Their tariffs are likely to come down to about, you know, anywhere between 15% to 20%. So, on that assumption, we are all moving forward, and if that sort of happens, the export side for mining equipment should start picking up significantly after that.

items.statement: Caterpillar senior management to inaugurate robotics division at Malur plant in early December during XCON exhibition
items.quote: a very senior management team of CAT, which is going to be in India. at the time of XCON. They will be visiting our plant in early December, and the entire robotics division will be inaugurated by the very senior executive from CATUS

items.statement: Gujarat retail sales online portal (cut/bent parts) beta testing complete; full launch in December 2025; first-of-kind in India for this product category
items.quote: by another, another 15 days or so, we will come online with full-fledged online portal ordering. So. That also will get on stream. We are also participating in a couple of very big exhibitions now, the next one in December in Kandi Nagar, and January in Bangalore, where also we will use those platforms to get, this, this, ordering platform online.

items.statement: Expects growth better than industry rate in power production with solar addition
items.quote: Any solar project of this size, 4 megawatts, that is purely going to add the topline and the bottom-line. So the machine, whatever windmill also what we are doing, trying internal accruals, we are trying to use a bit for improving efficiency. So we can expect a growth, which is definitely be better than like industry growth rate in terms of power production.

items.statement: Raising INR 49.5 crore via rights issue to fund 4 MW solar project in Karnataka
items.quote: This rights issue is 49.5 crore level. And promoters, we are taking almost like our entire quota. Maybe we'll be taking a little more also. But then we may not get going by the past history because generally our shareholders have picked up everything. But we'll be happy to take a little more.

items.statement: Operating 54 MW wind farms; 4 MW solar project targeted for commissioning 3-4 months after rights issue completion by December
items.quote: Yes, we are depending on once the rights issue is over by December, we hope. I mean, allotment, everything by December, money will come in the hands. So probably 3 months to 4 months is what we are targeting. So the generally 6 months is what we have shown in the offer document.

items.statement: Plans to add at least 50 MW solar in next few years and targets doubling capacity in 3-year horizon
items.quote: So maybe we are looking at about adding at least 50 megawatt in the next few years, depending on funding availability and whatever support from the government.

items.statement: Identified potential for 25 MW hybrid solar addition at existing wind farms without new transmission investment
items.quote: And then hybrids are, we have a potential internally to add about 25 megawatt of hybrid without paying, without spending more for the transmission lines, along with our existing wind farms.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 59.32% in Q2 FY26 from 57.21% YoY; expects solar ROI similar or slightly better than wind
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 59.32% compared to 57.21% last year.

items.statement: Solar project costs relatively less than wind; ROI more or less same, solar could be slightly better with good radiation
items.quote: The solar project costs are relatively less compared to the wind capacity cost. So in terms of ROI, actually they are more or less the same. But in fact, solar could be a little better if radiation things are slightly better and easy to handle, the solar one.

items.statement: Existing customers in Tamil Nadu demanding ~50% more power (currently supplying 6 crore units); corporate green power demand growing 30% globally
items.quote: Today we are only giving about, Tamil Nadu around 6 crore units of power to customers. They themselves are asking almost like 50% more. So we are under pressure to deliver more, produce more units.

items.statement: Third-party power sales net price around INR 5-5.5 per unit; market stabilized with orderly competition
items.quote: So the price of, net price of around INR 5 per unit is what is now coming, plus the discounts have formed, the rules have come for a transmission costing. So now the industry has learned and adjusted.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with net worth ~INR 300 crore; borrowing capacity up to INR 800-900 crore per RBI guidelines
items.quote: We are a debt-free company. That is the whole advantage now. So bankers are chasing us. Because the net worth is around 300 crores, they are can give 500 crores-700 crores.

items.statement: Evaluating bond issuance and bank borrowing for future expansion; targeting long-term lenders with 8-9% cost vs 15%+ project IRR
items.quote: Then we are looking at talking to a few banks subject to approvals and then bond issue also we are looking at options. Definitely our net worth is already about INR 300 crore level. So we have not borrowed any money. So as per the RBI guidelines, we have a balance sheet net worth easily, which can support borrowing up to maybe INR 800 crores-INR 900 crores also.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic growth via acquisition of stressed wind assets under IBC near existing locations for cost and transmission synergies
items.quote: So we are looking at the options for that. So adding a project, sorry, as I said, acquiring under IBC, still there are some lot of stress assets in the system. So giving us an opportunity for acquisition.

items.statement: Open to strategic partnerships and JVs to co-own assets; land bank and substation infrastructure available for hybrid projects
items.quote: Yes, we are open for that because we have a lot of land banks in our kitty now. So we are a debt-free company as on date. So there are options for either go for borrowing and grow, or we can go with the JVs and industries.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu hybrid policy ~90% clear; allows adding solar to existing wind farms with 25% production improvement requirement
items.quote: Even the Tamil Nadu government, Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation also has announced an option for a hybrid, adding hybrid solar project to their existing windmill. So we'll be looking more in hybrid into Tamil Nadu to start with.

items.statement: Regulators mandated 6% annual power tariff increase providing pricing visibility
items.quote: But now two years back, the regulators have put their foot down and then said that every year there is going to be a 6% increase in the power tariff also, which is all giving for a kind of a positivity.

items.statement: GST impact of 18% absorbed by company as power sector cannot pass through GST; strained margins historically
items.quote: Withdrawal of subsidies, there is no power price also, it got reduced. Then GST was added to our entire expenditure, power being in the final industry, where we cannot pass through the GST to others. That means indirectly, the Company absorbed that 18% GST impact also.

items.statement: Wind farm efficiency currently ~14%; hybrid policy requires minimum 25% production improvement for eligibility
items.quote: Because the existing wind farms are giving only around 14% efficiency. So here now the new policies have come wherein it says that if you can improve your production by a minimum 25%, then you can go for a hybrid project.

items.statement: Targeting 5-10% machine efficiency improvement on existing 54 MW capacity through upgrades and better O&M
items.quote: One is the total capacity. Maybe in that existing 54 capacity, we are trying to improve some of the machines which can be upgraded, maybe 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Planning to start third-party O&M vertical; currently no external O&M contracts but evaluating opportunity
items.quote: We are planning to start a separate vertical for it to take the O&M for others also. But as of now, no, but going forward, we'll be doing it.

items.statement: Adding solar to balance seasonal wind generation; 4 MW solar at Hanamsagar, Karnataka for group captive/third-party sale
items.quote: This solar project we are starting is 4 megawatt. But then we have many wind capacities and lands are there in Karnataka too. So in future, we'll be looking at more solar. So they go hand in hand with the wind now.

items.statement: Hybrid wind-solar projects planned in Tamil Nadu leveraging existing substations and land; policy supports hybrid addition
items.quote: We are looking and Tamil Nadu, there is a policy wherein it says the hybrid policies are now already announced or at least in the full 90% clear. Even the Tamil Nadu government, Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation also has announced an option for a hybrid, adding hybrid solar project to their existing windmill.

items.statement: No operational volatility concerns; machine availability maintained, no finance issues, wind/solar resource variability managed by hybrid approach
items.quote: Volatility in what way? Because wind is nature, sun is nature. Machine availability, we always keep it properly and we don't have any finance issues like many companies face today in India. So I don't see any volatility concerns.

items.statement: O&M mostly in-house (34 MW); 20 MW outsourced where machine groups too small; plans to internalize O&M for new similar machines
items.quote: Out of the 54 megawatt, 18 is outsourced, plus 2 MW Machine and one machine, is about 20 megawatt is outsourced and remaining we are doing ourselves.

items.statement: Exploring data center JV opportunities at village locations with growing power and data demand; considering power trading license
items.quote: We are also looking at opportunities like data center, if somebody can come for a joint venture, since you asked me about it, since we are producing power anyway, so every village also now the data consumption in India is growing like a big way, apart from agriculture and then data center also kind of opportunity.

items.statement: Targeting own production of at least 6,000 BOEPD in FY27 if everything goes well
items.quote: I think, see, if everything goes well, we are targeting about reaching our own production level of at least 6,000 barrels of oil equivalent.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 1,500 crores remains unchanged; continuous drilling program planned
items.quote: Absolutely, there is no change in it. We will be embarking on a continuous drilling program and I think every well which we drill will add value to it

items.statement: Expected capital outlay for Northeast region for next two financial years is Rs 250 crores and more
items.quote: Our expected capital outlay for the Northeast region for the next two financial years is Rs.250 crores and more, and we endeavour to complete our drilling in the Northeast within two years to commercialize the discovered resources.

items.statement: Secured term loan of Rs 250 crores exclusively for capex; no intention to borrow more than this amount
items.quote: With internal accruals, we secured a debt capital of Rs. 250 crores to meet the above capital expenditure. This term loan will be used exclusively for our capital expenditure.

items.statement: No plans to borrow more than Rs 250 crores already secured
items.quote: No, we do not want to borrow more than Rs. 250 crores which we already secured it.

items.statement: Kharsang production reached ~900 bpd from 5 wells, up from initial 350 bpd; 7th well drilling in progress
items.quote: We have reached a production level of about 900 barrels per day from this block, up from 350 barrels of initial production.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales 14 MMSCFD (0.34 BCF) in Q2 FY26 vs 20 MMSCFD (0.49 BCF) in previous quarter; condensate 5,858 bbl vs 8,893 bbl
items.quote: Dirok gas sales for the current quarter is 14 million standard cubic feet per day, while the offtake in the previous quarter was 20 million standard cubic feet per day. Accordingly, the sales volume of the current quarter is 0.34 BCF compared to 0.49 BCF in the previous quarter for our share. Condensate production is 5,858 barrels compared to 8,893 barrels in the previous quarter.

items.statement: B-80 production 31,468 bbl oil and 0.23 BCF gas in Q2 FY26 vs 48,406 bbl oil and 0.37 BCF gas in previous quarter due to monsoon disruptions
items.quote: In Block B-80, where we hold 100% participating interest, production for the current quarter stands at 31,468 barrels of oil and 0.23 BCF of gas compared to 48,406 barrels of oil and 0.37 BCF of gas in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cambay production remains same at 0.33 MMSCFD gas in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Current production from Cambay remains the same at 0.33 MMSCFD of gas in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Dirok field capacity up to 50 MMSCFD with existing facilities; historically constrained by limited demand
items.quote: The field has the capacity to produce up to 50 million standard cubic feet per day with the existing facilities, though the production has historically been constrained by limited demand.

items.statement: Plan to drill 3 more development wells in Dirok and further drilling in North Dirok to augment capacity
items.quote: We will augment our capacity by drilling three more development wells in Dirok and further drilling in North Dirok.

items.statement: B-80 workover planned in Q4 FY26 (30-day job), then 3 development wells after next monsoon via new platform
items.quote: See, actually we wanted to start the work over now, but that is getting delayed by one, one and a half months. So, initially our program is to do one work over and after this, after the next monsoon we will start drilling three development wells.

items.statement: B-15 development plan progressing; expect to bring field into production within 2 years
items.quote: With a water depth of approximately 40 meters, we are confident of bringing the field into production within two years.

items.statement: PY-1 drilling program to commence in FY27: 2 in-fill wells, 1 appraisal well, 1 exploration well
items.quote: We propose to drilling two in-fill wells, one appraisal well through the existing platform and one exploration well outside the platform.

items.statement: Demand expected to rise significantly once Northeast Gas Grid fully integrated with National Gas Grid; IGGL Guwahati-Numaligarh commissioned, DNPL-IGGL linkage underway
items.quote: Demand is expected to rise significantly once the Northeast Gas Grid is fully integrated with the National Gas Grid. The progress made on this front is that IGGL has successfully commissioned the connection from Guwahati to Numaligarh. The next milestone is the completion of the DNPL-IGGL linkage, which is actively underway.

items.statement: Expect grid operational within FY26 and offtake increase before Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect the grid to be operational within FY26 and hope that the increase in offtake will occur before Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Dirok gas price realized US$7.8/MMBTU in Q2 FY26 vs US$7.56/MMBTU previous quarter
items.quote: Price realized in the current quarter is US$7.8 per MMBTU compared to US$7.56 MMBTU in the previous quarter.

items.statement: B-80 average gas price realized 10.62/MMBTU in Q2 FY26 vs 11.41/MMBTU previous quarter
items.quote: The average gas price realized during this quarter is 10.62 per MMBTU versus 11.41 per MMBTU in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Dirok cost of production very low, less than $0.75/MMBTU
items.quote: The cost of production is very low, it is about less than 0.75 per MMBTU.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Rs 25.15 cr in Q2 FY26 vs Rs 35.02 cr previous quarter due to low Dirok offtake and B-80 monsoon impact
items.quote: In consolidated accounts EBITDA for this quarter is Rs.25.15 crores compared to Rs.35.02 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA Rs 28.81 cr in Q2 FY26 vs Rs 27.24 cr previous quarter
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for the current quarter is Rs. 28.81 crores compared to Rs. 27.24 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: At current gas prices linked to oil, projects yield >21% post-tax IRR; no impairment expected
items.quote: Even at this price, our return should be more than 21% IRR, post-tax, right? So, we do not find substantial downside in this and nothing will happen to the Company. So, the transition unless and until the entire transition fuel taken place by some other renewable or other things, oil and gas industry will survive. As long as oil and gas industry survives, this is reasonably a low price at the mome

items.statement: DNPL line mechanical work completed; needs IGGL connection, PESO license, PNGRB common carrier declaration
items.quote: Now, what do they do is next is they will be connecting with the IGGL line. Once the IGGL line gets connected, then they will be applying for a PESO license or something. Once that is done, then the next issue is they will come to PNGRB for declaring it as a common carrier, that is still pending with PNGRB.

items.statement: HPCL contamination claim has no legal liability under COSA; crude is sweet and light with no quality issue; discussing amicable resolution
items.quote: As per COSA, no warranty or representation regarding the quality of the crude is provided, thus Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Limited November 21, 2025 negating any basis for claims or cost or consequential damages, if any, against us. We are currently engaged in discussion with HPCL to resolve the matter amicably and realize the sales revenue

items.statement: Kharsang 6th well gas zone well-control issue being resolved; no liability, fully insured with Rs 2 cr deductible
items.quote: No liability is there. We are fully insured, we are covered, and accepted deduction is of Rs. 2 crores and it will get resolved quickly.

items.statement: B-80 1P reserves ~15 MMbbl oil and 40-45 BCF gas
items.quote: 1P reserves we already declared, it is about 15 million barrel of oil and about 40-45 BCF of gas as such.

items.statement: Targets 3x keys, 3x revenue, 4x PAT growth from FY20 to FY30
items.quote: What we hope to achieve with this strategy from the decade from F '20 to F '30 is a 3x growth in keys, a 3x growth in revenue and a 4x growth in PAT in that duration.

items.statement: Club M brand targets 10,000 keys by FY30
items.quote: Our goal for this brand will be 10,000 keys by F '30.

items.statement: Mahindra Signature Resorts brand targets 2,000 keys by FY30
items.quote: In this brand, we plan to add another 2,000 keys. So the total keys will be 12,000. 10,000 in the first brand, 2,000 in the second brand by F '30.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance INR500-600 crore, FY27 INR700-750 crore
items.quote: I think this year, we probably are going to be about INR500 crores to INR600 crores. I'm giving you broad numbers. And next year, we are looking at about INR700 crores to INR750 crores, give or take.

items.statement: Renovation capex to triple to ~INR120 crore/year for couple of years
items.quote: As we go through this heightened period, my sense is that number will go up to maybe thrice that for a couple of years.

items.statement: Expect to add 1,000 rooms gross in FY26, momentum to continue/increase in FY27
items.quote: I have given some indication of this year that in this financial year gross level, we will add 1,000 rooms. I do expect that kind of momentum to continue or increase going into F '27 also.

items.statement: First Signature resort at Theog, Himachal under construction, targeting Q3/Q4 FY27 opening
items.quote: We think in F '27, we are already constructing. So in F '27, sometime probably in the later part, maybe even Q3 or Q4 is where we would like it to come out because it's well under construction right now. The first one is coming in Theog in Himachal.

items.statement: Incremental inventory 30% owned, 70% leased/managed; management contracts later for Signature
items.quote: So right now the way we are building it is largely about lease. Of course, management contract could come in, in the last year. And the owned piece will be about -- maybe about 30%, give or take, is what we feel.

items.statement: Keystone membership plan launching: 12 plans (down from 23), 3 seasons (down from 4), added concierge, flexible booking, buyback provision
items.quote: We are reducing the plans from 23 to 12. We are reducing the seasons from 4 to 3. There are certain privileges like concierge services, which we are adding. And we are adding flexibility, which is the most important thing in terms of some of the booking rules, and we are introducing a buyback provision.

items.statement: Leisure growing at double in-city hospitality rate; 80% prefer experiential travel, 56% book week before travel; weddings/MICE fastest-growing segments
items.quote: is some of the emerging trends. When we did a survey, I think 80% of the people preferred experiential travel rather than normal travel. The other trend is the last-minute booking. I think 56% said that they book a week before travel. So of course, this is something, which is a strong trend. And lastly, weddings and MICE is going to be a large market, and it's one of the fastest-growing segments

items.statement: Himachal occupancy impacted by weather (~3-4% occupancy shortfall, ~10,000 room nights), now recovering; Goa marginal impact
items.quote: Overall weather contributed about 10,000 room nights shortfall in occupancy, which on our base is roughly about 3% to 4%, give or take, in terms of occupancy. I think as I mentioned earlier to some other questions, Himachal, we are starting to see it claw back. And Goa, given our model, while there is some impact, we are not seeing a very major impact in Goa.

items.statement: PAT growth muted due to declining treasury income from capex deployment; ex-treasury margins to increase sharply
items.quote: If you actually isolate that and take that away, our growth will be much higher. It won't be just the number, which is coming out. But what is going to happen is the cash balance on an average will start coming down as we do the capex. And that is going to impact overall PAT and that's where this comes in.

items.statement: Return ratios (ROE, ROCE) expected to improve due to capital-light model shift
items.quote: I think they potentially will improve because, as I said, we are moving to a more capital-light model over a period of time. So I think from that perspective, it will probably improve from here.

items.statement: Plan to fund growth through internal accruals; no debt raise expected
items.quote: I do believe we can meet it through internal accruals largely, and we wouldn't have to go into debt. That's our current viewpoint.

items.statement: Shift from member count to rooms and revenue per room as key metrics; limiting members to increase availability
items.quote: We are not looking at members as a key metric, we are looking at rooms and revenue per room as a key metric. And that's one shift we are doing. So I don't think you should extrapolate member growth as company growth. I think we are increasingly looking at a disconnected model as we go forward.

items.statement: AUR up 33% with upgrades showing strong growth; focus on premium members and cost of acquisition
items.quote: Our AUR is up, if I remember correctly, 33% and with upgrades, it is up even more. And what is happening is upgrades is showing strong growth. We are focused on metrics around cost of acquisition and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Inventory pipeline visibility of ~3,000 keys for Club M
items.quote: We are well on track to do this with about a visibility of almost 3,000 keys plus today from where we stand currently in terms of our funnel.

items.statement: Vacation ownership only 8% of leisure market; Club Mahindra holds 85% share of that 8%
items.quote: If you look at the leisure market today, I think only 8% of the market is convention -- is vacation ownership, while 92% of the market is more about regular hospitality. Within that 8%, of course, as many of you know, we have an 85% market share.

items.statement: Finnish/overseas business in rough patch; performance stabilized, no capital addition, will reassess when markets improve
items.quote: I think that business is going through a rough patch in terms of the overall market and the Finnish economy is not doing well. So the focus has been on optimization and we are not adding capital in any case. So the performance has stabilized compared to last year. So I think we are on a sustained mode right now.

items.statement: Signature Resorts team built over 18 months; leader joined 18 months ago, team of 8-10 actively working
items.quote: The team, which is putting this together, I think we have had the first person who is the leader join us about 18 months back, just to give you a sense of the kind of preparation we have done to get to this point. Under him, we have a team of probably about 8 to 10 people already, who are actively working on all of those elements.

items.statement: Government infrastructure push (roads, airports, new tourism destinations) seen as huge positive for leisure
items.quote: And clearly, the government push in terms of infrastructure, whether it is roads or airports and pushing the agenda of creating new tourism destinations is a huge positive.

items.statement: 4 resorts shut for complete transformation; reopening over next 6-12 months
items.quote: And lastly, for the first time in our history, we are shutting down, and some of them already shut down, 4 resorts for a complete transformation in terms of the infrastructure. And over a period of the next 6 to 12 months, we should see some of that start reopening also.

items.statement: Targeting revenue of more than INR260 crores for FY26
items.quote: We are targeting a turnover of more than INR260 crores, reflecting a healthy increase over the previous year.

items.statement: Expecting revenue of more than INR350 crores to INR400 crores for FY27
items.quote: And next financial year we are hoping to do, we are expecting more than INR350 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 2-wheeler volume of more than 60,000 units for FY26
items.quote: This year, we are targeting more than 60,000 units.

items.statement: Targeting 2-wheeler volume of more than 1 lakh units for FY27
items.quote: Sir, we are hoping to do more than 1 lakhs, to achieve 1 lakhs.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% market share in slow-speed EV segment long-term
items.quote: our target and expectations are that in the future, we want to incre ase our market share to 25

items.statement: Investing less than INR3 crores for Odisha plant setup
items.quote: We are investing less than three crores to set up in Odisha plant.

items.statement: 3-wheeler plant at Patan funded from IPO proceeds, operational by April 2026
items.quote: We had already closed its capex in DRHP and for that we have raised funds from IPO.

items.statement: Hisar plant has 72,000 units annual 2-wheeler capacity, expandable to 120,000
items.quote: The Hisar plant has an installed capacity of 72,000 units per year an d is expendable up to 120,000 units annually with the same premises because of its modular assembly line design

items.statement: Odisha plant to add 50,000 units annual 2-wheeler capacity, operational by February 2026
items.quote: The capacity of Odisha's plant will be approximately 50,000 units per annum.

items.statement: Patan plant to add 24,000 units annual 3-wheeler capacity, operational by April 2026
items.quote: The new unit that is going to be set up in Patan, then our capacity will be almost 24,000 units per annum.

items.statement: Current 3-wheeler capacity is 2,000 units annually at Hisar
items.quote: The existing capacity of 3-wheelers in this plant is almost 2,000 units per annum.

items.statement: Slow-speed EV demand estimated to reach 17.5 lakh units by FY28
items.quote: By financial year 28, slow speed EV demand is estimated to reach 17.5 la kh units and importantly, all segments are expected to grow in parallel serving different customer needs rather than competing with each other

items.statement: Rural markets dominating, Tier 1 city demand increasing rapidly
items.quote: Sir, in rural markets we are dominating the industry. And we are now also entering in the Tier 1 cities as well. Now, Tier 1 cities demand is also increasing rapidly.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA INR15.36 crores, up 71% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA, if we talk about EBITDA, EBITDA, we have done INR15.36 crores up by 71% year on year.

items.statement: 2-wheeler EBITDA margin at 13%, expected to remain constant
items.quote: In 2-wheeler segment, we have EBITDA margin of 13%.

items.statement: 3-wheeler EBITDA margin currently low, expected to improve to 7-8%+ after Patan plant operational
items.quote: And our EBITDA margins will be approx 7% to 8%, more than 8%.

items.statement: Odisha plant to reduce logistics costs and improve margins
items.quote: Like, now we are setting plant in Odisha. It will reduce our logistics cost. And number of dealers will increase.

items.statement: H1 FY26 sold approximately 30,000 2-wheeler units
items.quote: In H1 financial year '26, we have sold approximately more than 30,000 units.

items.statement: FY25 sold approximately 37,000 2-wheeler units
items.quote: In the last financial year, we have sold approximately 37,000 units.

items.statement: H1 FY26 sold 400 3-wheeler units
items.quote: Till now, we have only done 400 units of e-rickshaw.

items.statement: Average selling price of 2-wheeler INR40,000-45,000
Average selling price of 3-wheeler approx INR1,10,000
items.quote: Average selling price of 3-wheeler is approx INR1,10,000.

items.statement: Current localization at 30%, targeting 80% in upcoming years
items.quote: Now it is 30% Indianization. Now our target is 80%. We will take it to 80%, sir. We will take it to 80% within the upcoming years, sir

items.statement: Battery cells will not be indigenized, focus on plastic parts, painting, framework, electrical parts
items.quote: No, we will not indigenize the cell as of now. We will mostly work on the plastic parts, painting, framework and some of the electrical parts.

items.statement: 3-wheeler customers are unemployed people converting from 2-wheelers for livelihood
items.quote: Unemployed people who need work are driving rickshaws.

items.statement: Claims to be only organized brand in low-speed segment, confident against big players
items.quote: Sir, once we enter the market, no matter who comes, whether Hero or Bajaj, they will not be able to take us out of the market.

items.statement: Not currently included in PLI scheme, will work on it in future
items.quote: Sir, till now we don't have any PLI scheme. But in future we will surely work on it.

items.statement: Industry growing at roughly 30% CAGR, Zelio growing at 84% CAGR over last 3 years
items.quote: To put our performance in context, while the industry grows at roughly 30% CAGR, Zelio has grown at 84% CAGR.
